                              if (level_boxes_parse_number(v6, &tsid_f)) lex->target_spawner_id = (int)tsid_f;
                          }
                          out->level_exit_count++;
                          lecursor = leobj_end + 1;
                      }
                  }
              }
          }
      
          // Zones (BIG_O engine merge phase 7c) -- same real, small-scanner convention as level exits
          // above. Absent "zones" key is a real, honest "no authored zones for this level" state, not
          // an error -- zone_count stays 0, and level_boxes_zone_for_position (below) always returns
          // -1 for a level with none.
          out->zone_count = 0;
          const char *zn_arr_key = level_boxes_find_key(buf, end, "zones");
          if (zn_arr_key) {
              const char *zn_arr = level_boxes_skip_ws(zn_arr_key);
              if (*zn_arr == '[') {
                  const char *zn_arr_end = level_boxes_find_array_end(zn_arr, end);
                  if (zn_arr_end) {
                      const char *zncursor = zn_arr + 1;
                      while (zncursor < zn_arr_end && out->zone_count < LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_ZONES) {
                          zncursor = level_boxes_skip_ws(zncursor);
                          if (zncursor >= zn_arr_end) break;
                          if (*zncursor == ',') { zncursor++; continue; }
                          if (*zncursor != '{') { zncursor++; continue; }
                          const char *znobj_start = zncursor;
                          const char *znobj_end = strchr(znobj_start, '}');
                          if (!znobj_end || znobj_end > zn_arr_end) break;
      
                          LevelZone *zn = &out->zones[out->zone_count];
                          memset(zn, 0, sizeof(*zn));
                          const char *v7;
                          if ((v7 = level_boxes_find_key(znobj_start, znobj_end, "x"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v7, &zn->x);
                          if ((v7 = level_boxes_find_key(znobj_start, znobj_end, "y"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v7, &zn->y);
                          if ((v7 = level_boxes_find_key(znobj_start, znobj_end, "z"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v7, &zn->z);
                          if ((v7 = level_boxes_find_key(znobj_start, znobj_end, "radius"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v7, &zn->radius);
                          if ((v7 = level_boxes_find_key(znobj_start, znobj_end, "zone_type"))) {
                              float zt_f = 0.0f;
                              if (level_boxes_parse_number(v7, &zt_f)) zn->zone_type = (int)zt_f;
                          }
                          out->zone_count++;
                          zncursor = znobj_end + 1;
                      }
                  }
              }
          }
      
          // Programmable widgets ("edu_widgets"). Absent key = none authored, not an error. A malformed entry
          // (no entity_id, or a machine_type outside 1..5) is skipped, never half-loaded.
          out->edu_widget_count = 0;
          const char *ew_arr_key = level_boxes_find_key(buf, end, "edu_widgets");
          if (ew_arr_key) {
              const char *ew_arr = level_boxes_skip_ws(ew_arr_key);
              if (*ew_arr == '[') {
                  const char *ew_arr_end = level_boxes_find_array_end(ew_arr, end);
                  if (ew_arr_end) {
                      const char *ewc = ew_arr + 1;
                      while (ewc < ew_arr_end && out->edu_widget_count < LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS) {
                          ewc = level_boxes_skip_ws(ewc);
                          if (ewc >= ew_arr_end) break;
                          if (*ewc != '{') { ewc++; continue; }
                          const char *eo_start = ewc;
                          const char *eo_end = strchr(eo_start, '}');
                          if (!eo_end || eo_end > ew_arr_end) break;
                          LevelEduWidget tmp;
                          memset(&tmp, 0, sizeof tmp);
                          tmp.box_index = -1;
                          const char *ev;
                          float f = 0.0f;
                          int ok = 0;
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "entity_id")))
                              ok = level_boxes_parse_string(ev, tmp.entity_id, sizeof tmp.entity_id) > 0 && tmp.entity_id[0];
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "machine_type")) && level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &f)) tmp.machine_type = (int)f;
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "initial_state")) && level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &f)) tmp.initial_state = f != 0.0f;
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "memory_address")) && level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &f)) tmp.memory_address = (int)f;
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "x"))) level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &tmp.x);
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "y"))) level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &tmp.y);
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "z"))) level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &tmp.z);
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "radius"))) level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &tmp.radius);
                          if ((ev = level_boxes_find_key(eo_start, eo_end, "box_index")) && level_boxes_parse_number(ev, &f)) tmp.box_index = (int)f;
                          if (tmp.box_index >= out->count) tmp.box_index = -1;
                          if (ok && tmp.machine_type >= 1 && tmp.machine_type <= 5)
                              out->edu_widgets[out->edu_widget_count++] = tmp;
                          ewc = eo_end + 1;
                      }
                  }
              }
          }
      
          return 1;
      }
      
      /* level_boxes_zone_for_position -- BIG_O engine merge phase 7c. Returns the zone_type of the
       * FIRST authored zone volume (in authoring order) whose sphere contains (x,y,z) (flat-Euclidean,
       * y included -- unlike witness_live.h's own deliberately flat (x,z) checks, since zones are meant
       * to distinguish e.g. a lab basement from a street-level plaza at the same x/z), or -1 if the
       * level has no zones at all, or none of them contain this point ("no zone authored here" is a
       * real, honest, non-fatal outcome -- the caller decides the fallback, matching level_exits'/
       * spawners' own "absent is honest, not an error" convention throughout this file). Overlapping
       * zones are a real, deliberate author error this function does not detect or warn about -- first
       * match wins, same as every other array-scan helper in this file. */
      static inline int level_boxes_zone_for_position(const CustomLevelData *level, float x, float y, float z) {
          if (!level) return -1;
          for (int i = 0; i < level->zone_count; i++) {
              const LevelZone *zn = &level->zones[i];
              float dx = x - zn->x, dy = y - zn->y, dz = z - zn->z;
              float r = zn->radius;
              if (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz <= r * r) return zn->zone_type;
          }
          return -1;
      }

SERVER_BIN   := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_server
SERVERCTL_BIN:= $(BIN_DIR)/serverctl

EA_DIR       := dist/ea

# ---- Targets ----
.PHONY: test-witness-ai-zombies test-bullet-hole test-queue-level test-baked-levels bake-levels all lobby server serverctl clean setup print go-server ea ea-windows emily-bot rigid-ragdoll test-physics test-audio-chain ux-screenshot-test

all: $(LOBBY_BIN) $(SERVER_BIN)

$(BIN_DIR):

setup: $(BIN_DIR)

== changelog head ==
## 2026-10-16

- **fix(brick): the XPBD rigid-body debris is replaced by a cheap fake** (founder: it was slow, inconsistent, glass worse; "revert, fake it, no piling"). Shot-out cells shed the old flakes again. Cut-off geometry (glass disc, wall section) falls as one chunk with gravity + a seeded tumble, one level probe per chunk per tick, one small bounce, lies flat on the floor or whatever it lands on, then lingers 5 s. Max 32 chunks, no solver/pairs/piling; the dedicated server no longer simulates debris at all. Mass/density (NOCK material) kept as data. Headless tests only; live feel not verified.
- **feat(zombies): pheromone thrower is a real grenade.** `G` lobs a 0.8 kg canister (`packages/simulation/pheromone_grenade.h`: impulse/mass launch speed, ballistic arc, mass-dependent bounce, wall bounce, Coulomb roll to rest, inherits the thrower's velocity). The marker zombies chase rides the canister, so they track it in the air and through each bounce; the thud on landing startles zombies in range. Visuals: tumbling glowing canister with a streak, pulsing ground rings + scent wisps + smell-radius ring when down, G-key READY/cooldown HUD, red diamonds over starving zombies. `make test-pheromone-grenade`. Not seen in the live game.
- **feat(zombies): hunger infighting.** A zombie whose hunger >= 0.70 with the hero out of sense smells the nearest zombie / citizen / Man (up to 135 units), hunts it and bites (16 dmg, feeds it); a bitten zombie fights back; The Men melee zombies within 14 units. Dead victims are permanent corpses. Tuning (rates, radii) is a first pass.


- feat(brick): **physical broken brick + falling disconnected geometry.** Shot-out cells throw mass-carrying shards (brick ~15 kg, density x volume) and any group of cells cut off from the ground/static solids falls as a rigid chunk (shoot a circle out of glass and the disc drops, with a seeded tumble), all on GOLDEN BAND's `grb` XPBD solver via new `packages/simulation/brick_bodies.{h,c}` (shards pile as cubes, slide down ramps via `obb.h`). `brick_fracture.h`: bounded flood-fill detection `bf_detect_detached` (found and fixed a real bug in its own tests: a flood that met an earlier flood's cells wrongly treated itself as cut off), chunk id on the brick wire pad byte, shard queue, per-parent density. Mass configurable per NOCK material (`density` kg/m^3 in `level_boxes.h`; IDUNA migration + Materials screen field). Server and lobby tick the bodies; lobby draws them (glass translucent). New `make test-brick-bodies` / `test-brick-density`; `test-brick-fracture` and `test-brick-world` extended. Bodies are per-client cosmetic (not synced), do not hit players; live visual check not done (scripted input unreliable), headless tests only. README updated.

- fix(windows): real in-phone PELLEGRINO browser on Windows via `scripts/build_pgb_windows.sh` (mingw; stub fallback, cacert.pem shipped). Untested on Windows (CI-built).

- feat(lobby): **GFD phone app is on the cross-game chat bus** (`packages/gfd_chat/gfd_chat.h`, tested by `gfd_chat_test.c`). Messages typed in the phone's GFD terminal post to IDUNA `/api/v1/chat/messages` (channel `shankpit`) under the player's IDUNA display name and are polled back every 3s, so every SHANKPIT GFD phone sees them regardless of game/mode, plus the GFD MUD's `global` chat (shown as `[GFD] name`). Requires signing in via the phone's IDUNA app first (the token is the credential). Verified end to end with two lobby clients plus a simulated MUD post against a fake chat-bus server; NOT yet against the real IDUNA (needs the IDUNA `shankpit` channel deployed). Windows: stubbed no-op. README updated.
- **Phone IDUNA app is live in-game (2026-10-16):** the SHANKPHONE IDUNA tile (zombies/lab/story) now runs the exact same loopback SSO flow as the legacy menu's LOGIN IDUNA button (system browser -> IDUNA hosted login -> 127.0.0.1 token return), polled every frame during play; shows `CODE: BROWSER` while pending, `LINKED: <name>` on success, an error on timeout. Replaces the "use IDUNA.GAME" stub. Pending state verified live under Xvfb; the full token return is untested here (no IDUNA reachable).
- **feat(phone): PELLEGRINO in-phone browser now builds and runs.** `make lobby` links `packages/pellegrino_browser_embed` (mbedTLS + monocypher + embed objects, `PGB_OBJS`, kept out of `LOBBY_SRC`). Verified live under Xvfb `--zombies`: page renders in the phone panel, URL typing navigates, Esc returns to the home grid. Open: mouse, in-game `h3://` check, Windows/CI wiring. README updated.

## 2026-10-16

- ZOMBIES boot now always asks the network for the level NOCK flagged with "Set for ZOMBIES" (baked table stays the offline fallback), instead of ignoring it while LIVE LEVELS is OFF.- fix(edit-map): live-edit X/B now send the box geometry so NOCK removes/adds the same wall; F5 in a live session asks NOCK to save. F5's local `SAVE FAILED` was a missing `var/` dir (now created). Built; not driven against the live NOCK.
- fix(phone): `:` (and every typed character) now reaches the in-phone PELLEGRINO browser and the GFD terminal. SDL only emits text events while text input is started and nothing started it for the phone, so the address bar never opened; the lobby now starts/stops it with the open phone app. Built; not driven live. (boot straight into zombies)
- `shank_lobby` with no mode flag now skips the title/main menu and drops straight into MODE_ZOMBIES; Esc leaves to the legacy lobby menu (same exit as pause > QUIT, autosaves). `--menu` boots the legacy menu instead. Verified live under Xvfb (boot -> zombies city, Esc -> lobby).

## 2026-10-16

- fix(heli): the helicopter MESH turned the mirror way from the flight model (founder: "rotating the helicopter is visual only ... forward acts as though the nose is still pointed the other direction"). `draw_helicopter_model` rotated by `180 - yaw` but the nose is +Z and sim forward is `(-sin yaw, -cos yaw)`; now `180 + yaw`, and pitch/roll visuals negated for the +Z nose (forward flight was nose-up, right bank dipped the left side). Reverted my wrong earlier change that rotated velocity with the nose (momentum is meant to persist through a turn). Not run live (no GLU/display); math only.

== test_edit_map ==
#include <assert.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include "edit_map.h"
int main(void) {
    static CustomLevelData lvl; static EditLog log, log2; memset(&lvl, 0, sizeof lvl);
    lvl.boxes[0] = (LevelBox){0,0,0, 10,2,10}; lvl.count = 1;
    lvl.spawners[0].x = 1; lvl.spawner_count = 1;
    EditOp add = {EDIT_OP_ADD_BOX, 0, 5,3,5, 2,2,2, 0};
    assert(edit_map_do(&log, &lvl, &add) && lvl.count == 2);
    assert(edit_map_box_at(&lvl, 5, 3, 5, 0.01f) == 1);
    assert(edit_map_box_at(&lvl, 0, 0, 0, 0.01f) == 0);
    assert(edit_map_box_at(&lvl, 50, 0, 0, 0.01f) == -1);
    EditOp mv = {EDIT_OP_MOVE_SPAWNER, 0, 7,8,9, 0,0,0, 90};
    assert(edit_map_do(&log, &lvl, &mv) && lvl.spawners[0].x == 7 && lvl.spawners[0].yaw == 90);
    EditOp bad = {EDIT_OP_MOVE_SPAWNER, 3, 0,0,0, 0,0,0, 0};
    assert(!edit_map_do(&log, &lvl, &bad) && log.n == 2);
    EditOp del = {EDIT_OP_DEL_BOX, 0, 0,0,0, 0,0,0, 0};
    assert(edit_map_do(&log, &lvl, &del) && lvl.count == 1 && lvl.boxes[0].x == 5);
    assert(edit_map_save(&log, "t", "/tmp/edit_map_test.json"));
    static CustomLevelData l2; memset(&l2, 0, sizeof l2);
    l2.boxes[0] = (LevelBox){0,0,0, 10,2,10}; l2.count = 1; l2.spawners[0].x = 1; l2.spawner_count = 1;
    assert(edit_map_load_apply(&log2, &l2, "/tmp/edit_map_test.json") == 3);
    assert(l2.count == 1 && l2.boxes[0].x == 5 && l2.spawners[0].z == 9);
    assert(edit_map_load_apply(&log2, &l2, "/nonexistent") == -1);
    puts("edit_map ok"); return 0;
}

Both `level_boxes.h` and `edit_map.h` are already included by the lobby, so the F6 path is wired. Local level building now saves real level JSON with no IDUNA in the loop.

**What changed (all in `/content/MONOREPO/SHANKPIT`)**

- `packages/world/level_boxes.h` — new `level_boxes_write_json` / `level_boxes_save_to_file`: the reverse of the existing parser, emitting a complete level document in the same shape IDUNA's export returns. Every field the loader reads is written: walls/materials (incl. rotation, ramp, material name), spawners (id/team/yaw), buggy spawns, lab stations, doors (button subscriptions + script paths), buttons, nav nodes + neighbors, characters, exits (+ `target_spawner_id`), zones, edu widgets, brick damage, `enclosed`, `floor_tint`, `next_level_id`. `level_boxes_parse_string` now honours `\\ \" \n \t \r` escapes, needed because the writer emits real JSON (and it fixes Windows door script paths).
- `packages/world/edit_map.h` — `edit_map_save_level()` plus an updated rationale: the old comment said a C round-trip would drop doors/characters/widgets, which is exactly what the full writer now prevents.
- `apps/lobby/src/main.c` — **F6 in EDIT MAP saves the whole working level to `var/maps/<name>.json`**, and deletes the now-redundant `var/maps/<name>.edits.json` so a replay can't double-apply the edits. F5's op log stays (it's the live-NOCK streaming format).
- `packages/world/level_save_test.c` + `make test-level-save`, and a CHANGELOG entry.

**Usage:** `make lobby`, then `./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map var/maps/mymap.json` (or `--edit-map` to start from the checked-in map), build with B / X / M, press **F6**, and the file is a standalone level you can reopen or run with `--level`.

**Checks actually run**
- `make test-level-save` → `level_save ok` (one of every object kind: save → load → field-by-field compare, plus byte-identical re-save)
- `make test-baked-levels` → 64 main levels + zombies default, all pass (loader regression)
- `apps/tests/test_edit_map.c` compiled and run → `edit_map ok`
- `level_boxes_edu_widgets_test` → all PASS
- Round-trip of the checked-in real exports: `var/lab/lab.json` (34 boxes, 9 lab stations), the story-doors demo (2 doors), `nextown_zombies.json` (80 boxes) and all 8 `assets/tyler_levels/*.json` → all ok

**Limitation:** the lobby binary itself wasn't compiled or run — this container has no SDL2/GL headers or display, so F6's key handling is validated by the header-level round-trip test rather than by pressing the key in the running client. I also didn't try standing up a local IDUNA: it needs `MYSQL_DSN` plus a pile of env config, so file-backed levels were the smaller path to "batteries included".

      # SHANKPIT Game Architecture Document
      
      ## Current Status (2026-08-26)
      
      CI is green (`ShankPit Factory` #784+) after a real fix: the cutscene system and spatial
      audio engine (both real, shipped features) had never been added to the Windows client's hardcoded
      mingw build command, so every CI run since build #721 failed with undefined references. Also
      fixed: helicopter HUD text was overlapping into unreadable garbage — the real flight physics
      (enter/fly/hover) were never actually broken, just unreadable.
      
      **New since**: CTF-with-bots (MODE_CTFB) now randomly picks Voxworld or Oil Tanker instead of
      always Oil Tanker; story-mode enemies got real abilities (2 new threat roles, RedGarden-style
      squad AI and abilities — graphics stay stubs for now, abilities do not); GOLDENBAND skinned-mesh
      support landed (S144-02 Stage B). See `CHANGELOG.md`.
      
      ## What SHANKPIT is right now
      
      At a high level, SHANKPIT currently includes:
      
      - a lobby/client app with local and networked play flows
      - a UDP server-authoritative game server
      - multiple local and networked game modes
      - linked scenes connected by portals
      - terrain-backed worlds in addition to box/block geometry
      - team modes including team deathmatch and capture the flag
      - bot support for local team modes and online cold-start scenarios
      - a growing retro rendering stack with procedural textures, sky, fog, and stylized lighting
      - persistent skin selection
      - **sound engineering primitives from PARENA** (2026-09-27): `packages/audio/audio_dsp_gen.c` is C
        compiled from PARENA `stdlib/audio` (biquads, compressor/expander/de-esser/limiter, BS.1770
        loudness, plus DJ mixer/deck/MPC-sampler curves); `audio_chain.c` runs filter chains authored in
        IDUNA's NOCK Sounds tab. Set `SHANKPIT_SOUND_CHAIN=<name>` to run a NOCK chain over the whole
        engine mix (fetched from `SHANKPIT_SOUND_CHAIN_URL`, default
        `https://okemily.com/api/v1/nock-sound-filters`) -- with no chain set, the mixer path is
        byte-for-byte the old one. `make test-audio-chain` proves the C runner matches NOCK's TypeScript
        render bit-for-bit (max |diff| 0 over 24,000 samples). Not yet played through in a live session
        with a real chain against production IDUNA.
      - test coverage for protocol and gameplay regressions. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2} :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3} :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
      
      ---
      
      ## Current game modes
      
      The current lobby/game flow exposes these core modes:
      
      - **JOIN** — connect to the online deathmatch flow
      - **TDMO** — online team deathmatch with bots supporting cold start
      - **SOLO** — local single-player deathmatch flow
      - **TRAIN** — local training-oriented flow
      - **TDMB** — local team deathmatch with bots
      - **CTFB** — local capture the flag with bots. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
      
      Internally, the client also recognizes additional local mode IDs such as `battle`, `tdm`, `training`, `recorder`, and `garage`, but the player-facing lobby is currently centered on the six modes above. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
      
      ---
      
      ## OS menu = HTML + CSS (2026-10-15)
      
      The lobby's tile grid is no longer hand-placed GL rectangles: each page is a small generated HTML document with a
      plain stylesheet (`packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.c`), laid out and painted by PELLEGRINO -- the PARENA
      browser engine -- into an offscreen surface that the lobby draws as one textured quad. Clicks go through the
      engine's link hit-test back to the tile index. `make test-os-menu` (headless) and `make test-os-menu-gl` (needs a GL
      display) check it; `SHANKPIT_OS_MENU=classic` selects the old grid. Regenerate the vendored engine with
      `scripts/gen_pellegrino_embed.sh` (needs sibling `../PELLEGRINO` and a built `../PARENA/parena`). Status: tested in
      isolation; the whole lobby has not been built/run with it on the dev box yet, and the skin/level/spray overlays,
      title and the small corner buttons are still hand-drawn GL.
      
      ## Boot behaviour (2026-10-16)
      `./bin/shank_lobby` has no title screen or main menu: it drops straight into a ZOMBIES game. Esc goes to the legacy menu; `--menu` starts there instead. Explicit flags (`--survival`, `--lab`, `--city`, `--edit-map`) still win.
      
      ## In-phone PELLEGRINO browser (2026-10-16)
      
      The in-fiction SHANKPHONE (open with `P` during a match) has a `PELLEGRINO` tile that runs a real,
      embedded browser inside the phone panel — not the Apps-page launcher tile above (that one spawns a
      separate window). `packages/pellegrino_browser_embed/` wraps PELLEGRINO's `embed-nav-*` API (TLS 1.2/1.3
      and HTTP/3-over-QUIC; no HTTP/2) and is linked into `shank_lobby` by `make lobby` as pre-built objects
      (mbedTLS fetched via `../PELLEGRINO/scripts/fetch_mbedtls.sh`; needs sibling `../PELLEGRINO`,
      `../PARENA`, `../EDITOR.GAME`, and `libsdl2-ttf-dev`). Regenerate the package with
      `scripts/gen_pellegrino_browser_embed.sh`. Status: verified under Xvfb in `--zombies` — page renders in
      the panel (live `https://example.com/`), typing a URL navigates, Esc returns to the phone home grid.

l->name : \"(unnamed)\", (double)l->width, (double)l->height, (double)l->depth,\n           l->ground_plane_enabled ? \"on\" : \"off\", l->ground_plane_squares,\n           l->enclosed ? \"   enclosed\" : \"\");\n    printf(\"  walls %d   materials %d   spawners %d   doors %d   buttons %d\\n\",\n           l->count, l->material_count, l->spawner_count, l->door_count, l->button_count);\n    printf(\"  buggy spawns %d   lab stations %d   nav nodes %d   characters %d\\n\",\n           l->buggy_spawn_count, l->lab_station_count, l->nav_node_count, l->character_count);\n    printf(\"  exits %d   zones %d   edu widgets %d   brick damage cells %d%s\\n\",\n           l->level_exit_count, l->zone_count, l->edu_widget_count, l->brick_damage_count,\n           l->next_level_id ? \"\" : \"   (no next level)\");\n    if (l->next_level_id) printf(\"  next level id %d\\n\", l->next_level_id);\n    if (l->floor_tinted)\n        printf(\"  floor tint  r %g  g %g  b %g  a %g\\n\",\n               (double)l->floor_r, (double)l->floor_g, (double)l->floor_b, (double)l->floor_a);\n}\n\n/* Every array count plus the header fields that must survive. Deliberately structural (not\n * per-wall floats): packages/world/level_save_test.c already asserts the field-by-field detail. */\nstatic int same_shape(const CustomLevelData *a, const CustomLevelData *b) {\n    return strcmp(a->name, b->name) == 0 && a->count == b->count &&\n           a->material_count == b->material_count && a->spawner_count == b->spawner_count &&\n           a->door_count == b->door_count && a->button_count == b->button_count &&\n           a->buggy_spawn_count == b->buggy_spawn_count && a->lab_station_count == b->lab_station_count &&\n           a->nav_node_count == b->nav_node_count && a->character_count == b->character_count &&\n           a->level_exit_count == b->level_exit_count && a->zone_count == b->zone_count &&\n           a->edu_widget_count == b->edu_widget_count && a->brick_damage_count == b->brick_damage_count &&\n           a->next_level_id == b->next_level_id && a->enclosed == b->enclosed &&\n           a->ground_plane_enabled == b->ground_plane_enabled &&\n           a->ground_plane_squares == b->ground_plane_squares && a->floor_tinted == b->floor_tinted;\n}\n\nstatic int same_file(const char *pa, const char *pb) {\n    FILE *fa = fopen(pa, \"rb\"), *fb = fopen(pb, \"rb\");\n    if (!fa || !fb) { if (fa) fclose(fa); if (fb) fclose(fb); return 0; }\n    int same = 1, ca, cb;\n    do {\n        ca = fgetc(fa);\n        cb = fgetc(fb);\n        if (ca != cb) { same = 0; break; }\n    } while (ca != EOF);\n    fclose(fa); fclose(fb);\n    return same;\n}\n\nstatic int cmd_check(const char *path) {\n    static CustomLevelData a, b;\n    if (!load_or_die(path, &a)) return 1;\n\n    char pass1[512], pass2[512];\n    snprintf(pass1, sizeof pass1, \"%s/leveltool_%ld_a.json\", tmp_dir(), (long)getpid());\n    snprintf(pass2, sizeof pass2, \"%s/leveltool_%ld_b.json\", tmp_dir(), (long)getpid());\n\n    if (!level_boxes_save_to_file(pass1, &a)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"leveltool: cannot write %s\\n\", pass1);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    if (!load_or_die(pass1, &b)) return 1;\n    if (!same_shape(&a, &b)) {\n        fprintf(stderr,\n                \"leveltool: FAIL %s -- round-trip changed the level \"\n                \"(walls %d->%d, doors %d->%d, buttons %d->%d, characters %d->%d, exits %d->%d, \"\n                \"zones %d->%d, edu widgets %d->%d, brick cells %d->%d, stations %d->%d, \"\n                \"buggy spawns %d->%d, nav nodes %d->%d, materials %d->%d, spawners %d->%d)\\n\",\n                path, a.count, b.count, a.door_count, b.door_count, a.button_count, b.button_count,\n                a.character_count, b.character_count, a.level_exit_count, b.level_exit_count,\n                a.zone_count, b.zone_count, a.edu_widget_count, b.edu_widget_count,\n                a.brick_damage_count, b.brick_damage_count, a.lab_station_count, b.lab_station_count,\n                a.buggy_spawn_count, b.buggy_spawn_count, a.nav_node_count, b.nav_node_count,\n                a.material_count, b.material_count, a.spawner_count, b.spawner_count);\n        remove(pass1);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    if (!level_boxes_save_to_file(pass2, &b) || !same_file(pass1, pass2)) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"leveltool: FAIL %s -- writer is not stable (two saves differ)\\n\", path);\n        remove(pass1);\n        remove(pass2);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    remove(pass1);\n    remove(pass2);\n    printf(\"ok  %-48s %d walls, %d doors, %d characters, %d exits, %d zones\\n\",\n           path, b.count, b.door_count, b.character_count, b.level_exit_count, b.zone_count);\n    return 0;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    if (argc < 3) { usage(); return 2; }\n    const char *cmd = argv[1];\n\n    if (strcmp(cmd, \"info\") == 0) {\n        static CustomLevelData lvl;\n        if (!load_or_die(argv[2], &lvl)) return 1;\n        print_summary(argv[2], &lvl);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(cmd, \"check\") == 0) return cmd_check(argv[2]);\n\n    if (strcmp(cmd, \"save\") == 0) {\n        if (argc < 4) { usage(); return 2; }\n        static CustomLevelData lvl;\n        if (!load_or_die(argv[2], &lvl)) return 1;\n        if (!level_boxes_save_to_file(argv[3], &lvl)) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"leveltool: cannot write %s\\n\", argv[3]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n        printf(\"wrote %s (%d walls)\\n\", argv[3], lvl.count);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(cmd, \"new\") == 0) {\n        if (argc < 4) { usage(); return 2; }\n        static CustomLevelData lvl;\n        edit_map_init_new(&lvl, argv[2]);\n        if (!level_boxes_save_to_file(argv[3], &lvl)) {\n            fprintf(stderr, \"leveltool: cannot write %s\\n\", argv[3]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n        printf(\"wrote %s (new level '%s', %g x %g x %g, one spawner)\\n\",\n               argv[3], lvl.name, (double)lvl.width, (double)lvl.height, (double)lvl.depth);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    usage();\n    return 2;\n}\n"

Pushed: `29009f3 feat(tools): leveltool, a headless level JSON checker for offline maps`.

**Added this round**
- `tools/leveltool.c` — one binary over the same loader/writer the game uses:
  - `info <file>` — name, dimensions, ground plane, and a count of every object type
  - `check <file>` — load → save → load, fails if any parsed field changed shape, then re-saves and fails if the writer isn't byte-stable
  - `save <in> <out>` — normalize/re-emit
  - `new <name> <out>` — an empty level using EDIT MAP's new-level defaults
- `mk/leveltool.mk` (following the repo's per-package fragment convention, so the main Makefile stays untouched): `make leveltool`, `make test-leveltool`, `make check-levels`.
- README now documents `--level var/maps/<name>.json` for playing a locally saved map (I checked the flag's parsing — it does load a `.json` path, both sides need the same path) and the leveltool commands; CHANGELOG extended.

**Checks actually run**
- `make leveltool`, `make test-leveltool` → new → check → info all pass
- `make check-levels` → all 10 checked-in exports pass, including `var/lab/lab.json` (34 walls, 1 exit), the story-doors demo (2 doors) and `nextown_zombies.json` (80 walls, 12 characters)
- `make test-level-save` → `level_save ok` (still green after the edits)
- Exit codes: no args → 2, missing file → 1

**Limitations**
- Still no lobby build/run here (no SDL2/GL headers, no display), so the F6 key path and new-level start remain proven at the loader/tool level rather than by pressing keys.
- `leveltool check` compares structure (counts + header fields), not every float — the field-by-field detail is `make test-level-save`'s job.
- The tool is POSIX-only (uses `$TMPDIR`/`/tmp` and `getpid`), which is fine for a dev tool that never links into the game.

Deliberately rough\n * (one cell per (span / 75) units, Y ignored) -- enough to see a layout, not a screenshot. */\n#define MAP_MAX_W 76\n#define MAP_MAX_H 36\n\nstatic void map_plot(char grid[MAP_MAX_H][MAP_MAX_W], int w, int h, double x, double z,\n                     double minx, double minz, double cell, char ch) {\n    if (cell <= 0) return;\n    int cx = (int)((x - minx) / cell + 0.5);\n    int cz = (int)((z - minz) / cell + 0.5);\n    if (cx < 0 || cx >= w || cz < 0 || cz >= h) return;\n    grid[cz][cx] = ch;\n}\n\nstatic int cmd_map(const char *path) {\n    static CustomLevelData l;\n    if (!load_or_die(path, &l)) return 1;\n\n    double minx = 1e30, maxx = -1e30, minz = 1e30, maxz = -1e30;\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.count; i++) {\n        const LevelBox *b = &l.boxes[i];\n        double hx = (double)b->w * 0.5, hz = (double)b->d * 0.5;\n        if ((double)b->x - hx < minx) minx = (double)b->x - hx;\n        if ((double)b->x + hx > maxx) maxx = (double)b->x + hx;\n        if ((double)b->z - hz < minz) minz = (double)b->z - hz;\n        if ((double)b->z + hz > maxz) maxz = (double)b->z + hz;\n    }\n    if (l.count == 0) { minx = -20; maxx = 20; minz = -20; maxz = 20; }\n    double spanx = maxx - minx, spanz = maxz - minz;\n    if (spanx < 1) spanx = 1;\n    if (spanz < 1) spanz = 1;\n    double cell = spanx / (MAP_MAX_W - 1);\n    if (spanz / (MAP_MAX_H - 1) > cell) cell = spanz / (MAP_MAX_H - 1);\n    int w = (int)(spanx / cell) + 1, h = (int)(spanz / cell) + 1;\n    if (w > MAP_MAX_W) w = MAP_MAX_W;\n    if (h > MAP_MAX_H) h = MAP_MAX_H;\n    if (w < 1) w = 1;\n    if (h < 1) h = 1;\n\n    static char grid[MAP_MAX_H][MAP_MAX_W];\n    memset(grid, ' ', sizeof grid);\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.count; i++) {\n        const LevelBox *b = &l.boxes[i];\n        double hx = (double)b->w * 0.5, hz = (double)b->d * 0.5;\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)b->x, (double)b->z, minx, minz, cell, '#');\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)b->x - hx, (double)b->z - hz, minx, minz, cell, '#');\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)b->x + hx, (double)b->z + hz, minx, minz, cell, '#');\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)b->x - hx, (double)b->z + hz, minx, minz, cell, '#');\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)b->x + hx, (double)b->z - hz, minx, minz, cell, '#');\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.zone_count; i++)\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)l.zones[i].x, (double)l.zones[i].z, minx, minz, cell, 'z');\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.level_exit_count; i++)\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)l.level_exits[i].x, (double)l.level_exits[i].z, minx, minz, cell, 'E');\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.character_count; i++)\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)l.characters[i].x, (double)l.characters[i].z, minx, minz, cell, 'C');\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.spawner_count; i++)\n        map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)l.spawners[i].x, (double)l.spawners[i].z, minx, minz, cell, 'S');\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.door_count; i++) {\n        int bi = l.doors[i].box_index;\n        if (bi >= 0 && bi < l.count)\n            map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)l.boxes[bi].x, (double)l.boxes[bi].z, minx, minz, cell, 'D');\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < l.button_count; i++) {\n        int bi = l.buttons[i].box_index;\n        if (bi >= 0 && bi < l.count)\n            map_plot(grid, w, h, (double)l.boxes[bi].x, (double)l.boxes[bi].z, minx, minz, cell, 'B');\n    }\n\n    printf(\"%s -- top-down, -Z is up/north, Y ignored\\n\", path);\n    printf(\"  x %.1f..%.1f   z %.1f..%.1f   %dx%d cells, %.2f units/cell\\n\",\n           minx, maxx, minz, maxz, w, h, cell);\n    putchar('+');\n    for (int c = 0; c < w; c++) putchar('-');\n    printf(\"+\\n\");\n    for (int r = 0; r < h; r++) {\n        putchar('|');\n        fwrite(grid[r], 1, (size_t)w, stdout);\n        printf(\"|\\n\");\n    }\n    putchar('+');\n    for (int c = 0; c < w; c++) putchar('-');\n    printf(\"+\\n\");\n    printf(\"  '#' wall  'S' spawner  'C' character  'E' exit  'z' zone  'D' door  'B' button\\n\");\n    return 0;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    if (argc < 3) { usage(); return 2; }\n    const char *cmd = argv[1];\n\n    if (strcmp(cmd, \"info\") == 0) {\n        static CustomLevelData lvl;\n        if (!load_or_die(argv[2], &lvl)) return 1;\n        print_summary(argv[2], &lvl);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    if (strcmp(cmd, \"map\") == 0) return cmd_map(argv[2]);",

Pushed: `a3cd2a3 feat(leveltool): top-down ASCII map view`.

**Added**
- `leveltool map <file>` — projects a level's X/Z footprint into a 76×36 ASCII grid: `#` walls (centre + footprint corners), then `S` spawners, `C` characters, `E` exits, `z` zones, `D` doors, `B` buttons on top, with the x/z bounds and units-per-cell printed above. Y is ignored by design: it's a layout check, not a render.
- `mk/leveltool.mk`: `test-leveltool` now also renders an empty level and asserts `lab.json` actually draws walls (`grep -q '#'`), so a broken projection fails the target.
- README + CHANGELOG describe the new command.

**Verified**
- `make test-leveltool` → new → check → info → map all pass, exit 0
- `make map examples/story-doors/demo_level/level.json` → shows the corridor with both doors (`D`), the spawner (`S`) and the end walls
- `make map var/lab/lab.json` → 36×36 cells at 35.81 units/cell (coarse because the LAB has a 500-unit floor box), spawner and exit visible
- `make check-levels` still green on all 10 checked-in exports

**Limits**
- One cell per (span/75) units, so a large map like LAB loses detail; small maps like the demo read well.
- No lobby build/run here (no SDL2/GL, no display), so F6 and `--edit-map`'s new-level path still rest on the loader/tool tests rather than a live run.

The corridor walls are at x ±3.5 (thin, sx=1) → they appear as '#' at some columns; in rows shown we see only at row 9-10. Hmm, plot of wall center at x=-3.5: (x - minx)/cell = (−3.5 − (−37.5))/1 = 34; corners at -4 and -3 → cols 33.5..34.5 → rounds to 34. Should show '#' at column 34 every row. Yet rows 0-8 show none!
> 
> Wait — the walls' footprint z spans 0..40 (center 20, sz 40). Should cover the whole view. Why missing? Because `--cell 1` view z 2.5..37.5, and wall corners at z=0 and z=40, center z=20 → plotting center row = (20-2.5)/1 = 17.5 → 18; corners at z 0 (out of view, skipped) and 40 (out of view, skipped). So only center line at row 18, plus columns. That's why rows 0-8 lack walls: only the center z row plotted. In auto mode bounds fit tightly so corners were in view.
> 
> So the rendering uses center + 4 corners, which for a long corridor wall draws only endpoints/center — for the default auto view it looked fine because each wall's corners were at the ends. In the zoom window the walls are long and only their middle point shows.
> 
> Fix: for each wall, plot along its footprint edges at intervals of cell/2 (rasterize the AABB outline and maybe fill). Better: fill the footprint rectangle cells (walls are solid). For large walls filling an entire rectangle would flood the map (LAB's floor covers all). Hmm. Filling is actually more honest for large slabs but makes maps unreadable.

> Middle ground: draw the outline (rectangle border) sampled every half cell. For thin walls (sx or sz < cell) that yields a line; for big slabs it draws the border only — good for a plan view.

Pushed: `03004e1 feat(leveltool): zoom and height filter for the map view`.

**Added**
- `leveltool map <file> [--cell <units>] [--min-height <units>] [--center x,z]`:
  - `--cell` zooms to a fixed scale, centred on `--center`, else spawner 0, else the map's middle.
  - `--min-height` drops short geometry before computing bounds — that's what makes LAB readable, since its 500×535 floor slab (4 units tall) was dominating the auto-fit and squeezing everything into 36 cells at 35.8 units/cell.
  - Header reports the filter and zoom state so a truncated view is never mistaken for the whole map.
- Fixed a real rendering bug the zoom exposed: walls were drawn as centre + 4 corners, so a wall longer than the view showed only its middle. They now rasterise their footprint outline (sampled at half a cell, capped at 400 points per edge).
- `test-leveltool` asserts the zoomed demo actually draws wall cells, plus that `--min-height` and `--cell` are honoured; README and CHANGELOG updated.

**Verified**
- `make test-leveltool` → exit 0, all five steps pass
- Zoomed demo at `--cell 1 --center 0,20`: continuous corridor walls (`##`) down the view with the door (`####D####`) and spawner — previously just two rows of `#`
- LAB at `--min-height 10 --cell 8`: room-scale view with the walls and openings, instead of a flat 36×36 smear
- Bad usage still exits 2; `make check-levels` unchanged and green

**Limits**
- Y is ignored and walls draw as outlines, so a filled slab and a thin wall look identical; it's a plan check, not a render.
- Zoom window silently omits off-view geometry (the header says `(zoom window)`).
- Still no lobby build/run here (no SDL2/GL, no display), so F6 itself remains covered by the loader/tool tests rather than a live keypress.

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/world/edit_sync.h
  content: |
      #ifndef EDIT_SYNC_H
      #define EDIT_SYNC_H
      /* edit_sync.h -- SHANKPIT's side of a live NOCK edit session (kanban #518/#519/#520/#531, EDIT-3).
       * Talks to IDUNA's /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions (IDUNA/internal/http/handlers/shankpit_edit_sessions.go)
       * over the same curl-popen transport level_boxes.h uses. Blocking calls: run them on a worker
       * thread. Pure parsing (edit_sync_parse) is separate so it unit-tests without a network. */
      #include "level_boxes.h"
      
      #define EDIT_SYNC_MAX_EVENTS 64
      
      typedef struct {
          int seq;
          int from_nock;        /* source == "nock" */
          char kind[16];
          float x, y, z, yaw, pitch;
          int has_pos;
          int mode_crosshair;   /* spawn_mode: 1 = crosshair, 0 = spawner */
      } EditSyncEvent;
      
      /* Parse a GET poll response into events + the session's latest seq. Returns events parsed. */
      static inline int edit_sync_parse(const char *json, EditSyncEvent *out, int max, int *out_seq) {
          int n = 0;
          const char *end = json + strlen(json);
          const char *p = json;
          while (n < max && (p = strstr(p, "{\"seq\":")) != NULL) {
              const char *next = strstr(p + 1, "{\"seq\":");
              const char *seg_end = next ? next : end;
              EditSyncEvent *e = &out[n];
              memset(e, 0, sizeof *e);
              float f = 0;
              level_boxes_parse_number(p + 7, &f); e->seq = (int)f;
              char src[16] = "";
              const char *v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "source");
              if (v) level_boxes_parse_string(v, src, sizeof src);
              e->from_nock = strcmp(src, "nock") == 0;
              v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "kind");
              if (v) level_boxes_parse_string(v, e->kind, sizeof e->kind);
              v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "x");
              if (v && level_boxes_parse_number(v, &e->x)) {
                  e->has_pos = 1;
                  if ((v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "y"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v, &e->y);
                  if ((v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "z"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v, &e->z);
                  if ((v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "yaw"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v, &e->yaw);
                  if ((v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "pitch"))) level_boxes_parse_number(v, &e->pitch);
              }
              char mode[16] = "";
              if ((v = level_boxes_find_key(p, seg_end, "mode"))) level_boxes_parse_string(v, mode, sizeof mode);
              e->mode_crosshair = strcmp(mode, "crosshair") == 0;
              n++;
              p = seg_end;
          }
          /* the response's own top-level "seq" is the last "seq" key (Go marshals map keys sorted) */
          if (out_seq) {
              const char *last = NULL, *q = json;
              while ((q = strstr(q, "\"seq\":")) != NULL) { last = q; q++; }
              float f = 0;
              if (last && level_boxes_parse_number(last + 6, &f)) *out_seq = (int)f;
          }
          return n;
      }
      
      /* POST helper: body -> url. Optionally captures the response (malloc'd, caller frees). */
      static inline int edit_sync_http(const char *url, const char *body, char **resp) {
          char cmd[640];
          snprintf(cmd, sizeof cmd, "curl -s -f --max-time 30 -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" --data-binary @- \"%s\"", url);
          FILE *p = (body) ? level_boxes_popen_write(cmd) : NULL;
          (void)resp;
          if (!p) return 0;
          fwrite(body, 1, strlen(body), p);
          int st = LEVEL_BOXES_PCLOSE(p);
      #ifdef _WIN32
          return st == 0;
      #else
          return WIFEXITED(st) && WEXITSTATUS(st) == 0;
      #endif
      }
      
      /* Create a session; writes the 32-hex id into out_id (>=33 bytes). Needs the response, so it
       * reads via level_boxes_fetch_url-style popen with POST. */
      static inline int edit_sync_create(const char *base, int level_id, const char *level_name, char *out_id) {
          char cmd[768];
          snprintf(cmd, sizeof cmd,
                   "curl -s -f --max-time 10 -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d \"{\\\"level_id\\\":%d,\\\"level_name\\\":\\\"%.60s\\\"}\" \"%s\"",
                   level_id, level_name, base);
          FILE *p = level_boxes_popen_read(cmd);
          if (!p) return 0;
          char buf[512]; size_t n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, p); buf[n] = 0;
          LEVEL_BOXES_PCLOSE(p);
          const char *v = level_boxes_find_key(buf, buf + n, "id");
          char id[48] = "";
          if (!v || !level_boxes_parse_string(v, id, sizeof id) || strlen(id) != 32) return 0;
          memcpy(out_id, id, 33);
          return 1;
      }
      
      static inline int edit_sync_post_event(const char *base, const char *id, const char *kind, const char *data_json) {
          char url[320], body[640];
          snprintf(url, sizeof url, "%s/%s/events", base, id);
          snprintf(body, sizeof body, "{\"source\":\"shankpit\",\"kind\":\"%s\",\"data\":%s}", kind, data_json);
          return edit_sync_http(url, body, NULL);
      }
      
      /* Long-poll for events after `since`. Returns events parsed (>=0), -1 on transport error / 404. */
      static inline int edit_sync_poll(const char *base, const char *id, int since, int wait_s, EditSyncEvent *out, int max, int *out_seq) {
          char url[320]; char *buf = NULL;
          snprintf(url, sizeof url, "%s/%s?since=%d&wait=%d", base, id, since, wait_s);
          long n = level_boxes_fetch_url(url, &buf);
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          int c = edit_sync_parse(buf, out, max, out_seq);
          free(buf);
          return c;
      }
      
      /* GET <base>/<id>/level -> the session's working level (the NOCK editor's UNSAVED draft when it has pushed
       * one, else the saved level) in the same export JSON level_boxes_parse_json reads. malloc'd, caller frees.
       * Returns the byte count (>0) or -1. */
      static inline long edit_sync_fetch_level(const char *base, const char *id, char **buf) {
          char url[320];
          snprintf(url, sizeof url, "%s/%s/level", base, id);
          *buf = NULL;
          long n = level_boxes_fetch_url(url, buf);
          return n > 0 && *buf ? n : -1;
      }
      #endif

      package handlers
      
      // shankpit_edit_sessions.go -- live map-editing sessions shared by the NOCK web editor and the native
      // SHANKPIT client (kanban #518/#519/#520, plan cards EDIT-1..4; founder real-time: "shankpit map editor needs to
      // sync up live to NOCK tools so we can join a live editing session from either the shankpit side or the nock
      // side", "you move the spawner around in nock and it moves your character in shankpit -- move your character in
      // shankpit it moves the spawner", "a toggle between Spawning on spawner OR spawning where the characters
      // crosshairs is").
      //
      // Shape: a session is a small append-only event log plus a materialised "latest state". Either side creates a
      // session (POST), the other joins by its id, both POST events and long-poll GET ?since=<seq>. The session id is
      // a 128-bit random capability token, which is the only credential -- the same trade shankpit_levels_public.go's
      // snapshot endpoint makes (SHANKPIT has no player login to attach yet), bounded by a per-IP create rate limit,
      // body and event caps, a session count cap and a TTL. Nothing here writes a level: edits travel as events and the
      // NOCK editor (admin-gated) is what saves them.
      //
      // In memory on purpose: a session is a live editing room, not a record. A server restart ends every room and the
      // clients simply create a new one.
      
      import (
        "crypto/rand"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "net/http"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"
      
        "iduna/internal/http/middleware"
        "iduna/internal/shankpit"
      )
      
      const (
        editSessionTTL        = 6 * time.Hour
        editSessionMaxCount   = 200
        editSessionMaxEvents  = 2000
        editSessionMaxBody    = 8 * 1024
        editSessionMaxWaitSec = 25
        editSessionMaxDraft   = 4 << 20 // an unsaved level draft (walls/objects/...), far larger than an event
      )
      
      // editEventKinds are the events a session carries. Anything else is rejected so a room cannot be used as a
      // general-purpose message bus.
      //
      //  spawner     {x,y,z,yaw}            the spawner marker moved (either side)
      //  avatar      {x,y,z,yaw,pitch}      where the SHANKPIT character is (SHANKPIT -> NOCK; also drives the spawner)
      //  spawn_mode  {mode:"spawner"|"crosshair"}  where a "spawn/teleport" puts the character
      //  teleport    {x,y,z,yaw}            put the character here now (NOCK -> SHANKPIT; crosshair hits come from NOCK)
      //  box_add     {id,x,y,z,sx,sy,sz,r,g,b}  a wall box was added
      //  box_move    {id,x,y,z}             a wall box moved
      //  box_size    {id,sx,sy,sz}          a wall box was resized
      //  box_del     {id}                   a wall box was deleted
      //  save        {}                     SHANKPIT asked for the working level to be saved (NOCK performs the save)
      //  hello       {client:"nock"|"shankpit"}  presence
      //  level       {rev}                  the NOCK editor's working (possibly unsaved) level changed; fetch GET {id}/level
      //
      // The working level itself travels out-of-band: PUT {id}/level (NOCK, full draft) and GET {id}/level (SHANKPIT,
      // the native export shape of that draft). Falls back to the saved level when no draft has been pushed.
      var editEventKinds = map[string]bool{
        "spawner": true, "avatar": true, "spawn_mode": true, "teleport": true,
        "box_add": true, "box_move": true, "box_size": true, "box_del": true, "hello": true,
        "level": true, "save": true,
      }
      
      type editEvent struct {
        Seq    int             `json:"seq"`
        Source string          `json:"source"`
        Kind   string          `json:"kind"`
        Data   json.RawMessage `json:"data,omitempty"`
        At     time.Time       `json:"at"`
      }
      
      type editSession struct {
        id        string
        levelID   int64
        levelName string
        created   time.Time
        touched   time.Time
        events    []editEvent
        nextSeq   int
        // latest materialised state, so a late joiner does not have to replay the log
        spawner   json.RawMessage
        avatar    json.RawMessage
        spawnMode string
        // draft is the NOCK editor's latest working level (unsaved edits included), raw updateShankpitLevelReq-shaped JSON.
        draft    json.RawMessage
        draftRev int
        // wake is closed and replaced whenever an event lands, so long-pollers wake without busy-waiting.
        wake chan struct{}
      }
      
      // ShankpitEditSessionsHandler serves /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions...
      type ShankpitEditSessionsHandler struct {
        // CreateLimiter rate-limits session creation per client IP; nil disables the limit (tests).
        CreateLimiter *middleware.IPRateLimiter
        // Store builds the native export of a draft / the saved level for GET {id}/level; nil disables that route.
        Store *shankpit.LevelStore
        Now           func() time.Time
      
        mu       sync.Mutex
        sessions map[string]*editSession
      }
      
      func (h *ShankpitEditSessionsHandler) now() time.Time {
        if h.Now != nil {
          return h.Now()
        }
        return time.Now()
      }
      
      func (h *ShankpitEditSessionsHandler) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        const prefix = "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions"
        if !strings.HasPrefix(r.URL.Path, prefix) {
          http.NotFound(w, r)
          return
        }
        rest := strings.Trim(strings.TrimPrefix(r.URL.Path, prefix), "/")
        parts := []string{}
        if rest != "" {
          parts = strings.Split(rest, "/")
        }
        switch {
        case len(parts) == 0 && r.Method == http.MethodPost:
          h.create(w, r)
        case len(parts) == 1 && r.Method == http.MethodGet:
          h.poll(w, r, parts[0])
        case len(parts) == 2 && parts[1] == "events" && r.Method == http.MethodPost:
          h.post(w, r, parts[0])
        case len(parts) == 2 && parts[1] == "level" && r.Method == http.MethodPut:
          h.putLevel(w, r, parts[0])
        case len(parts) == 2 && parts[1] == "level" && r.Method == http.MethodGet:
          h.getLevel(w, r, parts[0])
        default:
          mmoWriteError(w, http.StatusMethodNotAllowed, "POST /shankpit-edit-sessions, GET /shankpit-edit-sessions/{id}?since=N, POST /shankpit-edit-sessions/{id}/events")
        }
      }
      
      func (h *ShankpitEditSessionsHandler) gcLocked(now time.Time) {
        for id, s := range h.sessions {
          if now.Sub(s.touched) > editSessionTTL {
            delete(h.sessions, id)
          }
        }
      }
      
      func (h *ShankpitEditSessionsHandler) create(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        if h.CreateLimiter != nil && !h.CreateLimiter.Allow(clientIPFor(r)) {
          w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "60")
          mmoWriteError(w, http.StatusTooManyRequests, "too many edit sessions; try again shortly")
          return
        }
        r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, editSessionMaxBody)
        var req struct {
          LevelID   int64  `json:"level_id"`
          LevelName string `json:"level_name"`
        }
        _ = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req) // an empty body is fine: a session for an unsaved/local map
        if len(req.LevelName) > 120 {
          req.LevelName = req.LevelName[:120]
        }
        var raw [16]byte
        if _, err := rand.Read(raw[:]); err != nil {
          mmoWriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "no entropy")
          return
        }
        now := h.now()
        h.mu.Lock()
        defer h.mu.Unlock()
        if h.sessions == nil {
          h.sessions = map[string]*editSession{}
        }
        h.gcLocked(now)
        if len(h.sessions) >= editSessionMaxCount {
          mmoWriteError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "too many live edit sessions")
          return
        }
        s := &editSession{id: hex.EncodeToString(raw[:]), levelID: req.LevelID, levelName: req.LevelName,
          created: now, touched: now, nextSeq: 1, spawnMode: "spawner", wake: make(chan struct{})}
        h.sessions[s.id] = s
        writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, map[string]any{"id": s.id, "level_id": s.levelID, "level_name": s.levelName, "seq": 0})
      }
      
      func (h *ShankpitEditSessionsHandler) lookup(id string) *editSession {
        h.mu.Lock()
        defer h.mu.Unlock()
        s := h.sessions[id]
        if s == nil {
          return nil
        }
        if h.now().Sub(s.touched) > editSessionTTL {
          delete(h.sessions, id)
          return nil
        }
        return s
      }
      
      // snapshotLocked returns the events after `since` plus the materialised state. Caller holds h.mu.
      func (s *editSession) snapshotLocked(since int) map[string]any {
        var out []editEvent
        for _, e := range s.events {
          if e.Seq > since {
            out = append(out, e)
          }
        }
        if out == nil {
          out = []editEvent{}
        }
        return map[string]any{
          "id": s.id, "level_id": s.levelID, "level_name": s.levelName,
          "seq": s.nextSeq - 1, "events": out, "level_rev": s.draftRev,
          "state": map[string]any{"spawner": s.spawner, "avatar": s.avatar, "spawn_mode": s.spawnMode},
        }
      }
      
      // poll returns events after ?since=N. With ?wait=<seconds> and nothing new it holds the request open
      // (long-poll, capped) until an event arrives -- SHANKPIT's curl-based client and the browser both just loop on it.
      func (h *ShankpitEditSessionsHandler) poll(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, id string) {
        if h.lookup(id) == nil {
          mmoWriteError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "no such edit session (it may have expired or the server restarted)")
          return
        }
        since, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.URL.Query().Get("since"))
        wait, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.URL.Query().Get("wait"))
        if wait > editSessionMaxWaitSec {
          wait = editSessionMaxWaitSec
        }
        deadline := time.NewTimer(time.Duration(wait) * time.Second)
        defer deadline.Stop()
        for {
          h.mu.Lock()
          s := h.sessions[id]
          if s == nil {
            h.mu.Unlock()
            mmoWriteError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "edit session ended")
            return
          }
          s.touched = h.now()
          if s.nextSeq-1 > since || wait == 0 {
            snap := s.snapshotLocked(since)
            h.mu.Unlock()
            writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, snap)
            return
          }
          wake := s.wake
          h.mu.Unlock()
          select {
          case <-wake:
          case <-deadline.C:
            h.mu.Lock()
            snap := s.snapshotLocked(since)
            h.mu.Unlock()
            writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, snap)
            return
          case <-r.Context().Done():
            return
          }
        }
      }

> Session class with lock/condition:

> ```python
> class Session:
>     def __init__(self, sid, level_id, level_name):
>         self.id = sid; self.level_id = level_id; self.level_name = level_name
>         self.events = []; self.next_seq = 1; self.draft = None; self.draft_rev = 0
>         self.created = self.touched = time.time()
>         self.cond = threading.Condition()
> 
>     def snapshot(self, since):
>         evs = [e for e in self.events if e["seq"] > since]
>         return {"id": self.id, "level_id": self.level_id, "level_name": self.level_name,
>                 "seq": self.next_seq - 1, "events": evs, "level_rev": self.draft_rev,
>                 "state": {}}
> 
>     def post(self, source, kind, data):
>         with self.cond:
>             e = {"seq": self.next_seq, "source": source, "kind": kind, "data": data}
>             self.next_seq += 1
>             self.events.append(e)
>             if len(self.events) > 2000: del self.events[:-2000]
>             self.touched = time.time()
>             self.cond.notify_all()
>             return e
> 
>     def poll(self, since, wait):
>         deadline = time.time() + wait
>         with self.cond:
>             while self.next_seq - 1 <= since and wait > 0 and time.time() < deadline:
>                 self.cond.wait(deadline - time.time())
>             self.touched = time.time()
>             return self.snapshot(since)
> ```

canvas.height = h; }\n  ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);\n  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);\n  if (!state.level) {\n    ctx.fillStyle = \"#7f8794\";\n    ctx.font = `${13 * dpr}px monospace`;\n    ctx.fillText(\"pick a level, or press New level\", 20 * dpr, 30 * dpr);\n    return;\n  }\n  const v = view(), W = state.level;\n  for (const b of W.walls || []) {\n    const [x0, z0] = v.toPx(b.x - Math.abs(b.sx) / 2, b.z - Math.abs(b.sz) / 2);\n    const [x1, z1] = v.toPx(b.x + Math.abs(b.sx) / 2, b.z + Math.abs(b.sz) / 2);\n    const shade = Math.max(40, Math.min(150, 60 + (b.sy || 4) * 2));\n    ctx.fillStyle = `rgb(${shade},${shade + 6},${shade + 14})`;\n    ctx.fillRect(x0, z0, Math.max(1, x1 - x0), Math.max(1, z1 - z0));\n  }\n  ctx.strokeStyle = \"#9aa3b2\"; ctx.lineWidth = 1 * dpr;\n  for (const sp of W.spawners || []) {\n    const [x, z] = v.toPx(sp.x, sp.z);\n    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, 5 * dpr, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.strokeStyle = \"#e05c5c\"; ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  for (const e of W.level_exits || []) {\n    const [x, z] = v.toPx(e.x, e.z);\n    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, Math.max(2, (e.radius || 2) * v.s), 0, Math.PI * 2);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = \"#5ce08a\"; ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  for (const zn of W.zones || []) {\n    const [x, z] = v.toPx(zn.x, zn.z);\n    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, Math.max(2, (zn.radius || 2) * v.s), 0, Math.PI * 2);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = \"#b07cff\"; ctx.setLineDash([4 * dpr, 4 * dpr]); ctx.stroke();\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n  }\n  for (const c of W.characters || []) {\n    const [x, z] = v.toPx(c.x, c.z);\n    ctx.fillStyle = \"#5ca8e0\"; ctx.fillRect(x - 3 * dpr, z - 3 * dpr, 6 * dpr, 6 * dpr);\n  }\n  if (state.remote) {\n    const [x, z] = v.toPx(state.remote.x, state.remote.z);\n    ctx.fillStyle = \"#8de05c\";\n    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, 6 * dpr, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();\n    const yaw = (state.remote.yaw || 0) * Math.PI / 180;\n    ctx.strokeStyle = \"#8de05c\"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, z);\n    ctx.lineTo(x - Math.sin(yaw) * 16 * dpr, z - Math.cos(yaw) * 16 * dpr); ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  const g = v.g;\n  ctx.fillStyle = \"#7f8794\";\n  ctx.font = `${11 * dpr}px monospace`;\n  ctx.fillText(`${state.name || \"untitled\"}  ·  ${(W.walls || []).length} walls  ·  x ${g.minx.toFixed(1)}..${g.maxx.toFixed(1)}  z ${g.minz.toFixed(1)}..${g.maxz.toFixed(1)}  ·  -Z up`, 12 * dpr, canvas.height - 10 * dpr);\n}\n\n/* ---------- editing ---------- */\n\nfunction snapshot() {\n  state.undo.push(JSON.stringify(state.level));\n  if (state.undo.length > 60) state.undo.shift();\n}\n\nfunction undo() {\n  if (!state.undo.length) return;\n  state.level = JSON.parse(state.undo.pop());\n  draw(); pushDraftSoon();\n}\n\nfunction wallIndexAt(x, z) {\n  const walls = state.level.walls;\n  for (let i = walls.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const b = walls[i];\n    if (Math.abs(x - b.x) <= Math.abs(b.sx) / 2 && Math.abs(z - b.z) <= Math.abs(b.sz) / 2) return i;\n  }\n  return -1;\n}\n\ncanvas.addEventListener(\"mousedown\", ev => {\n  if (!state.level) return;\n  const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();\n  const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;\n  const v = view();\n  const [x, z] = v.toWorld((ev.clientX - rect.left) * dpr, (ev.clientY - rect.top) * dpr);\n  const W = state.level;\n\n  if (state.tool === \"add\") {\n    snapshot();\n    const mat = (W.materials[0] && W.materials[0].name) || \"brick\";\n    const box = { x: +x.toFixed(2), y: 2, z: +z.toFixed(2), sx: 4, sy: 4, sz: 4,\n                  r: 0.6, g: 0.6, b: 0.65, friction: 0.8, material: mat };\n    W.walls.push(box);\n    log(`box at ${box.x}, ${box.z}`);\n    post(\"box_add\", { id: W.walls.length, x: box.x, y: box.y, z: box.z,\n                      sx: box.sx, sy: box.sy, sz: box.sz, r: box.r, g: box.g, b: box.b });\n  } else if (state.tool === \"delete\") {\n    const i = wallIndexAt(x, z);\n    if (i < 0) { log(\"nothing under the cursor\"); return; }\n    snapshot();\n    W.walls.splice(i, 1);\n    log(`deleted wall ${i}`);\n    post(\"box_del\", { id: -1, index: i });\n  } else {\n    snapshot();\n    if (!W.spawners.length) W.spawners.push({ id: 1, x: 0, y: 1, z: 0, yaw: 0, team: -1 });\n    W.spawners[0].x = +x.toFixed(2); W.spawners[0].z = +z.toFixed(2);\n    log(`spawner at ${W.spawners[0].x}, ${W.spawners[0].z}`);\n    post(\"spawner\", { x: W.spawners[0].x, y: W.spawners[0].y, z: W.spawners[0].z,\n                       yaw: W.spawners[0].yaw || 0 });\n  }\n  draw();\n  pushDraftSoon();\n});\n\ndocument.addEventListener(\"keydown\", ev => {\n  if ((ev.ctrlKey || ev.metaKey) && ev.key.toLowerCase() === \"z\") { ev.preventDefault(); undo(); }\n  if (ev.target.tagName === \"INPUT\") return;\n  const k = ev.key.toLowerCase();\n  const tool = k === \"b\" ? \"add\" : k === \"x\" ? \"delete\" : k === \"m\" ? \"spawner\" : null;\n  if (tool) selectTool(tool);\n});\n\nfunction selectTool(tool) {\n  state.tool = tool;\n  for (const b of document.querySelectorAll(\"[data-tool]\"))\n    b.classList.toggle(\"on\", b.dataset.tool === tool);\n}\n\nfor (const b of document.querySelectorAll(\"[data-tool]\"))\n  b.onclick = () => selectTool(b.dataset.tool);\n\n/* ---------- saving (file + git commit) ---------- */\n\nasync function save() {\n  if (!state.level) return;\n  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(state.name)) { alert(\"bad level name\"); return; }\n  try {\n    state.level.name = state.name;\n    const r = await api(\"PUT\", \"/api/levels/\" + encodeURIComponent(state.name), state.level);\n    state.dirty = false;\n    const g = r.git || {};\n    el(\"saveInfo\").textContent = g.committed\n      ? `committed ${g.commit}: ${g.message}`\n      : `saved ${r.file} (${g.detail || \"not committed\"})`;\n    log(el(\"saveInfo\").textContent);\n    loadLevelList();\n  } catch (e) {\n    el(\"saveInfo\").textContent = \"save failed: \" + e.message;\n    log(\"save failed: \" + e.message);\n  }\n}\nel(\"saveBtn\").onclick = save;\nel(\"newBtn\").onclick = newLevel;\n\n/* ---------- live session ---------- */\n\nasync function startSession() {\n  try {\n    const body = { level_id: 0, level_name: state.name || \"\" };\n    const r = await api(\"POST\", SESSION_BASE, body);\n    joinSession(r.id);\n    log(`started session ${r.id} — run the game with --edit-session ${r.id}`);\n  } catch (e) { log(\"start failed: \" + e.message); }\n}\n\nfunction joinSession(id) {\n  if (!/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/.test(id || \"\")) { log(\"session id must be 32 hex chars\"); return; }\n  state.session = id;\n  state.since = 0;\n  state.pollGen++;\n  el(\"sessionId\").value = id;\n  el(\"sessionInfo\").textContent = \"in session \" + id;\n  log(\"joined session \" + id);\n  pushDraft();          // hand the game our working level straight away\n  pollLoop(state.pollGen);\n}\n\nel(\"startBtn\").onclick = startSession;\nel(\"joinBtn\").onclick = () => joinSession(el(\"sessionId\").value.trim());\n\nasync function post(kind, data) {\n  if (!state.session) return;\n  try {\n    await api(\"POST\", `${SESSION_BASE}/${state.session}/events`, { source: \"nock\", kind, data });\n  } catch (e) { log(`event ${kind} failed: ${e.message}`); }\n}\n\nlet pushTimer = null;\nfunction pushDraftSoon() {\n  if (!state.session) return;\n  clearTimeout(pushTimer);\n  pushTimer = setTimeout(pushDraft, 180);\n}\n\nasync function pushDraft() {\n  if (!state.session || !state.level) return;\n  try {\n    const r = await api(\"PUT\", `${SESSION_BASE}/${state.session}/level`, state.level);\n    // \"level\" tells the native client to fetch the working level (edit_sync.h es_worker)\n    await post(\"level\", { rev: r.rev });\n  } catch (e) { log(\"draft push failed: \" + e.message); }\n}\n\nasync function pollLoop(gen) {\n  if (state.polling) return;\n  state.polling = true;\n  try {\n    while (state.session && gen === state.pollGen) {\n      const q = `${SESSION_BASE}/${state.session}?since=${state.since}&wait=10`;\n      let snap;\n      try {\n        snap = await api(\"GET\", q);\n      } catch (e) {\n        log(\"poll failed: \" + e.message + \" (session ended?)\");\n        state.session = null;\n        el(\"sessionInfo\").textContent = \"session lost\";\n        break;\n      }\n      if (gen !== state.pollGen) break;\n      applyEvents(snap.events || []);\n      state.since = snap.seq;\n    }\n  } finally {\n    state.polling = false;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction applyEvents(events) {\n  for (const ev of events) {\n    const d = ev.data || {};\n    if (ev.kind === \"spawner\" && d.x !== undefined) {\n      const W = state.level;\n      if (W) {\n        if (!W.spawners.length) W.spawners.push({ id: 1, x: 0, y: 1, z: 0, yaw: 0, team: -1 });\n        W.spawners[0].x = d.x; W.spawners[0].y = d.y; W.spawners[0].z = d.z;\n        if (d.yaw !== undefined) W.spawners[0].yaw = d.yaw;\n      }\n    } else if (ev.kind === \"avatar\" && d.x !== undefined) {\n      state.remote = { x: d.x, z: d.z, yaw: d.yaw || 0 };\n    } else if (ev.kind === \"box_add\" && d.sx !== undefined) {\n      // placed in-game (B): mirror it here so both views agree\n      const W = state.level;\n      if (W) {\n        W.walls.push({ x: d.x, y: d.y, z: d.z, sx: d.sx, sy: d.sy || 4, sz: d.sz || 4,\n                       r: d.r ?? 0.6, g: d.g ?? 0.6, b: d.b ?? 0.65, friction: 0.8,\n                       material: (W.materials[0] && W.materials[0].name) || \"brick\" });\n        log(\"game placed a box\");\n      }\n    } else if (ev.kind === \"box_del\" && d.index !== undefined) {\n      const W = state.level;\n      if (W && d.index >= 0 && d.index < W.walls.length) {\n        W.walls.splice(d.index, 1);\n        log(\"game deleted a box\");\n      }\n    } else if (ev.kind === \"save\") {\n      log(\"game asked to save — press Save + commit to land it in git\");\n    } else if (ev.kind === \"teleport\" && d.x !== undefined) {\n      state.remote = { x: d.x, z: d.z, yaw: d.yaw || 0 };\n    }\n  }\n  draw();\n}\n\n/* ---------- boot ---------- */\n\nel(\"note\").textContent =\n  \"SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL=\" + location.origin + SESSION_BASE + \"\\n\" +\n  \"./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map levels/\" + \"<name>.json --edit-live\\n\" +\n  \"(or --edit-session <id>)\";\n\nloadLevelList().then(() => {\n  const first = document.querySelector(\"#levels li[data-name]\");\n  if (first) openLevel(first.dataset.name);\n  draw();\n});\nwindow.addEventListener(\"resize\", draw);\n</script>\n</body>\n</html>\n"
}

{
