  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"test_local_nock.py -- integration test for tools/local_nock.py.\n\nRuns the real server on an ephemeral port over a throwaway git repo and exercises the wire contract\nthe native client and the browser editor both use. No browser needed, no network beyond loopback.\n\n  make test-local-nock\n\"\"\"\nimport json\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport tempfile\nimport threading\nimport urllib.error\nimport urllib.request\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))\nimport local_nock  # noqa: E402\n\nLEVEL = {\n    \"name\": \"testmap\", \"width\": 40, \"height\": 20, \"depth\": 40,\n    \"ground_plane_enabled\": True, \"ground_plane_squares\": 4,\n    \"materials\": [{\"name\": \"brick\", \"shader_name\": \"standard\", \"specular\": 0.04,\n                   \"shininess\": 6, \"friction\": 0.3}],\n    \"walls\": [{\"x\": 0, \"y\": 2, \"z\": 0, \"sx\": 8, \"sy\": 4, \"sz\": 2,\n               \"r\": 0.6, \"g\": 0.6, \"b\": 0.65, \"friction\": 0.8, \"material\": \"brick\"}],\n    \"spawners\": [{\"id\": 1, \"x\": 0, \"y\": 1, \"z\": 4, \"yaw\": 180, \"team\": -1}],\n}\n\n\ndef call(base, method, path, body=None):\n    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()\n    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=data, method=method,\n                                 headers={\"Content-Type\": \"application/json\"})\n    try:\n        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as r:\n            return r.status, r.read()\n    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:\n        return e.code, e.read()\n\n\ndef json_call(base, method, path, body=None):\n    status, raw = call(base, method, path, body)\n    return status, (json.loads(raw) if raw else None)\n\n\ndef main():\n    repo = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=\"local_nock_repo_\")\n    subprocess.run([\"git\", \"init\", \"-q\"], cwd=repo, check=True)\n    subprocess.run([\"git\", \"-C\", repo, \"config\", \"user.name\", \"local nock test\"], check=True)\n    subprocess.run([\"git\", \"-C\", repo, \"config\", \"user.email\", \"local-nock@localhost\"], check=True)\n\n    server = local_nock.build_server(port=0, levels_dir=os.path.join(repo, \"levels\"),\n                                     repo=repo, commit=True, verbose=False)\n    port = server.server_address[1]\n    base = f\"http://127.0.0.1:{port}\"\n    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()\n    ok = 0\n\n    try:\n        # 1. the editor page is served\n        status, raw = call(base, \"GET\", \"/\")\n        assert status == 200 and b\"local NOCK\" in raw and b\"canvas\" in raw, \"editor page\"\n        print(\"PASS editor page served\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 2. an empty level list, then save a level: file on disk + git commit\n        status, doc = json_call(base, \"GET\", \"/api/levels\")\n        assert status == 200 and doc[\"levels\"] == [], \"empty listing\"\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"PUT\", \"/api/levels/testmap\", LEVEL)\n        assert status == 200 and res[\"git\"][\"committed\"] is True, f\"save+commit: {res}\"\n        assert res[\"git\"][\"commit\"], \"commit hash\"\n        path = os.path.join(repo, \"levels\", \"testmap.json\")\n        assert os.path.isfile(path), \"level file written\"\n        log = subprocess.run([\"git\", \"-C\", repo, \"log\", \"--oneline\"], capture_output=True,\n                             text=True).stdout\n        assert \"level(testmap)\" in log, f\"git log: {log!r}\"\n        print(\"PASS save writes levels/testmap.json and commits it\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 3. list + read back through the API (what the editor/browser does)\n        status, doc = json_call(base, \"GET\", \"/api/levels\")\n        assert doc[\"levels\"][0][\"name\"] == \"testmap\" and doc[\"levels\"][0][\"walls\"] == 1\n        status, raw = call(base, \"GET\", \"/api/levels/testmap\")\n        assert status == 200 and json.loads(raw)[\"walls\"][0][\"sx\"] == 8\n        print(\"PASS level listing and read-back\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 4. saving the same content again is not a new commit\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"PUT\", \"/api/levels/testmap\", LEVEL)\n        assert status == 200 and res[\"git\"][\"committed\"] is False\n        print(\"PASS identical save does not create an empty commit\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 5. invalid levels are refused, nothing written\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"PUT\", \"/api/levels/broken\", {\"nope\": 1})\n        assert status == 400 and \"walls\" in res[\"error\"]\n        assert not os.path.exists(os.path.join(repo, \"levels\", \"broken.json\"))\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"PUT\", \"/api/levels/bad name\", LEVEL)\n        assert status == 400\n        print(\"PASS invalid levels rejected (missing walls, bad name)\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 6. session create -- 32 hex chars, the shape edit_sync_create checks for\n        status, sess = json_call(base, \"POST\", \"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions\",\n                                 {\"level_id\": 0, \"level_name\": \"testmap\"})\n        assert status == 201 and len(sess[\"id\"]) == 32, sess\n        sid = sess[\"id\"]\n        print(\"PASS session create returns a 32-hex id\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 7. the native client's own event shapes (source shankpit) come back on poll\n        for kind, data in ((\"hello\", {\"client\": \"shankpit\"}),\n                           (\"avatar\", {\"x\": 1.5, \"y\": 1, \"z\": 2.5, \"yaw\": 90, \"pitch\": 0}),\n                           (\"spawner\", {\"x\": 3, \"y\": 1, \"z\": 4, \"yaw\": 45}),\n                           (\"box_add\", {\"id\": 100001, \"x\": 5, \"y\": 2, \"z\": 5,\n                                        \"sx\": 4, \"sy\": 4, \"sz\": 4}),\n                           (\"save\", {})):\n            status, _ = json_call(base, \"POST\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/events\",\n                                  {\"source\": \"shankpit\", \"kind\": kind, \"data\": data})\n            assert status == 200, kind\n        status, snap = json_call(base, \"GET\",\n                                 f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}?since=0&wait=0\")\n        kinds = [e[\"kind\"] for e in snap[\"events\"]]\n        assert kinds == [\"hello\", \"avatar\", \"spawner\", \"box_add\", \"save\"], kinds\n        assert snap[\"seq\"] == 5\n        status, snap = json_call(base, \"GET\",\n                                 f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}?since=4&wait=0\")\n        assert [e[\"kind\"] for e in snap[\"events\"]] == [\"save\"], \"since filter\"\n        print(\"PASS events post/poll with since filtering\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 8. unknown event kind and source are rejected (a room is not a message bus)\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"POST\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/events\",\n                                {\"source\": \"nock\", \"kind\": \"rm -rf\", \"data\": {}})\n        assert status == 400\n        print(\"PASS unknown event kinds rejected\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 9. the browser pushes a working draft; the client fetches it (live reload path)\n        draft = dict(LEVEL)\n        draft[\"walls\"] = LEVEL[\"walls\"] + [{\"x\": 4, \"y\": 2, \"z\": 4, \"sx\": 2, \"sy\": 2, \"sz\": 2}]\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"PUT\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/level\", draft)\n        assert status == 200 and res[\"rev\"] == 1, res\n        status, raw = call(base, \"GET\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/level\")\n        served = json.loads(raw)\n        assert status == 200 and len(served[\"walls\"]) == 2, served\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"PUT\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/level\", draft)\n        assert res[\"rev\"] == 2\n        print(\"PASS working draft push/fetch (browser -> game live reload)\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 10. a session with no draft falls back to its saved level, then 404s when absent\n        status, sess2 = json_call(base, \"POST\", \"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions\",\n                                  {\"level_id\": 0, \"level_name\": \"testmap\"})\n        status, raw = call(base, \"GET\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sess2['id']}/level\")\n        assert status == 200 and len(json.loads(raw)[\"walls\"]) == 1, \"saved-level fallback\"\n        status, sess3 = json_call(base, \"POST\", \"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions\",\n                                  {\"level_id\": 0, \"level_name\": \"no-such-map\"})\n        status, res = json_call(base, \"GET\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sess3['id']}/level\")\n        assert status == 404\n        print(\"PASS level fetch falls back to the saved file, 404 when there is none\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 11. long-poll returns promptly once an event lands\n        status, sess4 = json_call(base, \"POST\", \"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions\",\n                                  {\"level_id\": 0, \"level_name\": \"testmap\"})\n        sid4 = sess4[\"id\"]\n        result = {}\n\n        def poll():\n            result[\"r\"] = json_call(base, \"GET\",\n                                    f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid4}?since=0&wait=10\")\n\n        t = threading.Thread(target=poll, daemon=True)\n        t.start()\n        json_call(base, \"POST\", f\"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid4}/events\",\n                  {\"source\": \"nock\", \"kind\": \"hello\", \"data\": {\"client\": \"nock\"}})\n        t.join(timeout=5)\n        status, snap = result[\"r\"]\n        assert status == 200 and [e[\"kind\"] for e in snap[\"events\"]] == [\"hello\"]\n        print(\"PASS long-poll wakes on a new event\")\n        ok += 1\n\n        # 12. unknown session ids are 404 (the client treats that as 'session lost')\n        status, _ = json_call(base, \"GET\", \"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/\" + \"0\" * 32 + \"?since=0\")\n        assert status == 404\n        print(\"PASS unknown session is 404\")\n        ok += 1\n\n    finally:\n        server.shutdown()\n        server.server_close()\n\n    print(f\"\\nlocal_nock ok ({ok} checks)\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"
}

# PARENA

**"PARENA is a language to make your software more programmable via fluid and composible plugin
APIS."** — founder's own mission statement. The adoption mechanism: bolt a plugin/FFI boundary
onto existing software first, let PARENA code live there, and PARENA eats more of the host from
the outside in, iteratively — not a rewrite. See `NORTHSTAR.md`'s "What this is" for the full
statement.

A new systems language: S-expression syntax, compile-time region-based memory safety (no GC, no
manual free), linear ownership for native resources, multiple compilation targets (C first, then
JVM/TypeScript/WebAssembly). Ships its own editor/plugin API as a first-class part of the design.
Full design: `NORTHSTAR.md`. Full standard-library design: `STDLIB.md`.

**Status (2026-08-20): all 5 VS0 DoD domains are complete** — lexer/parser, region analyzer, C
emitter, memory verification (ASan/UBSan/real Valgrind), and the CLI runner (`parena parse` /
`parena analyze` / `parena build file.prn -o out.c`) all real, all CI-verified. This is a closed
milestone for VS0 *itself* — it does not mean the mod-surface stdlib is finished; that's real,
separate, ongoing work tracked below and in `STDLIB.md`/`EMILY/BACKLOG.md`. The emitter has grown
well past the original spec-grounded minimum since VS0 closed: `defenum`/`defstruct` (real
user-defined tagged unions and structs), generic `Arena @ Region` params/returns, `Bool`/`F64`,
`(Vec T)` (a real, working, arena-allocated dynamic array — `vec/new`/`vec/push!`/`vec/get`/
`vec/len`), `&Type`/`&mut Type` reference parameters/fields/returns plus `deref`, `do`, and `set!`
— each landed by actually compiling real `.prn` files (not synthetic snippets) and their emitted C
with `gcc -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror`, not just trusting `parena build`'s own exit code.

The `stdlib/` directory holds real `.prn` source for the packages below, in the dependency order
given here. Most files parse and region-analyze cleanly; how far each one gets through the C
emitter varies by package — some compile completely end to end (`gfd.prn`, `csv.prn`'s pure-PARENA
portions), others are blocked on real, specific, itemized gaps (see `STDLIB.md`'s own gap-analysis
sections) rather than a blanket "not implemented yet." "Built out in Parena" means *real Parena
source exists*, checked per-file against the current compiler — not a claim that the whole
standard library links and runs.

**Real source exists today** (`stdlib/`) for: `vec`, `map`, `string`, `unicode` (strict UTF-8 codec, Unicode 15.1 properties/simple case mapping/width; `\u{...}` string escapes), `log`, `buffer`, `io`,
`thread`, `sdl2`, `net/tcp`, `net/udp`, `net/http`, `array`, `linalg` (matmul/transpose/dot;
inverse/solve deferred), `stats`, `dataframe` (column/select; read-csv/filter/group-by deferred),
`nn`, `tokenizer` (load; encode/decode deferred), `sort`, `regex/syntax`, `regex/nfa` (signatures
only), `regex/pcre` (a real, working backtracking matcher), `regex/posix`, `regex/glob`, `expr`,
`grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `gfd` (compiles completely, zero warnings), `csv` (the LONGMA port —
`split`/`generate`, pure PARENA except the real file-I/O gap every stdlib package still shares),
`editor/plugin`, `editor/buffer`, `editor/events`, `editor/ui`, `ringo`, `world`,
`mapbuilder/tools`, `pty`, `shell`, `ssh`, `crypto/hash`, `crypto/aes`, `crypto/ed25519`,
`gfd/browser`, `pentest/{scan,pcap,webapp,wireless,crack,exploit}` (5 of 6 compile clean; `pcap`
blocked on a reference-typed parameter), `yoko` (a real, native Metasploit-shaped module/payload
type system — `#target` at the genuine low-level boundary), `firefly` (**compiles completely,
verified with real `gcc -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror`**, not just `parena build`'s own exit
code — the first of the ladybug testing framework's own files to reach this bar), `firefly/ladybug`
(renamed from `firefly/gomega` — see the Testing section below; still blocked on the pre-existing
no-module-linking gap when compiled standalone), `firefly/gomega` (kept as a back-compat alias,
same blocker), `scarab` (still blocked on its own multi-field `defenum` payload gap). Every other
package in the tables below is designed in `STDLIB.md` but has no `.prn`
file yet (`otp/*`, `media/*`, `sql/*`, `mapbuilder/layout`, `mapbuilder/template`, `container/*` —
LXC/cgroups/Docker, designed for the Moltbook/OpenClaw hardening + Emily OS threads, blocked on the
shared file-I/O gap before real `.prn` source is worth writing).

## Standard library — full planned API surface

Every package below is designed in `STDLIB.md` with real function signatures (region-typed,
matching NORTHSTAR's own `(var : Type @ Region)` form). This table is the index; `STDLIB.md` is
the source of truth for signatures, grounding, and honestly-stated limitations.

== stdlib/http/router.prn (head) ==
;; stdlib/http/router.prn — real Phase B proof point for LO/FRAMEWORK_NORTHSTAR.md's own
;; "batteries included" plan (founder real-time: "ok well write the deps in parena" — build the
;; framework's real dependencies in PARENA now, ahead of LO's own Phase 2 (`qi`) landing, matching
;; this repo's own established pattern of LO's future emitted `.prn` calling into pre-built
;; PARENA primitives rather than waiting to hand-roll them later).
;;
;; Real, deliberate scope boundary, named rather than half-built: this is a real, minimal
;; Sinatra/Express-style router — literal path segments plus a single `:name` capture-segment
;; convention, split on `/`. It deliberately does NOT reuse `base4/pattern.prn`'s own real
;; wildcard/quantifier/anchor/ALT/GROUP backtracking matcher, even though FRAMEWORK_NORTHSTAR.md's
;; own "Router" section named that as the architectural precedent — that matcher operates on
;; base4 STATE vectors, not characters/Strings, and FRAMEWORK_NORTHSTAR.md itself named the
;; byte-to-base4 encoding question as real and undecided. This file answers that question for
;; real by NOT waiting on it: a plain String-segment router needs no base4 encoding at all, and
;; covers the actual, common routing need (`/repos/:name/commits`) directly. A real, separate
;; follow-up if quantifier/wildcard route patterns are ever needed beyond simple `:name` capture.

(module http/router)
(import string)
(export route-matches? extract-param)

;; vec-string-at -- same real, pre-existing compiler gap `regex/pcre.prn`'s own already-documented
;; `vec-string-at` works around (a plain LOCAL `(Vec String)` value has no elem-type hint
;; registered). Redefined locally rather than imported since `pcre.prn` doesn't export its own
;; copy — matches this stdlib's own established small-per-file-#target-helper convention.
;;
;; Real, GENUINE bug found and fixed in the process, not just copied over: `pcre.prn`'s own
;; `vec-string-at` casts as `*(char **)vec_get(v, idx)` (a double dereference) — but its own real
;; caller (`join-strings`) has no actual caller anywhere in this stdlib, so that cast was never
;; actually exercised end-to-end. Confirmed live, via a real segfault building THIS file: a
;; `String` element is ALREADY a `char *`, and `string/split` (this file's own real Vec String
;; producer) pushes it directly with no extra boxing step (unlike `vec_box_i32`/`vec_box_f64` for
;; scalars, which genuinely need a fresh heap slot) — so the correct read-back is a single cast,
;; `(char *)vec_get(v, idx)`, not a double dereference through a nonexistent extra indirection.
(defn vec-string-at [(v : &(Vec String)) (idx : I32)]
  : String @ Region
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "(char *)vec_get(v, idx)")})

;; is-capture-segment? -- real, minimal `:name` detection via the segment's own first char code
;; (58 = ':', ASCII), avoiding a `string/substring` call (and its own `dest` requirement) for a
;; check this simple.
(defn is-capture-segment? [(seg : String @ Region)] : Bool
  (and (> (string/length seg) 0) (= (string/char-at seg 0) 58)))

;; segments-match? -- real, direct recursive per-segment comparison: a capture segment always
;; matches (its value is extracted separately, by extract-param below); a literal segment must
;; match exactly.
(defn segments-match? [(pat-segs : &(Vec String)) (path-segs : &(Vec String)) (i : I32) (n : I32)] : Bool
  (if (>= i n)

== stdlib/net/http.prn (head) ==
;; stdlib/net/http.prn — depends on net/tcp, string, vec. Design:
;; STDLIB.md "net/http" section. Client-side only (http-get/http-post/
;; http-request) -- the original design also specified a server-side
;; `serve`, dropped here (see below).
;;
;; Rewritten 2026-08-25, closing two real gaps found while building
;; stdlib/net/webdriver.prn (a WebDriver-protocol client, "Selenium
;; bindings" -- see that file's own header comment) on top of this one:
;;
;; 1. This file never actually compiled. Its own original design used
;;    `(Map String String)` for headers, but stdlib/map.prn's `K`/`V`
;;    generic type parameters fail VS0's emitter today ("unsupported
;;    return type symbol 'K'") -- confirmed live, the exact same real
;;    constraint json.prn's own header comment already documents for
;;    its own JObject. Fixed the identical way: headers are two
;;    parallel `Vec String`s (names, values) at the same index, real
;;    and O(n)-lookup, not a hash map -- json.prn's JObject is the
;;    direct precedent.
;; 2. Every function called helper functions (`connect-from-url`,
;;    `build-get-request`, `build-post-request`, `parse-http-response`,
;;    `parse-http-request`, `serialize-response`) that this file never
;;    actually defined -- real, original implementation work below, not
;;    a fill-in-the-blank.
;;
;; `serve` (the original design's server side) is dropped, not merely
;; deferred: it depended on the same undefined `parse-http-request`/
;; `serialize-response` pair, and nothing in this codebase's real,
;; current consumers (webdriver.prn is a CLIENT of an external WebDriver
;; server) needs a PARENA-side HTTP server yet. Flagged as real,
;; deliberately out-of-scope work for whoever needs it next, not
;; silently dropped.
;;
;; URL strings are NOT parsed here -- callers pass host/port/path
;; separately. A real, deliberate simplification over the original
;; design (which took one `url : String` per call): general URL parsing
;; (scheme, userinfo, IPv6 literals, query strings) is real, separate
;; scope this file's actual callers don't need (webdriver.prn always
;; talks to a fixed local WebDriver host:port; a future caller that
;; genuinely needs URL parsing can add it as its own function without
;; touching this one).
;;
;; TLS is still not implemented (carried over from the original design
;; note): https:// needs a real TLS library via FFI, same judgment as
;; linalg's BLAS/LAPACK note. Everything below is plain HTTP.
;;

- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/net/tcp.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/net/tcp.prn — depends on string. Design: STDLIB.md "net/tcp"
      ;; section. Connection-oriented; thin FFI over real BSD sockets, the same
      ;; primitive REDGARDEN/SHANKPIT's own UDP servers sit on top of, just the
      ;; TCP half of it.
      ;;
      ;; Rewritten 2026-08-25, real host implementation closing the gap this
      ;; file's own previous version left open ("FFI declared, host
      ;; implementation not written yet") — same real bug class io.prn's own
      ;; 2026-08-24 rewrite found and fixed for file I/O, found again here by
      ;; the same discipline (actually compiling to C, not trusting `parena
      ;; build`'s success): every `#target` body below used to declare its
      ;; return type as `(Result TcpStream NetError)` directly, but `#target`
      ;; is trusted verbatim with no auto-boxing (emit.c's own
      ;; find_target_c_src comment) — that never produced valid C. Fixed by
      ;; io.prn's own already-established shape: the only `#target` bodies
      ;; left are genuinely-irreducible raw syscalls returning a plain scalar
      ;; (an fd, or -1 on failure) or a plain String; every Result/TcpStream
      ;; value is built with ordinary `(Ok ...)`/`(Err ...)`/`{:field val}`
      ;; PARENA syntax, same as io.prn's `file-open`.
      ;;
      ;; Second real bug found in the same pass, distinct from the boxing one
      ;; above: VS0 emits a top-level `defn`'s name as a BARE, unprefixed C
      ;; identifier (no module-path mangling for a module's own top-level
      ;; definitions — mangle()'s `/`-to-`_` prefixing is a call-site
      ;; convention for cross-module references, e.g. `vec/new` -> `vec_new`
      ;; from another file, not something the defining module applies to
      ;; itself). The original API names here (`connect`/`listen`/`accept`/
      ;; `read`/`write`/`close`) are also literal libc function names
      ;; declared in <sys/socket.h>/<unistd.h> -- gcc genuinely fails on the
      ;; conflicting redeclaration the instant this file and any system
      ;; header meet in the same translation unit (confirmed live, not
      ;; assumed: this is exactly what broke building the very first attempt
      ;; at a real end-to-end tcp test). io.prn's own public names
      ;; (`file-open`/`file-close`/`read-string`/`write-string`, never bare
      ;; `open`/`close`/`read`/`write`) already avoid this by convention, not
      ;; by any compiler-level namespacing -- there isn't any yet. Renamed to
      ;; match that same real, established house pattern: every exported name
      ;; below is `tcp-`-prefixed.
      
      (module net/tcp)
      (import string)
      (export tcp-listen tcp-accept tcp-connect tcp-read tcp-write tcp-close TcpListener TcpStream NetError)
      
      (defstruct TcpListener
        (fd : I32))
      
      (defstruct TcpStream
        (fd : I32))
      
      (defenum NetError
        (ConnectionRefused)
        (Timeout)
        (AddressInUse)
        (Other))
      
      ;; ---- raw syscall primitives -- the only #target bodies in this file,
      ;; each a single C expression against runtime/parena_runtime.h's own
      ;; tcp_*_impl functions, no boxing.
      
      (defn raw-connect [(host : String @ Region) (port : I32)]
        : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "tcp_connect_impl(host, port)")})
      
      (defn raw-listen [(port : I32)]
        : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "tcp_listen_impl(port)")})
      
      (defn raw-accept [(listener-fd : I32)]
        : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "tcp_accept_impl(listener_fd)")})
      
      (defn raw-read [(fd : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "tcp_read_impl(fd, dest)")})
      
      (defn raw-write [(fd : I32) (data : String @ Region)]
        : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "tcp_write_impl(fd, data)")})
      
      (defn raw-close [(fd : I32)]
        : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "tcp_close_impl(fd)")})
      
      ;; tcp-connect -- errno isn't inspected here (unlike io.prn's
      ;; file-open): getaddrinfo/socket/connect failures inside
      ;; tcp_connect_impl don't map cleanly onto plain libc errno
      ;; (getaddrinfo has its own EAI_* error space), so this deliberately
      ;; narrower NetError enum just reports ConnectionRefused for any
      ;; raw-connect failure -- a real, honest, coarser signal than io.prn's
      ;; per-errno mapping, not a fake finer one.
      (defn tcp-connect [(host : String @ :region/scratch) (port : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : (Result TcpStream NetError) @ Region
        (let [fd (raw-connect host port)]
          (if (< fd 0)
            (Err ConnectionRefused)
            (Ok {:fd fd}))))
      
      (defn tcp-listen [(port : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : (Result TcpListener NetError) @ Region
        (let [fd (raw-listen port)]
          (if (< fd 0)
            (Err AddressInUse)
            (Ok {:fd fd}))))
      
      (defn tcp-accept [(!l : &TcpListener) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : (Result TcpStream NetError) @ Region
        (let [fd (raw-accept (get-field !l :fd))]
          (if (< fd 0)
            (Err Other)
            (Ok {:fd fd}))))
      
      (defn tcp-read [(!s : &mut TcpStream) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : (Result String NetError) @ Region
        (Ok (raw-read (get-field !s :fd) dest)))
      
      (defn tcp-write [(!s : &mut TcpStream) (data : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : (Result I32 NetError) @ Region
        (if (< (raw-write (get-field !s :fd) data) 0)
          (Err Other)
          (Ok 0)))
      
      (defn tcp-close [(!s : &mut TcpStream) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
        : (Result Unit NetError) @ Region
        (if (< (raw-close (get-field !s :fd)) 0)
          (Err Other)
          (Ok unit)))
      
- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit460/sp_host.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit460/sp_host.prn -- the shankpit-460 web page's host code. PARENA, compiled to TypeScript
      ;; (parena build sp_host.prn -o sp_host.ts), then type-stripped to the .js the page loads.
      ;;
      ;; Same rule as BRAWLPIT web (founder, 2026-10-16: "make sure its actually wasm not faked with a bunch of garbage
      ;; js; whatever we do need to use js for use parena into TS"): this is the ONLY JavaScript on the page and it is
      ;; generated from this file. It contains no game logic. The game -- simulation, bots, the 3D renderer, the menus and
      ;; the matchmaking protocol -- is shankpit460.wasm (stdlib/shankpit460/sp_*.prn); the module imports nothing, so the
      ;; browser has to do exactly the things below because only a browser can:
      ;;   1. fetch + instantiate the wasm                        (boot ... on-instance)
      ;;   2. copy the framebuffer the wasm painted onto a canvas (tick: putImageData of a view onto wasm memory)
      ;;   3. forward keyboard / mouse / pointer-lock / gamepad   (on-keydown ... poll-pads -> sp_key / sp_mouse / sp_pad ...)
      ;;   4. own the WebSocket to IDUNA's matchmaker             (ensure-socket!, pump-out!: frames in and out of wasm memory)
      ;;   5. turn the engine's sound events into WebAudio blips  (play-sound!)
      ;;   6. keep the page's own DOM labels in step              (status pill, footer)
      
      ;; ---- module state ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (def canvas null)
      (def ctx null)
      (def image null)          ; ImageData viewing the wasm framebuffer in place
      (def wasm null)           ; the instance's exports
      (def memory null)
      (def view null)           ; DataView over wasm memory
      (def sock null)
      (def next-try 0.0)        ; performance.now() before which no new socket is opened
      (def idle-since 0.0)
      (def session null)
      (def wasm-bytes 0)
      (def wasm-imports 0)
      (def snd-seen 0)
      (def actx null)
      (def noise-buf null)
      (def muted false)
      (def last-phase -1)
      
      ;; ---- DOM helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn doc [] : Any (js/global "document"))
      (defn el [(id : String)] : Any (js/call (doc) "getElementById" id))
      (defn now [] : F64 (js/call (js/global "performance") "now"))
      
      (defn set-text! [(id : String) (text : String)] : Unit
        (let [e (el id)]
          (when (not (js/null? e)) (js/set! e "textContent" text))))
      
      (defn set-hidden! [(id : String) (hidden : Bool)] : Unit
        (let [e (el id)]
          (when (not (js/null? e)) (js/set! e "hidden" hidden))))
      
      (defn fail! [(msg : Any)] : Unit
        (do (set-text! "sp-pill" "Could not start")
            (set-text! "sp-load-msg" (str "shankpit-460 could not start: " msg))
            (js/call (js/global "console") "error" msg)))
      
      (defn ignore! [(e : Any)] : Unit unit)
      
      ;; ---- 1. fetch + instantiate the wasm --------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn boot [(canvas-id : String) (wasm-url : String)] : Unit
        (do
          (set! canvas (el canvas-id))
          (set! ctx (js/call canvas "getContext" "2d"))
          (set-text! "sp-pill" "Loading wasm...")
          (js/call
            (js/call
              (js/call
                (js/call (js/call-fn (js/global "fetch") wasm-url) "then" (callback on-response))
                "then" (callback on-bytes))
              "then" (callback on-instance))
            "catch" (callback fail!))))
      
      (defn on-response [(r : Any)] : Any
        (if (js/get r "ok")
            (js/call r "arrayBuffer")
            (js/call (js/global "Promise") "reject" (str "shankpit460.wasm: HTTP " (js/get r "status")))))
      
      (defn on-bytes [(bytes : Any)] : Any
        (do (set! wasm-bytes (js/get bytes "byteLength"))
            ;; the module takes NO imports: no allocator, no libc, no JS callbacks
            (js/call (js/global "WebAssembly") "instantiate" bytes (js/obj))))
      
      (defn on-instance [(result : Any)] : Unit
        (do
          (set! wasm (js/get (js/get result "instance") "exports"))
          (set! memory (js/get wasm "memory"))
          (set! view (js/new "DataView" (js/get memory "buffer")))
          (set! wasm-imports (js/get (js/call (js/global "WebAssembly.Module") "imports" (js/get result "module")) "length"))
          (js/call wasm "sp_init")
          (set! image
                (js/new "ImageData"
                        (js/new "Uint8ClampedArray" (js/get memory "buffer") (js/call wasm "sp_fb_addr")
                                (* (* (js/call wasm "sp_fb_w") (js/call wasm "sp_fb_h")) 4))
                        (js/call wasm "sp_fb_w") (js/call wasm "sp_fb_h")))
          (load-session!)
          (install-listeners)
          (set-hidden! "sp-load" true)
          (set-hidden! "sp-canvas" false)
          (set-text! "sp-pill" "Running in WebAssembly")
          (set-text! "sp-stat" (str "shankpit460.wasm " (math/round (/ wasm-bytes 1024)) " KB  -  "
                                    wasm-imports " imports  -  "
                                    (/ (js/get (js/get memory "buffer") "byteLength") 1048576) " MB fixed memory, no allocator  -  PARENA"))
          (let [b (el "sp-fullscreen")]
            (when (not (js/null? b))
              (js/set! b "disabled" false)
              (js/call b "addEventListener" "click" (callback on-fullscreen))))
          (let [b (el "sp-mute")]
            (when (not (js/null? b))
              (js/call b "addEventListener" "click" (callback on-mute-click))))
          (refresh-status-quiet!)
          (js/call-fn (js/global "setInterval") (callback refresh-status-quiet!) 15000)
          (js/call (js/global "window") "requestAnimationFrame" (callback tick))))
      
      ;; ---- 2. the frame loop ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn tick [(t : F64)] : Unit
        (do
          (poll-pads)
          (ensure-socket!)
          (js/call wasm "sp_frame" t)
          (pump-out!)
          (js/call ctx "putImageData" image 0 0)
          (play-sounds!)
          (sync-lock!)
          (sync-labels!)
          (js/call (js/global "window") "requestAnimationFrame" (callback tick))))
      
      (defn on-fullscreen [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (js/call (el "sp-stage") "requestFullscreen"))
      
      ;; ---- 3. input forwarding --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn game-key? [(e : Any)] : Bool
        (let [k (js/get e "keyCode")]
          (or (and (>= k 37) (<= k 40)) (or (= k 32) (= k 9)))))
      
      ;; keys belong to the game while the canvas has focus or the pointer is captured (or nothing has focus)
      (defn game-focused? [] : Bool
        (let [a (js/get (doc) "activeElement")]
          (or (js/null? a) (or (= a canvas) (or (= a (js/get (doc) "body")) (not (js/null? (js/get (doc) "pointerLockElement"))))))))
      
      (defn locked? [] : Bool (not (js/null? (js/get (doc) "pointerLockElement"))))
      
      (defn on-keydown [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (when (game-focused?)
          (let [k (js/get e "keyCode")]
            (if (and (= k 77) (not (js/get e "repeat")))
                (toggle-mute!)
                (js/call wasm "sp_key" k 1))
            (when (game-key? e) (js/call e "preventDefault")))))
      
      (defn on-keyup [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (when (game-focused?)
          (js/call wasm "sp_key" (js/get e "keyCode") 0)))
      
      (defn on-blur [(e : Any)] : Unit (js/call wasm "sp_blur"))
      
      ;; pointer position mapped from CSS pixels to the 640x360 framebuffer (only meaningful on the menus)
      (defn on-mousemove [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (if (locked?)
            (js/call wasm "sp_mouse" (js/get e "movementX") (js/get e "movementY"))
            (let [rect (js/call canvas "getBoundingClientRect")
                  x (/ (* (- (js/get e "clientX") (js/get rect "left")) (js/call wasm "sp_fb_w")) (js/get rect "width"))
                  y (/ (* (- (js/get e "clientY") (js/get rect "top")) (js/call wasm "sp_fb_h")) (js/get rect "height"))]
              (js/call wasm "sp_pointer" (math/floor x) (math/floor y)))))
      
      ;; a click is handled inside the wasm synchronously (it may start a match), and in the SAME gesture the page asks
      ;; for pointer lock if the engine now wants it -- browsers only grant it from a user gesture
      (defn on-mousedown [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (do
          (ensure-audio!)
          (when (not (locked?)) (on-mousemove e))
          (js/call wasm "sp_button" (js/get e "button") 1)
          (when (and (= (js/get e "button") 0) (= (js/call wasm "sp_wants_lock") 1) (not (locked?)))
            (let [r (js/call canvas "requestPointerLock")]
              (when (= (js/typeof r) "object") (js/call r "catch" (callback ignore!)))))
          (js/call e "preventDefault")))
      
      (defn on-mouseup [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (js/call wasm "sp_button" (js/get e "button") 0))
      
      (defn on-wheel [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (do (js/call wasm "sp_wheel" (if (> (js/get e "deltaY") 0.0) 1 -1))
            (when (locked?) (js/call e "preventDefault"))))
      
      (defn on-contextmenu [(e : Any)] : Unit (js/call e "preventDefault"))
      
      (defn on-lock-change [(e : Any)] : Unit
        (js/call wasm "sp_lock" (if (locked?) 1 0)))
      
      ;; the engine leaves the menus -> lock, back to them -> let go
      (defn sync-lock! [] : Unit
        (do
          (let [ph (js/call wasm "sp_phase")]
            (when (and (!= ph last-phase) (!= ph 1) (locked?))
              (js/call (doc) "exitPointerLock"))
            (set! last-phase ph))))
      
      (defn install-listeners [] : Unit
        (let [w (js/global "window")]
          (js/call w "addEventListener" "keydown" (callback on-keydown))
          (js/call w "addEventListener" "keyup" (callback on-keyup))
          (js/call w "addEventListener" "blur" (callback on-blur))
          (js/call w "addEventListener" "mousemove" (callback on-mousemove))
          (js/call w "addEventListener" "mouseup" (callback on-mouseup))
          (js/call (doc) "addEventListener" "pointerlockchange" (callback on-lock-change))
          (js/call canvas "addEventListener" "mousedown" (callback on-mousedown))
          (js/call canvas "addEventListener" "wheel" (callback on-wheel))
          (js/call canvas "addEventListener" "contextmenu" (callback on-contextmenu))))
      
      ;; ---- gamepads: poll every frame (the Gamepad API has no change events for sticks/buttons) ----------------------------
      (defn pad-api? [] : Bool
        (and (js/defined? "navigator")
             (= (js/typeof (js/get (js/global "navigator") "getGamepads")) "function")))
      
      (defn pad-mask [(gp : Any)] : I32

== http/routes.prn ==
;; stdlib/http/routes.prn — depends on http/router, string, vec. Real extension of LO/
;; FRAMEWORK_NORTHSTAR.md's own Rails-like "batteries included" plan (founder real-time: "ok lets
;; build SHITHUB using LO... define the api first of the web framework... make it like rails").
;; `http/router.prn` already answers path-PATTERN matching (`route-matches?`/`extract-param`);
;; this file adds the missing HTTP-METHOD + ROUTE-TABLE layer Rails' own `config/routes.rb`
;; provides: a real `Router` (an ordered `(Vec Route)`), `add-route!`, `match-route` (first
;; method+path match, Rails' own "routes are tried in declaration order" semantics), and a real
;; `resource-routes` helper generating Rails' own 5 standard RESTful entries for one resource name
;; (index/create/show/update/destroy).
;;
;; Real, honest, named scope restriction, not silently hidden: a Route's own `handler-name` is a
;; plain String, not a real callable function VALUE. PARENA's own `fn` literals are non-capturing,
;; file-scope-only C functions (`regex/pcre.prn`'s own header comment already documents this as
;; the real reason it dropped a continuation-passing design), and no cross-module first-class
;; function reference is confirmed working either -- so a Router can't literally dispatch BY
;; CALLING the matched route's own handler. The real, working v0 shape instead: `match-route`
;; returns WHICH Route matched (read its own `handler-name`, e.g. "repos#index"), and the app's
;; own generated dispatch code (today: a real, hand-written `cond`/`match` chain over that string;
;; once `qi` lands: real, named function calls) decides what to actually call. Matches this
;; stdlib's own established "name the real limitation, ship the useful real subset" precedent
;; (`base4/vector.prn`'s own dot-product boxing bug, `regex/pcre.prn`'s own closures pivot).

(module http/routes)
(import http/router)
(import string)
(import vec)
(export add-route! match-route resource-routes route-method route-pattern route-handler-name
        vec-route-at)

(defstruct Route
  (method : String)
  (pattern : String)
  (handler-name : String))

(defn route-method [(r : &Route)] : String (get-field r :method))
(defn route-pattern [(r : &Route)] : String (get-field r :pattern))
(defn route-handler-name [(r : &Route)] : String (get-field r :handler-name))

;; add-route! -- appends one real Route to an existing Router (a `(Vec Route)`), Rails' own
;; declarative `get "/repos", to: "repos#index"` shape, just called directly rather than through a
;; DSL macro (VS0 has none). Two real, found-live compiler constraints worked around here: (1) a
;; `{...}` struct literal can't be passed directly as a call argument (`parena build` rejects it
;; -- "map literal doesn't match any registered defstruct's own field set", no type context at a
;; bare call site, the same class of issue S222-09's own MatchBudget literal hit) -- bound via a
;; `let` first; (2) pushing a real by-VALUE struct (not a scalar) onto a Vec needs a real Arena to
;; box it into (`vec/push!`'s own boxing fallback, the same one `Ok`/`Err`/`Some` already use) --
;; `dest` added for exactly that.
(defn add-route! [(router : &mut (Vec Route)) (method : String) (pattern : String) (handler-name : String) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : Unit
  (let [r {:method method :pattern pattern :handler-name handler-name}]
    (vec/push! router r)))

;; vec-route-at -- same real, per-file #target elem-access convention every other Vec-of-struct
;; caller in this stdlib already uses (no generic elem-type hint exists yet).
(defn vec-route-at [(v : &(Vec Route)) (idx : I32)]
  : Route @ Region
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "*(Route *)vec_get(v, idx)")})

;; match-route-from -- real, direct recursive linear scan, Rails' own "routes are tried in
;; declaration order, first match wins" semantics -- not a radix-tree/trie lookup (a real,
;; separate, later optimization if route tables ever get large enough to matter).
(defn match-route-from [(router : &(Vec Route)) (method : String) (path : String) (i : I32) (n : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : I32 @ Region
  (if (>= i n)
    -1
    (let [r (vec-route-at router i)]
      (if (and (string/str-eq? (get-field r :method) method)
               (http/router/route-matches? (get-field r :pattern) path dest))
        i
        (match-route-from router method path (+ i 1) n dest)))))

;; match-route -- real, honest "not found" sentinel: -1, same convention http/router.prn's own
;; find-param-index already uses, rather than a real Option (VS0's own Option boxing needs a real
;; Arena for a non-pointer payload anyway -- I32 is already a real, simple, unambiguous sentinel
;; here, since -1 is never a valid Vec index).
(defn match-route [(router : &(Vec Route)) (method : String) (path : String) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : I32 @ Region
  (match-route-from router method path 0 (vec/len router) dest))

;; path), not a redesign.
(defstruct GitStatusEntry
  (index-status    : String) ;; single char: staged status ('M'/'A'/'D'/'R'/'C'/'U'/' ')
  (worktree-status : String) ;; single char: unstaged status, or '?' for untracked
  (path            : String))

;; git-status -- real, structured parse of `git status --porcelain=v1`, run inside repo-dir. One
;; real GitStatusEntry per real line; an empty/clean tree returns a real, empty Vec, not an
;; error (a clean working tree is a real, valid, common state, not a failure).
(defn git-status [(repo-dir : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Vec GitStatusEntry) @ Region
  (let [quoted-dir (shell-single-quote repo-dir dest)]
    (let [cmd (string/concat "git -C " (string/concat quoted-dir " status --porcelain=v1" dest) dest)]
      (let [raw (process/run-capture cmd dest)]
        (let [lines (string/split raw "\n" dest)]
          (let [result (vec/new dest)]
            (loop [i 0
                   n (vec/len &lines)]
              (if (>= i n)
                result
                (let [line (vec/get &lines i)]
                  (if (>= (string/length line) 3)
                    (do
                      (vec/push! &result
                        {:index-status    (string/substring line 0 1 dest)
                         :worktree-status (string/substring line 1 2 dest)
                         :path            (string/substring line 3 (string/length line) dest)})
                      (recur (+ i 1) n))
                    (recur (+ i 1) n)))))))))))

;; git-stage! -- `git add <path>`, staging exactly one real file. Real, honest v0 scope: one
;; path per call (VS Code's own "stage this file" per-row button, not "stage all").
(defn git-stage! [(repo-dir : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result Unit GitError) @ Region
  (let [quoted-dir (shell-single-quote repo-dir dest)]
    (let [quoted-path (shell-single-quote path dest)]
      (let [cmd (string/concat "git -C " (string/concat quoted-dir (string/concat " add -- " quoted-path dest) dest) dest)]
        (do
          (process/run-capture cmd dest)
          (if (= (process/run-capture-exit-code) 0)
            (Ok unit)
            (Err (CommandFailed (process/run-capture-exit-code)))))))))

;; git-unstage! -- `git reset HEAD -- <path>`, the real inverse of git-stage!.
(defn git-unstage! [(repo-dir : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result Unit GitError) @ Region
  (let [quoted-dir (shell-single-quote repo-dir dest)]
    (let [quoted-path (shell-single-quote path dest)]
      (let [cmd (string/concat "git -C " (string/concat quoted-dir (string/concat " reset HEAD -- " quoted-path dest) dest) dest)]
        (do
          (process/run-capture cmd dest)
          (if (= (process/run-capture-exit-code) 0)
            (Ok unit)
            (Err (CommandFailed (process/run-capture-exit-code)))))))))

;; git-commit! -- `git commit -m <message>`, committing whatever is currently staged. Real,
;; honest v0 scope: no amend, no author override, no GPG signing -- the real, plain "commit the
;; index" VS Code's own commit-message-box-plus-checkmark-button does.
(defn git-commit! [(repo-dir : String @ Region) (message : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result Unit GitError) @ Region
  (let [quoted-dir (shell-single-quote repo-dir dest)]
    (let [quoted-msg (shell-single-quote message dest)]
      (let [cmd (string/concat "git -C " (string/concat quoted-dir (string/concat " commit -m " quoted-msg dest) dest) dest)]
        (do
          (process/run-capture cmd dest)
          (if (= (process/run-capture-exit-code) 0)
            (Ok unit)
            (Err (CommandFailed (process/run-capture-exit-code)))))))))

;; git-diff -- real unstaged diff text for one path (`git diff -- <path>`), the same real content
;; VS Code's own inline diff editor renders when a Source Control panel row is clicked.
(defn git-diff [(repo-dir : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : String @ Region
  (let [quoted-dir (shell-single-quote repo-dir dest)]
    (let [quoted-path (shell-single-quote path dest)]
      (let [cmd (string/concat "git -C " (string/concat quoted-dir (string/concat " diff -- " quoted-path dest) dest) dest)]
        (process/run-capture cmd dest)))))

;; git-diff-staged -- the staged (`--cached`) counterpart to git-diff, the real content VS Code
;; shows when the diff is opened from the STAGED CHANGES section instead of CHANGES.
(defn git-diff-staged [(repo-dir : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]

== git.prn head (deps/imports) ==
;; stdlib/git.prn — real Git integration primitives for the PARENA editor (kanban cruise-queue
;; card 342534534535: "copy the git interface paradigms and idoms and affordances from vs codes
;; for GIT for our parena editor").
;;
;; Real scope, matching this session's own established "shell out to the real, well-known tool"
;; judgment (the exact same one MIXFORGE/import.prn already applies to yt-dlp -- FFI-binding or
;; reimplementing libgit2 is real, separate, much bigger work, not attempted here): every real
;; function below shells out to the actual `git` binary via `process/run-capture`, parsing its
;; real, stable, scriptable output formats (`--porcelain=v1`, not `git status`'s own human
;; formatting, which is explicitly NOT meant to be parsed).
;;
;; Real, named VS Code parity target -- the Source Control panel's own core affordances, not the
;; whole of VS Code's git integration (no GitLens-style blame annotations, no merge-conflict UI,
;; no stash management here):
;;   - a real, structured status list (staged / unstaged / untracked), the panel's own central
;;     view -- git-status
;;   - stage / unstage a single file -- git-stage! / git-unstage!
;;   - commit the currently staged changes -- git-commit!
;;   - view a real diff, staged or unstaged -- git-diff
;;   - the current branch name, shown in VS Code's own status bar -- git-current-branch
;;
;; Real, honest, deliberately NOT done here (a future, separate pass): renamed-file detection
;; (porcelain v1's own `R  old -> new` two-path shape is real but not parsed specially -- a
;; rename surfaces as one raw status line here, not split into old/new paths), branch
;; switching/creation, push/pull/fetch, merge/rebase, and the actual editor-side UI (a real
;; Source Control panel widget consuming these) -- this file is the real, testable backend layer
;; only, same "stdlib primitive first, editor wiring later" split every other stdlib/editor/*.prn
;; module already follows.
;;
;; Real, named security discipline, matching MIXFORGE/import.prn's own precedent exactly:
;; run-capture shells the whole command through `/bin/sh -c` -- every caller-supplied string
;; (repo-dir, a file path, a commit message) that lands in a real git command below is passed
;; through shell-single-quote (log/projector.prn's own proven helper) first, never concatenated
;; raw.

(module git)
(import string)
(import process)
(import log/projector)
(export git-status git-stage! git-unstage! git-commit! git-diff git-diff-staged
        git-current-branch GitStatusEntry GitError)

(defenum GitError
  (CommandFailed (exit-code : I32)))

;; GitStatusEntry mirrors one real line of `git status --porcelain=v1` output: a 2-character
;; status code (index/staged status, then worktree/unstaged status -- a space means "no change
;; in that column", '?' means untracked) plus the real path. Real, direct parity with what VS
;; Code's own Source Control panel shows per file (a staged/unstaged badge letter next to a
;; path), not a redesign.

/* tests/test_git.c -- real end-to-end verification of stdlib/git.prn (kanban cruise-queue card

 * GIT for our parena editor"). Unlike test_mixforge_import.c (which has to stub yt-dlp -- no
 * network access, no real account), a real `git` binary is always available in this sandbox, so
 * this exercises every real function against an actual, freshly-created git repository -- no

#include "parena_runtime.h"
#include <assert.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "test_git_gen.c"

static void run_or_die(const char *cmd) {
    int rc = system(cmd);
    if (rc != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "setup command failed (%d): %s\n", rc, cmd);
        exit(1);
    }
}

int main(void) {
    Arena arena;
    arena_init(&arena);

    /* Real, fresh, throwaway git repo -- not this actual PARENA checkout (never run destructive
       git operations against a real, live-tracked repo from a test). */
    const char *repo = "/tmp/test_git_prn_repo";
    char cmd[512];
    snprintf(cmd, sizeof(cmd), "rm -rf %s && mkdir -p %s", repo, repo);
    run_or_die(cmd);
    snprintf(cmd, sizeof(cmd), "cd %s && git init -q && git config user.email t@t.com && git config user.name t", repo);
    run_or_die(cmd);

    /* A clean, empty repo (no commits yet) has a real, empty status. */
    Vec clean_status = git_status((char *)repo, &arena);

/* tests/test_net_stream.c -- real end-to-end verification of stdlib/net/stream.prn (PELLEGRINO's
 * incremental TCP client) on loopback, no external network, no TLS library needed.
 *
 * A forked child is a one-shot HTTP-ish server that sends "first", pauses, sends "second", closes.
 * The parent drives the PARENA-level API (stream-connect/send/pull/buf/len/reset/close) and asserts:
 *   - bytes are readable BEFORE the peer closes (the whole point vs net/tcp.prn's read-to-EOF),
 *   - the final buffer is exactly first+second, then pull reports closed (-1),
 *   - a refused connection returns -1 fast,
 *   - the line buffer and slots behave,
 *   - a build without PARENA_WITH_TLS reports TLS as unavailable instead of pretending (code 5).
 */
#include "parena_runtime.h"
#include <assert.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "test_net_stream_gen.c"

static int listen_loopback(int *port_out) {
    int ls = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    assert(ls >= 0);
    int one = 1;
    setsockopt(ls, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &one, sizeof one);
    struct sockaddr_in a;
    memset(&a, 0, sizeof a);
    a.sin_family = AF_INET;
    a.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK);
    a.sin_port = 0;
    assert(bind(ls, (struct sockaddr *)&a, sizeof a) == 0);
    assert(listen(ls, 4) == 0);
    socklen_t al = sizeof a;
    assert(getsockname(ls, (struct sockaddr *)&a, &al) == 0);
    *port_out = ntohs(a.sin_port);
    return ls;
}

/* ---- stdlib/net/tcp.prn real host glue (2026-08-25) ------------------
 * Real BSD sockets -- net/tcp.prn's own #target bodies previously
 * declared `tcp_listen`/`tcp_accept`/`tcp_connect`/`tcp_read`/
 * `tcp_write` but this runtime never actually implemented any of them
 * ("FFI declared, host implementation not written yet", the exact same
 * class of gap io.prn's own 2026-08-24 rewrite closed for file I/O —
 * see that section's header comment above for the full reasoning this
 * mirrors). Closed here for real, first real network I/O anywhere in
 * this language: net/tcp.prn itself was also carrying io.prn's
 * pre-fix bug (a `#target` body declared to return `Result`/`TcpStream`
 * directly, which VS0 never auto-boxes -- see emit.c's own
 * find_target_c_src comment) until this same pass fixed it to match
 * io.prn's now-established shape: raw primitives return a plain
 * scalar/string here, Result/Option/struct construction happens in
 * ordinary PARENA source in net/tcp.prn itself.
 *
 * Real, honest, narrow limitation, stated plainly rather than silently
 * assumed away: tcp_read_impl below reads until the peer closes the
 * connection or a read() error, the same one-shot shape
 * raw_read_all_impl above already uses for files. That is CORRECT for
 * a server that closes after responding (HTTP/1.0-style, or HTTP/1.1
 * with a `Connection: close` request header -- which is exactly why
 * net/http.prn's own request builder sends one) and WRONG for a
 * keep-alive connection the peer intends to reuse -- reading would
 * simply block forever waiting for an EOF that never comes. No
 * Content-Length-aware early stop or chunked-encoding support exists
 * yet; a real future gap, not this pass's scope. */
static inline int tcp_connect_impl(const char *host, int port) {
    struct addrinfo hints, *res, *rp;
    memset(&hints, 0, sizeof hints);
    hints.ai_family = AF_UNSPEC;
    hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
    char portstr[16];
    snprintf(portstr, sizeof portstr, "%d", port);
    if (getaddrinfo(host, portstr, &hints, &res) != 0) return -1;
    int fd = -1;
    for (rp = res; rp != NULL; rp = rp->ai_next) {
        fd = socket(rp->ai_family, rp->ai_socktype, rp->ai_protocol);
        if (fd < 0) continue;
        if (connect(fd, rp->ai_addr, rp->ai_addrlen) == 0) break;
        close(fd);
        fd = -1;
    }
    freeaddrinfo(res);
    return fd;
}

static inline int tcp_listen_impl(int port) {
    int fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (fd < 0) return -1;
    int opt = 1;
    setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &opt, sizeof opt);
    struct sockaddr_in addr;
    memset(&addr, 0, sizeof addr);
    addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;
    addr.sin_port = htons((uint16_t)port);
    if (bind(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof addr) < 0) { close(fd); return -1; }
    if (listen(fd, 16) < 0) { close(fd); return -1; }
    return fd;
}

...
/* tcp_read_impl -- same grow-by-4096-and-copy shape as
 * raw_read_all_impl above, deliberately not shared code: that one is
 * documented as the io.prn-specific real host glue, this one is
 * net/tcp.prn's own, and the two stdlib files are never combined in
 * the same real build (net/tcp.prn's own header comment already
 * documents an identical reason for NetError's own duplication) so
 * keeping them textually separate costs nothing and avoids coupling
 * either file's future changes to the other's.
 *
 * Content-Length-aware since 2026-09-02 (see PARENA's own CHANGELOG for the
 * real trace): a real WebDriver server (chromedriver) sends a real
 * Content-Length header but does NOT actually close the TCP connection
 * after responding, despite its own response advertising
 * "Connection:close" -- confirmed live two ways: a byte-identical request
 * sent over a plain shell /dev/tcp socket also blocks forever waiting for
 * an EOF that never comes, and a raw C reproduction calling this exact
 * function directly (bypassing every other layer) hung the same way.
 * Reading strictly until EOF -- this function's entire previous behavior
 * -- therefore hung forever on every single real request to a real
 * WebDriver server, not a webdriver.prn-specific bug. Fixed generically
 * here (every real net/tcp.prn caller benefits, not just http.prn): once
 * the header/body boundary is seen and a real Content-Length value is
 * found, stop reading the moment that many body bytes have arrived,
 * without waiting for the peer to close. Falls back to the original
 * read-until-EOF behavior when no Content-Length header is present (a
 * real, honestly-scoped limitation for chunked/close-delimited responses,
 * unchanged from before). A bounded 30s idle-read timeout (via poll) is a
 * real, cheap safety net against ever hanging forever again on a response
 * shape this function's own parsing can't make sense of. */
static inline char *tcp_read_impl(int fd, Arena *dest) {
    size_t cap = 4096;
    size_t len = 0;
    char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);
    long content_length = -1; /* -1 = not yet known (boundary not seen, or no Content-Length header) */
    size_t header_end = 0;
    for (;;) {
        if (content_length >= 0 && len >= header_end + (size_t)content_length) break;
        if (len + 4096 > cap) {
            size_t new_cap = cap + 4096;
            char *grown = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, new_cap);
            memcpy(grown, buf, len);
            buf = grown;
            cap = new_cap;
        }
        struct pollfd pfd;
        pfd.fd = fd;
        pfd.events = POLLIN;
        int pr = poll(&pfd, 1, 30000);
        if (pr <= 0) break; /* timeout or poll error -- return whatever's been read so far */
        ssize_t n = read(fd, buf + len, 4096);
        if (n <= 0) break;
        len += (size_t)n;
        if (content_length < 0) {
            long cl = find_body_length_from_headers(buf, len, &header_end);
            if (cl >= 0) content_length = cl;
            /* cl == -2 (boundary seen, no real Content-Length): keep the
               original read-until-EOF/timeout behavior. cl == -1
               (boundary not seen yet): keep reading. */
        }
    }
    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, len + 1);
    memcpy(out, buf, len);
    out[len] = '\0';
    return out;
}

/* tcp_write_impl -- byte-for-byte the same loop as string_concat's
 * sibling raw_write_impl above (write() is write() whether the fd is a
 * file or a socket); kept as its own real, distinctly-named function
 * rather than reused across the file/socket boundary, matching this
 * runtime's own established preference for names that say what they
 * are (net/tcp.prn's own header comment on NetError draws the same
 * file/socket line for the identical reason). */
static inline int tcp_write_impl(int fd, const char *s) {
    size_t len = strlen(s);
    size_t written = 0;
    while (written < len) {
        ssize_t n = write(fd, s + written, len - written);
        if (n < 0) return -1;
        written += (size_t)n;
    }
    return 0;
}

static inline int tcp_close_impl(int fd) {
    return close(fd) == 0 ? 0 : -1;
}

This file only\n * provides what the emitter cannot express today (named in PARENA/STDLIB.md's gap notes):\n *   - the Arena the generated code runs in (the emitter has no pointer-typed return, so a module\n *     cannot create one itself),\n *   - argv/env (there is no argv in the language yet),\n *   - a session-id generator (32 hex chars, matching edit_sync_create's own check),\n *   - the four session strings that must outlive one request (the emitter rejects set! on a\n *     top-level def, so a module-level mutable value is not expressible).\n */\n#include \"parena_runtime.h\"\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <time.h>\n\n#define LN_FIELD_MAX 65536\n\ntypedef struct {\n    char id[64];\n    char name[256];\n    char draft[LN_FIELD_MAX];\n    char log[LN_FIELD_MAX];\n    char seq[32];\n    char levels[512];\n    char repo[512];\n    char editor[512];\n} LocalNockState;\n\nstatic LocalNockState g_state;\nstatic Arena g_arena;\nstatic Arena g_scratch;\n\nArena *ln_scratch(void) { return &g_scratch; }\n\nint ln_port(void) {\n    const char *p = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_PORT\");\n    return (p && *p) ? atoi(p) : 8787;\n}\n\nconst char *ln_new_id(Arena *dest) {\n    /* 128-bit-ish capability token, hex, 32 chars -- edit_sync_create rejects anything else. */\n    char raw[17];\n    static int seeded = 0;\n    if (!seeded) { srand((unsigned)time(NULL) ^ (unsigned)getpid_safe()); seeded = 1; }\n    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) raw[i] = (char)(rand() & 0xff);\n    raw[16] = 0;\n    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, 33);\n    static const char *hex = \"0123456789abcdef\";\n    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {\n        unsigned char b = (unsigned char)raw[i];\n        out[i * 2] = hex[b >> 4];\n        out[i * 2 + 1] = hex[b & 0xf];\n    }\n    out[32] = 0;\n    return out;\n}\n\nconst char *ln_state_get(const char *field, Arena *dest) {\n    const char *v = \"\";\n    if (!strcmp(field, \"id\")) v = g_state.id;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"name\")) v = g_state.name;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"draft\")) v = g_state.draft;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"log\")) v = g_state.log;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"seq\")) v = g_state.seq;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"levels\")) v = g_state.levels;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"repo\")) v = g_state.repo;\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"editor\")) v = g_state.editor;\n    size_t n = strlen(v);\n    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, n + 1);\n    memcpy(out, v, n + 1);\n    return out;\n}\n\nint ln_state_set(const char *field, const char *value) {\n    char *dst = NULL;\n    size_t cap = 0;\n    if (!strcmp(field, \"id\")) { dst = g_state.id; cap = sizeof g_state.id; }\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"name\")) { dst = g_state.name; cap = sizeof g_state.name; }\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"draft\")) { dst = g_state.draft; cap = sizeof g_state.draft; }\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"log\")) { dst = g_state.log; cap = sizeof g_state.log; }\n    else if (!strcmp(field, \"seq\")) { dst = g_state.seq; cap = sizeof g_state.seq; }\n    if (!dst) return 0;\n    snprintf(dst, cap, \"%s\", value ? value : \"\");\n    return 1;\n}\n\nint nock_run(Arena *dest);\n\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    (void)argc;\n    (void)argv;\n    arena_init(&g_arena);\n    arena_init(&g_scratch);\n\n    /* Levels live in <repo>/levels, committed by the PARENA side. Paths come from the environment\n       so the tool can run from anywhere: LOCAL_NOCK_REPO, LOCAL_NOCK_LEVELS, LOCAL_NOCK_EDITOR. */\n    const char *repo = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_REPO\");\n    snprintf(g_state.repo, sizeof g_state.repo, \"%s\", (repo && *repo) ? repo : \".\");\n    const char *levels = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_LEVELS\");\n    if (levels && *levels) snprintf(g_state.levels, sizeof g_state.levels, \"%s\", levels);\n    else snprintf(g_state.levels, sizeof g_state.levels, \"%s/levels\", g_state.repo);\n    const char *editor = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_EDITOR\");\n    if (editor && *editor) snprintf(g_state.editor, sizeof g_state.editor, \"%s\", editor);\n    else snprintf(g_state.editor, sizeof g_state.editor, \"%s/tools/nock_editor.html\", g_state.repo);\n    snprintf(g_state.seq, sizeof g_state.seq, \"0\");\n\n    return nock_run(&g_arena);\n}\n"
}

value : \"\");\n    return 1;\n}\n\nconst char *ln_level_path(const char *name, Arena *dest) {\n    char buf[1200];\n    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, \"%s/%s.json\", g_state.levels, name ? name : \"\");\n    size_t n = strlen(buf);\n    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, n + 1);\n    memcpy(out, buf, n + 1);\n    return out;\n}\n\nconst char *ln_read_file(const char *path, Arena *dest) {\n    FILE *f = fopen(path, \"rb\");\n    if (!f) return \"\";\n    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);\n    long n = ftell(f);\n    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);\n    if (n < 0) { fclose(f); return \"\"; }\n    char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, (size_t)n + 1);\n    size_t got = fread(buf, 1, (size_t)n, f);\n    fclose(f);\n    buf[got] = 0;\n    return buf;\n}\n\nint ln_write_file(const char *path, const char *text) {\n    FILE *f = fopen(path, \"wb\");\n    if (!f) return 0;\n    size_t n = strlen(text);\n    size_t wrote = fwrite(text, 1, n, f);\n    int ok = (wrote == n);\n    if (fclose(f) != 0) ok = 0;\n    return ok ? \"\" : \",\", stem, e->d_name, bytes);\n            first = 0;\n        }\n        closedir(d);\n    }\n    snprintf(out + len, cap - len, \"]}\");\n    return out;\n}\n\nint nock_run(Arena *dest);\n\nint main(void) {\n    arena_init(&g_arena);\n    arena_init(&g_scratch);\n\n    const char *repo = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_REPO\");\n    snprintf(g_state.repo, sizeof g_state.repo, \"%s\", (repo && *repo) ? repo : \".\");\n    const char *levels = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_LEVELS\");\n    if (levels && *levels) snprintf(g_state.levels, sizeof g_state.levels, \"%s\", levels);\n    else snprintf(g_state.levels, sizeof g_state.levels, \"%s/levels\", g_state.repo);\n    const char *editor = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_EDITOR\");\n    if (editor && *editor) snprintf(g_state.editor, sizeof g_state.editor, \"%s\", editor);\n    else snprintf(g_state.editor, sizeof g_state.editor, \"%s/tools/nock_editor.html\", g_state.repo);\n    snprintf(g_state.seq, sizeof g_state.seq, \"0\");\n\n    return nock_run(&g_arena);\n}\n"

Session/level decisions stay in the caller too: no first-class functions exist\n;; yet (http/routes.prn's own header documents the same constraint against a handler table), so the\n;; caller's own string dispatch chooses among these builders.\n\n(module net/http_server)\n(import string)\n\n(export Request parse-request request-method request-path request-body header-value find-sub\n        response json-response text-response)\n\n(defstruct Request\n  (method : String)\n  (path : String)\n  (body : String))\n\n(defn request-method [(r : &Request)] : String (get-field r :method))\n(defn request-path [(r : &Request)] : String (get-field r :path))\n(defn request-body [(r : &Request)] : String (get-field r :body))\n\n;; find-sub -- index of `needle` in `s` at or after `from`, or -1. Plain char scanning, no regex.\n(defn find-sub [(s : String @ Region) (needle : String @ Region) (from : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : I32\n  (let [n (string/length s) m (string/length needle)]\n    (if (> m n)\n      -1\n      (let [last (- n m)]\n        (loop [i from]\n          (if (> i last)\n            -1\n            (if (string/str-eq? (string/substring s i (+ i m) dest) needle)\n              i\n              (recur (+ i 1)))))))))\n\n;; header-value -- value of header `name`, or \"\" when absent. `name` is matched case-insensitively.\n(defn header-value [(raw : String @ Region) (name : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region\n  (let [nlen (string/length name)]\n    (let [hit (find-sub raw (string/concat \"\\n\" name \":\" dest) 0 dest)]\n      (if (< hit 0)\n        \"\"\n        (let [start (+ (+ hit nlen) 2)]\n          (let [stop (find-sub raw \"\\r\" start dest)]\n            (if (< stop 0) \"\" (string/substring raw start stop dest))))))))\n\n;; path-only -- strip a query string (\"/api/levels?x=1\" -> \"/api/levels\").\n(defn path-only [(target : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region\n  (let [q (find-sub target \"?\" 0 dest)]\n    (if (< q 0) target (string/substring target 0 q dest))))\n\n;; charset=utf-8\" text dest))\n"

**What works now**

`make local-nock` → `http://127.0.0.1:8787`

- **Browser editor** (`tools/nock_editor.html`, served by the tool): canvas plan view, B/X/M-equivalent tools, undo, level list, save.
- **One live room shared with the game**: `SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions ./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map levels/starter.json --edit-live` (or paste the game's `--edit-session <id>` into the editor and press Join). The browser's edits push the working level + a `level` event so the game reloads it; the game's `box_add`/`box_del`/`spawner`/`avatar` events render in the browser.
- **Levels as code**: saving writes `levels/<name>.json` and commits `level(<name>): N walls from local NOCK` (never pushes). `levels/starter.json` is the first map; `leveltool check` accepts it.
- Protocol is the same one the client already speaks (`edit_sync.h` ↔ IDUNA's handler), so nothing in the game changed.

**The PARENA answer, honestly**

PARENA had **no server-side HTTP at all** — `net/http.prn`'s own header says `serve` was deliberately dropped. I built the dependency first, per the repo's PARENA-first rule:

- `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` — request parsing, case-insensitive header lookup, complete HTTP/1.1 response serialisation. **Verified: `parena build` succeeds.**
- `tools/local_nock.prn` + `tools/local_nock_host.c` — the server itself in PARENA (routing, JSON, level validation, git commit) over a thin host boundary. **It parses (`parena parse` clean) but does not emit**, blocked on four gaps I hit by actually building it:
  1. reference params / `match` scrutinees naming a defstruct imported from another module (`&TcpListener`) → *"unsupported reference target type"*, then *"'void *' isn't a registered defstruct type"* — note `net/tcp.prn` itself emits fine, this is specifically cross-module;
  2. `: (Arena @ Region)` returns;
  3. `(set! <top-level-def> v)`;
  4. the 2-arg-only `+`/`-` (worked around already).

So the port is real source, not a claim, but the **runner is still `tools/local_nock.py`** until those land. I did not delete it, and the README/CHANGELOG say exactly this. That's the tradeoff I chose over shipping a server that doesn't build.

**Verified**
- `python3 tools/test_local_nock.py` → **12/12 checks**: editor page, level save + real git commit, no-op re-save, invalid level (missing `walls`) and bad name rejected, session create returns 32-hex, events post/poll with `since`, unknown kinds rejected, draft push/fetch, saved-level fallback + 404, long-poll wakes on an event, unknown session 404.
- `parena build stdlib/net/http_server.prn` → clean C; `parena parse tools/local_nock.prn` → clean.
- `leveltool check levels/starter.json` → ok (5 walls).

**Limits**
- Not driven in a browser (Chrome absent here) or in the lobby (no SDL2/GL/display), so the editor UI and the in-game join path are tested at the HTTP-contract level only.
- One room per run; `?since` is ignored (whole log replayed — the client's applied events are idempotent, so it just refetches).

      /* mangle_call_name -- real, structural fix for a call-site gap

       * (found 2026-08-21 via a real, deliberate multi-file test: a function

       * `length`). mangle() alone just blindly turns every `/` into `_`, so
       * `string/length` becomes the call-site text "string_length" -- a C
       * identifier that was NEVER what any real defn actually compiles to
       * (a defn's own name is never itself prefixed by its enclosing
       * module: `(defn length ...)` inside `(module string)` still compiles

       * cmd_build() comment) -- so a qualified call can only ever correctly
       * resolve by falling back to the BARE, unqualified function name.
       *

       * existed: try the bare (last `/`-segment) mangled name FIRST, but
       * ONLY use it if g_defn_return_types already knows a real defn by that
       * exact bare name (populated early by emit_c()'s own forward-

       * -- compile of array.prn's own `product`, whose real body calls

       * same file, so `vec/get`'s own bare-mangled "get" collided with a
       * REAL, unrelated defn's own name, and the (wrong) resolution silently

       * helper, needs no equivalent exclusion: a single-file build of a file
       * calling `string/concat` without string.prn combined in has no real
       * bare `concat` defn anywhere in that build, so the bare-name lookup
       * correctly misses there on its own, preserving that already-working,
       * already-tested call site exactly as before. */
      static const char *mangle_call_name(Arena *arena, const char *text) {
          if (strncmp(text, "vec/", 4) == 0) {
              return mangle(arena, text);
          }
          const char *last_slash = strrchr(text, '/');
          if (last_slash && last_slash[1] != '\0') {
              const char *bare_mangled = mangle(arena, last_slash + 1);
              if (find_defn_return_type(bare_mangled)) {
                  return bare_mangled;
              }
          }
          return mangle(arena, text);
      }

- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/net/http_server.prn -- the server half of net/http, the dependency STDLIB.md/net/http.prn
      ;; already names as deliberately dropped ("`serve` ... flagged as real, deliberately out-of-scope work
      ;; for whoever needs it next"). Whoever needs it next is SHANKPIT's local NOCK map tools
      ;; (SHANKPIT/tools/local_nock.prn): the cloud IDUNA/NOCK tooling is not always reachable and levels
      ;; still have to be authored.
      ;;
      ;; Deliberately minimal and honest: HTTP/1.1, one request per connection (tcp_read_impl already stops
      ;; at the Content-Length body), literal path/prefix matching (http/router.prn covers patterns), and
      ;; case-insensitive header lookup over the raw header block.
      ;;
      ;; Deliberately socket-free: this module builds response STRINGS only. Writing them out belongs to
      ;; the caller, because a `&mut TcpStream` parameter in a module that only *imports* net/tcp hits a
      ;; real VS0 limitation ("unsupported reference target type 'TcpStream'") -- found by building this
      ;; file, not assumed. Session/level decisions stay in the caller too: no first-class functions exist
      ;; yet (http/routes.prn's own header documents the same constraint against a handler table), so the
      ;; caller's own string dispatch chooses among these builders.
      
      (module net/http_server)
      (import string)
      
      (export parse-method parse-path parse-body header-value find-sub
              response json-response text-response)
      
      ;; parse-method / parse-path / parse-body -- three String accessors instead of one Request struct:
      ;; returning a defstruct across a module boundary is a real VS0 limitation found by building this
      ;; file ("'void *' isn't a registered defstruct type" at the caller's get-field), so the caller gets
      ;; plain Strings and never has to name this module's types.
      (defn parse-method [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [sp1 (find-sub raw " " 0 dest)]
          (if (< sp1 0) "" (string/substring raw 0 sp1 dest))))
      
      (defn parse-path [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [sp1 (find-sub raw " " 0 dest)]
          (if (< sp1 0)
            ""
            (let [sp2 (find-sub raw " " (+ sp1 1) dest)]
              (if (< sp2 0) "" (path-only (string/substring raw (+ sp1 1) sp2 dest) dest))))))
      
      (defn parse-body [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (body-of raw dest))
      
      (defn status-line [(status : I32)] : String @ Region
        (if (= status 200) "200 OK"
          (if (= status 201) "201 Created"
            (if (= status 400) "400 Bad Request"
              (if (= status 404) "404 Not Found"
                (if (= status 500) "500 Internal Server Error" "200 OK"))))))
      
      ;; response -- a complete HTTP/1.1 response with Content-Length and Connection: close.
      (defn response [(status : I32) (content-type : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (string/concat
          (string/concat "HTTP/1.1 "
            (string/concat (status-line status)
              (string/concat "\r\nContent-Type: "
                (string/concat content-type
                  (string/concat "\r\nContent-Length: "
                    (string/concat (string/i32-to-string (string/length body) dest)
                      "\r\nConnection: close\r\nCache-Control: no-store\r\n\r\n" dest) dest) dest) dest) dest) dest)
          body dest))
      
      (defn json-response [(status : I32) (json : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (response status "application/json" json dest))
      
      (defn text-response [(status : I32) (text : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (response status "text/plain; charset=utf-8" text dest))
