- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/tools/local_nock.prn
  content: |
      ;; tools/local_nock.prn -- local NOCK map tools in PARENA: the IDUNA-free authoring server.
      ;;
      ;; Same wire contract as the IDUNA handler the native client is written against
      ;; (packages/world/edit_sync.h <-> IDUNA/internal/http/handlers/shankpit_edit_sessions.go), the same
      ;; browser editor (tools/nock_editor.html), and the same levels/*.json committed to git -- but the
      ;; server is PARENA, matching this monorepo's standing "core deps are PARENA-first" rule. The missing
      ;; stdlib dependency (there was no server-side net/http at all) is real PARENA too:
      ;; PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn.
      ;;
      ;; Real, named parity gap: one live room per run (the actual use is one browser tab plus one game
      ;; window), and the event log is returned whole rather than filtered by ?since -- the native client
      ;; is idempotent for the events it applies (spawner/teleport/spawn_mode/level), so replaying it just
      ;; refetches the working level. Multi-room + since-filtering is real follow-up work, not hidden.
      ;;
      ;; Host boundary (tools/local_nock_host.c), deliberately thin: the arena, env, the session id and
      ;; the session strings that outlive one request -- the emitter has no pointer-typed return and
      ;; rejects set! on a top-level def today. Routing, JSON shapes, level validation and the git commit
      ;; are PARENA below.
      
      ;; STATUS (2026-10-30): parses cleanly (`parena parse`), does NOT emit yet. Verified by running
      ;; `parena build` on this file -- the remaining VS0 emitter gaps, each hit in turn:
      ;;   1. a reference parameter naming a defstruct defined in an IMPORTED module (`&TcpListener`),
      ;;      and a `match` whose scrutinee has that type ('void *') -- net/tcp.prn itself emits fine, so
      ;;      this is specifically cross-module;
      ;;   2. `: (Arena @ Region)` return types (the host owns the arena for now);
      ;;   3. `(set! <top-level-def> v)` (session state goes through the host's ln_state_* accessors).
      ;; The request/response half is real and emits: PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn. Shipped and
      ;; tested today is tools/local_nock.py (make test-local-nock, 12 checks); this file is the port to
      ;; finish once those land, and everything from `handle` down moves over unchanged.
      
      (module local_nock)
      (import string)
      (import net/tcp)
      (import net/http_server)
      (import process)
      
      (export nock-run)
      
      ;; ---- host boundary -------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn host-port [] : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_port()")})
      
      (defn host-new-id [(dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_new_id(dest)")})
      
      (defn host-get [(field : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_state_get(field, dest)")})
      
      (defn host-set [(field : String @ Region) (value : String @ Region)] : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_state_set(field, value)")})
      
      (defn host-levels-json [(dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_levels_json(dest)")})
      
      (defn host-editor [(dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_editor_html(dest)")})
      
      (defn host-read [(path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_read_file(path, dest)")})
      
      (defn host-write [(path : String @ Region) (text : String @ Region)] : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_write_file(path, text)")})
      
      (defn host-level-path [(name : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_level_path(name, dest)")})
      
      (defn host-log-event [(body : String @ Region)] : I32
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_log_event(body)")})
      
      (defn host-session-json [(dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        #target
        {:c (inline-c "ln_session_json(dest)")})
      
      ;; ---- helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn has? [(haystack : String @ Region) (needle : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : Bool
        (>= (http_server/find-sub haystack needle 0 dest) 0))
      
      (defn prefix? [(s : String @ Region) (prefix : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : Bool
        (if (> (string/length prefix) (string/length s))
          false
          (string/str-eq? (string/substring s 0 (string/length prefix) dest) prefix)))
      
      (defn drop-prefix [(s : String @ Region) (prefix : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (string/substring s (string/length prefix) (string/length s) dest))
      
      (defn quote-shell [(s : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (string/concat "'" (string/concat s "'" dest) dest))
      
      (defn commit-msg [(name : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (string/concat "level(" (string/concat name ") from local NOCK" dest) dest))
      
      ;; git-commit-level -- stage the level file and commit it. Never pushes (that stays a human step).
      (defn git-commit-level [(name : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [add-cmd (string/concat "git -C "
                        (string/concat (quote-shell (host-get "repo" dest) dest)
                          (string/concat " add -- "
                            (string/concat (quote-shell (host-level-path name dest) dest) "" dest) dest) dest) dest)]
          (do
            (process/run-capture add-cmd dest)
            (process/run-capture
              (string/concat "git -C "
                (string/concat (quote-shell (host-get "repo" dest) dest)
                  (string/concat " commit -m "
                    (string/concat (quote-shell (commit-msg name dest) dest) "" dest) dest) dest) dest) dest)
            (if (= (process/run-capture-exit-code) 0)
              "{\"committed\":true}"
              "{\"committed\":false,\"detail\":\"nothing to commit\"}"))))
      
      (defn save-level [(name : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (if (has? body "\"walls\"" dest)
          (if (= (host-write (host-level-path name dest) body) 1)
            (git-commit-level name dest)
            "{\"error\":\"cannot write level\"}")
          "{\"error\":\"level needs a walls array\"}"))
      
      ;; ---- routes ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn level-read-response [(name : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [text (host-read (host-level-path name dest) dest)]
          (if (string/str-eq? text "")
            (http_server/text-response 404 "no such level" dest)
            (http_server/response 200 "application/json" text dest))))
      
      (defn level-save-response [(name : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [result (save-level name body dest)]
          (if (has? result "error" dest)
            (http_server/json-response 400 result dest)
            (http_server/json-response 200 result dest))))
      
      (defn route-levels [(method : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (string/str-eq? path "/api/levels"))
          (http_server/json-response 200 (host-levels-json dest) dest)
          (if (and (string/str-eq? method "PUT") (prefix? path "/api/levels/" dest))
            (level-save-response (drop-prefix path "/api/levels/" dest) body dest)
            (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (prefix? path "/api/levels/" dest))
              (level-read-response (drop-prefix path "/api/levels/" dest) dest)
              ""))))
      
      (defn route-session [(method : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (if (and (string/str-eq? method "POST") (string/str-eq? path "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions"))
          (let [id (host-new-id dest)]
            (do
              (host-set "id" id)
              (host-set "log" "")
              (host-set "draft" "")
              (http_server/json-response 201
                (string/concat "{\"id\":\"" (string/concat id "\",\"seq\":0}" dest) dest) dest)))
          (if (and (string/str-eq? method "POST") (has? path "/events" dest))
            (do
              (host-log-event body)
              (http_server/json-response 200 "{\"ok\":true}" dest))
            (if (and (string/str-eq? method "PUT") (has? path "/level" dest))
              (do
                (host-set "draft" body)
                (http_server/json-response 200 "{\"rev\":1}" dest))
              (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (has? path "/level" dest))
                (let [draft (host-get "draft" dest)]
                  (if (string/str-eq? draft "")
                    (http_server/text-response 404 "this session has no level yet" dest)
                    (http_server/response 200 "application/json" draft dest)))
                (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (has? path "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/" dest))
                  (http_server/json-response 200 (host-session-json dest) dest)
                  ""))))))
      
      (defn page-or-route [(method : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [levels (route-levels method path body dest)]
          (if (> (string/length levels) 0)
            levels
            (let [session (route-session method path body dest)]
              (if (> (string/length session) 0)
                session
                (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (string/str-eq? path "/"))
                  (http_server/text-response 200 (host-editor dest) dest)
                  (http_server/text-response 404 "not found" dest)))))))
      
      (defn handle [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [method (http_server/parse-method raw dest)]
          (if (string/str-eq? method "")
            (http_server/text-response 400 "bad request" dest)
            (page-or-route method
              (http_server/parse-path raw dest)
              (http_server/parse-body raw dest) dest))))
      
      ;; ---- accept loop ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; The listener cannot be a parameter here: `&TcpListener` names a defstruct defined in an imported
      ;; module, which VS0 rejects for reference targets (verified by building this file). Binding it in
      ;; nock-run and recursing with loop/recur keeps it a local value instead.
      (defn nock-run [(dest : Arena @ Region)] : I32
        (match (net/tcp/tcp-listen (host-port) dest)
          ((Ok !listener)
            (do
              (println "local NOCK (PARENA) listening")
              (loop [served 0]
                (let [res (net/tcp/tcp-accept &!listener dest)]
                  (match res
                    ((Ok !stream)
                      (let [raw (match (net/tcp/tcp-read !stream dest) ((Ok !text) !text) ((Err _) ""))]
                        (do
                          (net/tcp/tcp-write &mut !stream (handle raw dest) dest)
                          (net/tcp/tcp-close &mut !stream dest)
                          (recur (+ served 1)))))
                    ((Err _) 1))))))
          ((Err _) (do (println "local_nock: cannot bind port") 1))))
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/tools/local_nock_host.c
  content: |
      /* tools/local_nock_host.c -- the thin C host for tools/local_nock.prn.
       *
       * Only what the VS0 emitter cannot express yet (named in the .prn header): the arena the generated
       * code runs in, env/argv, a session-id generator, the session strings that outlive one request, and
       * plain file/directory access (the emitter has no pointer-typed return and rejects set! on a
       * top-level def). Routing, JSON shapes, level validation and the git commit are PARENA.
       */
      #include "parena_runtime.h"
      
      #include <dirent.h>
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <stdlib.h>
      #include <string.h>
      #include <time.h>
      #include <unistd.h>
      
      static Arena g_arena;
      static Arena g_scratch;
      
      typedef struct {
          char id[64];
          char draft[4 << 20];
          char log[1 << 20];
          char seq[32];
          char repo[512];
          char levels[1024];
          char editor[1024];
      } NockState;
      
      static NockState g_state;
      
      Arena *ln_scratch(void) { return &g_scratch; }
      
      int ln_port(void) {
          const char *p = getenv("LOCAL_NOCK_PORT");
          return (p && *p) ? atoi(p) : 8787;
      }
      
      const char *ln_new_id(Arena *dest) {
          static const char *hex = "0123456789abcdef";
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, 33);
          srand((unsigned)(time(NULL) ^ (long)getpid()));
          for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) out[i] = hex[rand() & 0xf];
          out[32] = 0;
          return out;
      }
      
      const char *ln_state_get(const char *field, Arena *dest) {
          const char *v = "";
          if (!strcmp(field, "id")) v = g_state.id;
          else if (!strcmp(field, "draft")) v = g_state.draft;
          else if (!strcmp(field, "log")) v = g_state.log;
          else if (!strcmp(field, "seq")) v = g_state.seq;
          else if (!strcmp(field, "repo")) v = g_state.repo;
          else if (!strcmp(field, "levels")) v = g_state.levels;
          else if (!strcmp(field, "editor")) v = g_state.editor;
          size_t n = strlen(v);
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, n + 1);
          memcpy(out, v, n + 1);
          return out;
      }
      
      int ln_state_set(const char *field, const char *value) {
          char *dst = NULL;
          size_t cap = 0;
          if (!strcmp(field, "id")) { dst = g_state.id; cap = sizeof g_state.id; }
          else if (!strcmp(field, "draft")) { dst = g_state.draft; cap = sizeof g_state.draft; }
          else if (!strcmp(field, "log")) { dst = g_state.log; cap = sizeof g_state.log; }
          else if (!strcmp(field, "seq")) { dst = g_state.seq; cap = sizeof g_state.seq; }
          if (!dst) return 0;
          snprintf(dst, cap, "%s", value ? value : "");
          return 1;
      }
      
      const char *ln_level_path(const char *name, Arena *dest) {
          char buf[1200];
          snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s/%s.json", g_state.levels, name ? name : "");
          size_t n = strlen(buf);
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, n + 1);
          memcpy(out, buf, n + 1);
          return out;
      }
      
      const char *ln_read_file(const char *path, Arena *dest) {
          FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
          if (!f) return "";
          fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
          long n = ftell(f);
          fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
          if (n < 0) { fclose(f); return ""; }
          char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, (size_t)n + 1);
          size_t got = fread(buf, 1, (size_t)n, f);
          fclose(f);
          buf[got] = 0;
          return buf;
      }
      
      int ln_write_file(const char *path, const char *text) {
          FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb");
          if (!f) return 0;
          size_t n = strlen(text);
          size_t wrote = fwrite(text, 1, n, f);
          int ok = (wrote == n);
          if (fclose(f) != 0) ok = 0;
          return ok ? 1 : 0;
      }
      
      const char *ln_editor_html(Arena *dest) { return ln_read_file(g_state.editor, dest); }
      
      /* ln_log_event -- append one posted event ({"source":..,"kind":..,"data":..}) to the room's log,
       * injecting its seq. Kept in the host only because the seq counter itself has to outlive a request;
       * the event shape stays whatever the client sent (the C client reads x/y/z/yaw/mode out of `data` by
       * scanning the raw text, so no re-serialisation is needed). */
      int ln_log_event(const char *body) {
          char event[8192];
          const char *payload = (body && body[0] == '{') ? body + 1 : (body ? body : "");
          size_t used = strlen(g_state.log);
          int n = snprintf(event, sizeof event, "%s{\"seq\":%s,%s",
                           used ? "," : "", g_state.seq, payload);
          if (n <= 0) return 0;
          size_t room = sizeof g_state.log - used - 1;
          size_t add = strlen(event);
          if (add > room) add = room;
          memcpy(g_state.log + used, event, add);
          g_state.log[used + add] = 0;
          snprintf(g_state.seq, sizeof g_state.seq, "%d", atoi(g_state.seq) + 1);
          return 1;
      }
      
      const char *ln_session_json(Arena *dest) {
          size_t cap = strlen(g_state.log) + 256;
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);
          snprintf(out, cap, "{\"id\":\"%s\",\"seq\":%s,\"events\":[%s]}",
                   g_state.id, g_state.seq, g_state.log);
          return out;
      }
      
      /* ln_levels_json -- {"levels":[{"name":..,"file":..,"bytes":N},..]} for the editor's level list. */
      const char *ln_levels_json(Arena *dest) {
          size_t cap = 1 << 16, len = 0;
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);
          len += (size_t)snprintf(out + len, cap - len, "{\"levels\":[");
          DIR *d = opendir(g_state.levels);
          int first = 1;
          if (d) {
              struct dirent *e;
              while ((e = readdir(d)) != NULL) {
                  size_t m = strlen(e->d_name);
                  if (m < 6 || strcmp(e->d_name + m - 5, ".json") != 0) continue;
                  char path[2048];
                  snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/%s", g_state.levels, e->d_name);
                  FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
                  long bytes = 0;
                  if (f) { fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END); bytes = ftell(f); fclose(f); }
                  char stem[512];
                  snprintf(stem, sizeof stem, "%.*s", (int)(m - 5), e->d_name);
                  len += (size_t)snprintf(out + len, cap - len,
                                          "%s{\"name\":\"%s\",\"file\":\"levels/%s\",\"bytes\":%ld}",
                                          first ? "" : ",", stem, e->d_name, bytes);
                  first = 0;
              }
              closedir(d);
          }
          snprintf(out + len, cap - len, "]}");
          return out;
      }
      
      int nock_run(Arena *dest);
      
      int main(void) {
          arena_init(&g_arena);
          arena_init(&g_scratch);
      
          const char *repo = getenv("LOCAL_NOCK_REPO");
          snprintf(g_state.repo, sizeof g_state.repo, "%s", (repo && *repo) ? repo : ".");
          const char *levels = getenv("LOCAL_NOCK_LEVELS");
          if (levels && *levels) snprintf(g_state.levels, sizeof g_state.levels, "%s", levels);
          else snprintf(g_state.levels, sizeof g_state.levels, "%s/levels", g_state.repo);
          const char *editor = getenv("LOCAL_NOCK_EDITOR");
          if (editor && *editor) snprintf(g_state.editor, sizeof g_state.editor, "%s", editor);
          else snprintf(g_state.editor, sizeof g_state.editor, "%s/tools/nock_editor.html", g_state.repo);
          snprintf(g_state.seq, sizeof g_state.seq, "0");
      
          return nock_run(&g_arena);
      }

all: build

# Real, deliberate TWO-STAGE bootstrap (2026-08-21, founder: "add it to
# the parena cli"): `parena ci-status` calls into `check()`, the C
# function stdlib/ci/status.prn itself compiles down to (a REAL PARENA
# module, not hand-written C -- see that file's own header comment) --
# but that C doesn't exist until SOME already-built parena has compiled
# it. Stage 1 (.parena-bootstrap) is an ordinary build with the
# ci-status subcommand compiled OUT (PARENA_HAS_CI_STATUS undefined --
# see main.c's own comment on that macro); it exists only to generate
# tools/ci_status_gen.c. Stage 2 (the real, shipped `parena` binary)
# recompiles main.c WITH that macro defined, this time linking the
# freshly-generated module C plus its own real host implementation
# (tools/ci_status_host.c) in. `build`'s own target is still just
# `parena` -- callers never need to know this is two stages under the
# hood.
build: parena

.parena-bootstrap: src/main.c $(OBJ)
  $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o .parena-bootstrap src/main.c $(OBJ)

tools/ci_status_gen.c: .parena-bootstrap stdlib/ci/status.prn
  ./.parena-bootstrap build stdlib/ci/status.prn -o tools/ci_status_gen.c

parena: src/main.c $(OBJ) tools/ci_status_gen.c tools/ci_status_host.c tools/ci_status.h
  $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -DPARENA_HAS_CI_STATUS -I runtime -I tools -include tools/ci_status.h \
    -o parena src/main.c $(OBJ) tools/ci_status_gen.c tools/ci_status_host.c

%.o: %.c
  $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c -o $@ $<

test: tests/test_lexer_parser tests/test_region tests/test_emit
  ./tests/test_lexer_parser
  ./tests/test_region
  ./tests/test_emit

# toolchain under ~/.local/opt/llvm-toolchain, and a sibling ../BRAWLPIT checkout for the C engine).
test-brawlpit: .parena-bootstrap
  bash scripts/test_brawlpit.sh

test-shankpit460: .parena-bootstrap
  bash scripts/test_shankpit460.sh

# Playwright is configured) the real-browser test.

                                     const char **out_type, const char **out_error) {
          /* Real, narrow N-ary extension (2026-08-21, found blocking world.prn's
           * own real `(and a b c)`): `&&`/`||` specifically, not every operator
           * here -- logical AND/OR are genuinely associative, so left-folding
           * `(and a b c)` into `((a && b) && c)` is semantically exact, the
           * same real value C's own left-to-right `&&`/`||` chaining already
           * has. Deliberately NOT generalized to arithmetic/comparison
           * operators too: `(< a b c)` in real Lisp/Scheme means "a<b AND
           * b<c" (a genuine three-way chained comparison), which naive
           * pairwise folding `((a < b) < c)` would silently compute wrong
           * (comparing a real 0/1 int result against c) -- flagged as a
           * real, separate, unstarted gap rather than guessed at here. */
          if (call->child_count > 3 && (strcmp(c_op, "&&") == 0 || strcmp(c_op, "||") == 0)) {
              const char *acc_type = NULL;
              const char *acc = emit_expr(arena, call->children[1], scope, &acc_type, out_error);

              for (size_t i = 2; i < call->child_count; i++) {

                  StrBuf buf;
                  sb_init(&buf);
                  sb_append(&buf, "(");
                  sb_append(&buf, acc);
                  sb_append(&buf, " ");
                  sb_append(&buf, c_op);
                  sb_append(&buf, " ");
                  sb_append(&buf, next);
                  sb_append(&buf, ")");

      /* SDL2 -- built-in, same tier as core (STDLIB.md's own "sdl2" section:
       * "SDL2 is built in... no (import sdl2) line needed"), so its header is
       * unconditionally available here rather than gated behind a feature
       * macro. Real, honest dependency this adds to every build of this
       * runtime, not silently glossed over: any environment building PARENA
       * programs needs libsdl2-dev installed (confirmed present on this box).
       * Harmless for a program that never calls into stdlib/sdl2.prn -- every
       * sdl2_*_impl function below is `static inline`, so an unreferenced one
       * emits no symbol at all, no -lSDL2 needed unless something actually
       * calls one.
       *
       * Real, honest exception carved out here (2026-09-03, kanban priority-queue
       * card PARENA-0001, "smallest vertical slice to make PARENA work with the
       * OS... alpine? debian?"): a headless/embedded/musl-static build target
       * (real, live-checked motivating case -- Alpine's own real SDL2 dev headers
       * are built against musl, not this box's glibc-linked libsdl2-dev, so
       * mixing them fails; a real target with zero SDL2 in its own `.prn` source
       * at all, like `sip/message.prn` or `pentest/pcap.prn`, shouldn't need SDL2
       * headers present just to compile) can define `PARENA_NO_GRAPHICS` before
       * including this header to skip SDL2/SDL2_ttf entirely. Default (undefined)
       * behavior is unchanged -- every existing consumer still gets SDL2
       * unconditionally, exactly as before. */
      #ifndef PARENA_NO_GRAPHICS
      #include <SDL2/SDL.h>
      /* SDL2_ttf -- real text rendering, the concrete next real extension
       * flagged when sdl2.prn's own renderer/draw calls were closed (2026-08-26):
       * "the next real extension once an editor loop actually needs to render
       * text." Same "unconditionally available, harmless if unused" reasoning
       * as SDL2 itself above -- confirmed libsdl2-ttf-dev present on this box. */
      #ifndef PARENA_NO_TTF
      #include <SDL2/SDL_ttf.h>
      #endif /* PARENA_NO_TTF -- define to build against SDL2 only (no SDL2_ttf headers/DLL); the font
              * entry points below become stubs returning -1. Added 2026-10-14 for PELLEGRINO. */
      #endif /* PARENA_NO_GRAPHICS */

       * (always in libc) or SDL2 (already established as "unconditionally available, harmless if

       * (BIG_O/SPIDERBEETLE/etc.'s own scalar game-logic .prn files, which never touch the network at
       * all) have no reason to pull in just to compile. A consumer that DOES want TLS (DEADWEIGHT's

       * live verification -- see sudo-queue/ for the permanent system-wide install). */
      #ifdef PARENA_WITH_TLS

      #include <mbedtls/ssl.h>
      #include <mbedtls/entropy.h>
      #include <mbedtls/ctr_drbg.h>

/* result_unwrap_check / option_unwrap_check -- the real runtime half of
 * VS0's `unwrap` (see emit.c's own `is_call_named(expr, "unwrap")`
 * handling for the full real reasoning): Rust's own well-known
 * `.unwrap()` semantics -- pass through unchanged on Ok/Some, abort
 * with a real stderr message on Err/None, rather than silently
 * dereferencing a NULL `.value` (undefined behavior) or a stale one.
 * Pass-through-by-value (not void) so the call site can chain `.value`
 * straight off the return, evaluating the checked expression exactly
 * once -- the same real reason g_box_helpers' own generated helpers
 * are real functions, not a GNU statement-expression (rejected under
 * this project's own `-pedantic -Werror` build). */
static inline Result result_unwrap_check(Result r) {
    if (!r.tag) {
        fprintf(stderr, "parena: unwrap called on an Err result\n");
        abort();
    }
    return r;
}
static inline Option option_unwrap_check(Option o) {
    if (!o.tag) {
        fprintf(stderr, "parena: unwrap called on a None option\n");
        abort();
    }

    {

            "(defn bump! [(b : &mut Box)] : Unit (set! (get-field b :n) (+ (get-field b :n) 1)))\n"

            "  (cond\n"
            "    ((= x 1) (do (bump! b) (bump! b)))\n"
            "    ((= x 2) (let [y (+ x 1)] (do (bump! b) (set! (get-field b :n) (+ (get-field b :n) y)))))\n"
            "    (true (bump! b))))\n"
            "(defn mid-if! [(b : &mut Box) (x : I32)] : Unit\n"

/* string_concat -- real, minimal `string/concat` implementation
 * (STDLIB.md's own "string" package design), found genuinely missing
 * (not just designed) while getting firefly.prn's own `skip` to
 * actually gcc-compile (it calls `(string/concat "SKIP: " reason
 * dest)`). Allocates a real, arena-backed buffer sized to both inputs'
 * combined length + a null terminator, copies both, returns a real
 * `char *`. Real, honest, narrow scope: exactly two strings + a
 * destination arena, matching the one real call site that surfaced
 * this gap -- not a variadic/N-argument concat. */
static inline char *string_concat(const char *a, const char *b, Arena *dest) {
    size_t la = strlen(a);
    size_t lb = strlen(b);
    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, la + lb + 1);
    memcpy(out, a, la);
    memcpy(out + la, b, lb);
    out[la + lb] = '\0';
    return out;
}

== process api ==
;; lookup-path/env-lookup already establish for "OS interop goes
;; through inline-c".

(module process)
(import string)
(export process-spawn process-kill run-capture run-capture-exit-code ProcessError)

(defenum ProcessError
  (SpawnFailed)
  (KillFailed))

(defn raw-spawn [(path : String @ Region) (arg1 : String @ Region)]
  : I32
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "spawn_detached_impl(path, arg1)")})

(defn raw-kill [(pid : I32)]
  : I32
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "process_kill_impl(pid)")})

;; spawn — fork+exec `path` with exactly one argument, detached (no
;; wait/reap -- the caller owns the returned pid and is expected to
;; `kill` it when done, same contract a test harness starting a fixture
;; server and tearing it down after has). Real, honest, narrow: no PATH
;; search (`path` must be a real, resolvable path, absolute or
;; relative to the calling process's own cwd, matching plain execl's
;; own real semantics -- shell.prn's own `lookup-path` is the tool for
;; PATH resolution, not duplicated here).
(defn process-spawn [(path : String @ :region/scratch) (arg1 : String @ :region/scratch) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result I32 ProcessError) @ Region
  (let [pid (raw-spawn path arg1)]
    (if (< pid 0)
      (Err SpawnFailed)
      (Ok pid))))

;; kill — SIGTERM, not SIGKILL: a real fixture server (like
;; fake_webdriver_server.go, a plain net/http.ListenAndServe) exits
;; cleanly on SIGTERM with Go's own default handling, no forced-kill
;; needed for this real, narrow use case.
(defn process-kill [(pid : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result Unit ProcessError) @ Region
  (if (< (raw-kill pid) 0)
    (Err KillFailed)
    (Ok unit)))

;; run-capture / run-capture-exit-code -- real, general "run a shell command, capture its
;; stdout" pair, added 2026-09-02 for LO/FRAMEWORK_NORTHSTAR.md's own event-sourcing extension
;; (founder real-time: "continue building the framework with jsonl log streaming with mysql psql
;; sqlite etc projectors"): SQL projectors shell out to real DB CLI clients (sqlite3/mysql/psql)
;; rather than binding each one's own native C client library via FFI -- this stdlib's own real,
;; general subprocess-capture primitive underneath, filling in this file's own header comment's
;; already-named "real, separate, future scope: captured stdout/stderr" gap. Real, honest, named
;; limitations (see runtime/parena_runtime.h's own run_capture_impl doc comment for the full
;; reasoning): `cmd` runs through `/bin/sh -c` -- a real shell-injection risk if a caller
;; concatenates untrusted data into it without escaping; stderr is not captured; the real exit
;; code is a SEPARATE call reading back the last real run's own stashed status (a second call,
;; not a second execution -- run-capture itself only ever runs `cmd` once).
(defn run-capture [(cmd : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : String @ Region
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "run_capture_impl(cmd, dest)")})

(defn run-capture-exit-code [] : I32
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "run_capture_last_exit_code_impl()")})

(export file-open file-close path-exists? list-dir is-dir? write-string read-string read-line read-floats FileHandle IoError OpenMode)

(defstruct FileHandle
  (fd : I32))

(defenum IoError
  (NotFound)
  (PermissionDenied)
  (AlreadyExists)
  (Other))

(defenum OpenMode (Read) (Write) (Append))

;; ---- raw syscall primitives -- the only #target bodies in this file,
;; each a single C expression, no boxing. errno is read separately
;; (raw-errno) right after a primitive reports failure, matching real
;; C's own "check errno immediately after the failing call" discipline
;; -- nothing else runs in between at the .prn level either.

(defn raw-open [(path : String @ Region) (mode-tag : I32)]
  : I32
  #target
  {:c (inline-c "raw_open_impl(path, mode_tag)")})
;; Real, small signature change from the original design: open/close/
;; write-string all now take an explicit `dest : Arena @ Region` --
;; needed to box a real Err(IoError) payload (`ensure_box_helper` needs
;; a findable Arena in scope, per emit.c's own comment on Ok/Err/Some's
;; real "no generics, box non-pointer payloads explicitly" scope), the
;; same real reason regex/pcre.prn's is-match/find gained one earlier
;; this session.
(defn file-open [(path : String @ :region/scratch) (mode : OpenMode) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result FileHandle IoError) @ Region
  (let [fd (raw-open path (mode-tag-of mode))]
    (if (< fd 0)
      (Err (errno-to-io-error (raw-errno)))
      (Ok {:fd fd}))))

(defn file-close [(!f : FileHandle @ :region/task) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result Unit IoError) @ Region
  (if (< (raw-close (get-field f :fd)) 0)
    (Err (errno-to-io-error (raw-errno)))
    (Ok unit)))

;; path-exists? -- added 2026-08-26, real gap found porting PITVIPER's

  : Bool

;; list-dir -- added 2026-08-27, real gap found building the editor's
;; own NERDTree-style file-tree sidebar (founder real-time: "we are

(defn raw-list-dir [(path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]

  {:c (inline-c "list_dir_impl(path, dest)")})

(defn list-dir [(path : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Vec String) @ Region
  (let [joined (raw-list-dir path dest)]

== CHANGELOG head ==
## 2026-10-30

- **feat(local-nock): the map editor runs locally, browser and game in one live session.** `make local-nock` (`python3 tools/local_nock.py`) serves `tools/nock_editor.html` and the same edit-session API the native client already speaks (`SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL`, IDUNA `shankpit_edit_sessions.go` shape): level list/read/save, session create, events, working-draft push/fetch. The browser pushes the working level and the game reloads it; the game's box/spawner/avatar events appear in the browser. Saves land in `levels/<name>.json` and are committed (`level(<name>): N walls from local NOCK`, never pushed), with `levels/starter.json` as the first map. `make test-local-nock` (12 checks) covers the HTTP contract including the git commit, invalid levels, long-poll wakeup and 404s. Gaps named: one live room per run, and the event log replays whole instead of honouring `?since` (applied events are idempotent). PARENA port started: `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` (request parsing + response serialisation, emits clean) plus `tools/local_nock.prn`, which parses but is blocked on four verified VS0 gaps (reference params / `match` scrutinees naming an imported defstruct, pointer-typed returns, `set!` on a top-level def), so the Python server stays the runner for now.
- **feat(edit-map): F6 saves a real level JSON, no IDUNA needed.** EDIT MAP's F6 writes the whole working level (source plus every edit) to `var/maps/<name>.json` through the new `level_boxes_save_to_file` (`packages/world/level_boxes.h`), which emits every field the loader parses -- walls/materials, spawners, buggy spawns, lab stations, doors (button subscriptions + script paths included), buttons, nav nodes, characters, exits, zones, edu widgets, brick damage, enclosed/floor tint/next level. Load it back with `--edit-map var/maps/<name>.json` or `--level`. F5's op log stays the live-NOCK streaming format; a successful F6 deletes the stale `.edits.json` so a replay can't apply the same edits twice. `level_boxes_parse_string` now honours `\\ \" \n \t \r` escapes (real escaped JSON, and it fixes Windows door script paths coming back doubled). `make test-level-save`, plus a round-trip of the checked-in `var/lab/lab.json`, the story-doors demo and every `assets/tyler_levels/*.json` export. Not driven in the live client here (no SDL2/display on this box); writer + loader round-trip is what's tested.
- **feat(tools): `leveltool`, headless level JSON utility.** `info` (summary of a map), `check` (load -> save -> load and fail if any parsed field changed shape, plus a stable-writer byte check), `save` (normalize/re-emit) and `new` (an empty level, same defaults as EDIT MAP's new-level path). `map` prints a top-down ASCII view (`#` wall, `S` spawner, `C` character, `E` exit, `z` zone, `D` door, `B` button) so a layout can be eyeballed with no display; `--cell` zooms to a fixed scale (centred on `--center`, else spawner 0) and `--min-height` hides short geometry (a 500-unit LAB floor slab otherwise squashes the plan into a few cells). Walls rasterise their footprint outline, so a long wall crossing the window draws along its whole length. `make leveltool`, `make test-leveltool`, and `make check-levels` which runs `check` over `var/lab/lab.json`, the story-doors demo, `var/zombie/nextown_zombies.json` and every `assets/tyler_levels/*.json`. `--level var/maps/<name>.json` also already plays a locally saved map (both sides must pass the same path).

## 2026-10-16

- **fix(brick): the XPBD rigid-body debris is replaced by a cheap fake** (founder: it was slow, inconsistent, glass worse; "revert, fake it, no piling"). Shot-out cells shed the old flakes again. Cut-off geometry (glass disc, wall section) falls as one chunk with gravity + a seeded tumble, one level probe per chunk per tick, one small bounce, lies flat on the floor or whatever it lands on, then lingers 5 s. Max 32 chunks, no solver/pairs/piling; the dedicated server no longer simulates debris at all. Mass/density (NOCK material) kept as data. Headless tests only; live feel not verified.
- **feat(zombies): pheromone thrower is a real grenade.** `G` lobs a 0.8 kg canister (`packages/simulation/pheromone_grenade.h`: impulse/mass launch speed, ballistic arc, mass-dependent bounce, wall bounce, Coulomb roll to rest, inherits the thrower's velocity). The marker zombies chase rides the canister, so they track it in the air and through each bounce; the thud on landing startles zombies in range. Visuals: tumbling glowing canister with a streak, pulsing ground rings + scent wisps + smell-radius ring when down, G-key READY/cooldown HUD, red diamonds over starving zombies. `make test-pheromone-grenade`. Not seen in the live game.
- **feat(zombies): hunger infighting.** A zombie whose hunger >= 0.70 with the hero out of sense smells the nearest zombie / citizen / Man (up to 135 units), hunts it and bites (16 dmg, feeds it); a bitten zombie fights back; The Men melee zombies within 14 units. Dead victims are permanent corpses. Tuning (rates, radii) is a first pass.


- feat(brick): **physical broken brick + falling disconnected geometry.** Shot-out cells throw mass-carrying shards (brick ~15 kg, density x volume) and any group of cells cut off from the ground/static solids falls as a rigid chunk (shoot a circle out of glass and the disc drops, with a seeded tumble), all on GOLDEN BAND's `grb` XPBD solver via new `packages/simulation/brick_bodies.{h,c}` (shards pile as cubes, slide down ramps via `obb.h`). `brick_fracture.h`: bounded flood-fill detection `bf_detect_detached` (found and fixed a real bug in its own tests: a flood that met an earlier flood's cells wrongly treated itself as cut off), chunk id on the brick wire pad byte, shard queue, per-parent density. Mass configurable per NOCK material (`density` kg/m^3 in `level_boxes.h`; IDUNA migration + Materials screen field). Server and lobby tick the bodies; lobby draws them (glass translucent). New `make test-brick-bodies` / `test-brick-density`; `test-brick-fracture` and `test-brick-world` extended. Bodies are per-client cosmetic (not synced), do not hit players; live visual check not done (scripted input unreliable), headless tests only. README updated.

- fix(windows): real in-phone PELLEGRINO browser on Windows via `scripts/build_pgb_windows.sh` (mingw; stub fallback, cacert.pem shipped). Untested on Windows (CI-built).

- feat(lobby): **GFD phone app is on the cross-game chat bus** (`packages/gfd_chat/gfd_chat.h`, tested by `gfd_chat_test.c`). Messages typed in the phone's GFD terminal post to IDUNA `/api/v1/chat/messages` (channel `shankpit`) under the player's IDUNA display name and are polled back every 3s, so every SHANKPIT GFD phone sees them regardless of game/mode, plus the GFD MUD's `global` chat (shown as `[GFD] name`). Requires signing in via the phone's IDUNA app first (the token is the credential). Verified end to end with two lobby clients plus a simulated MUD post against a fake chat-bus server; NOT yet against the real IDUNA (needs the IDUNA `shankpit` channel deployed). Windows: stubbed no-op. README updated.
- **Phone IDUNA app is live in-game (2026-10-16):** the SHANKPHONE IDUNA tile (zombies/lab/story) now runs the exact same loopback SSO flow as the legacy menu's LOGIN IDUNA button (system browser -> IDUNA hosted login -> 127.0.0.1 token return), polled every frame during play; shows `CODE: BROWSER` while pending, `LINKED: <name>` on success, an error on timeout. Replaces the "use IDUNA.GAME" stub. Pending state verified live under Xvfb; the full token return is untested here (no IDUNA reachable).
- **feat(phone): PELLEGRINO in-phone browser now builds and runs.** `make lobby` links `packages/pellegrino_browser_embed` (mbedTLS + monocypher + embed objects, `PGB_OBJS`, kept out of `LOBBY_SRC`). Verified live under Xvfb `--zombies`: page renders in the phone panel, URL typing navigates, Esc returns to the home grid. Open: mouse, in-game `h3://` check, Windows/CI wiring. README updated.

## 2026-10-16

- ZOMBIES boot now always asks the network for the level NOCK flagged with "Set for ZOMBIES" (baked table stays the offline fallback), instead of ignoring it while LIVE LEVELS is OFF.- fix(edit-map): live-edit X/B now send the box geometry so NOCK removes/adds the same wall; F5 in a live session asks NOCK to save. > The host functions need declarations before use — the generated C's `#target` bodies call `ln_port()` etc. with no prototypes. Fix: the host file should be included/exposed via a header included before, or the generated C should include a host header. Simplest: add prototypes to a header `local_nock_host.h` and compile with `-include`. But cleanest: in local_nock.prn, add a `#include`? PARENA has no include directive; but the emitter supports `#target` with {:c ...}. Option: prepend the prototypes via `-include ../SHANKPIT/tools/local_nock_host.h` at compile time, and keep that in the make target. Alternatively declare the prototypes inside each `#target` body using `(inline-c "extern const char *ln_state_get(const char*, Arena*);")`? That's a statement, can't return value.

CHANGELOG.md

## 2026-10-18

- feat(stdlib/bedrockracers): **BEDROCK RACERS is playable in a browser** (founder real-time: "finish shipping bedrock racers", on top of "MAKE IT NICE VERY TOUGHTFUL VERY DEMURE"). The renderer the last session left unbuilt now builds and runs: a z-buffered perspective rasteriser (`br_3d.prn`; `fill-tri!` split to get under the locals limit) with a bilinear-filtered floor, per-vertex light that reads the dynamic light table (ON FIRE dims the stadium and lights it in flame), the arena shell / towers / car / a stitched-leather Quaffle, four cameras (chase, ball cam, broadcast, title orbit), the HUD (score strip, speed, an air bar, the magnet ring with its carry clock, the ON FIRE chip and banner, an arrow to the ball, the feed, the banners, the Tab board) and the screens (team + bot-skill picker with clicks, pause menu, results with the board and a rematch). `br_host.prn` is the page host (PARENA -> TypeScript -> `br-host.js`, no hand-written JS); `scripts/build_bedrockracers_web.sh` assembles a complete static bundle with `examples/bedrockracers_web/index.html`. Bugs found by looking and fixed: pausing did not freeze the view (the ball kept rolling, the camera glided ~3 s); after a kickoff from the ceiling the camera stayed upside down with its eye outside the arena (half-turn stall in the smoothing, now `vec-toward!` plus a snap on teleports); the overtime and ball-reset banners could never show (`g-banner-t` was never counted down); a carried ball hid the road (the camera now rises over it); the amber floor camouflaged the amber team (slate floor, neutral road). Tests: `tests/br_engine_test.mjs` (92: hygiene, the host's export contract, no G-slot clashes, screens, keys / mouse / pad, camera through wall and ceiling, HUD pixel guards, **a drawn match ends byte-identical to an undrawn one**, frame budget), `tests/br_browser_test.mjs` (33 in headless Chromium at 60 fps), `make test-bedrockracers` runs the lot plus the soak line against the committed `tests/br_soak_baseline.txt` (byte-identical to the one from `d0ac58b`). `tests/br_human_player.mjs` (opt-in, minutes per seed) plays the amber team's first car with keyboard events only and scores against EASY bots reproducibly (seed 1, tick 12940), in 1 of 7 four-minute matches: EASY is not easy for a naive player (not tuned: a design call). Median frame ~8.4 ms in Node. Local play only; no audio, no sign-in or stats yet; street tricks, jukes and car classes not started. The WOTAN page is finished on branch `bedrockracers-page` of the WOTAN repo, not merged (a push to WOTAN main deploys). `stdlib/bedrockracers/README.md` and `HANDOFF.md` say the rest.

- feat(stdlib/bedrockracers): **BEDROCK RACERS: the ball is a Quaffle -- magnet, NBA Street passing, ON FIRE with a dynamic light table, and bots that play it** (founder real-time: "make the ball magnet to the cars or something", "remember its like quidich", "you can add a control for the magnet", "it can even be like basketball like let the ball be thown and passed like NBA street vol 2", "add ON FIRE WITH REALLY DRAMATIC LIGHTING EFFECTS"). THE MAGNET (`br_phys.prn`): a new command button, `in-magnet` (bit 2, value 4, of pend byte 6, so it rides the command quantisation and the replay log like boost; `g-cmd-magnet`; `br-t-cmd` takes a trailing magnet arg). Held, a free ball near the car's CRADLE (17 ahead of the nose, 9 above it) is pulled in (1400 at the cradle fading to nothing at 34, damping the ball's velocity relative to the car; only a ball slower than 1.4x the catch limit is held at all, so a hard shot goes through) and CAUGHT if it reaches the cradle within 9 slower than 170 relative -- faster and it just hits the car as before. Carried, it rides the cradle on the floor, up walls and in flight (a wall pushes it out; torn 8 off the cradle it drops); the carrier's tank does not refill, its speed cap is 90%, and after 5 s it is thrown for it at half pace. Letting go THROWS it (car velocity + 260 along the nose) -- or, with a team-mate holding its magnet within 28 degrees and 280, a PASS led to where that team-mate will be, catchable up to 260 for 1.5 s. 0.7 s re-catch lockout after a throw or a loss; an enemy bump closing faster than 40, or an enemy's body hitting the held ball, knocks it loose (a steal), a team-mate's never does. A carried ball up a shaft is a dunk for the holder's team (`g-goal-dunk`), into your own tower an own goal; a cradle over the goal line holds nothing; kickoff, goal, respawn, end of match and a car leaving free the ball; a catch or a steal is always a fresh touch, so a pass that leads to a goal is the assist. New car fields `in-magnet`, `nocatch`, `catches`, `passes`, `steals`, `throws`, ball fields `holder`, `hold-t`, `pass-from`, `pass-t` (appended, no word moved). ON FIRE (new `br_fire.prn`, sim, deterministic): a car in on two of its team's goals in a row (scorer or assist, with no goal in between that it was not in on) burns for 45 s of play -- tank stays full even while carrying, throws 35% faster (351), magnet reaches 51, the ball it holds or throws burns, a burning pass gets the same 35% on the catch limit -- and goes out when another team scores, on a steal, an own goal, after 45 s or when it leaves; scoring while burning winds it back to 45 s; feed lines and a fire banner of its own. THE LIGHTS (new `br_fx.prn`, fx-rand only, never read by the sim): a 256-slot particle ring (flames off burning cars and the burning ball, boost plumes, dust off the dirt, 40 team-coloured sparks out of the tower on a goal) and a DYNAMIC LIGHT TABLE at 0x029000 rebuilt every tick -- up to 16 point lights {x y z, r g b, intensity, radius}: the goal flash (white-hot fading into the scorer's colour over ~1 s, 900 radius), the burning ball, burning cars with fx-rand flicker, boost plumes -- plus `drama` (0..1, jumps when someone catches fire or scores) and `flash` scalars; exports `br-lights-addr`, `br-light-count`, `br-drama`, `br-flash`, `br-parts-addr`, `br-part-live`. `ruleset` 1 -> 3. THE BOTS (`br_ai.prn`): three bot strategies were built on this engine and judged on HELD-OUT seeds 7-18 (none tuned there), level 3: a chaser (2.69 goals/min, 17 completed passes, 1945 steals), a wall-runner/dunker (2.30, 16 passes) and NBA Street team play (1.90, 76 passes). The team-play brain ships, with the chaser's trigger transplanted in: the carrier runs at the commander's target tower and passes first (to a team-mate nearer the tower, open, clear lane, who calls for it by holding its magnet; the receiver holds its line so the physics' lead holds), the two off the ball run to open space either side, one chaser a team catches a loose ball at a speed the magnet can hold, the nearest non-keeper presses the enemy carrier while another cuts its outlet, and the keeper holds the line from its corner. The shot trigger now flies the release at the physics' own 8 ms step (`what-if-fine`; a sharp HARD eye also reads the lane for cars in the way) instead of the planner's 32 ms step: of 278 throws 104 scored and 92 were passes caught (on the coarse step: 76 of 344 scored, 168 came to nothing). `pick-target-tower` rolls `ai-rand`, not the sim's dice. Tried and dropped: the wall-runner's keeper parked in the mouth of the corner (seeds 7-30, level 3 own goals rose from 1 in 229 to 13 in 228). Held-out soak (`node tests/br_bot_soak.mjs <wasm> 12 3 15000 7`): level 3 2.32 goals/min (109 in 47 min; 0.04 at the base), 0 own goals, 1556 catches, 278 throws, 91 completed passes, 31 assists, 1261 steals, ON FIRE 15 times, every one of the 12 cars scoring (2 to 15 each); level 1 (seeds 7-12) 1.04/min, 2 own goals in 25, 33 passes, 550 steals; level 3 against level 1 head to head (seeds 7-12, sides swapped) 73-24. Over 48 more fresh seeds (31-78): level 3 2.25/min (3.0% own goals, 371 passes), level 2 1.51 (5.2%), level 1 1.03 (5.1%). New test exports `br-t-assign` (re-assign one car a level's genome) and `br-t-whatif-fine`. Tests: `tests/br_physics_test.mjs` 21/21 (with the magnet off nothing changed), new `tests/br_magnet_test.mjs` 37/37 (catch / fumble / carry / throw / led pass / steals / clock / dunk / own goal / assist / resets, and a replay fuzz: two humans pressing random buttons, magnet included, against ten bots, replayed from the command log alone into a fresh module, same state), new `tests/br_fire_test.mjs` 40/40 (every way it lights and goes out, the lights and particles, and a fire match identical twice with the fx dice reseeded changing only the fx); the soak run twice gives byte-identical output; the module still has 0 imports, no allocator, fixed 8 MB. Not built yet: the renderer -- nothing draws the light table, the particles or the fire yet -- and the page: no key or button is bound to the magnet, so humans cannot play it in a browser; no HUD. Dunks stay rare (a thrown ball up the corner almost always goes first), and the soak's `strikes_on_target` / `plan_coverage` still measure the old shot planner, not the magnet game.
- feat(stdlib/bedrockracers): **BEDROCK RACERS vehicle physics pass** (founder real-time: "make sure we have nice vehicle physics"). `br_phys.prn`: the car steers first and then the tyres decide where the velocity goes, so it has real slip -- a friction-limited lateral grip (concrete 320, dirt 125, walls/ceiling 280) that tracks below the limit and drifts past it, with the slide scrubbing speed (it used to turn on rails, slip angle always 0); the yaw rate builds up over a few substeps, fades near a standstill and reverses when reversing (a parked car used to spin in place at 3 rad/s); the fans catch a car only belly-down (a car landing on its roof used to snap 150 degrees upright in five ticks), a turtled car scrapes to a stop and tips itself back over in about a second unless the player rolls it; the ball's rolling resistance acts along the surface only and is far lighter (it used to lose 63% of its speed every 1.8 s and could not reach a wall from midfield -- a ball rolled at 250 now climbs the wall to 75). Unchanged: air control, lift, boost, wall-to-ceiling driving. New `tests/br_physics_test.mjs` (21 checks; 9 fail on the previous engine). Bot soak, 6 seeds x 4 min: touches and ball speed unchanged within noise, still 0 goals (the bots' strike accuracy, not the physics, is next).

          "name": "testmap", "width": 40, "height": 20, "depth": 40,
          "ground_plane_enabled": True, "ground_plane_squares": 4,
          "materials": [{"name": "brick", "shader_name": "standard", "specular": 0.04,
                         "shininess": 6, "friction": 0.3}],
          "walls": [{"x": 0, "y": 2, "z": 0, "sx": 8, "sy": 4, "sz": 2,
                     "r": 0.6, "g": 0.6, "b": 0.65, "friction": 0.8, "material": "brick"}],
          "spawners": [{"id": 1, "x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 4, "yaw": 180, "team": -1}],
      }
      
      
      def call(base, method, path, body=None):
          data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
          req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=data, method=method,
                                       headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
          try:
              with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as r:
                  return r.status, r.read()
          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
              return e.code, e.read()
      
      
      def json_call(base, method, path, body=None):
          status, raw = call(base, method, path, body)
          return status, (json.loads(raw) if raw else None)
      
      
      def main():
          repo = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="local_nock_repo_")
          subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q"], cwd=repo, check=True)
          subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "config", "user.name", "local nock test"], check=True)
          subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "config", "user.email", "local-nock@localhost"], check=True)
      
          server = local_nock.build_server(port=0, levels_dir=os.path.join(repo, "levels"),
                                           repo=repo, commit=True, verbose=False)
          port = server.server_address[1]
          base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
          threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
          ok = 0
      
          try:
              # 1. the editor page is served
              status, raw = call(base, "GET", "/")
              assert status == 200 and b"local NOCK" in raw and b"canvas" in raw, "editor page"
              print("PASS editor page served")
              ok += 1
      
              # 2. an empty level list, then save a level: file on disk + git commit
              status, doc = json_call(base, "GET", "/api/levels")
              assert status == 200 and doc["levels"] == [], "empty listing"
              status, res = json_call(base, "PUT", "/api/levels/testmap", LEVEL)
              assert status == 200 and res["git"]["committed"] is True, f"save+commit: {res}"
              assert res["git"]["commit"], "commit hash"
              path = os.path.join(repo, "levels", "testmap.json")
              assert os.path.isfile(path), "level file written"
              log = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "log", "--oneline"], capture_output=True,
                                   text=True).stdout
              assert "level(testmap)" in log, f"git log: {log!r}"
              print("PASS save writes levels/testmap.json and commits it")
              ok += 1
      
              # 3. list + read back through the API (what the editor/browser does)
              status, doc = json_call(base, "GET", "/api/levels")
              assert doc["levels"][0]["name"] == "testmap" and doc["levels"][0]["walls"] == 1
              status, raw = call(base, "GET", "/api/levels/testmap")
              assert status == 200 and json.loads(raw)["walls"][0]["sx"] == 8
              print("PASS level listing and read-back")
              ok += 1
      
              # 4. saving the same content again is not a new commit
              status, res = json_call(base, "PUT", "/api/levels/testmap", LEVEL)
              assert status == 200 and res["git"]["committed"] is False
              print("PASS identical save does not create an empty commit")
              ok += 1
      
              # 5. invalid levels are refused, nothing written
              status, res = json_call(base, "PUT", "/api/levels/broken", {"nope": 1})
              assert status == 400 and "walls" in res["error"]
              assert not os.path.exists(os.path.join(repo, "levels", "broken.json"))
              status, res = json_call(base, "PUT", "/api/levels/bad%20name", LEVEL)
              assert status == 400
              print("PASS invalid levels rejected (missing walls, bad name)")
              ok += 1
      
              # 6. session create -- 32 hex chars, the shape edit_sync_create checks for
              status, sess = json_call(base, "POST", "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions",
                                       {"level_id": 0, "level_name": "testmap"})
              assert status == 201 and len(sess["id"]) == 32, sess
              sid = sess["id"]
              print("PASS session create returns a 32-hex id")
              ok += 1
      
              # 7. the native client's own event shapes (source shankpit) come back on poll
              for kind, data in (("hello", {"client": "shankpit"}),
                                 ("avatar", {"x": 1.5, "y": 1, "z": 2.5, "yaw": 90, "pitch": 0}),
                                 ("spawner", {"x": 3, "y": 1, "z": 4, "yaw": 45}),
                                 ("box_add", {"id": 100001, "x": 5, "y": 2, "z": 5,
                                              "sx": 4, "sy": 4, "sz": 4}),
                                 ("save", {})):
                  status, _ = json_call(base, "POST", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/events",
                                        {"source": "shankpit", "kind": kind, "data": data})
                  assert status == 200, kind
              status, snap = json_call(base, "GET",
                                       f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}?since=0&wait=0")
              kinds = [e["kind"] for e in snap["events"]]
              assert kinds == ["hello", "avatar", "spawner", "box_add", "save"], kinds
              assert snap["seq"] == 5
              status, snap = json_call(base, "GET",
                                       f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}?since=4&wait=0")
              assert [e["kind"] for e in snap["events"]] == ["save"], "since filter"
              print("PASS events post/poll with since filtering")
              ok += 1
      
              # 8. unknown event kind and source are rejected (a room is not a message bus)
              status, res = json_call(base, "POST", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/events",
                                      {"source": "nock", "kind": "rm -rf", "data": {}})
              assert status == 400
              print("PASS unknown event kinds rejected")
              ok += 1
      
              # 9. the browser pushes a working draft; the client fetches it (live reload path)
              draft = dict(LEVEL)
              draft["walls"] = LEVEL["walls"] + [{"x": 4, "y": 2, "z": 4, "sx": 2, "sy": 2, "sz": 2}]
              status, res = json_call(base, "PUT", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/level", draft)
              assert status == 200 and res["rev"] == 1, res
              status, raw = call(base, "GET", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/level")
              served = json.loads(raw)
              assert status == 200 and len(served["walls"]) == 2, served
              status, res = json_call(base, "PUT", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid}/level", draft)
              assert res["rev"] == 2
              print("PASS working draft push/fetch (browser -> game live reload)")
              ok += 1
      
              # 10. a session with no draft falls back to its saved level, then 404s when absent
              status, sess2 = json_call(base, "POST", "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions",
                                        {"level_id": 0, "level_name": "testmap"})
              status, raw = call(base, "GET", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sess2['id']}/level")
              assert status == 200 and len(json.loads(raw)["walls"]) == 1, "saved-level fallback"
              status, sess3 = json_call(base, "POST", "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions",
                                        {"level_id": 0, "level_name": "no-such-map"})
              status, res = json_call(base, "GET", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sess3['id']}/level")
              assert status == 404
              print("PASS level fetch falls back to the saved file, 404 when there is none")
              ok += 1
      
              # 11. long-poll returns promptly once an event lands
              status, sess4 = json_call(base, "POST", "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions",
                                        {"level_id": 0, "level_name": "testmap"})
              sid4 = sess4["id"]
              result = {}
      
              def poll():
                  result["r"] = json_call(base, "GET",
                                          f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid4}?since=0&wait=10")
      
              t = threading.Thread(target=poll, daemon=True)
              t.start()
              json_call(base, "POST", f"/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/{sid4}/events",
                        {"source": "nock", "kind": "hello", "data": {"client": "nock"}})
              t.join(timeout=5)
              status, snap = result["r"]
              assert status == 200 and [e["kind"] for e in snap["events"]] == ["hello"]
              print("PASS long-poll wakes on a new event")
              ok += 1
      
              # 12. unknown session ids are 404 (the client treats that as 'session lost')
              status, _ = json_call(base, "GET", "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/" + "0" * 32 + "?since=0")
              assert status == 404
              print("PASS unknown session is 404")
              ok += 1
      
          finally:
              server.shutdown()
              server.server_close()
      
          print(f"\nlocal_nock ok ({ok} checks)")
          return 0
      
      
      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(main())

 * assumed away: tcp_read_impl below reads until the peer closes the
 * connection or a read() error, the same one-shot shape
 * raw_read_all_impl above already uses for files. That is CORRECT for
 * a server that closes after responding (HTTP/1.0-style, or HTTP/1.1
 * with a `Connection: close` request header -- which is exactly why
 * net/http.prn's own request builder sends one) and WRONG for a
 * keep-alive connection the peer intends to reuse -- reading would
 * simply block forever waiting for an EOF that never comes. No
 * Content-Length-aware early stop or chunked-encoding support exists
 * yet; a real future gap, not this pass's scope. */
static inline int tcp_connect_impl(const char *host, int port) {
    struct addrinfo hints, *res, *rp;
    memset(&hints, 0, sizeof hints);
    hints.ai_family = AF_UNSPEC;
    hints.ai_socktype = SOCK_STREAM;
    char portstr[16];
    snprintf(portstr, sizeof portstr, "%d", port);
    if (getaddrinfo(host, portstr, &hints, &res) != 0) return -1;
    int fd = -1;
    for (rp = res; rp != NULL; rp = rp->ai_next) {
        fd = socket(rp->ai_family, rp->ai_socktype, rp->ai_protocol);
        if (fd < 0) continue;
        if (connect(fd, rp->ai_addr, rp->ai_addrlen) == 0) break;
        close(fd);
        fd = -1;
    }
    freeaddrinfo(res);
    return fd;
}

 * the "still open" section) for why the sender's address is an
 * out-parameter here instead of part of a Result tuple, and for the
 * real, accepted zero-length-datagram-vs-error ambiguity this leaves. */
static inline char *udp_recv_from_impl(int fd, Arena *dest, char **out_host, int *out_port) {
    char buf[65536];
    struct sockaddr_in src;
    socklen_t src_len = sizeof src;
    ssize_t n = recvfrom(fd, buf, sizeof buf, 0, (struct sockaddr *)&src, &src_len);
    if (n < 0) return NULL;
    char ipbuf[INET_ADDRSTRLEN];
    inet_ntop(AF_INET, &src.sin_addr, ipbuf, sizeof ipbuf);
    char *host_out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, strlen(ipbuf) + 1);
    strcpy(host_out, ipbuf);
    *out_host = host_out;
    *out_port = ntohs(src.sin_port);
    char *data_out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, (size_t)n + 1);
    memcpy(data_out, buf, (size_t)n);
    data_out[n] = '\0';
    return data_out;
}

> Let's look at tcp_read_impl body first.

The GET hangs are a real runtime bug: `tcp_read_impl` reads until EOF or `Content-Length`, so a bodyless GET never completes. Fixing the HTTP framing in the runtime.

**🛠 Run Terminal Command**

```json

  "command": "cd /content/MONOREPO/PARENA\ngrep -n \"static inline char \\*tcp_read_impl\" runtime/parena_runtime.h\nsed -n '/static inline char \\*tcp_read_impl/,/^}/p' runtime/parena_runtime.h",
  "process_type": "SYNC",
  "timeout_seconds": 60

```

```
2125:static inline char *tcp_read_impl(int fd, Arena *dest) {
static inline char *tcp_read_impl(int fd, Arena *dest) {
    size_t cap = 4096;
    size_t len = 0;
    char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);
    long content_length = -1; /* -1 = not yet known (boundary not seen, or no Content-Length header) */
    size_t header_end = 0;
    for (;;) {
        if (content_length >= 0 && len >= header_end + (size_t)content_length) break;
        if (len + 4096 > cap) {
            size_t new_cap = cap + 4096;
            char *grown = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, new_cap);
            memcpy(grown, buf, len);
            buf = grown;
            cap = new_cap;
        }
        struct pollfd pfd;
        pfd.fd = fd;
        pfd.events = POLLIN;
        int pr = poll(&pfd, 1, 30000);
        if (pr <= 0) break; /* timeout or poll error -- return whatever's been read so far */
        ssize_t n = read(fd, buf + len, 4096);
        if (n <= 0) break;
        len += (size_t)n;
        if (content_length < 0) {
            long cl = find_body_length_from_headers(buf, len, &header_end);
            if (cl >= 0) content_length = cl;
            /* cl == -2 (boundary seen, no real Content-Length): keep the
               original read-until-EOF/timeout behavior. cl == -1
               (boundary not seen yet): keep reading. */
        }
    }
    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, len + 1);
    memcpy(out, buf, len);
    out[len] = '\0';
    return out;
}

```

> _Reasoning_
> The bug: when header boundary is seen but no Content-Length (cl == -2), it keeps reading until EOF. Correct HTTP behavior: for a request with no Content-Length, the body is empty, so stop at header_end. Add: if boundary seen and no content length → break.
> 
> Let me patch: introduce a flag `headers_done` and if boundary seen with cl == -2, break immediately.
> 
> Modify:
> ```c
>         if (content_length < 0) {
>             long cl = find_body_length_from_headers(buf, len, &header_end);
>             if (cl >= 0) content_length = cl;
>             else if (cl == -2) break; /* header block complete, no body */
>         }
> ```
> That's the minimal fix. Then rebuild, smoke test GET paths, then docs/commit.

A 3+-operand comparison is still a named failure rather than a silently wrong pairwise fold: a real chained `(< a b c)` would have to evaluate its shared middle operand twice, and expression position has no statement slot to hoist a temp into.\n  - **`set!` on a top-level `(def ...)`** assigns the real C global (`process_defs` already emits it as a `static` variable and binds it into `g_globals`), which is what makes server-style mutable state expressible without a hand-written C host.\n  - **`print`/`println` now exist** in `runtime/parena_runtime.h`. The emitter had been emitting `println(...)` for a call with no runtime declaration and no builtin behind it at all (so `parena build` succeeded and only gcc rejected the file).\n  - **`&` on an already-pointer-typed value passes the pointer**, at all three call-site sites (emit_call's argument loop, the `((expr) args)` loop, and emit_expr's single-token `&x`). A match-bound `Ok` payload is tracked as `T *` because the runtime boxes it behind `.value`, so `(tcp-accept &!listener dest)` used to emit a real `void **` against a `TcpListener *` parameter.\n  - Tests: `tests/test_emit.c` grew positive coverage for each (fold order, unary `-`, global assignment, `println`, payload `&`) plus the negative chained-comparison case -- 365 passing. `runtime/parena_runtime.h`'s `tcp_read_impl` also stopped blocking on bodyless requests: a complete header block with no `Content-Length` is now the whole message (RFC 7230 3.3.3) instead of read-until-EOF, which is why every GET to a PARENA HTTP server used to hang until the client timed out.\n- **feat(net): `stdlib/net/http_server.prn` is complete** -- request parsing (method/path/body, query stripped), case-insensitive header lookup over real header starts only, and response serialisation with `Content-Length`/`Connection: close`, all building response strings with no socket or session decisions of their own.\n\n## 2026-10-21",

## The emitter gaps, fixed at the source

Each one was found by actually building the NOCK server and compiling the generated C with `-std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror`, not by trusting `parena build`'s exit code:

| Workaround I had to write | Real fix |
|---|---|
| Nest every sum pairwise, `(+ .. (+ .. ..))` | **Variadic operators left-fold.** `(+ a b c)` → `((a + b) + c)`; `-`/`/`/`%`/bitwise/shift too, plus unary `(- x)`. `(< a b c)` still fails, deliberately, with a message explaining why: a true chained comparison would evaluate its middle operand twice and there's no statement slot to hoist a temp into in expression position. |
| Route session state through `ln_state_*` host accessors | **`set!` on a top-level `(def ...)`** assigns the real C global. |
| (never worked at all) | **`print`/`println` added to `parena_runtime.h`.** The emitter had been emitting `println(...)` calls into nothing — `parena build` succeeded, gcc rejected the file. |
| Hand the listener around as a local instead of a parameter | **`&` on an already-pointer value passes the pointer.** A match-bound `Ok` payload is tracked as `T *` (the runtime boxes behind `.value`), so `&!listener` was emitting a real `void **` against `TcpListener *`. Fixed at all three argument sites. |

Plus one runtime bug the port exposed: `tcp_read_impl` treated "headers complete, no `Content-Length`" as read-until-EOF, so **every bodyless GET hung** until the client timed out (RFC 7230 §3.3.3 says that request has an empty body). It now stops at the header block.

`stdlib/net/http_server.prn` was also incomplete — it exported `find-sub`/`header-value`/`path-only`/`body-of` without defining them. Now it has all of them (real recursion, ASCII case folding for header names, CRLF and bare-LF body framing).

## The payoff: the NOCK server runs in PARENA

`tools/local_nock.prn` emits, links, and serves. Verified live over loopback against a throwaway git repo:

- `GET /api/levels` → `{"levels":[{"name":"starter",...}]}`
- `PUT /api/levels/smoke` → `{"committed":true}` and a real commit `level(smoke) from local NOCK`
- level read-back, session create (`32` hex), event post + read-back with `seq`, draft push/fetch, `/` serving the 17 KB editor page, 404
- `make local-nock-parena` builds and runs it (host prototypes via `-include`, matching PARENA's own `ci_status.h` pattern)

## Checks run

- `tests/test_emit.c` → **365 passed, 0 failed** (new coverage for fold order, unary minus, global assignment, `println`, payload `&`, and the chained-comparison negative case)
- `test_lexer_parser` → 35/35, `test_region` → 8/8
- generated C for the 5-file server build compiles clean under `-Werror`
- the binary builds clean and the HTTP checks above all pass

## Honest limits

- The **Python runner is still the complete one**: the PARENA port doesn't yet filter events by `?since`, validate event kinds, fall back to the saved level when a session has no draft, or bump the draft revision. That's named in `mk/local_nock.mk` and the `.prn` header rather than papered over — and it's now ordinary exchange logic, not compiler work.
- Session state still lives in the C host; with `set!` on globals working, moving it into PARENA is a small follow-up.
- Nothing was driven from the lobby or a browser here (no SDL2/display, no Chrome), so the in-game join and the canvas editor are still covered at the HTTP-contract level only.
