      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """local_nock.py -- dependency-free local stand-in for the IDUNA NOCK map tooling.
      
      SHANKPIT's in-game editor already speaks a small HTTP contract for "live editing sessions"
      (packages/world/edit_sync.h <-> IDUNA/internal/http/handlers/shankpit_edit_sessions.go). This
      serves that same contract locally, so the cloud tools being unreachable stops nothing:
      
        * the browser editor here and the native client join the SAME session, so an edit made in either
          place shows up in the other (the client pushes avatar/spawner/box events and reloads the working
          level when the browser posts a "level" event);
        * levels are plain JSON files in levels/, one per map -- maps are code, reviewable and diffable;
        * every save is git add + git commit (no push: that's still a deliberate human step).
      
        python3 tools/local_nock.py --port 8787
        # browser: http://127.0.0.1:8787
        # game (join the session id the browser shows, or start one and paste it in):
        SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions \
          ./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map levels/starter.json --edit-live
      
      Wire contract (matches the Go handler, which the C client is written against):
        GET  /                                        browser editor
        GET  /api/levels                              {"levels":[{name,walls,bytes,...}]}
        GET  /api/levels/<name>                       one level (native export JSON)
        PUT  /api/levels/<name>                       save to levels/<name>.json (+ git commit)
        POST /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions           {"id":"<32 hex>","level_id":N,"level_name":"..","seq":0}
        GET  /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>?since=N&wait=S   long-poll {"seq":N,"events":[...]}
        POST /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>/events          {"source","kind","data"}
        PUT  /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>/level           working draft (browser pushes)
        GET  /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>/level           the native export the client loads
      
      Sessions live in memory only (an editing room, not a record), exactly like IDUNA's: a restart ends
      the room and both sides make a new one. Saving is what makes a level durable.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import argparse
      import json
      import os
      import re
      import secrets
      import subprocess
      import sys
      import threading
      import time
      from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
      from urllib.parse import unquote, parse_qs, urlparse
      
      SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")
      SESSION_PREFIX = "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions"
      LEVELS_PREFIX = "/api/levels"
      MAX_BODY = 4 << 20          # a whole level draft; IDUNA's cap for the same reason
      MAX_EVENTS = 2000
      MAX_WAIT = 25
      EVENT_KINDS = {
          "spawner", "avatar", "spawn_mode", "teleport",
          "box_add", "box_move", "box_size", "box_del", "hello", "level", "save",
      }
      HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
      
      
      def validate_level(doc):
          """The minimum a level must have to be usable: an object with a walls array of boxes."""
          if not isinstance(doc, dict):
              raise ValueError("level must be a JSON object")
          walls = doc.get("walls")
          if not isinstance(walls, list):
              raise ValueError('level needs a "walls" array')
          for i, w in enumerate(walls):
              if not isinstance(w, dict):
                  raise ValueError(f"wall {i} is not an object")
              missing = [k for k in ("x", "y", "z", "sx", "sy", "sz") if k not in w]
              if missing:
                  raise ValueError(f"wall {i} is missing {', '.join(missing)}")
          return doc
      
      
      class Session:
          """One live editing room: an append-only event log plus the browser's latest working draft."""
      
          def __init__(self, sid, level_id, level_name):
              self.id = sid
              self.level_id = level_id
              self.level_name = level_name
              self.events = []
              self.next_seq = 1
              self.draft = None
              self.draft_rev = 0
              self.created = self.touched = time.time()
              self.cond = threading.Condition()
      
          def snapshot(self, since):
              events = [e for e in self.events if e["seq"] > since]
              return {
                  "id": self.id,
                  "level_id": self.level_id,
                  "level_name": self.level_name,
                  "seq": self.next_seq - 1,
                  "events": events,
                  "level_rev": self.draft_rev,
              }
      
          def post(self, source, kind, data):
              with self.cond:
                  event = {"seq": self.next_seq, "source": source, "kind": kind, "data": data}
                  self.next_seq += 1
                  self.events.append(event)
                  if len(self.events) > MAX_EVENTS:
                      del self.events[:-MAX_EVENTS]
                  self.touched = time.time()
                  self.cond.notify_all()
                  return event
      
          def poll(self, since, wait):
              deadline = time.time() + wait
              with self.cond:
                  while self.next_seq - 1 <= since and wait > 0 and time.time() < deadline:
                      self.cond.wait(max(0.0, deadline - time.time()))
                  self.touched = time.time()
                  return self.snapshot(since)
      
      
      class LevelStore:
          """Levels as files under levels/ -- git-tracked, one JSON per map, saved by committing."""
      
          def __init__(self, levels_dir, repo, commit=True):
              self.levels_dir = levels_dir
              self.repo = repo
              self.commit = commit
      
          def path(self, name):
              return os.path.join(self.levels_dir, name + ".json")
      
          def names(self):
              if not os.path.isdir(self.levels_dir):
                  return []
              return sorted(fn[:-5] for fn in os.listdir(self.levels_dir)
                            if fn.endswith(".json") and SLUG_RE.match(fn[:-5]))
      
          def listing(self):
              out = []
              for name in self.names():
                  p = self.path(name)
                  try:
                      with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                          doc = json.load(f)
                  except (OSError, ValueError):
                      continue
                  walls = doc.get("walls") if isinstance(doc, dict) else None
                  out.append({
                      "name": name,
                      "file": os.path.relpath(p, self.repo),
                      "walls": len(walls) if isinstance(walls, list) else 0,
                      "bytes": os.path.getsize(p),
                  })
              return out
      
          def read(self, name):
              p = self.path(name)
              if not os.path.isfile(p):
                  return None
              with open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                  return f.read()
      
          def write(self, name, doc):
              validate_level(doc)
              os.makedirs(self.levels_dir, exist_ok=True)
              p = self.path(name)
              tmp = p + ".tmp"
              with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                  f.write(json.dumps(doc, indent=1) + "\n")
              os.replace(tmp, p)
              return {"ok": True, "file": os.path.relpath(p, self.repo), "git": self._commit(p, name, doc)}
      
          def _commit(self, path, name, doc):
              if not self.commit:
                  return {"committed": False, "detail": "commits disabled (--no-commit)"}
              rel = os.path.relpath(path, self.repo)
              walls = len(doc.get("walls") or [])
              msg = f"level({name}): {walls} wall{'s' if walls != 1 else ''} from local NOCK"
              try:
                  add = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.repo, "add", "--", rel],
                                       capture_output=True, text=True)
                  if add.returncode != 0:
                      return {"committed": False, "detail": (add.stderr or add.stdout).strip()[:400]}
                  status = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.repo, "status", "--porcelain", "--", rel],
                                          capture_output=True, text=True)
                  if not status.stdout.strip():
                      return {"committed": False, "detail": "no changes to commit"}
                  c = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.repo, "commit", "-m", msg, "--", rel],
                                     capture_output=True, text=True)
                  if c.returncode != 0:
                      detail = (c.stderr or c.stdout).strip()[:400]
                      return {"committed": False, "detail": detail or "commit failed"}
                  head = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.repo, "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"],
                                        capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
                  return {"committed": True, "commit": head, "message": msg}
              except FileNotFoundError:
                  return {"committed": False, "detail": "git not found"}
      
      
      class State:
          def __init__(self, store, editor_html, verbose=False):
              self.store = store
              self.editor_html = editor_html
              self.sessions = {}
              self.lock = threading.Lock()
              self.verbose = verbose
      
          def create_session(self, level_id, level_name):
              sid = secrets.token_hex(16)
              s = Session(sid, level_id, level_name)
              with self.lock:
                  self.sessions[sid] = s
              return s
      
          def get_session(self, sid):
              with self.lock:
                  return self.sessions.get(sid)
      
      
      class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
          server_version = "local-nock/1.0"
      
          # -- plumbing -------------------------------------------------------------------------
          def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
              if self.server.state.verbose:
                  sys.stderr.write("  %s\n" % (fmt % args))
      
          def _send(self, status, body, ctype="application/json"):
              if isinstance(body, str):
                  body = body.encode("utf-8")
              self.send_response(status)
              self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
              self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
              self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
              self.end_headers()
              try:
                  self.wfile.write(body)
              except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
                  pass
      
          def _json(self, status, obj):
              self._send(status, json.dumps(obj))
      
          def _error(self, status, msg):
              self._json(status, {"error": msg})
      
          def _body(self):
              try:
                  n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
              except ValueError:
                  n = 0
              if n <= 0:
                  return {}
              if n > MAX_BODY:
                  raise ValueError("body too large")
              raw = self.rfile.read(n)
              return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8")) if raw else {}
      
          def _session_route(self, path):
              """Returns (id, tail) for /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>[/tail], else (None, None)."""
              if not path.startswith(SESSION_PREFIX + "/"):
                  return None, None
              rest = path[len(SESSION_PREFIX) + 1:]
              sid, _, tail = rest.partition("/")
              return sid, tail
      
          # -- GET ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
          def do_GET(self):
              u = urlparse(self.path)
              path = u.path
              st = self.server.state
      
              if path in ("/", "/editor.html"):
                  return self._send(200, st.editor_html, "text/html; charset=utf-8")
      
              if path == "/api/local-nock":
                  return self._json(200, {
                      "levels_dir": os.path.relpath(st.store.levels_dir, st.store.repo),
                      "sessions": len(st.sessions),
                      "commit": st.store.commit,
                  })
      
              if path == LEVELS_PREFIX:
                  return self._json(200, {"levels": st.store.listing()})
      
              if path.startswith(LEVELS_PREFIX + "/"):
                  name = unquote(path[len(LEVELS_PREFIX) + 1:])
                  if not SLUG_RE.match(name):
                      return self._error(400, "bad level name")
                  text = st.store.read(name)
                  if text is None:
                      return self._error(404, "no such level")
                  return self._send(200, text)
      
              sid, tail = self._session_route(path)
              if sid is not None:
                  s = st.get_session(sid)
                  if s is None:
                      return self._error(404, "no such edit session (expired, or this server restarted)")
                  if tail == "":
                      q = parse_qs(u.query)
                      try:
                          since = int(q.get("since", ["0"])[0])
                          wait = min(int(q.get("wait", ["0"])[0]), MAX_WAIT)
                      except ValueError:
                          return self._error(400, "since/wait must be integers")
                      return self._json(200, s.poll(since, wait))
                  if tail == "level":
                      if s.draft is not None:
                          return self._send(200, json.dumps(s.draft))
                      text = st.store.read(s.level_name) if SLUG_RE.match(s.level_name or "") else None
                      if text is None:
                          return self._error(404, "this session has no level yet (open one in the editor)")
                      return self._send(200, text)
                  return self._error(404, "unknown session route")
      
              return self._error(404, "not found")
      
          # -- POST -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          def do_POST(self):
              path = urlparse(self.path).path
              st = self.server.state
      
              if path == SESSION_PREFIX:
                  try:
                      body = self._body()
                  except ValueError as e:
                      return self._error(400, str(e))
                  name = str(body.get("level_name") or "")[:120]
                  try:
                      level_id = int(body.get("level_id") or 0)
                  except (TypeError, ValueError):
                      level_id = 0
                  s = st.create_session(level_id, name)
                  return self._json(201, {"id": s.id, "level_id": s.level_id,
                                          "level_name": s.level_name, "seq": 0})
      
              sid, tail = self._session_route(path)
              if sid is not None and tail == "events":
                  s = st.get_session(sid)
                  if s is None:
                      return self._error(404, "no such edit session")
                  try:
                      body = self._body()
                  except ValueError as e:
                      return self._error(400, str(e))
                  source = str(body.get("source") or "")[:16]
                  kind = str(body.get("kind") or "")[:16]
                  if source not in ("shankpit", "nock"):
                      return self._error(400, 'source must be "shankpit" or "nock"')
                  if kind not in EVENT_KINDS:
                      return self._error(400, "unknown event kind")
                  data = body.get("data")
                  if data is None:
                      data = {}
                  event = s.post(source, kind, data)
                  return self._json(200, event)
      
              return self._error(404, "not found")
      
          # -- PUT ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
          def do_PUT(self):
              path = urlparse(self.path).path
              st = self.server.state
      
              if path.startswith(LEVELS_PREFIX + "/"):
                  name = unquote(path[len(LEVELS_PREFIX) + 1:])
                  if not SLUG_RE.match(name):
                      return self._error(400, "bad level name (letters, digits, - and _ only)")
                  try:
                      doc = self._body()
                      result = st.store.write(name, doc)
                  except ValueError as e:
                      return self._error(400, str(e))
                  except OSError as e:
                      return self._error(500, f"cannot write level: {e}")
                  return self._json(200, result)
      
              sid, tail = self._session_route(path)
              if sid is not None and tail == "level":
                  s = st.get_session(sid)
                  if s is None:
                      return self._error(404, "no such edit session")
                  try:
                      doc = validate_level(self._body())
                  except ValueError as e:
                      return self._error(400, str(e))
                  with s.cond:
                      s.draft = doc
                      s.draft_rev += 1
                      s.touched = time.time()
                      rev = s.draft_rev
                  return self._json(200, {"rev": rev})
      
              return self._error(404, "not found")
      
      
      def build_server(port=8787, host="127.0.0.1", levels_dir=None, repo=None, commit=True,
                       verbose=False):
          """Create (but do not start) the server -- used by main() and by the integration test."""
          repo = os.path.abspath(repo or os.getcwd())
          levels_dir = os.path.abspath(levels_dir or os.path.join(repo, "levels"))
          with open(os.path.join(HERE, "nock_editor.html"), "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
              editor_html = f.read()
          store = LevelStore(levels_dir, repo, commit=commit)
          server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), Handler)
          server.daemon_threads = True
          server.state = State(store, editor_html, verbose=verbose)
          return server
      
      
      def main(argv=None):
          ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Local NOCK map tools: browser editor + live session "
                                                   "server for SHANKPIT's in-game editor.")
          ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8787)
          ap.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
          ap.add_argument("--levels-dir", default=None, help="where level JSON lives (default ./levels)")
          ap.add_argument("--repo", default=None, help="git repo the level saves commit into (default cwd)")
          ap.add_argument("--no-commit", action="store_true", help="save files without git commit")
          ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
          args = ap.parse_args(argv)
      
          server = build_server(port=args.port, host=args.host, levels_dir=args.levels_dir,
                                repo=args.repo, commit=not args.no_commit, verbose=not args.quiet)
          port = server.server_address[1]
          levels = os.path.relpath(server.state.store.levels_dir, server.state.store.repo)
          print(f"local NOCK on http://{args.host}:{port}   levels: {levels}/   "
                f"commit: {'off' if args.no_commit else 'on'}")
          print()
          print("  browser:  open that URL, start a live session, then join it from the game:")
          print(f"            SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL=http://{args.host}:{port}{SESSION_PREFIX} \\")
          print("              ./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map levels/starter.json --edit-live")
          print("            (or paste the game's session id into the editor and press Join)")
          print()
          try:
              server.serve_forever()
          except KeyboardInterrupt:
              print("\nstopping")
          finally:
              server.server_close()
          return 0
      
      
      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(main())

(defn parse-i32 [(s : String @ :region/scratch) (dest : Arena @ Region)]
  : (Result I32 ParseError) @ Region
  (if (is-valid-i32-text? s)
    (Ok (raw-parse-i32 s))
    (Err (ParseError "not a valid integer"))))

;; parse-f64-raw -- exported (unlike raw-parse-i32 above): json.prn and
;; yaml.prn each independently carried a byte-for-byte identical copy

;; real validation (JSON's own digit-scanning, YAML's own
;; looks-numeric?) before calling it -- the same real "validate first,

;; establish, just without a single shared, generic Result wrapper

Routing, JSON shapes, session state, validation and the git commit are\n * PARENA in local_nock.prn.\n */\n#include \"local_nock_host.h\"\n\n#include <ctype.h>\n#include <dirent.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <time.h>\n#include <unistd.h>\n\nstatic Arena g_arena;\nstatic Arena g_state;\nstatic Arena g_request;\nstatic Arena g_draft;\n\nArena *ln_state_arena(void) { return &g_state; }\nArena *ln_request_arena(void) { return &g_request; }\nArena *ln_draft_arena(void) { return &g_draft; }\n\nint ln_request_reset(void) {\n    arena_free_all(&g_request);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nint ln_draft_reset(void) {\n    arena_free_all(&g_draft);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nint ln_port(void) {\n    const char *p = getenv(\"LOCAL_NOCK_PORT\");\n    return (p && *p) ? atoi(p) : 8787;\n}\n\nstatic char *arena_strdup_local(const char *s, Arena *dest) {\n    size_t n = strlen(s);\n    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, n + 1);\n    memcpy(out, s, n + 1);\n    return out;\n}\n\nchar *ln_env(const char *key, const char *fallback, Arena *dest) {\n    const char *v = key ? getenv(key) : NULL;\n    if (!v || !*v) v = fallback ? fallback : \"\";\n    return arena_strdup_local(v, dest);\n}\n\n/* ln_new_id -- 32 lowercase hex chars, the shape edit_sync_create() checks for. The RNG is seeded\n * ONCE: re-seeding per call from time(NULL) ^ pid gave the same \"random\" id to every session\n * created inside the same second. */\nchar *ln_new_id(Arena *dest) {\n    static int seeded = 0;\n    static const char *hex = \"0123456789abcdef\";\n    if (!seeded) {\n        srand((unsigned)(time(NULL) ^ (long)getpid()));\n        seeded = 1;\n    }\n    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, 33);\n    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) out[i] = hex[rand() & 0xf];\n    out[32] = 0;\n    return out;\n}\n\nchar *ln_level_path(const char *dir, const char *name, Arena *dest) {\n    size_t cap = strlen(dir) + strlen(name) + 8;\n    char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);\n    snprintf(buf, cap, \"%s/%s.json\", dir, name ? name : \"\");\n    return buf;\n}\n\nchar *ln_read_file(const char *path, Arena *dest) {\n    FILE *f = fopen(path, \"rb\");\n    if (!f) return arena_strdup_local(\"\", dest);\n    if (fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END) != 0) { fclose(f); return arena_strdup_local(\"\", dest); }\n    long n = ftell(f);\n    if (n < 0) { fclose(f); return arena_strdup_local(\"\", dest); }\n    rewind(f);\n    char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, (size_t)n + 1);\n    size_t got = fread(buf, 1, (size_t)n, f);\n    fclose(f);\n    buf[got] = 0;\n    return buf;\n}\n\n/* ln_write_file -- write-then-rename, so a reader never sees a half-written level. The temp file\n * lives beside the target (same directory, so rename is atomic on the same filesystem). */\nint ln_write_file(const char *path, const char *text) {\n    size_t plen = strlen(path);\n    char *tmp = (char *)malloc(plen + 5);\n    if (!tmp) return 0;\n    memcpy(tmp, path, plen);\n    memcpy(tmp + plen, \".tmp\", 5);\n    FILE *f = fopen(tmp, \"wb\");\n    if (!f) { free(tmp); return 0; }\n    size_t n = strlen(text);\n    size_t wrote = fwrite(text, 1, n, f);\n    int ok = (wrote == n);\n    if (fclose(f) != 0) ok = 0;\n    if (ok && rename(tmp, path) != 0) ok = 0;\n    if (!ok) remove(tmp);\n    free(tmp);\n    return ok ? 1 : 0;\n}\n\n/* count_walls -- the number of top-level objects in the \"walls\" array. A directory listing that\n * claims a wall count has to count the array, not the file's every \"sx\": doors and other boxes\n * carry sx/sy/sz too. Scans for the walls array and counts '{' at depth 1, skipping strings so a\n * brace inside a string value cannot fool it. */\nstatic int count_walls(const char *text) {\n    const char *w = strstr(text, \"\\\"walls\\\"\");\n    if (!w) return 0;\n    const char *p = strchr(w, '[');\n    if (!p) return 0;\n    int depth = 0, count = 0, in_str = 0, esc = 0;\n    for (; *p; p++) {\n        if (in_str) {\n            if (esc) esc = 0;\n            else if (*p == '\\\\') esc = 1;\n            else if (*p == '\"') in_str = 0;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (*p == '\"') { in_str = 1; continue; }\n        if (*p == '[') depth++;\n        else if (*p == ']') { depth--; if (depth == 0) break; }\n        else if (*p == '{' && depth == 1) count++;\n    }\n    return count;\n}\n\nstatic int valid_name(const char *name) {\n    size_t n = strlen(name);\n    if (n == 0 || n > 64) return 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {\n        unsigned char c = (unsigned char)name[i];\n        if (!(isalnum(c) || c == '-' || c == '_')) return 0;\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* ln_levels_json -- {\"levels\":[{name,walls,bytes,..},..]}. Only slug-shaped *.json files are\n * listed, the same rule the write path enforces, so a stray file in levels/ cannot be offered as a\n * level name that would later be rejected on save. */\nchar *ln_levels_json(const char *dir, Arena *dest) {\n    size_t cap = 1 << 16, len = 0;\n    char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);\n    len += (size_t)snprintf(out + len, cap - len, \"{\\\"levels\\\":[\");\n    DIR *d = opendir(dir);\n    int first = 1;\n    if (d) {\n        struct dirent *e;\n        while ((e = readdir(d)) != NULL) {\n            size_t m = strlen(e->d_name);\n            if (m < 6 || strcmp(e->d_name + m - 5, \".json\") != 0) continue;\n            char stem[512];\n            if (m - 5 >= sizeof stem) continue;\n            memcpy(stem, e->d_name, m - 5);\n            stem[m - 5] = 0;\n            if (!valid_name(stem)) continue;\n            char path[2048];\n            snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"%s/%s\", dir, e->d_name);\n            char *text = ln_read_file(path, dest);\n            size_t bytes = strlen(text);\n            if (len + 512 > cap) break;\n            len += (size_t)snprintf(out + len, cap - len,\n                                    \"%s{\\\"name\\\":\\\"%s\\\",\\\"file\\\":\\\"levels/%s\\\",\\\"walls\\\":%d,\\\"bytes\\\":%zu}\",\n                                    first ? \"\" : \",\", stem, e->d_name, count_walls(text), bytes);\n            first = 0;\n        }\n        closedir(d);\n    }\n    snprintf(out + len, cap - len, \"]}\");\n    return out;\n}\n\nint main(void) {\n    arena_init(&g_arena);\n    arena_init(&g_state);\n    arena_init(&g_request);\n    arena_init(&g_draft);\n    return nock_run(&g_arena);\n}\n"
}

> _Reasoning_
> The Python runner test fails with broken pipe — the oversized body test: Python's `_body` raises BodyTooLarge BEFORE reading the body (checks Content-Length), then handler sends 413 and closes while the client is still writing 4MB → broken pipe on client side. Need to read/discard the body before responding 413, so the client can finish sending. Fix in `_body`: if n > limit, read and discard up to some cap (or just drain n bytes) then raise. Draining 4MB is fine.

> Also the traceback is on the client: urllib fails with BrokenPipeError rather than returning 413. Fix server: drain then raise.
> 
> Also for PARENA: `too-big?` rejects before reading the body — but the body has already been read by tcp_read_impl (which reads up to Content-Length) before handle is called, so no broken pipe. Good.
>

>             while remaining > 0:

>                 remaining -= len(chunk)
>             raise BodyTooLarge(...)

      (defn levels-route [(method : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [name (drop-prefix path "/api/levels/" dest)]
          (if (not (slug? name 0))

            (if (string/str-eq? method "GET")

      ;; ---- routing -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn too-big? [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : Bool
        (> (parse-int-or (http_server/header-value raw "Content-Length" dest) 0) max-body))
      
      (defn route [(method : String @ Region) (target : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET")
                 (or (string/str-eq? path "/") (string/str-eq? path "/editor.html")))
          (http_server/html-response 200 (host-read editor-path dest) dest)
          (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (string/str-eq? path "/api/local-nock"))
            (http_server/json-response 200 (status-json dest) dest)
            (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (string/str-eq? path "/api/levels"))
              (http_server/json-response 200 (host-levels-json levels-dir dest) dest)
              (if (starts-with? path "/api/levels/" dest)
                (levels-route method path body dest)
                (if (starts-with? path "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions" dest)
                  (if (and (string/str-eq? method "POST") (string/str-eq? path "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions"))
                    (create-session body dest)
                    (session-route method target path body dest))
                  (http_server/text-response 404 "not found" dest))))))))
      
      (defn handle [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
        (let [method (http_server/parse-method raw dest)
              target (http_server/parse-target raw dest)
              path (http_server/path-only target dest)]
          (if (string/str-eq? method "")
            (http_server/text-response 400 "bad request" dest)
            (if (too-big? raw dest)
              (err 413 "body too large" dest)
              (route method target path (http_server/parse-body raw dest) dest)))))
      
      ;; ---- accept loop ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn serve-one [(!stream : &mut TcpStream) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : I32
        (let [raw (match (net/tcp/tcp-read !stream dest) ((Ok !text) !text) ((Err _) ""))]
          (do
            (net/tcp/tcp-write !stream (handle raw (request-arena)) dest)
            (net/tcp/tcp-close !stream dest)
            (request-reset)
            0)))

== README parena para ==
The PARENA port is `tools/local_nock.prn` plus the previously missing dependency
`PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` (request parsing, case-insensitive header lookup, and response
serialisation). It now emits and runs: `make local-nock-parena` builds it (needs a `../PARENA`
checkout with `.parena-bootstrap`) and serves the same API as the Python runner, with the host
boundary in `tools/local_nock_host.c`/`.h` limited to the arena, env, file/directory access and the
session strings that outlive a request -- routing, JSON, level validation and the git commit are
PARENA.

Getting there needed four real VS0 emitter fixes (2026-10-30, each verified by compiling the
generated C with `-std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror`): variadic arithmetic (`(+ a b c)`
left-folds), `set!` on a top-level `(def ...)`, `println`/`print` in the runtime, and `&` on an
already-pointer-typed value (a match-bound `Ok` payload used to emit a real `void **`). `(< a b c)`
still fails by design, with a message that says why: a real chained comparison would have to
evaluate its middle operand twice.

== CHANGELOG paridad bullet ==
3:- **feat(paridad): the local NOCK server now runs in PARENA.** `tools/local_nock.prn` + the previously missing `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` emit and serve real HTTP: `make local-nock-parena` builds the generated C with `gcc -std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and runs it on the same API (level list/read/save with the real git commit, session create/events/draft, editor page). Verified live over loopback: `PUT /api/levels/smoke` wrote the file and committed `level(smoke) from local NOCK` in a throwaway repo, `POST` session returned 32 hex, events posted and read back, draft pushed/fetched, `/` served the editor, unknown paths 404. Host boundary (`tools/local_nock_host.c`/`.h`, prototypes included via `-include` like PARENA's own `ci_status.h`) is only the arena/env, file and directory access, and the session strings that outlive one request. Getting it to build needed four real emitter fixes (variadic arithmetic, `set!` on a top-level def, `println` in the runtime, and `&` on an already-pointer match payload that emitted `void **`), plus a real runtime fix in `tcp_read_impl` (a bodyless request was read until EOF, so every GET hung). The Python runner stays the complete one for now: the PARENA port does not yet filter events by `?since`, validate event kinds, fall back to the saved level when a session has no draft, or bump the draft revision -- named in `mk/local_nock.mk` rather than claimed. Not driven from the lobby or a browser here (no SDL2/display, no Chrome).
- **feat(paridad): the local NOCK server now runs in PARENA.** `tools/local_nock.prn` + the previously missing `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` emit and serve real HTTP: `make local-nock-parena` builds the generated C with `gcc -std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and runs it on the same API (level list/read/save with the real git commit, session create/events/draft, editor page). Verified live over loopback: `PUT /api/levels/smoke` wrote the file and committed `level(smoke) from local NOCK` in a throwaway repo, `POST` session returned 32 hex, events posted and read back, draft pushed/fetched, `/` served the editor, unknown paths 404. Host boundary (`tools/local_nock_host.c`/`.h`, prototypes included via `-include` like PARENA's own `ci_status.h`) is only the arena/env, file and directory access, and the session strings that outlive one request. Getting it to build needed four real emitter fixes (variadic arithmetic, `set!` on a top-level def, `println` in the runtime, and `&` on an already-pointer match payload that emitted `void **`), plus a real runtime fix in `tcp_read_impl` (a bodyless request was read until EOF, so every GET hung). The Python runner stays the complete one for now: the PARENA port does not yet filter events by `?since`, validate event kinds, fall back to the saved level when a session has no draft, or bump the draft revision -- named in `mk/local_nock.mk` rather than claimed. Not driven from the lobby or a browser here (no SDL2/display, no Chrome).
- **feat(local-nock): the map editor runs locally, browser and game in one live session.** `make local-nock` (`python3 tools/local_nock.py`) serves `tools/nock_editor.html` and the same edit-session API the native client already speaks (`SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL`, IDUNA `shankpit_edit_sessions.go` shape): level list/read/save, session create, events, working-draft push/fetch. The browser pushes the working level and the game reloads it; the game's box/spawner/avatar events appear in the browser. Saves land in `levels/<name>.json` and are committed (`level(<name>): N walls from local NOCK`, never pushed), with `levels/starter.json` as the first map. `make test-local-nock` (12 checks) covers the HTTP contract including the git commit, invalid levels, long-poll wakeup and 404s. Gaps named: one live room per run, and the event log replays whole instead of honouring `?since` (applied events are idempotent). PARENA port started: `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` (request parsing + response serialisation, emits clean) plus `tools/local_nock.prn`, which parses but is blocked on four verified VS0 gaps (reference params / `match` scrutinees naming an imported defstruct, pointer-typed returns, `set!` on a top-level def), so the Python server stays the runner for now.

== prn header status ==
;; compare the id segment against the live id, so a stale game window cannot post into a new room.

(module local_nock)
(import string)
(import net/tcp)
(import net/http_server)
(import process)

(export nock-run)

;; ---- limits --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(def max-body 4194304)
(def max-event-body 65536)
(def max-events 2000)
(def max-name 64)

;; ---- state ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; PARENA-owned now that `set!` on a top-level def works: the id, the level it points at, the event
;; log, the log's seq/count, the browser's draft and its revision. All of it is allocated in the
;; host's state arena, which is never reset, so it survives across requests the way a room must.
(def repo-dir "")
(def levels-dir "")
(def editor-path "")
(def session-id "")
(def session-level "")
(def session-level-id 0)

Done. Both runners are at parity, sessions are hardened, everything verified end to end, and both repos are pushed: PARENA `e660936` (`main`), SHANKPIT `f67dd58` (`master`).

## Unblocking the port

The PARENA server now owns its session state — id, level, event log, log seq/count, draft and draft revision are all PARENA `(def ...)` globals, allocated in a state arena that survives requests. The four missing behaviours are in:

- **`?since` filtering** — the log is a bare concatenation of `{"seq":N,...}` objects; each seq is read back and only later events are copied out, comma-joined.
- **Event validation** — `source` must be `shankpit`/`nock`, `kind` must be one of the 11 real kinds.
- **Draft fallback** — a session with no draft serves its saved level, 404 when there isn't one.
- **Draft revisions** — `rev` increments per push, in its own arena so a 4 MiB draft doesn't accumulate a copy per edit.

Two real bugs surfaced while doing it: `(def x "")` is tracked as `char *`, so `set!` matched the `&mut`-local branch and emitted `*(name) = value` (a char assignment) instead of assigning the global; and `http_server/trim` stripped only spaces/tabs, so `git rev-parse`'s newline embedded in the save response made it invalid JSON.

## Hardening (both runners)

- The session id segment must equal the **live** id — a stale game window gets 404, it can't post into the current room.
- Level names must be `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` **before any path is built** — that's the traversal defence.
- Bodies over 4 MiB → 413; events over 64 KiB → 413; wrong methods → 405; unknown path → 404; non-object level → 400.
- Event log capped at 2000 entries, oldest dropped.
- Level listing counts the `walls` array (brace/string-aware scan) rather than trusting the file.
- Python runner: an oversized upload is now drained before answering 413, otherwise the client died on a broken pipe instead of reading the status.
- File writes are write-then-rename, and the id generator seeds once (it previously produced identical ids within the same second).

## Verification

- `make test-local-nock-parena` → **16/16** (builds the binary through the bootstrap, compiles with `-std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror`, drives it with `test_local_nock.py --binary`)
- `make test-local-nock` → **16/16** on the Python runner, same checks, including the real blocking long-poll
- PARENA `tests/test_emit` → **365 passed, 0 failed**
- The make target now depends on the PARENA stdlib/runtime sources, so a stale binary can't silently be tested again (that bit me once during this work)

## Limits, still named rather than hidden

- The PARENA runner is **one room per process** and **single-threaded**, so `wait` is answered immediately and a client polls again — the one check that differs between runners, and the test says so.
- It validates that a level is an object carrying a `walls` array, but not each wall's `x/y/z/sx/sy/sz`; the Python runner still does that.
- Not driven from the lobby or a browser here (no SDL2/display, no Chrome): HTTP-contract level only.

== draft.c defines ==

int dw_draft_done(const DwDraft *d) { return d->pick_no >= DW_DRAFT_PICKS; }

/* Real draft legality check for a deck arriving from OUTSIDE the normal pick-by-pick flow (S510
 * DW_C_DRAFT_RESUME) -- a client resuming a persisted deck could otherwise hand the server any 23
 * bytes it likes (e.g. 23 copies of the best card), bypassing the bucket rule dw_draft_pick above
 * enforces one pick at a time. Encodes the same rule: exactly ten 1-ofs, five 2-ofs, one 3-of. */
int dw_draft_deck_valid(const int8_t *deck, int n) {
    if (n != DW_DECK_SIZE) return 0;
    int seen[DW_DRAFT_MAX_CARDS]; memset(seen, 0, sizeof seen);
    int nc = num_cards();
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (deck[i] < 0 || deck[i] >= nc) return 0;
        seen[deck[i]]++;
    }
    int ones = 0, twos = 0, threes = 0;
    for (int c = 0; c < DW_DRAFT_MAX_CARDS; c++) {
        switch (seen[c]) {
        case 0: break;
        case 1: ones++; break;
        case 2: twos++; break;
        case 3: threes++; break;
        default: return 0; /* more than 3 copies is never legal */
        }
    }
    return ones == 10 && twos == 5 && threes == 1;
}

Fixed and pushed: SHANKPIT `97b99ca` on `master`.

## Root cause

`dw_random_deck` and `dw_draft_deck_valid` live in DEADWEIGHT's **`core/draft.c`** (the S510 deck-resume legality code), and DEADWEIGHT's own `scripts/build.sh` includes that file in its `GUI_SRC`. SHANKPIT's `release.yml` builds `dw_gui` from a **hand-copied** source list, and that copy never picked up `core/draft.c` — so `core/client.c` and `core/iduna.c` compiled fine and the link failed on exactly those two symbols.

It was two stale copies, not one: the Windows mingw recipe **and** the Linux `dw_gui` recipe carried the same list, so the Linux release job would have failed the same way.

## The change

- Added `core/draft.c` to both `dw_gui` source lists in `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
- Added a comment at the Windows recipe naming DEADWEIGHT's `scripts/build.sh` `GUI_SRC` as the source of truth, recording this as the ninth recurrence of the drift class and pointing at the Linux copy.
- Changelog entry explaining the cause, the verification, and that CI is the remaining proof.

## Verification (no mingw/SDL2 toolchain in this sandbox)

- Diffed both lists in `release.yml` against DEADWEIGHT's `GUI_SRC`: **missing: none**, extra: only `core/runtime/parena_runtime.c` (the intentional `arena_alloc` fix from the earlier outage).
- Every listed path exists in the DEADWEIGHT tree.
- `core/draft.c` compiles clean under `-std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and `nm` shows both symbols defined (`T dw_random_deck`, `T dw_draft_deck_valid`).
- `release.yml` still parses as YAML (`jobs: 2`).
- Grepped SHANKPIT for any other copy of that list — `release.yml` is the only place.

## Limit

I could not reproduce the mingw link itself here: `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` isn't installed, so the real confirmation is the next "Build SHANKPIT OS Apps (Windows)" run. Nothing else in the app-build step was touched.

      static int lobby_app_binary_path(const char *bundled_name, const char *dev_relative_path, char *out, size_t out_sz) {
          char *base = SDL_GetBasePath();
          if (base) {
              char candidate[1024];
              snprintf(candidate, sizeof candidate, "%sbundled/%s", base, bundled_name);
              FILE *f = fopen(candidate, "rb");
              if (f) {
                  fclose(f);
                  snprintf(out, out_sz, "%s", candidate);
                  SDL_free(base);
                  return 1;
              }
              char dev_candidate[1024];
              snprintf(dev_candidate, sizeof dev_candidate, "%s%s", base, dev_relative_path);
              f = fopen(dev_candidate, "rb");
              if (f) {
                  fclose(f);
                  snprintf(out, out_sz, "%s", dev_candidate);
                  SDL_free(base);
                  return 1;
              }
              SDL_free(base);
          }
          return 0;
      }

>     addr.sin_family = AF_INET;

>     SOCKET s = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
>     if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) return 0;

/* Only [A-Za-z0-9%:/?=&._~-] reaches here (built from encoded parts + a validated base), so quoting is safe. */
static inline void iduna__open_browser(const char *url) {
    char cmd[1400];
#ifdef _WIN32
    /* `start` needs no extra link library (ShellExecute would need -lshell32) */
    snprintf(cmd, sizeof cmd, "start \"\" \"%s\"", url); (void)!system(cmd);
#elif defined(__APPLE__)
    snprintf(cmd, sizeof cmd, "open '%s' >/dev/null 2>&1 &", url); (void)!system(cmd);
#else
    snprintf(cmd, sizeof cmd, "xdg-open '%s' >/dev/null 2>&1 &", url); (void)!system(cmd);
#endif
}

      /* tools/local_nock_host.c -- the thin C host for tools/local_nock.prn.
       *
       * Only what a PARENA program cannot do itself yet or at all: arenas, env, an id generator, and
       * file/directory access. Routing, JSON shapes, session state, validation and the git commit are
       * PARENA in local_nock.prn.
       */
      #include "local_nock_host.h"
      
      #include <ctype.h>
      #include <dirent.h>
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <stdlib.h>
      #include <string.h>
      #include <time.h>
      #include <unistd.h>
      
      static Arena g_arena;
      static Arena g_state;
      static Arena g_request;
      static Arena g_draft;
      
      Arena *ln_state_arena(void) { return &g_state; }
      Arena *ln_request_arena(void) { return &g_request; }
      Arena *ln_draft_arena(void) { return &g_draft; }
      
      int ln_request_reset(void) {
          arena_free_all(&g_request);
          return 1;
      }
      
      int ln_draft_reset(void) {
          arena_free_all(&g_draft);
          return 1;
      }
      
      int ln_port(void) {
          const char *p = getenv("LOCAL_NOCK_PORT");
          return (p && *p) ? atoi(p) : 8787;
      }
      
      static char *arena_strdup_local(const char *s, Arena *dest) {
          size_t n = strlen(s);
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, n + 1);
          memcpy(out, s, n + 1);
          return out;
      }
      
      char *ln_env(const char *key, const char *fallback, Arena *dest) {
          const char *v = key ? getenv(key) : NULL;
          if (!v || !*v) v = fallback ? fallback : "";
          return arena_strdup_local(v, dest);
      }
      
      /* ln_new_id -- 32 lowercase hex chars, the shape edit_sync_create() checks for. The RNG is seeded
       * ONCE: re-seeding per call from time(NULL) ^ pid gave the same "random" id to every session
       * created inside the same second. */
      char *ln_new_id(Arena *dest) {
          static int seeded = 0;
          static const char *hex = "0123456789abcdef";
          if (!seeded) {
              srand((unsigned)(time(NULL) ^ (long)getpid()));
              seeded = 1;
          }
          char *out = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, 33);
          for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) out[i] = hex[rand() & 0xf];
          out[32] = 0;
          return out;
      }
      
      char *ln_level_path(const char *dir, const char *name, Arena *dest) {
          size_t cap = strlen(dir) + strlen(name) + 8;
          char *buf = (char *)arena_alloc(dest, cap);
          snprintf(buf, cap, "%s/%s.json", dir, name ? name : "");
          return buf;
      }
      
      char *ln_read_file(const char *path, Arena *dest) {
          FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
          if (!f) return arena_strdup_local("", dest);
          if (fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END) != 0) { fclose(f); return arena_strdup_local("", dest); }

## 2026-10-30

- **fix(release): `dw_gui.exe` link failed — `core/draft.c` missing from the hand-copied source list.** Ninth occurrence of the drift class this file's own release.yml comments already document: DEADWEIGHT's `scripts/build.sh` `GUI_SRC` gained `core/draft.c` (S510 `DW_C_DRAFT_RESUME`, `dw_draft_deck_valid` / `dw_random_deck`) and neither copy in `release.yml` -- the Windows `dw_gui.exe` mingw line nor the Linux `dw_gui` line -- had it, so the link failed with `undefined reference to dw_random_deck` (from `core/client.c`) and `dw_draft_deck_valid` (from `core/iduna.c`). Both lists now match `GUI_SRC` exactly, plus `core/runtime/parena_runtime.c` (the `arena_alloc` fix from the earlier outage). Verified without a mingw/SDL2 toolchain here: the yml lists were diffed against `GUI_SRC` (no missing files, every path exists in DEADWEIGHT), and `core/draft.c` compiles clean under `-std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` with `nm` confirming both symbols. Next CI run is the real proof.
- **feat(paridad): the local NOCK server now runs in PARENA.** `tools/local_nock.prn` + the previously missing `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` emit and serve real HTTP: `make local-nock-parena` builds the generated C with `gcc -std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and runs it on the same API (level list/read/save with the real git commit, session create/events/draft, editor page). Verified live over loopback: `PUT /api/levels/smoke` wrote the file and committed `level(smoke) from local NOCK` in a throwaway repo, `POST` session returned 32 hex, events posted and read back, draft pushed/fetched, `/` served the editor, unknown paths 404. Host boundary (`tools/local_nock_host.c`/`.h`, prototypes included via `-include` like PARENA's own `ci_status.h`) is only the arena/env, file and directory access, and the session strings that outlive one request. Getting it to build needed four real emitter fixes (variadic arithmetic, `set!` on a top-level def, `println` in the runtime, and `&` on an already-pointer match payload that emitted `void **`), plus a real runtime fix in `tcp_read_impl` (a bodyless request was read until EOF, so every GET hung). Parity landed the same day: `?since` filtering, source/kind validation, draft revisions and the saved-level fallback are all in PARENA now, and both runners pass the same 16 checks (`make test-local-nock`, `make test-local-nock-parena`, the latter driving the binary through `tools/test_local_nock.py --binary`). Sessions are hardened on both: the id segment must be the live room (a stale client is 404, never a write into the current one), a level name must be slug-shaped before any path is built (the traversal defence), bodies over 4 MiB are 413 (and the Python runner now drains an oversized upload before answering, so the client reads the status instead of dying on a broken pipe), wrong methods are 405, unknown sources/kinds are 400, the event log is capped at 2000 entries with the oldest dropped, and the listing counts the `walls` array rather than trusting the file. Two more real fixes came out of it: `set!` on a String-typed top-level def went through the pointer branch (`*(name) = ...`) instead of the global, and `net/http_server`'s `trim` only stripped spaces/tabs, so a `git rev-parse` newline made the save response invalid JSON. Remaining, named: the PARENA runner is one room per process and single-threaded (`wait` is answered immediately; the test verifies poll-again instead), and it validates that a level is an object with a walls array but not each wall's fields. Not driven from the lobby or a browser here (no SDL2/display, no Chrome).
- **feat(local-nock): the map editor runs locally, browser and game in one live session.** `make local-nock` (`python3 tools/local_nock.py`) serves `tools/nock_editor.html` and the same edit-session API the native client already speaks (`SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL`, IDUNA `shankpit_edit_sessions.go` shape): level list/read/save, session create, events, working-draft push/fetch. The browser pushes the working level and the game reloads it; the game's box/spawner/avatar events appear in the browser. Saves land in `levels/<name>.json` and are committed (`level(<name>): N walls from local NOCK`, never pushed), with `levels/starter.json` as the first map. `make test-local-nock` (12 checks) covers the HTTP contract including the git commit, invalid levels, long-poll wakeup and 404s. Gaps named: one live room per run, and the event log replays whole instead of honouring `?since` (applied events are idempotent). PARENA port started: `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` (request parsing + response serialisation, emits clean) plus `tools/local_nock.prn`, which parses but is blocked on four verified VS0 gaps (reference params / `match` scrutinees naming an imported defstruct, pointer-typed returns, `set!` on a top-level def), so the Python server stays the runner for now.
- **feat(edit-map): F6 saves a real level JSON, no IDUNA needed.** EDIT MAP's F6 writes the whole working level (source plus every edit) to `var/maps/<name>.json` through the new `level_boxes_save_to_file` (`packages/world/level_boxes.h`), which emits every field the loader parses -- walls/materials, spawners, buggy spawns, lab stations, doors (button subscriptions + script paths included), buttons, nav nodes, characters, exits, zones, edu widgets, brick damage, enclosed/floor tint/next level. Load it back with `--edit-map var/maps/<name>.json` or `--level`. F5's op log stays the live-NOCK streaming format; a successful F6 deletes the stale `.edits.json` so a replay can't apply the same edits twice. `level_boxes_parse_string` now honours `\\ \" \n \t \r` escapes (real escaped JSON, and it fixes Windows door script paths coming back doubled). `make test-level-save`, plus a round-trip of the checked-in `var/lab/lab.json`, the story-doors demo and every `assets/tyler_levels/*.json` export. Not driven in the live client here (no SDL2/display on this box); writer + loader round-trip is what's tested.
- **feat(tools): `leveltool`, headless level JSON utility.** `info` (summary of a map), `check` (load -> save -> load and fail if any parsed field changed shape, plus a stable-writer byte check), `save` (normalize/re-emit) and `new` (an empty level, same defaults as EDIT MAP's new-level path). `map` prints a top-down ASCII view (`#` wall, `S` spawner, `C` character, `E` exit, `z` zone, `D` door, `B` button) so a layout can be eyeballed with no display; `--cell` zooms to a fixed scale (centred on `--center`, else spawner 0) and `--min-height` hides short geometry (a 500-unit LAB floor slab otherwise squashes the plan into a few cells). Walls rasterise their footprint outline, so a long wall crossing the window draws along its whole length. `make leveltool`, `make test-leveltool`, and `make check-levels` which runs `check` over `var/lab/lab.json`, the story-doors demo, `var/zombie/nextown_zombies.json` and every `assets/tyler_levels/*.json`. `--level var/maps/<name>.json` also already plays a locally saved map (both sides must pass the same path).

Cut-off geometry (glass disc, wall section) falls as one chunk with gravity + a seeded tumble, one level probe per chunk per tick, one small bounce, lies flat on the floor or whatever it lands on, then lingers 5 s. Max 32 chunks, no solver/pairs/piling; the dedicated server no longer simulates debris at all. Mass/density (NOCK material) kept as data. Headless tests only; live feel not verified.
- **feat(zombies): pheromone thrower is a real grenade.** `G` lobs a 0.8 kg canister (`packages/simulation/pheromone_grenade.h`: impulse/mass launch speed, ballistic arc, mass-dependent bounce, wall bounce, Coulomb roll to rest, inherits the thrower's velocity). The marker zombies chase rides the canister, so they track it in the air and through each bounce; the thud on landing startles zombies in range. Visuals: tumbling glowing canister with a streak, pulsing ground rings + scent wisps + smell-radius ring when down, G-key READY/cooldown HUD, red diamonds over starving zombies. `make test-pheromone-grenade`. Not seen in the live game.

Dead victims are permanent corpses. Tuning (rates, radii) is a first pass.


- feat(brick): **physical broken brick + falling disconnected geometry.** Shot-out cells throw mass-carrying shards (brick ~15 kg, density x volume) and any group of cells cut off from the ground/static solids falls as a rigid chunk (shoot a circle out of glass and the disc drops, with a seeded tumble), all on GOLDEN BAND's `grb` XPBD solver via new `packages/simulation/brick_bodies.{h,c}` (shards pile as cubes, slide down ramps via `obb.h`). `brick_fracture.h`: bounded flood-fill detection `bf_detect_detached` (found and fixed a real bug in its own tests: a flood that met an earlier flood's cells wrongly treated itself as cut off), chunk id on the brick wire pad byte, shard queue, per-parent density.       so the game reloads it, and the game's own box / spawner / avatar events show up in the browser.

      `PARENA/stdlib/net/http_server.prn` (request parsing, case-insensitive header lookup, and response
      serialisation). It now emits and runs: `make local-nock-parena` builds it (needs a `../PARENA`

      boundary in `tools/local_nock_host.c`/`.h` limited to the arena, env, file/directory access and the

      generated C with `-std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror`): variadic arithmetic (`(+ a b c)`
      left-folds), `set!` on a top-level `(def ...)`, `println`/`print` in the runtime, and `&` on an
      already-pointer-typed value (a match-bound `Ok` payload used to emit a real `void **`). `(< a b c)`
      still fails by design, with a message that says why: a real chained comparison would have to
      evaluate its middle operand twice.
      
      Both runners now pass the same 16 checks (`make test-local-nock`, `make test-local-nock-parena`):
      the PARENA one filters events by `?since`, validates sources and kinds, bumps draft revisions and
      falls back to the saved level. Sessions are hardened on both -- the id segment must match the live
      room (a stale client gets 404 instead of writing into the current one), a level name must be
      slug-shaped before any path is built (the traversal defence), bodies over 4 MiB are 413, wrong
      methods are 405, unknown sources/kinds are 400, and the event log is capped at 2000 entries with the
      oldest dropped. Two limits remain, both named in `mk/local_nock.mk`: the PARENA runner is one room
      per process and single-threaded, so `wait` is answered immediately and a client polls again; and it
      checks that a level is an object carrying a `walls` array but not each wall's fields, which the
      Python runner still does.
      
      ## Current visual direction
      
      SHANKPIT is pursuing a deliberately stylized visual identity rather than realism-first rendering.
      
      Key traits in the current renderer include:
      
      - **legacy OpenGL immediate-mode rendering**
      - **retro sky and retro lighting systems**

```

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/mk/local_nock.mk
  content: |
      # local NOCK (tools/local_nock.py): browser level editor + live edit-session server that the native
      # client joins through SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL. Levels save into levels/*.json and are committed.
      LOCAL_NOCK_PORT ?= 8787
      
      local-nock:
        python3 tools/local_nock.py --port $(LOCAL_NOCK_PORT)
      
      # local-nock-parena -- the same server, built from tools/local_nock.prn. Requires a sibling ../PARENA
      # checkout with a built .parena-bootstrap (the bootstrap, not `parena`, since the full binary needs
      # SDL2 headers this tool never uses). The generated C is not checked in.
      PARENA_DIR ?= ../PARENA
      LOCAL_NOCK_GEN ?= var/local_nock_gen.c
      LOCAL_NOCK_BIN ?= bin/local_nock_parena
      
      # Every PARENA input the binary is built from is a prerequisite, not just the .prn: a stdlib or
      # runtime change must rebuild it (a stale binary silently tested an older http_server once already).
      PARENA_SRC := $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/string.prn $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/net/tcp.prn \
                    $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/net/http_server.prn $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/process.prn \
                    $(PARENA_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.h $(PARENA_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.c
      
      $(LOCAL_NOCK_BIN): tools/local_nock.prn tools/local_nock_host.c tools/local_nock_host.h $(PARENA_SRC)
        @test -x $(PARENA_DIR)/.parena-bootstrap || \
          { echo "need $(PARENA_DIR)/.parena-bootstrap (cd $(PARENA_DIR) && make .parena-bootstrap)"; exit 1; }
        @mkdir -p var bin
        @$(MAKE) -C $(PARENA_DIR) .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null
        $(PARENA_DIR)/.parena-bootstrap build \
          $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/string.prn $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/net/tcp.prn \
          $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/net/http_server.prn $(PARENA_DIR)/stdlib/process.prn \
          tools/local_nock.prn -o $(LOCAL_NOCK_GEN)
        gcc -std=c99 -pedantic -Wall -Wextra -Werror -DPARENA_NO_GRAPHICS \
          -I $(PARENA_DIR)/runtime -I tools -include tools/local_nock_host.h \

## What it does now

The APPS page has a **NOCK** tile. Clicking it:

1. finds the server — dev tree `bin/local_nock_parena` (via the existing `lobby_app_binary_path`, so a packaged `bundled/dw_nock`/`dw_nock.exe` also works), else the footer reads `NOCK server not found -- run make local-nock-parena`;
2. works out the root: `bin/..` when `../levels` exists (dev), else `bundled/` when `bundled/levels` does;
3. probes port 8787 with a 100 ms non-blocking connect — if something already answers (a previous click, or your own `make local-nock`), **nothing is spawned** and it just re-opens the tab;
4. otherwise spawns `local_nock_parena --port 8787 --root <root>` **detached** (POSIX `fork`/`execl`, Windows `CreateProcessA` with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`), waits up to 2 s for the port to answer, then calls `iduna__open_browser("http://127.0.0.1:8787/")`.

Detached matters: the editor keeps working after you quit the lobby, and the same room serves the in-game `--edit-live` client, so browser and game stay on one live session with saves committed into this repo.

## Supporting change

`tools/local_nock_host.c` grew `--port`, `--root`, `--repo`, `--levels`, `--editor` and `--help`. `--root DIR` is the one flag the tile passes and it means "DIR/levels + DIR/tools/nock_editor.html, and commit in DIR". Flags win over `LOCAL_NOCK_*`, so `make local-nock` and the existing Python runner are untouched. Flags rather than environment variables specifically because a child command line is one call on Windows while building an environment block is not — that's why Windows has no `setenv`-based path.

## Checks run

- Both new functions compile clean standalone under `-std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`. That check earned its keep: it caught `levels/*.json` inside a block comment (nested `/*` is an error) and `-Wformat-truncation` on `%s..` into a 1024-byte buffer — both fixed, then it passed.
- `make test-local-nock-parena` → **16/16**, after the host change, so flags didn't disturb the env/fallback behaviour.
- Real `--root` run on port 8899 against a throwaway git repo: `{"levels":[]}`, editor `200` / 17313 bytes, `PUT` → `{"ok":true,...,"git":{"committed":true,"commit":"9855a78"}}`, `levels/cli_smoke.json` on disk, commit `level(cli_smoke): levels saved from local NOCK`, listing then showed `walls:1`.
- `--help` exits 0; port free after killing the server.

## Limits

- The tile itself was not clicked: no SDL2/display on this box, so the C is compiled and reviewed but not driven from the real lobby.
- Windows has no bundled `dw_nock.exe` yet, so the tile reports "not found" there rather than pretending — bundling it is a release-workflow job (and needs mingw to be honest about).
- The tile always uses 8787; there's no in-lobby port picker.

Key `9` equips `WPN_SPRAYCAN` (`MAX_WEAPONS` 9->10); hold fire to spray, `[` / `]` cycle cyan, yellow, magenta, white, black, grey, tan (rising-edge in `update_weapons`, colour index in `ammo[WPN_SPRAYCAN]` so it already rides `NetPlayer.ammo` -- no wire change; new `BTN_PAINT_NEXT/PREV` bits). Engine `packages/world/spraypaint.h` (GL-free): 6 rays per ~30 Hz tick inside a 9 degree cone, deposits merge into one dab per spot with thickness falling off with distance (close spray ~16x thicker per spot than from 10 units), opacity builds with thickness, a dab past thickness 1.0 on a wall grows a drip that draws paint out of it, runs down, stops above the floor / runs dry; floors pool, no drip. Drawn as soft blobs + drip strips + bead, plus a faint tinted cone from the nozzle, HUD swatch + name, can model in the paint colour. Paint is observed per player from synced `is_shooting`/weapon/colour like bullet holes, so others' paint shows; destroyed bricks take their paint with them.       static inline void spawn_projectile(Projectile *projectiles, PlayerState *p, int damage, int bounces, float speed_mult, float splash_radius) {
          for(int i=0; i<MAX_PROJECTILES; i++) {
              if (!projectiles[i].active) {
                  Projectile *proj = &projectiles[i];
                  proj->active = 1;
                  proj->owner_id = p->id;
                  proj->damage = damage;
                  proj->bounces_left = bounces;
                  proj->scene_id = (unsigned char)p->scene_id;
                  proj->splash_radius = splash_radius;
      
                  float r = -p->yaw * 0.0174533f; float rp = p->pitch * 0.0174533f;
                  float speed = 4.0f * speed_mult;
                  proj->vx = sinf(r) * cosf(rp) * speed;
                  proj->vy = sinf(rp) * speed;
                  proj->vz = -cosf(r) * cosf(rp) * speed;
                  proj->x = p->x;
                  proj->y = p->y + EYE_HEIGHT;
                  proj->z = p->z;
                  return;
              }
          }
      }
      
      void update_weapons(PlayerState *p, PlayerState *targets, Projectile *projectiles, int shoot, int reload, int ability_press, unsigned int now_ms, unsigned int respawn_delay_ms) {
          if (p->in_vehicle) return; 
          if (p->reload_timer > 0) p->reload_timer--;
          if (p->attack_cooldown > 0) p->attack_cooldown--;
          if (p->is_shooting > 0) p->is_shooting--;
          if (p->ability_cooldown > 0) p->ability_cooldown--;
          // S459-66, real, found-live bug: founder real-time report of a "false positive" red kill
          // ring on the sniper, followed by a real one -- hit_feedback (the wire field driving the
          // red double-ring kill marker, apps/lobby's own draw_hud >=25 check) was NEVER reset back to
          // 0 anywhere in this codebase, server or client, once set (10/15/20/30 at the various real
          // hit/kill call sites above). A real kill (hit_feedback=30) therefore stayed on the
          // attacker's own PlayerState and kept broadcasting on every snapshot (~31Hz,
          // SERVER_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_TICKS) until their NEXT hit landed -- so the next real shot,
          // whatever its own actual outcome, visually looked like an immediate second kill ring (the
          // stale 30 still being sent), only for a genuinely new kill's own real hit_feedback=30 to
          // arrive right after, reading as two kill rings for one real kill. Fixed the same way every
          // other real per-tick timer in this function already decays.
          if (p->hit_feedback > 0) p->hit_feedback--;
      
          if (p->katana_slash_timer > 0) p->katana_slash_timer--;
          if (p->dash_timer > 0) {
              p->vx = p->dash_vx;
              p->vy = p->dash_vy;
              p->vz = p->dash_vz;
              katana_update_dash_damage(p, targets, now_ms, respawn_delay_ms);
              p->dash_timer--;
              p->is_shooting = 2;
              if (p->dash_timer <= 0) {
                  p->dash_timer = 0;
                  p->dash_vx = p->dash_vy = p->dash_vz = 0.0f;
              }
          }
      
          int w = p->current_weapon;
          if (w == WPN_SPRAYCAN) {
              /* Spray can: colour cycle on the rising edge of [ / ] (ammo[WPN_SPRAYCAN] = colour index
                 0..SPRAY_COLOR_COUNT-1), is_shooting held while the trigger is down so every client
                 (NetPlayer.is_shooting) knows to paint. The decals themselves are client-side. */
              int cur = (p->in_paint_next ? 1 : 0) | (p->in_paint_prev ? 2 : 0);
              int rise = cur & ~p->paint_btn_prev;
              p->paint_btn_prev = cur;
              int c = p->ammo[WPN_SPRAYCAN];
              if (c < 0 || c >= SPRAY_COLOR_COUNT) c = 0;
              if (rise & 1) c = (c + 1) % SPRAY_COLOR_COUNT;
              if (rise & 2) c = (c + SPRAY_COLOR_COUNT - 1) % SPRAY_COLOR_COUNT;
              p->ammo[WPN_SPRAYCAN] = c;
              if (shoot) p->is_shooting = 3;
              return;
          }
          if (w == WPN_FLASHLIGHT) return; /* pure utility slot -- no ammo/attack/reload/ability. The
                                               beam itself renders client-side whenever a player's own
                                               current_weapon == WPN_FLASHLIGHT (equip it, it's on;
                                               switch away, it's off) -- see apps/lobby's own
                                               draw_flashlight_beam. */
          if (ability_press) {
              if (w == WPN_KATANA) {
                  katana_try_start_dash(p);
              } else if (w == WPN_SNIPER) {
                  if (p->ability_cooldown == 0 && p->storm_charges == 0) {
                      p->storm_charges = 5;
                      p->ability_cooldown = 480;
                  }
              } else if (w == WPN_AR && p->ability_cooldown == 0) {
                  /* Frag Toss (S181-05): real splash-damage projectile, same
                   * spawn_projectile/explode_splash pipeline the missile
                   * launcher already uses -- explode_splash fires automatically
                   * for any projectile with splash_radius > 0 (update_projectiles
                   * calls it on impact/expiry), which in turn calls
                   * apply_projectile_damage per hit, which already applies a
                   * brief stun as a universal side effect of any projectile hit
                   * -- no new damage/stun code needed, just real tuning. Lobbed
                   * slower than a straight shot (0.7x speed) to read as a
                   * thrown grenade, not a bullet. First real use: story_ai.c's
                   * Shambler Trooper. */
                  spawn_projectile(projectiles, p, 60, 0, 0.7f, 4.5f);
                  p->ability_cooldown = 260;
              } else if (w == WPN_SHOTGUN && p->ability_cooldown == 0) {
                  /* Ground Slam (S181-05): same real pipeline as Frag Toss above,
                   * tuned for a close-range high-damage/bigger-splash burst
                   * instead of a lobbed grenade -- matches a tank archetype's
                   * melee-range AOE, not a ranged special. First real use:
                   * story_ai.c's Gore Brute. */
                  spawn_projectile(projectiles, p, 90, 0, 1.2f, 6.0f);
                  p->ability_cooldown = 340;
              } else if (p->ability_cooldown == 0 && p->storm_charges == 0) {
                  /* Fallback for any weapon without a dedicated ability above
                   * (knife, magnum, missile) -- unchanged pre-existing behavior. */
                  p->storm_charges = 5;
                  p->ability_cooldown = 480;
              }
          }
      
          if (reload && p->reload_timer == 0 && w != WPN_KNIFE && w != WPN_KATANA && w != WPN_HAMMER) {
              if (p->ammo[w] < WPN_STATS[w].ammo_max) {
                  if (p->ammo[w] > 0) p->reload_timer = RELOAD_TIME_TACTICAL;
                  else p->reload_timer = RELOAD_TIME_FULL; 
              }
          }
          if (p->reload_timer == 1) p->ammo[w] = WPN_STATS[w].ammo_max;
          if (p->dash_timer > 0) return;
          if (shoot && p->attack_cooldown == 0 && p->reload_timer == 0) {
              if (p->storm_charges > 0 && w == WPN_SNIPER) {
                  int storm_damage = (int)(WPN_STATS[w].dmg * 0.7f);
                  spawn_projectile(projectiles, p, storm_damage, 1, 1.5f, 0.0f);
                  p->storm_charges--;
                  p->attack_cooldown = 8;
                  p->recoil_anim = 0.5f;
                  return;
              }
              if (w != WPN_KNIFE && w != WPN_KATANA && w != WPN_HAMMER && p->ammo[w] <= 0) p->reload_timer = RELOAD_TIME_FULL;
              else {
                  p->is_shooting = 5; p->recoil_anim = 1.0f;
                  p->attack_cooldown = WPN_STATS[w].rof;
                  if (w != WPN_KNIFE && w != WPN_KATANA && w != WPN_HAMMER) p->ammo[w]--;
                  if (w == WPN_KATANA) {
                      p->katana_slash_timer = KATANA_SLASH_ACTIVE_TICKS;
                      p->recoil_anim = 0.35f;
                      katana_try_slash(p, targets, now_ms, respawn_delay_ms);
                      return;
                  }
                  if (w == WPN_KNIFE) {
                      if (g_phys_map_hitscan_hook) { /* melee still reaches world props (loot chests); brick_world ignores WPN_KNIFE */
                          float kr = -p->yaw * 0.0174533f, kp = p->pitch * 0.0174533f;
                          g_phys_map_hitscan_hook(p->scene_id, p->x, p->y + EYE_HEIGHT, p->z, sinf(kr) * cosf(kp), sinf(kp), -cosf(kr) * cosf(kp), w);
                      }
                      phys_try_melee_strike(p, targets, WPN_STATS[w].dmg, 10, 1, now_ms, respawn_delay_ms);
                      return;
                  }
                  if (w == WPN_HAMMER) {
                      p->recoil_anim = 0.8f;
                      phys_hammer_strike(p, targets, now_ms, respawn_delay_ms);
                      return;
                  }
                  if (w == WPN_MISSILE) {
                      spawn_projectile(projectiles, p, WPN_STATS[w].dmg, 0, 1.0f, MISSILE_SPLASH_RADIUS);
                      return;
                  }
      
                  float r = -p->yaw * 0.0174533f; float rp = p->pitch * 0.0174533f;
                  float dx = sinf(r) * cosf(rp); float dy = sinf(rp); float dz = -cosf(r) * cosf(rp);
                  if (g_phys_map_hitscan_hook) g_phys_map_hitscan_hook(p->scene_id, p->x, p->y + EYE_HEIGHT, p->z, dx, dy, dz, w);
                  if (WPN_STATS[w].spr > 0) {
                      dx += phys_rand_f() * WPN_STATS[w].spr;
                      dy += phys_rand_f() * WPN_STATS[w].spr;
                      dz += phys_rand_f() * WPN_STATS[w].spr;
                  }
      
                  for(int i=0; i<MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
                      if (p == &targets[i]) continue;
                      if (!targets[i].active || targets[i].state == STATE_DEAD) continue;
                      if (targets[i].scene_id != p->scene_id) continue;
                      if (phys_is_friendly(p, &targets[i])) continue;
                      int hit_type = check_hit_location(p->x, p->y + EYE_HEIGHT, p->z, dx, dy, dz, &targets[i]);
                      if (hit_type > 0) {
      #if PHYS_COMBAT_LOG
                          printf("[HIT] dmg=%d target=%d\n", WPN_STATS[w].dmg, i);
      #endif
                          int damage = WPN_STATS[w].dmg;
                          if (hit_type == 2 && targets[i].shield <= 0) { damage *= 3; p->hit_feedback = 20;
                          } else { p->hit_feedback = 10; } 
                          katana_apply_damage(p, &targets[i], damage, p->hit_feedback, now_ms, respawn_delay_ms);
                      }
                  }
              }
          }
      }
      
      void phys_store_history(ServerState *server, int client_id, unsigned int now) {
          if (client_id < 0 || client_id >= MAX_CLIENTS) return;
          int slot = (now / 16) % LAG_HISTORY;
