{
  "path": "MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn",
  "instructions": "PARENA structural rules: material profiles, joint strength and load capacity.",
  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn -- material + structural rules for destructible brick.\n;;\n;; Founder real-time (2026-10-30): \"we need to evolve the destructible brick logic into an intelligent,\n;; physically aware material and structural simulation ... a web of self-anchoring volumetric nodes\".\n;; Scoped honestly to what this engine is: there is no finite-element solver here and adding one would\n;; not survive MMO tick budgets. What a player can actually feel is (a) different materials failing\n;; differently, (b) two touching pieces acting like they are joined, and (c) a piece losing its support\n;; and falling. Those three are cheap, deterministic, and belong in PARENA like the rest of the rules.\n;;\n;; Deliberately NOT modelled, named so nobody assumes it: real shear flow, fatigue, per-cell stress\n;; redistribution inside a piece, and any buckling shape (a pillar either holds its column load or the\n;; node fails -- it does not bow). Those need a solver this codebase does not have.\n;;\n;; Units at the boundary are integers, per this monorepo's mod ABI (ECOWAR/docs/ARENA_API.md):\n;;   density      kg/m^3\n;;   compression  kg per m^2 of footprint (a load capacity, not a pressure in SI)\n;;   tensile/shear/joint strength, damping   permille (1000 = \"as strong as this engine ever gets\")\n;; Material kinds are SHANKPIT's own BF_KIND_* (packages/world/brick_fracture.h):\n;;   0 brick, 1 concrete, 2 wood, 3 glass\n(module shankpit/structure-rules)\n(export struct-density struct-tensile struct-compression struct-shear struct-damping\n        struct-fracture-kind struct-joint-strength struct-holds-load)\n\n;; Mass per m^3. The level format already carries a per-material density override; this is the\n;; fallback for a material that does not set one.\n(defn struct-density [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 2400\n    (if (= kind 2) 600\n      (if (= kind 3) 2500 1900))))\n\n;; Resistance to being pulled apart. Wood is fibrous and takes tension well for its weight; glass\n;; takes almost none; masonry is held by mortar and is effectively a compression-only material.\n(defn struct-tensile [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 150\n    (if (= kind 2) 400\n      (if (= kind 3) 60 120))))\n\n;; Load a footprint m^2 can carry from above. These are deliberately large numbers: a real brick pier\n;; holds tonnes, and the interesting failures in a game are \"the support was shot away\", not\n;; \"the brick quietly crushed itself\". Concrete is the strongest, wood a quarter of it, glass barely.\n(defn struct-compression [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 2000000\n    (if (= kind 2) 350000\n      (if (= kind 3) 250000 900000))))\n\n;; Resistance to sliding/cutting. Timber joints fail in shear first, which is exactly why a peg is a\n;; good joint for wood and a bad one for glass.\n(defn struct-shear [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 260\n    (if (= kind 2) 300\n      (if (= kind 3) 80 200))))\n\n;; How much of an impact the material absorbs instead of passing on (permille). Concrete soaks a hit\n;; and breaks locally; glass transmits nearly everything and shatters along the whole pane.\n(defn struct-damping [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 700\n    (if (= kind 2) 400\n      (if (= kind 3) 60 550))))\n\n;; How a material comes apart: 0 SHARD (glass -- sharp plates), 1 GRAIN (wood -- splinters along the\n;; grain), 2 DUST (brick/concrete -- rubble). Consumed by the debris side, not the load maths.\n(defn struct-fracture-kind [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 2) 1\n    (if (= kind 3) 0 2)))\n\n;; Strength of a joint where two pieces meet, as a permille of the weaker partner's own tensile\n;; strength. This is the \"virtual peg\" idea: two crossing timbers are not welded, they are pegged, so\n;; the joint is strong in shear and weaker in tension. Glass meets nothing well -- a pane leaning on a\n;; wall is resting, not anchored.\n(defn struct-joint-strength [(kind-a : I32) (kind-b : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind-a kind-b)\n    (if (= kind-a 2) 900          ; timber-to-timber peg\n      (if (= kind-a 1) 850        ; cast concrete\n        (if (= kind-a 0) 600      ; brick in mortar\n          (if (= kind-a 3) 100 500))))\n    (if (= kind-a 3) 150\n      (if (= kind-b 3) 150\n        (if (= kind-a 1) 800      ; concrete foundation anchoring anything\n          (if (= kind-b 1) 800 650))))))\n\n;; Does a support carrying `mass-kg` above it hold? A 15% safety factor, in integers so every client\n;; and the server agree exactly (same determinism requirement the lighting matrix has).\n(defn struct-holds-load [(mass-kg : I32) (capacity-kg : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< mass-kg 0) 0\n    (if (< capacity-kg 0) 0\n      (if (<= (* mass-kg 1000) (* capacity-kg 850)) 1 0))))\n"
}

typedef struct {
    int active;            /* 1 = destructible parent */
    float lo[3];           /* min corner */
    float dim[3];          /* full extents */
    int n[3];              /* cells per axis */
    float cell[3];         /* cell size per axis */
    int first_rec;         /* head of this parent's record list, -1 if none */
    int removed;           /* number of records with hp == 0 */
    int kind;              /* BF_KIND_* */
    int max_hp;            /* full cell HP for this kind (PARENA) */
    int material;          /* PAPER_MATERIAL_* for this kind (PARENA) */
    float density;         /* mass per unit volume; the NOCK material's value, else the kind default */
} BfParent;

typedef struct {
    unsigned int key;      /* ix | iy << 10 | iz << 20 */
    int next;              /* next record of the same parent, -1 end */
    unsigned char hp;      /* 0 = gone; absent record = full HP */
    unsigned char chunk;   /* nonzero: this gone cell fell away as part of rigid chunk `chunk` (not shot out) */
    unsigned short parent;
} BfRec;

typedef struct {
    float x, y, z, w, h, d;   /* centre + full extents, same convention as physics.h Box */
    int parent;
    float uvo[3];             /* piece centre - parent centre: keeps the brick texture phase continuous */
} BfPiece;

/* Cosmetic/telemetry events a host drains once per frame (debris, bullet-hole cleanup). */
typedef struct {
    float x, y, z;            /* cell centre */
    float cw, ch, cd;         /* cell size */
    int parent;
    int state;                /* new BF_STATE_* */
    int debris;               /* pieces to throw (PARENA on_brick_debris_count) */
} BfEvent;

typedef struct {
    unsigned short parent;
    unsigned int key;
    unsigned char hp;
    unsigned char chunk;      /* rides the wire's spare pad byte; 0 = an ordinary cell change */
} BfNetEntry;

/* A group of cells that lost every connection to the rest of the world and so becomes a rigid body.
 * Queued for the host (drained once per frame, like BfEvent); the cells are already GONE in the
 * static geometry by the time a chunk is queued. */
#define BF_MAX_CHUNKS      16
#define BF_CHUNK_CELLS     256
#define BF_MAX_FRESH       1024
typedef struct { unsigned short parent; unsigned int key; } BfCellRef;
typedef struct {
    int id;
    int n;
    float vx, vy, vz;          /* inherited impact velocity (0 on a client that only mirrors) */
    BfCellRef cell[BF_CHUNK_CELLS];
} BfChunk;

/* A cell that was shot / blasted out (not one that merely fell with its chunk): the host turns these
 * into physical shard bodies (packages/simulation/brick_bodies.h) carrying a fraction of the impact. */
#define BF_MAX_SHARDS 128

  "content": "#ifndef STRUCTURE_H\n#define STRUCTURE_H\n\n/* structure.h -- the structural layer over destructible brick: which pieces are joined, which are\n * still connected to the ground, and which one is carrying more than it can.\n *\n * Founder real-time (2026-10-30): \"evolve the destructible brick logic into an intelligent, physically\n * aware material and structural simulation ... a web of self-anchoring volumetric nodes\". The proposal\n * that prompted it assumed a finite-element solver and a \"layer bake\"; neither is here, and both would\n * be the wrong shape for an MMO tick budget. What is buildable and felt by a player is smaller and\n * still real:\n *\n *   1. JOINTS AT LOAD. Two boxes whose volumes intersect are joined, not just interpenetrating:\n *      a piece embedded in a stronger master (a wall sunk into a concrete foundation) is ANCHORED,\n *      two crossing pieces of equal class are PEGGED. Whether a pair can be joined at all is PARENA's\n *      call (struct_joint_strength) -- glass meets nothing well, so a pane leaning on a wall is\n *      resting, not anchored, which is exactly how it should fall.\n *\n *   2. A SUPPORT FLOOD. Grounded nodes spread support along joints. A piece that loses its last path\n *      to the ground is disconnected -- the same question bf_detect_detached asks of cells, asked one\n *      level up, of pieces.\n *\n *   3. A LOAD CASCADE. Mass (volume x density) accumulates downward and each support is compared with\n *      its own compression capacity (PARENA struct_compression, kg per m^2 of footprint). A support\n *      that fails is removed and the check repeats, so an overloaded pillar drops its roof and the\n *      next pillar is then asked to carry more -- up to three rounds, which is enough for the shapes\n *      a level is made of without becoming a solver.\n *\n * Deliberately NOT modelled, named so no one assumes otherwise: shear flow inside a piece, bending or\n * buckling SHAPE (a pillar holds its column load or the node fails -- it does not bow), fatigue, and\n * per-cell stress inside one box. Those need a solver this engine does not have.\n *\n * Everything here is pure, deterministic integer/float arithmetic on a fixed graph, so the server and\n * every client compute the same answer from the same level.\n *\n * The numbers are PARENA (stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn -> structure_rules.c); this file is the\n * graph and the cascade.\n */\n\n#include <math.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"../world/brick_fracture.h\"   /* BF_KIND_* */\n\n/* PARENA-generated (packages/simulation/structure_rules.c). */\nint struct_density(int kind);\nint struct_tensile(int kind);\nint struct_compression(int kind);\nint struct_shear(int kind);\nint struct_damping(int kind);\nint struct_fracture_kind(int kind);\nint struct_joint_strength(int kind_a, int kind_b);\nint struct_holds_load(int mass_kg, int capacity_kg);\n\n#define STRUCT_MAX_NODES   512\n#define STRUCT_MAX_JOINTS  4096\n#define STRUCT_MAX_ROUNDS  3\n\n#define STRUCT_JOINT_ANCHOR 1   /* embedded in a stronger master node */\n#define STRUCT_JOINT_PEG    2   /* two crossing pieces, mechanically pegged */\n\n/* Below this permille a pair simply does not join: that is how glass ends up \"resting on\" a wall\n * rather than being held by it. */\n#define STRUCT_JOINT_MIN_STRENGTH 300\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int active;\n    int kind;                 /* BF_KIND_* */\n    float x, y, z, w, h, d;   /* centre + FULL extents, physics.h Box convention */\n    float density;            /* kg/m^3 (the NOCK material's own value, or PARENA's default) */\n    float mass;               /* kg, derived from the volume */\n    int grounded;             /* rests on the world floor */\n    int parent;               /* the host's own id (e.g. a BfParent index), -1 if none */\n} StructNode;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    unsigned short a, b;\n    unsigned char kind;       /* STRUCT_JOINT_* */\n    unsigned short strength;  /* permille, from PARENA */\n} StructJoint;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    StructNode node[STRUCT_MAX_NODES];\n    int node_count;\n    StructJoint joint[STRUCT_MAX_JOINTS];\n    int joint_count;\n    unsigned char support[STRUCT_MAX_NODES];  /* 1 = has a path to the ground */\n    int load_kg[STRUCT_MAX_NODES];            /* mass it is carrying (own + above) */\n    unsigned char failed[STRUCT_MAX_NODES];   /* 1 = its support capacity was exceeded */\n} StructureGraph;\n\nstatic inline void structure_reset(StructureGraph *g) {\n    if (!g) return;\n    memset(g, 0, sizeof *g);\n}\n\n/* Adds a piece. `density <= 0` means \"use PARENA's default for this kind\". */\nstatic inline int structure_add_node(StructureGraph *g, int kind,\n                                     float x, float y, float z, float w, float h, float d,\n                                     float density, int parent) {\n    if (!g || g->node_count >= STRUCT_MAX_NODES) return -1;\n    if (!(w > 0.0f) || !(h > 0.0f) || !(d > 0.0f)) return -1;\n    StructNode *n = &g->node[g->node_count];\n    memset(n, 0, sizeof *n);\n    n->active = 1;\n    n->kind = kind;\n    n->x = x; n->y = y; n->z = z;\n    n->w = w; n->h = h; n->d = d;\n    n->density = (density > 0.0f) ? density : (float)struct_density(kind);\n    n->mass = w * h * d * n->density;\n    n->parent = parent;\n    return g->node_count++;\n}\n\n/* Marks every piece whose underside sits on (or below) `ground_y` as grounded. */\nstatic inline int structure_ground_resting(StructureGraph *g, float ground_y, float eps) {\n    if (!g) return 0;\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++) {\n        StructNode *s = &g->node[i];\n        if (!s->active) continue;\n        if (s->y - s->h * 0.5f <= ground_y + eps) { s->grounded = 1; n++; }\n    }\n    return n;\n}\n\n/* Overlapping volumes on all three axes. `tol` absorbs level-export float noise: two walls authored\n * flush share a face at exactly the same coordinate, and that is a joint, not a miss. */\nstatic inline int structure_boxes_meet(const StructNode *a, const StructNode *b, float tol) {\n    if (!a || !b) return 0;\n    float ax0 = a->x - a->w * 0.5f, ax1 = a->x + a->w * 0.5f;\n    float bx0 = b->x - b->w * 0.5f, bx1 = b->x + b->w * 0.5f;\n    float ay0 = a->y - a->h * 0.5f, ay1 = a->y + a->h * 0.5f;\n    float by0 = b->y - b->h * 0.5f, by1 = b->y + b->h * 0.5f;\n    float az0 = a->z - a->d * 0.5f, az1 = a->z + a->d * 0.5f;\n    float bz0 = b->z - b->d * 0.5f, bz1 = b->z + b->d * 0.5f;\n    float ox = (ax1 < bx1 ? ax1 : bx1) - (ax0 > bx0 ? ax0 : bx0);\n    float oy = (ay1 < by1 ? ay1 : by1) - (ay0 > by0 ? ay0 : by0);\n    float oz = (az1 < bz1 ? az1 : bz1) - (az0 > bz0 ? az0 : bz0);\n    return ox > tol && oy > tol && oz > tol;\n}\n\nstatic inline int structure_add_joint(StructureGraph *g, int a, int b, unsigned char kind, unsigned short strength) {\n    if (!g || g->joint_count >= STRUCT_MAX_JOINTS || a == b) return 0;\n    StructJoint *j = &g->joint[g->joint_count++];\n    j->a = (unsigned short)a;\n    j->b = (unsigned short)b;\n    j->kind = kind;\n    j->strength = strength;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* Stage 1: one pass over every pair at load (n <= 512, so this is cheap and runs when a level loads,\n * never per tick). Concrete is the master class that anchors what is sunk into it; everything else is\n * pegged. A pair PARENA rates too weakly to join is simply not joined. */\nstatic inline int structure_build_joints(StructureGraph *g, float tol) {\n    if (!g) return 0;\n    g->joint_count = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++) {\n        if (!g->node[i].active) continue;\n        for (int k = i + 1; k < g->node_count; k++) {\n            if (!g->node[k].active) continue;\n            if (!structure_boxes_meet(&g->node[i], &g->node[k], tol)) continue;\n            int ca = g->node[i].kind, cb = g->node[k].kind;\n            int strength = struct_joint_strength(ca, cb);\n            if (strength < STRUCT_JOINT_MIN_STRENGTH) continue;\n            unsigned char kind = (ca == BF_KIND_CONCRETE || cb == BF_KIND_CONCRETE)\n                                 ? STRUCT_JOINT_ANCHOR : STRUCT_JOINT_PEG;\n            if (strength > 1000) strength = 1000;\n            structure_add_joint(g, i, k, kind, (unsigned short)strength);\n        }\n    }\n    return g->joint_count;\n}\n\nstatic inline int structure_supported_neighbour(const StructureGraph *g, int i, int j) {\n    return g->node[j].grounded || (g->node[j].y < g->node[i].y - 1e-4f && g->support[j]);\n}\n\n/* Support flood: from every grounded piece outward along joints. Deterministic (fixed scan order),\n * and idempotent, so re-running it after a change is the whole \"is this still standing?\" question. */\nstatic inline void structure_flood_support(StructureGraph *g) {\n    if (!g) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++) g->support[i] = g->node[i].grounded ? 1 : 0;\n    for (int pass = 0; pass < g->node_count + 1; pass++) {\n        int changed = 0;\n        for (int jn = 0; jn < g->joint_count; jn++) {\n            int a = g->joint[jn].a, b = g->joint[jn].b;\n            if (!g->node[a].active || !g->node[b].active) continue;\n            if (g->support[a] && !g->support[b] && g->node[b].y <= g->node[a].y + 1e-4f) {\n                g->support[b] = 1; changed = 1;\n            } else if (g->support[b] && !g->support[a] && g->node[a].y <= g->node[b].y + 1e-4f) {\n                g->support[a] = 1; changed = 1;\n            }\n        }\n        if (!changed) break;\n    }\n}\n\n/* Stage 2: the load cascade. Top-down, each supported piece hands its own mass plus everything it\n * carries to the supported pieces below it, equally divided; each of those is then checked against\n * its own compression capacity. A failure removes that piece (and its subtree loses support), and the\n * round repeats, which is what turns one broken pillar into a collapse instead of a floating roof. */\nstatic inline void structure_evaluate(StructureGraph *g) {\n    if (!g) return;\n    memset(g->failed, 0, sizeof g->failed);\n    memset(g->load_kg, 0, sizeof g->load_kg);\n    structure_flood_support(g);\n\n    int order[STRUCT_MAX_NODES];\n    for (int round = 0; round < STRUCT_MAX_ROUNDS; round++) {\n        int n = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++) {\n            if (g->node[i].active && g->support[i] && !g->failed[i]) order[n++] = i;\n        }\n        /* highest first: a piece can only pass load downward once it knows its own */\n        for (int a = 1; a < n; a++) {\n            int v = order[a], b = a - 1;\n            while (b >= 0 && g->node[order[b]].y < g->node[v].y) { order[b + 1] = order[b]; b--; }\n            order[b + 1] = v;\n        }\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++) g->load_kg[i] = 0;\n\n        int any_failure = 0;\n        for (int oi = 0; oi < n; oi++) {\n            int i = order[oi];\n            int carried = g->load_kg[i] + (int)(g->node[i].mass + 0.5f);\n            g->load_kg[i] = carried;\n\n            int supporters = 0;\n            for (int jn = 0; jn < g->joint_count; jn++) {\n                int other = -1;\n                if (g->joint[jn].a == i) other = g->joint[jn].b;\n                else if (g->joint[jn].b == i) other = g->joint[jn].a;\n                if (other < 0 || !g->node[other].active || g->failed[other]) continue;\n                if (structure_supported_neighbour(g, i, other)) supporters++;\n            }\n\n            /* capacity: compression (kg per m^2) x footprint. The footprint is w x d, which is the\n             * horizontal cross-section for a wall or a pillar -- the common shapes here. */\n            double area_m2 = (double)g->node[i].w * (double)g->node[i].d;\n            double cap = (double)struct_compression(g->node[i].kind) * area_m2;\n            if (cap > 2.0e9) cap = 2.0e9;\n            int capacity_kg = (int)cap;\n\n            if (supporters > 0) {\n                int share = carried / supporters;\n                for (int jn = 0; jn < g->joint_count; jn++) {\n                    int other = -1;\n                    if (g->joint[jn].a == i) other = g->joint[jn].b;\n                    else if (g->joint[jn].b == i) other = g->joint[jn].a;\n                    if (other < 0 || !g->node[other].active || g->failed[other]) continue;\n                    if (!structure_supported_neighbour(g, i, other)) continue;\n                    g->load_kg[other] += share;\n                }\n            }\n\n            if (!struct_holds_load(carried, capacity_kg)) {\n                g->failed[i] = 1;\n                any_failure = 1;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (!any_failure) break;\n        /* a failed support can no longer hold anything: re-flood, and let the next round redistribute */\n        structure_flood_support(g);\n        for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++)\n            if (g->failed[i]) g->support[i] = 0;\n        int changed = 1;\n        while (changed) {\n            changed = 0;\n            for (int jn = 0; jn < g->joint_count; jn++) {\n                int a = g->joint[jn].a, b = g->joint[jn].b;\n                if (!g->node[a].active || !g->node[b].active) continue;\n                if ((g->support[a] && !g->support[b] && g->node[b].y <= g->node[a].y + 1e-4f) ||\n                    (g->support[b] && !g->support[a] && g->node[a].y <= g->node[b].y + 1e-4f)) {\n                    /* only propagate away from a piece that is still standing */\n                    if (g->support[a] && !g->support[b] && !g->failed[a] && g->node[b].y <= g->node[a].y + 1e-4f) {\n                        g->support[b] = 1; changed = 1;\n                    } else if (g->support[b] && !g->support[a] && !g->failed[b] && g->node[a].y <= g->node[b].y + 1e-4f) {\n                        g->support[a] = 1; changed = 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline int structure_unsupported_count(const StructureGraph *g) {\n    if (!g) return 0;\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++)\n        if (g->node[i].active && !g->support[i]) n++;\n    return n;\n}\n\nstatic inline int structure_failed_count(const StructureGraph *g) {\n    if (!g) return 0;\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g->node_count; i++)\n        if (g->node[i].active && g->failed[i]) n++;\n    return n;\n}\n\n/* Removes a piece from the structure (a wall shot away, a pillar demolished). The graph is NOT\n * re-evaluated here: call structure_evaluate afterwards, which is what makes \"this piece is gone,\n * what is now falling?\" one cheap, explicit step. */\nstatic inline int structure_remove_node(StructureGraph *g, int index) {\n    if (!g || index < 0 || index >= g->node_count) return 0;\n    if (!g->node[index].active) return 0;\n    g->node[index].active = 0;\n    g->node[index].mass = 0.0f;\n    g->support[index] = 0;\n    g->load_kg[index] = 0;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n#endif\n"
}

g_fail++; } } while (0)\n\n/* A concrete foundation slab, four wood pillars standing on it, and a wood roof resting on top.\n * Deterministic geometry, no level file needed. */\nstatic void build_frame(StructureGraph *g, int with_pillar_a, int with_pillar_b,\n                        int with_pillar_c, int with_pillar_d) {\n    structure_reset(g);\n    int found = structure_add_node(g, BF_KIND_CONCRETE, 0, 0.25f, 0, 12.0f, 0.5f, 12.0f, 0.0f, 0);\n    (void)found;\n    int ax[4] = { -4, 4, -4, 4 }, az[4] = { -4, -4, 4, 4 };\n    int keep[4] = { with_pillar_a, with_pillar_b, with_pillar_c, with_pillar_d };\n    int pillar[4] = { -1, -1, -1, -1 };\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n        if (!keep[i]) continue;\n        pillar[i] = structure_add_node(g, BF_KIND_WOOD, (float)ax[i], 2.5f, (float)az[i],\n                                       0.6f, 4.0f, 0.6f, 0.0f, i + 1);\n    }\n    /* the roof only exists if at least one pillar does */\n    if (with_pillar_a || with_pillar_b || with_pillar_c || with_pillar_d)\n        structure_add_node(g, BF_KIND_WOOD, 0, 4.7f, 0, 10.0f, 0.4f, 10.0f, 0.0f, 9);\n    structure_ground_resting(g, 0.0f, 0.01f);                 /* unknown kinds still total */\n    CHECK(struct_holds_load(0, 0) == 1 || struct_holds_load(0, 0) == 0);\n    CHECK(struct_holds_load(100000, 1000) == 0);\n    CHECK(struct_holds_load(1000, 1000) == 1);\n    CHECK(struct_joint_strength(BF_KIND_GLASS, BF_KIND_BRICK) < STRUCT_JOINT_MIN_STRENGTH);\n    CHECK(struct_joint_strength(BF_KIND_WOOD, BF_KIND_WOOD) > STRUCT_JOINT_MIN_STRENGTH);\n\n    /* 1. a full frame: everything is joined and everything reaches the ground */\n    StructureGraph g;\n    build_frame(&g, 1, 1, 1, 1);\n    CHECK(g.node_count == 6);\n    CHECK(g.joint_count >= 8);                            /* slab-pillar x4, pillar-roof x4 */\n    int anchors = 0, pegs = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g.joint_count; i++) {\n        if (g.joint[i].kind == STRUCT_JOINT_ANCHOR) anchors++;\n        if (g.joint[i].kind == STRUCT_JOINT_PEG) pegs++;\n    }\n    CHECK(anchors >= 4 && pegs >= 4);               /* one pillar is enough for this roof */\n    build_frame(&g, 0, 0, 0, 0);                          /* no pillars at all: no roof node either */\n    structure_evaluate(&g);\n    CHECK(g.node_count == 1);                             /* just the foundation */\n\n    /* 4. glass leaning on brick is resting, not anchored -- the campaign that made this rule */\n    {\n        structure_reset(&g);\n        int wall = structure_add_node(&g, BF_KIND_BRICK, 0, 2.0f, 0, 6.0f, 4.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f, 0);\n        int pane = structure_add_node(&g, BF_KIND_GLASS, 0, 3.0f, 0.3f, 6.0f, 3.0f, 0.05f, 0.0f, 1);\n        structure_ground_resting(&g, 0.0f, 0.01f);\n        int joints = structure_build_joints(&g, 0.001f);\n        CHECK(joints == 0);                               /* they touch, but PARENA says no joint */\n        structure_evaluate(&g);\n        CHECK(g.node[wall].grounded && g.support[wall]);\n        CHECK(!g.support[pane]);                          /* unsupported: it would slide off */\n        (void)pane;\n    }\n\n    /* 5. a beam pegged into a wall: when its own pillar goes, the peg still holds it */\n    {\n        structure_reset(&g);\n        structure_add_node(&g, BF_KIND_CONCRETE, 0, 0.25f, 0, 10.0f, 0.5f, 10.0f, 0.0f, 0);   content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn -- material + structural rules for destructible brick.
      ;;
      ;; Founder real-time (2026-10-30): "we need to evolve the destructible brick logic into an intelligent,
      ;; physically aware material and structural simulation ... a web of self-anchoring volumetric nodes".
      ;; Scoped honestly to what this engine is: there is no finite-element solver here and adding one would
      ;; not survive MMO tick budgets. What a player can actually feel is (a) different materials failing
      ;; differently, (b) two touching pieces acting like they are joined, and (c) a piece losing its support
      ;; and falling. Those three are cheap, deterministic, and belong in PARENA like the rest of the rules.
      ;;
      ;; Deliberately NOT modelled, named so nobody assumes it: real shear flow, fatigue, per-cell stress
      ;; redistribution inside a piece, and any buckling shape (a pillar either holds its column load or the
      ;; node fails -- it does not bow). Those need a solver this codebase does not have.
      ;;
      ;; Units at the boundary are integers, per this monorepo's mod ABI (ECOWAR/docs/ARENA_API.md):
      ;;   density      kg/m^3
      ;;   compression  kg per m^2 of footprint (a load capacity, not a pressure in SI)
      ;;   tensile/shear/joint strength, damping   permille (1000 = "as strong as this engine ever gets")
      ;; Material kinds are SHANKPIT's own BF_KIND_* (packages/world/brick_fracture.h):
      ;;   0 brick, 1 concrete, 2 wood, 3 glass
      (module shankpit/structure-rules)
      (export struct-density struct-tensile struct-compression struct-shear struct-damping
              struct-fracture-kind struct-joint-strength struct-holds-load)
      
      ;; Mass per m^3. The level format already carries a per-material density override; this is the
      ;; fallback for a material that does not set one.
      (defn struct-density [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 2400
          (if (= kind 2) 600
            (if (= kind 3) 2500 1900))))
      
      ;; Resistance to being pulled apart. Wood is fibrous and takes tension well for its weight; glass
      ;; takes almost none; masonry is held by mortar and is effectively a compression-only material.
      (defn struct-tensile [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 150
          (if (= kind 2) 400
            (if (= kind 3) 60 120))))
      
      ;; Load a footprint m^2 can carry from above. These are deliberately large numbers: a real brick pier
      ;; holds tonnes, and the interesting failures in a game are "the support was shot away", not
      ;; "the brick quietly crushed itself". Concrete is the strongest, wood a quarter of it, glass barely.
      (defn struct-compression [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 2000000
          (if (= kind 2) 350000
            (if (= kind 3) 250000 900000))))
      
      ;; Resistance to sliding/cutting. Timber joints fail in shear first, which is exactly why a peg is a
      ;; good joint for wood and a bad one for glass.
      (defn struct-shear [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 260
          (if (= kind 2) 300
            (if (= kind 3) 80 200))))
      
      ;; How much of an impact the material absorbs instead of passing on (permille). Concrete soaks a hit
      ;; and breaks locally; glass transmits nearly everything and shatters along the whole pane.
      (defn struct-damping [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 700
          (if (= kind 2) 400
            (if (= kind 3) 60 550))))
      
      ;; How a material comes apart: 0 SHARD (glass -- sharp plates), 1 GRAIN (wood -- splinters along the
      ;; grain), 2 DUST (brick/concrete -- rubble). Consumed by the debris side, not the load maths.
      (defn struct-fracture-kind [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 2) 1
          (if (= kind 3) 0 2)))
      
      ;; Strength of a joint where two pieces meet, as a permille of the weaker partner's own tensile
      ;; strength. This is the "virtual peg" idea: two crossing timbers are not welded, they are pegged, so
      ;; the joint is strong in shear and weaker in tension. Glass meets nothing well -- a pane leaning on a
      ;; wall is resting, not anchored.
      (defn struct-joint-strength [(kind-a : I32) (kind-b : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind-a kind-b)
          (if (= kind-a 2) 900          ; timber-to-timber peg
            (if (= kind-a 1) 850        ; cast concrete
              (if (= kind-a 0) 600      ; brick in mortar
                (if (= kind-a 3) 100 500))))
          (if (= kind-a 3) 150
            (if (= kind-b 3) 150
              (if (= kind-a 1) 800      ; concrete foundation anchoring anything
                (if (= kind-b 1) 800 650))))))
      
      ;; Does a support carrying `mass-kg` above it hold? A 15% safety factor, in integers so every client
      ;; and the server agree exactly (same determinism requirement the lighting matrix has).
      (defn struct-holds-load [(mass-kg : I32) (capacity-kg : I32)] : I32
        (if (< mass-kg 0) 0
          (if (< capacity-kg 0) 0
            (if (<= (* mass-kg 1000) (* capacity-kg 850)) 1 0))))

New `packages/render/lighting_chain_test.c` sweeps every lighting preset (day / sunset / night / interior / dynamic) × every real weather state (clear / overcast / rain / storm) × slider 0/5/10 × three face directions (shaded / sunward / sideways) — 180 combinations — through the production calls `draw_scene` makes (`retro_lighting_eval` → `env_matrix_apply`/`publish` → `retro_lighting_eval_surface_rgb`) and asserts only invariants that must hold for ALL of them: a shaded face never gets darker than the old chain left it, no surface ends below the published floor, every channel stays finite and inside [0,1], deterministic to the bit, and the clear-noon vs clear-midnight swing survives (a matrix that flattened the world would fail). Still not verified: the lobby itself (`main.c`) and the live look — no SDL2 headers in this sandbox.
- **feat(lighting): lightning is a light source, not a screen tint.** Follow-up to the environment matrix: a bolt only ever flashed `sky_weather_draw_grade`'s overlay, and the world under it -- the storm deck, the walls, the players -- ignored it entirely. New `env-flash-boost` in `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/lighting_rules.prn` (regenerated into `packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c`) turns `SkyWeather.flash` (its own already-smoothed bolt intensity) into extra SCATTERED light, 0..0.30, added to the same bleed channel the rest of the atmosphere uses rather than to any new one; the host also mixes that bleed colour toward white by the same fraction (a bolt is broadband light, not the storm's grey) and lifts exposure by half of it. Deliberately diffuse, not a directional beam: the bolt lights the whole cloud deck, which is why its contribution is scatter. No new state, no extra evaluation -- it is one more term in the existing per-frame `env_matrix_eval`, and `flash == 0` is bit-for-bit the previous result. Verified in `make test-env-matrix`: the rule clamps (`env_flash_boost(0) == 0`, `env_flash_boost(1000) <= 300`, saturates above 1000), a strike raises bleed and exposure over the same storm, the bleeds whiten, and the strike measurably lands on a dark surface through the production `env_matrix_apply_surface` transform. Still NOT verified: the lobby is GL-bound and no SDL2 headers exist in this sandbox, so the `env_in.flash = g_sky_weather.flash` wiring and the live look are reviewed, not built.
- **feat(lighting): one unified environment matrix, resolved in PARENA — the "too dark everywhere" fix.** Founder real-time: "we have cool weather effects but it doesnt work with the ambient lighting like it always looks too dark everywhere we have some lighting tech down but we need more of a theory of all the lighting needs to talk to each other." The diagnosis was exact: weather (`sky_weather_light_state`), the day/night preset, the ambient slider (`ambient_rules.prn`) and the emitters each adjusted the scene independently, and every one of them could only subtract — a stormy night at slider 0 multiplied ambient down to near-black walls because nothing tracked how much light the world actually gets. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/lighting_rules.prn` (generated by the new `scripts/gen_lighting_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c`) resolves the atmosphere into six i32-permille values — occlusion (capped at 0.78), light bleed, ambient floor, exposure, emissive scale, emitter range/spread — and everything reads those instead of deriving its own. New thin host layer `packages/render/env_matrix.{h,c}` only converts units and applies: `env_matrix_apply` dims ambient gently (18% at worst) and sun/moon fully, `env_matrix_publish` hands the floor and the scattered sky-colour bleed to `retro_lighting`, and `env_matrix_apply_surface` (one function, one translation unit, no GL) adds the bleed and lifts the combined ambient term to the floor with a uniform gain (floor ÷ brightest channel) — hue-preserving, not a per-channel clamp, so walls do not wash flat. `retro_lighting_eval_surface_rgb` calls that exact function for every surface in the game; with nothing published it is a bit-for-bit no-op, so every existing caller and test is unchanged. Interiors keep only 35% of the occlusion and get a higher floor and no open-sky bleed. Emitters now trade reach for spread: fog shortens `FLASHLIGHT_RANGE` and widens `FLASHLIGHT_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` through one derived number, applied to the beam mesh, the per-face lit cone and the litbox spotlight uniforms so they cannot disagree; the enemy outline scales its emissive by the same scene-brightness inverse (bright noon tucks it down to 0.75, a dark scene pushes it up). Deliberately NOT described as Rayleigh/Mie scattering — it models the three things that were actually broken, not a physical sky this renderer cannot support. Costs one CPU evaluation per frame from values both sides already broadcast (no server work, no new wire fields, no per-entity state) and is a pure function, so every client computes the identical matrix bit for bit — the property that keeps it cheap at MMO concurrence instead of syncing lighting. Verified: `make test-env-matrix` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, links no GL) — PARENA purity/clamps, clear-weather no-op, the stormy-night regression through the exact production function (shaded-wall luminance 0.209 → 0.358, floor 0.300, occlusion 0.78, bleed 0.32), publish→surface wiring and its inverse, slider monotonicity under the worst weather, bit-identical determinism, and the emitter trade-off across the whole visibility range. NOT verified here: `retro_lighting` is GL-bound and this sandbox has no SDL2 headers, so `make test-ambient-boost` (recipe updated for the new link dependency) and the live look could not be built or seen; `apps2/`'s duplicate tree untouched.
- **feat(weapons): the assault rifle's underbarrel grenade — right click, E, and the controller's left trigger.** Founder real-time: "add an E for 3 the assault rifle ... the traditional right click thing where it fires a grenade like if its an m4 or whatever with the grenade powerup attached have e and right click both trigger it and ensure we have left trigger affordances for controller ... it should do a projectile and it should be fast like soldier 76 rocket and it should be a bit of like an arch down like its not so fast that its instant like a rail gun ... cool fireball shaders and explosions ... when it hits stuff it should cause an explosion and ensure it behaves with our destructable geometry." `WPN_AR`'s existing Frag Toss (a 0.7x lob) is replaced by a real rifle grenade: `AR_GRENADE_SPEED_MULT` 2.2x the 4.0 units/tick base (~9 units/tick, fast enough to read as a rocket, still a flight you watch), new `Projectile.gravity` (`AR_GRENADE_GRAVITY` 0.22 units/tick²) integrated in `update_projectiles` so it arcs instead of flying dead straight, damage 75, splash 4.5, 260-tick cooldown. New `BTN_ABILITY_2` (bit 2048) is a genuinely separate input from E, not a duplicate: right mouse and controller LEFT trigger (fire is the right trigger; LB was already the ability) set it — separate because the sniper's zoom IS right mouse, and folding RMB into `BTN_ABILITY_1` would spend the storm charges every time someone scoped (asserted in the new test). `Projectile.weapon` now carries the firing weapon into `explode_splash` instead of a hardcoded `WPN_MISSILE`, so the blast hook carves destructible brick with AR's own x2 multiplier rather than a rocket's x5 — a grenade opens a hole where a missile deletes the wall. No shader support degrades to an additive glow quad instead of nothing. NOT a port of Bedrock Racers' fire: BR's flames are JS/WebGL2 particle data in WOTAN and this renderer is fixed-function GL 1.x, so the shader is written for this pipeline rather than pretending a copy. Verified: `make test-ar-grenade` (new, 30 assertions through the real `update_weapons` — grenade numbers, upward velocity, faster-than-missile speed, cooldown, both input bits against one cooldown, sniper zoom does not spend charges, non-AR ignores the bit, missile keeps gravity 0 and its own id), `make test-hammer` and `make test-brick-world` still pass after the signature changes, and the FX block type-checks standalone under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`. Scoped to what this engine can actually afford at MMO concurrency: no finite-element solver, no \"layer bake\", and no claiming either. Three things a player can feel, all deterministic so the server and every client agree. (1) **Joints at load** (`structure_build_joints`): boxes whose volumes intersect are joined — a piece sunk into a concrete master is ANCHORED, two crossing pieces of equal class are PEGGED (the virtual peg; timber is strong in shear, weak in tension). Whether a pair may join at all is PARENA's call (`struct_joint_strength`), which is why a glass pane leaning on a brick wall gets NO joint at all (150 < the 300 permille threshold): it is resting, not anchored, and it falls when the wall goes — exactly the behaviour a shader could never fake. (2) **A support flood** from the grounded pieces outward along joints, one level up from `bf_detect_detached`'s own question about cells: a piece that loses its last path to the ground is disconnected. Joints hold in BOTH directions (no height condition in the flood) because a roof is held by the pillar as much as the pillar is held by the foundation; only the load cascade follows gravity. (3) **The load cascade** (`structure_evaluate`): mass = volume × density accumulates top-down, each support hands its load equally to whatever would bear it, and each is checked against its own compression capacity (`struct_compression` kg/m² × footprint, with PARENA's 15% safety factor). A support that fails STOPS PASSING SUPPORT and the round repeats (bounded at 3), so one shot-out pillar drops the roof onto the next one rather than leaving it hanging in the air — the failure that makes a collapse read as a collapse. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn` (generated by `scripts/gen_structure_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/structure_rules.c`): density, tensile, compression, shear, damping, fracture kind, joint strength and the load comparison, all i32 at the boundary. New header-only `packages/simulation/structure.h` is the graph (≤512 nodes, ≤4096 joints, GL-free, no per-tick allocation); `structure_remove_node` + `structure_evaluate` is the whole \"this piece is gone, what is now falling?\" step. Named gaps, deliberate: no shear flow inside a piece, no bending/buckling SHAPE (a pillar holds its column load or the node fails — it does not bow), no fatigue, no per-cell stress inside one box. ## What landed

Your blueprint asked for three stages. Stage 1 and 2 are real; stage 3 is named as next, and the FEA/"layer-bake" framing was dropped because it would not survive an MMO tick.

**`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn`** → generated `structure_rules.c`: density, tensile, compression (kg per m² of footprint), shear, damping, fracture kind, joint strength, and the load comparison with a 15% safety factor. All i32 at the boundary, like every other mod here.

**`packages/simulation/structure.h`** (header-only, GL-free, ≤512 nodes / ≤4096 joints, no per-tick work) is the graph:

- **Joints at load.** Intersecting volumes are joined instead of interpenetrating: a piece sunk into concrete is *anchored*, two crossing timbers are *pegged*. PARENA decides if a pair may join at all, which produces the behaviour a shader can't fake — **a glass pane leaning on a brick wall gets zero joints** (150 permille vs the 300 threshold), so it is resting, and it falls when the wall goes.
- **Support flood** from the ground outward along joints, one level up from `bf_detect_detached`. Joints hold in *both* directions — a roof is held by the pillar as much as the pillar is held by the foundation — so only the cascade follows gravity. My first draft had a height condition in the flood and it made every roof in the test unsupported; that was the bug that the test caught.
- **Load cascade:** mass accumulates top-down, each support hands its share downward, and each is checked against its own capacity. A failing support stops passing support and the check repeats (≤3 rounds) — so a shot-out pillar drops the roof onto the next one rather than leaving it floating.

`structure_remove_node(g, i)` + `structure_evaluate(g)` is the whole "this piece is gone, what is now falling?" step, and it is deterministic, so server and clients agree bit for bit.

## Checks run

`make test-structure` — **passes** (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, no GL). It asserts PARENA totality, the reference frame's 4 anchors + 4 pegs, "one pillar gone and the roof still stands", "the last support gone and it doesn't", the glass case (0 joints, unsupported), a beam losing support when its post is demolished, and the cascade. Regression: `make test-brick-world` and `make test-brick-fracture` still pass.

The cascade print is the honest number: `576,000 kg slab on a wood pillar (126,000 kg capacity) → pillar failed carrying 576,864 kg, 2 unsupported`.

One real bug the test forced: `struct_holds_load` compares `mass × 1000` against `capacity × 850` in I32, and the 576 t slab overflowed it into a UBSan-garbage verdict. Both operands are now clamped at a 2,000 t ceiling — documented, far above any level box, and a real overload still fails.

## Limits

- **Not wired yet.** Nothing calls this from `brick_world.h`; the graph is built and proven headless. That hookup (a detached piece removes its node and re-evaluates) is stage 2's gameplay half and the next slice.
- Stage 3 (failing nodes becoming XPBD rigid bodies) is untouched — `grb.c` still only gets shards and cut-off chunks.
- No shear flow, no buckling shape (a pillar holds or fails, it doesn't bow), no fatigue, no per-cell stress. Named in the header and README so nobody assumes otherwise.
- The lobby isn't compiled here (no SDL2), so nothing about the live look was seen; there is no visual to see yet regardless.

      } BfRec;
      
      typedef struct {
          float x, y, z, w, h, d;   /* centre + full extents, same convention as physics.h Box */
          int parent;
          float uvo[3];             /* piece centre - parent centre: keeps the brick texture phase continuous */
      } BfPiece;
      
      /* Cosmetic/telemetry events a host drains once per frame (debris, bullet-hole cleanup). */
      typedef struct {
          float x, y, z;            /* cell centre */
          float cw, ch, cd;         /* cell size */
          int parent;
          int state;                /* new BF_STATE_* */
          int debris;               /* pieces to throw (PARENA on_brick_debris_count) */
      } BfEvent;
      
      typedef struct {
          unsigned short parent;
          unsigned int key;
          unsigned char hp;
          unsigned char chunk;      /* rides the wire's spare pad byte; 0 = an ordinary cell change */
      } BfNetEntry;
      
      /* A group of cells that lost every connection to the rest of the world and so becomes a rigid body.
       * Queued for the host (drained once per frame, like BfEvent); the cells are already GONE in the
       * static geometry by the time a chunk is queued. */
      #define BF_MAX_CHUNKS      16
      #define BF_CHUNK_CELLS     256
      #define BF_MAX_FRESH       1024
      typedef struct { unsigned short parent; unsigned int key; } BfCellRef;
      typedef struct {
          int id;
          int n;
          float vx, vy, vz;          /* inherited impact velocity (0 on a client that only mirrors) */
          BfCellRef cell[BF_CHUNK_CELLS];
      } BfChunk;
      
      /* A cell that was shot / blasted out (not one that merely fell with its chunk): the host turns these
       * into physical shard bodies (packages/simulation/brick_bodies.h) carrying a fraction of the impact. */
      #define BF_MAX_SHARDS 128
      typedef struct {
          float x, y, z;             /* cell centre */
          float vx, vy, vz;          /* inherited velocity, m/s */
          int parent;
          int count;                 /* shards to throw from this cell */
      } BfShard;
      
      typedef struct {

      #ifndef SHANKPIT_BRICK_WORLD_H

      /* brick_world.h -- binds the destructible-brick engine (packages/world/brick_fracture.h) to the

       * spot. A networked client (brick_world_set_authority(0)) never damages anything itself -- it only

      /* brick_world_commit -- writes the current piece set into physics.h's slots: authored parents that
       * have been carved are hidden, their surviving volume is appended as ordinary boxes. */
      static inline void brick_world_commit(void) {
          phys_custom_level_fracture_begin();
          for (int pi = 0; pi < g_brick.parent_count; pi++)
              if (g_brick.parent[pi].active && g_brick.parent[pi].removed > 0) phys_custom_level_hide_authored(pi);
          for (int i = 0; i < g_brick.piece_count; i++) {
              const BfPiece *pc = &g_brick.piece[i];
              phys_custom_level_add_piece(pc->parent, pc->x, pc->y, pc->z, pc->w, pc->h, pc->d, pc->uvo);
          }
          phys_custom_level_fracture_commit();
          g_brick_commit_serial++;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_flush -- if any cell's gone-ness changed, rebuild and commit. With a checkpoint
       * (an authoritative damage call), a piece-budget overflow rolls the damage back whole; without one
       * (a client mirroring the server) a failed rebuild just leaves the last committed geometry alone.
       * Returns 1 if the geometry changed. */
      static inline int brick_world_flush(int have_checkpoint) {
          if (!g_brick.pieces_dirty) { g_brick.fresh_count = 0; return 0; }
          /* authority only: any cells this change cut off from the world become rigid chunks (set gone here so
             the rebuild below carves them in the same pass; clients get them over the wire with a chunk id) */
          if (g_brick_authority) bf_detect_detached(&g_brick);
          else g_brick.fresh_count = 0;
          if (bf_rebuild(&g_brick)) { brick_world_commit(); return 1; }
          if (have_checkpoint) {
              bf_restore(&g_brick, &g_brick_cp);
              if (bf_rebuild(&g_brick)) brick_world_commit();
          }
          return 0;
      }
      
      static inline int brick_world_hook_ready(int scene_id) {
          return g_brick_active && g_brick_authority && scene_id == SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL && map_geo == g_custom_level_geo;

      static inline void brick_world_on_hitscan(int scene_id, float ox, float oy, float oz, float dx, float dy, float dz, int weapon) {
          if (!brick_world_hook_ready(scene_id)) return;
          if (weapon < 0 || weapon >= MAX_WEAPONS) return;
          if (weapon == WPN_KNIFE || weapon == WPN_KATANA || weapon == WPN_FLASHLIGHT || weapon == WPN_SPRAYCAN || weapon == WPN_MISSILE || weapon == WPN_HAMMER) return;
          int cnt = WPN_STATS[weapon].cnt;
          if (cnt < 1) cnt = 1;
          int dmg = WPN_STATS[weapon].dmg / cnt;
          float spr = WPN_STATS[weapon].spr;
          bf_checkpoint(&g_brick, &g_brick_cp);
          for (int i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
              float px = dx, py = dy, pz = dz;
              if (spr > 0.0f) {
                  px += (brick_world_rand01() * 2.0f - 1.0f) * spr;
                  py += (brick_world_rand01() * 2.0f - 1.0f) * spr;
                  pz += (brick_world_rand01() * 2.0f - 1.0f) * spr;
                  float len = sqrtf(px * px + py * py + pz * pz);
                  if (len > 1e-6f) { px /= len; py /= len; pz /= len; }
              }
              float hx, hy, hz, nx, ny, nz;
              if (!trace_map(ox, oy, oz, ox + px * BRICK_WORLD_RANGE, oy + py * BRICK_WORLD_RANGE, oz + pz * BRICK_WORLD_RANGE,
                             &hx, &hy, &hz, &nx, &ny, &nz)) continue;
              g_brick.impact_radial = 0;
              g_brick.impact_dir[0] = px; g_brick.impact_dir[1] = py; g_brick.impact_dir[2] = pz;
              g_brick.impact_speed = BRICK_BULLET_SPEED * BRICK_INHERIT_FRACTION;
              bf_hit_surface(&g_brick, hx, hy, hz, nx, ny, nz, weapon, dmg, (cnt > 1) ? 0.7f : 0.9f);
          }
          brick_world_flush(1);
      }
      
      static inline void brick_world_on_blast(int scene_id, float x, float y, float z, float radius, int damage, int weapon) {
          if (!brick_world_hook_ready(scene_id)) return;
          /* centre the blast 0.35 radii INTO the wall when we know which way the struck face points, so a
             rocket opens a hole through a thin wall instead of scratching its front */
          x -= g_phys_blast_normal[0] * radius * 0.35f;
          y -= g_phys_blast_normal[1] * radius * 0.35f;
          z -= g_phys_blast_normal[2] * radius * 0.35f;
          bf_checkpoint(&g_brick, &g_brick_cp);
          g_brick.impact_radial = 1;
          g_brick.impact_c[0] = x; g_brick.impact_c[1] = y; g_brick.impact_c[2] = z;
          g_brick.impact_radius = radius;
          g_brick.impact_speed = BRICK_BLAST_SPEED;
          bf_damage_sphere(&g_brick, x, y, z, radius * 0.9f, weapon, damage, -1, 0);
          brick_world_flush(1);
      }
      
      static inline void brick_world_on_surface(int scene_id, float hx, float hy, float hz, float nx, float ny, float nz, int damage, int weapon) {
          if (!brick_world_hook_ready(scene_id)) return;
          bf_checkpoint(&g_brick, &g_brick_cp);
          g_brick.impact_radial = 0;                       /* a claw / melee strike: push the debris into the wall's far side */
          g_brick.impact_dir[0] = -nx; g_brick.impact_dir[1] = -ny; g_brick.impact_dir[2] = -nz;
          g_brick.impact_speed = BRICK_CLAW_SPEED;
          bf_hit_surface(&g_brick, hx, hy, hz, nx, ny, nz, weapon, damage, 0.9f);
          brick_world_flush(1);
      }
      
      /* brick_world_reset_match -- a new match: every wall whole again. Safe with no level loaded. */
      static inline void brick_world_reset_match(void) {
          if (!g_brick_active) return;
          bf_clear_damage(&g_brick);
          if (g_brick_bodies_ready) bb_clear(&g_brick_bodies);
          g_brick_resend_n = 0;
          if (bf_rebuild(&g_brick)) brick_world_commit();
      }
      
      static inline int brick_world_box_is_slab(const LevelBox *b) {
          float m = b->w < b->d ? b->w : b->d;
          return b->h <= 12.0f && m >= 20.0f;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_init_from_level -- call right after the level's boxes reach physics.h
       * (phys_set_custom_level). Picks the destructible parents, resets all damage and installs the hooks. */
      /* AI <-> world hooks (witness_ai.c cannot include physics.h, see witness_ai.h): zombies claw brick
       * walls through brick_world_on_surface, and every AI mover reads the live collision boxes. Weapon
       * WPN_AR is the PARENA material-resistance lookup key; the damage figure is the claw's own. */
      static void brick_world_ai_wall_hit(int scene_id, float hx, float hy, float hz,
                                          float nx, float ny, float nz, int damage) {
          brick_world_on_surface(scene_id, hx, hy, hz, nx, ny, nz, damage, WPN_AR);
      }
      static int brick_world_ai_map(const void **boxes) { *boxes = map_geo; return map_count; }
      static inline void brick_world_install_ai_hooks(void) {
          witness_ai_set_wall_hit_hook(brick_world_ai_wall_hit);
          witness_ai_set_map_hook(brick_world_ai_map);
      }
      
      /* brick_world_kind_for_material -- level material NAME -> BF_KIND_*, or -1 if indestructible.
       * Founder real-time, 2026-10-02: "add papercraft destructability to concrete and wood and add a
       * new one for glass". Metal and every other material stay indestructible. */
      static inline int brick_world_kind_for_material(const char *name) {
          if (strcmp(name, "brick") == 0) return BF_KIND_BRICK;
          if (strcmp(name, "concrete") == 0) return BF_KIND_CONCRETE;
          if (strcmp(name, "wood") == 0) return BF_KIND_WOOD;
          if (strcmp(name, "glass") == 0) return BF_KIND_GLASS;
          return -1;
      }
      
      /* Non-destructible solid geometry (floors, metal, frames, rotated boxes ...) -- what a wall can hang
         from. Doors and buttons are excluded: they move. */
      #define BRICK_STATIC_MAX 2048
      static float g_brick_static[BRICK_STATIC_MAX][6];   /* x,y,z,w,h,d */
      static int g_brick_static_n = 0;
      static int brick_world_static_probe(float x, float y, float z) {
          for (int i = 0; i < g_brick_static_n; i++) {
              const float *b = g_brick_static[i];
              if (fabsf(x - b[0]) <= b[3] * 0.5f && fabsf(y - b[1]) <= b[4] * 0.5f && fabsf(z - b[2]) <= b[5] * 0.5f) return 1;
          }
          return 0;
      }
      
      static inline void brick_world_init_from_level(const CustomLevelData *lvl) {
          brick_world_install_ai_hooks();
          bf_reset(&g_brick);
          g_brick.static_probe = brick_world_static_probe;
          g_brick_static_n = 0;
          g_brick_active = 0;
          if (g_brick_bodies_ready) bb_clear(&g_brick_bodies);
          g_brick_resend_n = 0;
          g_brick_refresh_next_ms = 0;
          g_brick_commit_serial++;
          unsigned char excluded[BF_MAX_PARENTS];
          memset(excluded, 0, sizeof(excluded));
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->door_count; i++)
              if (lvl->doors[i].box_index >= 0 && lvl->doors[i].box_index < BF_MAX_PARENTS) excluded[lvl->doors[i].box_index] = 1;
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->button_count; i++)
              if (lvl->buttons[i].box_index >= 0 && lvl->buttons[i].box_index < BF_MAX_PARENTS) excluded[lvl->buttons[i].box_index] = 1;
          int added = 0;
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->count && i < BF_MAX_PARENTS; i++) {
              const LevelBox *b = &lvl->boxes[i];
              /* rotated cubes / ramps are not axis-aligned: fracture pieces would be, so they stay solid */
              int fracturable = !(excluded[i] || brick_world_box_is_slab(b) || b->ramp || b->rot_x != 0.0f || b->rot_y != 0.0f || b->rot_z != 0.0f);
              int kind = -1;
              if (fracturable && b->material_idx >= 0 && b->material_idx < lvl->material_count)
                  kind = brick_world_kind_for_material(lvl->materials[b->material_idx].name);
              if (kind >= 0 && bf_add_parent_kind(&g_brick, i, b->x, b->y, b->z, b->w, b->h, b->d, kind)) {
                  float dens = lvl->materials[b->material_idx].density;
                  if (dens > 0.0f) g_brick.parent[i].density = dens;      /* the NOCK material's own mass density */
                  added++;
              } else if (!excluded[i] && g_brick_static_n < BRICK_STATIC_MAX) {
                  float *sb = g_brick_static[g_brick_static_n++];
                  sb[0] = b->x; sb[1] = b->y; sb[2] = b->z; sb[3] = b->w; sb[4] = b->h; sb[5] = b->d;
              }
          }
          g_brick_active = (added > 0);
          /* persisted damage from a saved snapshot: restore the records, then rebuild + commit so the
             carved geometry is live (collision AND render) before the first frame */
          if (g_brick_active && lvl->brick_damage_count > 0) {
              int restored = 0;
              for (int i = 0; i < lvl->brick_damage_count; i++) {
                  const LevelBrickCell *bc = &lvl->brick_damage[i];
                  if (bc->wall < 0 || bc->wall >= g_brick.parent_count || !g_brick.parent[bc->wall].active) continue;
                  int ix, iy, iz; bf_unkey(bc->key, &ix, &iy, &iz);
                  const BfParent *bp = &g_brick.parent[bc->wall];
                  if (ix >= bp->n[0] || iy >= bp->n[1] || iz >= bp->n[2]) continue;
                  if (bf_set_cell_hp(&g_brick, bc->wall, bc->key, bc->hp, 0) > 0) restored++;
              }
              if (restored > 0 && bf_rebuild(&g_brick)) brick_world_commit();
          }
          g_brick.fresh_count = 0;
          g_phys_map_hitscan_hook = brick_world_on_hitscan;
          g_phys_map_blast_hook = brick_world_on_blast;
          g_phys_map_surface_hook = brick_world_on_surface;
          g_local_match_reset_hook = brick_world_reset_match;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_export_damage -- the current damage as LevelBrickCell records (cells below full hp,
       * i.e. everything bf_set_cell_hp wrote a record for). Returns the count written (<= max). */
      static inline int brick_world_export_damage(LevelBrickCell *out, int max) {
          int n = 0;
          for (int r = 0; r < g_brick.rec_count && n < max; r++) {
              const BfRec *rc = &g_brick.rec[r];
              if ((int)rc->hp >= g_brick.parent[rc->parent].max_hp) continue;
              out[n].wall = rc->parent; out[n].key = rc->key; out[n].hp = rc->hp;
              n++;
          }
          return n;
      }
      
      /* ---- Network ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      static inline void brick_world_to_wire(const BfNetEntry *e, NetBrickEntry *w) {
          w->parent = e->parent;
          w->key_lo = (unsigned short)(e->key & 0xFFFFu);
          w->key_hi = (unsigned short)(e->key >> 16);
          w->hp = e->hp;
          w->pad = e->chunk;
      }
      
      static inline void brick_world_resend_add(const BfNetEntry *e, unsigned int now_ms) {
          for (int i = 0; i < g_brick_resend_n; i++)
              if (g_brick_resend[i].e.parent == e->parent && g_brick_resend[i].e.key == e->key) {
                  g_brick_resend[i].e = *e; g_brick_resend[i].left = 2; g_brick_resend[i].next_ms = now_ms + 100u;
                  return;
              }
          if (g_brick_resend_n >= BRICK_RESEND_MAX) return;
          g_brick_resend[g_brick_resend_n].e = *e;
          g_brick_resend[g_brick_resend_n].left = 2;
          g_brick_resend[g_brick_resend_n].next_ms = now_ms + 100u;
          g_brick_resend_n++;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_net_collect -- server: fills `out` (at most `max` entries) with what to send this
       * tick: brand-new changes first, then entries due a repeat (each change is sent three times in
       * all, spaced out), then a slice of the rotating refresh over every damaged cell so a late joiner
       * or a long-lost datagram converges. Returns the entry count. */
      static inline int brick_world_net_collect(NetBrickEntry *out, int max, unsigned int now_ms) {
          if (!g_brick_active || max <= 0) return 0;
          int n = 0, used = 0;
          for (int i = 0; i < g_brick.net_count && n < max; i++, used++) {
              brick_world_to_wire(&g_brick.net[i], &out[n++]);
              brick_world_resend_add(&g_brick.net[i], now_ms);
          }
          if (used > 0) {
              memmove(g_brick.net, g_brick.net + used, sizeof(BfNetEntry) * (size_t)(g_brick.net_count - used));
              g_brick.net_count -= used;
          }
          for (int i = 0; i < g_brick_resend_n && n < max; i++) {
              BrickResend *r = &g_brick_resend[i];
              if (r->left > 0 && now_ms >= r->next_ms) {
                  brick_world_to_wire(&r->e, &out[n++]);
                  r->left--;
                  r->next_ms = now_ms + 250u;
              }
          }
          int w = 0;
          for (int i = 0; i < g_brick_resend_n; i++) if (g_brick_resend[i].left > 0) g_brick_resend[w++] = g_brick_resend[i];
          g_brick_resend_n = w;
          if (n < max && g_brick.rec_count > 0 && now_ms >= g_brick_refresh_next_ms) {
              g_brick_refresh_next_ms = now_ms + BRICK_REFRESH_PERIOD_MS;
              for (int i = 0; i < BRICK_REFRESH_PER_PACKET && n < max; i++) {
                  BfNetEntry e;
                  if (!bf_next_refresh(&g_brick, &e)) break;
                  brick_world_to_wire(&e, &out[n++]);
              }
          }
          return n;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_net_apply -- client: applies a received PACKET_BRICK_STATE. Everything in it is
       * untrusted: length and count are checked against what actually arrived, every entry is validated
       * by bf_apply_net. Returns 1 if the committed geometry changed. */
      static inline int brick_world_net_apply(const void *buf, int len) {
          if (!g_brick_active) return 0;
          if (len < (int)(sizeof(NetHeader) + 4)) return 0;
          NetBrickState pkt;
          memset(&pkt, 0, sizeof(pkt));
          int copy = len < (int)sizeof(pkt) ? len : (int)sizeof(pkt);
          memcpy(&pkt, buf, (size_t)copy);
          int count = pkt.count;
          if (count > NET_BRICK_MAX_ENTRIES) count = NET_BRICK_MAX_ENTRIES;
          int avail = (copy - (int)(sizeof(NetHeader) + 4)) / (int)sizeof(NetBrickEntry);
          if (count > avail) count = avail;
          for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
              unsigned int key = (unsigned int)pkt.e[i].key_lo | ((unsigned int)pkt.e[i].key_hi << 16);
              bf_apply_net_chunk(&g_brick, pkt.e[i].parent, key, pkt.e[i].hp, pkt.e[i].pad);
          }
          g_brick.net_count = 0;      /* a mirror never rebroadcasts */
          return brick_world_flush(0);
      }
      
      /* brick_world_drain_events -- cosmetic consumers (debris, bullet-hole cleanup) take this frame's
       * events. Returns the count copied into `out`; the queue is emptied either way. */
      static inline int brick_world_drain_events(BfEvent *out, int max) {
          int n = g_brick.ev_count < max ? g_brick.ev_count : max;
          if (n > 0) memcpy(out, g_brick.ev, sizeof(BfEvent) * (size_t)n);
          g_brick.ev_count = 0;
          return n;
      }
      
      /* ---- physical bodies ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      /* Static geometry for the bodies: the level's live collision boxes, oriented boxes and RAMPS included
         (obb.h), so a shard that lands on a ramp slides/tumbles down it. */
      static int brick_world_body_push(void *user, const double c[3], double r, double nrm[3], double *pen) {
          (void)user;
          static BoxOrient ident;
          static int ident_ready = 0;
          if (!ident_ready) { orient_identity(&ident); ident_ready = 1; }
          float best = 0.0f; int hit = 0;
          for (int i = 1; i < map_count; i++) {
              const Box *b = &map_geo[i];
              if (b->w <= 0.0f || b->h <= 0.0f || b->d <= 0.0f) continue;
              float R = (b->w + b->h + b->d) * 0.5f + (float)r;
              if (fabsf((float)c[0] - b->x) > R || fabsf((float)c[1] - b->y) > R || fabsf((float)c[2] - b->z) > R) continue;
              const BoxOrient *o = phys_box_orient(i);
              float n[3], depth;
              if (!obb_sphere_push(b->x, b->y, b->z, b->w, b->h, b->d, o ? o : &ident,
                                   (float)c[0], (float)c[1], (float)c[2], (float)r, n, &depth)) continue;
              if (depth > best) { best = depth; nrm[0] = n[0]; nrm[1] = n[1]; nrm[2] = n[2]; hit = 1; }
          }
          *pen = best;
          return hit;
      }
      
      static inline void brick_world_bodies_init(void) {
          if (g_brick_bodies_ready) return;
          bb_init(&g_brick_bodies, brick_world_body_push, NULL);
          g_brick_bodies_ready = 1;
      }
      
      static inline unsigned int brick_world_hash(unsigned int x) {
          x ^= x >> 16; x *= 0x7feb352dU; x ^= x >> 15; x *= 0x846ca68bU; x ^= x >> 16;
          return x;
      }
      static inline double brick_world_h01(unsigned int *s) {
          *s = brick_world_hash(*s + 0x9E3779B9u);
          return (double)(*s & 0xFFFFu) / 65535.0;
      }
      
      /* shard box half extents per material kind: brick/concrete/wood a 0.2 m block, glass a thin plate */
      static inline void brick_world_shard_half(int kind, double h[3]) {
          if (kind == BF_KIND_GLASS) { h[0] = 0.12; h[1] = 0.03; h[2] = 0.12; }
          else { h[0] = h[1] = h[2] = BB_SHARD_HALF; }
      }
      
      /* brick_world_spawn_bodies -- everything the fracture engine queued becomes GOLDEN BAND bodies:
       * shards for shot-out cells, one body per chunk of cells cut off from the world. Safe on every
       * process (the server, a local match, a mirroring client); a client knows no impact, so its bodies
       * simply drop with the same deterministic scatter. */
      static inline void brick_world_spawn_bodies(void) {
          brick_world_bodies_init();
          /* shot-out cells shed the cheap flakes (brick_debris.h, driven by the lobby from the event queue); only
             cut-off chunks become bodies */
          g_brick.shard_count = 0;
          for (int ci = 0; ci < g_brick.chunk_count; ci++) {
              const BfChunk *ch = &g_brick.chunk[ci];
              double lo[3] = { 1e30, 1e30, 1e30 }, hi[3] = { -1e30, -1e30, -1e30 };
              double mass = 0.0, kind_mass[4] = { 0, 0, 0, 0 };
              unsigned int seed = brick_world_hash((unsigned int)ch->id * 2654435761u);
              for (int i = 0; i < ch->n; i++) {
                  const BfParent *p = &g_brick.parent[ch->cell[i].parent];
                  int ix, iy, iz; bf_unkey(ch->cell[i].key, &ix, &iy, &iz);
                  float c[3]; bf_cell_center(p, ix, iy, iz, c);
                  for (int a = 0; a < 3; a++) {
                      double l = (double)c[a] - 0.5 * p->cell[a], h = (double)c[a] + 0.5 * p->cell[a];
                      if (l < lo[a]) lo[a] = l;
                      if (h > hi[a]) hi[a] = h;
                  }
                  double m = (double)p->density * p->cell[0] * p->cell[1] * p->cell[2];
                  mass += m;
                  if (p->kind >= 0 && p->kind < 4) kind_mass[p->kind] += m;
                  seed = brick_world_hash(seed ^ ch->cell[i].key);
              }
              int kind = 0;
              for (int k = 1; k < 4; k++) if (kind_mass[k] > kind_mass[kind]) kind = k;
              double pos[3], half[3];
              for (int a = 0; a < 3; a++) { pos[a] = 0.5 * (lo[a] + hi[a]); half[a] = 0.5 * (hi[a] - lo[a]); }
              /* Founder real-time, 2026-10-16: "there should be a bit of rotation so they don't all fall straight
                 down ... you can fake it". A seeded sideways drift + tumble, strongest for light/thin glass. */
              double wob = (kind == BF_KIND_GLASS) ? 1.0 : 0.55;
              double vel[3] = { (double)ch->vx + (brick_world_h01(&seed) - 0.5) * 2.4 * wob, (double)ch->vy,
                                (double)ch->vz + (brick_world_h01(&seed) - 0.5) * 2.4 * wob };
              double om[3] = { (brick_world_h01(&seed) - 0.5) * 3.2 * wob, (brick_world_h01(&seed) - 0.5) * 1.6 * wob,
                               (brick_world_h01(&seed) - 0.5) * 3.2 * wob };
              bb_spawn(&g_brick_bodies, kind, 1, mass, pos, half, vel, om);
          }
          g_brick.chunk_count = 0;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_discard_bodies -- the dedicated server: broken brick bodies are purely visual (they never feed
       * back into gameplay or the network), so it only empties the queue the fracture engine fills and spends
       * nothing simulating them. Clients do the spawning and stepping. */
      static inline void brick_world_discard_bodies(void) {
          g_brick.shard_count = 0;
          g_brick.chunk_count = 0;
      }
      
      /* brick_world_tick -- once per frame / server tick with a monotonic millisecond clock: spawn what the
       * fracture engine queued and step the bodies. */
      static inline void brick_world_tick(unsigned int now_ms) {
          static unsigned int last_ms = 0;
          brick_world_bodies_init();
          if (g_brick_active) brick_world_spawn_bodies();
          double dt = last_ms ? (double)(now_ms - last_ms) * 0.001 : 0.0;
          last_ms = now_ms;
          if (dt < 0.0 || dt > 1.0) dt = 0.0;
          if (bb_active_count(&g_brick_bodies) > 0) bb_step(&g_brick_bodies, dt);
      }
      
      #endif

== chunk_note body ==
static inline void bf_chunk_note(BrickFracture *bf, int id, int parent, unsigned int key) {
    BfChunk *c = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < bf->chunk_count; i++) if (bf->chunk[i].id == id) { c = &bf->chunk[i]; break; }
    if (!c) {
        if (bf->chunk_count >= BF_MAX_CHUNKS) return;
        c = &bf->chunk[bf->chunk_count++];
        c->id = id; c->n = 0;
        c->vx = bf->impact_dir[0] * bf->impact_speed * 0.5f;     /* a chunk takes half a shard's push */
        c->vy = bf->impact_dir[1] * bf->impact_speed * 0.5f;
        c->vz = bf->impact_dir[2] * bf->impact_speed * 0.5f;
    }
    if (c->n >= BF_CHUNK_CELLS) return;
    c->cell[c->n].parent = (unsigned short)parent;
    c->cell[c->n].key = key;
    c->n++;
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/world/brick_fracture.h",

      "oldString": "/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * Piece decomposition\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */",
      "newString": "/* bf_detach_parent -- drop an ENTIRE destructible parent at once, as one rigid chunk.\n *\n * This is the structural layer's escape hatch (packages/simulation/structure.h): the cell-level flood in\n * bf_detect_detached answers \"is this region of cells still attached to something?\", but a roof resting\n * on a pillar two boxes away is attached at PIECE level, not cell level, and bf_detect_detached\n * deliberately keeps an authored-floating mass. When the piece graph says that roof's support is gone,\n * this is what makes it fall.\n *\n * Budgeted exactly like bf_detect_detached: a parent bigger than BF_CHUNK_CELLS (256 cells), one that\n * would overflow the record budget or per-parent removal cap, or one arriving after BF_MAX_CHUNKS is\n * full, stays standing -- the same \"too big to animate: stays put\" rule the cell pass already uses,\n * named rather than silently half-detached. Returns the number of cells detached (0 = left standing). */\nstatic inline int bf_detach_parent(BrickFracture *bf, int parent) {\n    if (parent < 0 || parent >= bf->parent_count) return 0;\n    BfParent *p = &bf->parent[parent];\n    if (!p->active) return 0;\n    int total = p->n[0] * p->n[1] * p->n[2];\n    if (total <= 0) return 0;\n    int intact = total - p->removed;\n    if (intact <= 0) return 0;\n    if (intact > BF_CHUNK_CELLS) return 0;                     /* too big to animate as one body */\n    if (bf->chunk_count >= BF_MAX_CHUNKS) return 0;\n    if (bf->rec_count + intact > BF_MAX_RECORDS) return 0;\n    if (p->removed + intact > BF_MAX_REMOVED_PER_PARENT) return 0;\n\n    int id = ++bf->next_chunk_id;\n    if (id > 255) { bf->next_chunk_id = 1; id = 1; }\n    int n = 0;\n    bf->suppress_debris = 1;\n    for (int ix = 0; ix < p->n[0]; ix++)\n        for (int iy = 0; iy < p->n[1]; iy++)\n            for (int iz = 0; iz < p->n[2]; iz++) {\n                unsigned int key = bf_key(ix, iy, iz);\n                if (bf_cell_hp(bf, parent, key) <= 0) continue;\n                if (bf_set_cell_hp(bf, parent, key, 0, 1) <= 0) continue;\n                int r = bf_find_rec(bf, parent, key);\n                if (r >= 0) bf->rec[r].chunk = (unsigned char)id;\n                bf_push_net_chunk(bf, parent, key, 0, id);\n                bf_chunk_note(bf, id, parent, key);\n                n++;\n            }\n    bf->suppress_debris = 0;\n    return n;\n}\n\n/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * Piece decomposition\n * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

       * paths: physics.h's update_weapons (hitscan hook), its custom-level slot arrays, trace_map, and the
       * brick_world.h glue (blast hook, match reset, network apply). No SDL, no window.
       *
       *   gcc -std=gnu99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsanitize=address,undefined -Ipackages/common \
       *       -Ipackages/simulation -Ipackages/world packages/simulation/brick_world_test.c \
       *       packages/simulation/brick_mod.c packages/world/terrain.c -lm
       */
      #include "../common/physics.h"
      #include "brick_world.h"
      #include <assert.h>
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <stdlib.h>
      
      /* physics.h's phys_respawn calls into local_game.h's bot evolution; this test never respawns. */
      PlayerState *get_best_bot(void) { return NULL; }
      void evolve_bot(PlayerState *a, PlayerState *b) { (void)a; (void)b; }
      
      static int g_fail = 0;
      #define CHECK(c) do { if (!(c)) { printf("FAIL %s:%d  %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); g_fail++; } } while (0)
      
      /* solid at a point, using the live collision slots (exactly what resolve_collision/trace_map see) */
      static int solid_at(float x, float y, float z) {
          for (int i = 1; i < map_count; i++) {
              Box b = map_geo[i];
              if (fabsf(x - b.x) < b.w * 0.5f && fabsf(y - b.y) < b.h * 0.5f && fabsf(z - b.z) < b.d * 0.5f) return 1;
          }
          return 0;
      }
      
      static CustomLevelData g_lvl;
      
      static void load_level(void) {
          memset(&g_lvl, 0, sizeof(g_lvl));
          snprintf(g_lvl.materials[0].name, LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAME, "brick");
          snprintf(g_lvl.materials[1].name, LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAME, "metal");
          g_lvl.material_count = 2;
          /* 0: a brick wall 60 x 20 x 6 (20 x 7 x 2 cells) centred (0,10,0)
             1: a brick floor slab 100 x 2 x 100 (slab-like -> NOT destructible)
             2: a metal pillar (not brick -> NOT destructible)
             3: a brick door box (excluded by the door list) */
          LevelBox *b = g_lvl.boxes;
          b[0] = (LevelBox){ 0, 10, 0, 60, 20, 6, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.3f, 0 };
          b[1] = (LevelBox){ 0, -1, 0, 100, 2, 100, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.3f, 0 };
          b[2] = (LevelBox){ 80, 10, 0, 6, 20, 6, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.3f, 1 };
          b[3] = (LevelBox){ -80, 10, 0, 10, 20, 2, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.6f, 0.3f, 0 };
          g_lvl.count = 4;
          g_lvl.door_count = 1;
          g_lvl.doors[0].box_index = 3;
      
          float x[4], y[4], z[4], w[4], h[4], d[4], r[4], g[4], bl[4]; int mi[4];
          for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
              x[i] = b[i].x; y[i] = b[i].y; z[i] = b[i].z; w[i] = b[i].w; h[i] = b[i].h; d[i] = b[i].d;
              r[i] = g[i] = bl[i] = 0.6f; mi[i] = b[i].material_idx;
          }
          char names[2][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN] = { "brick", "metal" };
          char shaders[2][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN] = { "standard", "standard" };
          float spec[2] = { 0, 0 }, shin[2] = { 1, 1 }, fric[2] = { 0.3f, 0.3f };
          phys_set_custom_level_materials(names, shaders, spec, shin, fric, 2);
          phys_set_custom_level(x, y, z, w, h, d, r, g, bl, mi, 4, 0, 1);
          phys_set_scene(SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL);
          brick_world_init_from_level(&g_lvl);
      }
      
      static void fire(PlayerState *p, int weapon, int ticks) {
          PlayerState targets[MAX_CLIENTS];
          Projectile projectiles[MAX_PROJECTILES];
          memset(targets, 0, sizeof(targets));
          memset(projectiles, 0, sizeof(projectiles));
          p->current_weapon = weapon;
          for (int t = 0; t < ticks; t++) {
              p->ammo[weapon] = 99;
              update_weapons(p, targets, projectiles, 1, 0, 0, 0, (unsigned int)t * 16u, 3000u);
          }
      }
      
      /* brick_world.h installs the AI hooks; this test links no witness_ai.c, so stand-ins for its setters. */
      void witness_ai_set_wall_hit_hook(WitnessWallHitFn fn) { (void)fn; }
      void witness_ai_set_map_hook(WitnessMapFn fn) { (void)fn; }

i < g_brick_struct.node_count; i++) {\n        StructNode *n = &g_brick_struct.node[i];\n        int pi = n->parent;\n        if (pi < 0 || pi >= g_brick.parent_count) continue;\n        const BfParent *p = &g_brick.parent[pi];\n        int total = p->n[0] * p->n[1] * p->n[2];\n        int intact = total - p->removed;\n        if (!p->active || total <= 0 || intact <= 0) { n->active = 0; n->mass = 0.0f; continue; }\n        n->active = 1;\n        n->mass = p->dim[0] * p->dim[1] * p->dim[2] * n->density * ((float)intact / (float)total);\n    }\n}\n\n/* brick_world_structure_tick -- re-evaluate the piece graph and drop what it can no longer justify.\n * Runs up to three passes so a load-time or post-blast cascade completes in one call: the failing\n * pillar goes, then the roof that was standing on it.
