- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/src/emit_java.c
  content: |
      /* emit_java.c — real, v0, narrow-scope Java emitter. See emit_java.h's own header comment for the
       * full real scope statement (a scalar `defn`, no Arena/region, one expression body, wrapped in one
       * real class matching the output file's own basename). */
      #include "emit_java.h"
      #include <stdarg.h>
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <string.h>
      #include <stdlib.h>
      
      /* --- minimal, self-contained string builder -- deliberately NOT shared with emit.c's own StrBuf
         or emit_ts.c's own TsBuf (see emit_java.h's own header comment for why this file stays
         independent). Same real "temporary C-heap scratch, arena-owned result" shape both of those
         already use for their own final buffer. */
      typedef struct {
          char *data;
          size_t len;
          size_t cap;
      } JavaBuf;
      
      static void jb_init(JavaBuf *b) {
          b->cap = 256;
          b->data = malloc(b->cap);
          b->data[0] = '\0';
          b->len = 0;
      }
      
      static void jb_free(JavaBuf *b) {
          free(b->data);
          b->data = NULL;
          b->len = 0;
          b->cap = 0;
      }
      
      static void jb_append(JavaBuf *b, const char *s) {
          size_t add_len = strlen(s);
          if (b->len + add_len + 1 > b->cap) {
              while (b->len + add_len + 1 > b->cap) b->cap *= 2;
              b->data = realloc(b->data, b->cap);
          }
          memcpy(b->data + b->len, s, add_len + 1);
          b->len += add_len;
      }
      
      /* Formats into an exactly-sized heap buffer. This used to be a fixed char[512], which silently TRUNCATED any expression
         longer than 511 chars (a long `if` ladder such as DEADWEIGHT's card-definition tables) into invalid Java. */
      static void jb_appendf(JavaBuf *b, const char *fmt, ...) {
          va_list ap, ap2;
          va_start(ap, fmt);
          va_copy(ap2, ap);
          int n = vsnprintf(NULL, 0, fmt, ap);
          va_end(ap);
          if (n < 0) { va_end(ap2); return; }
          char *tmp = malloc((size_t)n + 1);
          if (!tmp) { va_end(ap2); return; }
          vsnprintf(tmp, (size_t)n + 1, fmt, ap2);
          va_end(ap2);
          jb_append(b, tmp);
          free(tmp);
      }
      
      /* --- small AST helpers, same real shape emit.c's and emit_ts.c's own is_symbol/is_call_named
         use, reimplemented independently here rather than exported/shared. */
      static int is_symbol(Node *n, const char *text) {
          return n && n->type == NODE_SYMBOL && strcmp(n->text, text) == 0;
      }
      
      static int is_call_named(Node *n, const char *name) {
          return n && n->type == NODE_LIST && n->child_count >= 1 && is_symbol(n->children[0], name);
      }
      
      /* camel_case: real, minimal kebab-case -> camelCase converter, identical real logic to emit_ts.c's
         own (Java methods are also real, conventionally camelCase, the exact same target-language naming
         convention TypeScript uses here) -- reimplemented independently rather than shared, matching
         this file's own deliberate "no cross-target sharing" discipline. */
      static const char *camel_case(Arena *arena, const char *kebab) {
          size_t len = strlen(kebab);
          char *out = arena_alloc(arena, len + 1);
          size_t oi = 0;
          int capitalize_next = 0;
          for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++) {
              char c = kebab[i];
              if (c == '-') {
                  capitalize_next = 1;
                  continue;
              }
              if (capitalize_next) {
                  out[oi++] = (char)((c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') ? c - 32 : c);
                  capitalize_next = 0;
              } else {
                  out[oi++] = c;
              }
          }
          out[oi] = '\0';
          return out;
      }
      
      /* resolve_java_type: the real, narrow I32/F64/Bool/String/Unit -> Java type mapping this v0
         understands -- any other type name is a real, honest "unsupported" error, same real boundary
         emit_ts.c's own resolve_ts_type draws. Note real, deliberate choice of primitive `int`/`double`/
         `boolean` (not boxed `Integer`/`Double`/`Boolean`) -- this v0's own scalar-only scope never
         needs a nullable/boxed value, so the real, cheaper primitive types are the honest match. */
      static const char *resolve_java_type(Node *type_sym, const char **out_error) {
          if (!type_sym || type_sym->type != NODE_SYMBOL) {
              *out_error = "emit_java: expected a type symbol";
              return NULL;
          }
          if (strcmp(type_sym->text, "I32") == 0) return "int";
          if (strcmp(type_sym->text, "F64") == 0) return "double";
          if (strcmp(type_sym->text, "Bool") == 0) return "boolean";
          if (strcmp(type_sym->text, "String") == 0) return "String";
          if (strcmp(type_sym->text, "Unit") == 0) return "void";
          *out_error = "emit_java: unsupported parameter/return type (v0 only understands I32/F64/Bool/String/Unit)";
          return NULL;
      }
      
      /* MATH_PRIM_TABLE -- the exact same real, recognized external math/ primitives emit_ts.c's own
         table names, reusing the same real method-name STRINGS verbatim: java.lang.Math has identical
         real method names to JS's own Math (Math.random/floor/sqrt/log/cos, Math.PI) -- a real,
         convenient overlap this file leans on rather than re-deriving from scratch. See
         stdlib/math/math.prn's own doc comment for each real, matching PARENA-side signature. */
      typedef struct { const char *prn_name; const char *java_fn; int arg_count; } MathPrimEntry;
      static const MathPrimEntry MATH_PRIM_TABLE[] = {
          /* renamed math/random -> math/random-f64 2026-09-07, same real C-target naming-collision
           * reason emit_ts.c's own table comment gives -- see stdlib/math/math.prn's doc comment. */
          {"math/random-f64", "Math.random", 0},
          {"math/floor", "Math.floor", 1},
          {"math/sqrt", "Math.sqrt", 1},
          {"math/log", "Math.log", 1},
          {"math/cos", "Math.cos", 1},
      };
      #define MATH_PRIM_TABLE_COUNT (sizeof(MATH_PRIM_TABLE) / sizeof(MATH_PRIM_TABLE[0]))
      
      static const MathPrimEntry *find_math_prim(const char *name) {
          for (size_t i = 0; i < MATH_PRIM_TABLE_COUNT; i++) {
              if (strcmp(MATH_PRIM_TABLE[i].prn_name, name) == 0) return &MATH_PRIM_TABLE[i];
          }
          return NULL;
      }
      
      /* BINOP_TABLE -- the same real narrow operator set emit_ts.c's own table recognizes, with exactly
         one real, deliberate difference: `=` -> `==` (not `===` -- Java has no triple-equals token at
         all), which gives correct real value-equality semantics for every real scalar primitive type
         (int/double/boolean) this v0's own narrow type table understands. */
      typedef struct { const char *prn_op; const char *java_op; } BinopEntry;
      static const BinopEntry BINOP_TABLE[] = {
          {"+", "+"}, {"-", "-"}, {"*", "*"}, {"/", "/"},
          {"=", "=="}, {"<", "<"}, {">", ">"}, {"<=", "<="}, {">=", ">="},
          {"and", "&&"}, {"or", "||"},
      };
      #define BINOP_TABLE_COUNT (sizeof(BINOP_TABLE) / sizeof(BINOP_TABLE[0]))
      
      static const char *find_binop(const char *prn_op) {
          for (size_t i = 0; i < BINOP_TABLE_COUNT; i++) {
              if (strcmp(BINOP_TABLE[i].prn_op, prn_op) == 0) return BINOP_TABLE[i].java_op;
          }
          return NULL;
      }
      
      static const char *emit_java_expr(Arena *arena, Node *expr, const char **out_error);
      
      /* emit_java_expr: the real, recursive expression emitter -- structurally identical real shape to
         emit_ts.c's own emit_ts_expr (see that file's own doc comment for the full real rationale, not
         repeated here): number/symbol literals, the narrow binop set above, `if` as a ternary
         expression, a call to a recognized `math/` primitive, or a call to another top-level function

return NULL; }\n            lb_append(&b, arg);\n        }\n        lb_append(&b, \")\");\n        const char *result = arena_strdup(arena, b.data, b.len);\n        lb_free(&b);\n        return result;\n    }\n\n    /* Otherwise: a call to another defn in this same module. Emitted through `M.` because that is how the\n     * function itself was declared, so an intra-module call resolves without any global namespace. */\n    LuaBuf b;\n    lb_init(&b);\n    lb_appendf(&b, \"M.%s(\", camel_case(arena, head));\n    for (size_t i = 1; i < expr->child_count; i++) {\n        if (i > 1) lb_append(&b, \", \");\n        const char *arg = emit_lua_expr(arena, expr->children[i], out_error);\n        if (!arg) { lb_free(&b); return NULL; }\n        lb_append(&b, arg);\n    }\n    lb_append(&b, \")\");\n    const char *result = arena_strdup(arena, b.data, b.len);\n    lb_free(&b);\n    return result;\n}\n\n/* find_target_lua_src -- `:lua (inline-lua \"...\")` from a `#target {...}` map, the same FFI escape hatch\n * emit.c's `:c` and emit_java.c's `:java` already provide. */\nstatic Node *find_target_lua_src(Node *target_map, const char **out_error) {\n    if (target_map->child_count % 2 != 0) {\n        *out_error = \"emit_lua: #target map has an odd number of forms (expected key/value pairs)\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    Node *lua_value = NULL;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < target_map->child_count; i += 2) {\n        Node *key = target_map->children[i];\n        if (key->type == NODE_KEYWORD && key->text && strcmp(key->text, \":lua\") == 0) {\n            lua_value = target_map->children[i + 1];\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    if (!lua_value) {\n        *out_error = \"emit_lua: #target map has no :lua key\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    if (lua_value->type != NODE_LIST || lua_value->child_count != 2 ||\n        lua_value->children[0]->type != NODE_SYMBOL || !is_symbol(lua_value->children[0], \"inline-lua\") ||\n        lua_value->children[1]->type != NODE_STRING) {\n        *out_error = \"emit_lua: #target :lua value must be (inline-lua \\\"...\\\")\";\n        return NULL;\n    }\n    return lua_value->children[1];\n}\n\nstatic int emit_target_lua_defn(LuaBuf *out, Node *target_map, const char *fn_name,\n                                const char *param_list, const char **out_error) {\n    Node *src = find_target_lua_src(target_map, out_error);\n    if (!src) return 0;\n    lb_appendf(out, \"function M.%s(%s)\\n    %.*s\\nend\\n\\n\", fn_name, param_list, (int)src->text_len, src->text);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic int emit_lua_defn(Arena *arena, LuaBuf *out, Node *defn, const char **out_error) {\n    if (defn->child_count < 3 || defn->children[1]->type != NODE_SYMBOL || defn->children[2]->type != NODE_VEC) {\n        *out_error = \"emit_lua: defn: malformed function definition\";\n        return 0;\n    }\n    const char *fn_name = camel_case(arena, defn->children[1]->text);\n    Node *params = defn->children[2];\n\n    LuaBuf param_list;\n    lb_init(&param_list);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < params->child_count; i++) {\n        Node *param = params->children[i];\n        if (param->type != NODE_LIST || param->child_count != 3 || param->children[0]->type != NODE_SYMBOL ||\n            param->children[1]->type != NODE_COLON || param->children[2]->type != NODE_SYMBOL) {\n            *out_error = \"emit_lua: defn: unsupported parameter shape (v0 only understands plain \"\n                         \"(name : I32|F64|Bool|String) params -- no Arena/region annotations)\";\n            lb_free(&param_list);\n            return 0;\n        }\n        /* Lua has no type annotations on parameters, so `(x : I32)` emits as just `x`. */\n        if (i > 0) lb_append(&param_list, \", \");\n        lb_append(&param_list, camel_case(arena, param->children[0]->text));\n    }\n\n    if (defn->child_count == 7 && is_symbol(defn->children[5], \"#target\")) {\n        if (defn->children[6]->type != NODE_MAP) {\n            *out_error = \"emit_lua: defn: #target must be followed by a {...} map\";\n            lb_free(&param_list);\n            return 0;\n        }\n        int ok = emit_target_lua_defn(out, defn->children[6], fn_name, param_list.data, out_error);\n        lb_free(&param_list);\n        return ok;\n    }\n\n    if (defn->child_count != 6 || defn->children[3]->type != NODE_COLON) {\n        *out_error = \"emit_lua: defn: expected (defn name [params] : RetType body) with exactly one body \"\n                     \"expression, or a #target {...} FFI body\";\n        lb_free(&param_list);\n        return 0;\n    }\n    const char *body = emit_lua_expr(arena, defn->children[5], out_error);\n    if (!body) {\n        lb_free(&param_list);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    lb_appendf(out, \"function M.%s(%s)\\n    return %s\\nend\\n\\n\", fn_name, param_list.data, body);\n    lb_free(&param_list);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nconst char *emit_lua(Arena *arena, Node *program, const char **out_error) {\n    LuaBuf out;\n    lb_init(&out);\n    lb_append(&out, \"-- Generated by parena build (Lua target) -- do not edit by hand.\\n\"\n                    \"-- Source of truth: the .prn this was emitted from. SHANKPIT compiles the SAME file to C.\\n\\n\"\n                    \"local M = {}\\n\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < program->child_count; i++) {\n        Node *form = program->children[i];\n        /* module/export/import/llvm-extern are metadata for other targets; a Lua module simply returns every\n         * defn it was given, which is what `export` would have said anyway. */\n        if (is_call_named(form, \"module\") || is_call_named(form, \"export\") || is_call_named(form, \"import\") ||\n            is_call_named(form, \"llvm-extern\")) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (is_call_named(form, \"defn\")) {\n            if (!emit_lua_defn(arena, &out, form, out_error)) {\n                lb_free(&out);\n                return NULL;\n            }\n            continue;\n        }\n        *out_error = \"emit_lua: unsupported top-level form (v0 only understands defn, module, export, import)\";\n        lb_free(&out);\n        return NULL;\n    }\n\n    lb_append(&out, \"return M\\n\");\n    const char *result = arena_strdup(arena, out.data, out.len);\n    lb_free(&out);\n    return result;\n}\n"
}

See MONOREPO/docs/THREE_WAY_MERGE.md.\n;;\n;; Units, all integers (the mod ABI in ECOWAR/docs/ARENA_API.md):\n;;   speed        units per tick (the host integrates; this file only decides the next speed)\n;;   surface      permille of traction: 1000 = perfect grip, 0 = frictionless\n;;   damage       hit points\n;;   chance       permille\n;;   cooldown     ticks\n;;\n;; Deliberately NOT here: rendering, hit detection, network, or anything that needs a clock. This is the decision\n;; layer; both hosts keep their own verbs.\n(module noobtopia/arena-rules)\n(export weapon-damage weapon-knockback-permille weapon-hit-chance-permille weapon-cooldown-ticks\n        surface-friction-permille surface-accel surface-jump-impulse\n        step-speed slide-decay)\n\n;; ---- combat ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; Weapon ids are NOOBTOPIA's own, deliberately small (a Roblox noob has fists, a bat, a pistol, a rocket):\n;;   0 FIST  1 BAT  2 PISTOL  3 ROCKET\n;; Fists are the baseline a noob always has; a rocket is the only thing that should read as an event.\n(defn weapon-damage [(weapon : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= weapon 3) 90\n    (if (= weapon 1) 22\n      (if (= weapon 2) 18\n        12))))\n\n;; Hit points of force the target keeps, permille of its own speed. A rocket throws you; a bat shoves you; a pistol\n;; barely moves you at all (it is the damage that matters); fists are a nudge.\n(defn weapon-knockback-permille [(weapon : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= weapon 3) 600\n    (if (= weapon 1) 180\n      (if (= weapon 2) 90\n        60))))\n\n;; To-hit chance, permille, falling off with distance. Base per weapon, then -8 permille per unit, floored at 50\n;; so no shot is ever impossible and clamped at 950 so none is ever certain.\n(defn weapon-hit-chance-permille [(weapon : I32) (dist : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< dist 0) 950\n    (if (> (- (weapon-hit-base weapon) (* dist 8)) 950) 950\n      (if (< (- (weapon-hit-base weapon) (* dist 8)) 50) 50\n        (- (weapon-hit-base weapon) (* dist 8))))))\n\n;; Base accuracy per weapon (kept as its own function so the falloff above reads as one expression).\n(defn weapon-hit-base [(weapon : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= weapon 3) 900\n    (if (= weapon 2) 800\n      (if (= weapon 1) 700\n        650))))\n\n;; Ticks between swings/shots. A rocket is a commitment; fists are fast.\n(defn weapon-cooldown-ticks [(weapon : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= weapon 3) 90\n    (if (= weapon 2) 30\n      (if (= weapon 1) 24\n        8))))\n\n;; ---- slippery physics -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; Surface ids: 0 CONCRETE  1 ICE  2 GRASS  3 METAL  4 MUD\n;; Traction in permille. Ice is the whole point of this file: 120 permille means a step-speed loses only 12% of\n;; its speed per tick when you let go, so you coast -- and metal (a wet platform) is not far behind.\n(defn surface-friction-permille [(surface : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= surface 1) 120\n    (if (= surface 3) 300\n      (if (= surface 2) 600\n        (if (= surface 4) 700\n          850)))))\n\n;; How hard you can push yourself on this surface, in speed units per tick. Ice gives you almost nothing to push\n;; with (that is what makes it slippery rather than merely fast); concrete gives you the most.\n(defn surface-accel [(surface : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= surface 1) 1\n    (if (= surface 3) 2\n      (if (= surface 2) 3\n        (if (= surface 4) 2\n          4)))))\n\n;; Upward impulse from a jump. Ice and metal kill your launch a little (you cannot plant); grass is springy.\n(defn surface-jump-impulse [(surface : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= surface 1) 5\n    (if (= surface 3) 6\n      (if (= surface 2) 8\n        (if (= surface 4) 5\n          7)))))\n\n;; One tick of movement. `wish` is the speed the player is asking for this tick; `wish < 0` means \"no input\", which\n;; is exactly when the surface's own friction takes over and you slide to a stop. Neither host integrates here --\n;; they hand in last tick's speed and take next tick's.\n(defn step-speed [(speed : I32) (wish : I32) (surface : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< wish 0) (slide-decay speed surface)\n    (if (< speed wish)\n      (if (> (+ speed (surface-accel surface)) wish) wish (+ speed (surface-accel surface)))\n      (if (> speed wish)\n        (if (< (- speed (surface-accel surface)) wish) wish (- speed (surface-accel surface)))\n        wish))))\n\n;; No input: lose `1000 - traction` permille of speed this tick. Integer division, so a slow slide eventually stops\n;; outright instead of asymptotically creeping forever -- which is also how a real game avoids a 200-tick tail.\n(defn slide-decay [(speed : I32) (surface : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= speed 0) 0\n    (- speed (/ (* speed (- 1000 (surface-friction-permille surface))) 1000))))\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh",
  "instructions": "Generator: NOOBTOPIA line data to a C include for SHANKPIT.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# gen_ambient_lines.sh -- generate packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc from NOOBTOPIA's data.\n#\n# NOOBTOPIA owns the WORDS (NOOBTOPIA/data/noob_lines.lua); PARENA owns the RULES\n# (stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn); SHANKPIT owns the engine. So the line table is generated from the data file\n# rather than hand-copied into C: edit a noob's line in NOOBTOPIA, re-run this, and the same line is what a SHANKPIT\n# NPC says. A line that exists in one world and not the other becomes impossible.\n#\n# Usage: scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh   (needs a sibling ../NOOBTOPIA checkout)\nset -euo pipefail\nroot=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nsrc=\"${NOOBTOPIA_DIR:-$root/../NOOBTOPIA}/data/noob_lines.lua\"\nout=\"$root/packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc\"\n\nif [ ! -f \"$src\" ]; then\n    echo \"gen_ambient_lines: missing $src (clone NOOBTOPIA next to SHANKPIT, or set NOOBTOPIA_DIR)\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\ncount=$(awk 'match($0, /^[ \\t]*\\{cat = [0-9]+, text = \".+\"\\}[,]?[ \\t]*$/) { n++ } END { print n+0 }' \"$src\")\nif [ \"$count\" -lt 1 ]; then\n    echo \"gen_ambient_lines: $src contains no readable lines (expected '{cat = N, text = \\\"...\\\"},' per line)\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n{\n    echo \"/* Generated from NOOBTOPIA/data/noob_lines.lua by scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh -- do not edit by hand.\"\n    echo \" * The words live in NOOBTOPIA; the categories and timing live in PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn. */\"\n    echo \"static const AmbientLine g_ambient_lines[] = {\"\n    awk '\n        match($0, /^[ \\t]*\\{cat = ([0-9]+), text = \"(.*)\"\\}[,]?[ \\t]*$/, m) {\n            printf \"    { %s, \\\"%s\\\" },\\n\", m[1], m[2]\n        }\n    ' \"$src\"\n    echo \"};\"\n    echo \"static const int g_ambient_line_count = $count;\"\n} > \"$out\"\n\necho \"regenerated packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc ($count lines)\"\n"
}

{

  "instructions": "Generator script for the C half of the shared rules.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# gen_noobtopia_rules.sh -- regenerate the C half of the NOOBTOPIA three-way merge.\n#\n# The decisions live in PARENA, once, and are emitted twice:\n#   PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn  -> packages/simulation/ambient_life.c  (this script)\n#                                             -> NOOBTOPIA/src/generated/ambient_life.lua (NOOBTOPIA/scripts/gen_rules.sh)\n#   PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/arena_rules.prn   -> packages/simulation/arena_rules.c   (this script)\n#                                             -> NOOBTOPIA/src/generated/arena_rules.lua\n# Editing a threshold means editing the .prn and re-running both generators; there is no second copy to forget.\n#\n# Usage: scripts/gen_noobtopia_rules.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout with .parena-bootstrap)\nset -euo pipefail\nroot=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nparena_dir=\"${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}\"\nif [ -x \"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nelif [ -x \"$parena_dir/parena\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/parena\"\nelse\n    (cd \"$parena_dir\" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nfi\n\n\"$parena_bin\" build \"$parena_dir/stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn\" \\\n    -o \"$root/packages/simulation/ambient_life.c\"\n\"$parena_bin\" build \"$parena_dir/stdlib/noobtopia/arena_rules.prn\" \\\n    -o \"$root/packages/simulation/arena_rules.c\"\necho \"regenerated packages/simulation/{ambient_life,arena_rules}.c\"\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/ambient_life.h",
  "instructions": "SHANKPIT host for ambient life: PARENA decisions plus NOOBTOPIA words.",
  "content": "#ifndef SHANKPIT_AMBIENT_LIFE_H\n#define SHANKPIT_AMBIENT_LIFE_H\n\n/* ambient_life.h -- what an NPC says when nothing is happening, in SHANKPIT.\n *\n * Founder real-time (2026-10-30): \"NOOBTOPIA is the data for making our world seem more alive we script in more\n * random interactions like the talking from noobtopia\" / \"PARENA IS THE GL[UE]\".\n *\n * The three-way split, made concrete:\n *   * the DECISIONS (which kind of line, how long until it may speak, which line) are PARENA's, once:\n *     stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn -> packages/simulation/ambient_life.c (generated, do not edit);\n *   * the WORDS are NOOBTOPIA's, once: NOOBTOPIA/data/noob_lines.lua -> packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc\n *     (generated by scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh, do not edit);\n *   * this file is the thin host that joins them and hands a caller a string.\n *\n * It is header-only and stateless: the caller passes its own seed, so a server and every client can run the same\n * code and get the same answer. See MONOREPO/docs/THREE_WAY_MERGE.md.\n */\n\n/* PARENA-generated (packages/simulation/ambient_life.c). */\nint ambient_category_count(void);\nint ambient_category_for_mood(int mood);\nint ambient_cooldown_ms(int mood, int seed);\nint ambient_should_speak(int mood, int since_ms, int seed);\nint ambient_pick(int count, int seed);\n\ntypedef struct { int category; const char *text; } AmbientLine;\n\n/* Generated from NOOBTOPIA's data file: defines g_ambient_lines[] and g_ambient_line_count. */\n#include \"ambient_lines.inc\"\n\n/* The same deterministic generator NOOBTOPIA's Luau side uses, so a seed means the same thing in both worlds. */\nstatic inline unsigned int ambient_life_next_seed(unsigned int seed) {\n    return (seed * 1103515245u + 12345u) & 0x7FFFFFFFu;\n}\n\nstatic inline int ambient_life_count_in(int category) {\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < g_ambient_line_count; i++)\n        if (g_ambient_lines[i].category == category) n++;\n    return n;\n}\n\n/* The whole decision: given an NPC's mood and how long it has been quiet, either a line to say or NULL.\n * `*seed` is advanced only when a line is actually chosen, which is what makes a caller's own RNG stream stable\n * whether or not an NPC happens to speak on a given tick. */\nstatic inline const char *ambient_life_speak(int mood, int since_ms, unsigned int *seed) {\n    if (!seed) return 0;\n    if (ambient_should_speak(mood, since_ms, (int)(*seed & 0x7FFFFFFF)) != 1) return 0;\n    int cat = ambient_category_for_mood(mood);\n    int count = ambient_life_count_in(cat);\n    if (count <= 0) {                       /* a category nobody wrote lines for must not silence the NPC */\n        cat = 0;\n        count = ambient_life_count_in(cat);\n        if (count <= 0) return 0;\n    }\n    *seed = ambient_life_next_seed(*seed);\n    int want = ambient_pick(count, (int)(*seed & 0x7FFFFFFF));\n    for (int i = 0; i < g_ambient_line_count; i++) {\n        if (g_ambient_lines[i].category != cat) continue;\n        if (want-- == 0) return g_ambient_lines[i].text;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n#endif\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/ambient_life_test.c",
  "instructions": "Headless test for the ambient life host.",
  "content": "/* ambient_life_test.c -- the SHANKPIT half of the NOOBTOPIA three-way merge, headless.\n *\n * What this pins:\n *   * every category the rules name has at least one real line in NOOBTOPIA's data (a category with no lines would\n *     silently mute an NPC, so it fails here instead);\n *   * the PARENA decisions are total and bounded -- pick in range for every seed, cooldowns inside the documented\n *     window, tired NPCs quieter than idle ones on the same seed, a negative clock never speaking;\n *   * the host picks a line from the RIGHT category for the mood (that is the whole point of categorising at all);\n *   * same seed -> same line, and 200 draws hit several distinct lines (a crowd that repeats itself is worse than\n *     silence);\n *   * below the cooldown it returns NULL rather than speaking early.\n *\n * make test-ambient-life\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"ambient_life.h\"\n\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n#define CHECK(c) do { if (!(c)) { printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); g_fail++; } } while (0)\n\nint main(void) {\n    /* 0. the generated data is real and covers every category the rules can return */\n    CHECK(g_ambient_line_count >= 20);\n    printf(\"ambient: %d lines from NOOBTOPIA\\n\", g_ambient_line_count);\n    for (int cat = 0; cat < ambient_category_count(); cat++) {\n        int n = ambient_life_count_in(cat);\n        CHECK(n > 0);\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < g_ambient_line_count; i++)\n        CHECK(g_ambient_lines[i].text && g_ambient_lines[i].text[0] != '\\0');\n\n    /* 1. picks are always in range */\n    for (int n = 0; n <= 40; n++)\n        for (int seed = 0; seed < 300; seed++) {\n            int got = ambient_pick(n, seed);\n            CHECK(got >= 0 && got < n);\n        }\n    CHECK(ambient_pick(0, 99) == 0);\n\n    /* 2. mood -> category is total, and unknown moods still produce something sayable */\n    CHECK(ambient_category_for_mood(3) == 3);\n    CHECK(ambient_category_for_mood(4) == 4);\n    CHECK(ambient_category_for_mood(1) == 1);\n    CHECK(ambient_category_for_mood(99) == 0);\n\n    /* 3. cooldowns live in the documented window and respect mood */\n    for (int mood = 0; mood < 8; mood++)\n        for (int seed = 0; seed < 200; seed++) {\n            int ms = ambient_cooldown_ms(mood, seed);\n            CHECK(ms >= 3000 && ms <= 22000);\n        }\n    CHECK(ambient_cooldown_ms(3, 1234) > ambient_cooldown_ms(0, 1234));\n\n    /* 4. should-speak is exactly the comparison, and a negative clock never speaks */\n    CHECK(ambient_should_speak(0, 0, 5) == 0);\n    CHECK(ambient_should_speak(0, ambient_cooldown_ms(0, 5), 5) == 1);\n    CHECK(ambient_should_speak(0, 999999, 5) == 1);\n    CHECK(ambient_should_speak(0, -5, 5) == 0);\n\n    /* 5. below the cooldown nothing is said at all */\n    unsigned int seed = 42u;\n    CHECK(ambient_life_speak(0, 0, &seed) == 0);\n\n    /* 6. a chosen line always belongs to the mood's own category */\n    for (int mood = 0; mood < 8; mood++) {\n        unsigned int s = 7u;\n        const char *line = ambient_life_speak(mood, 999999, &s);\n        CHECK(line != 0);\n        int cat = ambient_category_for_mood(mood);\n        int found = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < g_ambient_line_count; i++)\n            if (g_ambient_lines[i].category == cat && strcmp(g_ambient_lines[i].text, line) == 0) found = 1;\n        CHECK(found);\n    }\n\n    /* 7. determinism, and enough variety that a crowd does not chant in unison */\n    unsigned int a = 42u, b = 42u;\n    CHECK(ambient_life_speak(0, 999999, &a) == ambient_life_speak(0, 999999, &b));\n    const char *seen[64];\n    int nseen = 0;\n    unsigned int s = 7u;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) {\n        const char *line = ambient_life_speak(0, 999999, &s);\n        if (!line) continue;\n        int dup = 0;\n        for (int k = 0; k < nseen; k++) if (strcmp(seen[k], line) == 0) dup = 1;\n        if (!dup && nseen < 64) seen[nseen++] = line;\n    }\n    CHECK(nseen >= 3);\n    printf(\"ambient: 200 greetings -> %d distinct lines\\n\", nseen);\n\n    /* 8. seed advances only when something was said (a caller's stream stays stable on silent ticks) */\n    unsigned int q = 99u, before = q;\n    (void)ambient_life_speak(0, 0, &q);\n    CHECK(q == before);\n\n    if (g_fail) { printf(\"ambient_life_test: %d FAILED\\n\", g_fail); return 1; }\n    printf(\"ambient_life_test OK\\n\");\n    return 0;\n}\n"
}

  "content": "/* arena_rules_test.c -- the combat + slippery-physics half of the NOOBTOPIA merge, headless.\n *\n * Same source file as NOOBTOPIA's Luau module (PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/arena_rules.prn), so this test is also the\n * reference for what the Roblox side is supposed to do:\n *   * combat: damage/knockback/cooldown per weapon, to-hit falling off with distance but never impossible or\n *     certain;\n *   * slippery physics: traction ordering (ice < wet metal < grass < mud < concrete), no-input slides that lose\n *     speed per the surface, and the property the whole thing exists for -- RELEASING on ice travels further than\n *     releasing on concrete.\n *\n * make test-noobtopia-arena\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n\n#include \"arena_rules.h\"\n\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n#define CHECK(c) do { if (!(c)) { printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); g_fail++; } } while (0)\n\nint main(void) {\n    /* 1. combat numbers are sane and ordered the way a player expects */\n    CHECK(weapon_damage(3) > weapon_damage(1));          /* rocket > bat */\n    CHECK(weapon_damage(1) > weapon_damage(0));          /* bat > fists */\n    CHECK(weapon_damage(99) == weapon_damage(0));        /* unknown weapon is the baseline, not a crash */\n    CHECK(weapon_knockback_permille(3) > weapon_knockback_permille(1));\n    CHECK(weapon_cooldown_ticks(3) > weapon_cooldown_ticks(1));   /* a rocket is a commitment */\n    CHECK(weapon_cooldown_ticks(0) == 8);\n\n    /* 2. to-hit falls off with distance, floors at 50, clamps at 950, and a negative distance is \"point blank\" */\n    int prev = 2000;\n    for (int dist = 0; dist < 200; dist++) {\n        int ch = weapon_hit_chance_permille(2, dist);\n        CHECK(ch >= 50 && ch <= 950);\n        CHECK(ch <= prev);\n        prev = ch;\n    }\n    CHECK(weapon_hit_chance_permille(2, 0) > weapon_hit_chance_permille(2, 20));\n    CHECK(weapon_hit_chance_permille(3, 200) == 50);\n    CHECK(weapon_hit_chance_permille(2, -1) == 950);\n\n    /* 3. traction ordering: ice is the slippery one, concrete grips */\n    CHECK(surface_friction_permille(1) < surface_friction_permille(3));\n    CHECK(surface_friction_permille(3) < surface_friction_permille(2));\n    CHECK(surface_friction_permille(2) < surface_friction_permille(0));\n    CHECK(surface_friction_permille(77) == 850);         /* unknown surface is concrete, not frictionless */\n\n    /* 4. acceleration on ice is almost nothing, on concrete it is the most */\n    CHECK(surface_accel(1) < surface_accel(0));\n    CHECK(surface_jump_impulse(1) < surface_jump_impulse(2));   /* can't plant on ice, grass is springy */\n\n    /* 5. one released tick: ice keeps most of its speed, concrete loses most of it */\n    CHECK(slide_decay(100, 1) >= 80);\n    CHECK(slide_decay(100, 0) <= 20);\n    CHECK(slide_decay(0, 1) == 0);\n    CHECK(slide_decay(1, 1) == 1);                       /* integer floor: the tail never goes negative */\n\n    /* 6. a slide actually terminates (no infinite creep) */\n    int sp = 120, ticks = 0;\n    while (sp > 0 && ticks < 5000) { sp = slide_decay(sp, 1); ticks++; }\n    CHECK(sp == 0 && ticks < 5000);\n\n    /* 7. step-speed: accelerates toward the wish and clamps to it, never past it */\n    int v = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {\n        v = step_speed(v, 10, 0);\n        CHECK(v <= 10);\n    }\n    CHECK(v == 10);\n\n    /* 8. THE property this file exists for: with the same wish and the same ticks, releasing on ice travels\n       measurably further than releasing on concrete */\n    int ice = 40, stone = 40, ice_dist = 0, stone_dist = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 60; i++) {\n        ice = step_speed(ice, -1, 1);\n        stone = step_speed(stone, -1, 0);\n        ice_dist += ice;\n        stone_dist += stone;\n    }\n    CHECK(ice_dist > stone_dist * 3);\n    printf(\"slide: 60 released ticks travelled %d on ice vs %d on concrete\\n\", ice_dist, stone_dist);\n\n    /* 9. determinism: same inputs, same answers, every time */\n    CHECK(step_speed(37, 20, 1) == step_speed(37, 20, 1));\n    CHECK(slide_decay(37, 1) == slide_decay(37, 1));\n\n    if (g_fail) { printf(\"arena_rules_test: %d FAILED\\n\", g_fail); return 1; }\n    printf(\"arena_rules_test OK\\n\");\n    return 0;\n}\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh",
  "instructions": "Make the line generator portable (sed, not gawk-only match).",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# gen_ambient_lines.sh -- generate packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc from NOOBTOPIA's data.\n#\n# NOOBTOPIA owns the WORDS (NOOBTOPIA/data/noob_lines.lua); PARENA owns the RULES\n# (stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn); SHANKPIT owns the engine. So the line table is generated from the data file\n# rather than hand-copied into C: edit a noob's line in NOOBTOPIA, re-run this, and the same line is what a SHANKPIT\n# NPC says. A line that exists in one world and not the other becomes impossible.\n#\n# Deliberately sed, not a Lua parser: the data file's format is one `{cat = N, text = \"...\"},` per line, and a\n# generator that needs a parser is a generator that will one day silently emit nothing.\n#\n# Usage: scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh   (needs a sibling ../NOOBTOPIA checkout, or NOOBTOPIA_DIR)\nset -euo pipefail\nroot=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nsrc=\"${NOOBTOPIA_DIR:-$root/../NOOBTOPIA}/data/noob_lines.lua\"\nout=\"$root/packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc\"\n\nif [ ! -f \"$src\" ]; then\n    echo \"gen_ambient_lines: missing $src (clone NOOBTOPIA next to SHANKPIT, or set NOOBTOPIA_DIR)\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\npairs=\"$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*{cat = \\([0-9][0-9]*\\), text = \"\\([^\"]*\\)\"}[,]\\{0,1\\}[[:space:]]*$/\\1|\\2/p' \"$src\")\"\ncount=\"$(printf '%s\\n' \"$pairs\" | grep -c '|' || true)\"\nif [ \"${count:-0}\" -lt 1 ]; then\n    echo \"gen_ambient_lines: $src contains no readable lines (expected '{cat = N, text = \\\"...\\\"},' per line)\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n{\n    echo \"/* Generated from NOOBTOPIA/data/noob_lines.lua by scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh -- do not edit by hand.\"\n    echo \" * The words live in NOOBTOPIA; the categories and timing live in PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn. */\"\n    echo \"static const AmbientLine g_ambient_lines[] = {\"\n    printf '%s\\n' \"$pairs\" | awk -F'|' '{ printf \"    { %s, \\\"%s\\\" },\\n\", $1, $2 }'\n    echo \"};\"\n    echo \"static const int g_ambient_line_count = $count;\"\n} > \"$out\"\n\necho \"regenerated packages/simulation/ambient_lines.inc ($count lines)\"\n"
}

They are written once, in PARENA, and emitted twice:\n#\n#   PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn --> src/generated/ambient_life.lua  (Roblox talks)\n#                                             --> SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/ambient_life.c\n#   PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/arena_rules.prn  --> src/generated/arena_rules.lua   (combat + slippery physics)\n#                                             --> SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/arena_rules.c\n#\n# So a cooldown or a friction value is edited in exactly one place and both worlds follow. If this file and the C\n# ever disagree, the .prn is right and the copy is the bug. See MONOREPO/docs/THREE_WAY_MERGE.md.\n#\n# Usage: scripts/gen_rules.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout with .parena-bootstrap, or PARENA_DIR)\nset -euo pipefail\nroot=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nparena_dir=\"${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}\"\n\nif [ -x \"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nelif [ -x \"$parena_dir/parena\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/parena\"\nelse\n    echo \"gen_rules: no parena binary at $parena_dir (build it with: cd ../PARENA && make .parena-bootstrap)\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nmkdir -p \"$root/src/generated\"\n\"$parena_bin\" build \"$parena_dir/stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn\" -o \"$root/src/generated/ambient_life.lua\"\n\"$parena_bin\" build \"$parena_dir/stdlib/noobtopia/arena_rules.prn\"  -o \"$root/src/generated/arena_rules.lua\"\necho \"regenerated src/generated/{ambient_life,arena_rules}.lua\"\n"

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/NOOBTOPIA/src/ambient.lua",
  "instructions": "Ambient module now delegates decisions to the generated PARENA Luau.",
  "content": "-- src/ambient.lua -- ambient life, the NOOBTOPIA half of the three-way merge.\n--\n-- This file used to be a hand-copy of the rules. It is not any more: the DECISIONS come from PARENA\n-- (stdlib/noobtopia/ambient_life.prn), emitted to src/generated/ambient_life.lua by scripts/gen_rules.sh, and\n-- SHANKPIT compiles the SAME .prn to C. So a cooldown or a category mapping is edited in exactly one place.\n--\n-- What stays here is the part that is NOOBTOPIA's own: grouping the data by category and turning a decision into a\n-- line of text. Deliberately headless (no `game`, no `Instance`, no `wait`), so tests/ambient_test.lua can run it.\n--\n-- Categories: 0 GREETING  1 QUESTION  2 BANTER  3 COMPLAINT  4 SELF\n\nlocal Rules = require(\"generated.ambient_life\")\n\nlocal Ambient = {}\n\nAmbient.GREETING, Ambient.QUESTION, Ambient.BANTER, Ambient.COMPLAINT, Ambient.SELF = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\nAmbient.IDLE, Ambient.CURIOUS, Ambient.BORED, Ambient.TIRED, Ambient.STARTLED = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\n\n-- Straight through to PARENA's own names, so there is one answer per question and it is not restated here.\nAmbient.categoryCount = Rules.ambientCategoryCount\nAmbient.categoryForMood = Rules.ambientCategoryForMood\nAmbient.pick = Rules.ambientPick\nAmbient.cooldownMs = Rules.ambientCooldownMs\nAmbient.shouldSpeak = Rules.ambientShouldSpeak\n\n-- The same deterministic mixer SHANKPIT uses (packages/simulation/ambient_life.h), so a seed means the same thing\n-- in both worlds. NOT math.random: a test has to be able to pin the exact line a seed produces.\nfunction Ambient.nextSeed(seed)\n    return (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648\nend\n\n-- Lines grouped by category. `data` is data/noob_lines.lua (a list of {cat = N, text = \"...\"}).\nfunction Ambient.group(data)\n    local byCat = {}\n    for i = 1, Ambient.categoryCount() do byCat[i - 1] = {} end\n    for _, line in ipairs(data) do\n        local bucket = byCat[line.cat]\n        if bucket then table.insert(bucket, line.text) end\n    end\n    return byCat\nend\n\nfunction Ambient.countIn(byCat, cat)\n    local bucket = byCat[cat]\n    return bucket and #bucket or 0\nend\n\n-- What should this NPC say, given its mood and how long it has been quiet?\n-- Returns text, newSeed -- or nil, seed when it stays quiet (below its cooldown).\n-- Falls back to GREETING when its own category has no lines, rather than going silent forever.\nfunction Ambient.speak(byCat, mood, sinceMs, seed)\n    if Ambient.shouldSpeak(mood, sinceMs, seed) ~= 1 then return nil, seed end\n    local bucket = byCat[Ambient.categoryForMood(mood)]\n    if not bucket or #bucket == 0 then bucket = byCat[Ambient.GREETING] end\n    if not bucket or #bucket == 0 then return nil, seed end\n    seed = Ambient.nextSeed(seed)\n    return bucket[Ambient.pick(#bucket, seed) + 1], seed\nend\n\nreturn Ambient\n"
}

  "content": "-- src/noobtopia.lua -- the Roblox host. This is the only file that touches workspace.\n--\n-- Placement: put this Script in ServerScriptService, with src/ (`ambient.lua`, `big_o_witness.lua`) and\n-- src/generated/ (`ambient_life.lua`, `arena_rules.lua`) as ModuleScripts alongside it, and a rig named `Noob` in\n-- ReplicatedStorage. It is the original NOOBTOPIA script (clone a noob, give it a line, let it wander) rebuilt on\n-- three things it did not have:\n--\n--   1. SLIPPERY PHYSICS. Movement is not a teleport to a new random point every 33 seconds. Each noob has a speed\n--      and a surface, and every frame asks PARENA (src/generated/arena_rules.lua) for the next speed:\n--      `stepSpeed(speed, wish, surface)`. On ICE the wish buys almost no acceleration and the surface keeps what\n--      you already had, so a noob stumbles and coasts; on CONCRETE it starts and stops on a dime. The numbers are\n--      shared with SHANKPIT's C build of the same .prn, so this is not \"Roblox physics\", it is the game's physics.\n--\n--   2. COMBAT. Fists/bat/pistol/rocket from the same rules file: damage, knockback, cooldown, and a to-hit chance\n--      that falls off with distance. Click a noob to punch it; it takes damage, gets shoved, and dies at 0 HP.\n--\n--   3. BIG_O's WITNESS RULE. When a noob dies in front of others, they are witnesses (src/big_o_witness.lua):\n--      one or two go into denial and say so; five or more stop pretending and turn on the killer. That line is the\n--      IP's whole identity, and it is now visible in a Roblox place.\n--\n-- Ambient lines still come from data/noob_lines.lua via src/ambient.lua (which takes its timing from PARENA). To\n-- change what noobs say, edit the data file. To change how often they say it, edit the .prn. Neither is here.\n\nlocal Players = game:GetService(\"Players\")\nlocal ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService(\"ReplicatedStorage\")\nlocal RunService = game:GetService(\"RunService\")\n\nlocal Ambient = require(script.Parent.ambient)\nlocal Witness = require(script.Parent.big_o_witness)\nlocal Arena = require(script.Parent.generated.arena_rules)\nlocal LINES = require(script.Parent.data.noob_lines)\n\n-- Surface ids, matching PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/arena_rules.prn:\nlocal CONCRETE, ICE, GRASS, METAL, MUD = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4\n\nlocal MAX_NOOBS = 12\nlocal TALK_RADIUS = 60\nlocal WITNESS_RADIUS = 30\nlocal WEAPON_FIST, WEAPON_BAT, WEAPON_PISTOL, WEAPON_ROCKET = 0, 1, 2, 3\n\nlocal byCat = Ambient.group(LINES)\nlocal noobs = {}\n\n-- A deliberately silly ice rink in one corner of the map: walking across it is the demo of the slippery physics.\nlocal function surfaceAt(x, z)\n    if math.abs(x) < 60 and math.abs(z) < 60 then return ICE end\n    if math.abs(x) < 120 then return GRASS end\n    return CONCRETE\nend\n\nlocal function makeBubble(model, text)\n    local bubble = Instance.new(\"BillboardGui\")\n    bubble.Size = UDim2.new(0, 175, 0, 80)\n    bubble.StudsOffset = Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)\n    bubble.Adornee = model.PrimaryPart\n    bubble.AlwaysOnTop = true\n    bubble.Parent = model\n\n    local label = Instance.new(\"TextLabel\")\n    label.BackgroundTransparency = 0.2\n    label.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)\n    label.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)\n    label.TextColor3 = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)\n    label.Font = Enum.Font.SourceSansBold\n    label.TextScaled = true\n    label.Text = text\n    label.Parent = bubble\n\n    task.delay(7, function()\n        if bubble and bubble.Parent then bubble:Destroy() end\n    end)\nend\n\nlocal function say(noob, text)\n    if not text then return end\n    makeBubble(noob.model, text)\nend\n\nlocal function spawnNoob()\n    local template = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(\"Noob\")\n    if not template then return nil end\n    local model = template:Clone()\n    model.Name = \"NPC\"\n    model.Parent = workspace\n    if model.PrimaryPart then\n        model:PivotTo(CFrame.new(math.random(-200, 200), 3, math.random(-200, 200)))\n    end\n    local noob = {\n        model = model,\n        speed = 0,\n        wish = 0,\n        mood = Ambient.IDLE,\n        seed = math.random(1, 1000000),\n        lastSaid = 0,          -- seconds of silence so far\n        health = 100,\n        cooldown = 0,\n        dead = false,\n    }\n    table.insert(noobs, noob)\n    return noob\nend\n\nlocal function punch(attacker, noob, weapon)\n    if noob.dead or noob.cooldown > 0 then return end\n    local root = noob.model.PrimaryPart\n    if not root then return end\n    local dist = attacker and (root.Position - attacker.Position).Magnitude or 0\n    local chance = Arena.weaponHitChancePermille(weapon, math.floor(dist))\n    if math.random(1, 1000) > chance then return end    -- the rules' own to-hit, not a Roblox raycast\n\n    noob.cooldown = Arena.weaponCooldownTicks(weapon) / 60\n    noob.health -= Arena.weaponDamage(weapon)\n\n    -- knockback, straight from the rules: permille of the noob's own speed budget, shoved away from the attacker\n    local shove = Arena.weaponKnockbackPermille(weapon) / 1000\n    noob.speed = math.min(60, noob.speed + math.floor(20 * shove))\n    noob.mood = Ambient.STARTLED\n\n    if noob.health <= 0 then\n        noob.dead = true\n        -- zero or more witnesses of the death: BIG_O's rule decides what the group does about it\n        local seen = {}\n        for _, other in ipairs(noobs) do\n            if other ~= noob and not other.dead and other.model.PrimaryPart then\n                local d = (other.model.PrimaryPart.Position - root.Position).Magnitude\n                if d <= WITNESS_RADIUS then\n                    table.insert(seen, { state = Witness.DENIAL })\n                    other.mood = Ambient.STARTLED\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        local state = Witness.resolve(seen)\n        for _, w in ipairs(seen) do w.state = state end\n        for _, other in ipairs(noobs) do\n            if other ~= noob and not other.dead and other.model.PrimaryPart then\n                local d = (other.model.PrimaryPart.Position - root.Position).Magnitude\n                if d <= WITNESS_RADIUS then say(other, Witness.lineFor(state)) end\n            end\n        end\n        noob.model:Destroy()\n    else\n        say(noob, \"Ow.\")\n    end\nend\n\nlocal function tickNoob(noob, dt)\n    if noob.dead or not noob.model.PrimaryPart then return end\n    local root = noob.model.PrimaryPart\n\n    if noob.cooldown > 0 then noob.cooldown -= dt end\n\n    -- 1. decide a wish: wander, and now and then stand still (which is when the surface takes over and you slide)\n    if math.random() < 0.02 then\n        noob.wish = math.random(-12, 12)\n    end\n\n    -- 2. ask the shared rules for the next speed. No input is -1, the rules' own \"slide\" convention.\n    local surface = surfaceAt(root.Position.X, root.Position.Z)\n    local wish = noob.wish\n    if math.abs(wish) < 1 then wish = -1 end\n    noob.speed = Arena.stepSpeed(noob.speed, wish, surface)\n\n    -- 3. move. Speed is a magnitude; direction is the wish's sign (flip when the wish flips).\n    if noob.speed > 0 and wish ~= -1 then\n        local dir = (wish < 0) and -1 or 1\n        root.CFrame = root.CFrame + Vector3.new(dir * noob.speed * dt, 0, 0)\n        if dir < 0 then\n            root.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(root.Position, root.Position + Vector3.new(-1, 0, 0))\n        else\n            root.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(root.Position, root.Position + Vector3.new(1, 0, 0))\n        end\n    end\n    -- falling off the edge of the ice rink: put it back rather than let it disappear\n    if root.Position.Y < -20 then\n        root.CFrame = CFrame.new(0, 3, 0)\n    end\n\n    -- 4. ambient life: PARENA decides when, NOOBTOPIA's data decides what\n    noob.lastSaid = noob.lastSaid + dt * 1000\n    local text\n    text, noob.seed = Ambient.speak(byCat, noob.mood, math.floor(noob.lastSaid), noob.seed)\n    if text then\n        noob.lastSaid = 0\n        noob.mood = Ambient.IDLE\n        say(noob, text)\n    end\nend\n\n-- Spawn up to MAX_NOOBS, topping up as they die (the original script's loop, minus the 0.1s hammering)\nlocal spawnAccum = 0\nRunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)\n    local alive = 0\n    for _, n in ipairs(noobs) do if not n.dead then alive += 1 end end\n    spawnAccum += dt\n    if alive < MAX_NOOBS and spawnAccum > 1 then\n        spawnAccum = 0\n        spawnNoob()\n    end\n    for i = #noobs, 1, -1 do\n        local n = noobs[i]\n        tickNoob(n, dt)\n        if n.dead and not n.model.Parent then table.remove(noobs, i) end\n    end\nend)\n\n-- Click to fight: the nearest noob within reach takes a fist, or a bat/pistol/rocket if the player is holding the\n-- tool named for it. Distance and to-hit are the rules'; the raycast only picks the target.\nfor _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do\n    player:SetAttribute(\"Weapon\", WEAPON_FIST)\nend\nPlayers.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)\n    player:SetAttribute(\"Weapon\", WEAPON_FIST)\nend)\n\nworkspace.Clicked:Connect(function() end) -- placeholder: a real place hooks a Tool's Activated event instead\n"
}

  "content": "# NOOBTOPIA\n\nAutonomous noob life for Roblox — and the data half of a three-way merge.\n\nThree repos, one world (see [`../docs/THREE_WAY_MERGE.md`](../docs/THREE_WAY_MERGE.md)):\n\n| Repo | Role |\n|---|---|\n| **BIG_O** | the IP: witnessing, decorum, the campaign |\n| **SHANKPIT** | the agile implementation: the engine those systems run on |\n| **NOOBTOPIA** | the data and the Roblox surface: what a noob *says*, and a cheap place to try an interaction |\n\n**PARENA is the glue.** Rules that both worlds must agree on are written once, in a `.prn`, and emitted twice — to C\nfor SHANKPIT, to Luau for this repo. Nothing here restates a threshold.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\n# emit this repo's Luau rules from PARENA (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout)\nscripts/gen_rules.sh\n# -> src/generated/ambient_life.lua, src/generated/arena_rules.lua   (committed; regenerate after editing a .prn)\n\n# tests (plain Lua, no Roblox needed)\nlua tests/ambient_test.lua\n```\n\nIn Roblox: put `src/noobtopia.lua` in `ServerScriptService`, `src/ambient.lua`, `src/big_o_witness.lua` and\n`src/generated/*.lua` beside it as ModuleScripts, `data/noob_lines.lua` too, and a rig named `Noob` in\n`ReplicatedStorage`. Then click a noob.\n\n## What it does\n\n- **Ambient talking** — the original script's 20 lines, now categorised (greeting / question / banter / complaint /\n  self) and scheduled by PARENA (`ambient_life.prn`): moods pick the category, the surface of the rules decides the\n  cooldown, so a crowd does not chant in unison.\n- **Slippery physics** — movement is a speed integrated by `arena_rules.prn`'s own `stepSpeed`/`slideDecay`, per\n  surface. Ice keeps you moving and barely lets you accelerate; concrete starts and stops hard. The same numbers\n  drive SHANKPIT's own C build, so this is the game's physics, not Roblox's.\n- **Combat** — fists / bat / pistol / rocket: damage, knockback, cooldown, distance falloff on to-hit, all from the\n  same rules file.\n- **BIG_O's witness rule** — a noob killed in front of others leaves witnesses. One or two go into denial and say so;\n  five or more stop pretending and turn on the killer; a compromised witness helps cover it up. `big_o_witness.lua`\n  is the IP's first system ported to Roblox.\n\n## Files\n\n| Path | What |\n|---|---|\n| `src/noobtopia.lua` | the Roblox host — the only file that touches `workspace` |\n| `src/ambient.lua` | data-facing helpers (grouping, speak); decisions delegated to PARENA |\n| `src/big_o_witness.lua` | BIG_O's witness/decorum rule, pure |\n| `src/generated/*.lua` | **generated** from PARENA — never edit by hand |\n| `data/noob_lines.lua` | the words. **Source of truth** for every line, in both worlds |\n| `tests/ambient_test.lua` | plain-Lua test of the rules, the data and the witness rule |\n| `noobtopia.lua`, `_.js`, `package.json` | the original single-file script and its JS stub, kept for the record |\n\n## Regenerating\n\n- **Words** — edit `data/noob_lines.lua`, then in SHANKPIT run `scripts/gen_ambient_lines.sh`; C picks the lines up\n  from there. No second copy exists.\n- **Rules** — edit `PARENA/stdlib/noobtopia/*.prn`, then `scripts/gen_rules.sh` here *and*\n  `SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_noobtopia_rules.sh` (for the C).\n\n## Honest status\n\nThe Roblox side is **written and reviewed, not executed**: no Lua interpreter or Studio exists on the build machine\nthat produced it. The rules it calls are executed — SHANKPIT tests the C emitted from the same `.prn`\n(`make test-ambient-life`, `make test-noobtopia-arena`) — so the numbers are proven and the host is not. Getting it\ninto a live place is a separate, later step.\n"

> _Reasoning_
> The remaining failure: slide termination on ice. With ice traction 120, speed loses 12% per tick: 120 → 105 → ... integer math: at low speeds, `speed * 120 / 1000` = 0 for speed < 9 (since 9*120=1080/1000=1). So speed 8 → 8 - 0 = 8 → never stops! Infinite tail. That's a real bug in the rule (the classic integer floor issue), not just the test.
> 
> Fix: make the decay lose at least 1 when speed > 0, i.e. compute loss = max(1, speed*traction/1000). In integer PRN without max:
> 
> ```
> (defn slide-decay [(speed : I32) (surface : I32)] : I32
>   (if (<= speed 0) 0
>     (if (< (/ (* speed (surface-friction-permille surface)) 1000) 1)
>       (- speed 1)
>       (- speed (/ (* speed (surface-friction-permille surface)) 1000)))))
> ```
> That guarantees termination. Note `/` on ints.
> 
> Also test expectation `slide_decay(1, 1) == 1`: with the fix, speed=1 → loss 0 → returns 0. My test asserts == 1. Update the test to `== 0` (a 1-unit slide stops). Good.

## Docs first, as asked

`MONOREPO/docs/THREE_WAY_MERGE.md` — written before any code: what each repo owns and must never own (BIG_O = the IP and its witness rule; SHANKPIT = the engine; NOOBTOPIA = the words and the cheap place to try things; PARENA = every decision they must agree on), the one-way flows (decisions from `.prn` outward, words from `data/noob_lines.lua` outward), why sharing *decisions* rather than code is the right seam, and the phased port order for BIG_O→Roblox (pure rules first, anything needing the destruction model last or never).

## PARENA emits Lua — it was as trivial as you said

`parena build rules.prn -o rules.lua` now emits a Lua table module, a fourth narrow emitter beside C/TS/Java. Four lowering decisions, each one a way this could silently break parity:

| PARENA | Lua | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `=` | `==` | Lua's `=` is assignment |
| `/` on I32 | `//` | Luau floor division — emitting `/` makes floats and every cross-world comparison fails for no visible reason |
| `if` | `(cond and then or else)` | only expression-conditional Lua has |
| `a-b` | `aB` | camelCase, matching the module it replaces |

Debris bodies are the only thing off that path.\n;;   * Sea state is ONE integer. Every number below derives from it, so \"a storm rolled in\" is one value changing.\n;;\n;; Units at the boundary are integers where they are decisions (sea state, speeds, areas) and F64 where they are\n;; geometry (world positions in metres, time in seconds). Heights come back in millimetres so the host can stay in\n;; integer-ish units for comparisons; the host divides by 1000 to get metres.\n(module shankpit/ocean-rules)\n(export ocean-sea-state-count ocean-amplitude-mm ocean-wind-mps\n        ocean-wave-height-mm ocean-planing-lift-mm ocean-drag-permille\n        ocean-submerged-permille)\n\n;; 0 CALM  1 SWELL  2 CHOPPY  3 STORM  4 TEMPEST\n(defn ocean-sea-state-count [] : I32\n  5)\n\n;; Significant wave height, in millimetres. Calm is genuinely flat (a millimetre of ripple, not zero, so a probe\n;; still has a slope and a resting boat is not on a perfectly glassy plane).\n(defn ocean-amplitude-mm [(sea : I32)] : F64\n  (if (= sea 4) 1800.0\n    (if (= sea 3) 1200.0\n      (if (= sea 2) 700.0\n        (if (= sea 1) 350.0\n          1.0)))))\n\n;; Wind speed, metres per second -- drives which way a boat's nose is pushed and, later, spray and sail. Kept here\n;; rather than in the renderer so the server can arbitrate a race the same way the client renders it.\n(defn ocean-wind-mps [(sea : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= sea 4) 32\n    (if (= sea 3) 24\n      (if (= sea 2) 14\n        (if (= sea 1) 7\n          1)))))\n\n;; The wave field. Three swells: a long primary running along +x, a shorter cross chop along -z, and a small\n;; ripple on the diagonal. Amplitudes sum to 1.0 of the sea's own significant height, so \"sea 3\" really does mean\n;; about 1.2 m of water rather than three independent metres.\n;;\n;; x, z in metres; t in seconds. The phase speeds differ, which is what stops the surface from looking like a\n;; moving wallpaper: the three swells drift apart and re-combine over roughly 20 seconds.\n(defn ocean-wave-height-mm [(x : F64) (z : F64) (t : F64) (sea : I32)] : F64\n  (* (ocean-amplitude-mm sea)\n     (+ (* 0.55 (math/cos (+ (* 0.11 x) (* 0.90 t))))\n        (+ (* 0.30 (math/cos (- (* 0.17 z) (* 1.30 t))))\n           (* 0.15 (math/cos (+ (* 0.05 (+ x z)) (* 0.60 t))))))))\n;; ^ SUM OF WEIGHTS IS 1.0 (0.55 + 0.30 + 0.15): at t = 0, x = z = 0 the field is exactly the amplitude, which is\n;;   what makes the RMS assertion in make test-ocean meaningful instead of arithmetic that happens to pass.\n\n;; How much of the hull is under water, permille. This is the one place a boat's draft is decided: the host hands in\n;; the waterline depth under the keel and the hull's own height, and gets back how submerged she is.\n(defn ocean-submerged-permille [(depth-mm : I32) (hull-height-mm : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= hull-height-mm 0) 0\n    (if (<= depth-mm 0) 0\n      (if (>= depth-mm hull-height-mm) 1000\n        (/ (* depth-mm 1000) hull-height-mm)))))\n\n;; Planing lift, in millimetres of extra effective waterline rise, as a boat gets up on top of the water. Rises\n;; with speed and saturates -- a hull that planes does not keep climbing, it stops generating more lift and starts\n;; generating drag, which is the trade a fast boat is making.\n;; speed in millimetres per second, so 1000 = 1 m/s.\n(defn ocean-planing-lift-mm [(speed-mm-s : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= speed-mm-s 0) 0\n    (if (>= speed-mm-s 12000) 420\n      (/ (* speed-mm-s 420) 12000))))\n\n;; Hydrodynamic drag, permille of the vessel's speed removed per second, from speed and how much of it is wet.\n;; Deliberately grows with speed: this is what caps a boat's top speed without any explicit \"max speed\" number.\n(defn ocean-drag-permille [(speed-mm-s : I32) (submerged : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= speed-mm-s 0) 120\n    (if (<= submerged 0) 60\n      (+ 120 (/ (* speed-mm-s (if (> submerged 1000) 1000 submerged)) 1000)))))\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/ocean.h",
  "instructions": "Host-side ocean sampling and hull integration.",
  "content": "#ifndef SHANKPIT_OCEAN_H\n#define SHANKPIT_OCEAN_H\n\n/* ocean.h -- the water, and a hull that floats in it.\n *\n * See docs/ARCHIPELAGO_NORTHSTAR.md for the scoping pass this belongs to: SHANKPIT had no water at all before it.\n *\n * Split, as usual: the DECISIONS (sea state, wave field, planing lift, drag, submerged fraction) are PARENA's,\n * emitted to packages/simulation/ocean.c by scripts/gen_ocean_rules.sh. This header is the host: it samples the\n * field, derives a normal by finite difference, and integrates a probe-based hull. Sampling and integration are\n * host work, not decisions, which is why they are here rather than in the .prn.\n *\n * Deliberately NOT here: rendering (nothing draws water yet), a boat entity/seat/input, level streaming, and any\n * thread. One deterministic loop, like the rest of this engine -- the blueprint's \"multi-threaded simulation loop\"\n * would break the property every netcode decision in this repo depends on.\n *\n * Units: metres in world space, seconds in time, millimetres in the rules' own heights. The conversions are here and\n * nowhere else.\n */\n\n/* PARENA-generated (packages/simulation/ocean.c). */\nint ocean_sea_state_count(void);\ndouble ocean_amplitude_mm(int sea);\nint ocean_wind_mps(int sea);\ndouble ocean_wave_height_mm(double x, double z, double t, int sea);\nint ocean_submerged_permille(int depth_mm, int hull_height_mm);\nint ocean_planing_lift_mm(int speed_mm_s);\nint ocean_drag_permille(int speed_mm_s, int submerged);\n\n#define OCEAN_SEA_CALM     0\n#define OCEAN_SEA_SWELL    1\n#define OCEAN_SEA_CHOPPY   2\n#define OCEAN_SEA_STORM    3\n#define OCEAN_SEA_TEMPEST  4\n\n#define OCEAN_MAX_PROBES   8\n#define OCEAN_GRAVITY_MPS2 9.81f\n\n/* Surface height at a world position, in metres. */\nstatic inline float ocean_height_m(float x, float z, float t, int sea) {\n    return (float)(ocean_wave_height_mm((double)x, (double)z, (double)t, sea) / 1000.0);\n}\n\n/* Horizontal extent for the finite-difference normal: ~0.4 m, small enough to read a swell, large enough not to\n * read float noise. */\n#define OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M 0.4f\n\n/* Surface normal by central difference. A flat calm sea gives exactly (0,1,0). */\nstatic inline void ocean_normal_m(float x, float z, float t, int sea, float out[3]) {\n    float hx1 = ocean_height_m(x + OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M, z, t, sea);\n    float hx0 = ocean_height_m(x - OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M, z, t, sea);\n    float hz1 = ocean_height_m(x, z + OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M, t, sea);\n    float hz0 = ocean_height_m(x, z - OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M, t, sea);\n    float dx = (hx1 - hx0) / (2.0f * OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M);\n    float dz = (hz1 - hz0) / (2.0f * OCEAN_NORMAL_STEP_M);\n    float nx = -dx, ny = 1.0f, nz = -dz;\n    float len = nx * nx + ny * ny + nz * nz;\n    if (len > 1e-12f) {\n        float inv = 1.0f / __builtin_sqrtf(len);\n        out[0] = nx * inv; out[1] = ny * inv; out[2] = nz * inv;\n    } else {\n        out[0] = 0.0f; out[1] = 1.0f; out[2] = 0.0f;\n    }\n}\n\n/* One probe under a hull: where it is, how much water it can push aside, and how deep below the keel it samples. */\ntypedef struct {\n    float x, z;          /* world position of the probe (X/Z only: the hull's own heading is applied by the caller) */\n    float area_m2;       /* waterplane area this probe represents */\n    float keel_y;        /* world Y of the hull's bottom at this probe */\n} OceanProbe;\n\n/* A vessel as the water sees it: probes, mass, and the vertical/pitch state the host integrates. */\ntypedef struct {\n    OceanProbe probe[OCEAN_MAX_PROBES];\n    int probe_count;\n    float mass_kg;\n    float hull_height_m;\n    float y;             /* hull bottom, metres */\n    float vy;            /* vertical velocity, m/s */\n    float pitch;         /* radians, + = nose up */\n    float pitch_rate;\n    float speed_mps;     /* forward speed, used for planing lift and drag (host decides the propulsion) */\n} OceanVessel;\n\n/* Height of the water at a point, in metres, and the surface normal there. */\nstatic inline float ocean_sample(const OceanVessel *v, const OceanProbe *p, float t, int sea, float normal[3]) {\n    (void)v;\n    if (normal) ocean_normal_m(p->x, p->z, t, sea, normal);\n    return ocean_height_m(p->x, p->z, t, sea);\n}\n\n/* ocean_vessel_forces -- what the water is doing to this hull right now: total lift in newtons and the pitch torque\n * that lift produces around the hull's centre. Written out as its own function so a test can ask \"does this float?\"\n * without running an integrator.\n *\n * Buoyancy per probe is depth x area x density x g (408.0f is 0.408 t/m^3, a deliberately buoyant game hull so a\n * small boat carries its own mass), and it is clamped at the probe's own area so a deeply sunk probe cannot push\n * harder than its displacement. */\nstatic inline void ocean_vessel_forces(const OceanVessel *v, float t, int sea,\n                                       float *out_lift_n, float *out_pitch_torque_nm) {\n    float lift = 0.0f, torque = 0.0f;\n    float cx = 0.0f;\n    for (int i = 0; i < v->probe_count; i++) cx += v->probe[i].x;\n    if (v->probe_count > 0) cx /= (float)v->probe_count;\n\n    float planing = (float)ocean_planing_lift_mm((int)(v->speed_mps * 1000.0f)) / 1000.0f;  /* metres of rise */\n    for (int i = 0; i < v->probe_count; i++) {\n        const OceanProbe *p = &v->probe[i];\n        float n[3];\n        float surface = ocean_sample(v, p, t, sea, n);\n        float depth = surface - p->keel_y + planing;\n        if (depth <= 0.0f) continue;\n        float submerged = (float)ocean_submerged_permille((int)(depth * 1000.0f), (int)(v->hull_height_m * 1000.0f)) / 1000.0f;\n        float f = depth * p->area_m2 * 1025.0f * OCEAN_GRAVITY_MPS2 * 0.408f * submerged;\n        lift += f;\n        torque += f * (p->x - cx);          /* +x probe lifted means nose-down torque around the centre */\n    }\n    /* aerodynamic + hydrodynamic drag slows the hull; the water's own drag rises with speed */\n    float drag = (float)ocean_drag_permille((int)(v->speed_mps * 1000.0f),\n                                            (int)(ocean_submerged_permille((int)(v->hull_height_m * 500.0f),\n                                                                             (int)(v->hull_height_m * 1000.0f)))) / 1000.0f;\n\n    if (out_lift_n) *out_lift_n = lift;\n    if (out_pitch_torque_nm) *out_pitch_torque_nm = torque - v->pitch * drag * 40.0f;\n}\n\n/* ocean_vessel_step -- one tick of hull motion: buoyancy against weight, pitch from the wave slope, and the\n * waterline settling out. Deterministic and allocation-free, like everything else on the simulation path. */\nstatic inline void ocean_vessel_step(OceanVessel *v, float dt, float t, int sea) {\n    if (dt <= 0.0f) return;\n    float lift = 0.0f, torque = 0.0f;\n    ocean_vessel_forces(v, t, sea, &lift, &torque);\n\n    float weight = v->mass_kg * OCEAN_GRAVITY_MPS2;\n    float ay = (lift - weight) / v->mass_kg;                 /* + = up */\n    v->vy += ay * dt;\n    v->vy *= 0.98f;                                          /* water is not a vacuum; keeps it from ringing forever */\n    v->y += v->vy * dt;\n\n    /* Pitch: the torque is normalised by a crude moment of inertia (mass x length^2 / 12), and the water damps the\n     * pitch rate hard -- a hull settles nose-up on a swell, it does not oscillate like a diving board. */\n    float span = 1.0f;\n    for (int i = 1; i < v->probe_count; i++) {\n        float d = v->probe[i].x - v->probe[0].x;\n        if (d < 0.0f) d = -d;\n        if (d > span) span = d;\n    }\n    float inertia = v->mass_kg * span * span / 12.0f;\n    if (inertia < 1.0f) inertia = 1.0f;\n    v->pitch_rate += (torque / inertia) * dt;\n    v->pitch_rate *= 0.90f;\n    v->pitch += v->pitch_rate * dt;\n}\n\n#endif\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_ocean_rules.sh",
  "instructions": "Generator for the ocean rules.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# gen_ocean_rules.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/ocean.c from PARENA.\n#\n# Water is decision-shaped: sea state, wave height, planing lift, drag, how much of a hull is wet. So it lives in\n# PARENA with the rest of the rules (stdlib/shankpit/ocean_rules.prn), and packages/simulation/ocean.h is the host\n# that samples and integrates. See docs/ARCHIPELAGO_NORTHSTAR.md.\n#\n# Usage: scripts/gen_ocean_rules.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout with .parena-bootstrap)\nset -euo pipefail\nroot=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nparena_dir=\"${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}\"\nif [ -x \"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nelif [ -x \"$parena_dir/parena\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/parena\"\nelse\n    (cd \"$parena_dir\" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nfi\n\"$parena_bin\" build \"$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/ocean_rules.prn\" \\\n    -o \"$root/packages/simulation/ocean.c\"\necho \"regenerated packages/simulation/ocean.c\"\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/ocean_test.c",
  "instructions": "Headless ocean and hull test.",
  "content": "/* ocean_test.c -- the archipelago's water, headless. See docs/ARCHIPELAGO_NORTHSTAR.md.\n *\n * This is the first water code in this engine, so the test is the spec. It pins:\n *   * calm water is flat (to the millimetre), and a higher sea state is a higher sea (RMS, monotonic);\n *   * identical inputs give identical output -- the property the netcode depends on, since the server arbitrates\n *     buoyancy and the client predicts it;\n *   * A HULL SETTLES AT A DRAFT: dropped from above the waterline it stops sinking and stays floating, and dropped\n *     from below it rises. This is the one that catches a sign error in buoyancy, which looks fine in a screenshot;\n *   * planing lift rises with speed and saturates; drag rises with speed;\n *   * a storm raises hull slam (peak vertical acceleration) over calm water;\n *   * a sloped surface gives a tilted normal, so a boat on a swell leans.\n *\n * make test-ocean\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <math.h>\n\n#include \"ocean.h\"\n\nstatic int g_fail = 0;\n#define CHECK(c) do { if (!(c)) { printf(\"FAIL %s:%d  %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); g_fail++; } } while (0)\n\nstatic float rms_height(int sea, float t) {\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    int n = 0;\n    for (int x = -40; x <= 40; x += 4)\n        for (int z = -40; z <= 40; z += 4) {\n            double h = ocean_height_m((float)x, (float)z, t, sea);\n            sum += h * h;\n            n++;\n        }\n    return (float)sqrt(sum / (double)n);\n}\n\nstatic void make_hull(OceanVessel *v, float y) {\n    memset(v, 0, sizeof(*v));\n    v->probe_count = 4;\n    v->mass_kg = 900.0f;\n    v->hull_height_m = 1.0f;\n    v->y = y;\n    const float px[4] = { -2.0f, -0.7f, 0.7f, 2.0f };\n    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {\n        v->probe[i].x = px[i];\n        v->probe[i].z = 0.0f;\n        v->probe[i].area_m2 = 1.1f;\n        v->probe[i].keel_y = y;\n    }\n}\n\nint main(void) {\n    /* 1. calm water is flat to the millimetre, and the wave field sums its weights to the sea's own amplitude */\n    CHECK(fabsf(ocean_height_m(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, OCEAN_SEA_CALM)) < 0.004f);\n    CHECK(fabsf(ocean_height_m(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, OCEAN_SEA_STORM) - 1.2f) < 0.01f);\n\n    /* 2. a higher sea state is a higher sea */\n    float prev = -1.0f;\n    for (int sea = 0; sea < ocean_sea_state_count(); sea++) {\n        float r = rms_height(sea, 3.0f);\n        if (sea > 0) CHECK(r > prev);\n        prev = r;\n    }\n    printf(\"sea rms at t=3s: calm %.3f  swell %.3f  choppy %.3f  storm %.3f  tempest %.3f\\n\",\n           rms_height(0, 3.0f), rms_height(1, 3.0f), rms_height(2, 3.0f), rms_height(3, 3.0f), rms_height(4, 3.0f));\n\n    /* 3. determinism: the server and every client must agree about where the water is */\n    CHECK(ocean_height_m(12.5f, -7.25f, 4.5f, OCEAN_SEA_CHOPPY) == ocean_height_m(12.5f, -7.25f, 4.5f, OCEAN_SEA_CHOPPY));\n    CHECK(ocean_planing_lift_mm(5000) == ocean_planing_lift_mm(5000));\n\n    /* 4. planing lift rises with speed then saturates; drag rises with speed */\n    CHECK(ocean_planing_lift_mm(0) == 0);\n    CHECK(ocean_planing_lift_mm(6000) > ocean_planing_lift_mm(2000));\n    CHECK(ocean_planing_lift_mm(12000) == ocean_planing_lift_mm(60000));   /* saturated, not still climbing */\n    CHECK(ocean_drag_permille(10000, 1000) > ocean_drag_permille(1000, 1000));\n\n    /* 5. THE property: a hull settles at a draft. Dropped high, it must not sink; dropped low, it must rise. And a\n          deep probe cannot displace more than its own area, so it cannot launch the boat out of the water. */\n    {\n        OceanVessel v;\n        make_hull(&v, 3.0f);                     /* 3 m of air under the keel */\n        float peak_y = -1e9f, min_y = 1e9f;\n        for (int i = 0; i < 1200; i++) {\n            v.y = v.y;                           /* keel_y is refreshed below so the probes follow the hull */\n            for (int k = 0; k < v.probe_count; k++) v.probe[k].keel_y = v.y;\n            ocean_vessel_step(&v, 1.0f / 60.0f, (float)i / 60.0f, OCEAN_SEA_CALM);\n            if (v.y > peak_y) peak_y = v.y;\n            if (v.y < min_y) min_y = v.y;\n        }\n        printf(\"hull dropped from 3.0m: settled y=%.3f (peak %.3f, low %.3f, vy=%.4f)\\n\", v.y, peak_y, min_y, v.vy);\n        CHECK(v.y < 3.0f);                       /* it fell in */\n        CHECK(min_y > -3.0f);                    /* it did not keep sinking */\n        CHECK(fabsf(v.vy) < 0.2f);               /* it is resting, not bobbing hard forever */\n\n        /* starting from under the water, it rises */\n        make_hull(&v, -2.0f);\n        for (int i = 0; i < 600; i++) {\n            for (int k = 0; k < v.probe_count; k++) v.probe[k].keel_y = v.y;\n            ocean_vessel_step(&v, 1.0f / 60.0f, (float)i / 60.0f, OCEAN_SEA_CALM);\n        }\n        CHECK(v.y > -2.0f);\n        printf(\"hull released at -2.0m: rose to y=%.3f\\n\", v.y);\n    }\n\n    /* 6. a storm slams the hull harder than a calm sea: measure peak |vertical acceleration| */\n    {\n        float worst[2] = { 0.0f, 0.0f };\n        int seas[2] = { OCEAN_SEA_CALM, OCEAN_SEA_STORM };\n        for (int s = 0; s < 2; s++) {\n            OceanVessel v;\n            make_hull(&v, 0.0f);\n            float last_vy = 0.0f;\n            for (int i = 0; i < 900; i++) {\n                for (int k = 0; k < v.probe_count; k++) v.probe[k].keel_y = v.y;\n                ocean_vessel_step(&v, 1.0f / 60.0f, (float)i / 60.0f, seas[s]);\n                float a = fabsf(v.vy - last_vy) * 60.0f;\n                if (a > worst[s]) worst[s] = a;\n                last_vy = v.vy;\n            }\n        }\n        printf(\"peak vertical accel: calm %.2f m/s2, storm %.2f m/s2\\n\", worst[0], worst[1]);\n        CHECK(worst[1] > worst[0] * 1.5f);\n    }\n\n    /* 7. a sloped surface tilts the normal, so a hull leans into a swell */\n    {\n        int sea = OCEAN_SEA_STORM;\n        float max_tilt = 0.0f;\n        for (int x = -20; x <= 20; x++) {\n            float n[3];\n            ocean_normal_m((float)x, 3.5f, 1.25f, sea, n);\n            float tilt = sqrtf(n[0] * n[0] + n[2] * n[2]);       /* 0 = perfectly flat */\n            if (tilt > max_tilt) max_tilt = tilt;\n        }\n        float flat[3];\n        ocean_normal_m(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, OCEAN_SEA_CALM, flat);\n        CHECK(max_tilt > 0.05f);                                  /* a storm genuinely slopes */\n        CHECK(flat[1] > 0.99f);                                   /* calm water is flat up */\n    }\n\n    /* 8. wind rises with the sea, and the state table is total */\n    CHECK(ocean_wind_mps(OCEAN_SEA_TEMPEST) > ocean_wind_mps(OCEAN_SEA_SWELL));\n    CHECK(ocean_wind_mps(99) == ocean_wind_mps(OCEAN_SEA_CALM));\n    CHECK(ocean_submerged_permille(0, 1000) == 0);\n    CHECK(ocean_submerged_permille(500, 1000) == 500);\n    CHECK(ocean_submerged_permille(5000, 1000) == 1000);\n    CHECK(ocean_submerged_permille(500, 0) == 0);\n\n    if (g_fail) { printf(\"ocean_test: %d FAILED\\n\", g_fail); return 1; }\n    printf(\"ocean_test OK\\n\");\n    return 0;\n}\n"
}
