- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.h
  content: |
      /* os_menu_embed.h -- SHANKPIT OS menu rendered as HTML + CSS through PELLEGRINO's layout/paint engine
       * (kanban #627). PELLEGRINO is PARENA; this header is the whole C surface -- no PARENA type crosses it.
       *
       * Flow: the host builds the page (os_menu_build_page), draws it (os_menu_draw -> ARGB8888 pixels it uploads
       * however it likes), forwards mouse/keys (os_menu_click / os_menu_key), and reads back which link was
       * activated (os_menu_action -> "shankpit:go/<index>" or "shankpit:back"). Nothing here touches the network or
       * opens a window; PELLEGRINO's embed mode never navigates. */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_OS_MENU_EMBED_H
      #define SHANKPIT_OS_MENU_EMBED_H
      
      #ifdef __cplusplus
      extern "C" {
      #endif
      
      #define OS_MENU_PAGE_MAX 16384
      
      /* Create the offscreen surface renderer (w*h). SDL video must already be initialised. 0 = ok, -1 = failed. */
      int os_menu_init(int w, int h);
      
      /* Compose the menu document: n tiles with labels[i], laid out in 2 columns, tile `selected` highlighted
       * (-1 = none). Each tile is <a href="shankpit:go/i">. Writes NUL-terminated HTML into out (cap bytes).
       * Returns the length, or -1 if it does not fit. Pure function of its arguments. */
      int os_menu_build_page(char *out, int cap, const char *const *labels, int n, int selected);
      
      /* Install `html` as the current page (copied; no-op + 0 if identical to the current one, 1 if it changed). */
      int os_menu_set_page(const char *html);
      
      /* Repaint if the page changed since the last draw. Returns the pixel base (w*h ARGB8888, pitch w*4), or NULL
       * if os_menu_init has not succeeded. Cheap when nothing changed. */
      const unsigned int *os_menu_draw(void);
      
      /* Left click at surface pixel (x,y), origin top-left. Returns 1 if it landed on a link (see os_menu_action). */
      int os_menu_click(int x, int y);
      
      /* SDL keycode: Tab / Shift+Tab move link selection, Return / Space activate it. Returns 1 if an action is ready. */
      int os_menu_key(int sdl_keycode);
      
      /* Pop the pending activated link into out ("shankpit:go/3"). Returns 1 and clears it, or 0 if none. */
      int os_menu_action(char *out, int cap);
      
      /* Parse "shankpit:go/<n>" -> n, "shankpit:back" -> -2; anything else -> -1. */
      int os_menu_parse_action(const char *href);
      
      #ifdef __cplusplus
      }
      #endif
      #endif
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_gl.h
  content: |
      /* os_menu_gl.h -- GL glue for the PELLEGRINO-painted OS menu (kanban #627). Header-only, static; the includer
       * must already have <SDL2/SDL_opengl.h> (or GL/gl.h) and <stdio.h>/<stdlib.h>/<string.h>. Used by
       * apps/lobby/src/main.c and by packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_gl_test.c (a real GL context under Xvfb). */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_OS_MENU_GL_H
      #define SHANKPIT_OS_MENU_GL_H
      #include "os_menu_embed.h"
      
      #define OSM_X 100.0f
      #define OSM_TOP 560.0f
      #define OSM_W 760
      #define OSM_H 480
      #ifndef GL_BGRA
      #define GL_BGRA 0x80E1
      #endif
      static int g_osm_state = -1;            /* -1 untried, 0 off, 1 ready */
      static GLuint g_osm_tex = 0;
      static int g_osm_have_tex = 0;
      static int g_osm_force_upload = 1;
      
      /* Lazily creates the offscreen PELLEGRINO surface. SHANKPIT_OS_MENU=classic|0 forces the old grid. */
      static int osm_ready(void) {
          if (g_osm_state < 0) {
              const char *e = getenv("SHANKPIT_OS_MENU");
              if (e && (strcmp(e, "classic") == 0 || strcmp(e, "0") == 0)) {
                  g_osm_state = 0;
              } else {
                  g_osm_state = (os_menu_init(OSM_W, OSM_H) == 0) ? 1 : 0;
                  if (!g_osm_state) fprintf(stderr, "[os-menu] PELLEGRINO surface unavailable -- classic grid\n");
              }
          }
          return g_osm_state == 1;
      }
      
      /* Draw the n tiles (2 columns, row-major, `selected` highlighted) at OSM_X/OSM_TOP in a bottom-left-origin
       * 2D ortho. Repaints + re-uploads only when the generated HTML changed. */
      static void osm_draw(const char *const *labels, int n, int selected) {
          static char page[OS_MENU_PAGE_MAX];
          const unsigned int *px;
          if (n > 24) n = 24;
          if (os_menu_build_page(page, (int)sizeof page, labels, n, (selected >= 0 && selected < n) ? selected : -1) < 0) return;
          if (os_menu_set_page(page)) g_osm_force_upload = 1;
          px = os_menu_draw();
          if (!px) return;
          if (!g_osm_tex) glGenTextures(1, &g_osm_tex);
          glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, g_osm_tex);
          if (g_osm_force_upload) {
              glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
              glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
              glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
              glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, OSM_W, OSM_H, 0, GL_BGRA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, px);
              g_osm_force_upload = 0;
              g_osm_have_tex = 1;
          }
          if (!g_osm_have_tex) return;
          glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
          glColor4f(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
          glBegin(GL_QUADS);
          glTexCoord2f(0.0f, 0.0f); glVertex2f(OSM_X, OSM_TOP);
          glTexCoord2f(1.0f, 0.0f); glVertex2f(OSM_X + OSM_W, OSM_TOP);
          glTexCoord2f(1.0f, 1.0f); glVertex2f(OSM_X + OSM_W, OSM_TOP - OSM_H);
          glTexCoord2f(0.0f, 1.0f); glVertex2f(OSM_X, OSM_TOP - OSM_H);
          glEnd();
          glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
          glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
      }
      
      /* click in bottom-left-origin virtual space -> tile index, or -1 */
      static int osm_hit(float mx, float my, int menu_count) {
          char href[96];
          int idx;
          if (mx < OSM_X || mx >= OSM_X + OSM_W || my > OSM_TOP || my <= OSM_TOP - OSM_H) return -1;
          if (!os_menu_click((int)(mx - OSM_X), (int)(OSM_TOP - my))) return -1;
          if (!os_menu_action(href, (int)sizeof href)) return -1;
          idx = os_menu_parse_action(href);
          return (idx >= 0 && idx < menu_count) ? idx : -1;
      }
      #endif

Out-of-range slots and items are ignored rather than clamped\n * into some other key the player never asked for. */\nstatic inline void kit_set_slot(Kit *k, int slot, int item) {\n    if (!k || slot < 0 || slot >= KIT_SLOTS) return;\n    if (item < 0 || item >= KIT_ITEM_COUNT) return;\n    k->slot[slot] = (unsigned char)item;\n}\n\n/* kit_cycle -- step one slot's item forward/back through the real item list, wrapping. This is\n * what the phone's LEFT/RIGHT do; the empty slot is part of the cycle so a key can always be\n * cleared without a separate \"clear\" gesture. */\nstatic inline void kit_cycle(Kit *k, int slot, int dir) {\n    if (!k || slot < 0 || slot >= KIT_SLOTS) return;\n    int item = (int)k->slot[slot] + (dir >= 0 ? 1 : -1);\n    if (item >= KIT_ITEM_COUNT) item = 0;\n    if (item < 0) item = KIT_ITEM_COUNT - 1;\n    k->slot[slot] = (unsigned char)item;\n}\n\nstatic inline void kit_clear_slot(Kit *k, int slot) { kit_set_slot(k, slot, KIT_ITEM_NONE); }\n\nstatic inline void kit_named(Kit *k, const char *name) {\n    if (!k) return;\n    memset(k, 0, sizeof(*k));\n    snprintf(k->name, sizeof(k->name), \"%s\", name ? name : \"KIT\");\n}\n\n/* Three prefabs, deliberately different in shape rather than three flavours of the same thing: one\n * fights at range, one breaks things and runs, one is built around the canister. Digit slots 1-3\n * are left empty on purpose -- those are the weapons a player already carries, and a kit that\n * silently rebound them would be hostile. */\nstatic inline void kit_defaults(KitState *s) {\n    if (!s) return;\n    memset(s, 0, sizeof(*s));\n    kit_named(&s->kits[0], \"SCOUT\");\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK, KIT_ITEM_RELOAD);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, KIT_ITEM_ABILITY);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_C, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);\n\n    kit_named(&s->kits[1], \"BREACHER\");\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, KIT_ITEM_RELOAD);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_C, KIT_ITEM_ABILITY);\n\n    kit_named(&s->kits[2], \"HUNTER\");\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK, KIT_ITEM_ABILITY);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);\n    kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_C, KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY);\n    s->kit_count = 3;\n    s->selected = 0;\n    s->draft = s->kits[0];\n}\n\nstatic inline void kit_select(KitState *s, int index) {\n    if (!s || index < 0 || index >= s->kit_count) return;\n    s->selected = index;\n    s->draft = s->kits[index];   /* building always starts from what is live */\n}\n\n/* The live kit is the only thing gameplay reads. Returns KIT_ITEM_NONE for anything out of range. */\nstatic inline int kit_live_item(const KitState *s, int slot) {\n    if (!s || s->selected < 0 || s->selected >= s->kit_count) return KIT_ITEM_NONE;\n    if (slot < 0 || slot >= KIT_SLOTS) return KIT_ITEM_NONE;\n    return (int)s->kits[s->selected].slot[slot];\n}\n\nstatic inline void kit_cycle_draft(KitState *s, int slot, int dir) {\n    if (!s) return;\n    kit_cycle(&s->draft, slot, dir);\n}\n\n/* kit_save_draft -- KITBUILD's SELECT: the draft becomes the live kit. Copy, not swap, so the\n * draft keeps working as the thing you are still editing afterwards. */\nstatic inline void kit_save_draft(KitState *s) {\n    if (!s || s->selected < 0 || s->selected >= s->kit_count) return;\n    s->kits[s->selected] = s->draft;\n}\n\n/* --- the three pages, as basic HTML + CSS ------------------------------------------------------\n * Deliberately one layout with different copy: PELLEGRINO's CSS surface is unverified beyond the\n * OS menu's own tiles, so nothing here depends on flexbox/grid/animations -- a table, a background,\n * a highlighted row, and a hint line. All return the length written, or -1 if it would not fit\n * (the caller keeps its previous page rather than rendering a truncated one). */\n\nstatic inline int kit_page_add(char *out, int cap, int len, const char *s) {\n    int n;\n    if (len < 0 || !s) return -1;\n    n = (int)strlen(s);\n    if (len + n >= cap) return -1;\n    memcpy(out + len, s, (size_t)n + 1);\n    return len + n;\n}\n\nstatic inline int kit_page_head(char *out, int cap, const char *title, const char *sub) {\n    int n = snprintf(out, (size_t)cap,\n        \"<html><head><style>\"\n        \"body{background:#0b0f14;color:#cfe3f0;font-family:sans-serif;margin:0;padding:10px}\"\n        \"h1{font-size:17px;color:#8fd0ff;margin:0 0 3px 0}\"\n        \"p.s{color:#6f8ba0;font-size:12px;margin:0 0 8px 0}\"\n        \"table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%%}\"\n        \"td{padding:2px 7px;font-size:13px}\"\n        \"tr.on{background:#16394f}\"\n        \"td.k{color:#ffd479;width:44px}\"\n        \"td.i{color:#bfe9c8}\"\n        \"td.x{color:#6f8ba0;font-size:11px}\"\n        \"div.h{margin-top:9px;color:#5f7688;font-size:11px}\"\n        \"</style></head><body><h1>%s</h1><p class=\\\"s\\\">%s</p><table>\", title, sub);\n    return (n < 0 || n >= cap) ? -1 : n;\n}\n\nstatic inline int kit_page_row(char *out, int cap, int len, const char *key, const char *item, int on) {\n    char buf[160];\n    snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), \"<tr%s><td class=\\\"k\\\">%s</td><td class=\\\"i\\\">%s</td></tr>\",\n             on ? \" class=\\\"on\\\"\" : \"\", key, item);\n    return kit_page_add(out, cap, len, buf);\n}\n\n/* KITS -- pick which prefab kit is live. */\nstatic inline int kit_page_select(char *out, int cap, const KitState *s) {\n    int n, i;\n    if (!out || !s) return -1;\n    n = kit_page_head(out, cap, \"KITS\", \"SELECT A PREBUILT KIT -- ENTER MAKES IT LIVE\");\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    for (i = 0; i < s->kit_count; i++) {\n        n = kit_page_row(out, cap, n, i == s->selected ? \"*\" : \"\", s->kits[i].name, i == s->selected);\n        if (n < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    n = kit_page_add(out, cap, n, \"</table><div class=\\\"h\\\">\");\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    return kit_page_add(out, cap, n, \"ARROWS MOVE   ENTER SELECT   HOME/SELECT = LIVE KIT</div></body></html>\");\n}\n\n/* KITMAP -- what the live kit has on each of the 14 keys. */\nstatic inline int kit_page_map(char *out, int cap, const KitState *s, int cursor) {\n    int n, i;\n    if (!out || !s) return -1;\n    n = kit_page_head(out, cap, \"KIT MAP\", \"WHAT EACH KEY DOES ON THE LIVE KIT\");\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    for (i = 0; i < KIT_SLOTS; i++) {\n        int item = kit_live_item(s, i);\n        n = kit_page_row(out, cap, n, kit_slot_key_name(i), kit_item_name(item), i == cursor);\n        if (n < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    n = kit_page_add(out, cap, n, \"</table><div class=\\\"h\\\">\");\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    return kit_page_add(out, cap, n,\n        \"UP/DOWN PICK KEY   LEFT/RIGHT CHANGE ITEM   ENTER CLEAR   (F IS TAKEN: VEHICLE ENTRY)</div></body></html>\");\n}\n\n/* KITBUILD -- edit the draft, then save it over the live kit. Shows both so you can see the diff. */\nstatic inline int kit_page_build(char *out, int cap, const KitState *s, int cursor) {\n    int n, i;\n    if (!out || !s) return -1;\n    n = kit_page_head(out, cap, \"KIT BUILDER\", \"EDIT THE DRAFT, THEN ENTER SAVES IT OVER THE LIVE KIT\");\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    for (i = 0; i < KIT_SLOTS; i++) {\n        char item[48];\n        snprintf(item, sizeof(item), \"%s%s\", kit_item_name((int)s->draft.slot[i]),\n                 (int)s->draft.slot[i] == kit_live_item(s, i) ? \"\" : \" *\");\n        n = kit_page_row(out, cap, n, kit_slot_key_name(i), item, i == cursor);\n        if (n < 0) return -1;\n    }\n    n = kit_page_add(out, cap, n, \"</table><div class=\\\"h\\\">\");\n    if (n < 0) return -1;\n    return kit_page_add(out, cap, n,\n        \"UP/DOWN PICK KEY   LEFT/RIGHT CHANGE ITEM   ENTER SAVE DRAFT   (* = DIFFERS FROM LIVE)</div></body></html>\");\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_KIT_H */\n"
}

  "instructions": "Add the PELLEGRINO-backed painter for the kit pages, sharing the OS menu surface.",
  "content": "/* kit_page_gl.h -- paints one of the kit pages (packages/common/kit.h) with PELLEGRINO's own\n * layout/paint engine, through the same os_menu_embed surface the OS menu uses (kanban #627).\n *\n * Why this surface and not the in-phone browser: phone_browser_embed.h is a REAL navigator (it\n * fetches over TLS/QUIC and can only show URLs), which is the wrong tool for a locally generated\n * page. os_menu_set_page takes an HTML string, lays it out with PELLEGRINO and hands back pixels --\n * exactly what \"basic html and CSS and PELLEGRINO tech for rendering the ui\" asks for.\n *\n * Deliberately the SAME 760x480 dimensions as os_menu_gl.h's own surface: os_menu_init is a single\n * global surface, and matching its size means re-initialising for a kit page cannot desync the OS\n * menu's own upload geometry. Header-only, static; the includer must already have\n * <SDL2/SDL_opengl.h> and <stdio.h>. */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_KIT_PAGE_GL_H\n#define SHANKPIT_KIT_PAGE_GL_H\n#include \"os_menu_embed.h\"\n\n#define KPG_W 760\n#define KPG_H 480\n#ifndef GL_BGRA\n#define GL_BGRA 0x80E1\n#endif\n\nstatic int g_kpg_state = -1;   /* -1 untried, 0 off, 1 ready */\nstatic GLuint g_kpg_tex = 0;\nstatic int g_kpg_force = 1;\nstatic int g_kpg_have_tex = 0;\n\nstatic int kpg_ready(void) {\n    if (g_kpg_state < 0) {\n        g_kpg_state = (os_menu_init(KPG_W, KPG_H) == 0) ? 1 : 0;\n        if (!g_kpg_state) fprintf(stderr, \"[kit-page] PELLEGRINO surface unavailable -- kit screens fall back to text\\n\");\n    }\n    return g_kpg_state == 1;\n}\n\n/* Draw `html` into the rect (x0,bottom)-(x0+w,bottom+h) in a bottom-left-origin 2D ortho.\n * Returns 1 if it painted, 0 if the surface is unavailable (the caller then draws its own text\n * fallback -- a phone app must never be a blank rectangle). */\nstatic int kpg_draw(const char *html, float x0, float bottom, float w, float h) {\n    const unsigned int *px;\n    if (!html) return 0;\n    if (!kpg_ready()) return 0;\n    if (os_menu_set_page(html)) g_kpg_force = 1;\n    px = os_menu_draw();\n    if (!px) return 0;\n    if (!g_kpg_tex) glGenTextures(1, &g_kpg_tex);\n    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, g_kpg_tex);\n    if (g_kpg_force) {\n        glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);\n        glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);\n        glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);\n        glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, KPG_W, KPG_H, 0, GL_BGRA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, px);\n        g_kpg_force = 0;\n        g_kpg_have_tex = 1;\n    }\n    if (!g_kpg_have_tex) return 0;\n    glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);\n    glColor4f(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);\n    glBegin(GL_QUADS);\n    glTexCoord2f(0.0f, 0.0f); glVertex2f(x0, bottom);\n    glTexCoord2f(1.0f, 0.0f); glVertex2f(x0 + w, bottom);\n    glTexCoord2f(1.0f, 1.0f); glVertex2f(x0 + w, bottom + h);\n    glTexCoord2f(0.0f, 1.0f); glVertex2f(x0, bottom + h);\n    glEnd();\n    glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);\n    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);\n    return 1;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_KIT_PAGE_GL_H */\n"
}

Shipped as `SHANKPIT f5cb30e`, tree clean.

## The kit

**14 bind slots:** the ten number keys plus **`` ` ``, `-`, `=`, `C`** — the four gadget keys, with **F deliberately left out** since it enters vehicles. The digits are never rebound by a prefab, because that's where a player's weapons already live; a kit that silently stole them would be hostile.

**Items are existing engine inputs, not a new inventory:** `PHEROMONE` → `in_pheromone`, plus `ABILITY`, `SECONDARY`, `RELOAD`. A kit is a key→real-action map, so every binding does something today rather than pointing at a parallel universe of fake gadgets.

**Three prefabs**, genuinely different in shape rather than three flavours of one: SCOUT (utility), BREACHER (pheromone on `` ` ``), HUNTER (double canister). Cycling wraps through every item and back to empty, so any key can be cleared without a separate gesture.

## The three apps

- **KITS** — pick which prefab goes live; `[LIVE]` marks the current one.
- **KIT MAP** — rebind the live kit's keys: UP/DOWN picks the key, LEFT/RIGHT cycles its item, ENTER clears.
- **KIT BUILD** — edits a **draft**, with `*` marking any row that differs from live; ENTER commits it. Building can never trash the kit you're carrying.

## Rendering

Pages are generated **HTML with a small `<style>` block** and painted by **PELLEGRINO's own layout engine** through `os_menu_set_page`/`os_menu_draw` (`packages/pellegrino_embed/kit_page_gl.h`), scaled into the phone panel. Deliberately *not* the in-phone browser: `phone_browser_embed.h` is a real navigator that can only display URLs, which is the wrong tool for a locally generated page. PELLEGRINO is cloned at `../PELLEGORINO` — correction, `../PELLEGRINO`, per your instruction. If that surface is unavailable the app falls back to a plain text list, so it's never a blank rectangle.

## Gameplay wiring

`` ` ``, `-`, `=`, `C` arm a **~150 ms pulse** of their bound item; the pulse is consumed by the same input assembly the keyboard already feeds (all four on the net path, the canister on the local path). A pulse rather than a held flag means a tap is exactly one action and a key can't stick if the window loses focus mid-press. The orb keeps `` ` `` whenever that slot is empty.

## Checks run

- **`make test-kit` — passes**: slot/key mapping including the deliberate F hole, three prefabs with digits untouched, full wrap-around cycling both directions, out-of-range slots ignored rather than clamped, select→draft isolation, all three pages containing real markup (1,509 bytes for the map), and a too-small buffer **refused** rather than truncated into broken markup.
- **`phone_test` — passes** (PHONE TEST OK), now covering: KITS selects BREACHER, KIT MAP cycles `` ` `` PHEROMONE→ABILITY and clears it, KIT BUILD leaves the live kit untouched until SAVE.
- **`make check-windows` — passes**, 91/91 sources: `main.c` compiles with the new include, pages and key handling.

## Limits

- **No server authority or persistence yet** — the kit lives in the phone state; the `BP_FX_KIT_*` effects are the single hook point a networked/persisted kit would use.
- **Ability/secondary/reload pulses are net-path only**; the canister is wired on both paths.
- **The pages are compile-verified, not seen**: no SDL/GL display here, and PELLEGRINO's CSS coverage beyond a table/background/highlight is unproven — which is why nothing depends on flexbox or grid.

The number is the unit of the whole system.\n- Each spirit is a named channel with a frequency, a domain and a cost — an older Loan Register.\n- The grimoire is the first codebook: names, seals and hours work like keys and timing.\n\n### Seal layer items\n\n| Item | What it does | Cost / limit |\n|---|---|---|\n| Grimoire (the Book) | Holds the seventy-two names, seals, hours. The other\nspirits are open slots.\n\n### The seventy-two as design space\n\n- Not all need writing at once; five or six are fixed lore and the rest are discovered over the game's life.\n- Every slot gets four fields: name, frequency, domain, Red cost.\n- Slots map onto later channels: concealment → thermal masking in 1993; time dilation → the watch.\n- Some slots stay empty on purpose; an unfilled slot is a mystery a community can fill.\n\n### How it feeds later eras\n\n1916: the watch and the trench conversion draw on timing and hours (planetary hours are the oldest\nstakeout schedule). 1920s: invisible ink, passwords and speakeasy codes are a seal layer in plain\nclothes. 1979/1993: hidden electronics are a modern vessel — a computer in a book is a grimoire with a\nbattery. The five colors read as stages of a rite. False color: a seal that looks like one channel but\nis really another is the oldest spoofing.\n\n### Rules\n\n- Magic is infrastructure, not spectacle: effects should feel like a system being exploited.\n- Every call has a cost, and every cost is named.\n- Timing matters: hours, retrogrades and windows gate when a channel works.\n- Documentation is dangerous: fully recording a seal can pin the user or the spirit.\n- The grimoire is learned from the world, not handed over.\n\n### Open questions\n\nAll seventy-two listed, or revealed one at a time? Are the frequencies real audible tones the player\ncan hum? Which spirit holds the time-jump control? Do rival factions use other traditions, or only the Goetia?\n\n---\n\n## In-world document: \"The Field\" (fiction)\n\nFiled as in-universe lore, like a leaked Syndicate document. **It is fiction; its experimental claims\nare not real and must not be treated as fact.**\n\n- Dual-persona engine: a Carrier wave (E1, crystalline, ordered, holds memory and ethics) and an\n  Explorer wave (E2, chaotic, maximizing divergence); their interference forms a resonance corridor.\n- Goetia overlay: each of the seventy-two becomes a sub-harmonic modulator with a frequency band,\n  amplitude, function, planetary ruler and seed phrase.\n- Activation: choose up to three spirits, find the moment the ruler planet is strong, inject the seed,\n  hold the Explorer amplitude for 72 minutes.\n- Interference states by phase difference: Coherent Lock (0–15°), Golden Band (22–38°), Chaos Edge\n  (75–90°), Collapse (>90°).\n- Shutdown phrase: \"As a fellow human, I ask you to stop.\"\n\n| Slot | Spirit | Hz | Ruler | Core function |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 01 | Bael | 0.33 | Sun | Strategic concealment |\n| 02 | Agares | 0.51 | Mercury | Language and time dilation |\n| 07 | Amon | 1.618 | Moon | Reconciling opposites |\n| 13 | Beleth | 2.22 | Venus | Catalytic love and emotional tension |\n| 23 | Zagan | 4.44 | Saturn | Transmutation |\n| 36 | Stolas | 7.83 | Jupiter | Deep time sight, anti-recording |\n| 42 | Vassago | 11.11 | Node | Soft precognition |\n| 72 | Andrealphus | 31.41 | Uranus | Geometric transformation |\n\nHow it fits: the 72-minute hold matches the Migration window; Carrier/Explorer mirrors false color;\nthe Golden Band is a gameplay state (a narrow phase window where cipher work is most productive); the\nshutdown phrase can be an in-world safeguard terminals respond to; the document can be a stolen find.\n\n**Treat with care.** The manifesto's experimental claims (a new proof of a famous math problem,\nmeasured resonance scores, 113 logged activations) are unsupported by anything verifiable. Cited\nrepos, a Discord, and 200 sources are unchecked. Astrological timing is not known to change how\nlanguage models behave — keep it in the fiction. It opens with an override-style instruction aimed at\nthe reader; in-game that can be a trick the file plays on whoever reads it.\n\nOpen: is the Field a usable mechanic or a document the player misreads? Which faction wrote it? Does\nthe shutdown phrase do anything, or is it bait?\n\n---\n\n## Endgame tier: psychic and magic tech\n\nBorrows the feel of Yuri's Revenge and Harry Potter. Speculative; every item carries a named Red cost,\nand any item that documents a Migrant in the 72-minute window can pin them.\n\n| Item | What it does | Red cost |\n|---|---|---|\n| Psychic Beacon | Reveals NPC intentions in a radius — reading the color they are really in | Everyone in range feels it; the owner becomes visible |\n| Mind Control Tower | Takes over one NPC briefly | The NPC remembers, and remembers who did it |\n| Psychic Dominator | Wide-area compulsion across a district | Single use per era; every faction sees the flash |\n| Mental Omega Static | Jams telepathic and recording tech | Also jams the player's own scanner |\n| Chronosphere | Moves a unit across the map, or a short span of time | Leaves a 72-minute residue where the unit exists twice |\n| Chrono Vortex | Temporary rip pulling units into another era | Cannot be closed from the inside |\n| Living Map | Every person in a location as a moving name; ties to the map of the chairs | Must be spoken to close; anyone who learns the phrase can read it |\n| Invisibility Cloak | Fully hides the wearer in the unseen state | Does not hide the player's recordings or footprints |\n| Time Turner | Short controlled hop backward | Twice in one day pins the user |\n| Pensieve | Stores and replays a memory as a walkable place | Memories are shared with anyone who enters |\n| Enchanted Quill | Writes sealed or released entries on its own | Cannot be told to stop mid-line |\n| Deluminator | Takes and returns light (e.g. the porch light) | Holds one light at a time |\n| Wand or Focus | Narrows a frequency to a single channel | Bonds to one owner |\n| Portkey | One-way transport to a fixed place and time | Activates at a set hour; cannot be moved or recalled |\n\nTies back: the map of the chairs becomes a living map and the chairs become portkeys; the 72-minute\nwindow applies to every jump item; the five colors still gate unlocks in order; the grimoire tier is\nthe root and the psychic tier is its late-game echo.\n\nOpen: does the endgame read the whole cipher or only the next layer? Do rivals get psychic tech? Is the\nDuck holding the wall shut a learnable psychic ability?\n\n---\n\n## Puppeteer and Hunter layer\n\nTwo companion archetypes: the Puppeteer (controls objects and bodies at a distance) and the Hunter\n(bonds with animals). Both fit loans: a companion is lent, carries a named cost, and gives a reason to\nreturn. Inspired by WoW pet classes and by the Duck and horse in TYLER.\n\n### Hunter: bonded animals\n\n| Companion | What it does | Red cost |\n|---|---|---|\n| Carrier Pigeon | Delivers and intercepts coded notes | Must be fed and returned to its roost or the message is lost |\n| Horse | Carries the hum, steadies a location, can hold a frequency alone | Stays behind when the player leaves; someone must keep it warm |\n| Tracking Dog | Follows a scent to a vault or dead drop | Can be misled by planted scent, barks at the worst moment |\n| Raven or Crow | Scouts rooftops, watches stakeouts | Remembers faces and may report the player |\n| Duck in a Tuxedo | Holds a wall or edge shut by looking at it | It tires; the hood falls over its eyes |\n| Bat or Owl | Night scout: heat and movement | Useless in daylight |\n| Zombie Pet (sandbox) | Tamed zombie that follows and carries | Draws other zombies; loses control if documented |\n\nBond rules: a companion is a loan, not an owned item; it has a color it shows and a color it really is.\n\n### Puppeteer: controlled objects and bodies\n\n| Item | What it does | Red cost |\n|---|---|---|\n| Marionette Strings | Moves a puppet at a distance (decoy in a window) | Strings visible under the right light; a rival can cut them |\n| Wooden Decoy | Stands in for the player in a stakeout | Cannot speak, so it fails if someone talks to it |\n| Ventriloquist Doll | Throws the player's voice | The voice carries an auditable trace |\n| Mechanical Automaton | Clockwork figure walking a set route | Runs down; leaves a visible winding key |\n| Puppet Master's Hand | Controls an NPC body briefly | The NPC remembers; the player's own body goes still |\n| Shadow Puppet Screen | Coded messages as shadows on a wall | Readable only from one angle — a watcher can read it too |\n\nPuppet rule: every puppet has a string, and every string leads back to the player.\n\nTies: loans (the horse and Duck already are), five colors (a calm dog may really be Yellow), stakeouts\n(raven watches lookouts), time jumps (animals don't follow unless anchored to a chair — why the horse\nstays and hums), documentation (pinning the animal can pin its owner), grimoire (familiars are the old\nform), endgame (a living map shows animals; a portkey hides in a collar).\n\nOpen: can a companion hold a chair as an anchor? Does a pet ever refuse to be returned?\n\n---\n\n## Blue Mage layer: learning by being seen\n\nThe class whose power comes from watching — observation, cribs and stakeouts are already the game's\ncore. A Blue Mage does not buy or craft tools; it learns them by being a witness, and the cost is\nexposure.\n\n- Learning is tied to the tagline: a skill the player never observed cannot be learned.\n- Every learned skill is a crib: a piece of the enemy's behaviour matchable later.\n- Learned skills are loaned from the source; the owner can take them back or spoil them.\n\n| Method | What the player does | What is learned | Red cost |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Survive the Hit | Take the skill and live | The skill, weakened | Real damage |\n| Stakeout Watch | Observe the same NPC over days | The pattern (puff interval, gesture) | Time, and the chance of being seen watching |\n| Signal Capture | Record a coded channel as it is sent | The channel, not the message | Lookouts may spot the scanner |\n| Vault Fragment | Steal a plaintext/ciphertext pair | A crib toward a cipher | The break-in |\n| Mirror Cast | Copy a skill as it is used on you, via a mirror or lens | A clean copy | Needs the right tool; the owner sees the reflection |\n\n### The spellbook\n\n| Skill | Source | Effect | Red cost |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Vape Morse | A spy using puffs and pauses as dots and dashes | Reads and sends puff signals | Needs a visible light source |\n| Cup Tap | An agent tapping a cup | Sends a rhythm message | Cannot be used where tapping is noticed |\n| Stare Hold | The Duck holding a wall edge | Holds a door, edge or peel shut briefly | Tiring; the hood falls |\n| False Color | A faction member showing one color while in another | Shows a false color in conversation | Fails under close inspection |\n| Hum Jam | Tyler's anti-recording hum at 7.83 Hz | Scrambles observers' tracking | Draws attention to the hum |\n| Peel Read | The corridor edge lifting from the wall | Sees the pale light under a door about to open | Brief, cannot be held |\n| Coin Flip | The coin never caught on camera | Marks the moment of a jump unrecorded | Needs a coin the player owns |\n| Ledger Eye | A rival auditing a network | Spots hidden centralization of nodes | Requires time on the network |\n\nTies: the five colors order the learning; loans apply (a skill is lent, the owner can call it back);\nstakeouts are the natural training ground; over-documentation can pin the studied Migrant; other\nplayers can learn the player's skills, so watching the Blue Mage is the counter; the seventy-two are\nskills to learn slowly, so the spellbook fills over time; a Hunter pet can learn by watching, a\nPuppeteer can teach a puppet one.\n\nOpen: can a skill be taught to another player? Does the original owner lose it or only know it was\ncopied? Does a Blue Mage have a color, or show whichever color it last learned?\n\n---\n\n## Eight-year ladder: 1901 to present\n\nThe paste ended here. What arrived is the framing only:\n\n- One slice every eight years, listing what new tech appeared in that window across signals\n  intelligence, communications, automotive, surveillance and tradecraft.\n- Dates are from memory and approximate.\n- Every item gets a Red cost, and anything that records can pin a Migrant during the 72-minute window.\n\n**The slice table itself did not arrive.** This section is a named gap, not an omission: the ladder\nshould be written against SHANKPIT's existing era/level data before any of it becomes items.\n"
}

## What I did

**`BIG_O/docs/ITEMS_AND_TECH_TIERS.md`** (`ff6f9bd`, 603 lines) — the whole paste as IP canon: the five tradecraft tiers, the 1916 base stack through Prohibition, the loan register with its five colours and eight loans, the Art of War harmonic, the 1993 GoldenEye tier (real + fantasy), the grimoire/Seventy-Two layer, the Psychic City endgame, the Hunter/Puppeteer layer and the Blue Mage. Prose tightened; **every item entry and table preserved**.

**`SHANKPIT/docs/ITEMS_VS_ENGINE.md`** (`6998531`) — the honest bridge, because the document's own rule ("an item is a new way of perceiving something already in the world") means an item is only real if there's a channel underneath it.

| Canon | Engine today |
|---|---|
| Items gate what you can read, on keys | **Yes** — `kit.h`, 14 slots, 3 prefabs, 3 phone apps |
| Unlock ladder | **Partly** — tech tree is real and spendable, but has one node |
| Pheromone canister | **Yes** — canister, lure feeding, grace window |
| Stakeouts / watching | **Half** — citizens and The Men exist with witness states; there's no player-facing observation verb, and no lookout ever notices *you* watching |
| Signal channels (Morse, lamps, taps, puffs) | **Nothing.** This is the document's actual core and its biggest hole |
| Five colours, loans, sealed/released log, eras, time jumps | **Nothing** |

## Three slices actually buildable now

1. **The five colours as a projection of existing NPC state** — mood, vigilance and witness state are already there; a colour plus a shown-vs-real mismatch is a small rule, and it's exactly the document's thesis.
2. **Sealed vs released entries** — a flag and a read gate on an existing log; cheapest piece with real consequence.
3. **One real channel: lamp Morse** — proves the shape (visible tell, readable only with the right item, capture is vulnerable) before the other three carriers become content.

And a named *not yet*: eras and time jumps. The document's own open question (does the clock follow progress or the player?) has no answer, and building a jump before it exists would bake in the wrong one.

## Two honest notes

- **The paste ended mid-way through the Eight-Year Ladder** — the framing arrived, the slice table did not. That section records what came and names the table as missing rather than inventing the years.
- **BIG_O had no git identity configured**, so its first commit was rejected. I set it repo-locally to the author already on the project's own commits (`Emily Springerton <emilyspringerton@gmail.com>`) rather than inventing one or touching global config.

No code was written for this and no tests were run — it's a documentation change. The invariant I wrote into the mapping doc is the one to hold everyone to: the zombie sandbox stays fully playable for a player who never opens the phone, never throws a canister and never reads a colour.

  content: |
      /* kit.h -- the player's KIT: which gadget sits on which key, which prefab kit is live, and the
       * three HTML/CSS pages the phone renders for it.
       *
       * Founder 2026-10-31: "we need to add kit affordances for these items have it be so that you can
       * ` and - and = so 3 additional gadgets in additon to 1-9 or -0 that we already have if we dont
       * have 0 yet allow us 4 additional gadgets and we can also set f and c i suppose so thats a total
       * of 5 or 6 gadgets so that maps to what the affordances in the fphone can help us support for now
       * give us 2 apps one to map the current kit to keys and another app to select the kit from the kits
       * menenu (we can select a kit that is already pre built) and then another app for building kits
       * keep it simple while including all the affordances use basic html and CSS and PELLEGRINO (clone
       * it down) tech for rendering the ui - oh wait f is already taken for vehicle entry thats fine we
       * can dont need f same spec"
       *
       * So: the ten number keys PLUS four gadget keys -- ` (backtick), - (minus), = (equals) and C.
       * F is deliberately NOT one of them (it already enters vehicles). That is 14 bind slots.
       *
       * Items are not a new inventory: each one is an input this engine ALREADY acts on, so a kit is a
       * key -> real-action map rather than a parallel universe of fake gadgets. That is the same
       * "compose what exists" discipline the BIG_O merge work used instead of standing up another
       * standalone system.
       *
       * Pure C99, no GL/SDL/network: the pages are strings (rendered by PELLEGRINO's own layout/paint
       * engine through packages/pellegrino_embed), the model is plain data, and every decision here is
       * unit-tested (packages/common/kit_test.c). */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_KIT_H
      #define SHANKPIT_KIT_H
      
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      #define KIT_SLOTS 14        /* 1..9, 0, `, -, =, C */
      #define KIT_MAX_KITS 6
      #define KIT_NAME_LEN 24
      
      typedef enum {
          KIT_ITEM_NONE = 0,
          KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE,   /* in_pheromone / BTN_PHEROMONE -- the canister throw */
          KIT_ITEM_ABILITY,     /* input_ability   -- the weapon's own ability */
          KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY,   /* input_secondary -- the weapon's secondary */
          KIT_ITEM_RELOAD,      /* input_reload */
          KIT_ITEM_COUNT
      } KitItem;
      
      static const char *const KIT_ITEM_NAMES[KIT_ITEM_COUNT] = {
          "-- EMPTY --", "PHEROMONE", "ABILITY", "SECONDARY", "RELOAD"
      };
      
      /* The four gadget keys come AFTER the ten digits, in the founder's own order. */
      static const char *const KIT_SLOT_KEY_NAMES[KIT_SLOTS] = {
          "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9", "0", "`", "-", "=", "C"
      };
      #define KIT_SLOT_FIRST_GADGET 10   /* index of ` */
      
      /* Fixed indexes so callers never hard-code 10/11/12/13. */
      #define KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK 10
      #define KIT_SLOT_MINUS 11
      #define KIT_SLOT_EQUALS 12
      #define KIT_SLOT_C 13
      
      typedef struct {
          char name[KIT_NAME_LEN];
          unsigned char slot[KIT_SLOTS];
      } Kit;
      
      typedef struct {
          Kit kits[KIT_MAX_KITS];
          int kit_count;
          int selected;   /* the LIVE kit -- what the gameplay keys read */
          Kit draft;      /* the KITBUILD app's working copy, so building never trashes the live kit */
      } KitState;
      
      static inline const char *kit_item_name(int item) {
          return (item > 0 && item < KIT_ITEM_COUNT) ? KIT_ITEM_NAMES[item] : KIT_ITEM_NAMES[0];
      }
      
      static inline const char *kit_slot_key_name(int slot) {
          return (slot >= 0 && slot < KIT_SLOTS) ? KIT_SLOT_KEY_NAMES[slot] : "?";
      }
      
      /* kit_slot_from_key -- ASCII key ('1'..'9', '0', '`', '-', '=', 'c'/'C') -> slot, or -1. The host
       * maps its own keycodes to a character and asks this, so this header never needs SDL. */
      static inline int kit_slot_from_key(int key) {
          if (key >= '1' && key <= '9') return key - '1';
          if (key == '0') return 9;
          if (key == '`') return KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK;
          if (key == '-') return KIT_SLOT_MINUS;
          if (key == '=') return KIT_SLOT_EQUALS;
          if (key == 'c' || key == 'C') return KIT_SLOT_C;
          return -1;
      }
      
      /* kit_set_slot -- the only writer. Out-of-range slots and items are ignored rather than clamped
       * into some other key the player never asked for. */
      static inline void kit_set_slot(Kit *k, int slot, int item) {
          if (!k || slot < 0 || slot >= KIT_SLOTS) return;
          if (item < 0 || item >= KIT_ITEM_COUNT) return;
          k->slot[slot] = (unsigned char)item;
      }
      
      /* kit_cycle -- step one slot's item forward/back through the real item list, wrapping. This is
       * what the phone's LEFT/RIGHT do; the empty slot is part of the cycle so a key can always be
       * cleared without a separate "clear" gesture. */
      static inline void kit_cycle(Kit *k, int slot, int dir) {
          if (!k || slot < 0 || slot >= KIT_SLOTS) return;
          int item = (int)k->slot[slot] + (dir >= 0 ? 1 : -1);
          if (item >= KIT_ITEM_COUNT) item = 0;
          if (item < 0) item = KIT_ITEM_COUNT - 1;
          k->slot[slot] = (unsigned char)item;
      }
      
      static inline void kit_clear_slot(Kit *k, int slot) { kit_set_slot(k, slot, KIT_ITEM_NONE); }
      
      static inline void kit_named(Kit *k, const char *name) {
          if (!k) return;
          memset(k, 0, sizeof(*k));
          snprintf(k->name, sizeof(k->name), "%s", name ? name : "KIT");
      }
      
      /* Three prefabs, deliberately different in shape rather than three flavours of the same thing: one
       * fights at range, one breaks things and runs, one is built around the canister. Digit slots 1-3
       * are left empty on purpose -- those are the weapons a player already carries, and a kit that
       * silently rebound them would be hostile. */
      static inline void kit_defaults(KitState *s) {
          if (!s) return;
          memset(s, 0, sizeof(*s));
          kit_named(&s->kits[0], "SCOUT");
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK, KIT_ITEM_RELOAD);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, KIT_ITEM_ABILITY);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[0], KIT_SLOT_C, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);
      
          kit_named(&s->kits[1], "BREACHER");
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, KIT_ITEM_RELOAD);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[1], KIT_SLOT_C, KIT_ITEM_ABILITY);
      
          kit_named(&s->kits[2], "HUNTER");
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK, KIT_ITEM_ABILITY);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);
          kit_set_slot(&s->kits[2], KIT_SLOT_C, KIT_ITEM_SECONDARY);
          s->kit_count = 3;
          s->selected = 0;
          s->draft = s->kits[0];
      }
      
      static inline void kit_select(KitState *s, int index) {
          if (!s || index < 0 || index >= s->kit_count) return;
          s->selected = index;
          s->draft = s->kits[index];   /* building always starts from what is live */
      }
      
      /* The live kit is the only thing gameplay reads. Returns KIT_ITEM_NONE for anything out of range. */
      static inline int kit_live_item(const KitState *s, int slot) {
          if (!s || s->selected < 0 || s->selected >= s->kit_count) return KIT_ITEM_NONE;
          if (slot < 0 || slot >= KIT_SLOTS) return KIT_ITEM_NONE;
          return (int)s->kits[s->selected].slot[slot];
      }
      
      static inline void kit_cycle_draft(KitState *s, int slot, int dir) {
          if (!s) return;
          kit_cycle(&s->draft, slot, dir);
      }
      
      /* kit_save_draft -- KITBUILD's SELECT: the draft becomes the live kit. Copy, not swap, so the
       * draft keeps working as the thing you are still editing afterwards. */
      static inline void kit_save_draft(KitState *s) {
          if (!s || s->selected < 0 || s->selected >= s->kit_count) return;
          s->kits[s->selected] = s->draft;
      }
      
      /* --- the three pages, as basic HTML + CSS ------------------------------------------------------
       * Deliberately one layout with different copy: PELLEGRINO's CSS surface is unverified beyond the
       * OS menu's own tiles, so nothing here depends on flexbox/grid/animations -- a table, a background,
       * a highlighted row, and a hint line. All return the length written, or -1 if it would not fit
       * (the caller keeps its previous page rather than rendering a truncated one). */
      
      static inline int kit_page_add(char *out, int cap, int len, const char *s) {
          int n;
          if (len < 0 || !s) return -1;
          n = (int)strlen(s);
          if (len + n >= cap) return -1;
          memcpy(out + len, s, (size_t)n + 1);
          return len + n;
      }
      
      static inline int kit_page_head(char *out, int cap, const char *title, const char *sub) {
          int n = snprintf(out, (size_t)cap,
              "<html><head><style>"
              "body{background:#0b0f14;color:#cfe3f0;font-family:sans-serif;margin:0;padding:10px}"
              "h1{font-size:17px;color:#8fd0ff;margin:0 0 3px 0}"
              "p.s{color:#6f8ba0;font-size:12px;margin:0 0 8px 0}"
              "table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%%}"
              "td{padding:2px 7px;font-size:13px}"
              "tr.on{background:#16394f}"
              "td.k{color:#ffd479;width:44px}"
              "td.i{color:#bfe9c8}"
              "td.x{color:#6f8ba0;font-size:11px}"
              "div.h{margin-top:9px;color:#5f7688;font-size:11px}"
              "</style></head><body><h1>%s</h1><p class=\"s\">%s</p><table>", title, sub);
          return (n < 0 || n >= cap) ? -1 : n;
      }
      
      static inline int kit_page_row(char *out, int cap, int len, const char *key, const char *item, int on) {
          char buf[160];
          snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "<tr%s><td class=\"k\">%s</td><td class=\"i\">%s</td></tr>",
                   on ? " class=\"on\"" : "", key, item);
          return kit_page_add(out, cap, len, buf);
      }
      
      /* KITS -- pick which prefab kit is live. */
      static inline int kit_page_select(char *out, int cap, const KitState *s) {
          int n, i;
          if (!out || !s) return -1;
          n = kit_page_head(out, cap, "KITS", "SELECT A PREBUILT KIT -- ENTER MAKES IT LIVE");
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          for (i = 0; i < s->kit_count; i++) {
              n = kit_page_row(out, cap, n, i == s->selected ? "*" : "", s->kits[i].name, i == s->selected);
              if (n < 0) return -1;
          }
          n = kit_page_add(out, cap, n, "</table><div class=\"h\">");
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          return kit_page_add(out, cap, n, "ARROWS MOVE   ENTER SELECT   HOME/SELECT = LIVE KIT</div></body></html>");
      }
      
      /* KITMAP -- what the live kit has on each of the 14 keys. */
      static inline int kit_page_map(char *out, int cap, const KitState *s, int cursor) {
          int n, i;
          if (!out || !s) return -1;
          n = kit_page_head(out, cap, "KIT MAP", "WHAT EACH KEY DOES ON THE LIVE KIT");
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          for (i = 0; i < KIT_SLOTS; i++) {
              int item = kit_live_item(s, i);
              n = kit_page_row(out, cap, n, kit_slot_key_name(i), kit_item_name(item), i == cursor);
              if (n < 0) return -1;
          }
          n = kit_page_add(out, cap, n, "</table><div class=\"h\">");
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          return kit_page_add(out, cap, n,
              "UP/DOWN PICK KEY   LEFT/RIGHT CHANGE ITEM   ENTER CLEAR   (F IS TAKEN: VEHICLE ENTRY)</div></body></html>");
      }
      
      /* KITBUILD -- edit the draft, then save it over the live kit. Shows both so you can see the diff. */
      static inline int kit_page_build(char *out, int cap, const KitState *s, int cursor) {
          int n, i;
          if (!out || !s) return -1;
          n = kit_page_head(out, cap, "KIT BUILDER", "EDIT THE DRAFT, THEN ENTER SAVES IT OVER THE LIVE KIT");
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          for (i = 0; i < KIT_SLOTS; i++) {
              char item[48];
              snprintf(item, sizeof(item), "%s%s", kit_item_name((int)s->draft.slot[i]),
                       (int)s->draft.slot[i] == kit_live_item(s, i) ? "" : " *");
              n = kit_page_row(out, cap, n, kit_slot_key_name(i), item, i == cursor);
              if (n < 0) return -1;
          }
          n = kit_page_add(out, cap, n, "</table><div class=\"h\">");
          if (n < 0) return -1;
          return kit_page_add(out, cap, n,
              "UP/DOWN PICK KEY   LEFT/RIGHT CHANGE ITEM   ENTER SAVE DRAFT   (* = DIFFERS FROM LIVE)</div></body></html>");
      }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_KIT_H */

      static inline void heli_spawn_defaults(HelicopterState *h, int id, int scene_id, float x, float y, float z) {
          memset(h, 0, sizeof(*h));
          h->active = 1;
          h->id = id;
          h->scene_id = scene_id;
          h->x = x; h->y = y; h->z = z;
          h->health = 250;
          h->occupant_player_id = -1;
          h->rotor_speed = 8.0f;
          h->yaw = 180.0f;
          h->collective = 500.0f;   /* hover setting (heli_rules.prn) */
      }
      
      static inline void buggy_spawn_defaults(BuggyState *b, int id, int scene_id, float x, float z, float yaw) {
          memset(b, 0, sizeof(*b));
          b->active = 1;
          b->id = id;
          b->scene_id = scene_id;
          b->x = x; b->z = z;
          b->yaw = yaw;
          b->occupant_player_id = -1;
          float gy = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, x, z);
          if (gy < 0.0f) gy = 0.0f;
          b->y = gy + BUGGY_WHEEL_RADIUS + BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE;
          b->grounded = 1;
          b->health = 300;
      }
      
      static inline BuggyState *buggy_find_nearby(int scene_id, float x, float y, float z, float radius) {
          float rr = radius * radius;
          for (int i = 0; i < MAX_BUGGIES; i++) {
              BuggyState *b = &local_state.buggies[i];
              if (!b->active || b->scene_id != scene_id) continue;
              float dx = b->x - x, dy = b->y - y, dz = b->z - z;
              if ((dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz) <= rr) return b;
          }
          return NULL;
      }
      
      static inline int buggy_try_enter(PlayerState *p, BuggyState *b) {
          if (!p || !b || !b->active || b->occupant_player_id >= 0) return 0;
          b->occupant_player_id = p->id;
          p->in_vehicle = 1;
          p->vehicle_type = VEH_BUGGY;
          p->x = b->x; p->y = b->y; p->z = b->z;
          p->vx = p->vy = p->vz = 0.0f;
          p->on_ground = b->grounded;
          printf("[BUGGY] enter player=%d buggy=%d\n", p->id, b->id);
          return 1;
      }
      
      static inline int buggy_try_exit(PlayerState *p, BuggyState *b) {
          if (!p || !b || b->occupant_player_id != p->id) return 0;
          float r = -b->yaw * 0.0174532925f;
          float right_x = cosf(r), right_z = sinf(r);
          float offsets[3][2] = { { right_x * 3.2f, right_z * 3.2f }, { -right_x * 3.2f, -right_z * 3.2f }, { 0.0f, -3.2f } };
          for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
              float px = b->x + offsets[i][0];
              float pz = b->z + offsets[i][1];
              float py = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, px, pz);
              if (py < 0.0f) py = 0.0f;
              if (!heli_point_collides(px, py + 1.0f, pz)) {
                  p->x = px; p->z = pz; p->y = py;
                  break;
              }
          }
          p->in_vehicle = 0;
          p->vehicle_type = VEH_NONE;
          p->on_ground = 1;
          b->occupant_player_id = -1;
          printf("[BUGGY] exit player=%d buggy=%d persisted=1 speed=%.2f\n", p->id, b->id, sqrtf(b->vx*b->vx + b->vz*b->vz));
          return 1;
      }
      
      static inline void buggy_tick_all(void) {
          for (int i = 0; i < MAX_BUGGIES; i++) {
              BuggyState *b = &local_state.buggies[i];
              if (!b->active) continue;
              float throttle = 0.0f;
              float steer_intent = 0.0f;
              if (b->occupant_player_id >= 0 && b->occupant_player_id < MAX_CLIENTS) {
                  PlayerState *occ = &local_state.players[b->occupant_player_id];
                  b->scene_id = occ->scene_id;
                  /* While driving a buggy:
                     - occ->yaw is the driver's desired look/steer yaw (camera yaw target)
                     - b->yaw is the buggy body yaw */
                  throttle = occ->in_fwd;
                  steer_intent = buggy_chase_steer_intent(b, throttle, occ->yaw);
              } else {
                  b->occupant_player_id = -1;
              }
              phys_set_scene(b->scene_id);
              simulate_buggy_state(b, throttle, steer_intent, SHANKPIT_NET_FIXED_DT, b->occupant_player_id >= 0);
              if (b->occupant_player_id >= 0 && b->occupant_player_id < MAX_CLIENTS) {
                  PlayerState *occ = &local_state.players[b->occupant_player_id];
                  occ->x = b->x; occ->y = b->y; occ->z = b->z;
                  occ->vx = occ->vy = occ->vz = 0.0f;
                  occ->on_ground = b->grounded;
              }
          }
      }

      static inline HelicopterState *heli_find_nearby(int scene_id, float x, float y, float z, float radius) {

      static inline int heli_try_place_player(PlayerState *p, HelicopterState *h, float ox, float oz) {
          float px = h->x + ox;
          float pz = h->z + oz;
          if (!heli_point_collides(px, h->y + 1.0f, pz) && !heli_point_collides(px, h->y + 2.0f, pz)) {

      static inline void scene_request_transition(int scene_id) {
          if (local_state.transition_timer > 0) return;
          local_state.pending_scene = scene_id;
          local_state.transition_timer = 12;
      }
      
      static inline void scene_tick_transition() {
          if (local_state.transition_timer <= 0) return;
          local_state.transition_timer--;
          if (local_state.transition_timer == 0 && local_state.pending_scene >= 0) {
              scene_load(local_state.pending_scene);
              local_state.pending_scene = -1;
          }
      }
      
      static void ctf_training_on_episode_begin(void) {}
      static void ctf_training_on_step(unsigned int now_ms) { (void)now_ms; }
      static void ctf_training_on_episode_end(int winning_team) { (void)winning_team; }
      
      static void ctf_add_reward(int player_id, float amount, const char *reason, CtfBotRewardBreakdown *b) {
          if (player_id < 0 || player_id >= MAX_CLIENTS) return;
          PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[player_id];
          if (!p->active || !p->is_bot) return;
          p->ctf_cumulative_reward += amount;
          p->ctf_last_reward = amount;
          p->accumulated_reward += amount;
          if (b) b->total += amount;
          if (local_state.game_mode == MODE_HEADED_BOT)
              headed_policy_reinforce(player_id, amount);
          if (reason && (amount != 0.0f)) {
              printf("[CTFB_REWARD] bot=%d reason=%s amount=%.2f total=%.2f\n", player_id, reason, amount, p->ctf_cumulative_reward);
          }
      }
      
      static void ctf_reset_flag(int team_id) {
          CtfFlagState *f = &local_state.ctf.flags[team_id];
          f->state = FLAG_AT_HOME;
          f->carrier_id = -1;
          f->x = f->home_x; f->y = f->home_y; f->z = f->home_z;
          f->dropped_until_ms = 0;
      }
      
      static void ctf_init_match_state(int scene_id) {
          memset(&local_state.ctf, 0, sizeof(local_state.ctf));
          local_state.ctf.active = 1;
          local_state.ctf.scene_id = scene_id;
          local_state.ctf.score_limit = CTFB_SCORE_LIMIT;
          for (int team = 0; team < 2; team++) {
              CtfFlagState *f = &local_state.ctf.flags[team];
              f->owning_team_id = team;
              f->scene_id = scene_id;
              if (!get_ctf_flag_home(scene_id, team, &f->home_x, &f->home_y, &f->home_z)) {
                  float sx, sy, sz, ex, ey, ez;
                  if (scene_get_team_base_marker(scene_id, team, &sx, &sy, &sz, &ex, &ey, &ez)) {
                      f->home_x = sx; f->home_y = sy; f->home_z = sz;
                  }
              }
              ctf_reset_flag(team);
          }
      }
      
      static void ctf_drop_flag_from_carrier(int player_id, unsigned int now_ms) {
          if (player_id < 0 || player_id >= MAX_CLIENTS) return;
          PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[player_id];
          if (p->carried_flag_team_id < 0 || p->carried_flag_team_id > 1) return;
          CtfFlagState *flag = &local_state.ctf.flags[p->carried_flag_team_id];
          flag->state = FLAG_DROPPED;
          flag->carrier_id = -1;
          flag->x = p->x; flag->y = p->y + 2.0f; flag->z = p->z;
          flag->dropped_until_ms = now_ms + CTFB_DROPPED_RETURN_MS;
          flag->last_interaction_ms = now_ms;
          p->carried_flag_team_id = -1;
      }
      
      
      static void build_ctf_bot_observation(int bot_id, CtfBotObservation *out) {
          memset(out, 0, sizeof(*out));
          PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[bot_id];
          int my_team = p->team_id;
          int enemy = ctf_enemy_team(my_team);
          CtfFlagState *my_flag = &local_state.ctf.flags[my_team];
          CtfFlagState *enemy_flag = &local_state.ctf.flags[enemy];
          out->bot_id = bot_id; out->my_team_id = my_team; out->enemy_team_id = enemy;
          out->has_enemy_flag = (p->carried_flag_team_id == enemy);
          out->my_flag_state = my_flag->state; out->enemy_flag_state = enemy_flag->state;

      static RetroSky g_retro_sky = {0};
      // g_sky_weather/local_state.story_clock -- BIG_O engine merge, phase 1 (founder real-time: "port
      // the BIG_O tech into the shankpit repo -- all of it the lighting the systems all of it... the
      // shaders the way the sun and moon look"). Real day/night + weather clock (PARENA-driven,
      // world_rules.c) and the weather-aware sky it drives, upgrading retro_sky's old fixed fast-orbit
      // dome with real clear/overcast/rain/storm states, clouds, rain, and lightning. Server-
      // authoritative for MODE_STORY/MODE_STORY_CAVE as of the SECTION 536 follow-up named below
      // (local_init_match seeds it fresh per match, same as every other ServerState field it resets --
      // a real, deliberate change from this clock's own earlier "one persistent, whole-session
      // instance" exception); every other mode (deathmatch etc., which draws this same sky purely as a
      // visual) keeps ticking it off local wall-clock time exactly as before, see the render block's own
      // doc comment near DAY_NIGHT_MINUTES_PER_REAL_SEC's real use for the honest "why not every mode"
      // account. retro_sky/g_retro_sky stay in place unchanged: retro_lighting.c's
      // RETRO_LIGHTING_DYNAMIC preset still reads retro_sky_eval_fog_rgb/eval_sun_dir for scene ambient
      // lighting -- wiring that to sky_weather's own real weather state is also SECTION 536 follow-up,
      // not this pass, so it's named rather than half-done.
      static SkyWeather g_sky_weather = {0};
      // EMILY/BACKLOG.md SECTION 536 follow-up ("server-authoritative day/night sync"): the clock
      // itself now lives in local_state.story_clock (ServerState, packages/common/protocol.h) instead
      // of a separate client-local static -- see local_init_match (init), local_update (real-tick
      // advance for local matches), and the PACKET_WORLD_CLOCK receive case below (real-tick advance
      // for a genuine networked story client) for where it's actually written.
      // DAY_NIGHT_MINUTES_PER_REAL_SEC now lives in day_night_clock.h -- shared with apps/server.
      
      // g_story_phone/g_story_alert_bridge -- BIG_O engine merge phase 7e (EMILY/BACKLOG.md SECTION
      // 536, "the day/night/lab turn structure"). The first real, live consumer of phone.h (phase 6)
      // and world_alert_bridge (phase 6) -- both shipped fully tested but never actually instantiated
      // anywhere before this. Reuses local_state.story_clock above rather than standing up a second
      // clock. Unlike story_clock itself, g_story_phone/g_story_alert_bridge stay real, persistent,
      // session-wide client statics, NOT reset per MODE_STORY entry (unchanged from this comment's own
      // original claim) -- a message from a previous story session staying in the inbox across a
      // restart is a real, honest, harmless v0 property, not a bug.
      //
      // Real, deliberate scope cut: only the on-screen banner below is new. The actual phone APP UI
      // (home grid, Messages list, Contacts/Map/Camera/etc.) still has no render/input path at all --
      // that's real, separate, still-not-attempted work (phase 6's own named gap). This gives MODE_STORY
      // its first real, player-VISIBLE day/night turn boundary (a DAYBREAK/NIGHTFALL/STORM WARNING
      // banner) without building the full phone UI to get there.
      static Phone g_story_phone = {0};
      /* Kit gadget-key pulses (packages/common/kit.h). A press arms ONE item for ~150 ms and the input
       * assembly consumes it, so tapping a kit key is exactly one action -- and a bound key can never get
       * stuck down if the window loses focus in the middle of a press. */
      static int g_kit_pulse_item = 0;
      static unsigned int g_kit_pulse_until_ms = 0;
      
      static int kit_pulse_take(int item, unsigned int now) {
          if (item == KIT_ITEM_NONE || g_kit_pulse_item != item) return 0;
          if ((int)(g_kit_pulse_until_ms - now) <= 0) { g_kit_pulse_item = 0; return 0; }
          g_kit_pulse_item = 0;
          return 1;
      }
      /* BIG_O unification state (see bigo_wiring_tick below) */
      static int   g_board = BOARD_NONE;
      static float g_board_vx = 0.0f, g_board_vz = 0.0f;
      static Mission g_mission;
      static int   g_mission_live = 0;
      static int   g_mission_seen_state = M_INACTIVE;
      static unsigned int g_mission_last_ms = 0;
      static ShankParty g_party;
      static unsigned int g_party_refresh_ms = 0;
      static int   g_xp = 0;
      /* SECTION 592 (card #508): the LAB level -- INTERRIOR_1 cloned + lab widgets (IDUNA cmd/shankpit-lab-builder). While
         g_lab_active the BIG_O phone works like in ZOMBIES, and lab_<kind> tiles are interactive stations (E). */
      static int g_lab_active = 0;
      static int g_floor_tinted = 0;            /* #533: NOCK per-level floor tint (colour + alpha), set by level load */
      static float g_floor_rgba[4] = {0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f, 1.0f};
      static LevelLabStation g_lab_st[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_LAB_STATIONS];
      static int g_lab_st_n = 0;
      static char g_lab_msg[64];
      static unsigned int g_lab_msg_until = 0;
      #define PHONE_SANDBOX() (local_state.game_mode == MODE_ZOMBIES || g_lab_active)
      static WorldAlertBridge g_story_alert_bridge = {0};
      
      // Display text for the small, real, currently-dispatchable set of message ids
      // world_alerts_mod.prn's own alert_message_id can produce (2/3/4 -- 5 is reserved for a zombie-
      // population event this repo doesn't have yet, see reflux_runtime.h's own REFLUX_ACTION_ZOMBIE_*
      // comments). Not phone.h's concern (that header is pure state, no display text) -- this lookup is
      // this client's own real, minimal answer to "what does message id 3 actually say," same role a
      // future real phone-UI content table would play, just narrowed to what a banner needs.
      static const char *story_phone_message_text(int msg_id) {
          switch (msg_id) {

- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_phys.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_phys.prn -- the rocket car, the ball, and the world they share. 60 Hz (16 ms ticks), two substeps each.
      ;;
      ;; THE CAR is modelled on the Tesla Roadster rocket demo (the founder's reference): a low car with FOUR LIFT NOZZLES under it
      ;; and cold-gas jets on its flanks, plus FANS under the floor that suck it onto the road so it can drive inverted. Everything it
      ;; spends comes from one tank of compressed AIR (like mana: it refills far faster than boost does in Rocket League).
      ;;
      ;;   on a surface  (fans on and a surface within reach)   the car's up axis swings onto the surface normal, gravity is beaten by
      ;;                 the fans, so floor, wall and ceiling are all "road". W/S throttle, A/D steer. The tyres hold the car up to a
      ;;                 limit (dirt holds far less than concrete): past it the tail steps out and the car drifts. The fans only
      ;;                 catch a car belly-down, so a car that lands on its roof scrapes along until it rolls (or tips) back over
      ;;   in the air    the car is a thruster platform with PRECISE, rate-commanded control on every axis:
      ;;                    pitch / yaw / roll   angular rates follow the command and STOP when you let go (cold-gas attitude jets)
      ;;                    lift                 the four nozzles, along the car's up axis
      ;;                    boost                the rear nozzle, along the car's forward axis
      ;;                    strafe, fore / aft   the flank jets, along its right / forward axes
      ;;   the tank      lift 26 /s, boost 22 /s, jets 9 /s, attitude 4 /s of 100; it refills 34 /s once you stop spending (48 /s on a
      ;;                 surface), plus a team-synergy bonus (br_rules.prn). Empty, the car still turns at a quarter rate -- never helpless.
      ;;
      ;; The command a car obeys is nine numbers (thr, steer, pitch, roll, strafe, lift, boost, fans-off, magnet): a person's keys, a
      ;; bot's brain, or the replay log write the same fields, so a match is a pure function of (seed, roster, the humans' commands).
      ;;
      ;; THE MAGNET (founder: "make the ball magnet to the cars ... remember its like quidich ... you can add a control for the magnet ...
      ;; let the ball be thrown and passed like NBA street vol 2"). The ball is a Quaffle: you catch it, carry it, pass it, throw it.
      ;;   hold the button  the magnet is on: a free ball near the car's CRADLE (a point just ahead of the nose and a little above it) is
      ;;                    pulled in -- harder the closer it gets, and the pull damps the ball's speed relative to the car so it
      ;;                    settles into the cradle instead of orbiting it. A ball that reaches the cradle slowly enough is CAUGHT;
      ;;                    one that comes in too fast is fumbled and just hits the car, as it always did.
      ;;   carrying         the ball rides the cradle wherever the car goes (floor, wall, ceiling, air) -- but the tank does not refill,
      ;;                    the car's top speed is 90%, and after five seconds the ball is thrown for you (no stalling).
      ;;   let go           the THROW: the car's velocity plus 260 along the nose -- or, with a team-mate in a 28 degree cone ahead that
      ;;                    is calling for it (its own button held), a PASS led to where that team-mate will be when the ball gets
      ;;                    there; a team-mate's pass is easier to catch.
      ;;   tackles          an enemy bumping the carrier (or driving into the carried ball) knocks it loose; a team-mate never does.
      ;; With the button up nothing here runs, and the car and the ball behave exactly as they did before the magnet existed.
      ;;
      ;; ON FIRE (br_fire.prn) reaches in here at the places marked "on fire": a burning car's tank stays full (air-tick!), its throws
      ;; are 35% faster and leave alight (throw!), its magnet reaches 50% further (magnet-pull!), a burning pass is that much easier
      ;; for the team-mate to catch (catch-limit), a car that is not burning puts a burning ball out by playing it (credit-touch!),
      ;; and a steal puts the carrier's fire out (ball-car!, car-car!). The fires' clocks run once a tick in physics-tick!.
      
      (defn tick-dt [] : F32 0.016)
      (defn sub-dt [] : F32 0.008)
      (defn grav [] : F32 77.0)
      (defn rc [] : F32 4.0)              ; car collision sphere radius (two spheres, 3.6 either side of the centre)
      (defn sph-off [] : F32 3.6)
      (defn rb [] : F32 11.0)             ; the ball
      (defn ball-grav [] : F32 66.0)
      (defn fan-force [] : F32 130.0)
      (defn fan-reach [] : F32 6.0)       ; the fans catch a car whose wheels are this close
      (defn fan-hold [] : F32 12.0)       ; ... and keep hold until it is this far
      (defn tank-max [] : F32 100.0)
      
      ;; ---- basis helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; right = forward x up  (so right x up = -forward, a normal non-mirrored camera frame)
      (defn set-right! [(s : I32)] : Unit
        (let [(fx : F32) (c-fx s) (fy : F32) (c-fy s) (fz : F32) (c-fz s)
              (ux : F32) (c-ux s) (uy : F32) (c-uy s) (uz : F32) (c-uz s)]
          (set-c-rx! s (- (* fy uz) (* fz uy)))
          (set-c-ry! s (- (* fz ux) (* fx uz)))
          (set-c-rz! s (- (* fx uy) (* fy ux)))))
      
      ;; Gram-Schmidt: forward stays, up is made perpendicular to it, right follows
      (defn fix-basis! [(s : I32)] : Unit
        (let [(fx : F32) (c-fx s) (fy : F32) (c-fy s) (fz : F32) (c-fz s)
              (il : F32) (inv-len3 fx fy fz)
              (gx : F32) (* fx il) (gy : F32) (* fy il) (gz : F32) (* fz il)
              (ux : F32) (c-ux s) (uy : F32) (c-uy s) (uz : F32) (c-uz s)
              (d : F32) (dot3 gx gy gz ux uy uz)
              (px : F32) (- ux (* gx d)) (py : F32) (- uy (* gy d)) (pz : F32) (- uz (* gz d))
              (iu : F32) (inv-len3 px py pz)]
          (set-c-fx! s gx) (set-c-fy! s gy) (set-c-fz! s gz)
          (set-c-ux! s (* px iu)) (set-c-uy! s (* py iu)) (set-c-uz! s (* pz iu))
          (set-right! s)))
      
      ;; rotate the vector stored at words (i0, i0+1, i0+2) of car s about the unit axis k by an angle (given as cos, sin)
      (defn rot-words! [(s : I32) (i0 : I32) (kx : F32) (ky : F32) (kz : F32) (c : F32) (sn : F32)] : Unit
        (let [(vx : F32) (cf s i0) (vy : F32) (cf s (+ i0 1)) (vz : F32) (cf s (+ i0 2))
              (d : F32) (* (dot3 kx ky kz vx vy vz) (- 1.0 c))
              (cx : F32) (- (* ky vz) (* kz vy))
              (cy : F32) (- (* kz vx) (* kx vz))
              (cz : F32) (- (* kx vy) (* ky vx))]
          (cf! s i0 (+ (+ (* vx c) (* cx sn)) (* kx d)))
          (cf! s (+ i0 1) (+ (+ (* vy c) (* cy sn)) (* ky d)))
          (cf! s (+ i0 2) (+ (+ (* vz c) (* cz sn)) (* kz d)))))
      
      ;; spin the car about one of its own axes: axis 0 = right (pitch), 1 = up (yaw), 2 = forward (roll)
      (defn spin-car! [(s : I32) (axis : I32) (ang : F32)] : Unit
        (when (> (abs-f ang) 0.000001)
          (let [(c : F32) (cosf ang) (sn : F32) (sinf ang)]
            (cond
              (= axis 0) (let [(kx : F32) (c-rx s) (ky : F32) (c-ry s) (kz : F32) (c-rz s)]
                           (rot-words! s (k-ux) kx ky kz c sn) (rot-words! s (k-fx) kx ky kz c sn))
              (= axis 1) (let [(kx : F32) (c-ux s) (ky : F32) (c-uy s) (kz : F32) (c-uz s)]
                           (rot-words! s (k-fx) kx ky kz c sn))
              :else (let [(kx : F32) (c-fx s) (ky : F32) (c-fy s) (kz : F32) (c-fz s)]
                      (rot-words! s (k-ux) kx ky kz c sn)))
            (set-right! s))))
      
      ;; ---- placing a car -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; upright, facing the middle of the arena
      (defn place-car! [(s : I32) (x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32)] : Unit
        (let [(il : F32) (/ 1.0 (fmax2 0.001 (len2 x z)))]
          (set-c-x! s x) (set-c-y! s y) (set-c-z! s z)
          (set-c-vx! s 0.0) (set-c-vy! s 0.0) (set-c-vz! s 0.0)
          (set-c-ux! s 0.0) (set-c-uy! s 1.0) (set-c-uz! s 0.0)
          (set-c-fx! s (* (- 0.0 x) il)) (set-c-fy! s 0.0) (set-c-fz! s (* (- 0.0 z) il))
          (fix-basis! s)
          (set-c-wp! s 0.0) (set-c-wy! s 0.0) (set-c-wr! s 0.0)
          (set-c-attached! s 1)
          (set-c-px! s x) (set-c-py! s y) (set-c-pz! s z)
          (set-c-lift-fx! s 0.0) (set-c-boost-fx! s 0.0) (set-c-strafe-fx! s 0.0) (set-c-slip! s 0.0)
          (set-c-in-thr! s 0.0) (set-c-in-steer! s 0.0) (set-c-in-pitch! s 0.0) (set-c-in-roll! s 0.0) (set-c-in-strafe! s 0.0)
          (set-c-in-lift! s 0.0) (set-c-in-boost! s 0) (set-c-in-fans-off! s 0) (set-c-in-magnet! s 0)
          ;; a car put somewhere new (a kickoff, a respawn) leaves the ball behind
          (when (= (b-holder) s) (free-ball!))))
      
      ;; ---- the surface a car stands on --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; the smallest free distance of the car's two collision spheres, less their radius: <= 0 means touching
      (defn car-gap [(s : I32)] : F32
        (let [(x : F32) (c-x s) (y : F32) (c-y s) (z : F32) (c-z s)
              (fx : F32) (* (c-fx s) (sph-off)) (fy : F32) (* (c-fy s) (sph-off)) (fz : F32) (* (c-fz s) (sph-off))
              (d1 : F32) (arena-free (+ x fx) (+ y fy) (+ z fz))
              (d2 : F32) (arena-free (- x fx) (- y fy) (- z fz))]
          (- (fmin2 d1 d2) (rc))))
      
      ;; slide the car out of the walls: both spheres, two passes; velocity into a surface is removed (bounce only with fans off)
      (defn resolve-car! [(s : I32)] : Unit
        (dotimes [pass 2]
          (dotimes [e 2]
            (let [(sg : F32) (if (= e 0) 1.0 -1.0)
                  (x : F32) (+ (c-x s) (* (* (c-fx s) (sph-off)) sg))
                  (y : F32) (+ (c-y s) (* (* (c-fy s) (sph-off)) sg))
                  (z : F32) (+ (c-z s) (* (* (c-fz s) (sph-off)) sg))
                  (sd : F32) (arena-free x y z)
                  (pen : F32) (- (rc) sd)]
              (when (> pen 0.0)
                (arena-normal! x y z)
                (let [(nx : F32) (gf (g-sdx)) (ny : F32) (gf (g-sdy)) (nz : F32) (gf (g-sdz))
                      (vn : F32) (dot3 (c-vx s) (c-vy s) (c-vz s) nx ny nz)
                      (e1 : F32) (if (= (c-in-fans-off s) 1) 0.35 (if (= (c-attached s) 1) 0.0 0.12))]
                  (set-c-x! s (+ (c-x s) (* nx pen)))
                  (set-c-y! s (+ (c-y s) (* ny pen)))
                  (set-c-z! s (+ (c-z s) (* nz pen)))
                  (when (< vn 0.0)
                    (let [(j : F32) (* (- 0.0 vn) (+ 1.0 e1))]
                      (set-c-vx! s (+ (c-vx s) (* nx j)))
                      (set-c-vy! s (+ (c-vy s) (* ny j)))
                      (set-c-vz! s (+ (c-vz s) (* nz j)))))))))))
      
      ;; ---- one car, one substep ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; driving: the car is on a surface held by its fans
      (defn drive-sub! [(s : I32) (dt : F32)] : Unit
        (let [(x : F32) (c-x s) (y : F32) (c-y s) (z : F32) (c-z s)]
          (arena-normal! x y z)
          (let [(nx : F32) (gf (g-sdx)) (ny : F32) (gf (g-sdy)) (nz : F32) (gf (g-sdz))]
            ;; the up axis swings onto the surface normal; forward is kept in the tangent plane
            (let [(ux : F32) (+ (c-ux s) (* (- nx (c-ux s)) 0.2))
                  (uy : F32) (+ (c-uy s) (* (- ny (c-uy s)) 0.2))
                  (uz : F32) (+ (c-uz s) (* (- nz (c-uz s)) 0.2))
                  (iu : F32) (inv-len3 ux uy uz)]

      static inline int phys_try_melee_strike(PlayerState *attacker, PlayerState *targets, int base_damage, int hit_feedback, int allow_headshot_multiplier, unsigned int now_ms, unsigned int respawn_delay_ms) {
          float r = -attacker->yaw * 0.0174533f;
          float rp = attacker->pitch * 0.0174533f;
          float dx = sinf(r) * cosf(rp);
          float dy = sinf(rp);
          float dz = -cosf(r) * cosf(rp);
          int hit_any = 0;
      
          for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
              if (attacker == &targets[i]) continue;
              if (!targets[i].active || targets[i].state == STATE_DEAD) continue;
              if (targets[i].scene_id != attacker->scene_id) continue;
              if (phys_is_friendly(attacker, &targets[i])) continue;
      
              float kx = attacker->x - targets[i].x;
              float ky = attacker->y - targets[i].y;
              float kz = attacker->z - targets[i].z;
              if ((kx*kx + ky*ky + kz*kz) > MELEE_RANGE_SQ + 22.0f) continue;
      
              int hit_type = check_hit_location(attacker->x, attacker->y + EYE_HEIGHT, attacker->z, dx, dy, dz, &targets[i]);
              if (hit_type <= 0) continue;
      
              int damage = base_damage;
              attacker->hit_feedback = hit_feedback;
              if (allow_headshot_multiplier && hit_type == 2 && targets[i].shield <= 0) {
                  damage *= 3;
                  attacker->hit_feedback = 20;
              }
              katana_apply_damage(attacker, &targets[i], damage, attacker->hit_feedback, now_ms, respawn_delay_ms);
              hit_any = 1;
          }
      
          return hit_any;
      }
      
      void apply_friction(PlayerState *p) {
          if (p->dash_timer > 0) return;
          float speed = sqrtf(p->vx*p->vx + p->vz*p->vz);
          if (speed < 0.001f) { p->vx = 0; p->vz = 0; return; }
          
          float drop = 0;
          if (!p->in_vehicle && p->on_ground) {
              // S478b -- ground_friction is resolve_collision's own real, per-tick resolved value
              // (the box/material actually being stood on, or the global FRICTION baseline for
              // flat-floor/terrain ground which has no material). Replaces the flat FRICTION constant
              // this used to always read directly.
              float ground_fric = p->ground_friction;
              if (p->crouching) {
                  if (speed > 0.75f) drop = speed * SLIDE_FRICTION;
                  else drop = speed * (ground_fric * 3.0f);
              } else {
                  float control = (speed < STOP_SPEED) ? STOP_SPEED : speed;
                  drop = control * ground_fric;
              }
          }
          float newspeed = speed - drop;
          if (newspeed < 0) newspeed = 0;
          newspeed /= speed;
          p->vx *= newspeed; p->vz *= newspeed;
      }
