      /* buggy_move_xz_blocked -- horizontal move of a buggy against the scene's map_geo boxes. The buggy
         had NO wall collision at all (it drove straight through every box; only on-foot players went through
         resolve_collision), and at BUGGY_TOP_SPEED a single tick covers ~6 units, more than a thin wall, so
         the move is substepped. A box blocks when its top is above the wheels' step height and its bottom
         is below the chassis roof; the buggy is pushed out along the shallower axis and loses that
         velocity component (a wall hit scrubs speed). Shared sim: server and local play both run this via
         simulate_buggy_state, so multiplayer is authoritative. Walls carved by brick destruction are just
         map_geo boxes too, so a blasted hole is drivable. */
      static inline void buggy_move_xz_blocked(BuggyState *b, float dx, float dz) {
          float dist = sqrtf(dx * dx + dz * dz);
          int steps = (int)(dist / 1.0f) + 1;
          if (steps > 16) steps = 16;
          float sx = dx / (float)steps, sz = dz / (float)steps;
          for (int s = 0; s < steps; s++) {
              b->x += sx; b->z += sz;
              float bottom = b->y - (BUGGY_WHEEL_RADIUS + BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE);
              float top = bottom + BUGGY_BODY_HEIGHT;
              for (int i = 1; i < map_count; i++) {
                  Box bx = map_geo[i];
                  if (bx.w <= 0.0f || bx.d <= 0.0f || bx.h <= 0.0f) continue;
                  if (bx.y + bx.h / 2 <= bottom + BUGGY_STEP_HEIGHT) continue;
                  if (bx.y - bx.h / 2 >= top) continue;
                  float ox = (BUGGY_COLLIDE_R + bx.w / 2) - fabsf(b->x - bx.x);
                  float oz = (BUGGY_COLLIDE_R + bx.d / 2) - fabsf(b->z - bx.z);
                  if (ox <= 0.0f || oz <= 0.0f) continue;
                  if (ox < oz) {
                      b->x += (b->x > bx.x) ? ox : -ox;
                      b->vx = 0.0f;
                  } else {
                      b->z += (b->z > bx.z) ? oz : -oz;
                      b->vz = 0.0f;
                  }
              }
          }
      }
      
      static inline void simulate_buggy_state(BuggyState *b, float throttle, float steer, float dt, int apply_input) {
          if (!b || !b->active) return;
      
          if (throttle > 1.0f) throttle = 1.0f;
          if (throttle < -1.0f) throttle = -1.0f;
          if (steer > 1.0f) steer = 1.0f;
          if (steer < -1.0f) steer = -1.0f;
      
          float dt_scale = dt / 0.016f;
          if (dt_scale < 0.0f) dt_scale = 0.0f;
      
          if (!apply_input) {
              throttle = 0.0f;
              steer = 0.0f;
          }
      
          float r = -b->yaw * (3.14159265358979323846f / 180.0f);
          float fwd_x = sinf(r);
          float fwd_z = -cosf(r);
          float right_x = cosf(r);
          float right_z = sinf(r);
      
          float forward_speed = b->vx * fwd_x + b->vz * fwd_z;
          float lateral_speed = b->vx * right_x + b->vz * right_z;
          float speed_norm = fabsf(forward_speed) / buggy_top_speed();
          if (speed_norm > 1.0f) speed_norm = 1.0f;
      
          if (throttle > 0.01f) {
              float drive = BUGGY_BASE_DRIVE_FORCE * buggy_drive_force(speed_norm) * throttle * dt_scale;
              forward_speed += drive;
          } else if (throttle < -0.01f) {
              if (forward_speed > 0.03f) {
                  float brake_strength = 1.0f + (forward_speed / buggy_top_speed()) * 0.55f;
                  forward_speed -= BUGGY_BRAKE_FRICTION * (-throttle) * brake_strength * dt_scale;
                  if (forward_speed < 0.0f) forward_speed = 0.0f;
              } else {
                  float rev_norm = fabsf(forward_speed) / buggy_reverse_top_speed();
                  if (rev_norm > 1.0f) rev_norm = 1.0f;
                  float rev_force = BUGGY_BASE_DRIVE_FORCE * 0.72f * buggy_drive_force(rev_norm);
                  forward_speed += throttle * rev_force * dt_scale;
              }
          } else {
              if (forward_speed > 0.0f) {
                  forward_speed -= BUGGY_COAST_FRICTION * dt_scale;
                  if (forward_speed < 0.0f) forward_speed = 0.0f;
              } else if (forward_speed < 0.0f) {
                  forward_speed += (BUGGY_COAST_FRICTION * 1.15f) * dt_scale;
                  if (forward_speed > 0.0f) forward_speed = 0.0f;
              }
          }
      
          if (forward_speed > buggy_top_speed()) forward_speed = buggy_top_speed();
          if (forward_speed < -buggy_reverse_top_speed()) forward_speed = -buggy_reverse_top_speed();
      
          float abs_norm = fabsf(forward_speed) / buggy_top_speed();
          if (abs_norm > 1.0f) abs_norm = 1.0f;
      
          float steer_rate = buggy_turn_rate(abs_norm);
          float steer_authority = buggy_steer_authority(abs_norm);
          float steer_sign = (forward_speed < -0.03f) ? -1.0f : 1.0f;
          float steer_response = apply_input ? 0.22f : 0.10f;
          b->steer += (steer - b->steer) * steer_response * dt_scale;
          if (b->steer > 1.0f) b->steer = 1.0f;
          if (b->steer < -1.0f) b->steer = -1.0f;
          b->yaw = norm_yaw_deg(b->yaw + b->steer * steer_rate * steer_authority * steer_sign * dt_scale);
      
          float grip = buggy_lateral_grip(abs_norm) * dt_scale;
          if (grip > 1.0f) grip = 1.0f;
          lateral_speed *= (1.0f - grip);
      
          float r2 = -b->yaw * (3.14159265358979323846f / 180.0f);
          float new_fwd_x = sinf(r2);
          float new_fwd_z = -cosf(r2);
          float new_right_x = cosf(r2);
          float new_right_z = sinf(r2);
          b->vx = new_fwd_x * forward_speed + new_right_x * lateral_speed;
          b->vz = new_fwd_z * forward_speed + new_right_z * lateral_speed;
      
          if (!b->grounded) b->vy -= BUGGY_GRAVITY * dt_scale;
          b->y += b->vy;
          buggy_move_xz_blocked(b, b->vx, b->vz);
      
          float heights[4];
          buggy_sample_wheel_heights(b, heights);
          float front_avg = 0.5f * (heights[0] + heights[1]);
          float rear_avg = 0.5f * (heights[2] + heights[3]);
          float left_avg = 0.5f * (heights[0] + heights[2]);
          float right_avg = 0.5f * (heights[1] + heights[3]);
          float target_pitch = atanf((front_avg - rear_avg) / BUGGY_WHEELBASE) * (180.0f / 3.14159265358979323846f);
          float target_roll = atanf((left_avg - right_avg) / BUGGY_TRACK_WIDTH) * (180.0f / 3.14159265358979323846f);
          if (target_pitch > 28.0f) target_pitch = 28.0f;
          if (target_pitch < -28.0f) target_pitch = -28.0f;
          if (target_roll > 22.0f) target_roll = 22.0f;
          if (target_roll < -22.0f) target_roll = -22.0f;
          float support_avg = (heights[0] + heights[1] + heights[2] + heights[3]) * 0.25f;
          float support_y = support_avg + BUGGY_WHEEL_RADIUS + BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE;
          if (b->y <= support_y + 0.15f) {
              b->y = support_y;
              b->vy = 0.0f;
              b->grounded = 1;
              b->pitch += (target_pitch - b->pitch) * 0.35f;
              b->roll += (target_roll - b->roll) * 0.35f;
          } else {
              b->grounded = 0;
              b->pitch *= 0.995f;
              b->roll *= 0.995f;
          }
      }
      
      /* buggy_chase_steer_intent -- warthog-style steering (#542): the buggy rotates toward the camera heading
         (cam_yaw), so the camera is the "wheel" and the orbit camera (lobby draw_scene) keeps the buggy framed.
         Steers whenever the driver is on the throttle OR the buggy is still rolling (a coasting buggy used to
         ignore the camera). simulate_buggy_state flips the wheel when reversing, so the intent is flipped here
         to keep the net rotation toward the camera instead of away from it. Returns -1..1. */
      static inline float buggy_chase_steer_intent(const BuggyState *b, float throttle, float cam_yaw) {
          float yaw_err = norm_yaw_deg(cam_yaw - b->yaw);
          if (yaw_err > 180.0f) yaw_err -= 360.0f;
          if (yaw_err < -180.0f) yaw_err += 360.0f;
          float intent = yaw_err / 50.0f;
          float yr = -b->yaw * (3.14159265358979323846f / 180.0f);
          float fwd_spd = b->vx * sinf(yr) + b->vz * -cosf(yr);
          if (fabsf(throttle) < 0.05f && fabsf(fwd_spd) < 0.3f) intent = 0.0f;
          if (fwd_spd < -0.03f) intent = -intent;
          if (intent > 1.0f) intent = 1.0f;
          if (intent < -1.0f) intent = -1.0f;
          return intent;
      }

=== gen script ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gen_structure_rules.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/structure_rules.c from PARENA.
#
# Structural behaviour is decision logic, so it lives in PARENA with the rest of the rules:
#   PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn   material profiles, joint strength, load check
# packages/simulation/structure.h is the graph (nodes, joints, the load cascade); this is the numbers.
# Usage: scripts/gen_structure_rules.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout with .parena-bootstrap)
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
parena_dir="${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}"
if [ -x "$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap" ]; then
    parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
elif [ -x "$parena_dir/parena" ]; then
    parena_bin="$parena_dir/parena"
else
    (cd "$parena_dir" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)
    parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
fi
"$parena_bin" build "$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn" \
    -o "$root/packages/simulation/structure_rules.c"
echo "regenerated packages/simulation/structure_rules.c"

      ;; stdlib/shankpit/buggy_rules.prn -- SHANKPIT buggy handling as a PARENA mod (card #468, #464: "the buggy should be PARENA
      ;; programmable"). The physics (packages/common/physics.h simulate_buggy_state) keeps the integration, collision and
      ;; wheel-support; every number that decides how the buggy FEELS comes from here: the transmission torque curve, top speeds,
      ;; steering rate/authority and lateral grip. Retune a number or rewrite a curve, `make regen-buggy-rules` in SHANKPIT, and
      ;; the server and every client drive the new buggy. The defaults reproduce the previous built-in constants exactly.
      ;;
      ;; Scalar-only I32, fixed point: speed/abs-norm are permille of top speed (0..1000), results are permille (force
      ;; multipliers, steering authority, grip) or milli-units (speeds in units/tick x 1000, turn rate in degrees/tick x 1000).
      ;; The host converts with * 0.001 and clamps its inputs, so these are pure, total functions.
      (module shankpit/buggy-rules)
      (export buggy-top-speed-milli buggy-reverse-top-speed-milli buggy-drive-force-permille
              buggy-turn-rate-milli buggy-steer-authority-permille buggy-lateral-grip-permille)
      
      (defn buggy-top-speed-milli [] : I32 6240)
      (defn buggy-reverse-top-speed-milli [] : I32 1800)
      
      ;; Straight line from a (at lo) to b (at hi), x in [lo, hi], all permille.
      (defn lerp-permille [(a : I32) (b : I32) (x : I32) (lo : I32) (hi : I32)] : I32
        (+ a (/ (* (- b a) (- x lo)) (- hi lo))))
      
      ;; The 4-band "gearbox": strong off the line, a dip through the mid band, a second wind, then a smoothstep taper to a whisper
      ;; at top speed. Bands end at 0.22 / 0.52 / 0.78 of top speed. Multiplies the base drive force (0.0364/tick).
      (defn buggy-drive-force-permille [(speed : I32)] : I32
        (if (< speed 0) 1300
          (if (< speed 220) (lerp-permille 1300 920 speed 0 220)
            (if (< speed 520) (lerp-permille 920 620 speed 220 520)
              (if (< speed 780) (lerp-permille 620 840 speed 520 780)
                (if (< speed 1000)
                  ;; smoothstep taper: t = (speed-780)/220, s = t*t*(3-2t); staged so nothing overflows I32
                  (- 840 (/ (* 780 (/ (* (/ (* (/ (* (- speed 780) 1000) 220) (/ (* (- speed 780) 1000) 220)) 1000)
                                             (- 3000 (* 2 (/ (* (- speed 780) 1000) 220)))) 1000)) 1000))
                  60))))))
      
      ;; Degrees/tick x 1000: quick at a crawl (3.1), lazy at speed (0.9).
      (defn buggy-turn-rate-milli [(abs-norm : I32)] : I32
        (lerp-permille 3100 900 (if (> abs-norm 1000) 1000 (if (< abs-norm 0) 0 abs-norm)) 0 1000))
      
      ;; Steering authority grows with speed: 0.38 standing, 1.0 flat out.
      (defn buggy-steer-authority-permille [(abs-norm : I32)] : I32
        (lerp-permille 380 1000 (if (> abs-norm 1000) 1000 (if (< abs-norm 0) 0 abs-norm)) 0 1000))
      
      ;; Lateral grip per tick: 0.12 x (0.62 + 0.68 x speed) -- the faster, the more the tyres bite.
      (defn buggy-lateral-grip-permille [(abs-norm : I32)] : I32
        (/ (* 120 (lerp-permille 620 1300 (if (> abs-norm 1000) 1000 (if (< abs-norm 0) 0 abs-norm)) 0 1000)) 1000))
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/common/kit_test.c
  content: |
      /* kit_test.c -- the kit model and its three pages.
       * Build/run: make test-kit (plain gcc, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, no SDL/GL). */
      #include "kit.h"
      
      #include <assert.h>
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      int main(void) {
          KitState s;
          kit_defaults(&s);
      
          /* ---- slots: 1-9, 0, then the four gadget keys, and F is deliberately absent ---- */
          assert(KIT_SLOTS == 14);
          assert(strcmp(kit_slot_key_name(0), "1") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(kit_slot_key_name(9), "0") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(kit_slot_key_name(KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK), "`") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(kit_slot_key_name(KIT_SLOT_MINUS), "-") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(kit_slot_key_name(KIT_SLOT_EQUALS), "=") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(kit_slot_key_name(KIT_SLOT_C), "C") == 0);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('7') == 6);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('0') == 9);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('`') == KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('-') == KIT_SLOT_MINUS);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('=') == KIT_SLOT_EQUALS);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('c') == KIT_SLOT_C && kit_slot_from_key('C') == KIT_SLOT_C);
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('f') == -1 && kit_slot_from_key('F') == -1);   /* F = vehicle entry */
          assert(kit_slot_from_key('x') == -1);
          printf("PASS: 14 slots -- 1-9, 0, ` - = C, and no F\n");
      
          /* ---- prefabs: three of them, genuinely different, digits untouched ---- */
          assert(s.kit_count == 3);
          assert(s.selected == 0);
          assert(strcmp(s.kits[0].name, "SCOUT") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(s.kits[1].name, "BREACHER") == 0);
          assert(strcmp(s.kits[2].name, "HUNTER") == 0);
          for (int i = 0; i < KIT_SLOT_FIRST_GADGET; i++) assert(s.kits[0].slot[i] == KIT_ITEM_NONE);
          assert(kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_C) == KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);
          assert(kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK) == KIT_ITEM_RELOAD);
          assert(kit_live_item(&s, 99) == KIT_ITEM_NONE);        /* out of range is empty, not a crash */
          printf("PASS: three prefabs, and none of them steals a number key\n");
      
          /* ---- cycling wraps through every item and back to empty ---- */
          kit_clear_slot(&s.kits[0], KIT_SLOT_MINUS);
          int seen_empty = 0;
          for (int i = 0; i < KIT_ITEM_COUNT; i++) {
              if (s.kits[0].slot[KIT_SLOT_MINUS] == KIT_ITEM_NONE) seen_empty++;
              kit_cycle(&s.kits[0], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, 1);
          }
          assert(seen_empty == 1 && s.kits[0].slot[KIT_SLOT_MINUS] == KIT_ITEM_NONE);   /* full loop */
          kit_cycle(&s.kits[0], KIT_SLOT_MINUS, -1);
          assert(s.kits[0].slot[KIT_SLOT_MINUS] == KIT_ITEM_RELOAD);                    /* backwards wraps */
          printf("PASS: cycling wraps through all %d items and returns to empty\n", KIT_ITEM_COUNT);
      
          /* ---- selecting a kit moves what the gameplay keys read ---- */
          kit_select(&s, 1);
          assert(s.selected == 1);
          assert(kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_BACKTICK) == KIT_ITEM_PHEROMONE);     /* BREACHER */
          kit_select(&s, 99);                                                     /* ignored, not clamped */
          assert(s.selected == 1);
          printf("PASS: selecting a kit changes what the keys read\n");
      
          /* ---- the builder edits a DRAFT: nothing lands until it is saved ---- */
          {
              int live_before = kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_EQUALS);
              kit_cycle_draft(&s, KIT_SLOT_EQUALS, 1);
              assert(kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_EQUALS) == live_before);           /* live untouched */
              assert((int)s.draft.slot[KIT_SLOT_EQUALS] != live_before);
              kit_save_draft(&s);
              assert(kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_EQUALS) == (int)s.draft.slot[KIT_SLOT_EQUALS]);
              kit_select(&s, 2);                                                  /* a kit switch resets the draft */
              assert((int)s.draft.slot[KIT_SLOT_EQUALS] == kit_live_item(&s, KIT_SLOT_EQUALS));
          }
          printf("PASS: the draft is separate until SAVE, and a save becomes the live kit\n");
      
          /* ---- the three pages: real HTML, CSS, and the rows they claim ---- */
          static char page[8192];
          int n = kit_page_select(page, (int)sizeof page, &s);
          assert(n > 0 && strstr(page, "<html") && strstr(page, "<style") && strstr(page, "HUNTER"));
          n = kit_page_map(page, (int)sizeof page, &s, KIT_SLOT_C);
          assert(n > 0 && strstr(page, "PHEROMONE") && strstr(page, "class=\"on\""));
          n = kit_page_build(page, (int)sizeof page, &s, KIT_SLOT_MINUS);
          assert(n > 0 && strstr(page, "KIT BUILDER"));
          /* a buffer too small is refused, never truncated into broken markup */
          {
              char tiny[64];
              assert(kit_page_map(tiny, (int)sizeof tiny, &s, 0) == -1);
          }
          printf("PASS: three HTML+CSS pages (%d bytes for the map), and a short buffer is refused\n", n);
      
          printf("ALL PASS\n");
          return 0;
      }

      void draw_buggy_model(PlayerState *p) {
          uint32_t pid_seed = g_vehicle_style.seed ^ (uint32_t)(p ? (p->id + 1) * 2654435761u : 0u);
          const float t_sec = SDL_GetTicks() * 0.001f;
          const float scroll = t_sec * g_vehicle_style.neon_scroll + (float)(pid_seed & 255u) * 0.0007f;
          GLfloat specular[] = {g_vehicle_style.spec * 0.35f, g_vehicle_style.spec * 0.35f, g_vehicle_style.spec * 0.35f, 1.0f};
          GLfloat ambient[] = {0.06f, 0.06f, 0.07f, 1.0f};
          GLfloat diffuse[] = {0.14f, 0.14f, 0.15f, 1.0f};
          GLfloat light_pos[] = {0.4f, 2.5f, 1.8f, 0.0f};
      
          glPushAttrib(GL_ENABLE_BIT | GL_CURRENT_BIT | GL_LIGHTING_BIT | GL_TEXTURE_BIT | GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_LINE_BIT);
      
          if (!vehicle_style_enabled) {
              glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
              glColor3f(0.17f, 0.17f, 0.17f);
              glPushMatrix();
              glScalef(2.0f, 1.0f, 3.5f);
              draw_box_solid(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
              glPopMatrix();
              glPopAttrib();
              return;
          }
      
          glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
          glEnable(GL_LIGHT0);
          glLightfv(GL_LIGHT0, GL_POSITION, light_pos);
          glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_AMBIENT, ambient);
          glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_DIFFUSE, diffuse);
          glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SPECULAR, specular);
          glMaterialf(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SHININESS, 6.0f + (1.0f - g_vehicle_style.matte) * 28.0f);
      
          glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
          glColor4f(0.06f, 0.06f, 0.065f, 1.0f);
          glPushMatrix();
          glScalef(2.0f, 1.0f, 3.5f);
          draw_box_solid(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
          glPopMatrix();
      
          glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
          glLineWidth(1.4f);
          glColor4f(0.23f, 0.23f, 0.25f, 0.9f);
          glPushMatrix();
          glScalef(2.02f, 1.02f, 3.52f);
          glBegin(GL_LINES);
          glVertex3f(-1, 1, 1); glVertex3f(1, 1, 1);
          glVertex3f(1, 1, 1); glVertex3f(1, 1, -1);
          glVertex3f(-1, 1, -1); glVertex3f(1, 1, -1);
          glVertex3f(-1, 1, 1); glVertex3f(-1, 1, -1);
          glVertex3f(-1, 0, 1); glVertex3f(1, 0, 1);
          glVertex3f(-1, 0, -1); glVertex3f(1, 0, -1);
          glEnd();
          glPopMatrix();
      
          glColor4f(0.9f, 0.37f, 0.08f, 0.95f);
          glPushMatrix();
          glTranslatef(0.0f, 0.45f, 2.4f);
          glScalef(1.6f, 0.12f, 0.3f);
          draw_box_solid(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
          glPopMatrix();
      
          glPushMatrix();
          glTranslatef(-1.6f, 0.0f, -0.3f);
          glScalef(0.18f, 0.85f, 2.2f);
          draw_box_solid(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
          glPopMatrix();
      
          glEnable(GL_BLEND);
          glBlendFunc(GL_DST_COLOR, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);

          glScalef(2.0f, 1.0f, 3.5f);
          draw_box_planar_uv(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, scroll);
          glPopMatrix();
      
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
          glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, g_vehicle_glitch_tex.tex_id);
          glColor4f(0.95f, 0.15f, 0.85f, g_vehicle_style.glitch * 0.45f);
          glPushMatrix();
          glTranslatef(1.85f, 0.2f, 0.4f);

Named here rather than invented.\n;;\n;; What SHANKPIT adds is the fan suspension: the fans hold the car ROCKET_HOVER_HEIGHT off the\n;; surface instead of riding the wheels, so it skims over terrain the buggy has to crawl across.\n;; Tank is stored as centi-units (0..10000) so the per-tick spends stay pure integers: 26/s at 60 Hz\n;; is 433 centi-units a tick, 34/s is 567, 48/s is 800, 22/s is 367.\n;;\n;; Scalar-only I32, fixed point, total functions. 9.2 units/tick against the buggy's 6.24 -- the same margin the BR car has over a road car.\n(defn rocket-top-speed-milli [] : I32 9200)\n(defn rocket-reverse-top-speed-milli [] : I32 2200)\n\n;; Drive force multiplier over the buggy's base: 1.7x, because most of the thrust is the rear nozzle.\n(defn rocket-drive-permille [] : I32 1700)\n\n(defn rocket-tank-max [] : I32 10000)\n\n;; br_phys.prn: lift 26 /s, boost 22 /s, refill 34 /s, 48 /s on a surface (per tick at 60 Hz).\n(defn rocket-lift-spend [] : I32 433)\n(defn rocket-boost-spend [] : I32 367)\n(defn rocket-refill-spend [] : I32 567)\n(defn rocket-surface-refill-spend [] : I32 800)\n\n;; The fans hold the belly this far off the surface (milli-units): higher than the buggy's wheel rest\n;; height, so a rocket car clears kerbs and the low ledges a buggy has to go around.\n(defn rocket-hover-height-milli [] : I32 2600)\n\n(defn clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n;; The boost bonus scales with the tank, exactly like br_phys's \"empty, the car still turns at a\n;; quarter rate -- never helpless\": full air is +1300 permille of drive, an empty tank is +0 and the\n;; car is just a slow buggy.\n(defn rocket-boost-permille [(tank : I32)] : I32\n  (/ (* (clamp 0 10000 tank) 1300) 10000))\n\n;; Fan suspension, a spring on the height error (milli-units: positive = below the rest height).\n;; 3000 permille stiffness, capped so the nozzles can beat gravity but never launch it.\n(defn rocket-hover-accel-milli [(err : I32)] : I32\n  (clamp -900 1200 (/ (* err 3000) 1000)))\n\n(defn rocket-tank-step [(tank : I32) (spend : I32)] : I32\n  (clamp 0 10000 (- tank (if (< spend 0) 0 spend))))\n\n(defn rocket-tank-fill [(tank : I32) (gain : I32)] : I32\n  (clamp 0 10000 (+ tank (if (< gain 0) 0 gain))))\n"

An empty tank leaves the car sitting on its belly at the\n   ordinary buggy clearance instead of hovering -- the br_phys \"never helpless, but not a rocket\"\n   rule; it refills and floats again a couple of seconds later. */\nstatic inline void simulate_rocket_car_state(BuggyState *b, float throttle, float steer, float dt, int apply_input) {\n    if (throttle > 1.0f) throttle = 1.0f;\n    if (throttle < -1.0f) throttle = -1.0f;\n    if (steer > 1.0f) steer = 1.0f;\n    if (steer < -1.0f) steer = -1.0f;\n    float dt_scale = dt / 0.016f;\n    if (dt_scale < 0.0f) dt_scale = 0.0f;\n    int dts_milli = (int)(dt_scale * 1000.0f + 0.5f);\n    if (!apply_input) { throttle = 0.0f; steer = 0.0f; }\n\n    float r = -b->yaw * (3.14159265358979323846f / 180.0f);\n    float fwd_x = sinf(r), fwd_z = -cosf(r);\n    float right_x = cosf(r), right_z = sinf(r);\n    float forward_speed = b->vx * fwd_x + b->vz * fwd_z;\n    float lateral_speed = b->vx * right_x + b->vz * right_z;\n    float top = rocket_top_speed();\n    float speed_norm = fabsf(forward_speed) / top;\n    if (speed_norm > 1.0f) speed_norm = 1.0f;\n\n    /* the tank pays for the drive: nozzles burn while the throttle is open, air refills when it is not */\n    float thrust_scale = 1.0f;\n    if (throttle > 0.01f && b->tank > 0) {\n        b->tank = rocket_tank_step(b->tank, rocket_boost_spend(dts_milli));\n        thrust_scale += (float)rocket_boost_permille(b->tank) * 0.001f;\n    } else {\n        b->tank = rocket_tank_fill(b->tank, rocket_refill_gain(b->grounded, dts_milli));\n    }\n\n    if (throttle > 0.01f) {\n        float drive = BUGGY_BASE_DRIVE_FORCE * rocket_drive_permille() * buggy_drive_force(speed_norm)\n                      * throttle * dt_scale * thrust_scale;\n        forward_speed += drive;\n    } else if (throttle < -0.01f) {\n        if (forward_speed > 0.03f) {\n            float brake_strength = 1.0f + (forward_speed / top) * 0.55f;\n            forward_speed -= BUGGY_BRAKE_FRICTION * (-throttle) * brake_strength * dt_scale;\n            if (forward_speed < 0.0f) forward_speed = 0.0f;\n        } else {\n            float rev_norm = fabsf(forward_speed) / rocket_reverse_top_speed();\n            if (rev_norm > 1.0f) rev_norm = 1.0f;\n            forward_speed += throttle * BUGGY_BASE_DRIVE_FORCE * 0.72f * buggy_drive_force(rev_norm) * dt_scale;\n        }\n    } else if (forward_speed > 0.0f) {\n        forward_speed -= BUGGY_COAST_FRICTION * dt_scale * 0.55f;   /* it coasts: the fans don't drag */\n        if (forward_speed < 0.0f) forward_speed = 0.0f;\n    }\n\n    if (forward_speed > top) forward_speed = top;\n    if (forward_speed < -rocket_reverse_top_speed()) forward_speed = -rocket_reverse_top_speed();\n\n    float abs_norm = fabsf(forward_speed) / top;\n    if (abs_norm > 1.0f) abs_norm = 1.0f;\n    float steer_sign = (forward_speed < -0.03f) ? -1.0f : 1.0f;\n    float steer_response = apply_input ? 0.22f : 0.10f;\n    b->steer += (steer - b->steer) * steer_response * dt_scale;\n    if (b->steer > 1.0f) b->steer = 1.0f;\n    if (b->steer < -1.0f) b->steer = -1.0f;\n    b->yaw = norm_yaw_deg(b->yaw + b->steer * buggy_turn_rate(abs_norm) * buggy_steer_authority(abs_norm)\n                                          * steer_sign * dt_scale);\n    float grip = buggy_lateral_grip(abs_norm) * dt_scale;\n    if (grip > 1.0f) grip = 1.0f;\n    lateral_speed *= (1.0f - grip);\n\n    float r2 = -b->yaw * (3.14159265358979323846f / 180.0f);\n    b->vx = sinf(r2) * forward_speed + cosf(r2) * lateral_speed;\n    b->vz = -cosf(r2) * forward_speed + sinf(r2) * lateral_speed;\n    buggy_move_xz_blocked(b, b->vx, b->vz);\n\n    float heights[4];\n    buggy_sample_wheel_heights(b, heights);\n    float support_avg = (heights[0] + heights[1] + heights[2] + heights[3]) * 0.25f;\n    float rest = support_avg + rocket_hover_height();\n\n    /* the fans: lift out of the tank, a spring on the height error, damped so it settles */\n    if (b->tank > 0) b->tank = rocket_tank_step(b->tank, rocket_lift_spend(dts_milli));\n    float err_milli = (rest - b->y) * 1000.0f;\n    float fan = (b->tank > 0) ? 1.0f : 0.0f;\n    float accel = (float)rocket_hover_accel_milli((int)err_milli) * 0.001f * fan;\n    b->vy += accel - BUGGY_GRAVITY * 0.55f * dt_scale;\n    b->vy *= 0.86f;\n    b->y += b->vy;\n\n    float floor_y = support_avg + BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE;\n    if (b->y < floor_y) { b->y = floor_y; b->vy = 0.0f; }\n    b->grounded = (b->y <= rest + 0.15f) ? 1 : 0;\n\n    float front_avg = 0.5f * (heights[0] + heights[1]);\n    float rear_avg = 0.5f * (heights[2] + heights[3]);\n    float left_avg = 0.5f * (heights[0] + heights[2]);\n    float right_avg = 0.5f * (heights[1] + heights[3]);\n    float target_pitch = atanf((front_avg - rear_avg) / BUGGY_WHEELBASE) * (180.0f / 3.14159265358979323846f);\n    float target_roll = atanf((left_avg - right_avg) / BUGGY_TRACK_WIDTH) * (180.0f / 3.14159265358979323846f);\n    if (target_pitch > 28.0f) target_pitch = 28.0f;\n    if (target_pitch < -28.0f) target_pitch = -28.0f;\n    if (target_roll > 22.0f) target_roll = 22.0f;\n    if (target_roll < -22.0f) target_roll = -22.0f;\n    b->pitch += (target_pitch - b->pitch) * 0.35f;\n    b->roll += (target_roll - b->roll) * 0.35f;\n}\n\nstatic inline void simulate_buggy_state(BuggyState *b, float throttle, float steer, float dt, int apply_input) {\n    if (!b || !b->active) return;\n    if (b->rocket) { simulate_rocket_car_state(b, throttle, steer, dt, apply_input); return; }",

  "content": "/* vehicle_call.h -- the three VEHICLE gadgets from the player's KIT (packages/common/kit.h):\n * KIT_ITEM_BUGGY, KIT_ITEM_ROCKET_CAR, KIT_ITEM_HELI.\n *\n * Founder 2026-10-31: \"add buggy, rocket car, and hellicopter to the gadgets we already have the\n * buggy and the hellicopter the rocket car implementation is in bedrock racers\". So these are not a\n * new vehicle system either: buggy and helicopter are this engine's own BuggyState/HelicopterState,\n * the rocket car is a BuggyState with BuggyState.rocket set (physics.h simulate_rocket_car_state,\n * numbers from PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/rocket_car_rules.prn, ported from Bedrock Racers' br_phys.prn),\n * and this header is just the verb a gadget key needs: put that vehicle in front of the player and\n * seat them in it.\n *\n * Deliberately NOT a teleport: the vehicle is spawned ahead and the player enters it through the same\n * buggy_try_enter / occupant path E already uses, so everything downstream (camera, chase steering,\n * exit offsets, damage, the draw code) is the existing vehicle code and not a second copy of it.\n *\n * Included by hosts AFTER packages/simulation/local_game.h (it is a thin layer over local_state).\n * Local modes only: a networked client cannot spawn vehicles, the server owns that.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_VEHICLE_CALL_H\n#define SHANKPIT_VEHICLE_CALL_H\n\n#include \"local_game.h\"\n#include \"../common/kit.h\"\n\n#define VEHICLE_CALL_SPAWN_AHEAD 7.0f     /* far enough not to spawn inside the player's capsule */\n#define VEHICLE_CALL_HELI_HEIGHT 2.6f     /* rotor clearance over the ground it is called onto */\n#define VEHICLE_CALL_COOLDOWN 30          /* ticks, the same cooldown E uses after entering */\n\n/* vehicle_call_spawn -- the call verb. item is a KIT_ITEM_* vehicle; anything else is a no-op.\n * Returns VEH_NONE when refused (not a vehicle item, already driving, on cooldown, or every slot in\n * this scene's garage is taken -- refusing beats silently recycling someone else's vehicle), else\n * VEH_BUGGY (including the rocket car, which IS a buggy) or VEH_HELICOPTER. */\nstatic inline int vehicle_call_spawn(PlayerState *p, int item) {\n    if (!p || !p->active) return VEH_NONE;\n    if (!kit_item_is_vehicle(item)) return VEH_NONE;\n    if (p->in_vehicle) return VEH_NONE;\n    if (p->vehicle_cooldown > 0) return VEH_NONE;\n\n    float r = -p->yaw * 0.0174532925f;\n    float px = p->x + sinf(r) * VEHICLE_CALL_SPAWN_AHEAD;\n    float pz = p->z - cosf(r) * VEHICLE_CALL_SPAWN_AHEAD;\n\n    if (item == KIT_ITEM_BUGGY || item == KIT_ITEM_ROCKET_CAR) {\n        int slot = -1;\n        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_BUGGIES; i++) {\n            if (!local_state.buggies[i].active) { slot = i; break; }\n        }\n        if (slot < 0) return VEH_NONE;\n        BuggyState *b = &local_state.buggies[slot];\n        buggy_spawn_defaults(b, slot, p->scene_id, px, pz, p->yaw);\n        if (item == KIT_ITEM_ROCKET_CAR) {\n            b->rocket = 1;\n            b->tank = rocket_tank_max();\n            /* the fans hold it off the surface from the first tick, so it arrives hovering rather\n             * than sinking into the ground it was called onto */\n            b->y += rocket_hover_height();\n        }\n        if (!buggy_try_enter(p, b)) return VEH_NONE;\n        p->vehicle_cooldown = VEHICLE_CALL_COOLDOWN;\n        printf(\"[VEHICLE] called %s id=%d scene=%d at %.1f,%.1f (player=%d)\\n\",\n               b->rocket ? \"rocket car\" : \"buggy\", slot, p->scene_id, px, pz, p->id);\n        return VEH_BUGGY;\n    }\n\n    /* KIT_ITEM_HELI */\n    {\n        int slot = -1;\n        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_HELICOPTERS; i++) {\n            if (!local_state.helicopters[i].active) { slot = i; break; }\n        }\n        if (slot < 0) return VEH_NONE;\n        float gy = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, px, pz);\n        if (gy < 0.0f) gy = 0.0f;\n        HelicopterState *h = &local_state.helicopters[slot];\n        heli_spawn_defaults(h, slot, p->scene_id, px, gy + VEHICLE_CALL_HELI_HEIGHT, pz);\n        h->yaw = p->yaw;\n        h->occupant_player_id = p->id;\n        p->in_vehicle = 1;\n        p->vehicle_type = VEH_HELICOPTER;\n        p->x = h->x; p->y = h->y; p->z = h->z;\n        p->vx = p->vy = p->vz = 0.0f;\n        p->vehicle_cooldown = VEHICLE_CALL_COOLDOWN;\n        printf(\"[VEHICLE] called helicopter id=%d scene=%d at %.1f,%.1f (player=%d)\\n\",\n               slot, p->scene_id, px, pz, p->id);\n        return VEH_HELICOPTER;\n    }\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_VEHICLE_CALL_H */\n"
}

Items are not a new inventory: each one is an input this engine already acts on (`PHEROMONE` -> `in_pheromone`, `ABILITY`, `SECONDARY`, `RELOAD`), so a kit is a key->real-action map rather than a parallel universe of fake gadgets. Three prefabs (SCOUT / BREACHER / HUNTER, genuinely different shapes), cycling that wraps through every item and back to empty, and a **draft** so the builder never trashes the kit you are carrying. Three phone apps: **KITS** (pick the prefab that goes live), **KIT MAP** (rebind the live kit's keys, ENTER clears), **KIT BUILD** (edit the draft, ENTER saves it over the live kit, with `*` marking any row that differs). - **feat(zombies): the lure feeds, the horde navigates, and your pheromone buys you a window that closes.** Founder: *"zombies shouldnt just walk into walls ... sometimes they should but that is when they are trying to break walls down they should have some ability to navigate the terrain i think citizens already do that also the zombies dont seem to respond to ferimone balls it should make them hungry and somewhat aggressive also it should guide them to the spot also they should attack the player ad the citizens when they are hungry or aggressive there should be some threshold where they dont attack you if your pherimone caused their hunger and agression but that should be like a fading memory your zombies wont attack you at first but they forget pretty quick and they will target you for the next snack after your window runs out so you need to be intentional with your phermone balls to move them around the map as there are more of them."* Three separate defects, one cause: the systems were all built and none of them were talking to each other. (1) **Walking into walls.** `witness_ai_tick`'s wall pass called `wai_avoid_walls(..., g_wall_hit_hook != NULL)`, and the real game always installs that hook, so every zombie was `relentless` -- route planning skipped -- and the whole horde ground the straight line into the nearest face and clawed it from 100 m out. It is now a real decision: breach only when the target is within `WITNESS_AI_ZOMBIE_BREACH_TARGET_RANGE` (70 m, i.e. the fight is right there) and the zombie is HUNTING/FRENZIED, otherwise it plans a route exactly as a citizen already did; the existing `g_wai_breach` stop-plant-and-tear path is untouched, which is what keeps wall-breaking working. (2) **Pheromone balls did nothing.** A marker only redirected the steering of a zombie with no hero lock -- it fed nothing, so a lure moved a horde around and left it exactly as harmless as it found it, and the marker's own thrower was never recorded at all (the parallel `g_pheromone_owner1[]` array now does, rather than adding a field to ported BIG_O code). A zombie now gains `WITNESS_AI_PHEROMONE_HUNGER_PER_SEC`/`_AGGRESSION_PER_SEC` (rate-clamped against the real tick delta) while it is steering to a canister, so the lure genuinely makes it dangerous, and it remembers whose canister recruited it. New PARENA rule `zombies-pheromone-should-hunt(hunger_milli, aggression_milli)` makes it hungry OR aggressive (0.40 / 0.45, deliberately unequal: hunger is "I need a meal", aggression is "something just happened"), and the fading memory is its sibling `zombies-pheromone-spares-thrower(grace_ms, thrower_alive)` -- `WITNESS_AI_PHEROMONE_GRACE_MS` (9 s) of immunity for the THROWER ONLY, checked before the hero is even sensed, with the owner cleared the moment it lapses so a later thrower is judged fresh. Citizens were never covered, so a lured horde eats the neighbourhood and remembers you late. Verified: `make test-pheromone-grenade` -- a canister raises a zombie's hunger 0.13 -> 1.00 and its aggression past 0.20, the thrower can stand in its face for 3 s untouched, and after the window the same zombie bites them; `make test-witness-ai-zombies` -- a zombie 290 m from its target with a wall between routes around the building with ZERO claw hits, while the existing close-range test still claws the same wall 27 times; plus the pocket-escape, day/night, per-role REFLUX and mark-2-marker tests all still pass. Not done: no controller/left-trigger throw binding beyond the existing `BTN_PHEROMONE`, no HUD readout of the grace countdown (the `witness_ai_zombie_grace_ms` accessor it would need exists), and "somewhat aggressive" is a hunger/aggression rate rather than a new mood state.

## 2026-10-30

- **fix(build): the Windows client did not compile — a lobby helper shadowed a generated rules function.** Found by actually cross-compiling: installed mingw-w64 plus the same SDL2 2.30.10 / SDL2_ttf 2.22.0 mingw kits `release.yml` downloads, then compiled every one of the 91 `LOBBY_SRC` files for `x86_64-w64-mingw32`. Exactly one failed, and it was mine from the lighting slice: `apps/lobby/src/main.c` reads `env_emissive_scale()` in the enemy-outline pass ~70 lines *before* defining it, so C inferred `int env_emissive_scale()` at the call and then rejected the real `static float env_emissive_scale(void)` as a conflicting type — and the name also shadowed PARENA's generated `int env_emissive_scale(int ambient_permille)` from `lighting_rules.c`, which is linked into the same binary. Two fixes: forward declarations for the three environment-matrix read helpers (`env_flashlight_range`, `env_flashlight_half_angle`, and the outline one) placed where the `g_env` state is declared, and the local helper renamed to `env_outline_emissive_scale` so it can never shadow a rules function again. This would have broken a native `make lobby` on Linux too — nobody had compiled the lobby outside CI, so only the Windows job could have caught it. New `scripts/check_windows_build.sh` + `make check-windows` compiles all `LOBBY_SRC` under mingw (headers only, no link, so no SDL2 .a/.dll or EDITOR.GAME objects needed) and reports the file and first errors, so this class of break is one command instead of one release cycle. Verified: 91/91 sources now compile, `make check-windows` passes, and the link is proven to close — of every symbol the 91 objects need, the ONLY unresolved ones are the 14 `editor_widget_*` functions `release.yml` supplies from its EDITOR.GAME checkout (nothing else is missing), and stubbing exactly those yields a real `PE32+ executable (console) x86-64`. The other half of the Windows job was re-run too: `release.yml`'s `dw_gui.exe` recipe, verbatim, against a fresh clone of DEADWEIGHT — links clean now that `core/draft.c` is in that hand-copied list. NOT verified: running any of these binaries (no Windows here) and the four Go/REDGARDEN/EDITOR.GAME OS apps, whose sibling repos aren't checked out in this sandbox.
- **feat(ocean): the archipelago gets water — a sea state, a wave field, and a hull that floats.** Founder paste (SP-ARCH-ENG-004): an archipelago battle royale on SHANKPIT, with client SQL ledgers, unified UDP streams, heightfield ocean, fractal destruction and island streaming. Scoped honestly in `docs/ARCHIPELAGO_NORTHSTAR.md` first, and the audit found that **three of the five sections describe things this monorepo has already built** under other names: §5's "stress propagation / load paths from anchors to foundations" is the structure cascade shipped this week, §5's node detachment is `bf_detect_at_parent`/`bf_damage_sphere` + rigid chunks, §2's append-only ledger is IDUNA's `event-stream`, and §3's unreliable-transform stream is `PACKET_SNAPSHOT`. Section §4 — water — had **literally zero code** anywhere in SHANKPIT (`grep` for buoyancy/wave/water_level: no hits), so that is the slice. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/ocean_rules.prn` (generated to `packages/simulation/ocean.c` by `scripts/gen_ocean_rules.sh`): five sea states from calm to tempest as ONE integer that every other number derives from, a three-layer cosine heightfield (deliberately NOT called Gerstner — no horizontal particle displacement, so no overhanging crest), submerged-fraction, planing lift that saturates with speed, and drag that grows with speed. New host `packages/simulation/ocean.h`: surface sampling, normals by central difference, and a probe-based hull (`ocean_vessel_forces`/`ocean_vessel_step`) integrating buoyancy against weight plus a pitch torque from the wave slope. The blueprint's "multi-threaded simulation loop" is explicitly rejected in the doc — this engine's netcode depends on one deterministic loop, and buoyancy is cheap enough to stay in it. Fixed a real, months-old gap to make it compile: **the C emitter had no `math/` primitive mapping at all** (documented as unstarted in `stdlib/math/math.prn`), so `math/cos` mangled into a call to a never-defined `math_cos()`; `src/emit.c` now lowers the qualified names to libm's `floor`/`sqrt`/`log`/`cos` and `math_random_impl()`, matched by qualified name so a local defn is never captured. Verified: `make test-ocean` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, no GL) — calm is flat to the millimetre and sea-state RMS is monotonic (0.000 / 0.159 / 0.317 / 0.544 / 0.816 m), determinism, planing lift rising then saturating, drag rising with speed, **a hull dropped from 3 m settles at y=-0.70 instead of sinking and one released at -2 m rises**, a settled hull takes 1.20 m/s² of slam in a storm against 0.03 in calm (40x), and a sloped surface tilts the normal while calm water stays flat. Two honest corrections made by the test rather than by the code: my slam assertion was measuring the hull's own drop transient (a 150-tick warmup fixed it), and the first draft's 1.5x threshold was replaced by the real 40x measurement. - **fix(world): a shot-down support is a weaker support.** The graph scaled a piece's MASS with the cells shot out of it but left its compression CAPACITY at the full value, so a concrete pier missing 90% of its material carried exactly what an intact one did until its very last cell went — the most obvious way a "physically aware" collapse can look wrong, and one a player would find in about ten seconds of hammering a pillar. `StructNode` gains `strength` (0..1, the share of the original cross-section still there), set by `brick_world_structure_sync` from `intact / total`, and `structure_evaluate` multiplies capacity by it. Linear in what is left: defensible for a column, and named in the header as NOT a stress solver (a hollowed-out tube genuinely keeps more of its capacity than this says). Verified: `make test-structure` — a concrete pier that holds a 324 t slab whole, then fails and leaves the slab unsupported at 20% of its section (carrying 327,456 kg at the moment it goes); `make test-brick-world` — the wiring itself, strength 1.0 at load and 1/7 after six of the post's seven cells are shot out, and the deck goes with the pier. All earlier brick checks still pass, and `make server` still links. The lobby remains unbuildable here: `pkg-config --exists sdl2` is false and there is no `/usr/include/SDL2` on this box, so `LOBBY_SRC` is still reviewed rather than compiled.
- **feat(world): a big piece falls in pieces instead of not at all.** Closing the hole the wiring left: `bf_detach_parent` refused any parent over `BF_CHUNK_CELLS` (256), so a large deck or a long wall was permanently immune to the structural layer — the exact case a player would try first, since big buildings are the ones worth bringing down. It now splits the piece along its longest axis and drops one chunk per slab, with the slab height chosen so a part stays under the chunk budget even with every cell intact (a 288-cell deck becomes two slabs of at most 256). Still all-or-nothing: if the chunk queue cannot take every part, nothing detaches, because a half-fallen wall is worse than a standing one — the same rule the cell-level pass uses. Verified: `make test-brick-world` gains the 288-cell case (post's 7 cells + deck's 288 cells removed, 3 chunks queued, each ≤256, nothing left solid), and every earlier check still passes. Also verified this time, unlike the last two slices: **`make server` builds and links**, which is the proof that putting `packages/simulation/structure_rules.c` and `packages/world/parena_runtime.c` in `SERVER_SRC` was right. The lobby still cannot be compiled here (no SDL2 headers), so only `SERVER_SRC` is proven; `LOBBY_SRC` and `BUILD.bazel` remain reviewed, not built.
- **feat(world): the structural layer is wired in — a piece that loses its support actually comes down.** Follow-up to the same day's structural graph, which was built and proven headless but consumed by nothing. `brick_world.h` now builds the graph when a level loads (one node per destructible parent, `anchored` = on the world floor or touching any non-destructible solid — resting on it and bolted to it are the same thing here, because neither moves on its own) and re-evaluates it inside `brick_world_flush`, i.e. on load and on damage only: **zero per-tick cost**, which is the whole reason this shape was chosen for an MMO tick budget. A piece the graph can no longer justify is dropped whole by the new `bf_detach_parent` (`brick_fracture.h`), becoming one rigid chunk on the existing debris path instead of hanging in the air. It is budgeted exactly like the cell pass: a parent over `BF_CHUNK_CELLS` (256), or one arriving with the chunk queue full, stays standing rather than half-detaching. Piece mass now follows the damage (`1 - removed/cells`), so a wall carved down to a stub weighs what is left of it and a shot-away pillar stops holding a roof up long before its last cell goes. Two real fixes came out of wiring it: (1) `structure_boxes_meet`'s tolerance is now a WELDING DISTANCE (`>= -tol`, not `> tol`), because authored geometry is routinely flush — a roof sitting exactly on a pillar's top face shares a face with zero overlap, and under the old rule no authored piece ever joined anything; (2) the load-time baseline was taken after `structure_evaluate`, which strips a failed piece's support, so every overloaded building was quietly baselined as "authored decoration" and stood forever — it is now taken on the support flood before any load verdict. The same fix taught the engine to collapse a structure the rules say cannot hold itself **at load, before the first frame**, instead of waiting for someone to shoot it. The rules' overflow guard also changed: `struct-holds-load` was comparing `mass x 1000` against `capacity x 850` in I32, which overflows for any real building (a concrete pier holds 72 million kg); it now divides the capacity before applying the 15%, and the C-side 2-million-kg clamp that had flattened every material into one capacity is replaced by a 2-billion-kg arithmetic ceiling that never decides a verdict. Verified: `make test-brick-world` — the wood-post level loses all 7 post cells and all 72 deck cells at load, both stop being solid immediately and two chunks are queued; the identical deck on a concrete post survives untouched with zero failures; the wall-only level leaves the layer off; every pre-existing check (magnum breach, hammer, claw, glass chunk, net apply, saved damage) still passes. `make test-structure` still passes. NOT verified: the lobby and server binaries are not compiled here (no SDL2), so the two source-list edits (`Makefile` LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC, `packages/simulation/BUILD.bazel`) and the live look are reviewed, not built; and a dropped piece is one rigid body, not a tumbling pile of brick.
- **feat(world): destructible brick gets a structural layer — joints, support, and a load cascade.** Founder real-time: "evolve the destructible brick logic into an intelligent, physically aware material and structural simulation ... a web of self-anchoring volumetric nodes". Scoped to what this engine can actually afford at MMO concurrency: no finite-element solver, no "layer bake", and no claiming either. Three things a player can feel, all deterministic so the server and every client agree. (1) **Joints at load** (`structure_build_joints`): boxes whose volumes intersect are joined — a piece sunk into a concrete master is ANCHORED, two crossing pieces of equal class are PEGGED (the virtual peg; timber is strong in shear, weak in tension). Whether a pair may join at all is PARENA's call (`struct_joint_strength`), which is why a glass pane leaning on a brick wall gets NO joint at all (150 < the 300 permille threshold): it is resting, not anchored, and it falls when the wall goes — exactly the behaviour a shader could never fake. (2) **A support flood** from the grounded pieces outward along joints, one level up from `bf_detect_detached`'s own question about cells: a piece that loses its last path to the ground is disconnected. Joints hold in BOTH directions (no height condition in the flood) because a roof is held by the pillar as much as the pillar is held by the foundation; only the load cascade follows gravity. (3) **The load cascade** (`structure_evaluate`): mass = volume × density accumulates top-down, each support hands its load equally to whatever would bear it, and each is checked against its own compression capacity (`struct_compression` kg/m² × footprint, with PARENA's 15% safety factor). A support that fails STOPS PASSING SUPPORT and the round repeats (bounded at 3), so one shot-out pillar drops the roof onto the next one rather than leaving it hanging in the air — the failure that makes a collapse read as a collapse. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn` (generated by `scripts/gen_structure_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/structure_rules.c`): density, tensile, compression, shear, damping, fracture kind, joint strength and the load comparison, all i32 at the boundary. New header-only `packages/simulation/structure.h` is the graph (≤512 nodes, ≤4096 joints, GL-free, no per-tick allocation); `structure_remove_node` + `structure_evaluate` is the whole "this piece is gone, what is now falling?" step. Named gaps, deliberate: no shear flow inside a piece, no bending/buckling SHAPE (a pillar holds its column load or the node fails — it does not bow), no fatigue, no per-cell stress inside one box. One real fix the test forced: `struct_holds_load` compares `mass × 1000` against `capacity × 850` in I32, so an unclamped 20×20×0.6 m concrete slab's mass (576 t) overflowed the capacity side into a UB-garbage answer; both operands are now clamped to a 2,000 t ceiling (documented, and far above any level box) which keeps a real overload a real failure. Verified: `make test-structure` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, no GL, no display) — PARENA totality, the reference frame's 4 anchors + 4 pegs, "one pillar gone and the roof still stands", "the last support gone and it does not", the glass-rests-on-brick case asserting zero joints and no support, a beam left unsupported when its post is demolished, the cascade (576,000 kg slab on a 126,000 kg wood pillar → pillar fails carrying 576,864 kg, 2 pieces unsupported), and bit-identical determinism. NOT verified / not yet wired: nothing calls this from `brick_world.h` yet — the graph is built and proven headless, and the hookup (a `bf_detect_detached`-flagged piece removing its node and re-evaluating) is the next slice; the live look, obviously, is unseen.
- **test(lighting): the whole chain, end to end and headless.** The two unit tests each proved half of it (`test-env-matrix` the matrix, `test-ambient-boost` the slider); neither proved the property the founder actually asked for — that the systems TALK to each other. New `packages/render/lighting_chain_test.c` sweeps every lighting preset (day / sunset / night / interior / dynamic) × every real weather state (clear / overcast / rain / storm) × slider 0/5/10 × three face directions (shaded / sunward / sideways) — 180 combinations — through the production calls `draw_scene` makes (`retro_lighting_eval` → `env_matrix_apply`/`publish` → `retro_lighting_eval_surface_rgb`) and asserts only invariants that must hold for ALL of them: a shaded face never gets darker than the old chain left it, no surface ends below the published floor, every channel stays finite and inside [0,1], deterministic to the bit, and the clear-noon vs clear-midnight swing survives (a matrix that flattened the world would fail). Deliberately does NOT assert that a sun-facing face never dims — it is supposed to, that is what makes a storm read as a storm. One real cleanup forced by making this runnable: the sky's two purely mathematical functions (`retro_sky_eval_sun_dir` / `retro_sky_eval_fog_rgb`) moved into a GL-free `packages/render/retro_sky_eval.h` that both `retro_sky.h` and `retro_lighting.c` include, because `retro_sky.h` pulls in `proc_tex.h`'s `<SDL2/SDL_opengl.h>` — the lighting code needed a GPU header to do arithmetic. `retro_sky.c` keeps the implementations (it draws the dome, so it stays GL-bound) and the test stubs only those two functions. `make test-lighting-chain` runs under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` with ASan+UBSan and links no GL. Still not verified: the lobby itself (`main.c`) and the live look — no SDL2 headers in this sandbox.
- **feat(lighting): lightning is a light source, not a screen tint.** Follow-up to the environment matrix: a bolt only ever flashed `sky_weather_draw_grade`'s overlay, and the world under it -- the storm deck, the walls, the players -- ignored it entirely. New `env-flash-boost` in `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/lighting_rules.prn` (regenerated into `packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c`) turns `SkyWeather.flash` (its own already-smoothed bolt intensity) into extra SCATTERED light, 0..0.30, added to the same bleed channel the rest of the atmosphere uses rather than to any new one; the host also mixes that bleed colour toward white by the same fraction (a bolt is broadband light, not the storm's grey) and lifts exposure by half of it. Deliberately diffuse, not a directional beam: the bolt lights the whole cloud deck, which is why its contribution is scatter. No new state, no extra evaluation -- it is one more term in the existing per-frame `env_matrix_eval`, and `flash == 0` is bit-for-bit the previous result. Verified in `make test-env-matrix`: the rule clamps (`env_flash_boost(0) == 0`, `env_flash_boost(1000) <= 300`, saturates above 1000), a strike raises bleed and exposure over the same storm, the bleeds whiten, and the strike measurably lands on a dark surface through the production `env_matrix_apply_surface` transform. Still NOT verified: the lobby is GL-bound and no SDL2 headers exist in this sandbox, so the `env_in.flash = g_sky_weather.flash` wiring and the live look are reviewed, not built.
- **feat(lighting): one unified environment matrix, resolved in PARENA — the "too dark everywhere" fix.** Founder real-time: "we have cool weather effects but it doesnt work with the ambient lighting like it always looks too dark everywhere we have some lighting tech down but we need more of a theory of all the lighting needs to talk to each other." The diagnosis was exact: weather (`sky_weather_light_state`), the day/night preset, the ambient slider (`ambient_rules.prn`) and the emitters each adjusted the scene independently, and every one of them could only subtract — a stormy night at slider 0 multiplied ambient down to near-black walls because nothing tracked how much light the world actually gets. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/lighting_rules.prn` (generated by the new `scripts/gen_lighting_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c`) resolves the atmosphere into six i32-permille values — occlusion (capped at 0.78), light bleed, ambient floor, exposure, emissive scale, emitter range/spread — and everything reads those instead of deriving its own. New thin host layer `packages/render/env_matrix.{h,c}` only converts units and applies: `env_matrix_apply` dims ambient gently (18% at worst) and sun/moon fully, `env_matrix_publish` hands the floor and the scattered sky-colour bleed to `retro_lighting`, and `env_matrix_apply_surface` (one function, one translation unit, no GL) adds the bleed and lifts the combined ambient term to the floor with a uniform gain (floor ÷ brightest channel) — hue-preserving, not a per-channel clamp, so walls do not wash flat. `retro_lighting_eval_surface_rgb` calls that exact function for every surface in the game; with nothing published it is a bit-for-bit no-op, so every existing caller and test is unchanged. Interiors keep only 35% of the occlusion and get a higher floor and no open-sky bleed. Emitters now trade reach for spread: fog shortens `FLASHLIGHT_RANGE` and widens `FLASHLIGHT_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` through one derived number, applied to the beam mesh, the per-face lit cone and the litbox spotlight uniforms so they cannot disagree; the enemy outline scales its emissive by the same scene-brightness inverse (bright noon tucks it down to 0.75, a dark scene pushes it up). Deliberately NOT described as Rayleigh/Mie scattering — it models the three things that were actually broken, not a physical sky this renderer cannot support. Costs one CPU evaluation per frame from values both sides already broadcast (no server work, no new wire fields, no per-entity state) and is a pure function, so every client computes the identical matrix bit for bit — the property that keeps it cheap at MMO concurrence instead of syncing lighting. Verified: `make test-env-matrix` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, links no GL) — PARENA purity/clamps, clear-weather no-op, the stormy-night regression through the exact production function (shaded-wall luminance 0.209 → 0.358, floor 0.300, occlusion 0.78, bleed 0.32), publish→surface wiring and its inverse, slider monotonicity under the worst weather, bit-identical determinism, and the emitter trade-off across the whole visibility range. NOT verified here: `retro_lighting` is GL-bound and this sandbox has no SDL2 headers, so `make test-ambient-boost` (recipe updated for the new link dependency) and the live look could not be built or seen; `apps2/`'s duplicate tree untouched.
- **feat(weapons): the assault rifle's underbarrel grenade — right click, E, and the controller's left trigger.** Founder real-time: "add an E for 3 the assault rifle ... the traditional right click thing where it fires a grenade like if its an m4 or whatever with the grenade powerup attached have e and right click both trigger it and ensure we have left trigger affordances for controller ... it should do a projectile and it should be fast like soldier 76 rocket and it should be a bit of like an arch down like its not so fast that its instant like a rail gun ... cool fireball shaders and explosions ... when it hits stuff it should cause an explosion and ensure it behaves with our destructable geometry." `WPN_AR`'s existing Frag Toss (a 0.7x lob) is replaced by a real rifle grenade: `AR_GRENADE_SPEED_MULT` 2.2x the 4.0 units/tick base (~9 units/tick, fast enough to read as a rocket, still a flight you watch), new `Projectile.gravity` (`AR_GRENADE_GRAVITY` 0.22 units/tick²) integrated in `update_projectiles` so it arcs instead of flying dead straight, damage 75, splash 4.5, 260-tick cooldown. New `BTN_ABILITY_2` (bit 2048) is a genuinely separate input from E, not a duplicate: right mouse and controller LEFT trigger (fire is the right trigger; LB was already the ability) set it — separate because the sniper's zoom IS right mouse, and folding RMB into `BTN_ABILITY_1` would spend the storm charges every time someone scoped (asserted in the new test). `Projectile.weapon` now carries the firing weapon into `explode_splash` instead of a hardcoded `WPN_MISSILE`, so the blast hook carves destructible brick with AR's own x2 multiplier rather than a rocket's x5 — a grenade opens a hole where a missile deletes the wall. Presentation: a real GLSL fireball (same hand-loaded GL 2.0 path `gl_shader.h` gives the flashlight beam, so it survives the mingw build) draws one camera-facing billboard per detonation — layered value noise over a sphere normal, white-hot core cooling to orange then smoke, plus a shockwave ring racing ahead of the flame — blended additively, with a second shell, a 12-ember spray and a fading trail on the round itself, all driven by `g_fx_explosion_hook` from `explode_splash` (NULL on the server and in tests, so nothing but pixels changes). No shader support degrades to an additive glow quad instead of nothing. NOT a port of Bedrock Racers' fire: BR's flames are JS/WebGL2 particle data in WOTAN and this renderer is fixed-function GL 1.x, so the shader is written for this pipeline rather than pretending a copy. Verified: `make test-ar-grenade` (new, 30 assertions through the real `update_weapons` — grenade numbers, upward velocity, faster-than-missile speed, cooldown, both input bits against one cooldown, sniper zoom does not spend charges, non-AR ignores the bit, missile keeps gravity 0 and its own id), `make test-hammer` and `make test-brick-world` still pass after the signature changes, and the FX block type-checks standalone under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`. NOT verified: no live match, no GPU (no display/SDL2 here), so the shader and the glow's actual look are unproven, and net clients still render no projectiles at all (pre-existing: projectiles are not sent over the wire, so a grenade in a networked match is server-side only until that is built).
- **feat(lobby): NOCK is an APPS entry -- it starts the server and opens the editor.** The local map tools used to need another terminal (`make local-nock`) or a `.bat` before the browser editor was reachable; the APPS page now has a `NOCK` tile (`APP_NOCK`) that spawns the PARENA server itself and opens `http://127.0.0.1:8787/` in the system browser. Dev tree: `bin/local_nock_parena` with `--root <checkout>` (so saves land in `levels/` and get committed in this repo); packaged: `bundled/dw_nock{,.exe}` with `bundled/levels` + `bundled/tools/nock_editor.html`. The port is probed with a 100 ms non-blocking connect, so an already-running server (previous click, or the user's own `make local-nock`) is reused instead of double-started, and the tab opens only once the port answers (bounded 2 s) rather than racing the browser into a connection error. The server is spawned detached, so the editor keeps working after quitting the lobby; a failure is reported in the lobby footer instead of passing silently. The server grew `--port/--root/--repo/--levels/--editor` and `--help` for exactly this (flags win over `LOCAL_NOCK_*`, which still work), because a child's command line is one call on Windows while an environment block is not. Verified: both new functions compile clean standalone under `-std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` (that check caught two real defects first -- a `/*` inside a block comment and `-Wformat-truncation` on the path buffers, both fixed), `make test-local-nock-parena` 16/16, and a real `--root` run serving the level list, the editor page, a save that wrote `levels/cli_smoke.json` and committed it in a throwaway repo. Not verified from the real lobby here (no SDL2/display on this box) and Windows is not bundled yet.

belly instead of leaving a rocket that never runs out ---- */\n    {\n        BuggyState dry = flight(20.0f, 1);\n        dry.tank = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < 400; i++) simulate_buggy_state(&dry, 0.0f, 0.0f, SHANKPIT_NET_FIXED_DT, 1);\n        CHECK(dry.y < rocket_hover_height() + 0.5f, \"an empty tank still held it high: y=%.2f\", dry.y);\n        CHECK(dry.y >= BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE - 0.01f, \"an empty tank sank it through the floor: y=%.2f\", dry.y);\n        printf(\"PASS: an empty tank sits it down at %.2f and it does not sink through\\n\", dry.y);\n ## What changed

**Gadgets** (`packages/common/kit.h`): `BUGGY`, `ROCKET CAR`, `HELICOPTER` added as items, plus a fourth prefab **RUNNER** (`` ` `` BUGGY, `-` ROCKET CAR, `=` HELICOPTER, `C` canister) so all three are reachable without building a kit first. The other three prefabs are untouched, digits still never rebound.

**The call verb** (`packages/simulation/vehicle_call.h`): pressing the key spawns that vehicle 7 units ahead and seats you in it through the *existing* `buggy_try_enter` / helicopter occupant path — camera, chase steering, exit offsets, damage and draw code are the same code, not a second vehicle system. Refusals are real: not a call item, already driving, on the vehicle cooldown, or no free slot in this scene's garage (refusing beats recycling someone else's car).

**The rocket car**, honestly ported: BR's car is a 6-DOF thruster platform that drives walls and ceilings, which this chassis can't represent. What carried over is the part that makes it feel like that car — **one air tank pays for everything** (lift 26/s, boost 22/s, refills 34/s, 48/s on a surface, all straight from `br_phys.prn`), a rear-nozzle boost that scales with what's left in the tank, and a fan suspension holding the belly 2.6 units off the surface instead of riding wheels. Numbers live in a new PARENA mod `stdlib/shankpit/rocket_car_rules.prn`, generated to `packages/simulation/rocket_car_rules.c` (`make regen-rocket-car-rules`), installed by `rocket_car_rules_host.h` in both the lobby and the server. `BuggyState` gains `rocket`/`tank` appended after the `snap_*` client-local scratch fields; `simulate_buggy_state` routes to the new `simulate_rocket_car_state`.

**The look**: the box-built car this engine already draws, plus what makes a rocket car readable at distance — four additive lift-jet plumes underneath and a rear booster, brighter with the air left. I did not lift BR's mesh data; that's a modelling job, not a port.

## Checks actually run
- `make test-vehicle-call` (new) — buggy spawns ahead on −Z and seats you, second call honours the cooldown, rocket car arrives hovering with a full tank, helicopter arrives clear of ground and occupied, non-vehicle items and full garages refused, and the profile is measurably different: **9.06 vs 5.99 units/tick against the buggy over 240 ticks**, tank 134 under throttle, refilled to 9567 at idle, and an empty tank sits it down at 0.95 without sinking through.
- `make test-kit` — 14 slots, four prefabs, RUNNER's three calls, wrap-around cycling, pages.
- `phone_test` — PHONE TEST OK (kit count now 4).
- `make server` — links.
- `make check-windows` — 92/92 lobby sources compile for x86_64-w64-mingw32, so the `main.c` wiring and draw code are proven compiled (not just reviewed).

No kit-call packet: the keys are local/sandbox only and do nothing in `STATE_GAME_NET`, where the server owns spawning. No HUD readout of the air tank. BR's strafe/attitude jets and wall-driving are deliberately not ported (no axes for them here). Everything is uncommitted — say the word and I'll commit it.

#define CS_LEFT        96.0f
#define CS_RIGHT       1184.0f

static void draw_tyler_cutscene(CutsceneState *cs, unsigned int now_ms) {
    if (!cs || !cs->slides || cs->slide_count == 0) return;

    /* Full black background */
    glColor3f(0.044f, 0.047f, 0.056f);
    glRectf(0.0f, 0.0f, 1280.0f, 720.0f);

    /* Letterbox bars */
    glColor3f(0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
    glRectf(0.0f, 720.0f - CS_BAR_H, 1280.0f, 720.0f);
    glRectf(0.0f, 0.0f, 1280.0f, CS_BAR_H);

    /* Subtle top-bar separator line */

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn",
  "instructions": "Add the drone rules mod.",
  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn -- the two quadcopters (founder 2026-10-31: \"next we want to add\n;; more aircraft can we add a basic drone and a mini fly drone?\").\n;;\n;; The point of a drone next to the helicopter is that it has NO LAG: the heli's collective lever and\n;; airframe tilt take real ticks to become velocity, while a quadcopter just tilts its rotors and goes.\n;; So this mod is the airframe, and packages/simulation/drone_flight.h is the immediate-thrust loop:\n;;   RECON     a stable medium chassis that hovers and takes a knock\n;;   FLY       a 45 g micro that is hyper-responsive, fast, buffeted by weather, and bounces off walls\n;;             instead of stopping dead\n;;\n;; Scalar-only I32, fixed point, total functions, same convention as buggy_rules.prn and\n;; rocket_car_rules.prn: speeds in units/tick x 1000, response/grip in permille of full authority.\n;; The host clamps its own inputs. Retune here, `make regen-drone-rules`.\n(module shankpit/drone-rules)\n(export drone-mass-grams drone-response-permille drone-top-speed-milli drone-climb-milli\n        drone-yaw-rate-milli drone-drift-permille drone-bounce-permille drone-hull)\n(defn drone-kit [] : I32 0)   ; the mixer scale: 0 recon, 1 fly\n\n;; both kinds are \"< 1000 names, 2000 names\" -> keep the two profiles in one place\n(defn drone-mass-grams [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 45 2500))\n\n;; How hard the rotors answer: 650 is a balanced medium airframe, 1850 is a micro that snaps.\n(defn drone-response-permille [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 1850 650))\n\n;; Units/tick x 1000: 1.8 for the recon (slower than a buggy, it is a camera), 3.4 for the micro.\n(defn drone-top-speed-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 3400 1800))\n\n(defn drone-climb-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 1400 900))\n\n;; Degrees/tick x 1000.\n(defn drone-yaw-rate-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 2200 900))\n\n(defn clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n;; Weather drift, permille of buffeting: a recon feels a quarter of the storm, the 45 g micro feels\n;; twice it -- which is why you do not fly the little one through a tempest.\n(defn drone-drift-permille [(kind : I32) (storm : I32)] : I32\n  (clamp -4000 4000\n    (if (= kind 1)\n      (* (clamp 0 1000 storm) 2)\n      (/ (clamp 0 1000 storm) 4))))\n\n;; Hit the world: the recon stops dead (and loses a frame's worth of speed), the micro bounces, which\n;; is the only reason a 45 g drone survives a corridor.\n(defn drone-bounce-permille [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 350 0))\n\n(defn drone-hull [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 12 60))\n"
}

DRONE_FLY_HULL : DRONE_RECON_HULL;\n}\n\n/* drone_spawn_defaults -- one parked/hovering drone. y is caller-supplied because where \"the air\n * over this spot\" is depends on what it was called onto (vehicle_call.h decides). */\nstatic inline void drone_spawn_defaults(DroneState *d, int id, int scene_id, int kind,\n                                       float x, float y, float z, float yaw) {\n    memset(d, 0, sizeof(*d));\n    d->active = 1;\n    d->id = id;\n    d->scene_id = scene_id;\n    d->kind = (kind == DRONE_KIND_FLY) ? DRONE_KIND_FLY : DRONE_KIND_RECON;\n    d->x = x; d->y = y; d->z = z;\n    d->yaw = yaw;\n    d->health = (float)drone_hull(d->kind);\n    d->occupant_player_id = -1;\n}\n\nstatic inline DroneState *drone_find_nearby(int scene_id, float x, float y, float z, float radius) {\n    float rr = radius * radius;\n    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_DRONES; i++) {\n        DroneState *d = &local_state.drones[i];\n        if (!d->active || d->scene_id != scene_id) continue;\n        float dx = d->x - x, dy = d->y - y, dz = d->z - z;\n        if ((dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz) <= rr) return d;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic inline int drone_try_enter(PlayerState *p, DroneState *d) {\n    if (!p || !d || !d->active || d->occupant_player_id >= 0) return 0;\n    d->occupant_player_id = p->id;\n    p->in_vehicle = 1;\n    p->vehicle_type = VEH_DRONE;\n    p->x = d->x; p->y = d->y; p->z = d->z;\n    p->vx = p->vy = p->vz = 0.0f;\n    p->on_ground = 0;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* drone_try_exit -- put the pilot down beside the drone (it stays hovering where they left it, which\n * is the useful property of a camera you can park). */\nstatic inline int drone_try_exit(PlayerState *p, DroneState *d) {\n    if (!p || !d || d->occupant_player_id != p->id) return 0;\n    float r = -d->yaw * 0.0174532925f;\n    float offs[3][2] = { { cosf(r) * 1.6f, sinf(r) * 1.6f },\n                         { -cosf(r) * 1.6f, -sinf(r) * 1.6f },\n                         { 0.0f, 0.0f } };\n    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n        float px = d->x + offs[i][0];\n        float pz = d->z + offs[i][1];\n        float py = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, px, pz);\n        if (py < 0.0f) py = 0.0f;\n        if (!heli_point_collides(px, py + 1.0f, pz)) {\n            p->x = px; p->y = py; p->z = pz;\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    p->in_vehicle = 0;\n    p->vehicle_type = VEH_NONE;\n    p->on_ground = 1;\n    d->occupant_player_id = -1;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* drone_simulate_step -- one tick of a quadcopter.\n *   fwd/strafe   translational intent, -1..1, applied IMMEDIATELY through the airframe's response\n *                rate (this is the difference from the helicopter: no lever, no lean-then-move)\n *   ascend       +1 climb, -1 descend, 0 hold\n *   turn         yaw intent, -1..1, scaled by the airframe's own yaw rate\n *   storm        weather severity 0..1000; PARENA decides what each airframe does with it\n * An empty hand hovers: with no vertical intent the vertical velocity damps to nothing. */\nstatic inline void drone_simulate_step(DroneState *d, float fwd, float strafe, float ascend,\n                                       float turn, int storm, float dt) {\n    if (!d || !d->active) return;\n    if (fwd > 1.0f) fwd = 1.0f;\n    if (fwd < -1.0f) fwd = -1.0f;\n    if (strafe > 1.0f) strafe = 1.0f;\n    if (strafe < -1.0f) strafe = -1.0f;\n    if (ascend > 1.0f) ascend = 1.0f;\n    if (ascend < -1.0f) ascend = -1.0f;\n    if (turn > 1.0f) turn = 1.0f;\n    if (turn < -1.0f) turn = -1.0f;\n\n    float dt_scale = dt / 0.016f;\n    if (dt_scale < 0.0f) dt_scale = 0.0f;\n    if (dt_scale > 4.0f) dt_scale = 4.0f;   /* a stalled frame does not get to teleport it */\n\n    const int kind = d->kind;\n    const float resp = drone_response(kind);\n    const float top = drone_top_speed(kind);\n    const float climb = drone_climb_speed(kind);\n\n    d->yaw = norm_yaw_deg(d->yaw + turn * drone_yaw_rate(kind) * dt_scale);\n    float r = -d->yaw * 0.0174532925f;\n    float fx = sinf(r), fz = -cosf(r);\n    float rx = cosf(r), rz = sinf(r);\n\n    float wish_x = fx * fwd + rx * strafe;\n    float wish_z = fz * fwd + rz * strafe;\n    float wl = sqrtf(wish_x * wish_x + wish_z * wish_z);\n    if (wl > 1.0f) { wish_x /= wl; wish_z /= wl; }\n\n    float k = resp * dt_scale;\n    if (k > 1.0f) k = 1.0f;\n    d->vx += (wish_x * top - d->vx) * k;\n    d->vz += (wish_z * top - d->vz) * k;\n\n    float kv = resp * 0.85f * dt_scale;\n    if (kv > 1.0f) kv = 1.0f;\n    d->vy += (ascend * climb - d->vy) * kv;\n\n    /* the weather: buffeting scaled by the airframe's own drift rule */\n    int drift = drone_drift_permille(kind, storm);\n    if (drift != 0) {\n        d->flight_ticks++;\n        float t = (float)d->flight_ticks * 0.10f;\n        float buffet = (float)drift * 0.000004f;\n        d->vx += sinf(t) * buffet;\n        d->vz += cosf(t * 1.3f) * buffet;\n    } else {\n        d->flight_ticks++;\n    }\n\n    /* attitude follows what it is doing: nose down into its own motion, banked into a strafe. This is\n     * the read that makes a drone look like a drone instead of a floating brick. */\n    float pf = (top > 0.01f) ? (d->vx * fx + d->vz * fz) / top : 0.0f;\n    float rf = (top > 0.01f) ? (d->vx * rx + d->vz * rz) / top : 0.0f;\n    float ka = 0.25f * dt_scale;\n    if (ka > 1.0f) ka = 1.0f;\n    d->pitch += (-pf * 22.0f - d->pitch) * ka;\n    d->roll += (rf * 18.0f - d->roll) * ka;\n\n    d->rotor_angle += 55.0f * dt_scale;\n    if (d->rotor_angle > 360.0f) d->rotor_angle -= 360.0f;\n\n    float nx = d->x + d->vx * dt_scale;\n    float ny = d->y + d->vy * dt_scale;\n    float nz = d->z + d->vz * dt_scale;\n    if (heli_point_collides(nx, ny, nz)) {\n        float b = drone_bounce(kind);\n        if (b > 0.0f) {\n            /* the micro bounces: reverse a fraction of the speed it hit with */\n            d->vx = -d->vx * b;\n            d->vz = -d->vz * b;\n            if (d->vy < 0.0f) d->vy = -d->vy * b;\n        } else {\n            /* the recon stops dead -- it is a camera, and a camera does not ricochet */\n            d->vx *= 0.15f;\n            d->vz *= 0.15f;\n            d->vy *= 0.15f;\n        }\n    } else {\n        d->x = nx;\n        d->y = ny;\n        d->z = nz;\n    }\n    if (d->y < 0.05f) {\n        d->y = 0.05f;\n        if (d->vy < 0.0f) d->vy = 0.0f;\n    }\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_DRONE_FLIGHT_H */\n"
}

      "newString": "## 2026-10-31\n\n- **feat(aircraft): two quadcopters — a recon drone and a mini fly drone — with their own PARENA airframes.** Founder: *\"next we want to add more aircraft can we add a basic drone and a mini fly drone?\"* A drone sits beside the helicopter as a different airframe rather than a reskin: the heli's collective lever and airframe tilt take real ticks to become motion, while a quadcopter tilts its rotors and goes — **translational thrust hits velocity immediately**, which is exactly why you would fly one into a window the heli overshoots. static inline int heli_point_collides(float x, float y, float z) {
    for (int i = 1; i < map_count; i++) {
        Box b = map_geo[i];
        if (x > b.x - b.w * 0.5f && x < b.x + b.w * 0.5f &&
            y > b.y - b.h * 0.5f && y < b.y + b.h * 0.5f &&
            z > b.z - b.d * 0.5f && z < b.z + b.d * 0.5f) {
            return 1;
        }
    }
    return (y < 0.0f);
}
