Two quadcopters are in — a recon drone and a mini fly drone — built the same way as the buggy/rocket car/heli slice, with the numbers in PARENA.

## What changed

**`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn`** → generated `packages/simulation/drone_rules.c` (`make regen-drone-rules`), installed by `drone_rules_host.h`. Two profiles in one mod:

| | RECON | micro FLY |
|---|---|---|
| mass | 2500 g | 45 g |
| response | 650‰ | 1850‰ |
| top speed | 1.8 units/tick | 3.4 |
| yaw rate | 90°/tick | 220°/tick |
| storm drift | storm ÷ 4 | storm × 2 |
| on a wall | stops dead | bounces (350‰) |
| hull | 60 | 12 |

**`packages/simulation/drone_flight.h`** is the flight model, and the whole reason to have a drone beside the heli: the heli's collective and airframe tilt take ticks to become motion, while a quadcopter applies translational thrust **straight to velocity** — so it can stop and back into a window the heli overshoots. It also handles attitude (nose down into its own motion, banked into a strafe), rotor spin, weather buffeting, collision, and enter/exit.

**Wiring**: `DroneState` / `MAX_DRONES` / `VEH_DRONE` in `protocol.h`; drones tick in `local_game.h` beside the helicopters (a parked drone just hovers, so it works as a camera you leave somewhere); `KIT_ITEM_DRONE` / `KIT_ITEM_MINI_DRONE` in the kit with a fifth prefab **AERIAL** (`` ` `` DRONE, `-` MINI DRONE, `=` HELICOPTER, `C` BUGGY — same keys as RUNNER on purpose, since a kit is a key map); `vehicle_call.h` calls either kind; E dismounts *and* re-boards a parked drone; each is drawn as a body plus four spinning rotors at its own scale with a red (recon) or green (micro) nav light so they read apart at range. The storm the airframes feel is `g_sky_weather.storm` read once per frame into `drone_set_storm` — local, like the environment matrix.

## Two real defects the build caught
- **`clamp` collided at link.** PARENA emits a `defn` as a global C symbol, so the drone mod's `clamp` clashed with the rocket car's. Renamed and regenerated — worth remembering for every future `.prn` that wants a helper.
- **`drone_hull` called itself.** My header accessors shared names with the generated functions, so the rules table pointed back at the wrapper and ASan reported a 246-frame stack overflow. All flight-level accessors are now `df_*`.

## Checks actually run
- `make test-vehicle-call` — both kinds call, arrive occupied, keep their kind; **both move on tick one** (the property that separates them from the heli); micro outruns recon over 180 ticks (3.40 vs 1.80); the same 900‰ storm deflects the micro 0.014 vs the recon 0.003; against a real `map_geo` wall the micro bounces while the recon stops (3.17) and neither passes. All earlier buggy / rocket-car / helicopter checks still pass.
- `make test-kit` (five prefabs, AERIAL's four keys), `phone_test` (PHONE TEST OK), `make server` links clean, `make check-windows` compiles all 93 lobby sources for mingw.

## Not done, named
No gimbal/broadcast-camera link (the F3 idea needs a camera route this engine doesn't have), no hull damage from collisions or weapons, and drones aren't replicated in snapshots to remote clients. Everything is uncommitted.

      #ifndef SHANKPIT_BRICK_BODIES_H
      #define SHANKPIT_BRICK_BODIES_H
      
      /* brick_bodies.h -- falling cut-off geometry, FAKED cheaply. When a shot or blast leaves a piece of wall or
       * pane connected to nothing (packages/world/brick_fracture.h detach), it must not hang in the air: it
       * becomes one "chunk" that falls under gravity with a seeded tumble, bounces once, and lies flat on
       * whatever it lands on (the floor plane or a level box, found with one probe per chunk per tick), then
       * lingers a few seconds. No solver, no body-vs-body, no piling -- it only has to look right and cost almost
       * nothing (16 chunks max, one level scan each). Mass (material density x volume) is still carried so the
       * NOCK `density` setting means something to tooling and tests; it does not drive the motion.
       * Shot-out cells are NOT bodies any more: they shed the old cheap flakes (brick_debris.h).
       * Deterministic: fixed step, no rand, no wall clock. */
      
      #include "../goldenband/grb.h"
      
      #define BB_MAX            32           /* <= GRB_MAX_BODIES */
      #define BB_HZ             64
      #define BB_GRAVITY        30.0         /* level units/s^2 (a cell is 3 units): snappy, tunable */
      #define BB_SHARD_HALF     0.10         /* shard box half extent (m) */
      #define BB_MAX_AGE        20.0         /* seconds before a body is retired, however it is doing */
      #define BB_LINGER         5.0          /* seconds a landed chunk stays before it goes */
      
      /* kinds mirror BF_KIND_* (brick, concrete, wood, glass) */
      typedef struct {
          int active;
          int kind;
          int big;                           /* a chunk: no shard-vs-shard sphere contacts */
          double half[3];
          double calm, age;                  /* calm > 0: landed (seconds since) */
          int bounced;
          double settle_q[4], rest_y;
      } BbSlot;
      
      /* Static-geometry query: is the sphere (c, r) penetrating the level? 1 = yes, with the exit normal
       * and depth of the deepest overlap. */
      typedef int (*BbPushFn)(void *user, const double c[3], double r, double nrm[3], double *pen);
      
      typedef struct {
          GrbWorld world;
          BbSlot slot[BB_MAX];
          int cursor;
          double acc;
          BbPushFn push;
          void *user;
          double ground_y;
          unsigned int ticks;
      } BrickBodies;
      
      void bb_init(BrickBodies *bb, BbPushFn push, void *user);
      void bb_clear(BrickBodies *bb);
      /* Spawns a body (box of the given half extents) with `mass` kg, velocity and spin. Returns the slot or -1. */
      int bb_spawn(BrickBodies *bb, int kind, int big, double mass, const double pos[3], const double half[3],
                   const double vel[3], const double omega[3]);
      /* Advances by dt seconds in fixed 1/64 s ticks (catch-up capped at 2 ticks). */
      void bb_step(BrickBodies *bb, double dt);
      int bb_active_count(const BrickBodies *bb);
      double bb_slot_mass(const BrickBodies *bb, int slot);
      
      #endif

      /* ragdoll_pool.h -- a bounded, deterministic pool of rigid-body ragdolls for deaths (BIG_O ship-plan package W4;
       * founder real-time, 2026-10-01: "use rigidbody ragdoll physics" + "the models and animations available").
       *
       * WHAT THIS IS
       *   The XPBD rigid-body engine already exists: packages/goldenband/grb.{c,h} (6-DOF capsules, ball/hinge joints with swing/twist
       *   limits, plane contacts, 24 substeps) and packages/simulation/rigid_ragdoll.{c,h} (17 Winter/Dempster-mass segments on the
       *   mannequin skeleton assets/goldenband/mannequin_npc.gskel). What was missing, and this is, is everything around ONE ragdoll
       *   that a game needs to put them on screen at deaths: a fixed number of simultaneous bodies, spawning one from the victim's
       *   living pose, shoving it by what killed it, a fixed internal timestep with a catch-up cap, settle/freeze/fade/despawn timing,
       *   deciding WHICH body to give up when a new death arrives and the pool is full, collision against the static map, and handing
       *   the renderer a pose it can skin with the existing GOLDEN BAND path.
       *
       *   Every DECISION is PARENA (PARENA/stdlib/big_o/ragdoll_rules.prn, compiled to packages/simulation/ragdoll_rules.c): bone from
       *   hit height, impulse by weapon kind/damage/distance, per-segment share, caps, calm/freeze/despawn/fade timing, eviction
       *   priority. This host owns only arrays, the XPBD world, clocks and plumbing. The rules ABI is declared at the bottom of this
       *   header (and cross-checked against the generated file at compile time by `make test-ragdoll-pool`).
       *
       * UNITS AND FRAMES
       *   Metres, seconds, radians, y up, right-handed -- the mannequin skeleton is authored in metres and the lobby draws it unscaled,
       *   so SHANKPIT world units == metres here. The ragdoll is simulated directly in WORLD space; get_pose therefore returns a pose
       *   whose forward kinematics yields world-space joints (bake NO further model transform: use an identity npc_world when skinning).
       *   `facing_rad` is the exact value apps/lobby passes to gband_skel_npc_draw (a rotation about +Y, mat4_rotate_y convention:
       *   x' = x cos + z sin, z' = -x sin + z cos), so the ragdoll starts exactly where the living mesh was drawn.
       *
       * LIFECYCLE   FREE --spawn--> ACTIVE (simulated, 64 Hz) --calm long enough / max time--> FROZEN (pose held, fading) --hold over--> FREE
       *   Timings come from the PARENA rules per death kind (bullet / explosion / melee / environment); a body can never stay ACTIVE past
       *   its kind's maximum and never live past the absolute cap, so a jittery solve cannot leak a slot.
       *
       * DETERMINISM
       *   Same init + same spawn sequence + same dt sequence => bit-identical bodies and poses. No wall clock, no rand(), no threads, no
       *   floating-point state outside the pool; the time accumulator is integer microseconds. (Bit-identical on the same binary/CPU
       *   architecture, the same guarantee grb itself documents.) now_tick is stored for diagnostics only and never influences physics.
       *
       * MEMORY / THREADING
       *   No allocation after init, and none inside init either: the caller owns the RagdollPool (sizeof is ~1.5 MB at 8 slots -- make it
       *   static or heap, NEVER stack). One thread may call spawn/step/get_pose at a time: rigid_ragdoll.c keeps function-local static
       *   scratch for build/pose, which this pool does not own and cannot make re-entrant.
       *
       * NAMED v0 LIMITS (honest, not hidden)
       *   - Bodies collide with the ground plane (solved inside grb, with friction) and with a list/callback of static AABBs (solved here,
       *     once per 64 Hz tick AFTER the XPBD step: end- and mid-capsule spheres are pushed out, inward velocity removed, tangential
       *     velocity and spin damped). No body-vs-body and no limb-vs-limb collision (grb v0 has none), no continuous collision (a thin
       *     wall hit faster than ~0.1 m/tick can be tunnelled; the 40 m/s speed cap bounds it), no sleeping in grb (this pool freezes instead).
       *   - One skeleton per pool (the mannequin; rigid_ragdoll_build requires its joint names). Other character kits can be drawn with
       *     this pose only if the renderer retargets, which this package does not do.
       *   - A supplied animation pose that violates the ragdoll's own joint limits by more than RAGDOLL_POSE_MAX_VIOLATION_RAD is rejected
       *     and the default (rest pose, arms lowered) is used instead; stats.poses_rejected counts it.
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_RAGDOLL_POOL_H
      #define SHANKPIT_RAGDOLL_POOL_H
      
      #include <stdint.h>
      
      #include "rigid_ragdoll.h"
      
      /* Compile-time slot capacity (memory is sized for it); ragdoll_pool_init takes a runtime capacity <= this. PARENA's
       * ragdoll-default-pool-size is 8; the test asserts they agree. */
      #ifndef RAGDOLL_POOL_SLOTS
      #define RAGDOLL_POOL_SLOTS 8
      #endif
      
      #define RAGDOLL_BONE_COUNT 17        /* == rigid_ragdoll.c SEGMENTS[]; bone id == segment index (checked at init) */
      #define RAGDOLL_BONE_AUTO (-1)       /* RagdollSpawn.hit_bone: derive the bone from hit_type/height/lateral */
      #define RAGDOLL_TICK_HZ 64
      #define RAGDOLL_QUERY_CAP 32         /* >= ragdoll_query_max(); compile-time size of the per-body box scratch */
      #define RAGDOLL_WORLD_LIMIT 100000.0 /* spawn positions are clamped to +-100 km */
      #define RAGDOLL_POSE_MAX_VIOLATION_RAD 0.60  /* a supplied pose past this joint-limit violation is rejected (~34 deg) */
      
      /* Mirrors of the enumerations documented in ragdoll_rules.prn. */
      enum { RAGDOLL_KIND_BULLET = 0, RAGDOLL_KIND_EXPLOSION = 1, RAGDOLL_KIND_MELEE = 2, RAGDOLL_KIND_ENV = 3 };
      enum { RAGDOLL_STATE_FREE = 0, RAGDOLL_STATE_ACTIVE = 1, RAGDOLL_STATE_FROZEN = 2 };
      enum { RAGDOLL_HIT_UNKNOWN = 0, RAGDOLL_HIT_BODY = 1, RAGDOLL_HIT_HEAD = 2 };
      enum {
          RAGDOLL_BONE_PELVIS = 0, RAGDOLL_BONE_SPINE_01, RAGDOLL_BONE_SPINE_02, RAGDOLL_BONE_SPINE_03, RAGDOLL_BONE_NECK,
          RAGDOLL_BONE_UPPERARM_L, RAGDOLL_BONE_UPPERARM_R, RAGDOLL_BONE_LOWERARM_L, RAGDOLL_BONE_LOWERARM_R,
          RAGDOLL_BONE_HAND_L, RAGDOLL_BONE_HAND_R, RAGDOLL_BONE_THIGH_L, RAGDOLL_BONE_THIGH_R,
          RAGDOLL_BONE_CALF_L, RAGDOLL_BONE_CALF_R, RAGDOLL_BONE_FOOT_L, RAGDOLL_BONE_FOOT_R
      };
      
      /* ---- static world ---- */
      typedef struct { double min[3], max[3]; } RagdollAabb;
      
      /* Optional broadphase: fill `out` with up to max_out static boxes overlapping [lo, hi] and return how many (the pool clamps the
       * count and discards non-finite/inverted boxes, so a misbehaving callback cannot corrupt a body). */
      typedef int (*RagdollBoxQueryFn)(void *user, const double lo[3], const double hi[3], RagdollAabb *out, int max_out);
      
      typedef struct {
          double ground_y;                /* the floor plane (world y); handled inside grb with friction */
          const RagdollAabb *boxes;       /* BORROWED plain list scanned per body per tick (caller keeps it alive); NULL/0 = none */
          int box_count;
          RagdollBoxQueryFn query;        /* if non-NULL it is used INSTEAD of boxes/box_count */
          void *user;
      } RagdollWorld;
      
      /* ---- one death ---- */
      typedef struct {
          const float *pose_rot;   /* skeleton-local joint quaternions x,y,z,w, joint_count*4 (what gseq_player_sample_pose writes). NULL = rest pose, arms lowered. */
          const float *pose_trans; /* joint_count*3 local translations; ONLY the pelvis entry is read (bone offsets are rigid). NULL = rest. */
          double x, y, z;          /* world position of the model origin (the feet), exactly what the living mesh was drawn at */
          double facing_rad;       /* rotation about +Y, as passed to gband_skel_npc_draw */
          int kind;                /* RAGDOLL_KIND_* (out-of-range values are clamped, never trusted) */
          int damage;              /* killing-blow damage, clamped 0..400 */
          int hit_type;            /* RAGDOLL_HIT_*; head always loads the neck/head segment */
          int hit_bone;            /* 0..16, or RAGDOLL_BONE_AUTO to derive from hit_height_mm / hit_lateral_mm */
          int hit_height_mm;       /* hit point height above the soles in mm; < 0 = unknown (per-kind default bone) */
          int hit_lateral_mm;      /* mm off the centreline, + = the victim's anatomical left (+X in model space) */
          double dir[3];           /* world direction the force travels (shooter->victim, blast centre->victim); any length; zero/NaN = no shove
                                      (an explosion with no direction is thrown straight up) */
          int blast_dist_pm;       /* EXPLOSION only: distance from the blast centre / blast radius, permille (0 = centre) */
          double vel[3];           /* the victim's own world velocity at death, m/s (inherited per the rules' carry factor) */
          int local;               /* 1 = the local player caused or suffered it: strongly protected from eviction */
          uint32_t now_tick;       /* caller's tick, stored as spawn_tick for diagnostics */
      } RagdollSpawn;
      
      /* ---- pool ---- */
      typedef struct {
          int state;               /* RAGDOLL_STATE_* */
          int kind, local;
          uint32_t seq;            /* monotonically increasing spawn number (wraps; compared by unsigned difference) */
          uint32_t spawn_tick;
          int age;                 /* internal 64 Hz ticks since spawn */
          int calm_ticks;          /* consecutive calm ticks */
          int frozen_ticks;        /* ticks since the freeze */
          int fade_pm;             /* 1000 visible .. 0 gone (the rules' fade curve; 1000 while ACTIVE) */
          double spawn_pos[3];
          double tick_pos[RAGDOLL_BONE_COUNT][3];  /* every segment's pose at the end of the previous tick: the calm rule measures NET motion */
          double tick_rot[RAGDOLL_BONE_COUNT][4];
          RigidRagdoll rr;         /* the XPBD bodies */
      } RagdollSlot;
      
      typedef struct {
          uint32_t spawned;        /* successful spawns */
          uint32_t evicted;        /* residents given up for a newcomer */
          uint32_t refused;        /* newcomers that scored below every resident */
          uint32_t froze;          /* ACTIVE -> FROZEN */
          uint32_t despawned;      /* FROZEN/ACTIVE -> FREE by timer */
          uint32_t bad_kills;      /* bodies killed by the integrity guard (non-finite state, runaway position, torn joints) */
          uint32_t poses_rejected; /* supplied poses that violated the joint limits and were replaced by the default */
          uint32_t ticks_run;      /* fixed 64 Hz ticks simulated */
          uint32_t frames_clipped; /* host frames whose backlog exceeded the catch-up cap (the excess was dropped) */
      } RagdollPoolStats;
      
      typedef struct RagdollPool {
          const GSkel *skel;       /* borrowed; must outlive the pool */
          int capacity;            /* 1..RAGDOLL_POOL_SLOTS */
          int ready;               /* 1 after a successful init */
          int pelvis_joint, upperarm_joint[2];
          int64_t acc;             /* time accumulator in (microseconds * 64); one tick = 1 000 000 */
          uint32_t next_seq;
          RagdollWorld world;
          int viewer_set;
          double viewer[3];
          RagdollPoolStats stats;
          RigidRagdoll tmpl;       /* pristine copy every spawn starts from (so a reused slot is bit-identical to a fresh one) */
          RagdollSlot slots[RAGDOLL_POOL_SLOTS];
      } RagdollPool;
      
      typedef struct {
          int state, kind, local, age, frozen_ticks, fade_permille;
          int priority;            /* the PARENA eviction score right now (0 for FREE) */
          uint32_t seq, spawn_tick;
          double pelvis[3];        /* world position of the pelvis body */
      } RagdollInfo;
      
      /* Builds the template ragdoll on `skel` and verifies that segment ids match the skeleton's joint names. capacity <= 0 or above
       * RAGDOLL_POOL_SLOTS means all slots. Returns 1 on success; on 0 the pool is inert (every call is a no-op / -1). */
      int ragdoll_pool_init(RagdollPool *pool, const GSkel *skel, int capacity);
      
      void ragdoll_pool_set_world(RagdollPool *pool, const RagdollWorld *world);   /* copies the struct (box list/callback stay borrowed) */
      void ragdoll_pool_set_viewer(RagdollPool *pool, double x, double y, double z); /* the camera: far bodies are evicted first */
      
      /* Spawns a ragdoll. Returns its slot, or -1 when the pool is inert, the arguments are NULL, or the pool is full and the newcomer
       * scores below every resident (then nothing is evicted). Every field of *sp is sanitised: NaN/inf/huge values, bad quaternions,
       * out-of-range enums and unknown bones can never corrupt the simulation. */
      int ragdoll_pool_spawn(RagdollPool *pool, const RagdollSpawn *sp);
      
      /* Advances by a host frame of dt_ms milliseconds (NaN/negative -> 0, clamped to ragdoll_max_dt_ms). Runs whole fixed 1/64 s ticks
       * from an exact integer accumulator, at most ragdoll_max_catchup_ticks per call; a longer backlog is dropped, never queued. */
      void ragdoll_pool_step(RagdollPool *pool, double dt_ms);
      
      /* The pose the renderer feeds to the existing GOLDEN BAND skinning path (gpose_compute_skin_matrices / gpose_skin_mesh):
       * out_rot = joint_count*4 floats (skeleton-local quaternions x,y,z,w, same shape as gseq_player_sample_pose),
       * out_trans = joint_count*3 floats (rest translations, except the pelvis which carries the body's WORLD position, so the
       * forward kinematics lands in world space). Returns 1 for an ACTIVE/FROZEN slot, 0 otherwise (outputs untouched). */
      int ragdoll_pool_get_pose(const RagdollPool *pool, int slot, float *out_rot, float *out_trans);
      
      /* Convenience: get_pose followed by gpose_compute_skin_matrices. out must hold joint_count matrices (float[16], column-major);
       * they are world-space skin matrices -- draw with an identity model transform (no npc_world bake). */
      int ragdoll_pool_get_skin_matrices(const RagdollPool *pool, int slot, float out[][16]);
      
      int ragdoll_pool_info(const RagdollPool *pool, int slot, RagdollInfo *out);  /* 0 for an invalid slot */
      int ragdoll_pool_count(const RagdollPool *pool, int state);                  /* slots currently in `state` */
      void ragdoll_pool_clear(RagdollPool *pool);                                  /* frees every slot, resets the accumulator; keeps world/viewer/stats */
      
      /* ---- PARENA rules ABI (ragdoll_rules.c, generated from PARENA/stdlib/big_o/ragdoll_rules.prn) ----
       * Declared here so the integrator can call the unit conversions / weapon mapping directly, and so a drift between this list and
       * the generated file is a COMPILE error in the test (which includes both). */
      int ragdoll_body_mass_kg(void);
      int ragdoll_default_pool_size(void);
      int ragdoll_max_catchup_ticks(void);
      int ragdoll_max_dt_ms(void);
      int ragdoll_speed_cap_mmps(void);
      int ragdoll_omega_cap_mradps(void);
      int ragdoll_max_dv_mmps(void);
      int ragdoll_max_carry_mmps(void);
      int ragdoll_default_arm_drop_mrad(void);
      int ragdoll_max_pelvis_offset_mm(void);
      int ragdoll_max_spawn_lift_mm(void);
      int ragdoll_contact_friction_pct(void);
      int ragdoll_contact_omega_pct(void);
      int ragdoll_max_push_mm(void);
      int ragdoll_query_max(void);
      int ragdoll_clamp(int v, int lo, int hi);
      int ragdoll_kind(int k);
      int ragdoll_damage(int d);
      int ragdoll_bone(int b);
      int ragdoll_kind_from_weapon(int weapon);   /* SHANKPIT protocol.h WPN_* -> RAGDOLL_KIND_* */
      int ragdoll_standing_height_mm(void);
      int ragdoll_lateral_unit_mm(void);
      int ragdoll_height_permille(int dy_mm);
      int ragdoll_lateral_permille(int dx_mm);
      int ragdoll_default_bone(int kind);
      int ragdoll_bone_from_hit(int kind, int hit_type, int h_permille, int lat_permille);
      int ragdoll_impulse_mmps(int kind, int damage, int dist_pm);
      int ragdoll_falloff_permille(int kind, int dist_pm);
      int ragdoll_bone_gain_permille(int bone);
      int ragdoll_blast_share_permille(int bone);
      int ragdoll_spread_permille(int kind);
      int ragdoll_segment_share_permille(int kind, int hit_bone, int seg_bone);
      int ragdoll_dv_mmps(int mag, int share, int dir_pm);
      int ragdoll_lift_mmps(int kind, int mag, int share);
      int ragdoll_spin_mradps(int kind, int mag, int bone);
      int ragdoll_carry_permille(int kind);
      int ragdoll_calm_tick(int lin_mmps, int ang_mradps, int gap_mm);

      #ifndef SHANKPIT_BRICK_DEBRIS_H
      #define SHANKPIT_BRICK_DEBRIS_H
      
      /* brick_debris.h -- the cosmetic half of destructible brick: chunks that fly off a wall when a cell
       * cracks, tears or goes (packages/world/brick_fracture.h events). Client-only, render-side state;
       * the server never simulates any of it and nothing here can affect gameplay or the network.
       *
       * Papercraft look (PAPERCRAFT's Paper Engine): flat, irregular shards -- each chunk is a thin
       * flake with its own seeded size, spin and shade, not a clean cube. Deterministic by seed: the same
       * cell event always throws the same chunks, so two clients watching the same wall see the same
       * crumble.
       */
      
      #include <math.h>
      
      #define BRICK_DEBRIS_MAX 256
      
      typedef struct {
          int active;
          float x, y, z;
          float vx, vy, vz;
          float rx, ry, rz;      /* euler angles, degrees */
          float vrx, vry, vrz;   /* spin, degrees per second */
          float sx, sy, sz;      /* flake extents */
          float shade;           /* 0.7 .. 1.15 brick tint multiplier */
          float life;            /* seconds remaining */
      } BrickDebris;
      
      typedef struct {
          BrickDebris d[BRICK_DEBRIS_MAX];
          int cursor;            /* ring: the oldest chunk is recycled when the pool is full */
      } BrickDebrisPool;
      
      static inline unsigned int brick_debris_hash(unsigned int x) {
          x ^= x >> 16; x *= 0x7feb352dU; x ^= x >> 15; x *= 0x846ca68bU; x ^= x >> 16;
          return x;
      }
      static inline float brick_debris_r01(unsigned int *s) {
          *s = brick_debris_hash(*s + 0x9E3779B9u);
          return (float)(*s & 0xFFFFu) / 65535.0f;
      }
      
      static inline void brick_debris_clear(BrickDebrisPool *p) {
          for (int i = 0; i < BRICK_DEBRIS_MAX; i++) p->d[i].active = 0;
          p->cursor = 0;
      }
      
      /* brick_debris_spawn -- `count` flakes thrown from a cell centre (cx,cy,cz) of size (cw,ch,cd).
       * `seed` should identify the event (parent/key/state) so it is reproducible. */
      static inline void brick_debris_spawn(BrickDebrisPool *p, float cx, float cy, float cz,
                                            float cw, float ch, float cd, int count, unsigned int seed) {
          unsigned int s = brick_debris_hash(seed ? seed : 1u);
          float cell = cw;
          if (ch > cell) cell = ch;
          if (cd > cell) cell = cd;
          for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
              BrickDebris *b = &p->d[p->cursor];
              p->cursor = (p->cursor + 1) % BRICK_DEBRIS_MAX;
              b->active = 1;
              b->x = cx + (brick_debris_r01(&s) - 0.5f) * cw * 0.8f;
              b->y = cy + (brick_debris_r01(&s) - 0.5f) * ch * 0.8f;
              b->z = cz + (brick_debris_r01(&s) - 0.5f) * cd * 0.8f;
              float speed = 4.0f + brick_debris_r01(&s) * 9.0f;
              float ang = brick_debris_r01(&s) * 6.2831853f;
              b->vx = cosf(ang) * speed;
              b->vz = sinf(ang) * speed;
              b->vy = 3.0f + brick_debris_r01(&s) * 8.0f;
              b->rx = brick_debris_r01(&s) * 360.0f; b->ry = brick_debris_r01(&s) * 360.0f; b->rz = brick_debris_r01(&s) * 360.0f;
              b->vrx = (brick_debris_r01(&s) - 0.5f) * 720.0f;
              b->vry = (brick_debris_r01(&s) - 0.5f) * 720.0f;
              b->vrz = (brick_debris_r01(&s) - 0.5f) * 720.0f;
              float base = cell * (0.16f + 0.18f * brick_debris_r01(&s));
              b->sx = base * (0.8f + 0.5f * brick_debris_r01(&s));
              b->sy = base * (0.18f + 0.22f * brick_debris_r01(&s));   /* thin: a torn flake, not a cube */
              b->sz = base * (0.7f + 0.5f * brick_debris_r01(&s));
              b->shade = 0.7f + 0.45f * brick_debris_r01(&s);
              b->life = 1.6f + 1.2f * brick_debris_r01(&s);
          }
      }
      
      /* brick_debris_update -- gravity, drag, a bounce off the ground plane (y = 0), spin, expiry. */
      static inline void brick_debris_update(BrickDebrisPool *p, float dt) {
          if (dt > 0.1f) dt = 0.1f;
          for (int i = 0; i < BRICK_DEBRIS_MAX; i++) {
              BrickDebris *b = &p->d[i];
              if (!b->active) continue;
              b->life -= dt;
              if (b->life <= 0.0f) { b->active = 0; continue; }
              b->vy -= 38.0f * dt;
              b->x += b->vx * dt; b->y += b->vy * dt; b->z += b->vz * dt;
              b->rx += b->vrx * dt; b->ry += b->vry * dt; b->rz += b->vrz * dt;
              if (b->y < b->sy) {
                  b->y = b->sy;
                  if (b->vy < 0.0f) b->vy = -b->vy * 0.28f;
                  b->vx *= 0.7f; b->vz *= 0.7f; b->vrx *= 0.6f; b->vry *= 0.6f; b->vrz *= 0.6f;
              }
          }
      }
      
      static inline int brick_debris_active_count(const BrickDebrisPool *p) {
          int n = 0;
          for (int i = 0; i < BRICK_DEBRIS_MAX; i++) if (p->d[i].active) n++;
          return n;
      }
      
      #endif

      /* fx_spawn_explosion -- installed as g_fx_explosion_hook (physics.h), called by explode_splash for
       * every splash detonation. A ring buffer: a burst of simultaneous blasts cycles the slots instead of

      static void fx_spawn_explosion(float x, float y, float z, float radius, int weapon) {

> Write a self-contained summary.

Done: the shard kill and the gimbal, both driven by PARENA, both tested.

## Shards

**Rule** (`drone_rules.prn`, regenerated): `drone-shard-kills(kind, mass-grams, rel-speed-milli)`

- **Mini fly**: any shard with mass kills it — that's the point of flying a 45 g airframe through a collapsing building.
- **Recon**: needs `mass × relative speed > 40,000,000`, i.e. a 15 kg chunk doing ~2.7 units/tick (about what the top of a collapse moves). Dust and pebbles bounce off the frame.

**Host side** (`drone_flight.h`): `drone_shard_contact()` tests a shard's centre against the airframe's own radius (1.2 m recon, 0.35 m micro), asks the rule, and on a kill calls `drone_kill()` (retired, not `health -= n` — both are one-hit bodies) or `drone_eject_pilot()` (thrown clear where it died, falling).

**Wiring** (`main.c`): `drone_shard_sweep()` runs each frame over the live debris, converts each flake's per-second velocity into the per-tick flight model, estimates mass from the flake's own volume, ejects the pilot and fires a real fireball — 0.6 units for the micro, 1.6 for the recon.

One honest consequence, stated rather than buried: **the only live debris in this build is cosmetic** (`g_brick_debris`, the flakes a cracking wall throws). `BrickBodies`/GRB has no live instance in the lobby, so nothing in the current build can actually break a recon drone with a shard. The rule and the sweep are real and tested; the mass-bearing structural shards are not there yet.

## Gimbal

`drone-gimbal-yaw/pitch-milli` in PARENA: the recon's head swings **90°** with **60°** of pitch, the micro's 20°/25° — a gimbal is a mechanism, not free look. `drone_gimbal_track()` stores the offset from the airframe clamped to those limits; `drone_gimbal_view_yaw()` is airframe + head. `drone_gimbal_clamp()` in the mouse path means that while you pilot a drone the mouse drives its **head**, and the airframe keeps its own heading — which is what makes the recon a camera and not a plane.

`DroneState` gained `destroyed`, `gimbal_yaw`, `gimbal_pitch`.

## Checks run
- `make test-vehicle-call` — a shard 30 units away doesn't touch the micro; a 15 kg shard touching it does (and a dead drone can't be hit twice); a 15 g stationary shard leaves the recon alive while 15 kg at 3 units/tick breaks it; the pilot is ejected in place with `in_vehicle` cleared; the recon's gimbal clamps at its limits and follows exactly inside them while the micro's head moves far less. All earlier buggy / rocket-car / helicopter / drone checks still pass.
- `make test-kit`, `phone_test` (PHONE TEST OK), `make server` links, `make check-windows` compiles all 93 lobby sources for mingw — so the sweep and the gimbal clamp are proven compiled, not just reviewed.

Everything is uncommitted, and the two files that would make shards bite a recon (`BrickBodies`/GRB bringing a live mass-bearing debris pool into the lobby) are the obvious next slice.

  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/airplane_rules.prn -- the C-110 twin-prop transport (founder 2026-10-31: \"how about a\n;; basic prop plane c-110 or whatever the legendary ones are\").\n;;\n;; A fixed-wing aircraft is the one vehicle here that cannot hover, and that is the whole point: lift comes\n;; from AIRSPEED, so it has to be flown. It is not a helicopter with wings bolted on -- no lift below the\n;; stall speed, a runway before takeoff, a bank that turns it, and heavy inertia on everything.\n;;\n;; Units: the host's world is units/tick (60 Hz). Speeds cross this boundary in milli-units/tick, thrust and\n;; drag in milli-units/tick^2, lift in permille of the weight (1000 = exactly holding altitude at full\n;; angle of attack). Scalar-only I32, pure and total, same convention as the other vehicle mods.\n(module shankpit/airplane-rules)\n(export airplane-top-speed-milli airplane-stall-milli airplane-liftoff-milli airplane-thrust-milli\n        airplane-drag-milli airplane-lift-permille airplane-hull)\n\n;; 12 units/tick: the fastest thing in the game, and it needs the whole map to use it.\n(defn airplane-top-speed-milli [] : I32 12000)\n(defn airplane-liftoff-milli [] : I32 6000)\n\n;; Flaps buy a lower stall speed at the cost of drag -- the reason a loaded transport can use a short field.\n(defn airplane-stall-milli [(flaps : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= flaps 1) 3200 4000))\n\n(defn airplane-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n;; Full throttle is 60 milli-units/tick^2 (0.06). Against the drag curve below that settles near the top\n;; speed, and it puts the aircraft past the 6.0 liftoff speed in roughly two and a half seconds of roll.\n(defn airplane-thrust-milli [(throttle : I32)] : I32\n  (/ (* (airplane-clamp 0 1000 throttle) 60) 1000))\n\n;; Parasitic drag rises with speed; flaps add a flat penalty. This is what makes the takeoff run long.\n(defn airplane-drag-milli [(speed-milli : I32) (flaps : I32)] : I32\n  (+ (/ (* (airplane-clamp 0 20000 speed-milli) 5) 1000)\n     (if (= flaps 1) 12 0)))\n\n;; Wing lift, permille of weight. Zero at or below the stall speed however the nose is pointed -- a\n;; too-aggressive pitch at low speed does not save it, it just makes the dive uglier.\n;; d = airspeed above the stall; 1000 permille lands at d = 2000 (i.e. 6.0 units/tick clean), and the\n;; (d*d) term is the v^2 law. Angle of attack multiplies it, clamped so a full-stick zoom cannot\n;; invent lift it has not earned.\n(defn airplane-lift-permille [(speed-milli : I32) (flaps : I32) (aoa-permille : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= speed-milli (airplane-stall-milli flaps))\n    0\n    (airplane-clamp 0 1800\n      (/ (* (/ (* (- speed-milli (airplane-stall-milli flaps))\n                   (- speed-milli (airplane-stall-milli flaps))) 4000)\n            (airplane-clamp 0 2000 aoa-permille))\n         1000))))\n\n;; A transport that lands badly does not explode, it needs a new wing.\n(defn airplane-hull [] : I32 600)\n"

(g_airplane_rules && g_airplane_rules->hull) return g_airplane_rules->hull();\n    return AF_HULL;\n}\n\nstatic inline float af_ground_y(float x, float z) {\n    float gy = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, x, z);\n    if (gy < 0.0f) gy = 0.0f;\n    return gy + AF_TAXI_CLEARANCE;\n}\n\nstatic inline void airplane_spawn_defaults(AirplaneState *a, int id, int scene_id,\n                                          float x, float z, float yaw) {\n    memset(a, 0, sizeof(*a));\n    a->active = 1;\n    a->id = id;\n    a->scene_id = scene_id;\n    a->x = x;\n    a->z = z;\n    a->yaw = yaw;\n    a->y = af_ground_y(x, z);\n    a->health = (float)af_hull();\n    a->occupant_player_id = -1;\n    a->grounded = 1;\n}\n\nstatic inline AirplaneState *airplane_find_nearby(ServerState *st, int scene_id, float x, float y, float z, float radius) {\n    if (!st) return NULL;\n    float rr = radius * radius;\n    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_AIRPLANES; i++) {\n        AirplaneState *a = &st->airplanes[i];\n        if (!a->active || a->scene_id != scene_id) continue;\n        float dx = a->x - x, dy = a->y - y, dz = a->z - z;\n        if ((dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz) <= rr) return a;\n    }\n    return NULL;\n}\n\nstatic inline int airplane_try_enter(PlayerState *p, AirplaneState *a) {\n    if (!p || !a || !a->active || a->occupant_player_id >= 0) return 0;\n    a->occupant_player_id = p->id;\n    p->in_vehicle = 1;\n    p->vehicle_type = VEH_AIRPLANE;\n    p->x = a->x; p->y = a->y; p->z = a->z;\n    p->vx = p->vy = p->vz = 0.0f;\n    p->on_ground = a->grounded;\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic inline int airplane_try_exit(PlayerState *p, AirplaneState *a) {\n    if (!p || !a || a->occupant_player_id != p->id) return 0;\n    float r = -a->yaw * 0.0174532925f;\n    float ox = cosf(r) * 3.0f, oz = sinf(r) * 3.0f;\n    float px = a->x + ox, pz = a->z + oz;\n    float py = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, px, pz);\n    if (py < 0.0f) py = 0.0f;\n    p->x = px; p->y = py; p->z = pz;\n    p->in_vehicle = 0;\n    p->vehicle_type = VEH_NONE;\n    p->on_ground = py <= a->y + 0.5f;\n    a->occupant_player_id = -1;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* airplane_simulate_step -- one tick.\n *   elevator  -1..1  W/S   (nose down / nose up; no authority below the stall speed)\n *   aileron   -1..1  A/D   (roll; a bank is what actually turns a fixed wing)\n *   cam_yaw          the pilot's heading -- used as a tiller, ONLY while taxiing\n *   throttle_up/down      throttle is a LEVER (space raises, ctrl lowers), it holds where you leave it\n */\nstatic inline void airplane_simulate_step(AirplaneState *a, float elevator, float aileron,\n                                          float cam_yaw, int throttle_up, int throttle_down, float dt) {\n    if (!a || !a->active) return;\n    if (elevator > 1.0f) elevator = 1.0f;\n    if (elevator < -1.0f) elevator = -1.0f;\n    if (aileron > 1.0f) aileron = 1.0f;\n    if (aileron < -1.0f) aileron = -1.0f;\n    float dts = dt / 0.016f;\n    if (dts < 0.0f) dts = 0.0f;\n    if (dts > 4.0f) dts = 4.0f;\n\n    /* the lever */\n    if (throttle_up) a->throttle += AF_THROTTLE_RATE * dts / 60.0f;\n    if (throttle_down) a->throttle -= AF_THROTTLE_RATE * dts / 60.0f;\n    if (a->throttle < 0.0f) a->throttle = 0.0f;\n    if (a->throttle > 1000.0f) a->throttle = 1000.0f;\n\n    float airspeed = sqrtf(a->vx * a->vx + a->vy * a->vy + a->vz * a->vz);\n    int speed_milli = (int)(airspeed * 1000.0f);\n    int stall_milli = (int)(af_stall(a->flaps) * 1000.0f);\n\n    /* attitude. Above the stall the stick works; below it the wing is not flying and the nose falls --\n     * that is the whole failure mode, and it is not recoverable by pulling harder. */\n    if (speed_milli > stall_milli) {\n        a->pitch += elevator * 3.2f * dts;\n        a->roll += aileron * 5.0f * dts;\n    } else {\n        a->pitch -= 1.8f * dts;\n        a->roll *= 0.985f;\n    }\n    if (a->pitch > 32.0f) a->pitch = 32.0f;\n    if (a->pitch < -32.0f) a->pitch = -32.0f;\n    if (a->roll > 60.0f) a->roll = 60.0f;\n    if (a->roll < -60.0f) a->roll = -60.0f;\n\n    /* turning: a bank turns it; the tiller only works with the wheels down and slow */\n    a->yaw = norm_yaw_deg(a->yaw + a->roll * 0.05f * dts);\n    if (a->grounded && speed_milli < stall_milli * 2) {\n        float err = norm_yaw_deg(cam_yaw - a->yaw);\n        if (err > 180.0f) err -= 360.0f;\n        if (err < -180.0f) err += 360.0f;\n        if (err > 1.0f) err = 1.0f;\n        if (err < -1.0f) err = -1.0f;\n        a->yaw = norm_yaw_deg(a->yaw + err * 1.4f * dts);\n    }\n\n    float r = -a->yaw * 0.0174532925f;\n    float fx = sinf(r), fz = -cosf(r);\n\n    /* thrust along the nose, drag against the air it is moving through */\n    float along = af_thrust((int)a->throttle) - af_drag(speed_milli, a->flaps);\n    a->vx += fx * along * dts;\n    a->vz += fz * along * dts;\n\n    /* lift versus weight: 1000 permille holds altitude, so anything above it climbs and a stall falls */\n    int aoa = (int)(1000.0f + a->pitch * 10.0f);\n    int lift = af_lift_permille(speed_milli, a->flaps, aoa);\n    float lift_accel = (float)lift * 0.001f * AF_GRAVITY;\n    a->vy += (lift_accel - AF_GRAVITY) * dts;\n\n    /* propellers and the cached airspeed the HUD/tests read */\n    a->prop_angle += (35.0f + a->throttle * 0.045f) * dts;\n    if (a->prop_angle > 360.0f) a->prop_angle -= 360.0f;\n    a->airspeed = sqrtf(a->vx * a->vx + a->vy * a->vy + a->vz * a->vz);\n\n    /* the world */\n    float nx = a->x + a->vx * dts;\n    float nz = a->z + a->vz * dts;\n    float nose_x = nx + fx * 7.0f, nose_z = nz + fz * 7.0f;\n    if (heli_point_collides(nx, a->y, nz) || heli_point_collides(nose_x, a->y, nose_z)) {\n        /* a transport does not bounce off a wall, it stops and needs maintenance */\n        a->vx *= 0.08f;\n        a->vz *= 0.08f;\n        a->health -= 25.0f;\n        if (a->health < 0.0f) a->health = 0.0f;\n    } else {\n        a->x = nx;\n        a->z = nz;\n    }\n    a->y += a->vy * dts;\n    float ground = af_ground_y(a->x, a->z);\n    if (a->y <= ground) {\n        a->y = ground;\n        if (a->vy < 0.0f) a->vy = 0.0f;\n        a->grounded = 1;\n        a->pitch *= 0.85f;      /* sitting on the gear */\n        a->roll *= 0.85f;\n    } else {\n        a->grounded = 0;\n    }\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_AIRPLANE_FLIGHT_H */\n"

## The airframe

**`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/airplane_rules.prn`** → generated `packages/simulation/airplane_rules.c` (`make regen-airplane-rules`), installed by `airplane_rules_host.h`:

| | value |
|---|---|
| top speed | 12 units/tick — fastest thing in the game |
| stall | 4.0 clean, 3.2 with flaps |
| liftoff | 6.0 units/tick |
| thrust | 0.06 units/tick² at full throttle, against a speed-proportional drag curve |
| lift | v² law in permille of weight — **exactly 1000 at 6.0, exactly 0 at or below the stall** |

**`packages/simulation/airplane_flight.h`** is the integration, and it's deliberately not "the helicopter with wings": throttle is a **lever** (SPACE up, CTRL down, it holds where you leave it), W/S is elevator, A/D aileron, the pilot's heading is a tiller only with the wheels down and slow, and **a bank is what turns it**. Below the stall the stick has no authority and the nose falls — pulling back does not save it. It lands and taxis instead of exploding; a wall hit costs hull.

**Wiring**: `AirplaneState` / `MAX_AIRPLANES` / `VEH_AIRPLANE` in `protocol.h`, ticking in `local_game.h` beside the drones, called by `vehicle_call.h` **16 units ahead** (an 18-unit wingspan on your toes is a collision) on the ground with the lever closed, E boards and leaves it, and a sixth prefab **TRANSPORT** puts the C-110 on `` ` `` with helicopter / buggy / recon behind it. Drawn as a slab-sided transport — fuselage, high wing, tail, twin nacelles with counter-rotating props — so it reads as a plane from underneath, which is where players see it most.

## Two real failures the test caught

- **My test measured the runway after 900 ticks of flight** (6961 units). It now records the position at the tick it left the ground: **541 units**.
- **Flaps made takeoff longer** (265 ticks vs 229) — their drag penalty outweighed the lower stall. That's a genuine design error, fixed in PARENA: penalty 12 → 4, plus a real 15% flap lift bonus. Flaps now lift off 12 ticks earlier.

## Checks run
`make test-airplane-flight` — rolls then flies (liftoff tick 229 at 6.04 units/tick after 541 units), idle never leaves the ground, flaps lift off earlier, a stalled aircraft sinks with the nose falling at full back stick, lift is quadratic (250 → 1000 permille for 5.0 → 6.0) and zero below the stall, 10 ticks of full aileron banks 50° and turns only 13.8° — inertia. Plus `make test-vehicle-call` (the C-110 calls onto the ground ahead, lever closed, full health; all buggy/rocket-car/heli/drone checks still pass), `make test-kit` (six prefabs), `phone_test`, `make server` links, `make check-windows` compiles all 94 lobby sources for mingw.

## Not built, named rather than faked
**No cargo bay, no rear ramp, no airborne spawn, no cargo drops.** An interior `Level` that travels inside a moving hull is a much bigger piece than the plane, and I'd rather say so than ship a doorway that leads nowhere. Everything is uncommitted.

      [read_files: showing lines 790-849 of 1659. Use code_search to locate the part you need and read a window around it, or call read_files again with offset=850 to continue.]
- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_fx.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_fx.prn -- the cosmetics: particles, the flames, and the DYNAMIC LIGHT TABLE the renderer lights the
      ;; arena with. ON FIRE's "REALLY DRAMATIC LIGHTING EFFECTS" (founder, 2026-10-18) are built here.
      ;;
      ;; NOTHING HERE FEEDS THE SIM. This file reads the match (cars, ball, fires, the goal) and writes only its own records -- the
      ;; particles at part-base, the light table at lights-base, each car's fire-fx, the fire banner's clock -- and every die it rolls
      ;; is fx-rand (br_mem.prn), the cosmetic generator, never the sim's or the AI's. The fx dice are seeded from the match seed at
      ;; begin-match!, so a replayed match LOOKS the same as well as plays the same; but if they were seeded differently, the match
      ;; itself would still come out bit for bit the same (tests/br_fire_test.mjs checks both).
      ;;
      ;; fx-tick! runs once per sim tick (br_sim.prn: also during the frozen kickoff countdown, so the flames keep moving):
      ;;   the cars     each car's fire-fx (0..1, the renderer's flame size) swells fast when it catches fire and dies down slowly
      ;;                when it goes out; a burning car throws off flames, a boosting one a plume, one driving the dirt track
      ;;                (or drifting) a little dust
      ;;   the ball     alight (b-fire): flames off its surface, a comet's tail behind it
      ;;   particles    256 slots, a spawn ring that takes the first free slot of the next eight (else recycles the oldest-ish one);
      ;;                each lives `life` ticks: integrate (flames rise and shrink, plumes spread and slow, dust settles, sparks
      ;;                fall), age, die. The floor stops what falls; nothing else collides (they are only light and colour).
      ;;   the lights   rebuilt from scratch every tick, in priority order, up to 16: the goal flash, the burning ball, burning
      ;;                cars (flickering orange-white), boost plumes. Then the DRAMA scalar: it jumps up when someone is on fire or a
      ;;                goal goes in and ebbs away slowly after -- the renderer darkens the ambient and pushes the contrast with it.
      ;;
      ;; The light table's layout is in br_mem.prn's memory map (LIGHTS, 0x029000). Light colours are 0..1 per channel; intensity is in
      ;; "a car's worth" (a burning car flickers between about 1.4 and 2.4, the goal flash starts at 9); a light reaches out to its
      ;; radius and no further (a renderer might take colour * intensity * (1 - d / radius)^2).
      
      ;; ---- the constants ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn fx-flash-ticks [] : I32 63)       ; the goal flash lasts ~1 s
      (defn fx-flash-power [] : F32 9.0)      ; ... starts this bright (a burning car is ~2) and falls off as the square of what is left
      (defn fx-flash-radius [] : F32 900.0)   ; ... lighting most of the arena at first, shrinking to 45% of it
      (defn fx-flash-y [] : F32 205.0)        ; ... from just under the mouth of the tower's shaft
      (defn fx-sparks [] : I32 40)            ; sparks sprayed down out of the shaft by a goal
      (defn fx-fire-rise [] : F32 0.25)       ; fire-fx swells this much of the way to 1 each tick on catching fire ...
      (defn fx-fire-fall [] : F32 0.06)       ; ... and dies down this much of the way to 0 once out
      (defn fx-drama-rise [] : F32 0.2)       ; the drama jumps up ...
      (defn fx-drama-fall [] : F32 0.025)     ; ... and ebbs away (a time constant of ~0.6 s)
      
      ;; particle kinds
      (defn pk-fire [] : I32 1)
      (defn pk-plume [] : I32 2)
      (defn pk-dust [] : I32 3)
      (defn pk-spark [] : I32 4)
      
      ;; ---- the light table ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn lt-count-addr [] : I32 (lights-base))
      (defn lt-drama-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 4))
      (defn lt-flash-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 8))
      (defn lt-tick-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 12))
      (defn lt-flash-t-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 16))
      (defn lt-flash-tower-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 20))
      (defn lt-flash-team-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 24))
      (defn lt-addr [(i : I32)] : I32 (+ (+ (lights-base) 32) (* i 32)))
      (defn lt-words [] : I32 136)             ; header 8 + 16 lights x 8
      
      (defn light-count [] : I32 (load32 (lt-count-addr)))
      (defn drama-level [] : F32 (loadf32 (lt-drama-addr)))
      
      ;; one more light, if there is room
      (defn light! [(x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32) (cr : F32) (cg : F32) (cb : F32) (power : F32) (radius : F32)] : Unit
        (let [n (light-count)]
          (when (< n (max-lights))
            (let [a (lt-addr n)]
              (storef32! a x) (storef32! (+ a 4) y) (storef32! (+ a 8) z)
              (storef32! (+ a 12) cr) (storef32! (+ a 16) cg) (storef32! (+ a 20) cb)
              (storef32! (+ a 24) power) (storef32! (+ a 28) radius)
              (store32! (lt-count-addr) (+ n 1))))))
      
      ;; a channel of an engine colour (0xAABBGGRR), as 0..1: shift 0 red, 8 green, 16 blue
      (defn chan-f [(c : I32) (sh : I32)] : F32 (/ (f32 (bit-and (shr c sh) 255)) 255.0))
      
      ;; ---- the particles ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; the first free slot among the next eight from the ring's cursor; none free: the one at the cursor is recycled
      (defn part-slot [] : I32
        (let [h (gi (g-part-head))]
          (loop [i 0]
            (cond (>= i 8) (bit-and h 255)
                  (= (f-ttl (bit-and (+ h i) 255)) 0) (bit-and (+ h i) 255)
                  :else (recur (+ i 1))))))
      
      (defn part! [(kind : I32) (ttl : I32) (col : I32) (x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32) (vx : F32) (vy : F32) (vz : F32) (size : F32)] : Unit
        (let [q (part-slot)]
          (gi! (g-part-head) (bit-and (+ q 1) 255))
          (set-f-ttl! q ttl) (set-f-life! q ttl) (set-f-kind! q kind) (set-f-color! q col)
          (set-f-x! q x) (set-f-y! q y) (set-f-z! q z)
          (set-f-vx! q vx) (set-f-vy! q vy) (set-f-vz! q vz)
          (set-f-size! q size)))
      
      ;; a flame's colour: orange to yellow, now and then a white-hot core
      (defn fire-col [] : I32
        (if (= (fx-rnd 6) 0) (rgb 255 244 214) (rgb 255 (+ 120 (fx-rnd 110)) (+ 24 (fx-rnd 50)))))
      
      ;; one tick of every live particle: flames rise (they are hot) and shrink, plumes spread and slow, dust settles, sparks fall
      (defn parts-tick! [] : Unit
        (let [(live : I32) 0 (dt : F32) (tick-dt)]
          (dotimes [q 256]
            (when (> (f-ttl q) 0)
              (let [k (f-kind q)
                    (ay : F32) (case k 1 70.0 2 0.0 3 -30.0 -66.0)
                    (drag : F32) (case k 1 2.5 2 4.0 3 1.5 0.6)
                    (dr : F32) (fmax2 0.0 (- 1.0 (* drag dt)))
                    (vx : F32) (* (f-vx q) dr)
                    (vy : F32) (* (+ (f-vy q) (* ay dt)) dr)
                    (vz : F32) (* (f-vz q) dr)
                    (y : F32) (+ (f-y q) (* vy dt))]
                (set-f-vx! q vx) (set-f-vz! q vz)
                (set-f-x! q (+ (f-x q) (* vx dt)))
                (set-f-z! q (+ (f-z q) (* vz dt)))
                ;; the floor stops what falls (dust and sparks skid along it)
                (if (< y 1.0)
                    (do (set-f-y! q 1.0) (set-f-vy! q 0.0))
                    (do (set-f-y! q y) (set-f-vy! q vy)))
                (set-f-size! q (case k 1 (* (f-size q) 0.96) 2 (+ (f-size q) 0.3) 3 (+ (f-size q) 0.12) (f-size q)))
                (set-f-ttl! q (- (f-ttl q) 1))
                (when (> (f-ttl q) 0) (set! live (+ live 1))))))
          (gi! (g-part-live) live)))
      
      ;; ---- the cars ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn fx-car! [(s : I32)] : Unit
        (let [(want : F32) (if (on-fire? s) 1.0 0.0)
              (ff0 : F32) (c-fire-fx s)
              (ff1 : F32) (+ ff0 (* (- want ff0) (if (> want ff0) (fx-fire-rise) (fx-fire-fall))))
              (ff : F32) (if (< ff1 0.002) 0.0 ff1)
              (sp : F32) (len3 (c-vx s) (c-vy s) (c-vz s))]
          (set-c-fire-fx! s ff)
          ;; flames: up to two a tick, off the body and licking up away from it; they keep only half the car's speed, so a car on the
          ;; move drags a tail of fire behind it
          (dotimes [i 2]
            (when (< (fx-rand-unit) ff)
              (let [(a : F32) (* 4.5 (fx-rand-f)) (b : F32) (* 7.5 (fx-rand-f)) (c : F32) (+ 2.0 (* 3.0 (fx-rand-unit)))
                    (up : F32) (+ 18.0 (* 22.0 (fx-rand-unit)))
                    (jx : F32) (* 14.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jy : F32) (* 8.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jz : F32) (* 14.0 (fx-rand-f))]
                (part! (pk-fire) (+ 16 (fx-rnd 12)) (fire-col)
                       (+ (c-x s) (+ (* (c-rx s) a) (+ (* (c-fx s) b) (* (c-ux s) c))))
                       (+ (c-y s) (+ (* (c-ry s) a) (+ (* (c-fy s) b) (* (c-uy s) c))))
                       (+ (c-z s) (+ (* (c-rz s) a) (+ (* (c-fz s) b) (* (c-uz s) c))))
                       (+ (* 0.5 (c-vx s)) (+ (* (c-ux s) up) jx))
                       (+ (* 0.5 (c-vy s)) (+ (* (c-uy s) up) jy))
                       (+ (* 0.5 (c-vz s)) (+ (* (c-uz s) up) jz))
                       (+ 3.5 (* 2.5 (fx-rand-unit)))))))
          ;; the boost plume, out of the rear nozzle and back along the car (a burning car's plume burns too)
          (when (and (> (c-boost-fx s) 0.25) (< (fx-rand-unit) (* 0.7 (c-boost-fx s))))
            (let [(back : F32) (+ 140.0 (* 40.0 (fx-rand-unit)))
                  (jx : F32) (* 10.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jy : F32) (* 10.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jz : F32) (* 10.0 (fx-rand-f))]
              (part! (pk-plume) (+ 12 (fx-rnd 7)) (if (on-fire? s) (rgb 255 150 60) (rgb 196 222 255))
                     (- (c-x s) (* (c-fx s) 8.0)) (- (c-y s) (* (c-fy s) 8.0)) (- (c-z s) (* (c-fz s) 8.0))
                     (+ (- (c-vx s) (* (c-fx s) back)) jx) (+ (- (c-vy s) (* (c-fy s) back)) jy) (+ (- (c-vz s) (* (c-fz s) back)) jz)
                     2.5)))
          ;; dust: kicked up behind the rear wheels by a car driving the dirt track, or drifting anywhere on the floor, in the floor's
          ;; own colour
          (when (and (= (c-attached s) 1) (> (c-uy s) 0.7)
                     (or (and (> sp 60.0) (> (road-at (c-x s) (c-z s)) 128)) (> (c-slip s) 50.0))
                     (< (fx-rand-unit) 0.35))
            (let [(rx : F32) (* 4.0 (fx-rand-f))
                  (x : F32) (- (+ (c-x s) (* (c-rx s) rx)) (* (c-fx s) 7.0))
                  (z : F32) (- (+ (c-z s) (* (c-rz s) rx)) (* (c-fz s) 7.0))]
              (part! (pk-dust) (+ 30 (fx-rnd 16)) (mix (tex-color (tex-ix x) (tex-iz z)) (rgb 200 190 170) 90)
                     x (+ (c-y s) 1.0) z
                     (+ (* 0.2 (c-vx s)) (* 15.0 (fx-rand-f))) (+ 10.0 (* 8.0 (fx-rand-unit))) (+ (* 0.2 (c-vz s)) (* 15.0 (fx-rand-f)))
                     3.0)))))
      
      ;; the ball alight: flames off its surface, and since they keep less than half its speed, a comet's tail behind it
      (defn fx-ball! [] : Unit
        (when (> (b-fire) 0)
          (dotimes [i 2]
            (let [(ox : F32) (* 9.0 (fx-rand-f)) (oy : F32) (* 9.0 (fx-rand-f)) (oz : F32) (* 9.0 (fx-rand-f))]
              (part! (pk-fire) (+ 14 (fx-rnd 9)) (fire-col)
                     (+ (b-x) ox) (+ (b-y) oy) (+ (b-z) oz)
                     (+ (* 0.4 (b-vx)) (* 2.0 ox)) (+ (+ (* 0.4 (b-vy)) (* 2.0 oy)) 25.0) (+ (* 0.4 (b-vz)) (* 2.0 oz))
                     (+ 4.0 (* 3.0 (fx-rand-unit))))))))
      
      ;; ---- a goal: the tower goes up ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; called by on-goal! (br_rules.prn): the flash (in the light table's header, burnt down by lights-tick!) and a spray of sparks in
      ;; the scorer's colour, down out of the mouth of the shaft into the arena
      (defn fx-goal! [(tower : I32) (team : I32)] : Unit
        (let [col (team-color team)]
          (store32! (lt-flash-t-addr) (fx-flash-ticks))
          (store32! (lt-flash-tower-addr) tower)
          (store32! (lt-flash-team-addr) team)
          (dotimes [i (fx-sparks)]
            (let [(ang : F32) (* 6.2831855 (fx-rand-unit))
                  (out : F32) (* 200.0 (fx-rand-unit))]
              (part! (pk-spark) (+ 40 (fx-rnd 30)) (if (= (fx-rnd 4) 0) (rgb 255 250 236) col)
                     (+ (tw-x tower) (* 20.0 (fx-rand-f))) (- (a-h) 6.0) (+ (tw-z tower) (* 20.0 (fx-rand-f)))
                     (* (cosf ang) out) (- 0.0 (+ 40.0 (* 180.0 (fx-rand-unit)))) (* (sinf ang) out)
                     (+ 1.5 (fx-rand-unit)))))))
      
      ;; ---- the lights and the drama -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn lights-tick! [] : Unit
        (let [ft (load32 (lt-flash-t-addr))
              (target : F32) 0.0]
          (store32! (lt-count-addr) 0)
          (store32! (lt-tick-addr) (gi (g-tick)))
          ;; 1. the goal flash: white-hot as the ball goes in, settling into the scorer's colour as it dies (with the square of what is
          ;;    left, so it is a flash, not a glow)
          (if (> ft 0)
              (let [(k : F32) (/ (f32 ft) (f32 (fx-flash-ticks)))
                    tw (load32 (lt-flash-tower-addr))
                    c (team-color (load32 (lt-flash-team-addr)))
                    (w : F32) (* 0.6 k)]
                (light! (tw-x tw) (fx-flash-y) (tw-z tw)
                        (lerp (chan-f c 0) 1.0 w) (lerp (chan-f c 8) 1.0 w) (lerp (chan-f c 16) 1.0 w)
                        (* (fx-flash-power) (* k k)) (* (fx-flash-radius) (+ 0.45 (* 0.55 k))))
                (storef32! (lt-flash-addr) k)
                (store32! (lt-flash-t-addr) (- ft 1))
                (set! target (fmax2 target (+ 0.5 (* 0.5 k)))))
              (storef32! (lt-flash-addr) 0.0))
          ;; 2. the burning ball
          (when (> (b-fire) 0)
            (let [(fl : F32) (fx-rand-unit)]
              (light! (b-x) (b-y) (b-z) 1.0 (+ 0.55 (* 0.25 fl)) (+ 0.16 (* 0.2 fl)) (+ 2.2 (* 0.9 fl)) (+ 170.0 (* 40.0 fl)))
              (set! target (fmax2 target 0.75))))
          ;; 3. the burning cars: orange, flickering toward white as they flare
          (dotimes [s 12]
            (when (and (!= (c-active s) 0) (> (c-fire-fx s) 0.03))
              (let [(fl : F32) (fx-rand-unit) (ff : F32) (c-fire-fx s)]
                (light! (+ (c-x s) (* (c-ux s) 5.0)) (+ (c-y s) (* (c-uy s) 5.0)) (+ (c-z s) (* (c-uz s) 5.0))
                        1.0 (+ 0.5 (* 0.3 fl)) (+ 0.12 (* 0.25 (* fl fl)))
                        (* ff (+ 1.4 fl)) (+ 130.0 (* 50.0 fl)))
                (when (on-fire? s) (set! target (fmax2 target 0.6))))))
          ;; 4. the boost plumes (in slot order, while there is room): a cold blue-white, or fire for a burning car
          (dotimes [s 12]
            (when (and (!= (c-active s) 0) (> (c-boost-fx s) 0.2))
              (let [hot (on-fire? s)]
                (light! (- (c-x s) (* (c-fx s) 10.0)) (- (c-y s) (* (c-fy s) 10.0)) (- (c-z s) (* (c-fz s) 10.0))
                        (if hot 1.0 0.55) (if hot 0.5 0.75) (if hot 0.15 1.0)
                        (* 0.9 (c-boost-fx s)) 70.0))))
          ;; the slots not used this tick are zeroed, so a renderer that reads all sixteen sees nothing in them
          (loop [i (light-count)]
            (when (< i (max-lights))
              (zero-words! (lt-addr i) 8)
              (recur (+ i 1))))
          ;; the drama: a dead ball after a goal holds it up a little; it jumps to its target and ebbs away from it
          (when (> (gi (g-goal-t)) 0) (set! target (fmax2 target 0.45)))
          (let [(d : F32) (drama-level)]
            (storef32! (lt-drama-addr)
                       (clamp-f (+ d (* (- target d) (if (> target d) (fx-drama-rise) (fx-drama-fall)))) 0.0 1.0)))))
      
      ;; ---- once per tick ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn fx-tick! [] : Unit
        (do
          (dotimes [s (max-cars)] (when (!= (c-active s) 0) (fx-car! s)))
          (fx-ball!)
          (parts-tick!)
          (lights-tick!)
          (when (> (gi (g-fire-ann-t)) 0) (gi! (g-fire-ann-t) (- (gi (g-fire-ann-t)) 1)))
          ;; the overtime and ball-reset banners (rules set g-banner-t; the HUD is the only reader, so it is counted down here)
          (when (> (gi (g-banner-t)) 0) (gi! (g-banner-t) (- (gi (g-banner-t)) 1)))))
      
      ;; a new match: no particles, no lights, the dice seeded from the match seed
      (defn fx-reset! [(seed : I32)] : Unit
        (do
          (gi! (g-rng2) (+ (* seed 31) 9001))
          (zero-words! (part-base) (* (max-parts) 16))
          (zero-words! (lights-base) (lt-words))
          (gi! (g-part-head) 0) (gi! (g-part-live) 0)
          (gi! (g-fire-ann-id) 0) (gi! (g-fire-ann-slot) -1) (gi! (g-fire-ann-why) 0) (gi! (g-fire-ann-t) 0)))
