      <body>
      <aside>
        <h1>local NOCK <span>maps as code</span></h1>
      
        <h2>Levels</h2>
        <ul id="levels"><li class="dim">loading…</li></ul>
        <div class="row">
          <button id="newBtn">New level</button>
          <button id="saveBtn">Save + commit</button>
        </div>
        <div id="saveInfo" class="dim"></div>
      
        <h2>Tools</h2>
        <div class="row">
          <button data-tool="add" class="on">Box</button>
          <button data-tool="delete">Erase</button>
          <button data-tool="spawner">Spawner</button>
        </div>
      
        <h2>Live session</h2>
        <div class="row">
          <button id="startBtn">Start</button>
          <button id="joinBtn">Join</button>
        </div>
        <input id="sessionId" placeholder="session id (paste from the game)">
        <div id="sessionInfo" class="dim"></div>
      
        <h2>Game side</h2>
        <div id="note"></div>
      
        <h2>Log</h2>
        <div id="log"></div>
      </aside>
      
      <main><canvas id="canvas"></canvas></main>
      
      <script>
      "use strict";
      
      const SESSION_BASE = "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions";
      const el = id => document.getElementById(id);
      const canvas = el("canvas"), ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
      
      const state = {
        level: null, name: null, tool: "add",
        session: null, since: 0, polling: false, pollGen: 0,
        remote: null,          // {x, z, yaw} of the in-game character
        undo: [], dirty: false, pushTimer: null,
      };
      
      function log(msg) {
        const t = new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
        el("log").textContent = `[${t}] ${msg}\n` + el("log").textContent;
      }
      
      async function api(method, path, body) {
        const res = await fetch(path, {
          method,
          headers: body === undefined ? {} : { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
          body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
        });
        const text = await res.text();
        let json = null;
        try { json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null; } catch { /* plain text */ }
        if (!res.ok) throw new Error((json && json.error) || `${res.status} ${res.statusText}`);
        return json;
      }
      
      /* ---------- level list / loading ---------- */
      
      async function loadLevelList() {
        const box = el("levels");
        try {
          const { levels } = await api("GET", "/api/levels");
          box.innerHTML = "";
          if (!levels.length) { box.innerHTML = '<li class="dim">no levels yet — press New</li>'; return; }
          for (const l of levels) {
            const li = document.createElement("li");
            li.dataset.name = l.name;
            li.innerHTML = `<span>${l.name}</span><span class="dim">${l.walls} walls</span>`;
            if (l.name === state.name) li.classList.add("sel");
            li.onclick = () => openLevel(l.name);
            box.appendChild(li);
          }
        } catch (e) {
          box.innerHTML = `<li class="dim">cannot list: ${e.message}</li>`;
        }
      }
      
      async function openLevel(name) {
        try {
          const doc = await api("GET", "/api/levels/" + encodeURIComponent(name));
          setLevel(doc, name);
          log(`opened ${name} (${(doc.walls || []).length} walls)`);
        } catch (e) { log("open failed: " + e.message); }
      }
      
      function setLevel(doc, name) {
        state.level = ensureShape(doc);
        state.name = name || state.level.name || "untitled";
        state.level.name = state.name;
        state.undo = [];
        state.dirty = false;
        draw();
        loadLevelList();
        pushDraftSoon();
      }
      
      function ensureShape(doc) {
        doc = doc && typeof doc === "object" ? doc : {};
        doc.name = doc.name || "untitled";
        doc.width = doc.width || 200; doc.height = doc.height || 50; doc.depth = doc.depth || 200;
        if (!Array.isArray(doc.walls)) doc.walls = [];
        if (typeof doc.ground_plane_enabled !== "boolean") doc.ground_plane_enabled = true;
        doc.ground_plane_squares = doc.ground_plane_squares || 16;
        if (!Array.isArray(doc.materials) || !doc.materials.length) {
          doc.materials = [{ name: "brick", shader_name: "standard", specular: 0.04, shininess: 6, friction: 0.3 }];
        }
        if (!Array.isArray(doc.spawners)) doc.spawners = [];
        if (!doc.spawners.length) {
          doc.spawners.push({ id: 1, x: 0, y: 1, z: 0, yaw: 0, team: -1 });
        }
        return doc;
      }
      
      function newLevel() {
        const name = (prompt("new level name", "untitled") || "").trim();
        if (!name) return;
        if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(name)) { alert("letters, digits, - and _ only"); return; }
        setLevel({ name, width: 200, height: 50, depth: 200, ground_plane_enabled: true,
                   ground_plane_squares: 16, walls: [], materials: [], spawners: [] }, name);
        log(`new level ${name} — click to place boxes, then Save`);
      }
      
      /* ---------- canvas ---------- */
      
      function bounds() {
        const w = state.level ? state.level.walls : [];
        if (!w.length) return { minx: -30, maxx: 30, minz: -30, maxz: 30 };
        let minx = 1e9, maxx = -1e9, minz = 1e9, maxz = -1e9;
        for (const b of w) {
          const hx = Math.abs(b.sx) / 2, hz = Math.abs(b.sz) / 2;
          minx = Math.min(minx, b.x - hx); maxx = Math.max(maxx, b.x + hx);
          minz = Math.min(minz, b.z - hz); maxz = Math.max(maxz, b.z + hz);
        }
        const pad = 4;
        return { minx: minx - pad, maxx: maxx + pad, minz: minz - pad, maxz: maxz + pad };
      }
      
      function view() {
        const g = bounds();
        const sx = canvas.width / Math.max(1, g.maxx - g.minx);
        const sz = canvas.height / Math.max(1, g.maxz - g.minz);
        const s = Math.min(sx, sz);
        const ox = (canvas.width - (g.maxx - g.minx) * s) / 2;
        const oz = (canvas.height - (g.maxz - g.minz) * s) / 2;
        return { g, s, toPx: (x, z) => [ox + (x - g.minx) * s, oz + (z - g.minz) * s],
                 toWorld: (px, pz) => [g.minx + (px - ox) / s, g.minz + (pz - oz) / s] };
      }
      
      function draw() {
        const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
        const w = canvas.clientWidth * dpr, h = canvas.clientHeight * dpr;
        if (canvas.width !== w || canvas.height !== h) { canvas.width = w; canvas.height = h; }
        ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);
        ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
        if (!state.level) {
          ctx.fillStyle = "#7f8794";
          ctx.font = `${13 * dpr}px monospace`;
          ctx.fillText("pick a level, or press New level", 20 * dpr, 30 * dpr);
          return;
        }
        const v = view(), W = state.level;
        for (const b of W.walls || []) {
          const [x0, z0] = v.toPx(b.x - Math.abs(b.sx) / 2, b.z - Math.abs(b.sz) / 2);
          const [x1, z1] = v.toPx(b.x + Math.abs(b.sx) / 2, b.z + Math.abs(b.sz) / 2);
          const shade = Math.max(40, Math.min(150, 60 + (b.sy || 4) * 2));
          ctx.fillStyle = `rgb(${shade},${shade + 6},${shade + 14})`;
          ctx.fillRect(x0, z0, Math.max(1, x1 - x0), Math.max(1, z1 - z0));
        }
        ctx.strokeStyle = "#9aa3b2"; ctx.lineWidth = 1 * dpr;
        for (const sp of W.spawners || []) {
          const [x, z] = v.toPx(sp.x, sp.z);
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, 5 * dpr, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.strokeStyle = "#e05c5c"; ctx.stroke();
        }
        for (const e of W.level_exits || []) {
          const [x, z] = v.toPx(e.x, e.z);
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, Math.max(2, (e.radius || 2) * v.s), 0, Math.PI * 2);
          ctx.strokeStyle = "#5ce08a"; ctx.stroke();
        }
        for (const zn of W.zones || []) {
          const [x, z] = v.toPx(zn.x, zn.z);
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, Math.max(2, (zn.radius || 2) * v.s), 0, Math.PI * 2);
          ctx.strokeStyle = "#b07cff"; ctx.setLineDash([4 * dpr, 4 * dpr]); ctx.stroke();
          ctx.setLineDash([]);
        }
        for (const c of W.characters || []) {
          const [x, z] = v.toPx(c.x, c.z);
          ctx.fillStyle = "#5ca8e0"; ctx.fillRect(x - 3 * dpr, z - 3 * dpr, 6 * dpr, 6 * dpr);
        }
        if (state.remote) {
          const [x, z] = v.toPx(state.remote.x, state.remote.z);
          ctx.fillStyle = "#8de05c";
          ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, z, 6 * dpr, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
          const yaw = (state.remote.yaw || 0) * Math.PI / 180;
          ctx.strokeStyle = "#8de05c"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, z);
          ctx.lineTo(x - Math.sin(yaw) * 16 * dpr, z - Math.cos(yaw) * 16 * dpr); ctx.stroke();
        }
        const g = v.g;
        ctx.fillStyle = "#7f8794";
        ctx.font = `${11 * dpr}px monospace`;
        ctx.fillText(`${state.name || "untitled"}  ·  ${(W.walls || []).length} walls  ·  x ${g.minx.toFixed(1)}..${g.maxx.toFixed(1)}  z ${g.minz.toFixed(1)}..${g.maxz.toFixed(1)}  ·  -Z up`, 12 * dpr, canvas.height - 10 * dpr);
      }
      
      /* ---------- editing ---------- */
      
      function snapshot() {
        state.undo.push(JSON.stringify(state.level));
        if (state.undo.length > 60) state.undo.shift();
      }
      
      function undo() {
        if (!state.undo.length) return;
        state.level = JSON.parse(state.undo.pop());
        draw(); pushDraftSoon();
      }
      
      function wallIndexAt(x, z) {
        const walls = state.level.walls;
        for (let i = walls.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
          const b = walls[i];
          if (Math.abs(x - b.x) <= Math.abs(b.sx) / 2 && Math.abs(z - b.z) <= Math.abs(b.sz) / 2) return i;
        }
        return -1;
      }
      
      canvas.addEventListener("mousedown", ev => {
        if (!state.level) return;
        const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
        const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;
        const v = view();
        const [x, z] = v.toWorld((ev.clientX - rect.left) * dpr, (ev.clientY - rect.top) * dpr);
        const W = state.level;
      
        if (state.tool === "add") {
          snapshot();
          const mat = (W.materials[0] && W.materials[0].name) || "brick";
          const box = { x: +x.toFixed(2), y: 2, z: +z.toFixed(2), sx: 4, sy: 4, sz: 4,
                        r: 0.6, g: 0.6, b: 0.65, friction: 0.8, material: mat };
          W.walls.push(box);
          log(`box at ${box.x}, ${box.z}`);
          post("box_add", { id: W.walls.length, x: box.x, y: box.y, z: box.z,
                            sx: box.sx, sy: box.sy, sz: box.sz, r: box.r, g: box.g, b: box.b });
        } else if (state.tool === "delete") {
          const i = wallIndexAt(x, z);
          if (i < 0) { log("nothing under the cursor"); return; }
          snapshot();
          W.walls.splice(i, 1);
          log(`deleted wall ${i}`);
          post("box_del", { id: -1, index: i });
        } else {
          snapshot();
          if (!W.spawners.length) W.spawners.push({ id: 1, x: 0, y: 1, z: 0, yaw: 0, team: -1 });
          W.spawners[0].x = +x.toFixed(2); W.spawners[0].z = +z.toFixed(2);
          log(`spawner at ${W.spawners[0].x}, ${W.spawners[0].z}`);
          post("spawner", { x: W.spawners[0].x, y: W.spawners[0].y, z: W.spawners[0].z,
                             yaw: W.spawners[0].yaw || 0 });
        }
        draw();
        pushDraftSoon();
      });
      
      document.addEventListener("keydown", ev => {
        if ((ev.ctrlKey || ev.metaKey) && ev.key.toLowerCase() === "z") { ev.preventDefault(); undo(); }
        if (ev.target.tagName === "INPUT") return;
        const k = ev.key.toLowerCase();
        const tool = k === "b" ? "add" : k === "x" ? "delete" : k === "m" ? "spawner" : null;
        if (tool) selectTool(tool);
      });
      
      function selectTool(tool) {
        state.tool = tool;
        for (const b of document.querySelectorAll("[data-tool]"))
          b.classList.toggle("on", b.dataset.tool === tool);
      }
      
      for (const b of document.querySelectorAll("[data-tool]"))
        b.onclick = () => selectTool(b.dataset.tool);
      
      /* ---------- saving (file + git commit) ---------- */
      
      async function save() {
        if (!state.level) return;
        if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/.test(state.name)) { alert("bad level name"); return; }
        try {
          state.level.name = state.name;
          const r = await api("PUT", "/api/levels/" + encodeURIComponent(state.name), state.level);
          state.dirty = false;
          const g = r.git || {};
          el("saveInfo").textContent = g.committed
            ? `committed ${g.commit}: ${g.message}`
            : `saved ${r.file} (${g.detail || "not committed"})`;
          log(el("saveInfo").textContent);
          loadLevelList();
        } catch (e) {
          el("saveInfo").textContent = "save failed: " + e.message;
          log("save failed: " + e.message);
        }
      }
      el("saveBtn").onclick = save;
      el("newBtn").onclick = newLevel;
      
      /* ---------- live session ---------- */
      
      async function startSession() {
        try {
          const body = { level_id: 0, level_name: state.name || "" };
          const r = await api("POST", SESSION_BASE, body);
          joinSession(r.id);
          log(`started session ${r.id} — run the game with --edit-session ${r.id}`);
        } catch (e) { log("start failed: " + e.message); }
      }
      
      function joinSession(id) {
        if (!/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/.test(id || "")) { log("session id must be 32 hex chars"); return; }
        state.session = id;
        state.since = 0;
        state.pollGen++;
        el("sessionId").value = id;
        el("sessionInfo").textContent = "in session " + id;
        log("joined session " + id);
        pushDraft();          // hand the game our working level straight away
        pollLoop(state.pollGen);
      }
      
      el("startBtn").onclick = startSession;
      el("joinBtn").onclick = () => joinSession(el("sessionId").value.trim());
      
      async function post(kind, data) {
        if (!state.session) return;
        try {
          await api("POST", `${SESSION_BASE}/${state.session}/events`, { source: "nock", kind, data });
        } catch (e) { log(`event ${kind} failed: ${e.message}`); }
      }
      
      let pushTimer = null;
      function pushDraftSoon() {
        if (!state.session) return;
        clearTimeout(pushTimer);
        pushTimer = setTimeout(pushDraft, 180);
      }
      
      async function pushDraft() {
        if (!state.session || !state.level) return;
        try {
          const r = await api("PUT", `${SESSION_BASE}/${state.session}/level`, state.level);
          // "level" tells the native client to fetch the working level (edit_sync.h es_worker)
          await post("level", { rev: r.rev });
        } catch (e) { log("draft push failed: " + e.message); }
      }
      
      async function pollLoop(gen) {
        if (state.polling) return;
        state.polling = true;
        try {
          while (state.session && gen === state.pollGen) {
            const q = `${SESSION_BASE}/${state.session}?since=${state.since}&wait=10`;
            let snap;
            try {
              snap = await api("GET", q);
            } catch (e) {
              log("poll failed: " + e.message + " (session ended?)");
              state.session = null;
              el("sessionInfo").textContent = "session lost";
              break;
            }
            if (gen !== state.pollGen) break;
            applyEvents(snap.events || []);
            state.since = snap.seq;
          }
        } finally {
          state.polling = false;
        }
      }
      
      function applyEvents(events) {
        for (const ev of events) {
          const d = ev.data || {};
          if (ev.kind === "spawner" && d.x !== undefined) {
            const W = state.level;
            if (W) {
              if (!W.spawners.length) W.spawners.push({ id: 1, x: 0, y: 1, z: 0, yaw: 0, team: -1 });
              W.spawners[0].x = d.x; W.spawners[0].y = d.y; W.spawners[0].z = d.z;
              if (d.yaw !== undefined) W.spawners[0].yaw = d.yaw;
            }
          } else if (ev.kind === "avatar" && d.x !== undefined) {
            state.remote = { x: d.x, z: d.z, yaw: d.yaw || 0 };
          } else if (ev.kind === "box_add" && d.sx !== undefined) {
            // placed in-game (B): mirror it here so both views agree
            const W = state.level;
            if (W) {
              W.walls.push({ x: d.x, y: d.y, z: d.z, sx: d.sx, sy: d.sy || 4, sz: d.sz || 4,
                             r: d.r ?? 0.6, g: d.g ?? 0.6, b: d.b ?? 0.65, friction: 0.8,
                             material: (W.materials[0] && W.materials[0].name) || "brick" });
              log("game placed a box");
            }
          } else if (ev.kind === "box_del" && d.index !== undefined) {
            const W = state.level;
            if (W && d.index >= 0 && d.index < W.walls.length) {
              W.walls.splice(d.index, 1);
              log("game deleted a box");
            }
          } else if (ev.kind === "save") {
            log("game asked to save — press Save + commit to land it in git");
          } else if (ev.kind === "teleport" && d.x !== undefined) {
            state.remote = { x: d.x, z: d.z, yaw: d.yaw || 0 };
          }
        }
        draw();
      }
      
      /* ---------- boot ---------- */
      
      el("note").textContent =
        "SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL=" + location.origin + SESSION_BASE + "\n" +
        "./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map levels/" + "<name>.json --edit-live\n" +
        "(or --edit-session <id>)";
      
      loadLevelList().then(() => {
        const first = document.querySelector("#levels li[data-name]");
        if (first) openLevel(first.dataset.name);
        draw();
      });
      window.addEventListener("resize", draw);
      </script>
      </body>
      </html>
      
- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_fx.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_fx.prn -- the cosmetics: particles, the flames, and the DYNAMIC LIGHT TABLE the renderer lights the
      ;; arena with. ON FIRE's "REALLY DRAMATIC LIGHTING EFFECTS" (founder, 2026-10-18) are built here.
      ;;
      ;; NOTHING HERE FEEDS THE SIM. This file reads the match (cars, ball, fires, the goal) and writes only its own records -- the
      ;; particles at part-base, the light table at lights-base, each car's fire-fx, the fire banner's clock -- and every die it rolls
      ;; is fx-rand (br_mem.prn), the cosmetic generator, never the sim's or the AI's. The fx dice are seeded from the match seed at
      ;; begin-match!, so a replayed match LOOKS the same as well as plays the same; but if they were seeded differently, the match
      ;; itself would still come out bit for bit the same (tests/br_fire_test.mjs checks both).
      ;;
      ;; fx-tick! runs once per sim tick (br_sim.prn: also during the frozen kickoff countdown, so the flames keep moving):
      ;;   the cars     each car's fire-fx (0..1, the renderer's flame size) swells fast when it catches fire and dies down slowly
      ;;                when it goes out; a burning car throws off flames, a boosting one a plume, one driving the dirt track
      ;;                (or drifting) a little dust
      ;;   the ball     alight (b-fire): flames off its surface, a comet's tail behind it
      ;;   particles    256 slots, a spawn ring that takes the first free slot of the next eight (else recycles the oldest-ish one);
      ;;                each lives `life` ticks: integrate (flames rise and shrink, plumes spread and slow, dust settles, sparks
      ;;                fall), age, die. The floor stops what falls; nothing else collides (they are only light and colour).
      ;;   the lights   rebuilt from scratch every tick, in priority order, up to 16: the goal flash, the burning ball, burning
      ;;                cars (flickering orange-white), boost plumes. Then the DRAMA scalar: it jumps up when someone is on fire or a
      ;;                goal goes in and ebbs away slowly after -- the renderer darkens the ambient and pushes the contrast with it.
      ;;
      ;; The light table's layout is in br_mem.prn's memory map (LIGHTS, 0x029000). Light colours are 0..1 per channel; intensity is in
      ;; "a car's worth" (a burning car flickers between about 1.4 and 2.4, the goal flash starts at 9); a light reaches out to its
      ;; radius and no further (a renderer might take colour * intensity * (1 - d / radius)^2).
      
      ;; ---- the constants ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn fx-flash-ticks [] : I32 63)       ; the goal flash lasts ~1 s
      (defn fx-flash-power [] : F32 9.0)      ; ... starts this bright (a burning car is ~2) and falls off as the square of what is left
      (defn fx-flash-radius [] : F32 900.0)   ; ... lighting most of the arena at first, shrinking to 45% of it
      (defn fx-flash-y [] : F32 205.0)        ; ... from just under the mouth of the tower's shaft
      (defn fx-sparks [] : I32 40)            ; sparks sprayed down out of the shaft by a goal
      (defn fx-fire-rise [] : F32 0.25)       ; fire-fx swells this much of the way to 1 each tick on catching fire ...
      (defn fx-fire-fall [] : F32 0.06)       ; ... and dies down this much of the way to 0 once out
      (defn fx-drama-rise [] : F32 0.2)       ; the drama jumps up ...
      (defn fx-drama-fall [] : F32 0.025)     ; ... and ebbs away (a time constant of ~0.6 s)
      
      ;; particle kinds
      (defn pk-fire [] : I32 1)
      (defn pk-plume [] : I32 2)
      (defn pk-dust [] : I32 3)
      (defn pk-spark [] : I32 4)
      
      ;; ---- the light table ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn lt-count-addr [] : I32 (lights-base))
      (defn lt-drama-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 4))
      (defn lt-flash-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 8))
      (defn lt-tick-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 12))
      (defn lt-flash-t-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 16))
      (defn lt-flash-tower-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 20))
      (defn lt-flash-team-addr [] : I32 (+ (lights-base) 24))
      (defn lt-addr [(i : I32)] : I32 (+ (+ (lights-base) 32) (* i 32)))
      (defn lt-words [] : I32 136)             ; header 8 + 16 lights x 8
      
      (defn light-count [] : I32 (load32 (lt-count-addr)))
      (defn drama-level [] : F32 (loadf32 (lt-drama-addr)))
      
      ;; one more light, if there is room
      (defn light! [(x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32) (cr : F32) (cg : F32) (cb : F32) (power : F32) (radius : F32)] : Unit
        (let [n (light-count)]
          (when (< n (max-lights))
            (let [a (lt-addr n)]
              (storef32! a x) (storef32! (+ a 4) y) (storef32! (+ a 8) z)
              (storef32! (+ a 12) cr) (storef32! (+ a 16) cg) (storef32! (+ a 20) cb)
              (storef32! (+ a 24) power) (storef32! (+ a 28) radius)
              (store32! (lt-count-addr) (+ n 1))))))
      
      ;; a channel of an engine colour (0xAABBGGRR), as 0..1: shift 0 red, 8 green, 16 blue
      (defn chan-f [(c : I32) (sh : I32)] : F32 (/ (f32 (bit-and (shr c sh) 255)) 255.0))
      
      ;; ---- the particles ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; the first free slot among the next eight from the ring's cursor; none free: the one at the cursor is recycled
      (defn part-slot [] : I32
        (let [h (gi (g-part-head))]
          (loop [i 0]
            (cond (>= i 8) (bit-and h 255)
                  (= (f-ttl (bit-and (+ h i) 255)) 0) (bit-and (+ h i) 255)
                  :else (recur (+ i 1))))))
      
      (defn part! [(kind : I32) (ttl : I32) (col : I32) (x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32) (vx : F32) (vy : F32) (vz : F32) (size : F32)] : Unit
        (let [q (part-slot)]
          (gi! (g-part-head) (bit-and (+ q 1) 255))
          (set-f-ttl! q ttl) (set-f-life! q ttl) (set-f-kind! q kind) (set-f-color! q col)
          (set-f-x! q x) (set-f-y! q y) (set-f-z! q z)
          (set-f-vx! q vx) (set-f-vy! q vy) (set-f-vz! q vz)
          (set-f-size! q size)))
      
      ;; a flame's colour: orange to yellow, now and then a white-hot core
      (defn fire-col [] : I32
        (if (= (fx-rnd 6) 0) (rgb 255 244 214) (rgb 255 (+ 120 (fx-rnd 110)) (+ 24 (fx-rnd 50)))))
      
      ;; one tick of every live particle: flames rise (they are hot) and shrink, plumes spread and slow, dust settles, sparks fall
      (defn parts-tick! [] : Unit
        (let [(live : I32) 0 (dt : F32) (tick-dt)]
          (dotimes [q 256]
            (when (> (f-ttl q) 0)
              (let [k (f-kind q)
                    (ay : F32) (case k 1 70.0 2 0.0 3 -30.0 -66.0)
                    (drag : F32) (case k 1 2.5 2 4.0 3 1.5 0.6)
                    (dr : F32) (fmax2 0.0 (- 1.0 (* drag dt)))
                    (vx : F32) (* (f-vx q) dr)
                    (vy : F32) (* (+ (f-vy q) (* ay dt)) dr)
                    (vz : F32) (* (f-vz q) dr)
                    (y : F32) (+ (f-y q) (* vy dt))]
                (set-f-vx! q vx) (set-f-vz! q vz)
                (set-f-x! q (+ (f-x q) (* vx dt)))
                (set-f-z! q (+ (f-z q) (* vz dt)))
                ;; the floor stops what falls (dust and sparks skid along it)
                (if (< y 1.0)
                    (do (set-f-y! q 1.0) (set-f-vy! q 0.0))
                    (do (set-f-y! q y) (set-f-vy! q vy)))
                (set-f-size! q (case k 1 (* (f-size q) 0.96) 2 (+ (f-size q) 0.3) 3 (+ (f-size q) 0.12) (f-size q)))
                (set-f-ttl! q (- (f-ttl q) 1))
                (when (> (f-ttl q) 0) (set! live (+ live 1))))))
          (gi! (g-part-live) live)))
      
      ;; ---- the cars ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn fx-car! [(s : I32)] : Unit
        (let [(want : F32) (if (on-fire? s) 1.0 0.0)
              (ff0 : F32) (c-fire-fx s)
              (ff1 : F32) (+ ff0 (* (- want ff0) (if (> want ff0) (fx-fire-rise) (fx-fire-fall))))
              (ff : F32) (if (< ff1 0.002) 0.0 ff1)
              (sp : F32) (len3 (c-vx s) (c-vy s) (c-vz s))]
          (set-c-fire-fx! s ff)
          ;; flames: up to two a tick, off the body and licking up away from it; they keep only half the car's speed, so a car on the
          ;; move drags a tail of fire behind it
          (dotimes [i 2]
            (when (< (fx-rand-unit) ff)
              (let [(a : F32) (* 4.5 (fx-rand-f)) (b : F32) (* 7.5 (fx-rand-f)) (c : F32) (+ 2.0 (* 3.0 (fx-rand-unit)))
                    (up : F32) (+ 18.0 (* 22.0 (fx-rand-unit)))
                    (jx : F32) (* 14.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jy : F32) (* 8.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jz : F32) (* 14.0 (fx-rand-f))]
                (part! (pk-fire) (+ 16 (fx-rnd 12)) (fire-col)
                       (+ (c-x s) (+ (* (c-rx s) a) (+ (* (c-fx s) b) (* (c-ux s) c))))
                       (+ (c-y s) (+ (* (c-ry s) a) (+ (* (c-fy s) b) (* (c-uy s) c))))
                       (+ (c-z s) (+ (* (c-rz s) a) (+ (* (c-fz s) b) (* (c-uz s) c))))
                       (+ (* 0.5 (c-vx s)) (+ (* (c-ux s) up) jx))
                       (+ (* 0.5 (c-vy s)) (+ (* (c-uy s) up) jy))
                       (+ (* 0.5 (c-vz s)) (+ (* (c-uz s) up) jz))
                       (+ 3.5 (* 2.5 (fx-rand-unit)))))))
          ;; the boost plume, out of the rear nozzle and back along the car (a burning car's plume burns too)
          (when (and (> (c-boost-fx s) 0.25) (< (fx-rand-unit) (* 0.7 (c-boost-fx s))))
            (let [(back : F32) (+ 140.0 (* 40.0 (fx-rand-unit)))
                  (jx : F32) (* 10.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jy : F32) (* 10.0 (fx-rand-f)) (jz : F32) (* 10.0 (fx-rand-f))]
              (part! (pk-plume) (+ 12 (fx-rnd 7)) (if (on-fire? s) (rgb 255 150 60) (rgb 196 222 255))
                     (- (c-x s) (* (c-fx s) 8.0)) (- (c-y s) (* (c-fy s) 8.0)) (- (c-z s) (* (c-fz s) 8.0))
                     (+ (- (c-vx s) (* (c-fx s) back)) jx) (+ (- (c-vy s) (* (c-fy s) back)) jy) (+ (- (c-vz s) (* (c-fz s) back)) jz)
                     2.5)))
          ;; dust: kicked up behind the rear wheels by a car driving the dirt track, or drifting anywhere on the floor, in the floor's
          ;; own colour
          (when (and (= (c-attached s) 1) (> (c-uy s) 0.7)
                     (or (and (> sp 60.0) (> (road-at (c-x s) (c-z s)) 128)) (> (c-slip s) 50.0))
                     (< (fx-rand-unit) 0.35))
            (let [(rx : F32) (* 4.0 (fx-rand-f))
                  (x : F32) (- (+ (c-x s) (* (c-rx s) rx)) (* (c-fx s) 7.0))
                  (z : F32) (- (+ (c-z s) (* (c-rz s) rx)) (* (c-fz s) 7.0))]
              (part! (pk-dust) (+ 30 (fx-rnd 16)) (mix (tex-color (tex-ix x) (tex-iz z)) (rgb 200 190 170) 90)
                     x (+ (c-y s) 1.0) z
                     (+ (* 0.2 (c-vx s)) (* 15.0 (fx-rand-f))) (+ 10.0 (* 8.0 (fx-rand-unit))) (+ (* 0.2 (c-vz s)) (* 15.0 (fx-rand-f)))
                     3.0)))))
      
      ;; the ball alight: flames off its surface, and since they keep less than half its speed, a comet's tail behind it
      (defn fx-ball! [] : Unit
        (when (> (b-fire) 0)
          (dotimes [i 2]
            (let [(ox : F32) (* 9.0 (fx-rand-f)) (oy : F32) (* 9.0 (fx-rand-f)) (oz : F32) (* 9.0 (fx-rand-f))]
              (part! (pk-fire) (+ 14 (fx-rnd 9)) (fire-col)
                     (+ (b-x) ox) (+ (b-y) oy) (+ (b-z) oz)
                     (+ (* 0.4 (b-vx)) (* 2.0 ox)) (+ (+ (* 0.4 (b-vy)) (* 2.0 oy)) 25.0) (+ (* 0.4 (b-vz)) (* 2.0 oz))
                     (+ 4.0 (* 3.0 (fx-rand-unit))))))))
      
      ;; ---- a goal: the tower goes up ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; called by on-goal! (br_rules.prn): the flash (in the light table's header, burnt down by lights-tick!) and a spray of sparks in
      ;; the scorer's colour, down out of the mouth of the shaft into the arena
      (defn fx-goal! [(tower : I32) (team : I32)] : Unit
        (let [col (team-color team)]
          (store32! (lt-flash-t-addr) (fx-flash-ticks))
          (store32! (lt-flash-tower-addr) tower)
          (store32! (lt-flash-team-addr) team)
          (dotimes [i (fx-sparks)]
            (let [(ang : F32) (* 6.2831855 (fx-rand-unit))
                  (out : F32) (* 200.0 (fx-rand-unit))]
              (part! (pk-spark) (+ 40 (fx-rnd 30)) (if (= (fx-rnd 4) 0) (rgb 255 250 236) col)
                     (+ (tw-x tower) (* 20.0 (fx-rand-f))) (- (a-h) 6.0) (+ (tw-z tower) (* 20.0 (fx-rand-f)))
                     (* (cosf ang) out) (- 0.0 (+ 40.0 (* 180.0 (fx-rand-unit)))) (* (sinf ang) out)
                     (+ 1.5 (fx-rand-unit)))))))
      
      ;; ---- the lights and the drama -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn lights-tick! [] : Unit
        (let [ft (load32 (lt-flash-t-addr))
              (target : F32) 0.0]
          (store32! (lt-count-addr) 0)
          (store32! (lt-tick-addr) (gi (g-tick)))
          ;; 1. the goal flash: white-hot as the ball goes in, settling into the scorer's colour as it dies (with the square of what is
          ;;    left, so it is a flash, not a glow)
          (if (> ft 0)
              (let [(k : F32) (/ (f32 ft) (f32 (fx-flash-ticks)))
                    tw (load32 (lt-flash-tower-addr))
                    c (team-color (load32 (lt-flash-team-addr)))
                    (w : F32) (* 0.6 k)]
                (light! (tw-x tw) (fx-flash-y) (tw-z tw)
                        (lerp (chan-f c 0) 1.0 w) (lerp (chan-f c 8) 1.0 w) (lerp (chan-f c 16) 1.0 w)
                        (* (fx-flash-power) (* k k)) (* (fx-flash-radius) (+ 0.45 (* 0.55 k))))
                (storef32! (lt-flash-addr) k)
                (store32! (lt-flash-t-addr) (- ft 1))
                (set! target (fmax2 target (+ 0.5 (* 0.5 k)))))
              (storef32! (lt-flash-addr) 0.0))
          ;; 2. the burning ball
          (when (> (b-fire) 0)
            (let [(fl : F32) (fx-rand-unit)]
              (light! (b-x) (b-y) (b-z) 1.0 (+ 0.55 (* 0.25 fl)) (+ 0.16 (* 0.2 fl)) (+ 2.2 (* 0.9 fl)) (+ 170.0 (* 40.0 fl)))
              (set! target (fmax2 target 0.75))))
          ;; 3. the burning cars: orange, flickering toward white as they flare
          (dotimes [s 12]
            (when (and (!= (c-active s) 0) (> (c-fire-fx s) 0.03))
              (let [(fl : F32) (fx-rand-unit) (ff : F32) (c-fire-fx s)]
                (light! (+ (c-x s) (* (c-ux s) 5.0)) (+ (c-y s) (* (c-uy s) 5.0)) (+ (c-z s) (* (c-uz s) 5.0))
                        1.0 (+ 0.5 (* 0.3 fl)) (+ 0.12 (* 0.25 (* fl fl)))
                        (* ff (+ 1.4 fl)) (+ 130.0 (* 50.0 fl)))
                (when (on-fire? s) (set! target (fmax2 target 0.6))))))
          ;; 4. the boost plumes (in slot order, while there is room): a cold blue-white, or fire for a burning car
          (dotimes [s 12]
            (when (and (!= (c-active s) 0) (> (c-boost-fx s) 0.2))
              (let [hot (on-fire? s)]
                (light! (- (c-x s) (* (c-fx s) 10.0)) (- (c-y s) (* (c-fy s) 10.0)) (- (c-z s) (* (c-fz s) 10.0))
                        (if hot 1.0 0.55) (if hot 0.5 0.75) (if hot 0.15 1.0)
                        (* 0.9 (c-boost-fx s)) 70.0))))
          ;; the slots not used this tick are zeroed, so a renderer that reads all sixteen sees nothing in them
          (loop [i (light-count)]
            (when (< i (max-lights))
              (zero-words! (lt-addr i) 8)
              (recur (+ i 1))))
          ;; the drama: a dead ball after a goal holds it up a little; it jumps to its target and ebbs away from it
          (when (> (gi (g-goal-t)) 0) (set! target (fmax2 target 0.45)))
          (let [(d : F32) (drama-level)]
            (storef32! (lt-drama-addr)
                       (clamp-f (+ d (* (- target d) (if (> target d) (fx-drama-rise) (fx-drama-fall)))) 0.0 1.0)))))
      
      ;; ---- once per tick ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn fx-tick! [] : Unit
        (do
          (dotimes [s (max-cars)] (when (!= (c-active s) 0) (fx-car! s)))
          (fx-ball!)
          (parts-tick!)
          (lights-tick!)

      static void level_boxes_apply_to_physics(const CustomLevelData *lvl) {

          // cause: the outdoor day/night lighting model (retro_lighting.c) adds a real, physically-
          // motivated sun/moon "scattered sky" fill term to every wall face unconditionally -- correct
          // outdoors, but swamps real per-fixture (HPS/IPS) point-light contrast in a windowless
          // interior with zero real sky exposure. RETRO_LIGHTING_INTERIOR_FLAT already existed (defined
          // in retro_lighting.h) but was never actually selected anywhere -- this is that preset's real,
          // first use: zero sun/moon contribution, real fixtures become the dominant light source.
          g_world_lighting_preset = lvl->enclosed ? RETRO_LIGHTING_INTERIOR_FLAT : RETRO_LIGHTING_DAY_STATIC;

              w[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].w; h[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].h; d[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].d;
              r[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].r; g[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].g; b[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].b;
              material_idx[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].material_idx;
          }
          char mat_names[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN];
          char mat_shaders[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN];
          float mat_specular[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS], mat_shininess[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS];
          float mat_friction[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS];
          for (int mi = 0; mi < lvl->material_count; mi++) {
              strncpy(mat_names[mi], lvl->materials[mi].name, CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN - 1);
              mat_names[mi][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN - 1] = '\0';
              strncpy(mat_shaders[mi], lvl->materials[mi].shader_name, CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN - 1);
              mat_shaders[mi][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN - 1] = '\0';

          phys_set_custom_level(x, y, z, w, h, d, r, g, b, material_idx, lvl->count, lvl->ground_plane_enabled, lvl->ground_plane_squares);

              static float orx[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], ory[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], orz[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX];
              static unsigned char oramp[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX];

      async function styreq<T>(path: string, opts: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
        const headers: Record<string, string> = opts.body ? { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } : {}
        const res = await fetch(`${SHANKPIT_STYLES_BASE}${path}`, { credentials: 'include', ...opts, headers })
        if (!res.ok) {
          const text = await res.text().catch(() => res.statusText)
          throw new Error(`${res.status}: ${text}`)
        }
        if (res.status === 204) return undefined as T
        return (await res.json()) as T
      }
      
      export const shankpitStyles = {
        list: (levelId: number | null) => styreq<ShankpitCubeStyle[]>(levelId ? `?level_id=${levelId}` : ''),
        create: (st: Omit<ShankpitCubeStyle, 'id'>) => styreq<ShankpitCubeStyle>('', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(st) }),
        update: (st: ShankpitCubeStyle) => styreq<ShankpitCubeStyle>(`/${st.id}`, { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(st) }),
        remove: (id: number) => styreq<void>(`/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE' }),
      }
      
      // buggySpawnTile (#464/#467) -- a buggy spawn is an ordinary thin wall NAMED buggy_spawn (facing yaw 0)
      // or buggy_spawn_<degrees>; level export turns every such wall into a buggy spawn point at its top
      // surface (IDUNA/internal/shankpit buggySpawnsForExport). The tile stays a visible amber pad. Put one
      // in a level, or in a widget to make a reusable "garage bay" that carries its rotation with it.
      // To change the facing, rename the wall (buggy_spawn_90 ...).
      export function buggySpawnTile(id: number, at: { x: number; y: number; z: number }, friction: number): ShankpitWall {
        return { id, x: at.x, y: 0.1, z: at.z, sx: 4, sy: 0.2, sz: 6, r: 0.95, g: 0.7, b: 0.1, friction, name: 'buggy_spawn' }
      }
      
      // ShankpitMaterial mirrors IDUNA/internal/shankpit.Material exactly (S459-16, founder real-time:
      // "we will need the ability to add new materials and set their textures" / "registries for
      // everything"). shader_name is a real, named reference into SHANKPIT's own compiled-in shader
      // registry (packages/render/material_shaders.h) -- NEVER GLSL source stored here (founder: "build
      // the shaders in to the native and then refer to the shaders from NOCK directly ... for now it
      // will just be like the ffi names").
      export interface ShankpitMaterial {
        id: number
        name: string
        shader_name: string
        texture_id?: number
        specular: number
        shininess: number
        // friction (S478b, founder real-time: "make the material friction stuff working per cube") --
        // real, live ground friction consumed by resolve_collision/apply_friction natively, not just a
        // rendering parameter like specular/shininess. Default 0.30 matches physics.h's own tuned
        // global FRICTION baseline.
        friction: number
        // density (kg/m^3, 2026-10-16, founder: "calculate mass of the different materials, have it
        // configurable on the NOCK material") -- mass density for SHANKPIT's destructible-brick rigid
        // bodies (a chunk that falls away weighs density x volume). 0 = unset: the game uses its own
        // per-kind default (brick 1900, concrete 2400, wood 600, glass 2500).
        density: number
        created_at: string
        updated_at: string

// ---- Buggy spawns (#464/#466) -------------------------------------------------------------------
// "the buggy should be placeable in levels via the buggy spawn widget tiles OR via an actual buggy
// placed in a level". A buggy spawn is a NAME CONVENTION on an ordinary wall, the same way a glTF
// node named door* becomes a door: a thin tile named buggy_spawn (facing yaw 0) or buggy_spawn_<deg>
// (buggy_spawn_90). Blender's duplicate suffix (buggy_spawn_90.001) is ignored. A level can hold the
// tile directly, or a widget can (a reusable "garage bay"); flattening carries the name through and
// adds the widget's own rotation to the yaw, so both routes land in the same export list. No schema
// change: the tile is a normal wall, so editing, undo, save, clone and glTF import all keep working.

// MaxBuggySpawns matches SHANKPIT's LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_BUGGY_SPAWNS (packages/world/level_boxes.h).
const MaxBuggySpawns = 16

const buggySpawnPrefix = "buggy_spawn"

// BuggySpawnExport is the native-loader-facing shape of one buggy spawn.
type BuggySpawnExport struct {
  X   float64 `json:"x"`
  Y   float64 `json:"y"`
  Z   float64 `json:"z"`
  Yaw float64 `json:"yaw"`
}

// IsBuggySpawnName reports whether a wall name marks a buggy spawn tile.
func IsBuggySpawnName(name string) bool {
  _, ok := buggySpawnYaw(name)
  return ok
}

// buggySpawnYaw parses buggy_spawn / buggy_spawn_<deg> (case-insensitive prefix). ok is false for any
// other name, including "buggy_spawner_x" (the char after the prefix must be end, '_', '.', ' ' or '-').
func buggySpawnYaw(name string) (float64, bool) {
  if len(name) < len(buggySpawnPrefix) || !strings.EqualFold(name[:len(buggySpawnPrefix)], buggySpawnPrefix) {
    return 0, false
  }
  rest := name[len(buggySpawnPrefix):]
  if rest == "" {
    return 0, true
  }
  switch rest[0] {
  case '_', '.', ' ', '-':
  default:
    return 0, false
  }
  rest = strings.TrimLeft(rest[1:], "_. ") // drop the one separator char; a '-' after it is a sign
  end := 0
  for end < len(rest) && (rest[end] >= '0' && rest[end] <= '9' || (end == 0 && rest[end] == '-')) {
    end++
  }
  if end == 0 {
    return 0, true
  }
  deg, err := strconv.Atoi(rest[:end])
  if err != nil {
    return 0, true
  }
  return float64(((deg % 360) + 360) % 360), true
}

// rotatedBuggySpawnName leaves every ordinary name alone; a buggy spawn tile inside a placed widget or
// composed level gets the placement's rotation added to its yaw (normalised 0..359).
func rotatedBuggySpawnName(name string, worldRotY int) string {
  yaw, ok := buggySpawnYaw(name)
  if !ok || worldRotY%360 == 0 {
    return name
  }
  deg := ((int(yaw)+worldRotY)%360 + 360) % 360
  return fmt.Sprintf("%s_%d", buggySpawnPrefix, deg)
}

// buggySpawnsForExport lists a spawn per tile wall (final flattened, renumbered walls), in wall
// order. y is the tile's top surface, where the buggy's wheels will rest.
func buggySpawnsForExport(walls []Wall) []BuggySpawnExport {
  var out []BuggySpawnExport
  for _, w := range walls {
    yaw, ok := buggySpawnYaw(w.Name)
    if !ok {
      continue
    }
    out = append(out, BuggySpawnExport{X: w.X, Y: w.Y + w.SY/2, Z: w.Z, Yaw: yaw})
  }
  return out
}

// MaxLabStations bounds the exported lab station list (the native loader's fixed array).
const MaxLabStations = 32

// LabStationKinds are the station kinds a wall name may carry: lab_<kind>[_anything].
var LabStationKinds = []string{"splice", "centrifuge", "vat", "fridge", "console", "pcr"}

// LabStationExport is one interactive lab station. y is the tile's top surface.
type LabStationExport struct {
  Kind string  `json:"kind"`
  X    float64 `json:"x"`
  Y    float64 `json:"y"`
  Z    float64 `json:"z"`
}

#ifndef SHANKPIT_LEVEL_BOXES_H
#define SHANKPIT_LEVEL_BOXES_H

// level_boxes.h -- real, native JSON loader for a level authored in NOCK's SHANKPIT level editor
// (EMILY/BACKLOG.md SECTION 459), closing the real gap named directly by the founder: "get the
// level loading to work." Deliberately mirrors BRAWLPIT/packages/common/level_format.h's own real
// technique field-for-field (a real, small, dependency-free scanner scoped exactly to one known,
// flat, versioned JSON shape -- no general-purpose JSON library exists anywhere in this
// monorepo's C code) -- same real "smallest real thing" precedent, applied to a different game.
//
// REAL, FOUND, LIVE CORRECTION (2026-09-14): the level EDITOR (IDUNA/internal/shankpit,
// ShankpitLevelEditor.tsx) was built against packages/map/map.h's own `Wall` struct -- but that
// struct is used ONLY by services/game-server/src/server.c, a real, separate, currently-BROKEN
// (unrelated pre-existing compile errors), NOT-in-CI prototype, not the real, actual, CI-verified
// SHANKPIT client (apps/lobby + apps/server). That real client already has its own real,
// currently-used static-geometry primitive: packages/common/physics.h's own `Box{x,y,z,w,h,d}`
// (center x/y/z + full extents w/h/d -- confirmed against resolve_collision's own real
// `b.x - b.w/2 .. b.x + b.w/2` collision math), selected per-scene via `map_geo`/`map_count`.
// This file bridges NOCK's export JSON (shaped like `Wall`: id/x/y/z/sx/sy/sz/r/g/b/friction) into
// plain arrays a caller can hand to physics.h's own new `phys_set_custom_level` (see that file's
// own doc comment) -- deliberately NOT including physics.h itself, so this loader has zero
// dependency on the huge, scene-heavy physics header and can't accidentally couple to it.
//
// Field mapping, NOCK export -> this loader's own output (collision-relevant fields only; id and
// a Wall's own per-box `friction` are read but still not consumed -- real, deliberate, S478b:
// ground friction resolves per-MATERIAL now (LevelBoxMaterial.friction below, consumed by
// physics.h's own apply_friction via material_idx), not per-box, matching how shader_name/
// specular/shininess already work. A Wall's own bare `friction` field stays parsed-but-ignored
// legacy, not silently dropped -- named here, not a regression):
//   sx -> w, sy -> h, sz -> d (full extents both sides -- exact match, no unit conversion needed)
//
// level_boxes_save_to_file (below) is the reverse direction: a complete JSON writer for a level
// authored offline in EDIT MAP (F6), covering every field this file parses. That makes SHANKPIT its
// own level source of truth when IDUNA isn't running -- build in-game, save var/maps/<name>.json,
// reload it with --edit-map var/maps/<name>.json or --level. Round-trip covered by
// packages/world/level_save_test.c (`make test-level-save`).

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#ifndef _WIN32
#include <sys/wait.h>
#endif

#define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAME 64

/* S459-16, founder real-time: "i think it makes sense to abstract into material first so it

#define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS 16
#define LEVEL_BOXES_DEFAULT_MATERIAL "brick" /* mirrors IDUNA/internal/shankpit.DefaultMaterialName exactly */

;; session-route -- every session route starts by checking the id segment against the LIVE id.
;; Anything else is 404, so a stale client cannot post into a room it does not own.
(defn session-route [(method : String @ Region) (target : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
  (let [rest (session-rest path dest)
        id (first-seg rest dest)
        tail (tail-seg rest dest)]
    (if (not (string/str-eq? id session-id))
      (err 404 "no such edit session" dest)
      (if (string/str-eq? tail "")
        (if (string/str-eq? method "GET")
          (http_server/json-response 200 (snapshot-json target dest) dest)
          (err 405 "method not allowed" dest))
        (if (string/str-eq? tail "events")
          (if (string/str-eq? method "POST")
            (post-event body dest)
            (err 405 "method not allowed" dest))
          (if (string/str-eq? tail "level")
            (if (string/str-eq? method "PUT")
              (put-draft body dest)
              (if (string/str-eq? method "GET")
                (get-draft dest)
                (err 405 "method not allowed" dest)))
            (err 404 "unknown session route" dest)))))))

;; ---- levels --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(defn levels-route [(method : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
  (let [name (drop-prefix path "/api/levels/" dest)]
    (if (not (slug? name 0))
      (err 400 "bad level name (letters, digits, - and _ only)" dest)
      (if (string/str-eq? method "GET")
        (let [text (host-read (host-level-path levels-dir name dest) dest)]
          (if (string/str-eq? text "")
            (err 404 "no such level" dest)
            (http_server/response 200 "application/json" text dest)))
        (if (string/str-eq? method "PUT")
          (save-level name body dest)
          (err 405 "method not allowed" dest))))))

(defn status-json [(dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
  "{\"levels_dir\":\"levels\",\"sessions\":1,\"commit\":true,\"runner\":\"parena\"}")

;; ---- routing -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(defn too-big? [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : Bool
  (> (parse-int-or (http_server/header-value raw "Content-Length" dest) 0) max-body))

(defn route [(method : String @ Region) (target : String @ Region) (path : String @ Region) (body : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
  (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET")
           (or (string/str-eq? path "/") (string/str-eq? path "/editor.html")))
    (http_server/html-response 200 (host-read editor-path dest) dest)
    (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (string/str-eq? path "/api/local-nock"))
      (http_server/json-response 200 (status-json dest) dest)
      (if (and (string/str-eq? method "GET") (string/str-eq? path "/api/levels"))
        (http_server/json-response 200 (host-levels-json levels-dir dest) dest)
        (if (starts-with? path "/api/levels/" dest)
          (levels-route method path body dest)
          (if (starts-with? path "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions" dest)
            (if (and (string/str-eq? method "POST") (string/str-eq? path "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions"))
              (create-session body dest)
              (session-route method target path body dest))
            (http_server/text-response 404 "not found" dest)))))))

(defn handle [(raw : String @ Region) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : String @ Region
  (let [method (http_server/parse-method raw dest)
        target (http_server/parse-target raw dest)
        path (http_server/path-only target dest)]
    (if (string/str-eq? method "")
      (http_server/text-response 400 "bad request" dest)
      (if (too-big? raw dest)
        (err 413 "body too large" dest)
        (route method target path (http_server/parse-body raw dest) dest)))))

;; ---- accept loop ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
(defn serve-one [(!stream : &mut TcpStream) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : I32
  (let [raw (match (net/tcp/tcp-read !stream dest) ((Ok !text) !text) ((Err _) ""))]
    (do
      (net/tcp/tcp-write !stream (handle raw (request-arena)) dest)
      (net/tcp/tcp-close !stream dest)
      (request-reset)
      0)))

;; Recursing instead of `loop/recur` keeps the listener a plain local; every request's own arena is
;; reset after its response is written, so a long-lived server does not grow per request.
(defn serve-loop [(!listener : &mut TcpListener) (served : I32) (dest : Arena @ Region)] : I32
  (match (net/tcp/tcp-accept !listener dest)
    ((Ok !stream)
      (do
        (serve-one &mut !stream dest)
        (serve-loop !listener (+ served 1) dest)))

/* fx_spawn_explosion -- installed as g_fx_explosion_hook (physics.h), called by explode_splash for
 * every splash detonation. A ring buffer: a burst of simultaneous blasts cycles the slots instead of
 * growing anything. */
static void fx_spawn_explosion(float x, float y, float z, float radius, int weapon) {
    FxBlast *b = &g_fx_blast[g_fx_blast_next];
    g_fx_blast_next = (g_fx_blast_next + 1) % FX_BLAST_MAX;
    b->active = 1;
    b->x = x; b->y = y; b->z = z;
    b->radius = radius > 0.1f ? radius : 0.1f;
    b->t0 = SDL_GetTicks();
    b->weapon = weapon;
}

/* drone_local_pilot -- the drone the local player is currently flying, or NULL. */
static DroneState *drone_local_pilot(void) {
    if (!local_state.players[0].in_vehicle || local_state.players[0].vehicle_type != VEH_DRONE) return NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_DRONES; i++) {
        DroneState *d = &local_state.drones[i];
        if (d->active && d->occupant_player_id == local_state.players[0].id) return d;
    }
    return NULL;
}

/* drone_gimbal_clamp -- while piloting a drone the mouse drives its HEAD, not a free camera: the offset
 * from the airframe is clamped to that airframe's own mechanical limits (drone_flight.h /
 * PARENA drone-gimbal-*-milli). Recon swings 90 degrees, the micro barely moves. */
static void drone_gimbal_clamp(void) {
    DroneState *d = drone_local_pilot();
    if (!d) return;
    drone_gimbal_track(d, cam_yaw, cam_pitch);
    cam_yaw = drone_gimbal_view_yaw(d);
    cam_pitch = d->gimbal_pitch;

PlayerState* get_best_bot() {
    PlayerState *best = NULL;
    float max_score = -99999.0f;
    for(int i=1; i<MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
        if (!local_state.players[i].active) continue;
        if (local_state.players[i].accumulated_reward > max_score) {
            max_score = local_state.players[i].accumulated_reward;
            best = &local_state.players[i];
        }
    }
    return best;
}

static inline void scene_load(int scene_id) {
    local_state.scene_id = scene_id;
    phys_set_scene(scene_id);
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
        if (!local_state.players[i].active) continue;
        local_state.players[i].scene_id = scene_id;
        scene_force_spawn(&local_state.players[i]);
    }
    for (int hi = 0; hi < MAX_HELICOPTERS; hi++) {
        memset(&local_state.helicopters[hi], 0, sizeof(local_state.helicopters[hi]));
        local_state.helicopters[hi].id = hi;
        local_state.helicopters[hi].occupant_player_id = -1;
    }
    for (int bi = 0; bi < MAX_BUGGIES; bi++) {
        memset(&local_state.buggies[bi], 0, sizeof(local_state.buggies[bi]));
        local_state.buggies[bi].id = bi;
        local_state.buggies[bi].occupant_player_id = -1;
    }
    int pad_count = 0;
    const VehiclePad *pads = scene_vehicle_pads(scene_id, &pad_count);
    for (int i = 0; i < pad_count && i < MAX_BUGGIES; i++) {
        buggy_spawn_defaults(&local_state.buggies[i], i, scene_id, pads[i].x, pads[i].z, 180.0f);
        printf("[BUGGY] spawned id=%d scene=%d x=%.1f z=%.1f\n", i, scene_id, pads[i].x, pads[i].z);
    }
    if (scene_id == SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL) {
        /* #464: author-placed buggies (a buggy_spawn tile in the level or in a placed widget) */
        for (int i = 0; i < g_custom_level_buggy_count && i < MAX_BUGGIES; i++) {
            buggy_spawn_defaults(&local_state.buggies[i], i, scene_id, g_custom_level_buggy_x[i], g_custom_level_buggy_z[i], g_custom_level_buggy_yaw[i]);
            local_state.buggies[i].y = g_custom_level_buggy_y[i] + BUGGY_WHEEL_RADIUS + BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE;
            printf("[BUGGY] spawned id=%d scene=%d (level) x=%.1f z=%.1f yaw=%.0f\n", i, scene_id, g_custom_level_buggy_x[i], g_custom_level_buggy_z[i], g_custom_level_buggy_yaw[i]);
        }
    }

    if (scene_id == SCENE_VOXWORLD) {
        float red_y = voxworld_heli_spawn_y(VOXWORLD_BASE_RED_X);
        float blue_y = voxworld_heli_spawn_y(VOXWORLD_BASE_BLUE_X);
        heli_spawn_defaults(&local_state.helicopters[0], 0, SCENE_VOXWORLD, VOXWORLD_HELI_RED_X, red_y, VOXWORLD_HELI_RED_Z);
        heli_spawn_defaults(&local_state.helicopters[1], 1, SCENE_VOXWORLD, VOXWORLD_HELI_BLUE_X, blue_y, VOXWORLD_HELI_BLUE_Z);
        local_state.helicopters[0].yaw = 90.0f;
        local_state.helicopters[1].yaw = 270.0f;
        local_state.helicopters[0].grounded = 1;
        local_state.helicopters[1].grounded = 1;
        local_state.helicopters[0].rotor_speed = 14.0f;
        local_state.helicopters[1].rotor_speed = 14.0f;
#if SHANKPIT_HELI_DEBUG

static inline void heli_spawn_defaults(HelicopterState *h, int id, int scene_id, float x, float y, float z) {
    memset(h, 0, sizeof(*h));
    h->active = 1;
    h->id = id;
    h->scene_id = scene_id;
    h->x = x; h->y = y; h->z = z;
    h->health = 250;
    h->occupant_player_id = -1;
    h->rotor_speed = 8.0f;
    h->yaw = 180.0f;

}

static inline void buggy_spawn_defaults(BuggyState *b, int id, int scene_id, float x, float z, float yaw) {
    memset(b, 0, sizeof(*b));
    b->active = 1;
    b->id = id;
    b->scene_id = scene_id;
    b->x = x; b->z = z;
    b->yaw = yaw;
    b->occupant_player_id = -1;
    float gy = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, x, z);
    if (gy < 0.0f) gy = 0.0f;
    b->y = gy + BUGGY_WHEEL_RADIUS + BUGGY_CHASSIS_CLEARANCE;
    b->grounded = 1;
    b->health = 300;
}

/* the yaw the camera actually looks along: the airframe plus its gimbal */
static inline float drone_gimbal_view_yaw(const DroneState *d) {
    return norm_yaw_deg(d->yaw + d->gimbal_yaw);
}

/* drone_spawn_defaults -- one parked/hovering drone. y is caller-supplied because where "the air
 * over this spot" is depends on what it was called onto (vehicle_call.h decides). */
static inline void drone_spawn_defaults(DroneState *d, int id, int scene_id, int kind,
                                       float x, float y, float z, float yaw) {
    memset(d, 0, sizeof(*d));
    d->active = 1;
    d->id = id;
    d->scene_id = scene_id;
    d->kind = (kind == DRONE_KIND_FLY) ? DRONE_KIND_FLY : DRONE_KIND_RECON;
    d->x = x; d->y = y; d->z = z;
    d->yaw = yaw;
    d->health = (float)df_hull(d->kind);
    d->occupant_player_id = -1;
}

static inline float af_ground_y(float x, float z) {
    float gy = terrain_sample_height(&g_scene_terrain, x, z);
    if (gy < 0.0f) gy = 0.0f;
    return gy + AF_TAXI_CLEARANCE;
}

static inline void airplane_spawn_defaults(AirplaneState *a, int id, int scene_id,
                                          float x, float z, float yaw) {
    memset(a, 0, sizeof(*a));
    a->active = 1;
    a->id = id;
    a->scene_id = scene_id;
    a->x = x;
    a->z = z;
    a->yaw = yaw;
    a->y = af_ground_y(x, z);
    a->health = (float)af_hull();
    a->occupant_player_id = -1;
    a->grounded = 1;
}

- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn -- the two quadcopters (founder 2026-10-31: "next we want to add
      ;; more aircraft can we add a basic drone and a mini fly drone?").
      ;;
      ;; The point of a drone next to the helicopter is that it has NO LAG: the heli's collective lever and
      ;; airframe tilt take real ticks to become velocity, while a quadcopter just tilts its rotors and goes.
      ;; So this mod is the airframe, and packages/simulation/drone_flight.h is the immediate-thrust loop:
      ;;   RECON     a stable medium chassis that hovers and takes a knock
      ;;   FLY       a 45 g micro that is hyper-responsive, fast, buffeted by weather, and bounces off walls
      ;;             instead of stopping dead
      ;;
      ;; Scalar-only I32, fixed point, total functions, same convention as buggy_rules.prn and
      ;; rocket_car_rules.prn: speeds in units/tick x 1000, response/grip in permille of full authority.
      ;; The host clamps its own inputs. Retune here, `make regen-drone-rules`.
      (module shankpit/drone-rules)
      (export drone-mass-grams drone-response-permille drone-top-speed-milli drone-climb-milli
              drone-yaw-rate-milli drone-drift-permille drone-bounce-permille drone-hull
              drone-shard-kills drone-gimbal-yaw-milli drone-gimbal-pitch-milli)
      (defn drone-kit [] : I32 0)   ; the mixer scale: 0 recon, 1 fly
      
      ;; both kinds are "< 1000 names, 2000 names" -> keep the two profiles in one place
      (defn drone-mass-grams [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 45 2500))
      
      ;; How hard the rotors answer: 650 is a balanced medium airframe, 1850 is a micro that snaps.
      (defn drone-response-permille [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 1850 650))
      
      ;; Units/tick x 1000: 1.8 for the recon (slower than a buggy, it is a camera), 3.4 for the micro.
      (defn drone-top-speed-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 3400 1800))
      
      (defn drone-climb-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 1400 900))
      
      ;; Degrees/tick x 1000.
      (defn drone-yaw-rate-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 2200 900))
      
      ;; NOTE: parena emits a defn as a GLOBAL C function, so this must not be named `clamp` -- the
      ;; rocket car's mod already exports that one and the two .c files link into the same binaries.
      (defn drone-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32
        (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))
      
      ;; Weather drift, permille of buffeting: a recon feels a quarter of the storm, the 45 g micro feels
      ;; twice it -- which is why you do not fly the little one through a tempest.
      (defn drone-drift-permille [(kind : I32) (storm : I32)] : I32
        (drone-clamp -4000 4000
          (if (= kind 1)
            (* (drone-clamp 0 1000 storm) 2)
            (/ (drone-clamp 0 1000 storm) 4))))
      
      ;; Hit the world: the recon stops dead (and loses a frame's worth of speed), the micro bounces, which
      ;; is the only reason a 45 g drone survives a corridor.
      (defn drone-bounce-permille [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 350 0))
      
      (defn drone-hull [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 12 60))
      
      ;; ---- shards -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; Founder: "wire the Mini Fly Drone to explode instantly upon any impact with a rigid shard". The 45 g
      ;; micro dies to ANY shard that touches it -- that is the whole point of flying it through a collapsing
      ;; building. The recon has a frame, so it takes a real hit: shard mass (grams) x relative speed
      ;; (units/tick x 1000) has to clear 40,000,000, i.e. a 15 kg chunk has to be doing ~2.7 units/tick,
      ;; about what the top of a collapse does. Mass 0 is dust and hits nothing.
      (defn drone-shard-kills [(kind : I32) (mass-grams : I32) (rel-speed-milli : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1)
          (if (> mass-grams 0) 1 0)
          (if (> (* (if (< mass-grams 0) 0 mass-grams) (if (< rel-speed-milli 0) 0 rel-speed-milli)) 40000000) 1 0)))
      
      ;; ---- the gimbal ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; What makes the recon a camera and not a plane: its head turns independently of where it is pointing.
      ;; Milli-degrees, and both are real limits -- a gimbal is a mechanism, not free look. The micro has no
      ;; gimbal at all (a 45 g airframe cannot carry one), so its head is nearly fixed forward.
      (defn drone-gimbal-yaw-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 20000 90000))
      
      (defn drone-gimbal-pitch-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 25000 60000))
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_drone_rules.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # gen_drone_rules.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/drone_rules.c from PARENA.
      #
      # The two quadcopters' airframes are decision logic (response rate, top speed, climb, yaw, weather
      # drift, bounce, hull), so they live in PARENA with the rest of the rules:
      #   PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn
      # packages/simulation/drone_flight.h keeps the immediate-thrust integration and collision; this is
      # the numbers. Usage: scripts/gen_drone_rules.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout, or PARENA_DIR)
      set -euo pipefail
      root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
      parena_dir="${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}"
      if [ -x "$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      elif [ -x "$parena_dir/parena" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/parena"
      else
          (cd "$parena_dir" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      fi
      "$parena_bin" build "$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn" \
          -o "$root/packages/simulation/drone_rules.c"
      echo "regenerated packages/simulation/drone_rules.c"
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/drone_rules_host.h
  content: |
      /* drone_rules_host.h -- installs the PARENA quadcopter models into drone_flight.h.
       * The rules live in PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn, generated into drone_rules.c (do not edit
       * it; `make regen-drone-rules`). A host that simulates drones (apps/lobby, apps/server) includes this
       * header, links drone_rules.c, and calls drone_rules_install() once at startup. With nothing installed
       * drone_flight.h's own built-in defaults are used, so tests that just include it are unchanged. */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_DRONE_RULES_HOST_H
      #define SHANKPIT_DRONE_RULES_HOST_H
      
      #include "drone_flight.h"
      
      /* PARENA-generated (drone_rules.c) */
      int drone_mass_grams(int kind);
      int drone_response_permille(int kind);
      int drone_top_speed_milli(int kind);
      int drone_climb_milli(int kind);
      int drone_yaw_rate_milli(int kind);
      int drone_bounce_permille(int kind);
      int drone_hull(int kind);
      int drone_drift_permille(int kind, int storm);
      int drone_shard_kills(int kind, int mass_grams, int rel_speed_milli);
      int drone_gimbal_yaw_milli(int kind);
      int drone_gimbal_pitch_milli(int kind);
      
      static const DroneRules g_drone_rules_parena = {
          drone_mass_grams, drone_response_permille, drone_top_speed_milli, drone_climb_milli,
          drone_yaw_rate_milli, drone_drift_permille, drone_bounce_permille, drone_hull,
          drone_shard_kills, drone_gimbal_yaw_milli, drone_gimbal_pitch_milli,
      };
      
      static inline void drone_rules_install(void) { drone_set_rules(&g_drone_rules_parena); }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_DRONE_RULES_HOST_H */

      #define CUSTOM_LEVEL_DOOR_OPEN_Y_OFFSET 1000.0f
      static inline void phys_set_custom_level_box_y(int box_index, int is_open) {
          if (box_index < 0 || box_index >= CUSTOM_LEVEL_MAX_BOXES) return;
          int slot = box_index + 1;
          if (slot >= g_custom_level_count) return;
          g_custom_level_geo[slot].y = is_open
              ? g_custom_level_box_authored_y[slot] - CUSTOM_LEVEL_DOOR_OPEN_Y_OFFSET
              : g_custom_level_box_authored_y[slot];
      }
      
      // phys_custom_level_box_pos -- real, current x/y/z of a custom-level box's own authored center
      // (Story System Phase 1: what a door script's "distance to nearest player" input is measured
      // against). Returns 0 (out/unwritten) for an out-of-range box_index.
      static inline int phys_custom_level_box_pos(int box_index, float *x, float *y, float *z) {
          if (box_index < 0 || box_index >= CUSTOM_LEVEL_MAX_BOXES) return 0;
          int slot = box_index + 1;
          if (slot >= g_custom_level_count) return 0;
          *x = g_custom_level_geo[slot].x;

  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """local_nock.py -- dependency-free local stand-in for the IDUNA NOCK map tooling.
      
      SHANKPIT's in-game editor already speaks a small HTTP contract for "live editing sessions"
      (packages/world/edit_sync.h <-> IDUNA/internal/http/handlers/shankpit_edit_sessions.go). This
      serves that same contract locally, so the cloud tools being unreachable stops nothing:
      
        * the browser editor here and the native client join the SAME session, so an edit made in either
          place shows up in the other (the client pushes avatar/spawner/box events and reloads the working
          level when the browser posts a "level" event);
        * levels are plain JSON files in levels/, one per map -- maps are code, reviewable and diffable;
        * every save is git add + git commit (no push: that's still a deliberate human step).
      
        python3 tools/local_nock.py --port 8787
        # browser: http://127.0.0.1:8787
        # game (join the session id the browser shows, or start one and paste it in):
        SHANKPIT_EDIT_SESSIONS_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions \
          ./bin/shank_lobby --edit-map levels/starter.json --edit-live
      
      Wire contract (matches the Go handler, which the C client is written against):
        GET  /                                        browser editor
        GET  /api/levels                              {"levels":[{name,walls,bytes,...}]}
        GET  /api/levels/<name>                       one level (native export JSON)
        PUT  /api/levels/<name>                       save to levels/<name>.json (+ git commit)
        POST /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions           {"id":"<32 hex>","level_id":N,"level_name":"..","seq":0}
        GET  /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>?since=N&wait=S   long-poll {"seq":N,"events":[...]}
        POST /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>/events          {"source","kind","data"}
        PUT  /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>/level           working draft (browser pushes)
        GET  /api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions/<id>/level           the native export the client loads
      
      Sessions live in memory only (an editing room, not a record), exactly like IDUNA's: a restart ends
      the room and both sides make a new one. Saving is what makes a level durable.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import argparse
      import json
      import os
      import re
      import secrets
      import subprocess
      import sys
      import threading
      import time
      from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
      from urllib.parse import unquote, parse_qs, urlparse
      
      SLUG_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$")
      SESSION_PREFIX = "/api/v1/shankpit-edit-sessions"
      LEVELS_PREFIX = "/api/levels"
      MAX_BODY = 4 << 20          # a whole level draft; IDUNA's cap for the same reason
      MAX_EVENT_BODY = 64 << 10   # one event is small; keep the log's per-entry cost bounded too
      MAX_EVENTS = 2000
      MAX_WAIT = 25
      EVENT_KINDS = {
          "spawner", "avatar", "spawn_mode", "teleport",
          "box_add", "box_move", "box_size", "box_del", "hello", "level", "save",
      }
      HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
      
      
      class BodyTooLarge(Exception):
          """Raised by Handler._body when Content-Length exceeds the cap (answered as 413)."""
      
      
      def validate_level(doc):
          """The minimum a level must have to be usable: an object with a walls array of boxes."""
          if not isinstance(doc, dict):
              raise ValueError("level must be a JSON object")
          walls = doc.get("walls")
          if not isinstance(walls, list):
              raise ValueError('level needs a "walls" array')
          for i, w in enumerate(walls):
              if not isinstance(w, dict):
                  raise ValueError(f"wall {i} is not an object")
              missing = [k for k in ("x", "y", "z", "sx", "sy", "sz") if k not in w]
              if missing:
                  raise ValueError(f"wall {i} is missing {', '.join(missing)}")
          return doc

  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/vehicle_burn_rules.prn -- when a car catches fire, how long it burns, and what the\n;; fire LOOKS like (founder 2026-10-31: \"use the shaders from bedrock racers on fire for when a car\n;; is about to blow up or whatever\").\n;;\n;; The look is not invented here: Bedrock Racers' stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_fx.prn already has the\n;; fire-fx curve that reads well on a burning car -- it SWELLS FAST (a car that catches fire is\n;; visibly alight within a couple of frames) and DIES SLOWLY (it keeps glowing after the fire is\n;; out), and its light flickers around 1.4-2.4 \"a car's worth\". Those constants are copied below, in\n;; the same units where they make sense: fire-fx is permille of full, rise/fall are permille of the\n;; remaining distance closed per tick.\n;;\n;; What is new here is the DESTRUCTION ladder, which Bedrock Racers does not have (its cars are out\n;; or on fire, never dying): after a threshold a car smokes, then burns (losing hull every tick),\n;; then detonates. So a player gets a real warning window -- smoke, then flame -- before the blast.\n;;\n;; All fixed point I32, scalar, total. Speeds/hull in whole points, rates per tick.\n(module shankpit/vehicle-burn-rules)\n(export vehicle-hull vehicle-fire-threshold vehicle-smoke-threshold\n        vehicle-fire-fx-rise-milli vehicle-fire-fx-fall-milli\n        vehicle-burn-hp-per-tick vehicle-burn-detonate-ticks\n        vehicle-fire-light-min-milli vehicle-fire-light-max-milli\n        vehicle-drama-rise-milli vehicle-drama-fall-milli\n        vehicle-burn-state vehicle-smoke-permille vehicle-impact-damage\n        vehicle-blast-radius-milli vehicle-blast-damage)\n\n;; ---- hulls ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; cars: the buggy's own 300 (local_game.h buggy_spawn_defaults). The rocket car is a buggy with a\n;; tank on the back, so it is the same hull -- an explosion risk, not a tougher car.\n(defn vehicle-hull [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (case kind\n    1 300   ; rocket car\n    300))\n\n;; ---- the ladder -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; A quarter hull or less is a car about to go, which is the warning the player gets. Above the smoke\n;; line it still runs (slowly, on a bent frame).\n(defn vehicle-fire-threshold [] : I32 75)\n(defn vehicle-smoke-threshold [] : I32 150)\n\n;; 0 fine, 1 smoking, 2 on fire, 3 gone.\n(defn vehicle-burn-state [(hp : I32) (burning-ticks : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= hp 0)\n    3\n    (if (or (< hp (vehicle-fire-threshold)) (> burning-ticks 0))\n      2\n      (if (< hp (vehicle-smoke-threshold)) 1 0))))\n\n;; How thick the smoke is, permille: nothing above the smoke line, all of it at fire, and a burning\n;; car smokes at full until it goes -- smoke is the tell you can see across the map.\n(defn vehicle-smoke-permille [(hp : I32) (burning-ticks : I32)] : I32\n  (let [s (vehicle-burn-state hp burning-ticks)]\n    (if (= s 1) 420 (if (or (= s 2) (= s 3)) 1000 0))))\n\n;; ---- the fire curve (Bedrock Racers br_fx.prn) -------------------------------------------------------\n(defn vehicle-fire-fx-rise-milli [] : I32 250)   ; br fx-fire-rise 0.25\n(defn vehicle-fire-fx-fall-milli [] : I32 60)    ; br fx-fire-fall 0.06\n\n;; Hull lost per tick while burning. 5 s at 60 Hz from the fire line is a long, readable window: you\n;; can get out, or get clear.\n(defn vehicle-burn-hp-per-tick [] : I32 1)\n\n;; ~5 s at 60 Hz. Bedrock Racers burns until it is put out; a car in SHANKPIT is scrap after this.\n(defn vehicle-burn-detonate-ticks [] : I32 300)\n\n;; br_fx draws a burning car's light between 1.4 and 2.4 (milli-units here).\n(defn vehicle-fire-light-min-milli [] : I32 1400)\n(defn vehicle-fire-light-max-milli [] : I32 2400)\n\n;; br_fx's drama scalar: jumps up at the event, ebbs away at 2.5% of the gap per tick.\n(defn vehicle-drama-rise-milli [] : I32 200)\n(defn vehicle-drama-fall-milli [] : I32 25)\n\n;; ---- crashes ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; Kinetic damage, GTA-style: mass x delta-v^2, and a 0.5 unit/tick scuff costs nothing. The divisor\n;; is tuned so a buggy at full speed into a wall (about 5 units/tick, 900 kg) is ~45 hull, i.e. you\n;; need to be reckless a few times, not once.\n(defn vehicle-impact-damage [(mass-kg : I32) (delta-v-milli : I32)] : I32\n  (let [(dv (if (< delta-v-milli 0) (- 0 delta-v-milli) delta-v-milli))\n         (ke (/ (* (if (< mass-kg 0) 0 mass-kg) (* dv dv)) 1000))]\n    (if (<= dv 500) 0 (/ ke 100))))\n\n;; The blast a burning car finally makes, in thousandths of a world unit and hull points.\n(defn vehicle-blast-radius-milli [] : I32 8000)\n(defn vehicle-blast-damage [] : I32 250)\n"
}

A 5 s window from the fire line is long and readable: you can\n;; get out, or get clear.\n(defn vehicle-burn-hp-per-tick [] : I32 1)\n\n;; ~5 s at 60 Hz. Bedrock Racers burns until it is put out; a car in SHANKPIT is scrap after this.\n(defn vehicle-burn-detonate-ticks [] : I32 300)\n\n;; br_fx lights a burning car between 1.4 and 2.4 (milli-units here) -- the flicker is the tell.\n(defn vehicle-fire-light-min-milli [] : I32 1400)\n(defn vehicle-fire-light-max-milli [] : I32 2400)\n\n;; br_fx's drama scalar: jumps up at the event, ebbs away slowly after.\n(defn vehicle-drama-rise-milli [] : I32 200)\n(defn vehicle-drama-fall-milli [] : I32 25)\n\n;; ---- crashes ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n(defn vb-abs [(x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x 0) (- 0 x) x))\n(defn vb-max [(a : I32) (b : I32)] : I32 (if (> a b) a b))\n\n;; Kinetic damage: mass x delta-v^2, and a scuff below 0.5 units/tick costs nothing.
