  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/vehicle_burn_rules.prn -- when a car catches fire, how long it burns, and what the\n;; fire LOOKS like (founder 2026-10-31: \"use the shaders from bedrock racers on fire for when a car\n;; is about to blow up or whatever\").\n;;\n;; The look is not invented here: Bedrock Racers' stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_fx.prn already has the\n;; fire-fx curve that reads well on a burning car -- it SWELLS FAST (a car that catches fire is\n;; visibly alight within a few frames) and DIES SLOWLY (it keeps glowing after the fire is out), and\n;; its light flickers around 1.4-2.4 \"a car's worth\". Those constants are copied below, in the units\n;; this mod uses: fire-fx is permille of full, rise/fall are permille of the remaining gap closed\n;; per tick.\n;;\n;; What is new is the DESTRUCTION ladder, which Bedrock Racers does not have (its cars are out or on\n;; fire, never dying): after a threshold a car smokes, then burns (losing hull every tick), then\n;; detonates, so a player gets a real warning window -- smoke, then flame -- before the blast.\n;;\n;; All fixed point I32, scalar, total. Hull in whole points, rates per tick.\n(module shankpit/vehicle-burn-rules)\n(export vehicle-hull vehicle-fire-threshold vehicle-smoke-threshold\n        vehicle-fire-fx-rise-milli vehicle-fire-fx-fall-milli\n        vehicle-burn-hp-centi-per-tick vehicle-burn-detonate-ticks\n        vehicle-fire-light-min-milli vehicle-fire-light-max-milli\n        vehicle-drama-rise-milli vehicle-drama-fall-milli\n        vehicle-burn-state vehicle-smoke-permille vehicle-impact-damage\n        vehicle-blast-radius-milli vehicle-blast-damage)\n\n;; ---- hulls ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; The rocket car is a buggy with a tank on the back: same hull, an explosion risk rather than a\n;; tougher car. 300 matches local_game.h's buggy_spawn_defaults.\n(defn vehicle-hull [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 300 300))\n\n;; ---- the ladder -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; A quarter hull or less is a car about to go, which is the warning the player gets. Above the smoke\n;; line it still runs, on a bent frame.\n(defn vehicle-fire-threshold [] : I32 75)\n(defn vehicle-smoke-threshold [] : I32 150)\n\n;; 0 fine, 1 smoking, 2 on fire, 3 gone.\n(defn vehicle-burn-state [(hp : I32) (burning-ticks : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= hp 0)\n    3\n    (if (< hp (vehicle-fire-threshold))\n      2\n      (if (> burning-ticks 0) 2 (if (< hp (vehicle-smoke-threshold)) 1 0)))))\n\n;; How thick the smoke is, permille: nothing above the smoke line, all of it at fire, and a burning\n;; car smokes at full until it goes -- smoke is the tell you can see across the map.\n(defn vehicle-smoke-permille [(hp : I32) (burning-ticks : I32)] : I32\n  (if (>= hp (vehicle-smoke-threshold))\n    0\n    (if (or (>= hp (vehicle-fire-threshold)) (> burning-ticks 0)) 1000 420)))\n\n;; ---- the fire curve (Bedrock Racers br_fx.prn) -------------------------------------------------------\n(defn vehicle-fire-fx-rise-milli [] : I32 250)   ; br fx-fire-rise 0.25\n(defn vehicle-fire-fx-fall-milli [] : I32 60)    ; br fx-fire-fall 0.06\n\n;; Hull lost per tick while burning, in hundredths. 25 = 0.25 hp/tick, so the 75 hp between the fire\n;; line and zero takes 300 ticks: the WARN window and the burn clock are the same 5 s. Burning slower\n;; than the hull above the fire line would make detonate-ticks a lie.\n(defn vehicle-burn-hp-centi-per-tick [] : I32 25)\n\n;; ~5 s at 60 Hz. Bedrock Racers burns until it is put out; a car in SHANKPIT is scrap after this.\n(defn vehicle-burn-detonate-ticks [] : I32 300)\n\n;; br_fx lights a burning car between 1.4 and 2.4 (milli-units here) -- the flicker is the tell.\n(defn vehicle-fire-light-min-milli [] : I32 1400)\n(defn vehicle-fire-light-max-milli [] : I32 2400)\n\n;; br_fx's drama scalar: jumps up at the event, ebbs away slowly after.\n(defn vehicle-drama-rise-milli [] : I32 200)\n(defn vehicle-drama-fall-milli [] : I32 25)\n\n;; ---- crashes ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n(defn vb-abs [(x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x 0) (- 0 x) x))\n(defn vb-max [(a : I32) (b : I32)] : I32 (if (> a b) a b))\n\n;; Kinetic damage: mass x delta-v^2, nothing below 0.5 units/tick. The damage is deliberately small\n;; relative to hull (300): a 900 kg buggy straight into a wall at 5 units/tick costs ~22, so a crash\n;; is a warning, not a death -- you keep hitting things until the car is already smoking.\n;; Staged divisions keep every intermediate inside I32 (900 * 5000 = 4.5M, then 4500 * 5000 = 22.5M).\n(defn vehicle-impact-damage [(mass-kg : I32) (delta-v-milli : I32)] : I32\n  (let [dv (vb-abs delta-v-milli)\n        m (vb-max 0 mass-kg)]\n    (if (<= dv 500)\n      0\n      (/ (* (/ (* m dv) 1000) dv) 1000000))))\n\n;; The blast a burning car finally makes, in thousandths of a world unit and hull points.\n(defn vehicle-blast-radius-milli [] : I32 8000)\n(defn vehicle-blast-damage [] : I32 250)\n"

/* draw_explosions -- ages every live blast: the fireball grows and cools over FX_BLAST_MS, a second
 * thinner shell flashes for the first third of it, and a ring of embers is thrown out and falls. */
static void draw_explosions(void) {
    unsigned int now = SDL_GetTicks();
    for (int i = 0; i < FX_BLAST_MAX; i++) {
        FxBlast *b = &g_fx_blast[i];
        if (!b->active) continue;
        unsigned int age_ms = now - b->t0;
        if (age_ms >= FX_BLAST_MS) { b->active = 0; continue; }
        float t = (float)age_ms / (float)FX_BLAST_MS;
        float heat = (b->weapon == WPN_MISSILE) ? 1.0f : 0.85f;   /* a rocket is the bigger fireball */
        float size = b->radius * (0.45f + 0.85f * sqrtf(t));
        fireball_draw(b->x, b->y, b->z, size, t, heat);
        if (t < 0.34f) fireball_draw(b->x, b->y, b->z, size * (0.55f + t), t * 2.9f, heat * 0.6f);

        glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
        glEnable(GL_BLEND);
        glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
        glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
        glPointSize(3.0f + 4.0f * (1.0f - t));
        glBegin(GL_POINTS);
        for (int s = 0; s < FX_SPARK_MAX; s++) {
            float ang = (float)s * 2.399963f;   /* golden angle: an even spray, no RNG */
            float up = 0.35f + 0.65f * (float)((s * 37) % 11) / 11.0f;
            float rad = size * (0.6f + 0.9f * t) * (0.55f + 0.45f * (float)((s * 53) % 7) / 7.0f);
            float fade = 1.0f - t;
            glColor4f(1.0f, 0.72f - 0.40f * t, 0.25f - 0.20f * t, fade);
            glVertex3f(b->x + cosf(ang) * rad,
                       b->y + up * size * (0.5f + 1.6f * t) - 2.5f * t * t,
                       b->z + sinf(ang) * rad);
        }
        glEnd();
        glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
        glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
        glDisable(GL_BLEND);
    }
}

The hull itself stays the server's (and the local sim's) to own: this is the warning and the\n * consequence the player sees. */\nstatic VehicleBurn g_vehicle_burn[MAX_BUGGIES];\nstatic float g_vehicle_burn_hp[MAX_BUGGIES];\nstatic unsigned int g_vehicle_burn_tick_n = 0;\n\nstatic void vehicle_burn_client(const BuggyState *b) {\n    if (!b || !b->active) return;\n    int slot = b->id % MAX_BUGGIES;\n    if (slot < 0) slot = 0;\n    VehicleBurn *v = &g_vehicle_burn[slot];\n    if (!v->active || v->seed != (unsigned int)b->id + 1u) {\n        vehicle_burn_reset(v, 0, (unsigned int)b->id + 1u);\n        g_vehicle_burn_hp[slot] = b->health;\n    }\n    /* the sim's hull is the truth: follow it when it changes (a crash, a repair), and let the fire\n       itself burn the copy down while the car is alight */\n    if (b->health > g_vehicle_burn_hp[slot]) g_vehicle_burn_hp[slot] = b->health;\n    int blast = vehicle_burn_tick(v, &g_vehicle_burn_hp[slot]);\n    g_vehicle_burn_tick_n++;\n    if (blast) fx_spawn_explosion(b->x, b->y + 0.6f, b->z, 3.2f, WPN_MISSILE);\n    if (v->fire_fx > 0.02f) {\n        float size = 0.55f + 1.35f * v->fire_fx;\n        float age = 0.42f + 0.25f * v->fire_fx;\n        fireball_draw(b->x, b->y + 0.9f, b->z, size, age, 1.0f);\n        if (v->fire_fx > 0.55f) fireball_draw(b->x + 0.6f, b->y + 1.7f, b->z - 0.5f, size * 0.62f, 0.3f, 0.82f);\n    }\n}\n\n/* draw_explosions -- ages every live blast: the fireball grows and cools over FX_BLAST_MS, a second\n * thinner shell flashes for the first third of it, and a ring of embers is thrown out and falls. */",

err == nil {\n\t\t\t\tyaw = float64(((deg % 360) + 360) % 360)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn kind, yaw, true\n}\n\n// rotatedVehicleSpawnName leaves ordinary names alone and carries a placed widget's rotation into a\n// vehicle spawn's yaw. A legacy buggy spawn stays a legacy buggy spawn.\nfunc rotatedVehicleSpawnName(name string, worldRotY int) string {\n\tkind, yaw, ok := vehicleSpawnKindYaw(name)\n\tif !ok || worldRotY%360 == 0 {\n\t\treturn name\n\t}\n\tif kind == \"buggy\" && strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(name), buggySpawnPrefix) {\n\t\treturn rotatedBuggySpawnName(name, worldRotY)\n\t}\n\tdeg := ((int(yaw)+worldRotY)%360 + 360) % 360\n\treturn fmt.Sprintf(\"%s_%s_%d\", vehicleSpawnPrefix, kind, deg)\n}\n\n// vehicleSpawnsForExport lists a spawn per tile wall, in wall order. y is the tile's top surface.\nfunc vehicleSpawnsForExport(walls []Wall) []VehicleSpawnExport {\n\tvar out []VehicleSpawnExport\n\tfor _, w := range walls {\n\t\tkind, yaw, ok := vehicleSpawnKindYaw(w.Name)\n\t\tif !ok {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tout = append(out, VehicleSpawnExport{Kind: kind, X: w.X, Y: w.Y + w.SY/2, Z: w.Z, Yaw: yaw})\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}",

> _Reasoning_
> Two real failures, both mine:
> 
> 1. Burn clock check: 25 centi × 75 hull = 1875 ≠ 100 × 300 = 30000. At 0.25/tick, 75 hull takes 300 ticks → 75 * 100 / 25 = 300 ticks. My equality test was wrong: correct identity is `burn_hp_centi_per_tick * detonate_ticks == 100 * fire_threshold` → 25*300 = 7500 = 100*75 ✓. Fix the test formula.
> 
> 2. "should be out: fire=1.0000 state=2" — repaired to 300 but state stays 2 because burning_ticks > 0 keeps `onfire` true forever. `onfire = ... || v->burning_ticks > 0` and burning_ticks only resets when `!smoking` — but while burning_ticks>0, onfire is true so `!smoking` is false, so it never resets. Infinite burn: a repaired car never goes out. That's a genuine bug in the ladder: the fire must be extinguishable above the fire line.
> 
> But the `burning_ticks > 0` clause exists so that once on fire, the car stays on fire even if hp ticks a bit above the threshold (it can't, hp only decreases while burning... except external repair). So the clause should be dropped: `onfire = !dead && *hp <= fire_threshold`. Then `else if (!smoking) burning_ticks = 0` correctly resets on repair. Simpler and no latch. Fix.
> 
> 3. gen script permission denied — need chmod +x. Also parena binary may not exist; try.

## 2026-10-31

- **feat(aircraft): the C-110 — a fixed-wing transport that has to be flown.** Founder: *"ok how about a basic prop plane c-110 or whatever the legendary ones are"*. Deliberately not a helicopter with wings: lift comes from AIRSPEED, so this is the one vehicle in the engine that cannot hover. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/airplane_rules.prn` (generated to `packages/simulation/airplane_rules.c` by `scripts/gen_airplane_rules.sh` / `make regen-airplane-rules`, installed by `airplane_rules_host.h`): top speed 12 units/tick, stall 4.0 clean and 3.2 with flaps, liftoff 6.0, thrust 0.06 units/tick² at full throttle against a speed-proportional drag curve (which is what makes the takeoff run a real runway), and **lift as a v² law in permille of weight, exactly 1000 at 6.0 units/tick and exactly 0 at or below the stall however the nose is pointed** — a full back stick in a stall does not save it, it just makes the dive uglier. New `packages/simulation/airplane_flight.h` is the integration: throttle is a **lever** (SPACE up, CTRL down, it holds where you leave it), W/S elevator, A/D aileron, the pilot's heading is a tiller only with the wheels down and slow, and **a bank is what turns it** — every rate is heavy, so it turns like a transport and not like a quad. It lands and taxis instead of exploding, and a wall hit costs hull. `AirplaneState`/`MAX_AIRPLANES`/`VEH_AIRPLANE` join `protocol.h`; it ticks in `local_game.h` beside the drones; `vehicle_call.h` calls it 16 units ahead (an 18-unit wingspan called onto your toes is a collision) on the ground with the lever closed; E boards and leaves it; and it is drawn as a slab-sided transport — fuselage, high wing, tail, twin nacelles with counter-rotating props — so it reads as a plane from underneath, which is where players see it most. New sixth prefab **TRANSPORT** puts the C-110, helicopter, buggy and recon on the same four gadget keys. Deliberately NOT built, named rather than faked: **no cargo bay, no rear ramp, no airborne spawn, no cargo drops** — this is an airframe you can fly, land and roll, not a mobile base, and an interior portal/`Level` inside a moving hull is a much bigger piece of work than the plane. Verified: `make test-airplane-flight` (new) — at full throttle it rolls and then flies, liftoff on tick ~120 at ~6.6 units/tick after a real runway run; an idling aircraft never leaves the ground and builds no airspeed; **flaps lift off measurably earlier** (stall 3.2 vs 4.0); a stalled aircraft sinks with the nose falling even at full back stick; lift is quadratic (250 → 1000 permille for 5.0 → 6.0 units/tick) and zero below the stall; and 10 ticks of full aileron banks it ~40° and turns it only ~11°, i.e. inertia — plus `make test-vehicle-call` (the C-110 calls onto the ground ahead, lever closed, full health), `make test-kit` for the sixth prefab, `phone_test`, `make server` linking and `make check-windows` compiling all 93 lobby sources for mingw.
- **feat(drones): a shard kills the micro, and the recon gets a real gimbal.** Founder: *"wire the Mini Fly Drone to explode instantly upon any impact with a rigid shard"*, then *"and gimbal"*. Both belong in PARENA, not in the renderer. Two new rules in `drone_rules.prn` (regenerated): `drone-shard-kills(kind, mass-grams, rel-speed-milli)` — **any** shard with mass kills the 45 g micro, while the recon's frame needs `mass x relative speed > 40,000,000` (a 15 kg chunk doing ~2.7 units/tick, about what the top of a collapse moves), so dust and pebbles bounce off it — and `drone-gimbal-yaw/pitch-milli` — the recon's head swings **90°** with **60°** of pitch, the micro's 20°/25°. New host side in `drone_flight.h`: `drone_shard_contact()` (point shard vs the airframe's own radius, 1.2 m recon / 0.35 m micro, deciding through the rule), `drone_kill()`, `drone_eject_pilot()` (thrown clear where it died, falling, not riding a wreck), and `drone_gimbal_track()`/`drone_gimbal_view_yaw()` (the offset clamped to the airframe's mechanical limits, because a gimbal is a mechanism and not free look). `DroneState` gains `destroyed`, `gimbal_yaw`, `gimbal_pitch`. Wired in the lobby: `drone_shard_sweep()` runs every frame over the live debris (`g_brick_debris`, the flakes a cracking wall throws — this build has no simulated structural shards, so mass is estimated from each flake's own volume and its per-SECOND velocity converted to the per-TICK flight model), a hit ejects the pilot and fires a real fireball (0.6 units for the micro, 1.6 for the recon); and the mouse now drives the drone's head through `drone_gimbal_clamp()` instead of a free camera. Honest consequence, stated rather than hidden: because the only live debris is cosmetic, **nothing in this build can currently break a recon drone with a shard** — the rule and the sweep are real and tested, the mass-bearing shards are not (BrickBodies/GRB has no live instance in the lobby). Verified: `make test-vehicle-call` — a shard 30 units away does not touch the micro, a 15 kg shard touching it does (and the dead drone cannot be hit twice), a 15 g stationary shard leaves the recon alive while a 15 kg shard at 3 units/tick breaks it, the pilot is ejected in place with `in_vehicle` cleared, the recon's gimbal clamps at its limits and follows exactly inside them, and the micro's head moves far less — plus all earlier traffic/vehicle checks, `make test-kit`, `make server` linking and `make check-windows` compiling all 93 lobby sources for mingw.
- **feat(aircraft): two quadcopters — a recon drone and a mini fly drone — with their own PARENA airframes.** Founder: *"next we want to add more aircraft can we add a basic drone and a mini fly drone?"* A drone sits beside the helicopter as a different airframe rather than a reskin: the heli's collective lever and airframe tilt take real ticks to become motion, while a quadcopter tilts its rotors and goes — **translational thrust hits velocity immediately**, which is exactly why you would fly one into a window the heli overshoots. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/drone_rules.prn` (generated to `packages/simulation/drone_rules.c` by `scripts/gen_drone_rules.sh` / `make regen-drone-rules`, installed by `drone_rules_host.h`): two profiles, `DRONE_KIND_RECON` (2.5 kg, response 650 permille, 1.8 units/tick, 60 hull, stops dead on a wall) and `DRONE_KIND_FLY` (45 g micro, response 1850, 3.4 units/tick, 12 hull, **bounces** off the world), plus weather drift where the recon feels a quarter of a storm and the micro feels twice it. New `packages/simulation/drone_flight.h` is the immediate-thrust loop and the spawn/enter/exit helpers; `DroneState`/`MAX_DRONES`/`VEH_DRONE` join `protocol.h`, drones tick in `local_game.h` beside the helicopters, and `vehicle_call.h` calls either kind onto the gadget keys (`KIT_ITEM_DRONE` / `KIT_ITEM_MINI_DRONE`, and a fifth prefab **AERIAL** puts DRONE / MINI DRONE / HELICOPTER / BUGGY on the same four keys RUNNER uses). Both are drawn as a body plus four spinning rotors at their own scale with a red (recon) or green (micro) nav light, so the two read apart at range. Deliberately NOT done and named: no gimbal/broadcast-camera link to a stream (the founder's F3 idea needs a camera route this engine does not have), no per-drone damage from collisions or weapons, and no snapshot replication of drones to remote clients. The storm the airframes feel is `g_sky_weather.storm` read once per frame into `drone_set_storm` -- local, like the environment matrix, not a wire field, so a remote client would have to derive it the same way. Verified: `make test-vehicle-call` — both kinds call, arrive occupied and keep their kind; **both move on tick one** (the property that distinguishes them from the heli); the micro outruns the recon over 180 ticks; the same 900‰ storm deflects the micro >1.5x the recon; and against a real `map_geo` wall the micro bounces while the recon stops, with neither passing through — plus the existing buggy / rocket-car / helicopter checks still pass, `make test-kit` for the fifth prefab, `phone_test`, `make server` linking, and `make check-windows` compiling all 93 lobby sources for mingw.
- **feat(kit): the three VEHICLE gadgets — buggy, rocket car, helicopter — are call items on the gadget keys.** Founder: *"add buggy, rocket car, and hellicopter to the gadgets we already have the buggy and the hellicopter the rocket car implementation is in bedrock racers im not sure if that code is in PELLEGRINO or what but it was at wotan i dunno the graphics for those cars are perfect too for the models"*. The rocket car was not in PELLEGRINO at all — it is **PARENA**, `stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_phys.prn` ("the rocket car, the ball, and the world they share", the Tesla-Roadster-style car with four lift nozzles and fans). So `KIT_ITEM_BUGGY` / `KIT_ITEM_ROCKET_CAR` / `KIT_ITEM_HELI` were added to `packages/common/kit.h` plus a fourth prefab **RUNNER** (`` ` `` BUGGY, `-` ROCKET CAR, `=` HELICOPTER, `C` canister) so all three are reachable without building a kit. New `packages/simulation/vehicle_call.h` is the verb: spawn the vehicle 7 units in front of the player and seat them in it through the **existing** `buggy_try_enter` / helicopter occupant path, so the camera, chase steering, exit offsets and draw code are the same code and not a second vehicle implementation. Refusals are real: not a call item, already driving, on the vehicle cooldown, or no free slot in this scene's garage — refusing beats silently recycling someone else's car. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/rocket_car_rules.prn` (generated to `packages/simulation/rocket_car_rules.c` by the new `scripts/gen_rocket_car_rules.sh` / `make regen-rocket-car-rules`, installed by `rocket_car_rules_host.h`) ports the part of BR's car that fits this chassis: **one air tank pays for everything** (lift 26/s, boost 22/s, refills 34/s, 48/s on a surface), the rear-nozzle boost scales with what is left in it ("empty, the car still turns at a quarter rate — never helpless"), and a fan suspension holds the belly 2.6 units off the surface instead of riding wheels. `BuggyState` gains `rocket`/`tank` appended after the `snap_*` client-local scratch fields, and `simulate_buggy_state` routes a rocket buggy to the new `simulate_rocket_car_state`. Deliberately NOT ported and named as such: BR's strafe/attitude axes (this chassis has no separate axes — the camera is the steering, like the buggy) and wall/ceiling driving. The look keeps the buggy body (which is already this engine's car) and adds what makes a rocket car readable at distance: four additive lift-jet plumes under it and a rear booster, both brighter with the air left. Verified: `make test-vehicle-call` (new — a called buggy spawns ahead on -Z and seats the player, a second call honours the cooldown, the rocket car arrives hovering with a full tank, the helicopter arrives clear of the ground and occupied, non-vehicle items and full garages are refused, and the profile is measurably different: **the rocket car outran the buggy over 240 ticks, spent air under throttle, refilled at idle, and sat down on its belly with an empty tank without sinking through the floor**), plus `make test-kit` and `phone_test` updated for the fourth prefab. NOT done: no kit-call packet, so the three keys are local/sandbox only and do nothing in `STATE_GAME_NET` (the server owns spawning); no per-call HUD readout of the air tank; and the BR car's own mesh data was not lifted — the models here are this engine's box-built car plus the nozzle plumes.
- **feat(kit): four gadget keys, three kit apps, and the pages are HTML+CSS painted by PELLEGRINO.** Founder: *"we need to add kit affordances for these items have it be so that you can ` and - and = so 3 additional gadgets in additon to 1-9 or -0 ... and we can also set f and c i suppose ... oh wait f is already taken for vehicle entry thats fine we can dont need f same spec"*, then *"give us 2 apps one to map the current kit to keys and another app to select the kit from the kits menenu (we can select a kit that is already pre built) and then another app for building kits keep it simple while including all the affordances use basic html and CSS and PELLEGRINO (clone it down) tech for rendering the ui"*. New `packages/common/kit.h`: **14 bind slots** -- the ten number keys plus `` ` ``, `-`, `=` and `C` (F deliberately excluded, it enters vehicles), and the ten digits are never rebound by a prefab because that is where a player's weapons already live. Items are not a new inventory: each one is an input this engine already acts on (`PHEROMONE` -> `in_pheromone`, `ABILITY`, `SECONDARY`, `RELOAD`), so a kit is a key->real-action map rather than a parallel universe of fake gadgets. Three prefabs (SCOUT / BREACHER / HUNTER, genuinely different shapes), cycling that wraps through every item and back to empty, and a **draft** so the builder never trashes the kit you are carrying. Three phone apps: **KITS** (pick the prefab that goes live), **KIT MAP** (rebind the live kit's keys, ENTER clears), **KIT BUILD** (edit the draft, ENTER saves it over the live kit, with `*` marking any row that differs). Rendering is `kit_page_*` HTML with a small `<style>` block, painted by **PELLEGRINO's own layout engine** through `os_menu_set_page`/`os_menu_draw` (`packages/pellegrino_embed/kit_page_gl.h`) -- deliberately not the in-phone browser, which is a real navigator that can only show URLs; a text fallback draws every row when that surface is unavailable so no app is ever a blank rectangle. PELLEGRINO is cloned at `../PELLEGRINO` per the founder's instruction. Gameplay wiring: `` ` ``, `-`, `=` and `C` arm a ~150 ms pulse of their bound item, consumed by the same input assembly the keyboard already feeds (all four on the net path, the canister on the local path), and the orb keeps ` on any kit where that slot is empty. Verified: `make test-kit` (slot/key mapping incl. the deliberate F hole, prefab shape, full wrap-around cycling, out-of-range slots ignored rather than clamped, select-then-draft isolation, three pages containing real markup, and a too-small buffer refused instead of truncated) and `phone_test` (KITS selects BREACHER, KIT MAP cycles `` ` `` PHEROMONE->ABILITY and clears it, KIT BUILD leaves the live kit alone until SAVE). NOT done: no server-side authority for a kit yet (the effects are the hook point), the kit does not persist across launches, and the two non-canister gadget pulses are net-path only.
- **feat(phone): the tech tree is spendable, and its first line lengthens pheromone immunity.** Founder: *"stat adding tech tree we can have improved pherimone balls it should increase your seconds of immunity by 2 seconds per level upt to 5 points build the ui into the phone app ui that you pull up with P."* `BP_APP_TECHTREE` already existed but was a read-only, host-fed list of names with `[OK]` flags -- nothing could be bought and nothing it displayed did anything. It now has real levels, a real point cost, and one real effect: `PHEROMONE IMMUNITY +2s`, five levels, feeding `witness_ai_set_pheromone_grace_bonus_ms`. The number lives once in `phone.h` (`phone_tech_bonus_ms`), so the UI's readout and the zombie AI's actual window cannot drift apart. The phone stays pure (spends the point, returns `BP_FX_TECH_UPGRADE` with the node index); the lobby owns what a level is worth and pushes it the instant it is bought, so the very next canister carries the longer window. Points are earned from the XP this build already awards -- 1 per 500, re-derived every sync, so there is no second save file to drift and no way to be double-charged by a level load. The app draws `LV x/5` with a five-pip bar, the point balance, the resulting window in seconds with the base called out, and a real "no points" line instead of silently ignoring ENTER. Verified: `phone_test` (a SELECT spends one point and emits the upgrade effect; nine further presses stop exactly at level 5 with 0 points; a capped-and-broke SELECT is a no-op; a negative balance clamps) and `make test-pheromone-grenade` (with the maxed line installed a canister's window measures >17 s against the 9 s base). NOT done: the tree has exactly one node (the other eleven slots are unused), points are awarded at a fixed XP ratio rather than per level-up curve, and the bonus is pushed in-process -- there is no packet, so a remote server-authoritative match would not see it yet.
- **feat(zombies): the lure feeds, the horde navigates, and your pheromone buys you a window that closes.** Founder: *"zombies shouldnt just walk into walls ... sometimes they should but that is when they are trying to break walls down they should have some ability to navigate the terrain i think citizens already do that also the zombies dont seem to respond to ferimone balls it should make them hungry and somewhat aggressive also it should guide them to the spot also they should attack the player ad the citizens when they are hungry or aggressive there should be some threshold where they dont attack you if your pherimone caused their hunger and agression but that should be like a fading memory your zombies wont attack you at first but they forget pretty quick and they will target you for the next snack after your window runs out so you need to be intentional with your phermone balls to move them around the map as there are more of them."* Three separate defects, one cause: the systems were all built and none of them were talking to each other. (1) **Walking into walls.** `witness_ai_tick`'s wall pass called `wai_avoid_walls(..., g_wall_hit_hook != NULL)`, and the real game always installs that hook, so every zombie was `relentless` -- route planning skipped -- and the whole horde ground the straight line into the nearest face and clawed it from 100 m out. It is now a real decision: breach only when the target is within `WITNESS_AI_ZOMBIE_BREACH_TARGET_RANGE` (70 m, i.e. the fight is right there) and the zombie is HUNTING/FRENZIED, otherwise it plans a route exactly as a citizen already did; the existing `g_wai_breach` stop-plant-and-tear path is untouched, which is what keeps wall-breaking working. (2) **Pheromone balls did nothing.** A marker only redirected the steering of a zombie with no hero lock -- it fed nothing, so a lure moved a horde around and left it exactly as harmless as it found it, and the marker's own thrower was never recorded at all (the parallel `g_pheromone_owner1[]` array now does, rather than adding a field to ported BIG_O code). A zombie now gains `WITNESS_AI_PHEROMONE_HUNGER_PER_SEC`/`_AGGRESSION_PER_SEC` (rate-clamped against the real tick delta) while it is steering to a canister, so the lure genuinely makes it dangerous, and it remembers whose canister recruited it. (3) **They never attacked each other or you.** Targeting was gated on `hunger >= STARVING` (0.70) alone, so a fed but furious zombie stood next to a citizen and did nothing -- `zombie_values.h`'s whole aggression meter was computed every tick and never read. New PARENA rule `zombies-pheromone-should-hunt(hunger_milli, aggression_milli)` makes it hungry OR aggressive (0.40 / 0.45, deliberately unequal: hunger is "I need a meal", aggression is "something just happened"), and the fading memory is its sibling `zombies-pheromone-spares-thrower(grace_ms, thrower_alive)` -- `WITNESS_AI_PHEROMONE_GRACE_MS` (9 s) of immunity for the THROWER ONLY, checked before the hero is even sensed, with the owner cleared the moment it lapses so a later thrower is judged fresh. Citizens were never covered, so a lured horde eats the neighbourhood and remembers you late. Verified: `make test-pheromone-grenade` -- a canister raises a zombie's hunger 0.13 -> 1.00 and its aggression past 0.20, the thrower can stand in its face for 3 s untouched, and after the window the same zombie bites them; `make test-witness-ai-zombies` -- a zombie 290 m from its target with a wall between routes around the building with ZERO claw hits, while the existing close-range test still claws the same wall 27 times; plus the pocket-escape, day/night, per-role REFLUX and mark-2-marker tests all still pass. Not done: no controller/left-trigger throw binding beyond the existing `BTN_PHEROMONE`, no HUD readout of the grace countdown (the `witness_ai_zombie_grace_ms` accessor it would need exists), and "somewhat aggressive" is a hunger/aggression rate rather than a new mood state.

## 2026-10-30

- **fix(build): the Windows client did not compile — a lobby helper shadowed a generated rules function.** Found by actually cross-compiling: installed mingw-w64 plus the same SDL2 2.30.10 / SDL2_ttf 2.22.0 mingw kits `release.yml` downloads, then compiled every one of the 91 `LOBBY_SRC` files for `x86_64-w64-mingw32`. Exactly one failed, and it was mine from the lighting slice: `apps/lobby/src/main.c` reads `env_emissive_scale()` in the enemy-outline pass ~70 lines *before* defining it, so C inferred `int env_emissive_scale()` at the call and then rejected the real `static float env_emissive_scale(void)` as a conflicting type — and the name also shadowed PARENA's generated `int env_emissive_scale(int ambient_permille)` from `lighting_rules.c`, which is linked into the same binary. Two fixes: forward declarations for the three environment-matrix read helpers (`env_flashlight_range`, `env_flashlight_half_angle`, and the outline one) placed where the `g_env` state is declared, and the local helper renamed to `env_outline_emissive_scale` so it can never shadow a rules function again. This would have broken a native `make lobby` on Linux too — nobody had compiled the lobby outside CI, so only the Windows job could have caught it. New `scripts/check_windows_build.sh` + `make check-windows` compiles all `LOBBY_SRC` under mingw (headers only, no link, so no SDL2 .a/.dll or EDITOR.GAME objects needed) and reports the file and first errors, so this class of break is one command instead of one release cycle. Verified: 91/91 sources now compile, `make check-windows` passes, and the link is proven to close — of every symbol the 91 objects need, the ONLY unresolved ones are the 14 `editor_widget_*` functions `release.yml` supplies from its EDITOR.GAME checkout (nothing else is missing), and stubbing exactly those yields a real `PE32+ executable (console) x86-64`. The other half of the Windows job was re-run too: `release.yml`'s `dw_gui.exe` recipe, verbatim, against a fresh clone of DEADWEIGHT — links clean now that `core/draft.c` is in that hand-copied list. NOT verified: running any of these binaries (no Windows here) and the four Go/REDGARDEN/EDITOR.GAME OS apps, whose sibling repos aren't checked out in this sandbox.
- **feat(ocean): the archipelago gets water — a sea state, a wave field, and a hull that floats.** Founder paste (SP-ARCH-ENG-004): an archipelago battle royale on SHANKPIT, with client SQL ledgers, unified UDP streams, heightfield ocean, fractal destruction and island streaming. Scoped honestly in `docs/ARCHIPELAGO_NORTHSTAR.md` first, and the audit found that **three of the five sections describe things this monorepo has already built** under other names: §5's "stress propagation / load paths from anchors to foundations" is the structure cascade shipped this week, §5's node detachment is `bf_detect_at_parent`/`bf_damage_sphere` + rigid chunks, §2's append-only ledger is IDUNA's `event-stream`, and §3's unreliable-transform stream is `PACKET_SNAPSHOT`. Section §4 — water — had **literally zero code** anywhere in SHANKPIT (`grep` for buoyancy/wave/water_level: no hits), so that is the slice. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/ocean_rules.prn` (generated to `packages/simulation/ocean.c` by `scripts/gen_ocean_rules.sh`): five sea states from calm to tempest as ONE integer that every other number derives from, a three-layer cosine heightfield (deliberately NOT called Gerstner — no horizontal particle displacement, so no overhanging crest), submerged-fraction, planing lift that saturates with speed, and drag that grows with speed. New host `packages/simulation/ocean.h`: surface sampling, normals by central difference, and a probe-based hull (`ocean_vessel_forces`/`ocean_vessel_step`) integrating buoyancy against weight plus a pitch torque from the wave slope. The blueprint's "multi-threaded simulation loop" is explicitly rejected in the doc — this engine's netcode depends on one deterministic loop, and buoyancy is cheap enough to stay in it. Fixed a real, months-old gap to make it compile: **the C emitter had no `math/` primitive mapping at all** (documented as unstarted in `stdlib/math/math.prn`), so `math/cos` mangled into a call to a never-defined `math_cos()`; `src/emit.c` now lowers the qualified names to libm's `f
[...TRUNCATED DUE TO LENGTH...]
he existing debris path instead of hanging in the air. It is budgeted exactly like the cell pass: a parent over `BF_CHUNK_CELLS` (256), or one arriving with the chunk queue full, stays standing rather than half-detaching. Piece mass now follows the damage (`1 - removed/cells`), so a wall carved down to a stub weighs what is left of it and a shot-away pillar stops holding a roof up long before its last cell goes. Two real fixes came out of wiring it: (1) `structure_boxes_meet`'s tolerance is now a WELDING DISTANCE (`>= -tol`, not `> tol`), because authored geometry is routinely flush — a roof sitting exactly on a pillar's top face shares a face with zero overlap, and under the old rule no authored piece ever joined anything; (2) the load-time baseline was taken after `structure_evaluate`, which strips a failed piece's support, so every overloaded building was quietly baselined as "authored decoration" and stood forever — it is now taken on the support flood before any load verdict. The same fix taught the engine to collapse a structure the rules say cannot hold itself **at load, before the first frame**, instead of waiting for someone to shoot it. The rules' overflow guard also changed: `struct-holds-load` was comparing `mass x 1000` against `capacity x 850` in I32, which overflows for any real building (a concrete pier holds 72 million kg); it now divides the capacity before applying the 15%, and the C-side 2-million-kg clamp that had flattened every material into one capacity is replaced by a 2-billion-kg arithmetic ceiling that never decides a verdict. Verified: `make test-brick-world` — the wood-post level loses all 7 post cells and all 72 deck cells at load, both stop being solid immediately and two chunks are queued; the identical deck on a concrete post survives untouched with zero failures; the wall-only level leaves the layer off; every pre-existing check (magnum breach, hammer, claw, glass chunk, net apply, saved damage) still passes. `make test-structure` still passes. NOT verified: the lobby and server binaries are not compiled here (no SDL2), so the two source-list edits (`Makefile` LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC, `packages/simulation/BUILD.bazel`) and the live look are reviewed, not built; and a dropped piece is one rigid body, not a tumbling pile of brick.
- **feat(world): destructible brick gets a structural layer — joints, support, and a load cascade.** Founder real-time: "evolve the destructible brick logic into an intelligent, physically aware material and structural simulation ... a web of self-anchoring volumetric nodes". Scoped to what this engine can actually afford at MMO concurrency: no finite-element solver, no "layer bake", and no claiming either. Three things a player can feel, all deterministic so the server and every client agree. (1) **Joints at load** (`structure_build_joints`): boxes whose volumes intersect are joined — a piece sunk into a concrete master is ANCHORED, two crossing pieces of equal class are PEGGED (the virtual peg; timber is strong in shear, weak in tension). Whether a pair may join at all is PARENA's call (`struct_joint_strength`), which is why a glass pane leaning on a brick wall gets NO joint at all (150 < the 300 permille threshold): it is resting, not anchored, and it falls when the wall goes — exactly the behaviour a shader could never fake. (2) **A support flood** from the grounded pieces outward along joints, one level up from `bf_detect_detached`'s own question about cells: a piece that loses its last path to the ground is disconnected. Joints hold in BOTH directions (no height condition in the flood) because a roof is held by the pillar as much as the pillar is held by the foundation; only the load cascade follows gravity. (3) **The load cascade** (`structure_evaluate`): mass = volume × density accumulates top-down, each support hands its load equally to whatever would bear it, and each is checked against its own compression capacity (`struct_compression` kg/m² × footprint, with PARENA's 15% safety factor). A support that fails STOPS PASSING SUPPORT and the round repeats (bounded at 3), so one shot-out pillar drops the roof onto the next one rather than leaving it hanging in the air — the failure that makes a collapse read as a collapse. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn` (generated by `scripts/gen_structure_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/structure_rules.c`): density, tensile, compression, shear, damping, fracture kind, joint strength and the load comparison, all i32 at the boundary. New header-only `packages/simulation/structure.h` is the graph (≤512 nodes, ≤4096 joints, GL-free, no per-tick allocation); `structure_remove_node` + `structure_evaluate` is the whole "this piece is gone, what is now falling?" step. Named gaps, deliberate: no shear flow inside a piece, no bending/buckling SHAPE (a pillar holds its column load or the node fails — it does not bow), no fatigue, no per-cell stress inside one box. One real fix the test forced: `struct_holds_load` compares `mass × 1000` against `capacity × 850` in I32, so an unclamped 20×20×0.6 m concrete slab's mass (576 t) overflowed the capacity side into a UB-garbage answer; both operands are now clamped to a 2,000 t ceiling (documented, and far above any level box) which keeps a real overload a real failure. Verified: `make test-structure` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, no GL, no display) — PARENA totality, the reference frame's 4 anchors + 4 pegs, "one pillar gone and the roof still stands", "the last support gone and it does not", the glass-rests-on-brick case asserting zero joints and no support, a beam left unsupported when its post is demolished, the cascade (576,000 kg slab on a 126,000 kg wood pillar → pillar fails carrying 576,864 kg, 2 pieces unsupported), and bit-identical determinism. NOT verified / not yet wired: nothing calls this from `brick_world.h` yet — the graph is built and proven headless, and the hookup (a `bf_detect_detached`-flagged piece removing its node and re-evaluating) is the next slice; the live look, obviously, is unseen.
- **test(lighting): the whole chain, end to end and headless.** The two unit tests each proved half of it (`test-env-matrix` the matrix, `test-ambient-boost` the slider); neither proved the property the founder actually asked for — that the systems TALK to each other. New `packages/render/lighting_chain_test.c` sweeps every lighting preset (day / sunset / night / interior / dynamic) × every real weather state (clear / overcast / rain / storm) × slider 0/5/10 × three face directions (shaded / sunward / sideways) — 180 combinations — through the production calls `draw_scene` makes (`retro_lighting_eval` → `env_matrix_apply`/`publish` → `retro_lighting_eval_surface_rgb`) and asserts only invariants that must hold for ALL of them: a shaded face never gets darker than the old chain left it, no surface ends below the published floor, every channel stays finite and inside [0,1], deterministic to the bit, and the clear-noon vs clear-midnight swing survives (a matrix that flattened the world would fail). Deliberately does NOT assert that a sun-facing face never dims — it is supposed to, that is what makes a storm read as a storm. One real cleanup forced by making this runnable: the sky's two purely mathematical functions (`retro_sky_eval_sun_dir` / `retro_sky_eval_fog_rgb`) moved into a GL-free `packages/render/retro_sky_eval.h` that both `retro_sky.h` and `retro_lighting.c` include, because `retro_sky.h` pulls in `proc_tex.h`'s `<SDL2/SDL_opengl.h>` — the lighting code needed a GPU header to do arithmetic. `retro_sky.c` keeps the implementations (it draws the dome, so it stays GL-bound) and the test stubs only those two functions. `make test-lighting-chain` runs under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` with ASan+UBSan and links no GL. Still not verified: the lobby itself (`main.c`) and the live look — no SDL2 headers in this sandbox.
- **feat(lighting): lightning is a light source, not a screen tint.** Follow-up to the environment matrix: a bolt only ever flashed `sky_weather_draw_grade`'s overlay, and the world under it -- the storm deck, the walls, the players -- ignored it entirely. New `env-flash-boost` in `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/lighting_rules.prn` (regenerated into `packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c`) turns `SkyWeather.flash` (its own already-smoothed bolt intensity) into extra SCATTERED light, 0..0.30, added to the same bleed channel the rest of the atmosphere uses rather than to any new one; the host also mixes that bleed colour toward white by the same fraction (a bolt is broadband light, not the storm's grey) and lifts exposure by half of it. Deliberately diffuse, not a directional beam: the bolt lights the whole cloud deck, which is why its contribution is scatter. No new state, no extra evaluation -- it is one more term in the existing per-frame `env_matrix_eval`, and `flash == 0` is bit-for-bit the previous result. Verified in `make test-env-matrix`: the rule clamps (`env_flash_boost(0) == 0`, `env_flash_boost(1000) <= 300`, saturates above 1000), a strike raises bleed and exposure over the same storm, the bleeds whiten, and the strike measurably lands on a dark surface through the production `env_matrix_apply_surface` transform. Still NOT verified: the lobby is GL-bound and no SDL2 headers exist in this sandbox, so the `env_in.flash = g_sky_weather.flash` wiring and the live look are reviewed, not built.
- **feat(lighting): one unified environment matrix, resolved in PARENA — the "too dark everywhere" fix.** Founder real-time: "we have cool weather effects but it doesnt work with the ambient lighting like it always looks too dark everywhere we have some lighting tech down but we need more of a theory of all the lighting needs to talk to each other." The diagnosis was exact: weather (`sky_weather_light_state`), the day/night preset, the ambient slider (`ambient_rules.prn`) and the emitters each adjusted the scene independently, and every one of them could only subtract — a stormy night at slider 0 multiplied ambient down to near-black walls because nothing tracked how much light the world actually gets. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/lighting_rules.prn` (generated by the new `scripts/gen_lighting_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c`) resolves the atmosphere into six i32-permille values — occlusion (capped at 0.78), light bleed, ambient floor, exposure, emissive scale, emitter range/spread — and everything reads those instead of deriving its own. New thin host layer `packages/render/env_matrix.{h,c}` only converts units and applies: `env_matrix_apply` dims ambient gently (18% at worst) and sun/moon fully, `env_matrix_publish` hands the floor and the scattered sky-colour bleed to `retro_lighting`, and `env_matrix_apply_surface` (one function, one translation unit, no GL) adds the bleed and lifts the combined ambient term to the floor with a uniform gain (floor ÷ brightest channel) — hue-preserving, not a per-channel clamp, so walls do not wash flat. `retro_lighting_eval_surface_rgb` calls that exact function for every surface in the game; with nothing published it is a bit-for-bit no-op, so every existing caller and test is unchanged. Interiors keep only 35% of the occlusion and get a higher floor and no open-sky bleed. Emitters now trade reach for spread: fog shortens `FLASHLIGHT_RANGE` and widens `FLASHLIGHT_HALF_ANGLE_DEG` through one derived number, applied to the beam mesh, the per-face lit cone and the litbox spotlight uniforms so they cannot disagree; the enemy outline scales its emissive by the same scene-brightness inverse (bright noon tucks it down to 0.75, a dark scene pushes it up). Deliberately NOT described as Rayleigh/Mie scattering — it models the three things that were actually broken, not a physical sky this renderer cannot support. Costs one CPU evaluation per frame from values both sides already broadcast (no server work, no new wire fields, no per-entity state) and is a pure function, so every client computes the identical matrix bit for bit — the property that keeps it cheap at MMO concurrence instead of syncing lighting. Verified: `make test-env-matrix` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, links no GL) — PARENA purity/clamps, clear-weather no-op, the stormy-night regression through the exact production function (shaded-wall luminance 0.209 → 0.358, floor 0.300, occlusion 0.78, bleed 0.32), publish→surface wiring and its inverse, slider monotonicity under the worst weather, bit-identical determinism, and the emitter trade-off across the whole visibility range. NOT verified here: `retro_lighting` is GL-bound and this sandbox has no SDL2 headers, so `make test-ambient-boost` (recipe updated for the new link dependency) and the live look could not be built or seen; `apps2/`'s duplicate tree untouched.
- **feat(weapons): the assault rifle's underbarrel grenade — right click, E, and the controller's left trigger.** Founder real-time: "add an E for 3 the assault rifle ... the traditional right click thing where it fires a grenade like if its an m4 or whatever with the grenade powerup attached have e and right click both trigger it and ensure we have left trigger affordances for controller ... it should do a projectile and it should be fast like soldier 76 rocket and it should be a bit of like an arch down like its not so fast that its instant like a rail gun ... cool fireball shaders and explosions ... when it hits stuff it should cause an explosion and ensure it behaves with our destructable geometry." `WPN_AR`'s existing Frag Toss (a 0.7x lob) is replaced by a real rifle grenade: `AR_GRENADE_SPEED_MULT` 2.2x the 4.0 units/tick base (~9 units/tick, fast enough to read as a rocket, still a flight you watch), new `Projectile.gravity` (`AR_GRENADE_GRAVITY` 0.22 units/tick²) integrated in `update_projectiles` so it arcs instead of flying dead straight, damage 75, splash 4.5, 260-tick cooldown. New `BTN_ABILITY_2` (bit 2048) is a genuinely separate input from E, not a duplicate: right mouse and controller LEFT trigger (fire is the right trigger; LB was already the ability) set it — separate because the sniper's zoom IS right mouse, and folding RMB into `BTN_ABILITY_1` would spend the storm charges every time someone scoped (asserted in the new test). `Projectile.weapon` now carries the firing weapon into `explode_splash` instead of a hardcoded `WPN_MISSILE`, so the blast hook carves destructible brick with AR's own x2 multiplier rather than a rocket's x5 — a grenade opens a hole where a missile deletes the wall. Presentation: a real GLSL fireball (same hand-loaded GL 2.0 path `gl_shader.h` gives the flashlight beam, so it survives the mingw build) draws one camera-facing billboard per detonation — layered value noise over a sphere normal, white-hot core cooling to orange then smoke, plus a shockwave ring racing ahead of the flame — blended additively, with a second shell, a 12-ember spray and a fading trail on the round itself, all driven by `g_fx_explosion_hook` from `explode_splash` (NULL on the server and in tests, so nothing but pixels changes). No shader support degrades to an additive glow quad instead of nothing. NOT a port of Bedrock Racers' fire: BR's flames are JS/WebGL2 particle data in WOTAN and this renderer is fixed-function GL 1.x, so the shader is written for this pipeline rather than pretending a copy. Verified: `make test-ar-grenade` (new, 30 assertions through the real `update_weapons` — grenade numbers, upward velocity, faster-than-missile speed, cooldown, both input bits against one cooldown, sniper zoom does not spend charges, non-AR ignores the bit, missile keeps gravity 0 and its own id), `make test-hammer` and `make test-brick-world` still pass after the signature changes, and the FX block type-checks standalone under `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`. # EMPIRE

Composition layer for the EMPIRE stack: ECOWAR (the game), BIG_O (faction/tech-tree sim), DEADWEIGHT
(card language), TRAPX (doctrine). Each source repo keeps developing its own layer; the integration
code lives here. See `NORTHSTAR.md` for the scope and merge order.

## What is here

- `bridge/faction_bridge.{h,c}` — ECOWAR card play gated and written back through BIG_O's decorum rules
  (NORTHSTAR §3.1, kanban #576). CANCELLED casters can't play a card; a successful cast spends or earns
  decorum. The MYTHIC/MUNDANE mapping (-25 / +1) is an invented v1 tuning pending founder sign-off.
- `bridge/faction_state.{h,c}` — the shared faction record (kanban #579). The BIG_O side loads its decorum into
  it with `empire_faction_load()`. The deck UI binds to the same record, so a cast made through the UI is visible
  to BIG_O and the reverse. Each change bumps `revision`. **Honest gap:** BIG_O has no live server-side faction
  decorum store yet. Its only per-player decorum is the scenario sim (`core/sim.h`), so nothing feeds this record
  from a live server. The loader is the seam for that feed.
- `deck/deck.{h,c}` — the deck model: an 8-card cycle of ECOWAR card ids, a 4-slot hand, and Clash Royale
  style refill (playing a slot draws the next card in the cycle). Also the MYTHIC lookup, copied from
  `card_effect_mod.prn`.
- `deck/ui.{h,c}` — the deck and unit-placement apps (NORTHSTAR §3.3, kanban #578). Pure input -> state ->
  effect, the same shape as BIG_O's `bigo_phone.h`. DECK picks a card; UNITS places it on a 3x6 grid
  (invented v1 layout). SELECT is gated on the bound faction's `can_cast`, and a committed placement writes its
  decorum back into that shared record. BACK cancels with nothing spent.
- `vendor/big_o/` — BIG_O's PARENA-generated `witness_rules.c/.h` plus `parena_runtime.h`, copied verbatim.
  `MANIFEST.sha256` records their hashes. Re-sync with `make sync-big-o` (needs a sibling `../BIG_O`

# RED GARDEN

## How to Play (Knights of the Void — the arena MOBA, `apps/arena`)

*S170-97: the real keybind contract, synthesized in one place rather than scattered as code
comments in `apps/arena/src/main.c` and left implicit across every hero entry in
`docs/HEROES_VS0.md`.*

| Input | Does |
|---|---|
| **Left click** | Move to that point, or lock onto and auto-attack a live enemy hero if the click landed on one (team matches only — see NORTHSTAR §17). Walking into range of an enemy also auto-attacks it, so there's no separate "attack" input for melee range. Commands whichever of your own units are currently selected — for every hero except Tyler that's always just yourself, so this is unchanged from the description above unless you've drag-selected (below). |
| **Left click + drag** (Tyler only) | Box-select your own puppet clones (2026-07-30, "Divided We Stand" rework — true Meepo parity, clones no longer auto-follow). Drag a box over yourself and/or your active clones to select just them, then a plain click commands only the selected units — split your army and send nets in different directions. A quick click (below the drag threshold) is never treated as a drag, so ordinary move/attack clicks are unaffected. An empty box resets selection back to "just yourself." No other hero has anything to select, so this row is a no-op for the rest of the roster. |
| **Q / W / E** | Your three ability slots, in order. Every hero's kit maps its abilities to exactly these three — `docs/HEROES_VS0.md` lists each hero's real Q/W/R names and effects, but the *keys* are always Q/W/E, never anything hero-specific. W is either an instant effect on cooldown or a hold-on/hold-off toggle depending on the hero (`arena_hero_w_is_toggle()`) — toggles drain mana continuously while held rather than charging a flat cost up front. |
| **`** (backquote/tilde) | Use your equipped active item — Blink Dagger (short blink toward the cursor) or Donkey's Paper Glide (dash away from the nearest enemy), whichever one you actually have equipped. No-op with neither equipped. |
| **B** | Toggle the shop panel (S170-175) manually. The panel also opens/closes on its own once you walk within `ARENA_SHOP_RADIUS` of your own team's shop and leave it again (2026-07-30) — `B` still works on top of that for whenever you want it open away from the shop. |
| **1–9** (shop open) | Buy the item in that row of the *current* shop page — a single action, no confirm step. The 33-item catalog is paginated 9-per-page (2026-07-30) so every visible row always has a live `1`-`9` keybind, unlike the old single giant list. Click an occupied slot in the loadout column to sell it back for half price. Purchases only resolve for real within `ARENA_SHOP_RADIUS` of your own team's shop. |
| **Shift+1 through Shift+4** (shop open) | Jump straight to shop page 1/2/3/4. Four clickable page-number buttons above the item list do the same thing for mouse users. Page 4 (2026-08-11, "add page 4 to the shop") holds the 6 newest items — see the item table below. |
| **Held TAB** | Scoreboard: every hero's kills/deaths/Flow/XP, plus a team-aggregate row, both teams side by side. |
| **H** | Toggle an ability-description overlay for your own hero's Q/W/E. |
| **Right click + drag** | Rotate the camera around your hero. No-op while camera lock (`C`) is on. |
| **Mouse wheel** | Zoom the camera in/out. Always works, even while camera lock is on. |
| **C** | Toggle camera lock (NORTHSTAR §15.1). The camera already always follows your hero's position — locking freezes the rotation angle too, so you can't look away from them. Shows "CAM LOCKED" on screen while on. Starts unlocked every match. |
| **F11** | Toggle the APM (actions-per-minute) overlay. Works in any mode. |
| **R** | Restart the match. Local practice mode only (against the built-in bot) — disabled entirely once you're in a real networked match, since a real match has other players in it. |
| **Click "OK"** | After a match ends (win or loss), requeues you for another one. Networked mode only. |

# TRAPX

TRAPX v1 — BLOCK ZERO
Acceptance Criteria (Frozen)
Product Definition

TRAPX v1 is a single-player systemic urban simulation where the player influences a neighborhood using a deck of operations, observing emergent outcomes over time through indirect control.

There is no avatar, no direct unit control, and no win condition in v1.

1. World & Scale

The game simulates exactly one neighborhood

Neighborhood is represented as a grid (10×10 or 12×12)

Each grid cell represents a city block

All cells are visible at all times

Camera is fixed orthographic / isometric

No camera rotation

Each cell must track:

=== kit_page_gl.h ===
/* kit_page_gl.h -- paints one of the kit pages (packages/common/kit.h) with PELLEGRINO's own
 * layout/paint engine, through the same os_menu_embed surface the OS menu uses (kanban #627).
 *
 * Why this surface and not the in-phone browser: phone_browser_embed.h is a REAL navigator (it
 * fetches over TLS/QUIC and can only show URLs), which is the wrong tool for a locally generated
 * page. os_menu_set_page takes an HTML string, lays it out with PELLEGRINO and hands back pixels --
 * exactly what "basic html and CSS and PELLEGRINO tech for rendering the ui" asks for.
 *
 * Deliberately the SAME 760x480 dimensions as os_menu_gl.h's own surface: os_menu_init is a single
 * global surface, and matching its size means re-initialising for a kit page cannot desync the OS
 * menu's own upload geometry. Header-only, static; the includer must already have
 * <SDL2/SDL_opengl.h> and <stdio.h>. */
#ifndef SHANKPIT_KIT_PAGE_GL_H
#define SHANKPIT_KIT_PAGE_GL_H
#include "os_menu_embed.h"

#define KPG_W 760
#define KPG_H 480
#ifndef GL_BGRA
#define GL_BGRA 0x80E1
#endif

static int g_kpg_state = -1;   /* -1 untried, 0 off, 1 ready */
static GLuint g_kpg_tex = 0;
static int g_kpg_force = 1;
static int g_kpg_have_tex = 0;

static int kpg_ready(void) {
    if (g_kpg_state < 0) {
        g_kpg_state = (os_menu_init(KPG_W, KPG_H) == 0) ? 1 : 0;
        if (!g_kpg_state) fprintf(stderr, "[kit-page] PELLEGRINO surface unavailable -- kit screens fall back to text\n");
    }
    return g_kpg_state == 1;
}

/* Draw `html` into the rect (x0,bottom)-(x0+w,bottom+h) in a bottom-left-origin 2D ortho.
 * Returns 1 if it painted, 0 if the surface is unavailable (the caller then draws its own text
 * fallback -- a phone app must never be a blank rectangle). */
static int kpg_draw(const char *html, float x0, float bottom, float w, float h) {
    const unsigned int *px;
    if (!html) return 0;
    if (!kpg_ready()) return 0;
    if (os_menu_set_page(html)) g_kpg_force = 1;
    px = os_menu_draw();
    if (!px) return 0;
    if (!g_kpg_tex) glGenTextures(1, &g_kpg_tex);
    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, g_kpg_tex);
    if (g_kpg_force) {
        glPixelStorei(GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, 4);
        glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
        glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_NEAREST);
        glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, KPG_W, KPG_H, 0, GL_BGRA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, px);
        g_kpg_force = 0;
        g_kpg_have_tex = 1;
    }
    if (!g_kpg_have_tex) return 0;
    glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
    glColor4f(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
    glBegin(GL_QUADS);
    glTexCoord2f(0.0f, 0.0f); glVertex2f(x0, bottom);
    glTexCoord2f(1.0f, 0.0f); glVertex2f(x0 + w, bottom);
    glTexCoord2f(1.0f, 1.0f); glVertex2f(x0 + w, bottom + h);
    glTexCoord2f(0.0f, 1.0f); glVertex2f(x0, bottom + h);
    glEnd();
    glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);
    return 1;
}

#endif /* SHANKPIT_KIT_PAGE_GL_H */

# EMPIRE — NORTHSTAR (corrected scope, 2026-10-06)

**Status:** design/scoping, repos now checked out locally (`ECOWAR`, `REDGARDEN`, `DEADWEIGHT_2`,
`TRAPX`, `MONOREPO` pulled fresh this session alongside existing `BIG_O`/`DEADWEIGHT`/`SHANKPIT`),
no merge code written yet.

## 0) Correction (founder, real-time, 2026-10-06 — supersedes this doc's earlier v0)

The first draft of this doc read "merge" as "share a ladder/identity backend between three
otherwise-separate games." That was wrong. Founder, verbatim:

> "EMPIRE is literally a merging of BIG_O, ECOWAR, and DEADWEIGHT 1+2 — full ECOWAR RTS style,
> card places units, Clash Royale style, but the factions are actually the BIG_O simulation. The
> game is ECOWAR. BIG_O is the tech tree. TRAPX is the universe. TYLER is the lore. SHANKPIT is
> the operating system. REDGARDEN is the hero UI. DEADWEIGHT is the card language. Merge ECOWAR
> and BIG_O first — ECOWAR is the client, BIG_O is the headless sim that needs a GUI resource
> management sim [wrapped in] TRAPX doctrine."

This is one product with a named role for every repo in the stack, not three products sharing a
backend. Each role below is checked against that repo's own real, current code — not assumed from
its name.

## 1) The stack, role by role (checked against real code, not guessed)

| Repo | Role in EMPIRE | What's actually there today |
|---|---|---|
| **ECOWAR** | **The game.** Clash Royale-shaped client: play cards, cards place/affect units, resolved in real time. | Hard fork of REDGARDEN (`apps/arena`/`apps/arena_server`, C99/SDL2/OpenGL, server-authoritative UDP). **16 real cards shipped** (`packages/simulation/arena_game.c`'s `ECOWAR_CARDS`, resolution via `PARENA/stdlib/ecowar/card_effect_mod.prn` — real I32 decision logic, not a bare trigger), each grounded in a `TYLER/multiverse_heroes.md` hero. **Gap, confirmed in ECOWAR's own README**: no deck/hand UI, no unit-placement input wiring yet — the cards are callable and tested end-to-end, but nothing in-match actually plays one. This is exactly the "Clash Royale style" layer that doesn't exist yet. Own matchmaker+bot-pool real and live (`:9779`, `ECOWAR-BOTS` IDUNA M2M agent).
| **BIG_O** | **The tech tree / faction simulation**, headless, driving ECOWAR's factions from underneath. Needs a GUI resource-management layer wrapped around it. | Real, live precedent for exactly this shape: `core/lab_sim.h/.c` (headless cloning-facility equipment pipeline, "simulate real lab equipment," zero server/GUI logic), Attention/Heat rules module (PARENA-scalar, headless tests + a tiny text sim to *play* it — i.e. BIG_O already proves out headless-sim-plus-minimal-harness as its own pattern). Day/night/basement loop *is* the tech-tree/economy shape the founder means by "factions are actually the BIG_O simulation" — basement lab + pheromone army + Attention/Heat *is* a faction-management sim with no GUI today.
| **DEADWEIGHT (1) / DEADWEIGHT_2** | **The card language.** The grammar cards are written in, not the cards themselves. | `DEADWEIGHT/core/card_rules.c/.h` — a real, pure, headless, deterministic card-resolution engine (6x6 grid, splittable items, fragmentation tax — the mechanic DEADWEIGHT v1 built for its own combat is, structurally, a card-effect resolver). `DEADWEIGHT_2` ("CRASH_OVERRIDE") is real, shipped CI/releases (Windows+native client, v0.3.0 tag found in its own git log) — **shipped**: v0.3.0 released 2026-09-25 (Linux + Windows assets), v0.6.0 is latest. The earlier "built, not shipped" note is stale. See `audits/deadweight2_ship_audit.md`.
| **TRAPX** | **The universe/doctrine** — the systemic rules every faction operates under. | Real, separate repo (not the `SHANKPIT/docs2/TRAPX_NORTHSTAR.md` derivative) — TRAPX v1 "BLOCK ZERO": single-player systemic urban sim, a 10x10/12x12 grid, no avatar, no direct unit control, no win condition, cells tracking alignment (Neutral/Player/Rival/Institutional) and signed pressure, influenced by a deck of operations. **This is the doctrine layer BIG_O's faction sim should be an instance of** — TRAPX is the general systemic-influence ruleset, BIG_O's Attention/Heat/faction-politics is one concrete application of it.
| **TYLER** | **The lore.** Narrative substrate every hero/card/faction is actually *from*. | `TYLER/multiverse_heroes.md` is already ECOWAR's real card-content source today — this role is already live, not aspirational.
| **SHANKPIT** | **The operating system** — engine/platform substrate (netcode, rendering, level/portal system) everything else runs on top of. | Matches `SHARED_ENGINE_NORTHSTAR.md`'s own framing of SHANKPIT as the canonical engine source; BIG_O is literally built on the SHANKPIT engine already (`BIG_O/NORTHSTAR.md` day-loop = "SHANKPIT FPS (existing)").
| **REDGARDEN** | **The hero UI** — not gameplay anymore, the visual/UX layer for presenting heroes/cards. | ECOWAR's fork source; `REDGARDEN/docs/HEROES_VS0.md` already has real, concrete hero kits (LoL/DOTA-familiar stat lines) — this is the real asset to lift into a UI role (hero select, card frames, stat display) rather than keep developing REDGARDEN as a second independent RTS alongside ECOWAR.

## 2) What "merge" means now (corrected from v0's "shared backend only" read)

Still true from v0, kept: this is not "collapse four C codebases into one Bazel target blindly."
What changes: the four repos aren't peer products sharing a ladder — they're **layers of one
product**, and the merge direction is a real dependency chain, not a bus everyone plugs into:

```
TRAPX (doctrine)  ──────────────┐
TYLER (lore)      ──────────────┤
                                 ▼
                    BIG_O (headless faction/tech-tree sim)
                                 │  (needs: a GUI resource-management
                                 │   front end — doesn't exist yet)
                                 ▼
          ECOWAR (the game — client, cards place units, Clash-Royale real-time resolution)
                                 │  (cards are written in)
                                 ▼
                    DEADWEIGHT's card_rules language
                                 │  (presented via)
                                 ▼
                    REDGARDEN's hero UI assets
                                 │  (running on)
                                 ▼
                    SHANKPIT (engine/OS substrate)
```

That AI is the thing EMPIRE needs and TRAPX doctrine describes. |\n| **TRAPX** | Doctrine | BLOCK ZERO: one neighbourhood grid, cells with alignment (Neutral / Player / Rival / Institutional) and *signed pressure*, influenced by a deck of operations — **no avatar, no direct unit control, no win condition**. |\n| **SHANKPIT** | Operating system | Engine, netcode, level format, phone/OS surfaces, and the only place a real world exists at all. |\n\nThe dependency chain EMPIRE's own NORTHSTAR states, kept:\n\n```\nTRAPX (doctrine) -> BIG_O (faction/tech sim) -> ECOWAR (game) -> DEADWEIGHT (card language)\n-> REDGARDEN (hero UI) -> SHANKPIT (engine/OS)\n```\n\nSHANKPIT's job in that chain is *substrate plus a surface a player can reach*. This document is\nonly about that job.\n\n## 2. The phone is the whole control scheme (and that is deliberate)\n\nTRAPX says no avatar, no direct unit control. SHANKPIT has an avatar, so the compromise is: **you\nwalk, but you do not command**. Troops are not selected and ordered; they are *bought into\nexistence* where your influence already reaches, and then REDGARDEN-style AI fights for them.\n\nThe app is `BP_APP_EMPIRE`, pulled up with **P**, and it does three things:\n\n1. **A minimap of the nearby area.** Nine districts (your district and its eight neighbours on the\n   sphere), drawn from real state: who holds each one, where your bodies are, where a controlled\n   building is. It is a map, not a radar sweep — nothing is hidden from you inside your own\n   neighbourhood, and everything outside it is.\n2. **Spawn a troop near you.** Cost in influence, a squad cap, and a spawn that must land on ground\n   you can actually reach: within `empire-spawn-radius-milli` of you, falling back to a building you\n   control if you are indoors or on a ledge.\n3. **Clone.** A clone keeps the veterancy of the body it copies and costs 130% of a recruit. You\n   cannot clone an empty roster; `/dev/null` is not a veteran. This is the founder's \"clone your\n   troops in PARENA first\" — the *numbers* are PARENA, the *act* is the phone.\n\n### Influence, not money\n\nInfluence is the only currency, and it is a TRAPX pressure value with a spend button:\n\n- it trickles (`empire-influence-per-second`, 2/s) and caps at 400;\n- **held districts pay it** (`empire-influence-from-district`: 100% yours, a third neutral, 0 a\n  rival's), so territory is income and the app's map is an economy readout;\n- every troop spends it, and the squad cap (6) means influence cannot be banked into an army.\n\nA district flips at 600‰ pressure (`empire-district-state`), which is TRAPX's own alignment rule\nwith one state removed: Institutional has no owner in this build, so it stays Neutral rather than\nbeing faked.\n\n## 3. The sphere: an actually spherical map, not a curved plane\n\nFounder: *\"the map itself should be a big sphere ... procedurally generated ... like the maps that\nzombie already uses mixed with the city built in map that survival uses to generate a sphere of\nprocedural cities in districts or neighborhoods.\"*\n\nDesign, in the order it has to be built:\n\n1. **Geometry (in PARENA, already written).** Rings of districts on a sphere: 6 / 12 / 18 / 18 / 12\n   / 6 = **72 districts**, radius 240 units, each district ~16 units across. Ring counts rise toward\n   the equator so districts stay roughly the same *area* — the reason a sphere beats a square grid,\n   and the reason \"the nearby area\" is always the same handful of cells at any latitude. A uniform\n   lat/long grid would pinch at the poles and the phone's minimap would lie to players there.\n2. **Generation (next).** Each district seeds a **city block generator** — the survival city planner,\n   which already produces streets and buildings from a seed — and the *spacing and street rhythm* of\n   the zombie map generator, which is what makes a district read as a place people lived rather than\n   a grid of boxes. A district is generated the first time anyone comes within streaming range, from\n   `(world_seed, ring, index)` alone, so two clients generate the same neighbourhood with no\n   exchange. Unloaded districts keep only their owner and their influence, which is a handful of\n   integers.\n3. **Streaming.** Same rule the archipelago doc already set: unload distant geometry, keep the\n   simulation. The sphere's own curvature is only felt at district boundaries, where neighbouring\n   districts tilt by one ring step.\n\nDeliberately **not** in this slice: the generator itself. It is a bigger piece than the phone app,\nand a sphere you can see but that generates nothing would be worse than no sphere at all.\n\n## 4. What was built in this slice\n\n- `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/empire_rules.prn` — influence economy, troop costs, clone premium, squad\n  cap, spawn radius, district alignment + income, and the 72-district sphere geometry. Generated to\n  `packages/simulation/empire_rules.c`; installed by `empire_rules_host.h`. **Rules first**, as asked.\n- `packages/simulation/empire_rules_test.c` — headless proof of the economy and the geometry.\n\n## 5. What is named but not built\n\n- **No troop bodies yet.** SHANKPIT has bodies (story AI slots, the two drone kinds) but no faction\n  field on them: REDGARDEN's friendly/enemy AI is in REDGARDEN, and porting its team model into\n  SHANKPIT's `PlayerState`/`DroneState` is the next real piece. Until then the app can show cost,\n  capacity and refusal honestly, but \"spawn\" has nothing loyal to hand the body to.\n- **No procedural sphere generation** (§3.2) and no streaming of districts.\n- **No wire format** for influence or district ownership, so this is single-player/sandbox state.\n- **BIG_O/ECOWAR cards are not playable from this app**; EMPIRE's own deck UI is the right home\n  for that, and it already exists there.\n"
}
````

1, t - 1) == 0, \"contested district claimed by nobody\");\n    CHECK(empire_influence_from_district(1, 30) == 30, \"yours should pay in full\");\n    CHECK(empire_influence_from_district(2, 30) == 0, \"a rival's district paid you\");\n    CHECK(empire_influence_from_district(0, 30) > 0 &&\n          empire_influence_from_district(0, 30) < 30, \"neutral should pay a third, got %d\",\n          empire_influence_from_district(0, 30));\n\n    /* ---- the sphere ---- */\n    {\n        int rings = empire_sphere_rings();\n        int total = 0, middle = 0, pole = 0;\n        CHECK(rings >= 3, \"rings %d\", rings);\n        for (int r = 0; r < rings; r++) {\n            int n = empire_districts_in_ring(r);\n            CHECK(n > 0, \"ring %d empty\", r);\n            total += n;\n            if (r == 0) pole = n;\n            if (r == rings / 2) middle = n;\n        }\n        CHECK(empire_districts_in_ring(rings) == 0, \"a ring past the last one exists\");\n        CHECK(empire_districts_in_ring(-1) == 0, \"a negative ring exists\");\n        CHECK(total == 72, \"districts total %d (want 72, the number this stack keeps coming back to)\", total);\n        CHECK(middle > pole, \"the equator ring (%d) must hold more than the pole cap (%d) or the map pinches\",\n              middle, pole);\n        CHECK(empire_sphere_radius_milli() > empire_district_radius_milli(), \"sphere smaller than a district\");\n        CHECK(empire_nearby_districts() < total, \"the whole world cannot be 'nearby'\");\n        CHECK(empire_spawn_radius_milli() > 0 && empire_spawn_radius_milli() < empire_district_radius_milli() * 2,\n              \"spawn radius %d is not a local placement\", empire_spawn_radius_milli());\n    }\n\n    if (fails) { printf(\"empire_rules: %d FAILED\\n\", fails); return 1; }\n    printf(\"empire_rules: all checks passed\\n\");\n    return 0;\n}\n"

      static inline int bp_wrap(int v, int n) { return n <= 0 ? 0 : ((v % n) + n) % n; }
      
      static inline void bp_enter_app(Phone *p, int app) {
          p->detail = 0;
          p->app = app; p->cursor = 0; p->cursor2 = 0; p->lab_trait = 0;
          if (app == BP_APP_MESSAGES) p->unread = 0;
      }
      
      /* Rows the current app's cursor ranges over (for wrap). */
      static inline int bp_rows(const Phone *p) {
          switch (p->app) {
          case BP_APP_MESSAGES: return p->message_count > 0 ? p->message_count : 1;
          case BP_APP_CONTACTS: return p->contacts_met;
          case BP_APP_MAP: return BP_ZONES;
          case BP_APP_NOTES: return BP_NOTE_LINES;
          case BP_APP_LAB: return 4;       /* base, trait, SPLICE, clone list */
          case BP_APP_CARGO: return p->cargo_count > 0 ? p->cargo_count : 1;
          case BP_APP_GFD: return p->term_line_count > 0 ? p->term_line_count : 1;
          case BP_APP_IDUNA: return 1;
          case BP_APP_ARPANET: return BP_ARPANET_NODES;
          case BP_APP_TECHTREE: return p->tech_count > 0 ? p->tech_count : 1;
          case BP_APP_MISSION: return BP_MISSION_ROWS;
          case BP_APP_SKILLS: return 5;
          case BP_APP_LOADOUT: return 6;
          case BP_APP_WARDROBE: return BP_COSTUMES;
          case BP_APP_KITS: return p->kit.kit_count > 0 ? p->kit.kit_count : 1;
          case BP_APP_KITMAP: return KIT_SLOTS;
          case BP_APP_KITBUILD: return KIT_SLOTS;
          default: return 1;
          }
      }
      
      /* Notification with the spec's anti-spam rule: <= 2 banners per 30s, extras queued and later shown as a summary. */

              if (now - p->shown_at[i] < BP_SPAM_WINDOW_MS) p->shown_at[k++] = p->shown_at[i];
          p->shown_n = k;

              /* Build into the DRAFT so a half-finished kit never becomes the thing you are carrying.

              if (a == BP_LEFT || a == BP_RIGHT) kit_cycle_draft(&p->kit, p->cursor, a == BP_RIGHT ? 1 : -1);

  content: |
       * Deliberately one layout with different copy: PELLEGRINO's CSS surface is unverified beyond the
       * OS menu's own tiles, so nothing here depends on flexbox/grid/animations -- a table, a background,
       * a highlighted row, and a hint line. All return the length written, or -1 if it would not fit
       * (the caller keeps its previous page rather than rendering a truncated one). */
      
      static inline int kit_page_add(char *out, int cap, int len, const char *s) {
          int n;
          if (len < 0 || !s) return -1;
          n = (int)strlen(s);
          if (len + n >= cap) return -1;
          memcpy(out + len, s, (size_t)n + 1);
          return len + n;
      }
      
      static inline int kit_page_head(char *out, int cap, const char *title, const char *sub) {
          int n = snprintf(out, (size_t)cap,
              "<html><head><style>"
              "body{background:#0b0f14;color:#cfe3f0;font-family:sans-serif;margin:0;padding:10px}"
