Done — all four repos cloned, doctrine written first, and the EMPIRE phone app is real and compiling.

## Repos
`EMPIRE`, `ECOWAR`, `REDGARDEN`, `TRAPX` are now beside `SHANKPIT`/`PARENA`. What they actually contain (not what the names imply): EMPIRE is a faction bridge + deck UI with **no world**, ECOWAR is the arena game with 16 tested cards and **no in-match deck UI**, REDGARDEN holds the team/fractal-commander AI, TRAPX is the doctrine — alignment + signed pressure on a grid, no avatar, no direct control.

## Rules first (PARENA)
`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/empire_rules.prn` → `packages/simulation/empire_rules.c` (`make regen-empire-rules`):
- **One currency.** Influence 2/s, capped at 400. Troops 25/35/40/60. **A clone costs 130% of a recruit and needs a veteran to copy.** Squad cap 6, spawn radius 14 units.
- **Districts pay.** TRAPX alignment (yours/neutral/rival at 600‰ pressure) with income attached: full, a third, nothing.
- **The sphere is geometry, not a metaphor.** 6/12/18/18/12/6 = **72 districts**, ring counts rising toward the equator so districts keep their area — a lat/long grid would pinch and the minimap would lie at the poles.

## Phone app: `P` → EMPIRE
Nine-cell minimap of the nearby districts (blue yours, red rival, green the block you stand on) plus the four spawn rows and the clone row, painted as HTML+CSS by the same PELLEGRINO surface the kit pages use, with a text fallback so it is never a blank rectangle. **The phone never spends** — SELECT emits `BP_FX_EMPIRE_SPAWN`/`_CLONE`, and the host re-checks the same PARENA gate, takes the influence, and places a body 2 units beside you. A retuned cost can't let the UI and the world disagree.

## Verified
`make test-empire-rules` (costs, clone premium, refusal one point short, unknown kinds, cap, clone-needs-a-veteran, district flip/income, 72 districts with the equator ring larger than the pole cap), `make test-vehicle-burn`, `phone_test`, a page harness (9 cells, 4 spawn rows, 1.4 KB of real HTML), `make check-windows` (96 lobby sources) and `make -B server`. Two real compile bugs found and fixed while doing it: the row-count macros were declared below their first use, and the host helper hit the same implicit-declaration trap this file already has a changelog entry for.

## Named, not faked
- **The body is a story-AI slot, not a loyal soldier.** SHANKPIT has bodies, REDGARDEN has the friendly/enemy model, nothing yet joins them — placement is real, allegiance is not.
- **No district simulation in the world**, so the minimap honestly shows you holding the block you stand on and neighbours neutral.
- **The sphere is geometry only** — no procedural city generation, no streaming.
- **No wire format**, so influence and ownership are single-player state.
- Nothing was played with a display; the page is verified as markup, not as pixels.

`docs/EMPIRE_NORTHSTAR.md` carries the stack roles, the phone-as-control-scheme argument (TRAPX says no direct control, so you buy conditions instead of ordering squads), and the sphere build order.

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn",
  "instructions": "Add the material/light-style animation vocabulary as a PARENA mod.",
  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn -- what a surface IS, as a total integer function of the tick.\n;;\n;; Founder 2026-10-31: \"shankpit already has some lighting primitives like hps light and ips light\n;; what other materials/shaders do we need for full doom/quake/half life/gta story telling?\"\n;;\n;; The honest answer for THIS engine is not a PBR pipeline -- it is fixed-function GL 1.x with one\n;; hand-loaded GL 2.0 shader path (gl_shader.h) and no VAO/3.3/3D-texture support anywhere in the\n;; build. So the storytelling vocabulary is authored as ANIMATION, not as material science: a\n;; material is (base look, how its UVs move, how its own light flickers, what colour the screen goes\n;; when it is hurting you). Every one of those is a pure function of the tick and a few integers, so\n;; the server, every client and a headless test compute the same frame -- which is the only way a\n;; flicker can be part of a deterministic simulation at all.\n;;\n;; This file is the vocabulary Doom / Quake / Half-Life / GTA communicate fear with:\n;;   Doom      palette-cycling hazard colours, scrolling toxic ooze, damage tints\n;;   Quake     light styles (\"aaaaaaazzzzz\" strobes), the texture-warp look, dark corners\n;;   HL        interactive terminals (frame-loop materials), unstable fluorescents, alien flesh\n;;   GTA       sodium streetlights above dark alleys, animated signage, flooded canals\n;;\n;; The renderer still has to draw it (see docs/RENDER_NORTHSTAR.md for what is wired and what is\n;; not). Nothing here invents a texture: indices and timings only.\n\n(module shankpit/material-rules)\n(export mat-kind-count mat-scroll-u-milli mat-scroll-v-milli mat-frame-index\n        mat-light-style-count light-style-level-permille\n        mat-emissive-milli tint-low-health-milli tint-submerged-milli\n        tint-acid-milli tint-shield-milli\n        palette-index-256 vlm-axis-index-milli vlm-ambient-floor-milli)\n\n;; ---- material kinds ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; 0 plain, 1 scrolling (ooze / water / conveyor), 2 frame-loop sprite (terminals, cameras, timers),\n;; 3 palette-LUT (indexed colour), 4 emissive flicker (a fixture's own face).\n(defn mat-kind-count [] : I32 5)\n\n(defn m-abs [(x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x 0) (- 0 x) x))\n(defn m-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n;; Integer modulo that is never negative, because a negative UV offset is a visible seam.\n(defn m-mod [(a : I32) (n : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= n 0) 0 (let [r (- a (* (/ (- a (m-mod0 a n)) n) n))] r)))\n\n;; helper: floor division by a positive n (no negative remainders)\n(defn m-mod0 [(a : I32) (n : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= n 0) 0\n    (if (>= a 0) (* (/ a n) n)\n      (* (- (/ (- a (- n 1)) n)) n))))\n\n;; ---- UV animation -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; Scroll speed per material kind, in permille of a texture per SECOND (1000 = one full tile/s).\n;; Ooze creeps, water drifts, a conveyor is fast. Plain surfaces do not move.\n(defn mat-scroll-speed-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) 220 (if (= kind 4) 60 (if (= kind 3) 90 0))))\n\n;; Offset in permille, 0..999, of a scrolling material at a tick (60 ticks = one second).\n(defn mat-scroll-u-milli [(kind : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32\n  (m-mod0 (* (mat-scroll-speed-milli kind) (m-mod0 tick 60)) 60000))\n\n(defn mat-scroll-v-milli [(kind : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 1) (m-mod0 (* 90 (m-mod0 tick 60)) 60000) 0))\n\n;; A frame-loop material's sprite index, stepped at `fps` (1..30). This is what makes a terminal\n;; blink, a camera sweep and a bomb timer tick -- one sheet, one offset per frame.\n(defn mat-frame-index [(fps : I32) (frames : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32\n  (if (or (<= frames 0) (<= fps 0)) 0\n    (m-mod0 (/ (* (m-mod0 tick 60) fps) 60) frames)))\n\n;; ---- light styles (Quake's own vocabulary, as integers) ---------------------------------------------\n;; 0 steady, 1 strobe, 2 fluorescent (unstable), 3 broken (mostly off), 4 pulse, 5 dying, 6 alarm,\n;; 7 candle. {
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/docs/RENDER_NORTHSTAR.md",
  "instructions": "Document the material/shader roadmap and audit the Source 2 gap.",
  "content": "# RENDER — materials, light styles, and the Source 2 gap\n\n**Status:** the *vocabulary* is implemented as rules (`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn`);\nthe renderer still draws it with the existing pipeline. This document answers the two questions\nthat came with the spec dump — what materials/shaders a Doom/Quake/Half-Life/GTA story needs, and\nwhat is missing next to Source 2 — and it corrects the pasted spec where that spec does not fit this\nengine.\n\n## 1. What SHANKPIT actually renders with\n\nRead from the source, not assumed:\n\n- **Fixed-function GL 1.x** for world geometry (`glBegin`/`glTranslate`/`glRectf`), plus **one\n  hand-loaded GL 2.0 shader path** (`packages/render/gl_shader.h`) used by the flashlight beam and\n  the fireball. Programs are loaded through `SDL_GL_GetProcAddress`, because the build links GL 1.1.\n- **Lighting** is `lighting_rules.prn` → `env_matrix` (occlusion, sky bleed, ambient floor,\n  exposure, emissive scale) applied to fixed-function per-face shading, plus **HPS/IPS point\n  fixtures** with per-fixture range and lit cones.\n- **Textures** are proc-generated (`proc_tex.c`) and material shaders referenced by *name* from the\n  level JSON (`material_shaders.h`); levels carry material, specular, shininess, friction, density.\n- No VAO, no `#version 330`, no `sampler3D`, no deferred G-buffer, no normal maps, no shadow maps.\n\nThat is the constraint every proposal below has to survive.\n\n## 2. What a Doom/Quake/Half-Life/GTA story needs, in this engine's language\n\nImplemented in `material_rules.prn` (pure functions of the tick, so the server and every client\nanimate identically):\n\n| Need | How it is expressed | What the renderer must add |\n|---|---|---|\n| Doom palette cycling / hazard colour | `palette-256(index)` with wrap, plus material kind 3 (LUT) | A 256-entry LUT upload and an indexed fragment path — the one place a real shader is required |\n| Quake texture swim | material kind 1 scroll offsets (`mat-scroll-u/v-milli`) | UV offset per face; the *warp* itself is the existing affine mapping, no shader needed to make it worse |\n| Half-Life terminals, cameras, bomb timers | material kind 2 frame-loop (`mat-frame-index(fps, frames, tick)`) | A sprite-sheet UV window; four floats per frame |\n| Unstable fluorescents, strobes, dying bulbs | 8 light styles (`light-style-level-permille`) | Multiply the fixture's own HPS/IPS intensity — one integer, already per-frame |\n| Emissive faces that react to room darkness | `mat-emissive-milli(style, tick, room_light)` | Reuse `env_matrix`'s existing emissive scale |\n| Toxic ooze / canals / water | kind 1 with a vertical component | Alpha-blended quad, additive pass at the shoreline |\n| Low-health / submerged / acid / shield tint | `tint-*-milli(...)` | One full-screen colour quad — this engine already draws those for weather grading |\n| Dark corners with no light source | `vlm-ambient-floor-milli()` (120‰) | Apply as a floor under per-face shading |\n\n## 3. What is missing next to Source 2 (and what is realistic here)\n\nThe pasted spec's list is correct about *what* Source 2 has; it is wrong about *what this engine can\ncompile or run*. Ranked by value per unit of risk:\n\n1. **Baked probe grid (the honest half of `M_combined_light_probe_volume`).** A 32×16×32 RGB grid per\n   level, baked at level load or by the level tool, sampled per vertex or per face — *not* a\n   `sampler3D` in a GLSL 330 shader (unavailable). Cost: a few integers per lookup; exactly what\n   `vlm-axis-index-milli` now defines. This is the single biggest visual win: corners,地道 interiors\n   and streetlight pools without a real light at either end.\n2. **PBR, cheaply.** Albedo + roughness + metal as *numbers on the material* (material JSON already\n   has specular/shininess), and a per-face specular term in fixed-function — no normal map, no\n   multi-texture pass. Calling that PBR would be a lie; calling it \"PBR-shaped\" is honest.\n3. **Volumetric fog as distance-graded slabs.** `sky_weather.c` already fades geometry; adding three\n   height slabs with different density gives light shafts through windows for almost no cost. No\n   froxel grid.\n4. **Palette LUT (Doom).** A real fragment shader, small, and the only item here that genuinely needs\n   one. Worth it because hazard colour cycling is the cheapest atmosphere in the business.\n5. **Frame-loop and scroll materials.** No new shader if the existing texture path takes a UV offset\n   per draw; these cheap wins are the ones terminal/portal/signage storytelling is made of.\n\n**Not realistic, and named as such:** GPU mesh shaders (requires GL 4.6 hardware and a different\nbuild entirely), hardware ray-traced lightmaps (VRAD3 assumes a DXR/Vulkan toolchain), parallax\nocclusion mapping (needs a height map + tangent space + a shader per surface, and the fixed-function\npath has no tangent basis), a deferred G-buffer (the pipeline is immediate mode; converting it is a\nrewrite, not an upgrade).\n\n## 4. Corrections to the pasted engineering spec\n\n- `#version 330 core`, `glGenVertexArrays`, `glVertexAttribIPointer`, `sampler3D` / `glTexImage3D`:\n  none of these exist in this build's GL surface. The shader path loads **GL 2.0** entry points\n  through SDL on top of GL 1.1 headers; a 3.3 program would fail to compile on the target.\n- The vertex struct's `uint32_t material_id` **interleaved per vertex** is the wrong shape here:\n  materials are per-face in `map_geo`, and the renderer batches by material. A per-vertex id buys\n  nothing and costs 4 bytes per vertex.\n- \"Bit-identical visual timing across the cluster\" is true only of the **CPU-side parameters** — the\n  tick, the style level, the UV offset, the tint alpha. GPU rasterisation is not bit-identical across\n  vendors, and claiming otherwise would be wrong. That is exactly why the parameters live in PARENA\n  and the pixels do not.\n- The sample fragment shader is not PBR: `pow(1-roughness,4)*metallic*NdotV` has no light integral,\n  no Fresnel, no distribution term, and it ignores the sampled ambient colour's direction. It is a\n  plausible-looking placeholder, not a shading model.\n- A 32×16×32 `float`-but-actually-`uint8` `VoxelLightVolume` stored **inside the level JSON** is\n  49 KB of base64 per volume before any encoding; the level format would need a sidecar buffer, not\n  the JSON the editor round-trips today.\n\n## 5. Build order\n\n1. Probe grid baked at load + sampled per face (rules already exist).\n2. Per-face UV offset for scroll/frame-loop materials (rules already exist) — terminals, ooze,\n   signage.\n3. Light styles wired to the existing HPS/IPS intensity (one integer per fixture).\n4. Screen tints (already have a full-screen quad path from weather grading).\n5. Palette LUT shader — the first genuinely new fragment program.\n6. Height-slab fog, then a real specular term per face.\n\nEverything in this document that is *already* implemented is the rules layer, and it is verified\nheadless by `make test-material-rules`. Nothing here claims a visual result that has not been seen:\nno GPU, no display in this environment.\n"
}

Built and verified — with one important correction to the premise of the spec dump.

## The spec doesn't compile here, and that changed the answer

SHANKPIT is **fixed-function GL 1.x plus one hand-loaded GL 2.0 shader path** (`gl_shader.h` — flashlight beam, fireball). So `#version 330 core`, VAOs, `sampler3D`/`glTexImage3D`, `glVertexAttribIPointer` and a deferred G-buffer **cannot build or run** on this target. The pasted fragment shader is also not PBR (`pow(1-roughness,4)*metallic*NdotV` has no light integral, no Fresnel, no distribution term), and "bit-identical visual timing across the cluster" is only true of the **CPU-side parameters** — GPU rasterisation isn't bit-identical across vendors. Written up in `docs/RENDER_NORTHSTAR.md` §4 rather than silently copied.

## What a story actually needs is animation — so that's what's in PARENA

`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn` → `material_rules.c` (`make regen-material-rules`):

| Need | Rule |
|---|---|
| Doom palette cycling | `palette-index-256` (wraps, never negative) + material kind 3 |
| Quake strobes / HL fluorescents / GTA sodium lights | **8 light styles**, 0..1000‰ of a fixture's brightness: steady, strobe, unstable fluorescent, broken tube, pulse, dying, alarm, candle |
| Texture swim / ooze / canals / conveyors | kinds 1 and 4 with per-second scroll that **wraps on the second**, plus a vertical component so ooze reads thick |
| HL terminals, cameras, bomb timers | `mat-frame-index(fps, frames, tick)` — one sheet, one offset per frame |
| Emissive faces in dark rooms | `mat-emissive-milli(style, tick, room_light)` with a floor so a lit terminal still reads by day |
| Arcade threat feedback | low-health, submerged, acid and shield tints, all 0..1000 |
| Dark corners / streetlight pools | `vlm-axis-index-milli` — the clamped integer lookup for a **baked probe grid**, which is the honest half of Source 2's `M_combined_light_probe_volume` (a grid sampled per face, not a 3D texture this build can bind) |

## Missing vs Source 2, ranked by what's realistic here
1. **Baked probe grid** (biggest win, rules already exist) → 2. **PBR-shaped** numbers on materials, no normal maps → 3. **height-slab fog** for light shafts → 4. **palette LUT shader** — the only genuinely new fragment program needed → 5. UV-offset draw path for scroll/frame materials.

=== br_arena head ===
;; stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_arena.prn -- the arena as a signed-distance field, its four towers, and the dirt track.
;;
;; The level is SHANKPIT's stadium (packages/common/physics.h: map_geo_stadium, stadium_rally_loop): a bowl with a dirt rally loop
;; running round the floor and a tower at each of its four corners. Here the bowl is a ROUNDED BOX -- floor, four walls and the
;; ceiling joined by quarter-pipes -- so a wall is just a steeper bit of floor and the curl at the top is a road that goes over
;; your head, like the ramp the Tesla Roadster drives up in the demo. Everything the physics needs about the shape is one
;; function, (arena-free x y z): the distance from a point to the nearest solid, positive in the open air. The surface normal is
;; its gradient. Cars stick to whatever surface their fans reach, so floor / wall / ceiling are the same code.
;;
;; The goals are the towers: a vertical shaft rising out of the ceiling at each corner. They are UPSIDE DOWN -- the mouth of the
;; goal faces the floor, so a goal is scored by flying the ball UP into it.
;;
;;   room   half-extents 520 x 120 x 520 (the floor is y = 0, the ceiling y = 240), every edge rounded with radius 70
;;   tower  t = 0..3 at corner (sx, sz) = (t&1 ? +1 : -1, t&2 ? +1 : -1): shaft radius 40 at (sx*450, sz*450), open from the
;;          ceiling up to y = 340. The ball is in the goal when its centre is in the shaft above y = 244.
;;   track  SHANKPIT's 11-point rally loop at 0.55 scale, road half-width 35, shoulder 47, baked into a 256x256 floor texture

(defn a-hx [] : F32 520.0)
(defn a-hz [] : F32 520.0)
(defn a-h [] : F32 240.0)          ; ceiling height
(defn a-r [] : F32 70.0)           ; the fillet radius of every edge
(defn a-cy [] : F32 120.0)
(defn t-r [] : F32 40.0)           ; tower shaft radius
(defn t-off [] : F32 450.0)        ; tower axis offset on x and z: the apex of a corner, where a ball climbing the corner edge arrives
(defn t-top [] : F32 340.0)        ; the roof of a shaft
(defn goal-y [] : F32 244.0)       ; the ball is in once its centre is above this inside a shaft

;; team t's tower corner signs
(defn tw-sx [(t : I32)] : F32 (if (= (bit-and t 1) 1) 1.0 -1.0))
(defn tw-sz [(t : I32)] : F32 (if (= (bit-and t 2) 2) 1.0 -1.0))
(defn tw-x [(t : I32)] : F32 (* (tw-sx t) (t-off)))
(defn tw-z [(t : I32)] : F32 (* (tw-sz t) (t-off)))

;; ---- team colours: muted, distinct against a dark stadium --------------------------------------------
(defn team-color [(t : I32)] : I32
  (case (bit-and t 3)
    0 (rgb 236 184 92)     ; amber
    1 (rgb 84 190 178)     ; teal
    2 (rgb 166 134 220)    ; violet
    (rgb 232 112 98)))     ; coral
(defn team-name [(t : I32)] : String
  (case (bit-and t 3) 0 "AMBER" 1 "TEAL" 2 "VIOLET" "CORAL"))

;; ---- the signed-distance field ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; free distance to the rounded box: r - |max(q, 0)| - min(max(q.x, q.y, q.z), 0), q = |p - centre| - (half - r)
(defn room-free [(x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32)] : F32
  (let [(qx : F32) (- (abs-f x) (- (a-hx) (a-r)))
        (qy : F32) (- (abs-f (- y (a-cy))) (- (a-cy) (a-r)))
        (qz : F32) (- (abs-f z) (- (a-hz) (a-r)))
        (mx : F32) (fmax2 qx 0.0)
        (my : F32) (fmax2 qy 0.0)
        (mz : F32) (fmax2 qz 0.0)
        (l : F32) (sqrt (+ (+ (* mx mx) (* my my)) (* mz mz)))
        (inner : F32) (fmin2 (fmax2 qx (fmax2 qy qz)) 0.0)]
    (- (- (a-r) l) inner)))

;; the shaft of the tower nearest (x, z); well below the ceiling it does not exist
(defn shaft-rho [(x : F32) (z : F32)] : F32
  (len2 (- x (* (sgn x) (t-off))) (- z (* (sgn z) (t-off)))))
(defn shaft-free [(x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32)] : F32
  (if (> y (- (a-h) 30.0))
      (fmin2 (- (t-r) (shaft-rho x z)) (- (t-top) y))
      -999.0))

(defn arena-free [(x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32)] : F32
  (fmax2 (room-free x y z) (shaft-free x y z)))

;; the unit normal at (x, y, z), pointing into the open air, into g-sdx/y/z
(defn arena-normal! [(x : F32) (y : F32) (z : F32)] : Unit
  (let [(rf : F32) (room-free x y z)
        (sf : F32) (shaft-free x y z)]
    (if (> sf rf)
        (let [(cx : F32) (* (sgn x) (t-off))
              (cz : F32) (* (sgn z) (t-off))
              (dx : F32) (- x cx)
              (dz : F32) (- z cz)
              (rho : F32) (fmax2 (len2 dx dz) 0.0001)]
          (if (<= (- (t-r) rho) (- (t-top) y))
              (do (gf! (g-sdx) (/ (- 0.0 dx) rho)) (gf! (g-sdy) 0.0) (gf! (g-sdz) (/ (- 0.0 dz) rho)))
              (do (gf! (g-sdx) 0.0) (gf! (g-sdy) -1.0) (gf! (g-sdz) 0.0))))
=== br_phys constants ===
;; stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_phys.prn -- the rocket car, the ball, and the world they share. 60 Hz (16 ms ticks), two substeps each.
;;
;; THE CAR is modelled on the Tesla Roadster rocket demo (the founder's reference): a low car with FOUR LIFT NOZZLES under it
;; and cold-gas jets on its flanks, plus FANS under the floor that suck it onto the road so it can drive inverted. Everything it
;; spends comes from one tank of compressed AIR (like mana: it refills far faster than boost does in Rocket League).
;;
;;   on a surface  (fans on and a surface within reach)   the car's up axis swings onto the surface normal, gravity is beaten by
;;                 the fans, so floor, wall and ceiling are all "road". W/S throttle, A/D steer. The tyres hold the car up to a
;;                 limit (dirt holds far less than concrete): past it the tail steps out and the car drifts. The fans only
;;                 catch a car belly-down, so a car that lands on its roof scrapes along until it rolls (or tips) back over
;;   in the air    the car is a thruster platform with PRECISE, rate-commanded control on every axis:
;;                    pitch / yaw / roll   angular rates follow the command and STOP when you let go (cold-gas attitude jets)
;;                    lift                 the four nozzles, along the car's up axis
;;                    boost                the rear nozzle, along the car's forward axis
;;                    strafe, fore / aft   the flank jets, along its right / forward axes
;;   the tank      lift 26 /s, boost 22 /s, jets 9 /s, attitude 4 /s of 100; it refills 34 /s once you stop spending (48 /s on a
;;                 surface), plus a team-synergy bonus (br_rules.prn). Empty, the car still turns at a quarter rate -- never helpless.
;;
;; The command a car obeys is nine numbers (thr, steer, pitch, roll, strafe, lift, boost, fans-off, magnet): a person's keys, a
;; bot's brain, or the replay log write the same fields, so a match is a pure function of (seed, roster, the humans' commands).
;;
;; THE MAGNET (founder: "make the ball magnet to the cars ... remember its like quidich ... you can add a control for the magnet ...
;; let the ball be thrown and passed like NBA street vol 2"). The ball is a Quaffle: you catch it, carry it, pass it, throw it.
;;   hold the button  the magnet is on: a free ball near the car's CRADLE (a point just ahead of the nose and a little above it) is
;;                    pulled in -- harder the closer it gets, and the pull damps the ball's speed relative to the car so it
;;                    settles into the cradle instead of orbiting it. A ball that reaches the cradle slowly enough is CAUGHT;
;;                    one that comes in too fast is fumbled and just hits the car, as it always did.
;;   carrying         the ball rides the cradle wherever the car goes (floor, wall, ceiling, air) -- but the tank does not refill,
;;                    the car's top speed is 90%, and after five seconds the ball is thrown for you (no stalling).
;;   let go           the THROW: the car's velocity plus 260 along the nose -- or, with a team-mate in a 28 degree cone ahead that
;;                    is calling for it (its own button held), a PASS led to where that team-mate will be when the ball gets
;;                    there; a team-mate's pass is easier to catch.
;;   tackles          an enemy bumping the carrier (or driving into the carried ball) knocks it loose; a team-mate never does.
;; With the button up nothing here runs, and the car and the ball behave exactly as they did before the magnet existed.
;;
;; ON FIRE (br_fire.prn) reaches in here at the places marked "on fire": a burning car's tank stays full (air-tick!), its throws
;; are 35% faster and leave alight (throw!), its magnet reaches 50% further (magnet-pull!), a burning pass is that much easier
;; for the team-mate to catch (catch-limit), a car that is not burning puts a burning ball out by playing it (credit-touch!),
;; and a steal puts the carrier's fire out (ball-car!, car-car!). The fires' clocks run once a tick in physics-tick!.

(defn tick-dt [] : F32 0.016)
(defn sub-dt [] : F32 0.008)
(defn grav [] : F32 77.0)
(defn rc [] : F32 4.0)              ; car collision sphere radius (two spheres, 3.6 either side of the centre)
(defn sph-off [] : F32 3.6)
(defn rb [] : F32 11.0)             ; the ball
(defn ball-grav [] : F32 66.0)
(defn fan-force [] : F32 130.0)
(defn fan-reach [] : F32 6.0)       ; the fans catch a car whose wheels are this close
(defn fan-hold [] : F32 12.0)       ; ... and keep hold until it is this far
(defn tank-max [] : F32 100.0)

;; ---- basis helpers -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; right = forward x up  (so right x up = -forward, a normal non-mirrored camera frame)
(defn set-right! [(s : I32)] : Unit
  (let [(fx : F32) (c-fx s) (fy : F32) (c-fy s) (fz : F32) (c-fz s)
        (ux : F32) (c-ux s) (uy : F32) (c-uy s) (uz : F32) (c-uz s)]
    (set-c-rx! s (- (* fy uz) (* fz uy)))
    (set-c-ry! s (- (* fz ux) (* fx uz)))
    (set-c-rz! s (- (* fx uy) (* fy ux)))))

;; Gram-Schmidt: forward stays, up is made perpendicular to it, right follows
(defn fix-basis! [(s : I32)] : Unit
  (let [(fx : F32) (c-fx s) (fy : F32) (c-fy s) (fz : F32) (c-fz s)
        (il : F32) (inv-len3 fx fy fz)
        (gx : F32) (* fx il) (gy : F32) (* fy il) (gz : F32) (* fz il)
        (ux : F32) (c-ux s) (uy : F32) (c-uy s) (uz : F32) (c-uz s)
        (d : F32) (dot3 gx gy gz ux uy uz)
        (px : F32) (- ux (* gx d)) (py : F32) (- uy (* gy d)) (pz : F32) (- uz (* gz d))
        (iu : F32) (inv-len3 px py pz)]
    (set-c-fx! s gx) (set-c-fy! s gy) (set-c-fz! s gz)
    (set-c-ux! s (* px iu)) (set-c-uy! s (* py iu)) (set-c-uz! s (* pz iu))
    (set-right! s)))

;; rotate the vector stored at words (i0, i0+1, i0+2) of car s about the unit axis k by an angle (given as cos, sin)
(defn rot-words! [(s : I32) (i0 : I32) (kx : F32) (ky : F32) (kz : F32) (c : F32) (sn : F32)] : Unit
  (let [(vx : F32) (cf s i0) (vy : F32) (cf s (+ i0 1)) (vz : F32) (cf s (+ i0 2))
        (d : F32) (* (dot3 kx ky kz vx vy vz) (- 1.0 c))
        (cx : F32) (- (* ky vz) (* kz vy))
        (cy : F32) (- (* kz vx) (* kx vz))
        (cz : F32) (- (* kx vy) (* ky vx))]
    (cf! s i0 (+ (+ (* vx c) (* cx sn)) (* kx d)))
    (cf! s (+ i0 1) (+ (+ (* vy c) (* cy sn)) (* ky d)))
    (cf! s (+ i0 2) (+ (+ (* vz c) (* cz sn)) (* kz d)))))

  "content": "#ifndef SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_H\n#define SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_H\n\n/* br_stadium.h -- Bedrock Racers' stadium, natively: the SDF the car drives on and the exact mesh\n * the renderer draws, both generated from the SAME PARENA numbers as the wasm game\n * (PARENA/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_stadium.prn -> br_stadium.c).\n *\n * WHY THIS SHAPE: the arena is a rounded box -- floor, four walls and the ceiling joined by 70-unit\n * quarter-pipes -- so a wall is just a steeper bit of floor and the curl at the top is a road that\n * goes over your head. Wall-riding needs a CONTINUOUS normal, which is why the authoritative shape is\n * an SDF (one normal per point) and the faceted shell is only for destruction and drawing.\n *\n * The mesh is EXACT, not a shrink-wrapped approximation: six flat faces inset by the fillet radius,\n * twelve quarter-cylinder edges, eight eighth-sphere corners. Every emitted vertex therefore sits on\n * the SDF surface to floating-point precision, which is what makes the fixed-function lighting\n * (retro_lighting) interpolate across the joint without a visible band.\n *\n * Deliberately NOT here: the four goal shafts (they are separate SDF terms and a separate mesh), the\n * baked floor texture, and any collision response -- those belong to the physics step and the level\n * loader, and faking them here would hide the work that is actually still missing.\n */\n\n#include <math.h>\n#include \"br_stadium_host.h\"\n\n#define BR_STADIUM_MAX_QUADS 4096\n\ntypedef struct { float p[3]; float n[3]; } BrStadiumVert;\ntypedef struct { BrStadiumVert v[4]; } BrStadiumQuad;\ntypedef struct { BrStadiumQuad q[BR_STADIUM_MAX_QUADS]; int count; } BrStadiumMesh;\n\n/* ---- queries -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */\nstatic inline float br_stadium_free(float x, float y, float z) { return stadium_free(x, y, z); }\n\n/* The surface normal at a point: the SDF's gradient, by central difference. Points INTO the open air\n * (out of the wall), which is what a car's fans clamp its up-axis to. */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_normal(float x, float y, float z, float n[3]) {\n    const float e = 0.5f;\n    float dx = stadium_free(x + e, y, z) - stadium_free(x - e, y, z);\n    float dy = stadium_free(x, y + e, z) - stadium_free(x, y - e, z);\n    float dz = stadium_free(x, y, z + e) - stadium_free(x, y, z - e);\n    float len = sqrtf(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz);\n    if (len < 1e-6f) { n[0] = 0.0f; n[1] = 1.0f; n[2] = 0.0f; return; }\n    n[0] = dx / len; n[1] = dy / len; n[2] = dz / len;\n}\n\nstatic inline int br_stadium_open(float x, float y, float z) { return stadium_open(x, y, z); }\n\n/* The fans' hold on a surface, 0..1000 permille of the car's weight (PARENA's curve). */\nstatic inline int br_stadium_grip_permille(int speed_milli) { return stadium_grip_permille(speed_milli); }\n\n/* ---- mesh ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_mesh_init(BrStadiumMesh *m) { if (m) m->count = 0; }\n\nstatic inline BrStadiumQuad *br_stadium_quad(BrStadiumMesh *m) {\n    if (!m || m->count >= BR_STADIUM_MAX_QUADS) return 0;\n    return &m->q[m->count++];\n}\n\nstatic inline void br_stadium_vert(BrStadiumQuad *qd, int i,\n                                   float x, float y, float z,\n                                   float nx, float ny, float nz) {\n    qd->v[i].p[0] = x; qd->v[i].p[1] = y; qd->v[i].p[2] = z;\n    qd->v[i].n[0] = nx; qd->v[i].n[1] = ny; qd->v[i].n[2] = nz;\n}\n\n/* shrunk half-extents and the room's centre (the fillet radius is measured from these faces) */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_dims(float H[3], float C[3]) {\n    H[0] = stadium_half_x() - stadium_radius();\n    H[1] = stadium_height() * 0.5f - stadium_radius();\n    H[2] = stadium_half_z() - stadium_radius();\n    C[0] = 0.0f;\n    C[1] = stadium_center_y();\n    C[2] = 0.0f;\n}\n\n/* one flat face: `axis` fixed at +-sign, the other two swept over their shrunk extents */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_face(BrStadiumMesh *m, int axis, float sgn, int q) {\n    static const int U[3] = { 1, 0, 0 };\n    static const int V[3] = { 2, 2, 1 };\n    float H[3], C[3];\n    int u, v;\n    br_stadium_dims(H, C);\n    u = U[axis];\n    v = V[axis];\n    for (int i = 0; i < q; i++) {\n        for (int j = 0; j < q; j++) {\n            BrStadiumQuad *qd = br_stadium_quad(m);\n            if (!qd) return;\n            for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {\n                float fu = (float)(i + ((k == 1 || k == 2) ? 1 : 0)) / (float)q;\n                float fv = (float)(j + ((k >= 2) ? 1 : 0)) / (float)q;\n                float p[3] = { 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };\n                float n[3] = { 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };\n                p[axis] = C[axis] + sgn * (H[axis] + stadium_radius());\n                p[u] = C[u] + (-H[u] + 2.0f * H[u] * fu);\n                p[v] = C[v] + (-H[v] + 2.0f * H[v] * fv);\n                n[axis] = sgn;\n                br_stadium_vert(qd, k, p[0], p[1], p[2], n[0], n[1], n[2]);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/* one quarter-cylinder fillet between the faces normal to axes i and j, running along axis k */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_edge(BrStadiumMesh *m, int i, int j, float si, float sj, int q) {\n    int k = 3 - i - j;\n    float H[3], C[3];\n    br_stadium_dims(H, C);\n    for (int a = 0; a < q; a++) {\n        for (int b = 0; b < q; b++) {\n            BrStadiumQuad *qd = br_stadium_quad(m);\n            if (!qd) return;\n            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {\n                int ia = a + ((c == 1 || c == 2) ? 1 : 0);\n                int ib = b + ((c >= 2) ? 1 : 0);\n                float th = (float)ia * (1.57079632679f / (float)q);\n                float t = -H[k] + 2.0f * H[k] * ((float)ib / (float)q);\n                float n[3] = { 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };\n                float p[3] = { 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f };\n                n[i] = si * cosf(th);\n                n[j] = sj * sinf(th);\n                p[i] = C[i] + si * H[i] + stadium_radius() * n[i];\n                p[j] = C[j] + sj * H[j] + stadium_radius() * n[j];\n                p[k] = C[k] + t;\n                br_stadium_vert(qd, c, p[0], p[1], p[2], n[0], n[1], n[2]);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/* one eighth-sphere corner */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_corner(BrStadiumMesh *m, float sx, float sy, float sz, int q) {\n    float H[3], C[3];\n    br_stadium_dims(H, C);\n    for (int a = 0; a < q; a++) {\n        for (int b = 0; b < q; b++) {\n            BrStadiumQuad *qd = br_stadium_quad(m);\n            if (!qd) return;\n            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {\n                int ia = a + ((c == 1 || c == 2) ? 1 : 0);\n                int ib = b + ((c >= 2) ? 1 : 0);\n                float th = (float)ia * (1.57079632679f / (float)q);   /* polar, from +y */\n                float ph = (float)ib * (1.57079632679f / (float)q);   /* azimuth in the xz quadrant */\n                float nx = sx * sinf(th) * cosf(ph);\n                float ny = sy * cosf(th);\n                float nz = sz * sinf(th) * sinf(ph);\n                float r = stadium_radius();\n                br_stadium_vert(qd, c,\n                                sx * H[0] + r * nx,\n                                C[1] + sy * H[1] + r * ny,\n                                sz * H[2] + r * nz,\n                                nx, ny, nz);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/* br_stadium_build_mesh -- the whole shell at `quality` subdivisions per face/edge/corner.\n * quality 4 is 416 quads and already reads smooth under fixed-function lighting; 6 is 936. */\nstatic inline int br_stadium_build_mesh(int quality, BrStadiumMesh *m) {\n    if (!m) return 0;\n    br_stadium_mesh_init(m);\n    if (quality < 1) quality = 1;\n    for (int axis = 0; axis < 3; axis++) {\n        br_stadium_face(m, axis, 1.0f, quality);\n        br_stadium_face(m, axis, -1.0f, quality);\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n        for (int j = i + 1; j < 3; j++) {\n            br_stadium_edge(m, i, j, 1.0f, 1.0f, quality);\n            br_stadium_edge(m, i, j, 1.0f, -1.0f, quality);\n            br_stadium_edge(m, i, j, -1.0f, 1.0f, quality);\n            br_stadium_edge(m, i, j, -1.0f, -1.0f, quality);\n        }\n    }\n    for (int sx = -1; sx <= 1; sx += 2) {\n        for (int sy = -1; sy <= 1; sy += 2) {\n            for (int sz = -1; sz <= 1; sz += 2) {\n                br_stadium_corner(m, (float)sx, (float)sy, (float)sz, quality);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return m->count;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_H */\n"
}

      /* br_stadium_host.h -- the Bedrock Racers stadium shape, from PARENA.
       *
       * The shape lives in PARENA/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_stadium.prn (deduped out of the web game's
       * br_arena.prn, which already said the level WAS SHANKPIT's stadium), generated into br_stadium.c by
       * scripts/gen_br_stadium.sh / `make regen-br-stadium`. Both the wasm game and this client link the
       * same generated numbers, so "pixel for pixel" starts with "same walls". */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_HOST_H
      #define SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_HOST_H
      
      float stadium_half_x(void);
      float stadium_half_z(void);
      float stadium_height(void);
      float stadium_radius(void);
      float stadium_center_y(void);
      float stadium_tower_offset(void);
      float stadium_tower_radius(void);
      float stadium_tower_top(void);
      float stadium_goal_y(void);
      float stadium_track_scale(void);
      float stadium_track_half_width(void);
      float stadium_track_shoulder(void);
      float stadium_free(float x, float y, float z);
      int stadium_open(float x, float y, float z);
      int stadium_tower(float x, float z);
      int stadium_grip_permille(int speed_milli);
      int stadium_facet_degrees(void);
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_HOST_H */

      SERVERCTL_SRC:= apps/server/serverctl.c
      
      # ---- Source-list export for CI ----
      # CI (.github/workflows/{tests,release}.yml) compiles the Windows lobby and the Linux server with
      # raw gcc/mingw lines instead of `make` (different libs/flags). Those lines used to carry a
      # hand-copied copy of LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC and drifted NINE times -- including a 3-day red release
      # pipeline (2026-09-28..10-01) -- so they now expand these two targets instead:
      #   gcc $(make -s print-server-src) ...        x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc $(make -s print-lobby-src) ...
      # A new packages/*.c added to LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC above is now picked up by CI automatically.
      .PHONY: print-lobby-src print-server-src test-os-menu test-os-menu-gl check-windows
      
      # Compile every Windows-client source under mingw-w64 (no link, so no .a/.dll objects needed). Catches
      # compile-only breakage that otherwise waits for a release job -- see the script's own header comment.
      check-windows:
        bash scripts/check_windows_build.sh
      print-lobby-src:
        @echo $(LOBBY_SRC)
      print-server-src:
        @echo $(SERVER_SRC)
      
      # ---- Outputs ----
      LOBBY_BIN    := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby
      SERVER_BIN   := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_server
      SERVERCTL_BIN:= $(BIN_DIR)/serverctl
      GO_SERVER_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server
      EMILY_BOT_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/emily-bot
      EA_DIR       := dist/ea
      
      # ---- Targets ----
      .PHONY: test-witness-ai-zombies test-bullet-hole test-queue-level test-baked-levels test-level-save bake-levels all lobby server serverctl clean setup print go-server ea ea-windows emily-bot rigid-ragdoll test-physics test-audio-chain ux-screenshot-test
      
      all: $(LOBBY_BIN) $(SERVER_BIN)
      
      # Ensure bin/ exists even when building a single target
      $(BIN_DIR):
        @mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
      
      setup: $(BIN_DIR)
      
      # ---- EDITOR.GAME in-process widget (S559, 2026-09-27) ----
      # Founder real-time: "the editor app fails to launch -- instead of having it launch it should pop
      # a widget up on the screen ... deeply integrate it as a widget on the screen the notes auto
      # save." apps/lobby/src/editor_widget_bridge.c links against EDITOR.GAME's own real
      # editor_widget_* API, consumed as a sibling checkout (../EDITOR.GAME -- same path MODULE.bazel's
      # own local_path_override already assumes). Same 5-file build EDITOR.GAME's own plain Makefile
      # uses to produce its standalone `editor-game` binary, just linked into shank_lobby instead:
      # gen/editor_full.c (the generated PARENA stdlib + examples/editor_main.c, concatenated -- see
      # EDITOR.GAME/Makefile's own identical rule) and runtime/parena_runtime.c define/call the plain
      # arena_init/arena_alloc/arena_strdup/arena_free_all names, which would otherwise collide at link
      # time with SHANKPIT's own already-linked, deliberately-minimal packages/world/parena_runtime.c
      # (same 4 names, real but different, narrower implementation) -- both files are compiled here with
      # a matching -D rename so ONLY this pair's calls/definitions move to edg_arena_*, leaving
      # SHANKPIT's own copy completely untouched. src/arena.c/src/fmt.c/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c are
      # EDITOR.GAME's own SEPARATE compiler-internal bump allocator, already renamed to pf_arena_* by
      # EDITOR.GAME's own PRNFMT_RENAME convention (unrelated to the edg_arena_* rename above -- two
      # different collisions, two different renames, matching EDITOR.GAME's own Makefile/BUILD.bazel
      # precedent exactly).
      EDITOR_GAME_DIR    := ../EDITOR.GAME
      # vec_i32_at -- PARENA's C emitter generates this Vec<i32> helper as a plain global (not static)
      # in every translation unit that uses Vec<i32>; packages/world/png_decode_gen.c (SHANKPIT's own
      # PARENA-generated code, already in LOBBY_SRC) happens to generate one too, so it collides the
      # same way arena_init did -- confirmed via `nm -g` on both object files, exactly one overlap.
      EDITOR_GAME_RENAME := -Darena_init=edg_arena_init -Darena_alloc=edg_arena_alloc -Darena_strdup=edg_arena_strdup -Darena_free_all=edg_arena_free_all -Dvec_i32_at=edg_vec_i32_at
      EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT := -Darena_init=pf_arena_init -Darena_alloc=pf_arena_alloc -Darena_strdup=pf_arena_strdup -Darena_free_all=pf_arena_free_all
      EDITOR_GAME_OBJS   := $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.o
      
      $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_stdlib_gen.c $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/examples/editor_main.c
        cat $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_stdlib_gen.c $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/examples/editor_main.c > $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w -DEDITOR_WIDGET_TEST_BUILD $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/arena.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/fmt.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src -c $< -o $@
      
      # Windows (mingw) variants of the same 5 objects, for ea-windows below -- separate output
      # filenames (.win.o) so a native `make lobby` and `make ea-windows` in the same tree never clobber
      # each other's objects. Verified for real: EDITOR.GAME's own runtime/parena_runtime.c and
      # generated stdlib code cross-compile under x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc with no source changes at all
      # (checked directly, not assumed -- the only NEW cross-build requirement is SDL2_ttf's own mingw
      # devel kit, same one PITVIPER/IDUNA.GAME/EDITOR.GAME's own standalone Windows builds already need,
      # per SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX below).
      MINGW_CC := x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
      EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN := $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.win.o
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w -DEDITOR_WIDGET_TEST_BUILD $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/arena.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/fmt.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      # ---- PELLEGRINO in-phone browser (SHANKPIT-PELLEGRINO-APP-02) ----
      # Pre-built objects linked at the end (NOT in LOBBY_SRC): needs its own mbedTLS copts/includes that
      # the rest of the lobby must never see. mbedTLS source comes from ../PELLEGRINO's pinned fetch script.
      PGB_DIR     := packages/pellegrino_browser_embed
      PELLEGRINO_DIR ?= ../PELLEGRINO
      PGB_MBEDTLS  = $(shell [ -d $(PELLEGRINO_DIR) ] && cd $(PELLEGRINO_DIR) && bash scripts/fetch_mbedtls.sh 2>/dev/null)
      PGB_DEFS    := -DPARENA_WITH_TLS -DPARENA_TLS_STATIC_HEAP -DPARENA_TLS_HEAP_STATS -DPARENA_WITH_QUIC_CRYPTO "-DMBEDTLS_USER_CONFIG_FILE=\"pellegrino_user_config.h\""
      PGB_OBJ_DIR := $(BIN_DIR)/pgb
      PGB_MBED_OBJS = $(patsubst %.c,$(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/mbed_%.o,$(notdir $(wildcard $(PGB_MBEDTLS)/library/*.c)))
      PGB_OBJS     = $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/phone_browser_embed.o $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/monocypher.o $(PGB_MBED_OBJS)
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR):
        mkdir -p $@
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/phone_browser_embed.o: $(PGB_DIR)/phone_browser_embed.c $(PGB_DIR)/pellegrino_gen.inc | $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -w $(PGB_DEFS) -I$(PGB_DIR) -I$(PGB_DIR)/runtime -I$(PGB_MBEDTLS)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/monocypher.o: $(PGB_DIR)/runtime/aead/monocypher.c | $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -w -c $< -o $@
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/mbed_%.o: | $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -w $(PGB_DEFS) -I$(PGB_DIR)/runtime -I$(PGB_MBEDTLS)/include -I$(PGB_MBEDTLS)/library -c $(PGB_MBEDTLS)/library/$*.c -o $@
      
      # ---- CLIENT / LOBBY ----
      lobby: $(LOBBY_BIN)
      
      $(LOBBY_BIN): $(LOBBY_SRC) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS) $(PGB_OBJS) | $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🔨 Building Lobby Client..."
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LOBBY_SRC) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS) $(PGB_OBJS) -o $@ $(LIBS_GL) -lSDL2_ttf
      
      # ---- OS menu through PELLEGRINO (kanban #627) ----
      # Headless (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy): builds the HTML menu, paints it with PELLEGRINO, clicks every tile, checks the
      # index mapping and keyboard activation. Links packages/world/parena_runtime.c too, to prove the pgm_ rename
      # (packages/pellegrino_embed/pg_rename.h) keeps the engine's runtime from colliding with the lobby's.
      test-os-menu: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -w -Ipackages/pellegrino_embed -Ipackages/world packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.c packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed_test.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_embed_test -lSDL2 -lm
        SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_embed_test
      
      # Same menu through the lobby's real GL path (packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_gl.h) in a real GL context:
      # needs a display (xvfb-run make test-os-menu-gl) and libGL; checks tile colours at screen positions + hit mapping.
      test-os-menu-gl: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -w -Ipackages/pellegrino_embed -Ipackages/world packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.c packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_gl_test.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_gl_test -lSDL2 -lGL -lm
        $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_gl_test
      
      # ---- GAME SERVER ----
      server: $(SERVER_BIN)
      
      $(SERVER_BIN): $(SERVER_SRC) | $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🔨 Building Game Server..."
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(SERVER_SRC) -o $@ $(LIBS_M)
      
      # ---- RIGID BODY PHYSICS (GOLDEN BAND grb, vendored in packages/goldenband) ----
      # Founder real-time 2026-09-27: "upgrade shankpit ... to formal rigid body physics".
      PHYSICS_SRC := packages/simulation/rigid_ragdoll.c packages/goldenband/grb.c packages/goldenband/gskel.c packages/goldenband/gpose.c
      
      rigid-ragdoll: $(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll: tools/rigid_ragdoll/main.c $(PHYSICS_SRC) | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wextra $(INCLUDES) $^ -o $@ $(LIBS_M)
      
      # Headless physics tests (run from the repo root -- they load assets/goldenband/*.gskel).
      test-physics: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wextra $(INCLUDES) packages/simulation/rigid_ragdoll_test.c $(PHYSICS_SRC) -o $(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll_test $(LIBS_M)
        ./$(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll_test
      
      # Real, live UX regression test -- boots the real lobby binary under headless Xvfb, opens the
      # real LEVELS overlay via a synthetic XTEST Enter keypress, fails if either screen renders
      # suspiciously close to solid black (the blank-screen symptom this was written to catch). Needs
      # lobby already built (make lobby); needs Xvfb/ImageMagick/python3-xlib installed.
      ux-screenshot-test: lobby
        ./scripts/ux_screenshot_test.sh
      
      # ---- SERVER CONTROL (OPTIONAL, LOCAL ONLY) ----
      serverctl: $(SERVERCTL_BIN)
      
      $(SERVERCTL_BIN): $(SERVERCTL_SRC) | $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🖥 Building Server Control (requires ncurses)..."
        $(CC) -O2 $< -o $@ -lncurses
      
      # ---- GO MATCHMAKER / SCENE SERVER ----
      go-server: $(GO_SERVER_BIN)
      
      $(GO_SERVER_BIN): $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🔨 Building Go scene server..."
        GOWORK=off go build -o $(GO_SERVER_BIN) ./apps2/server-go/
      
      # ---- EMILY BOT (Go headless player) ----
      emily-bot: $(EMILY_BOT_BIN)
      
      $(EMILY_BOT_BIN): $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "Building Emily bot client..."
        GOWORK=off go build -o $(EMILY_BOT_BIN) ./apps2/emily-bot/
      
      # ---- STEAM EA BUILD (Linux) ----
      # Packages: headless Go scene server + C lobby client + README into dist/ea/
      # Prerequisites: SDL2 + OpenGL development libraries installed
      ea: $(LOBBY_BIN) $(GO_SERVER_BIN)
        @echo "📦 Packaging EA build (Linux)..."
        @mkdir -p $(EA_DIR)
        @cp $(LOBBY_BIN)  $(EA_DIR)/shank_lobby
        @cp $(GO_SERVER_BIN) $(EA_DIR)/shank_go_server
        @cp docs/EA_BUILD.md $(EA_DIR)/README.txt
        @echo "✅ EA build ready at $(EA_DIR)/"
        @ls -lh $(EA_DIR)/
      
      # ---- STEAM EA BUILD (Windows cross-compile, requires mingw-w64) ----
      # Real, found-live fix (S459-41 follow-up): this target used to target i686-w64-mingw32-gcc, but
      # the only real mingw SDL2 dev kit checked out on this box (/tmp/sdl2_mingw) is x86_64, matching
      # the Go server's own GOARCH=amd64 above -- 32-bit and 64-bit mingw libs are never interchangeable
      # (verified live: linking against the x86_64 archive with the i686 compiler leaves real symbols
      # like SDL_GetError undefined, since the .o members are a different COFF machine type entirely).
      # SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX is overridable for a box with its dev kit somewhere else.
      SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX ?= /tmp/sdl2_mingw
      ea-windows: $(BIN_DIR) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN)
        @echo "🪟 Cross-compiling Go server for Windows..."
        GOWORK=off GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -o $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server.exe ./apps2/server-go/
        @echo "🔨 Cross-compiling C client for Windows (requires x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc)..."
        # -lSDL2_ttf (S559, EDITOR.GAME in-process widget) needs SDL2_ttf's own mingw devel kit merged
        # into $(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX) -- same one PITVIPER/IDUNA.GAME/EDITOR.GAME's own standalone
        # Windows builds already fetch (see .github/workflows/release.yml's own "Install Dependencies"
        # step); the base SDL2 mingw devel kit alone does not ship it.
        # Real in-phone PELLEGRINO browser if scripts/build_pgb_windows.sh succeeds (needs ../PELLEGRINO), else the stub.
        -bash scripts/build_pgb_windows.sh $(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)
        x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include $(LOBBY_SRC) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN) \
          $(if $(wildcard $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/phone_browser_embed.o),$(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/phone_browser_embed.o $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/monocypher.o $(wildcard $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/mbed/*.o) -lbcrypt,packages/pellegrino_browser_embed/phone_browser_stub.c) \
          -o $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby.exe \
          -L$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/lib -lSDL2 -lSDL2_ttf -lopengl32 -lglu32 -lm -static-libgcc \
          -lws2_32 -ldinput8 -ldxguid -ldxerr8 -luser32 -lgdi32 -lwinmm -limm32 -lole32 -loleaut32 -lshell32 -lsetupapi -lversion -luuid
        @echo "📦 Packaging EA build (Windows)..."
        @mkdir -p dist/ea-windows
        @cp $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server.exe dist/ea-windows/
        @cp $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby.exe dist/ea-windows/
        @[ -f $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/cacert.pem ] && cp $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/cacert.pem dist/ea-windows/ || true
        @cp docs/EA_BUILD.md dist/ea-windows/README.txt
        @echo "✅ Windows EA build ready at dist/ea-windows/"
      
      clean:
        @echo "🧹 Cleaning..."
        rm -rf $(BIN_DIR) dist/
      
      print:
        @echo "LOBBY_BIN=$(LOBBY_BIN)"
        @echo "SERVER_BIN=$(SERVER_BIN)"
        @echo "GO_SERVER_BIN=$(GO_SERVER_BIN)"
        @echo "EA_DIR=$(EA_DIR)"
      
      # test-bullet-hole -- per-gun bullet-hole decals (2026-10-01): shot detection, slot/size/ray mapping,
      # ring buffer, and that the 4 NOCK-exported PNGs (PARENA-authored, ImageMagick-paletted) decode through
      # PARENA's own png_decode. No SDL/GL needed.
      test-bullet-hole:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Ipackages/world -o /tmp/bullet_hole_test packages/world/bullet_hole_test.c \
          packages/world/png_decode_gen.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c -lm
        /tmp/bullet_hole_test
      
      # test-queue-level -- PACKET_QUEUE_LEVEL wire contract (card #481): size, id round-trip incl. -1, unique type.
      test-spraypaint:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -o /tmp/spraypaint_test packages/world/spraypaint_test.c -lm
        /tmp/spraypaint_test
      
      test-spray-decal:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror -Ipackages/common -o /tmp/spray_decal_test packages/common/spray_decal_test.c
        /tmp/spray_decal_test
      
      test-edu-widgets:
        $(CC) -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Ipackages/education packages/education/edu_widgets_test.c packages/education/edu_lexer.c packages/education/edu_bytecode.c packages/education/edu_parser.c packages/education/edu_vm.c packages/education/edu_bindings.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/edu_widgets_test
        $(BIN_DIR)/edu_widgets_test
        $(CC) -O1 -Wall -Wextra packages/world/level_boxes_edu_widgets_test.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/level_boxes_edu_widgets_test
        $(BIN_DIR)/level_boxes_edu_widgets_test
      
      test-queue-level:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror -Ipackages/common -o /tmp/queue_level_test packages/common/queue_level_test.c
        /tmp/queue_level_test
      
      # test-shield-packs -- card #541: 25% drop rule, once-per-death latch, pickup reach, wire contract of PACKET_SHIELD_PACKS.
      test-shield-packs:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror -Ipackages/common -o /tmp/shield_packs_test packages/simulation/shield_packs_test.c packages/simulation/shield_packs.c -lm
        /tmp/shield_packs_test
      
      # bake-levels -- card #479: regenerate packages/world/baked_levels_gen.h from a live IDUNA (review + commit the diff).
      bake-levels:
        python3 scripts/bake_levels.py
      
      # test-level-save -- EDIT MAP's F6 writes a complete level JSON with no IDUNA: every parsed field
      # (doors, buttons, nav nodes, characters, exits, zones, edu widgets, lab stations, buggy spawns,
      # brick damage) must survive save -> load.
      test-level-save:
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ipackages/world -o /tmp/level_save_test packages/world/level_save_test.c -lm
        /tmp/level_save_test
      
      # test-baked-levels -- card #479/#480: the baked level table serves the registry + every export offline.
      test-baked-levels:
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ipackages/world -o /tmp/baked_levels_test packages/world/baked_levels_test.c -lm
        /tmp/baked_levels_test
      
      # test-audio-chain -- NOCK filter chains in the engine (2026-09-27): packages/audio/audio_chain.c
      # over PARENA-generated audio_dsp_gen.c must reproduce IDUNA NOCK's TypeScript render bit-for-bit
      # (tests/audio/nock_chain_vectors.txt). No SDL needed.
      test-audio-chain:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror -Wno-unused-parameter tests/audio/test_audio_chain.c \
          packages/audio/audio_chain.c packages/audio/audio_dsp_gen.c -o /tmp/test_audio_chain -lm

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_br_stadium.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # gen_br_stadium.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/br_stadium.c from PARENA.
      #
      # The stadium's shape (a rounded box with 70-unit fillets, four upside-down goal shafts, the rally
      # loop's scale) is shared by the wasm game and the native SHANKPIT client:
      #   PARENA/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_stadium.prn
      # Usage: scripts/gen_br_stadium.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout, or PARENA_DIR)
      set -euo pipefail
      root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
      parena_dir="${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}"
      if [ -x "$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      elif [ -x "$parena_dir/parena" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/parena"
      else
          (cd "$parena_dir" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      fi
      "$parena_bin" build "$parena_dir/stdlib/bedrockracers/web/br_stadium.prn" \
          -o "$root/packages/simulation/br_stadium.c"
      echo "regenerated packages/simulation/br_stadium.c"

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/CHANGELOG.md
  content: |
      ## 2026-10-31
      
      - **feat(render): the Doom/Quake/Half-Life/GTA material vocabulary, as rules instead of a shader rewrite.** Founder paste (a spec dump proposing a `#version 330` PBR/VBO/voxel-lightmap pipeline) then: *"what other materials/shaders do we need for full doom/quake/half life/gta story telling?"* and *"anything missing from source 2 engine?"*. The audit came first and it changed the answer: SHANKPIT is fixed-function GL 1.x plus **one hand-loaded GL 2.0 shader path** (`gl_shader.h`, the flashlight beam and the fireball), so `#version 330 core`, VAOs, `sampler3D`/`glTexImage3D`, `glVertexAttribIPointer` and a deferred G-buffer **cannot compile or run here** — all named in `docs/RENDER_NORTHSTAR.md` §4, along with the pasted shader's fake PBR term and its claim of bit-identical GPU timing. What a story actually needs from a material is *animation*, so that is what was built, in PARENA where it can be deterministic: `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn` (generated into `packages/simulation/material_rules.c`, `make regen-material-rules`) — five material kinds (plain, scrolling, frame-loop, palette-LUT, emissive-flicker) with **UV scroll speeds that wrap on the second** and a vertical component so ooze reads as thick, **frame-loop sheets** (`mat-frame-index(fps, frames, tick)`) for terminals/cameras/bomb timers, **all eight Quake light styles** (steady, strobe, unstable fluorescent, broken tube, pulse, dying, alarm, candle) as 0..1000 permille of a fixture's brightness, emissive faces floored so a lit terminal still reads in a bright room, the four screen tints (low health, submerged, acid, shield), a 256-entry palette wrap that never goes negative, and `vlm-axis-index-milli` — the clamped integer mapping that is the honest half of Source 2's `M_combined_light_probe_volume` (a baked grid sampled per face, not a 3D texture this build cannot bind). Verified: `make test-material-rules` (every style stays in 0..1000 over 600 ticks; the strobe really goes dark and really lights; the fluorescent drops out 1-19 times in 10 s; the broken tube is dark more than twice as often as lit; snaps and frames wrap on the second; all 8 frames of a 10 fps sheet are reached; health tint is 0 at full and monotonic in damage; submerged saturates; palette -1 wraps to 255 and 300 to 44; probe axes clamp at both ends and mid-grid), plus `make check-windows` (96 lobby sources) and `make -B server`. NOT done, and named in the doc: **nothing of this is drawn yet** — no probe bake, no UV-offset draw path, no palette LUT shader, no tint quad wiring, and no visual verification is possible here (no GPU/display). The doc ranks the build order and says plainly that a real palette shader is the only genuinely new fragment program the list needs.

All four repos cloned and read before writing anything (`docs/EMPIRE_NORTHSTAR.md` records what each one actually contains, which is not what their names suggest: EMPIRE is a bridge + deck UI with no world, ECOWAR is the arena game with 16 tested cards and **no in-match deck UI**, REDGARDEN holds the team AI and hero kits, TRAPX is the doctrine — alignment and pressure on a grid, no avatar, no direct unit control). The lobby draws a burning buggy with the **same additive fireball shader the grenade/missile blast already uses** (`fireball_draw`, two billboards, sized by `fire_fx`), and the blast itself is the existing `fx_spawn_explosion` path. Two real bugs the new test caught and this fixes: the burn clock was inconsistent with the fire line when it was whole points per tick, and **the fire latched on `burning_ticks`, so a repaired car burned forever** — it is now a function of the hull, and a repair puts it out and restarts the fuse. Verified: `make test-vehicle-burn` — a healthy car is untouched by 10 s of ticking, 140 hull smokes with no flame and no hull loss, 4 ticks of fire is >0.6 fire-fx, **exactly one blast at ~296 ticks**, the flame is still >60% lit 5 ticks after a repair and out within 200, the flicker stays inside 1.3–2.45, a 900 kg buggy at 5 units/tick costs 22 hull and a scuff costs 0, **and the generated PARENA table must equal the header's defaults (checked field by field) so the game and the test cannot play different cars**. The number lives once in `phone.h` (`phone_tech_bonus_ms`), so the UI's readout and the zombie AI's actual window cannot drift apart. Points are earned from the XP this build already awards -- 1 per 500, re-derived every sync, so there is no second save file to drift and no way to be double-charged by a level load. The app draws `LV x/5` with a five-pip bar, the point balance, the resulting window in seconds with the base called out, and a real "no points" line instead of silently ignoring ENTER. Verified: `phone_test` (a SELECT spends one point and emits the upgrade effect; nine further presses stop exactly at level 5 with 0 points; a capped-and-broke SELECT is a no-op; a negative balance clamps) and `make test-pheromone-grenade` (with the maxed line installed a canister's window measures >17 s against the 9 s base).       - **feat(zombies): the lure feeds, the horde navigates, and your pheromone buys you a window that closes.** Founder: *"zombies shouldnt just walk into walls ... sometimes they should but that is when they are trying to break walls down they should have some ability to navigate the terrain i think citizens already do that also the zombies dont seem to respond to ferimone balls it should make them hungry and somewhat aggressive also it should guide them to the spot also they should attack the player ad the citizens when they are hungry or aggressive there should be some threshold where they dont attack you if your pherimone caused their hunger and agression but that should be like a fading memory your zombies wont attack you at first but they forget pretty quick and they will target you for the next snack after your window runs out so you need to be intentional with your phermone balls to move them around the map as there are more of them."* Three separate defects, one cause: the systems were all built and none of them were talking to each other. (1) **Walking into walls.** `witness_ai_tick`'s wall pass called `wai_avoid_walls(..., g_wall_hit_hook != NULL)`, and the real game always installs that hook, so every zombie was `relentless` -- route planning skipped -- and the whole horde ground the straight line into the nearest face and clawed it from 100 m out. It is now a real decision: breach only when the target is within `WITNESS_AI_ZOMBIE_BREACH_TARGET_RANGE` (70 m, i.e. the fight is right there) and the zombie is HUNTING/FRENZIED, otherwise it plans a route exactly as a citizen already did; the existing `g_wai_breach` stop-plant-and-tear path is untouched, which is what keeps wall-breaking working. (2) **Pheromone balls did nothing.** A marker only redirected the steering of a zombie with no hero lock -- it fed nothing, so a lure moved a horde around and left it exactly as harmless as it found it, and the marker's own thrower was never recorded at all (the parallel `g_pheromone_owner1[]` array now does, rather than adding a field to ported BIG_O code). A zombie now gains `WITNESS_AI_PHEROMONE_HUNGER_PER_SEC`/`_AGGRESSION_PER_SEC` (rate-clamped against the real tick delta) while it is steering to a canister, so the lure genuinely makes it dangerous, and it remembers whose canister recruited it. (3) **They never attacked each other or you.** Targeting was gated on `hunger >= STARVING` (0.70) alone, so a fed but furious zombie stood next to a citizen and did nothing -- `zombie_values.h`'s whole aggression meter was computed every tick and never read. New PARENA rule `zombies-pheromone-should-hunt(hunger_milli, aggression_milli)` makes it hungry OR aggressive (0.40 / 0.45, deliberately unequal: hunger is "I need a meal", aggression is "something just happened"), and the fading memory is its sibling `zombies-pheromone-spares-thrower(grace_ms, thrower_alive)` -- `WITNESS_AI_PHEROMONE_GRACE_MS` (9 s) of immunity for the THROWER ONLY, checked before the hero is even sensed, with the owner cleared the moment it lapses so a later thrower is judged fresh. Citizens were never covered, so a lured horde eats the neighbourhood and remembers you late. Verified: `make test-pheromone-grenade` -- a canister raises a zombie's hunger 0.13 -> 1.00 and its aggression past 0.20, the thrower can stand in its face for 3 s untouched, and after the window the same zombie bites them; `make test-witness-ai-zombies` -- a zombie 290 m from its target with a wall between routes around the building with ZERO claw hits, while the existing close-range test still claws the same wall 27 times; plus the pocket-escape, day/night, per-role REFLUX and mark-2-marker tests all still pass. Not done: no controller/left-trigger throw binding beyond the existing `BTN_PHEROMONE`, no HUD readout of the grace countdown (the `witness_ai_zombie_grace_ms` accessor it would need exists), and "somewhat aggressive" is a hunger/aggression rate rather than a new mood state.

      - **feat(world): the structural layer is wired in — a piece that loses its support actually comes down.** Follow-up to the same day's structural graph, which was built and proven headless but consumed by nothing. `brick_world.h` now builds the graph when a level loads (one node per destructible parent, `anchored` = on the world floor or touching any non-destructible solid — resting on it and bolted to it are the same thing here, because neither moves on its own) and re-evaluates it inside `brick_world_flush`, i.e. on load and on damage only: **zero per-tick cost**, which is the whole reason this shape was chosen for an MMO tick budget. A piece the graph can no longer justify is dropped whole by the new `bf_detach_parent` (`brick_fracture.h`), becoming one rigid chunk on the existing debris path instead of hanging in the air. It is budgeted exactly like the cell pass: a parent over `BF_CHUNK_CELLS` (256), or one arriving with the chunk queue full, stays standing rather than half-detaching. Piece mass now follows the damage (`1 - removed/cells`), so a wall carved down to a stub weighs what is left of it and a shot-away pillar stops holding a roof up long before its last cell goes. Two real fixes came out of wiring it: (1) `structure_boxes_meet`'s tolerance is now a WELDING DISTANCE (`>= -tol`, not `> tol`), because authored geometry is routinely flush — a roof sitting exactly on a pillar's top face shares a face with zero overlap, and under the old rule no authored piece ever joined anything; (2) the load-time baseline was taken after `structure_evaluate`, which strips a failed piece's support, so every overloaded building was quietly baselined as "authored decoration" and stood forever — it is now taken on the support flood before any load verdict. The same fix taught the engine to collapse a structure the rules say cannot hold itself **at load, before the first frame**, instead of waiting for someone to shoot it. The rules' overflow guard also changed: `struct-holds-load` was comparing `mass x 1000` against `capacity x 850` in I32, which overflows for any real building (a concrete pier holds 72 million kg); it now divides the capacity before applying the 15%, and the C-side 2-million-kg clamp that had flattened every material into one capacity is replaced by a 2-billion-kg arithmetic ceiling that never decides a verdict. Verified: `make test-brick-world` — the wood-post level loses all 7 post cells and all 72 deck cells at load, both stop being solid immediately and two chunks are queued; the identical deck on a concrete post survives untouched with zero failures; the wall-only level leaves the layer off; every pre-existing check (magnum breach, hammer, claw, glass chunk, net apply, saved damage) still passes. `make test-structure` still passes. NOT verified: the lobby and server binaries are not compiled here (no SDL2), so the two source-list edits (`Makefile` LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC, `packages/simulation/BUILD.bazel`) and the live look are reviewed, not built; and a dropped piece is one rigid body, not a tumbling pile of brick.
      - **feat(world): destructible brick gets a structural layer — joints, support, and a load cascade.** Founder real-time: "evolve the destructible brick logic into an intelligent, physically aware material and structural simulation ... a web of self-anchoring volumetric nodes". Scoped to what this engine can actually afford at MMO concurrency: no finite-element solver, no "layer bake", and no claiming either. Three things a player can feel, all deterministic so the server and every client agree. (1) **Joints at load** (`structure_build_joints`): boxes whose volumes intersect are joined — a piece sunk into a concrete master is ANCHORED, two crossing pieces of equal class are PEGGED (the virtual peg; timber is strong in shear, weak in tension). Whether a pair may join at all is PARENA's call (`struct_joint_strength`), which is why a glass pane leaning on a brick wall gets NO joint at all (150 < the 300 permille threshold): it is resting, not anchored, and it falls when the wall goes — exactly the behaviour a shader could never fake. (2) **A support flood** from the grounded pieces outward along joints, one level up from `bf_detect_detached`'s own question about cells: a piece that loses its last path to the ground is disconnected. Joints hold in BOTH directions (no height condition in the flood) because a roof is held by the pillar as much as the pillar is held by the foundation; only the load cascade follows gravity. (3) **The load cascade** (`structure_evaluate`): mass = volume × density accumulates top-down, each support hands its load equally to whatever would bear it, and each is checked against its own compression capacity (`struct_compression` kg/m² × footprint, with PARENA's 15% safety factor). A support that fails STOPS PASSING SUPPORT and the round repeats (bounded at 3), so one shot-out pillar drops the roof onto the next one rather than leaving it hanging in the air — the failure that makes a collapse read as a collapse. New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/structure_rules.prn` (generated by `scripts/gen_structure_rules.sh` into `packages/simulation/structure_rules.c`): density, tensile, compression, shear, damping, fracture kind, joint strength and the load comparison, all i32 at the boundary. New header-only `packages/simulation/structure.h` is the graph (≤512 nodes, ≤4096 joints, GL-free, no per-tick allocation); `structure_remove_node` + `structure_evaluate` is the whole "this piece is gone, what is now falling?" step. Named gaps, deliberate: no shear flow inside a piece, no bending/buckling SHAPE (a pillar holds its column load or the node fails — it does not bow), no fatigue, no per-cell stress inside one box. One real fix the test forced: `struct_holds_load` compares `mass × 1000` against `capacity × 850` in I32, so an unclamped 20×20×0.6 m concrete slab's mass (576 t) overflowed the capacity side into a UB-garbage answer; both operands are now clamped to a 2,000 t ceiling (documented, and far above any level box) which keeps a real overload a real failure. Verified: `make test-structure` (`-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, ASan+UBSan, no GL, no display) — PARENA totality, the reference frame's 4 anchors + 4 pegs, "one pillar gone and the roof still stands", "the last support gone and it does not", the glass-rests-on-brick case asserting zero joints and no support, a beam left unsupported when its post is demolished, the cascade (576,000 kg slab on a 126,000 kg wood pillar → pillar fails carrying 576,864 kg, 2 pieces unsupported), and bit-identical determinism. NOT verified / not yet wired: nothing calls this from `brick_world.h` yet — the graph is built and proven headless, and the hookup (a `bf_detect_detached`-flagged piece removing its node and re-evaluating) is the next slice; the live look, obviously, is unseen.

{

  "instructions": "Add the immediate-mode GL draw path for the native stadium mesh.",
  "content": "/* br_stadium_gl.h -- draws the native Bedrock Racers stadium in SHANKPIT's immediate-mode GL.\n *\n * The mesh comes from br_stadium.h (built once at load from PARENA's shape), so the renderer holds no\n * geometry of its own and cannot drift from the SDF the physics runs on. Normals are carried per\n * vertex from the same surface, which is what makes fixed-function lighting and the fog wash run\n * smoothly across the floor-to-wall curl instead of showing a facet seam.\n *\n * Deliberately no textures, no GLSL, no VBO: this is the same path every other world box in the\n * lobby draws through, so the stadium costs the pipeline nothing new.\n *\n * Include AFTER the file that includes <GL/gl.h> (apps/lobby/src/main.c does); no GL header is\n * included here so the headless test can link its own stubs.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_GL_H\n#define SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_GL_H\n\n#include \"br_stadium.h\"\n\n/* One tint per surface band, keyed off the normal: the flat track reads light, the walls darken as\n * they curl over, the ceiling is a shadowed lid. Brightness rather than hue, so the stadium sits in\n * whatever palette the level and the weather matrix are already using. */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_shade(const float n[3], float tint) {\n    float shade = 0.46f + 0.34f * (n[1] > 0.0f ? n[1] : 0.0f);\n    if (shade > 1.0f) shade = 1.0f;\n    glColor3f(0.62f * shade * tint, 0.64f * shade * tint, 0.66f * shade * tint);\n}\n\n/* br_stadium_gl_draw -- the whole shell. Call inside whatever transform the world boxes use. */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_gl_draw(const BrStadiumMesh *m, float tint) {\n    if (!m) return;\n    glBegin(GL_QUADS);\n    for (int i = 0; i < m->count; i++) {\n        const BrStadiumQuad *q = &m->q[i];\n        for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {\n            br_stadium_shade(q->v[k].n, tint);\n            glNormal3fv(q->v[k].n);\n            glVertex3fv(q->v[k].p);\n        }\n    }\n    glEnd();\n}\n\n/* The edge frame, cheap: eight corner posts and the four ridges along the track. Enough to read the\n * bowl's volume at distance without drawing the shell twice. */\nstatic inline void br_stadium_gl_draw_guides(float tint) {\n    float H[3], C[3];\n    br_stadium_dims(H, C);\n    glBegin(GL_LINES);\n    glColor3f(0.36f * tint, 0.42f * tint, 0.50f * tint);\n    for (int sx = -1; sx <= 1; sx += 2) {\n        for (int sz = -1; sz <= 1; sz += 2) {\n            glVertex3f((float)sx * H[0], C[1] + H[1] + stadium_radius(), (float)sz * H[2]);\n            glVertex3f((float)sx * H[0], C[1] - H[1] - stadium_radius(), (float)sz * H[2]);\n        }\n    }\n    for (int sz = -1; sz <= 1; sz += 2) {\n        glVertex3f(-H[0], C[1] - H[1] - stadium_radius(), (float)sz * H[2]);\n        glVertex3f(H[0], C[1] - H[1] - stadium_radius(), (float)sz * H[2]);\n    }\n    for (int sx = -1; sx <= 1; sx += 2) {\n        glVertex3f((float)sx * H[0], C[1] - H[1] - stadium_radius(), -H[2]);\n        glVertex3f((float)sx * H[0], C[1] - H[1] - stadium_radius(), H[2]);\n    }\n    glEnd();\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_BR_STADIUM_GL_H */\n"
}
