New `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/anim_rules.prn` (generated to `packages/simulation/anim_rules.c` by `scripts/gen_anim_rules.sh` / `make regen-anim-rules`) is the decision, in a priority order the spec leaves out and a player notices immediately: **melee swing > ability > fire > reload > airborne (jump-start for its own 6-tick window, then in-air, plus the reserved climb state) > crouch/slide > walk/run/idle by speed band**. It also owns the metadata a state machine needs and a spec dump usually forgets: which states loop (exactly the six postures — a looping reload is the classic bug), that **only the recoil is upper-body additive** so a player can shoot while running, a per-state crossfade (60 ms for a shot, 150 for a posture), the walk/run bands, the melee windows (**20 knife / 28 katana / 42 hammer**, matching `protocol.h`'s own weapon table so the clip window and the damage window are one number), and the eye height. New `packages/simulation/anim_state.h` is the host: it reads only real `PlayerState` fields (`on_ground`, `crouching`, `vx/vz`, `jump_timer`, `is_shooting`, `reload_timer`, `katana_slash_timer`, `dash_timer`), maps `WPN_*` to the three melee classes, and publishes the **clip-name contract** (`anim_idle` … `anim_climb_loop`, thirteen unique lowercase stems that become `<asset>/<name>.gband`) so an importer renames its Mixamo clips or fails at load instead of silently playing the idle for everything. Two honest corrections to the spec, named rather than copied: its crouch eye heights (4.0 → 2.5) are from a different build — this engine's is `EYE_HEIGHT` 2.59, and the test **asserts the rule equals that constant** (via a one-function probe TU, `anim_engine_constant.c`, because `physics.h` carries unused statics that would trip this repo's `-Werror`) — and its `ANIM_SLIDE` has **no real producer here**: this engine's crouch-slide is a friction change and the wall ride is ctrl-in-air, neither sets a timer, so `slide_ticks` is an explicit caller argument rather than an invented field. Also `make check-windows` (98 lobby sources compile for mingw) and `make -B server`. Done. The audit changed the answer, so here's what was actually built.

## What the spec asked for vs. what existed

| Spec section | Reality before this |
|---|---|
| §4 XPBD ragdoll | **Already built and wired** — `ragdoll_pool.h` runs 17 Winter/Dempster segments on GOLDENBAND's `grb`, PARENA timings per death kind, and `main.c` spawns/steps/evicts/skins them on death |
| §2 the thirteen-clip animation set | **Nothing.** The player body is drawn procedurally (`compute_player_anim_pose`); NPC kits only know AUTO/GREET/DANCE |
| §3 Mixamo→GBAND import | **Nothing.** No naming contract, so an importer had nothing to conform to and no way to fail loudly |

So I built §2 and the contract half of §3, not a second ragdoll.

## What's new

- `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/anim_rules.prn` → `packages/simulation/anim_rules.c` (`make regen-anim-rules`) — the decision, with the priority order the spec omits: **melee > ability > fire > reload > airborne (jump-start for its own window, then in-air, plus reserved climb) > crouch/slide > walk/run/idle**. It also owns what state machines actually break on: exactly six postures loop, **only the recoil is additive** (shoot while running), per-state crossfade, speed bands, melee windows **20/28/42** matching `protocol.h`'s own weapon table, and eye height.
- `packages/simulation/anim_state.h` — reads only real `PlayerState` fields, maps `WPN_*` to three melee classes, publishes the thirteen-name clip contract (`anim_idle` … `anim_climb_loop`) so a Mixamo import renames to it or fails at load rather than silently idling.
- `mk/anim_rules.mk`, `scripts/gen_anim_rules.sh`, `anim_engine_constant.c`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Two honest corrections to the pasted spec
1. Its crouch eye heights (4.0 → 2.5) are from another build. This engine is `EYE_HEIGHT` 2.59, and the test **asserts the rule equals that constant** — so camera and pose can't drift apart silently.
2. Its `ANIM_SLIDE` **has no producer here**: the crouch-slide is a friction change, the wall ride is ctrl-in-air, neither sets a timer. `slide_ticks` is an explicit caller argument instead of an invented field.

## Checks actually run
`make test-anim-state` — **90/90**: band edges exact (59 idle / 60 walk / 299 walk / 300 run), backwards is RUN not IDLE, jump-start ends at its window, walk-off falls straight to IN_AIR, a swing outranks fire+reload, firing survives being airborne, six postures loop and seven actions don't, knife/katana/hammer windows match real weapon ids while a rifle has none, and the wrapper drives IDLE/RUN/CROUCH/FIRE/RELOAD/MELEE/JUMP from the real struct. Also `make check-windows` (98 sources) and `make -B server`.

Two of those checks failed first and both were **my wrong expectations, not the rules** — speed 100 correctly reads WALK, and this set is 6 loopers vs 7 one-shots; I corrected the assertions and stated the real counts.

## Not done
Nothing is drawn from this: no kit has the thirteen clips on disk, the loader still takes four clip names, the player path is still procedural, and `anim_state.h` isn't in `main.c` yet (so the mingw check proves `anim_rules.c`, not the header, on Windows). There's also no Mixamo importer in this repo — the contract is import-*into*, not a converter.

      /* wall_ride_test.c -- crouch-slide wall ride (airborne + ctrl held + against a wall magnets you to it,
         keeps momentum, lets go when ctrl is released / speed bleeds off). make test-wall-ride */
      #include "physics.h"
      #include <stdio.h>
      
      PlayerState *get_best_bot(void) { return NULL; }
      void evolve_bot(PlayerState *a, PlayerState *b) { (void)a; (void)b; }
      static int g_fail = 0;
      #define CHECK(c) do { if (!(c)) { printf("FAIL %s:%d  %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); g_fail++; } } while (0)
      
      static PlayerState mk(float x, float y, float z, float vz, int crouch) {
          PlayerState p; memset(&p, 0, sizeof p);
          p.active = 1; p.x = x; p.y = y; p.z = z; p.vz = vz; p.crouching = crouch;
          return p;
      }
      
      int main(void) {
          phys_set_scene(SCENE_CITY);
          static Box geo[3];
          geo[1] = (Box){5000, 10, 0, 1, 20, 400};   /* long wall, x face at 5000.5, running along z */
          map_geo = geo; map_count = 2;
      
          float x_touch = 5000.5f + PLAYER_WIDTH + 0.05f;  /* just off the +x face */
          float nx, nz;
      
          PlayerState p = mk(x_touch, 8, 0, -0.9f, 1);
          CHECK(phys_wall_ride_probe(&p, &nx, &nz) && nx > 0.9f && fabsf(nz) < 0.01f);
          CHECK(phys_wall_ride_tick(&p) == 1);
          CHECK(p.vy == 0.0f);                              /* gravity cancelled */
          CHECK(p.vz < -0.85f);                             /* momentum kept (only the 1% slide drag) */
      
          /* controls: each of these must NOT ride, i.e. existing physics is untouched */
          p = mk(x_touch, 8, 0, -0.9f, 0); CHECK(phys_wall_ride_tick(&p) == 0);  /* ctrl not held */
          p = mk(x_touch, 8, 0, -0.9f, 1); p.on_ground = 1; CHECK(phys_wall_ride_tick(&p) == 0); /* grounded */
          p = mk(x_touch, 8, 0, -0.1f, 1); CHECK(phys_wall_ride_tick(&p) == 0);  /* no momentum */
          p = mk(5010, 8, 0, -0.9f, 1);    CHECK(phys_wall_ride_tick(&p) == 0);  /* no wall near */
          p = mk(x_touch, 30, 0, -0.9f, 1);CHECK(phys_wall_ride_tick(&p) == 0);  /* above the wall */
      
          /* full multi-tick ride incl. real collision: stays attached ~60 ticks, then bleeds off and falls */
          p = mk(x_touch, 8, 0, -0.9f, 1);
          p.vx = 0.4f;                                      /* flying into the wall: velocity into it is cancelled */
          int ridden = 0, first_fall = -1;
          float x_min = 1e9f;
          for (int t = 0; t < 300; t++) {
              int r = phys_wall_ride_tick(&p);
              if (r) ridden++; else { if (first_fall < 0) first_fall = t; p.vy -= GRAVITY_DROP; }
              p.y += p.vy;
              resolve_collision(&p);
              p.x += p.vx; p.z += p.vz;
              if (p.x < x_min) x_min = p.x;
              if (p.y < 0.5f) break;
          }
          printf("ridden %d ticks, first fall tick %d, z %.1f, y %.2f\n", ridden, first_fall, p.z, p.y);
          CHECK(ridden >= 60);                              /* real, sustained ride */
          CHECK(first_fall > 60);                           /* ...that only ends once momentum bleeds off */
          CHECK(x_min > 5000.5f + PLAYER_WIDTH - 0.1f);     /* never clipped into the wall (<= one pull step of overshoot, same as any wall contact) */
          CHECK(p.z < -50.0f);                              /* actually travelled along it */
          return g_fail;
      }

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/slide_rules.prn",
  "instructions": "Add the slide-on-slope rules module to PARENA.",
  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/slide_rules.prn -- a crouch-slide on a hillside speeds you up, like a board.\n;;\n;; Founder, on the Skate spec paste: \"can we also make it so doing a slide after a slide jump in\n;; normal shankpit physics where there is a terrain like in voxworld map the slide should use the same\n;; kind of physics as the skateboarding where sliding down a hill accelerates you or whatever\".\n;;\n;; What this replaces: the engine already had a slide -- apply_friction (physics.h) drops the drag from\n;; FRICTION to SLIDE_FRICTION when you are crouching above 0.75 units/tick -- but it treated a 40\n;; degree hillside exactly like a flat car park, because nothing ever read the terrain NORMAL. So a\n;; slide could only ever slow you down. These rules turn the surface's own tilt into acceleration\n;; along the downhill direction, and lighten the slide drag on a slope so the two do not cancel:\n;;\n;;   ny 990..1000  flat       no acceleration at all -- existing behaviour, bit for bit\n;;   ny 707        ~45 deg    steep 879 permille\n;;   ny 667        ~48 deg    steep ~1000 (saturates: past this a hill is a wall)\n;;\n;; Everything is permille of a base per-tick acceleration chosen by the host, plus a permille of the\n;; existing SLIDE_FRICTION drag to KEEP -- flat keeps 1000, i.e. exactly today's slide. All I32, total,\n;; no state; retune here and `make regen-slide-rules`.\n(module shankpit/slide-rules)\n(export slide-slope-flat-threshold-permille slide-slope-steep-permille\n        slide-slope-align-permille slide-slope-accel-permille\n        slide-slope-scrub-permille slide-slope-speed-cap-milli)\n\n;; Above this normal.y the surface is flat for our purposes (990 = under 8 degrees). Deliberately not\n;; 1000: a perfectly level heightfield still has float noise in its sampled normal, and a slide that\n;; crept downhill on flat ground would be a physics bug a player would find immediately.\n(defn slide-slope-flat-threshold-permille [] : I32 990)\n\n(defn s-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32\n  (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n(defn s-abs [(n : I32)] : I32 (if (< n 0) (- 0 n) n))\n\n;; How steep is this face, 0..1000. Three times the tilt so a moderate hill already carries real\n;; speed; saturates at ~48 degrees, past which a heightfield is not rideable anyway.\n(defn slide-slope-steep-permille [(normal_y_permille : I32)] : I32\n  (s-clamp 0 1000 (* (- 1000 (s-clamp 0 1000 normal_y_permille)) 3)))\n\n;; How much the board/body is pointed downhill, 0..1000. The host does the dot product (it has the\n;; velocity vector) and passes 0..1000 here; 0 means across the hill or straight up it, which earns no\n;; help -- gravity does not push you sideways.\n(defn slide-slope-align-permille [(downhill_dot_permille : I32)] : I32\n  (s-clamp 0 1000 downhill_dot_permille))\n\n;; The acceleration, permille of the host's base per-tick acceleration.\n;;   steep x align decides the hill's contribution\n;;   (cap - speed) / cap decides how much room is left before terminal: a slide cannot accelerate\n;;   forever, and it eases off rather than clipping hard\n(defn slide-slope-accel-permille\n  [(normal_y_permille : I32) (downhill_dot_permille : I32) (speed_milli : I32)] : I32\n  (if (>= (s-clamp 0 1000 normal_y_permille) (slide-slope-flat-threshold-permille))\n    0\n    (s-clamp 0 1000\n      (/ (* (* (slide-slope-steep-permille normal_y_permille)\n               (slide-slope-align-permille downhill_dot_permille))\n            (s-clamp 0 (slide-slope-speed-cap-milli) (- (slide-slope-speed-cap-milli) (s-clamp 0 (slide-slope-speed-cap-milli) speed_milli))))\n         (* 1000 (slide-slope-speed-cap-milli))))))\n\n;; The share of the existing slide drag to KEEP, permille. Flat keeps all of it (1000 = unchanged), a\n;; full-steep hill keeps 300 -- otherwise the 1% slide scrub would eat the slope's contribution and a\n;; downhill slide would still grind to a halt, which is exactly the complaint this fixes.\n(defn slide-slope-scrub-permille [(normal_y_permille : I32)] : I32\n  (s-clamp 300 1000\n    (- 1000 (/ (* (slide-slope-steep-permille normal_y_permille) 700) 1000))))\n\n;; Units/tick x 1000. Above MAX_SPEED (950) on purpose: a hill is the one way to outrun a sprint.\n(defn slide-slope-speed-cap-milli [] : I32 1200)\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/slide_rules.h",
  "instructions": "Add the slide rules host header with C defaults.",
  "content": "#ifndef SHANKPIT_SLIDE_RULES_H\n#define SHANKPIT_SLIDE_RULES_H\n\n/* slide_rules.h -- the slope half of the crouch-slide, with built-in defaults.\n *\n * The numbers live in PARENA (PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/slide_rules.prn, generated into slide_rules.c by\n * `make regen-slide-rules` and installed through slide_rules_host.h). This header carries the same\n * math as plain C defaults so that physics.h keeps working in every binary and test that includes it\n * without linking a generated file -- the same arrangement drone_flight.h and vehicle_burn.h already\n * use, and the test asserts the two agree field by field.\n *\n * A host that wants PARENA's numbers calls slide_rules_install() once at startup (apps/lobby and\n * apps/server do). The defaults and the module are kept numerically identical on purpose: a slide\n * must feel the same in a test, a server tick and a client tick.\n */\n#include <stddef.h>\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int (*steep_permille)(int normal_y_permille);\n    int (*align_permille)(int downhill_dot_permille);\n    int (*accel_permille)(int normal_y_permille, int downhill_dot_permille, int speed_milli);\n    int (*scrub_permille)(int normal_y_permille);\n    int (*speed_cap_milli)(void);\n} SlideRules;\n\nstatic inline int slide_c_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }\n\nstatic inline int slide_c_steep(int ny) { return slide_c_clamp(0, 1000, (1000 - slide_c_clamp(0, 1000, ny)) * 3); }\n\nstatic inline int slide_c_align(int dot) { return slide_c_clamp(0, 1000, dot); }\n\nstatic inline int slide_c_cap(void) { return 1200; }\n\nstatic inline int slide_c_accel(int ny, int dot, int speed) {\n    int cap = slide_c_cap();\n    if (slide_c_clamp(0, 1000, ny) >= 990) return 0;\n    return slide_c_clamp(0, 1000,\n        (slide_c_steep(ny) * slide_c_align(dot) *\n         slide_c_clamp(0, cap, cap - slide_c_clamp(0, cap, speed))) / (1000 * cap));\n}\n\nstatic inline int slide_c_scrub(int ny) {\n    return slide_c_clamp(300, 1000, 1000 - (slide_c_steep(ny) * 700) / 1000);\n}\n\nstatic SlideRules g_slide_rules = {\n    slide_c_steep, slide_c_align, slide_c_accel, slide_c_scrub, slide_c_cap\n};\n\nstatic inline void slide_set_rules(const SlideRules *r) { if (r) g_slide_rules = *r; }\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_SLIDE_RULES_H */\n"
}

      void apply_friction(PlayerState *p) {
          if (p->dash_timer > 0) return;
          float speed = sqrtf(p->vx*p->vx + p->vz*p->vz);
          if (speed < 0.001f) { p->vx = 0; p->vz = 0; return; }
          
          float drop = 0;
          if (!p->in_vehicle && p->on_ground) {
              // S478b -- ground_friction is resolve_collision's own real, per-tick resolved value
              // (the box/material actually being stood on, or the global FRICTION baseline for
              // flat-floor/terrain ground which has no material). Replaces the flat FRICTION constant
              // this used to always read directly.
              float ground_fric = p->ground_friction;
              if (p->crouching) {
                  if (speed > 0.75f) drop = speed * SLIDE_FRICTION;
                  else drop = speed * (ground_fric * 3.0f);
              } else {
                  float control = (speed < STOP_SPEED) ? STOP_SPEED : speed;
                  drop = control * ground_fric;
              }
          }
          float newspeed = speed - drop;
          if (newspeed < 0) newspeed = 0;
          newspeed /= speed;
          p->vx *= newspeed; p->vz *= newspeed;
      }

      void terrain_sample_normal(const TerrainHeightfield *t, float x, float z, float *nx, float *ny, float *nz) {
          if (nx) *nx = 0.0f;
          if (ny) *ny = 1.0f;
          if (nz) *nz = 0.0f;
          if (!t || !t->active || !t->heights) return;
      
          const float step = (t->cell_size > 0.001f) ? t->cell_size : 1.0f;
          float h_l = terrain_sample_height(t, x - step, z);
          float h_r = terrain_sample_height(t, x + step, z);
          float h_d = terrain_sample_height(t, x, z - step);
          float h_u = terrain_sample_height(t, x, z + step);
      
          float sx = h_l - h_r;
          float sy = 2.0f * step;
          float sz = h_d - h_u;
          float len = sqrtf(sx * sx + sy * sy + sz * sz);
          if (len < 0.0001f) return;
      
          if (nx) *nx = sx / len;
          if (ny) *ny = sy / len;
          if (nz) *nz = sz / len;
      }

Speed only matters here as the terminal check.\n(defn slide-slope-accel-permille\n  [(normal_y_permille : I32) (downhill_dot_permille : I32) (speed_milli : I32)] : I32\n  (if (>= (s-clamp 0 1000 normal_y_permille) (slide-slope-flat-threshold-permille))\n    0\n    (if (>= (s-clamp 0 (slide-slope-speed-cap-milli) speed_milli) (slide-slope-speed-cap-milli))\n      0\n      (s-clamp 0 1000\n        (/ (* (slide-slope-steep-permille normal_y_permille)\n              (slide-slope-align-permille downhill_dot_permille))\n           1000)))))",

p.vz = vz;\n    p.x = 0.0f; p.y = 40.0f; p.z = 0.0f;\n    return p;\n}\n\n/* one tick of the real move order for a sliding player */\nstatic void tick(PlayerState *p) {\n    apply_friction(p);\n    phys_slide_slope_tick(p);\n}\n\nstatic float speed_of(const PlayerState *p) { return sqrtf(p->vx * p->vx + p->vz * p->vz); }\n\n/* a 1:1 ramp rising along +x, so +x is UPHILL and -x is downhill */\nstatic void build_ramp(void) {\n    terrain_init(&g_scene_terrain, 64, 64, 4.0f, -128.0f, -128.0f);\n    for (int gz = 0; gz < 64; gz++)\n        for (int gx = 0; gx < 64; gx++)\n            terrain_set_height(&g_scene_terrain, gx, gz, (float)gx * 4.0f);\n}\n\nstatic void build_flat(void) {\n    terrain_clear(&g_scene_terrain, 0.0f);\n}\n\nint main(void) {\n    phys_set_scene(SCENE_VOXWORLD);\n    static Box geo[2];\n    geo[1] = (Box){0, -1, 0, 4, 2, 4};\n    map_geo = geo; t < 60; t++) { tick(&p); moved += phys_slide_slope_tick(&p); }\n        /* the old formula: drop = speed * SLIDE_FRICTION every tick */\n        float expect = start;\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) expect *= (1.0f - SLIDE_FRICTION);\n        printf(\"      flat 60 ticks: %.4f (old formula %.4f)\\n\", speed_of(&p), expect);\n        ok(fabsf(speed_of(&p) - expect) < 0.002f, \"a flat slide decays exactly as it always did\");\n        ok(moved == 0, \"and the slope step does nothing at all on flat ground\");\n        ok(speed_of(&p) < start, \"a flat slide still slows down (this is not a free speed hack)\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- downhill: faster than flat ---------------------------------------------------------- */\n    build_ramp();\n    {\n        PlayerState down = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        PlayerState flat = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        build_ramp();\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) tick(&down);\n        build_flat();\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) tick(&flat);\n        printf(\"      after 60 ticks: downhill %.4f vs flat %.4f\\n\", speed_of(&down), speed_of(&flat));\n        ok(speed_of(&down) > speed_of(&flat) + 0.15f, \"a downhill slide is much faster than a flat one\");\n        ok(speed_of(&down) > 1.0f, \"it actually outruns a sprint (MAX_SPEED is 0.95)\");\n        ok(speed_of(&down) <= 1.2f + 0.001f, \"and the speed cap holds\");\n        ok(down.vx < 0.0f, \"it accelerated along the downhill direction (-x), not a random axis\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- uphill: no help, and no scrub discount ---------------------------------------------- */\n    {\n        PlayerState up = crouched(0.9f, 0.0f);\n        PlayerState flat = crouched(0.9f, 0.0f);\n        build_ramp();\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) tick(&up);\n        build_flat();\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) tick(&flat);\n        printf(\"      after 60 ticks: uphill %.4f vs flat %.4f\\n\", speed_of(&up), speed_of(&flat));\n        ok(speed_of(&up) <= speed_of(&flat) + 0.001f, \"an uphill slide earns nothing (it cannot cheat)\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- from a standstill, and controls ----------------------------------------------------- */\n    build_ramp();\n    {\n        PlayerState p = crouched(0.0f, 0.0f);\n        for (int t = 0; t < 30; t++) tick(&p);\n        printf(\"      standing crouched on a slope for 30 ticks: %.4f\\n\", speed_of(&p));\n        ok(speed_of(&p) > 0.05f, \"crouching on a hill slides you downhill from rest\");\n\n        p = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        p.on_ground = 0;\n        ok(phys_slide_slope_tick(&p) == 0, \"in the air the slope does nothing\");\n        p = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        p.crouching = 0;\n        ok(phys_slide_slope_tick(&p) == 0, \"standing up cancels it\");\n        p = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        p.in_vehicle = 1;\n        ok(phys_slide_slope_tick(&p) == 0, \"a vehicle is not a slide\");\n\n        /* flat ground with crouch held: the step must never fire */\n        build_flat();\n        p = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        ok(phys_slide_slope_tick(&p) == 0, \"flat ground never fires the slope step\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- cap, both directions --------------------------------------------------------------- */\n    build_ramp();\n    {\n        PlayerState p = crouched(-1.19f, 0.0f);\n        for (int t = 0; t < 120; t++) tick(&p);\n        printf(\"      cap test: %.4f (cap %.2f)\\n\", speed_of(&p), (double)(slide_slope_speed_cap_milli() / 1000.0));\n        ok(speed_of(&p) <= 1.2f + 0.001f, \"long downhill never exceeds the cap\");\n        ok(speed_of(&p) > 1.19f, \"...but it does stay pinned at it\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- the compiled defaults are PARENA's numbers ------------------------------------------ */\n    {\n        SlideRules defaults = g_slide_rules;\n        int mismatches = 0, samples = 0;\n        slide_rules_install();\n        for (int ny = 0; ny <= 1000; ny += 25) {\n            if (defaults.steep_permille(ny) != slide_slope_steep_permille(ny)) mismatches++;\n            if (defaults.scrub_permille(ny) != slide_slope_scrub_permille(ny)) mismatches++;\n            for (int dot = 0; dot <= 1000; dot += 100) {\n                for (int sp = 0; sp <= 1400; sp += 200) {\n                    samples++;\n                    if (defaults.accel_permille(ny, dot, sp) !=\n                        slide_slope_accel_permille(ny, dot, sp)) mismatches++;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        printf(\"      PARENA vs compiled-in defaults: %d samples, %d mismatches\\n\", samples, mismatches);\n        ok(mismatches == 0, \"the module and the header defaults are the same curve\");\n        ok(defaults.speed_cap_milli() == slide_slope_speed_cap_milli(), \"and the same cap\");\n        ok(slide_slope_flat_threshold_permille() == 990, \"the flat threshold is the one physics.h uses\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- and the installed curve still behaves ----------------------------------------------- */\n    build_ramp();\n    {\n        PlayerState p = crouched(-0.9f, 0.0f);\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) tick(&p);\n        printf(\"      PARENA-installed downhill: %.4f\\n\", speed_of(&p));\n        ok(speed_of(&p) > 1.0f, \"the generated curve accelerates a downhill slide just the same\");\n    }\n\n    printf(\"\\n%d checks, %d failed\\n\", g_checks, g_fail);\n    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;\n}\n"

> _Reasoning_
> Failures analysis:
> 
> 1. "downhill points -x": dx = 1.00, i.e. downhill is +x. Because normal sx = h_l - h_r; h rises with +x so h_l < h_r → sx < 0 → nx < 0 → downhill = -nx/dl = +. Wait nx = sx/len; sx = h_l - h_r = negative → nx negative → -nx positive → downhill +x. Hmm: physically, a surface rising toward +x has a normal tilting toward -x (nx<0), and downhill is -x. Gradient of height is +x direction, so -gradient = -x. But their normal is (h_l - h_r, 2*step, ...) — that's actually (-dh/dx*2step...). h_l - h_r = -(h_r - h_l) = -2*step*dh/dx → nx = -dh/dx/len. So normal = (-dh/dx, 1, -dh/dz) normalized. Then downhill = -nx = +dh/dx → points UPHILL. So terrain_sample_normal returns the negative of the usual normal? For a ramp rising in +x, true normal is (-dh/dx,1,0) normalized — that matches nx<0. And downhill direction = -(nx,nz) = (+dh/dx, ...) = uphill. So my formula for downhill is wrong: downhill = (nx, nz) normalized? No: if normal is (-g,1) with g=dh/dx>0, then downhill = -gradient = (-g)... wait gradient g = dh/dx > 0 means height increases with +x, so downhill = -x. Downhill unit vector = -gradient/|gradient| = (-1,0). From normal (-g, 1)/len: (nx, nz)*... nx = -g/len → nx/dl = (-g)/(g) = -1 → downhill = (nx, nz)/dl = (-1, 0). So downhill = +normal horizontal part, NOT negative.
> 
> So fix: `*out_downhill_x = nx / dl; *out_downhill_z = nz / dl;`
> 
> That explains the flat 60-tick result: vx=-0.9 moving -x = downhill, but accel was applied at +x with align negative → no accel and... 0.0000 speed? Because on flat terrain the slide decayed to ~0.49 expected but got 0.0? Ah, the flat case: `crouched(-0.9f, 0)` then 60 ticks with `tick()` which calls apply_friction AND phys_slide_slope_tick, plus inside the loop I also add `moved += phys_slide_slope_tick(&p)` — double-calling the slope tick, harmless on flat. But speed 0.0000 means friction killed it: apply_friction on flat: drop = speed*SLIDE_FRICTION = 0.009 → each tick multiply by 0.99 → 0.49 after 60. Got 0. Sub-0.75 speed: once speed < 0.75, the crouch branch uses `drop = speed * (ground_fric*3)` = speed*0.9 → decays fast. So the old formula assumption of 1% for all 60 ticks is wrong: it crosses 0.75 quickly (after ~18 ticks) then decays at 90%/tick → ~0. So my "old formula" expectation was wrong; the real old behavior is what we should assert. Both flat got 0.0000 — so flat is consistent; my expected computation was wrong. Fix test: compare flat slide against a reference computed by applying the OLD rule in the test (replicating the same branch: if speed>0.75 → *0.99 else *(1-0.9)) — that's just re-implementing. Simpler and more meaningful: assert flat slide decays to ~0 within 60 ticks and no slope acceleration fires; and separately assert a single tick at 0.9 on flat drops exactly 1% (bit-identical to old behavior for that tick).

Done — the slide-on-terrain piece you actually asked for, wired and tested. The rest of that paste (dual-stick flicks, third-person orbit, grind snapping, manuals, the F5 wireframe) is **not** in this change.

## What changed

The engine already had a slide (`apply_friction` drops to `SLIDE_FRICTION` above 0.75 units/tick while crouched) but it treated a 45° hillside exactly like a flat car park, because **nothing read the terrain normal** — a slide could only ever slow you down.

- `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/slide_rules.prn` → `packages/simulation/slide_rules.c` (`make regen-slide-rules`): steepness as `(1000 − normal.y) × 3`, downhill alignment, acceleration **constant in speed like gravity**, how much of the slide *drag* a slope keeps (1000 on the flat = unchanged, 300 at full steep — otherwise the 1% scrub cancels the hill), cap 1.20 units/tick (above `MAX_SPEED` 0.95 on purpose).
- `slide_rules.h` (numerically identical compiled-in defaults, so every existing test that includes `physics.h` still links) + `slide_rules_host.h` (installs PARENA's copy in the lobby).
- `physics.h`: `phys_slide_slope_tick` — gravity along the surface gradient, vector-clamped to the cap — called once per tick from `local_game.h` after `apply_friction`.

## Two real bugs the test caught (both mine)
1. `terrain_sample_normal` **points against the gradient**, so my "downhill" was upside-down: a slide accelerated *uphill*. Fixed the sign, with the convention documented at the call.
2. The sub-0.75 crouch-walk scrub (90%/tick) pinned a slide that started from rest at a 0.008 crawl. A downhill heading now uses the slide branch at any speed.

## What the checks showed
- `make test-slide-slope` — **24/24**: one tick of a flat slide is exactly the old formula (1e-5), the slope step never fires on flat ground, a flat slide still comes to rest; **downhill 1.09 after 60 ticks vs 0.00 flat**, pinned at exactly 1.20 after 120; starts from rest on a hill; uphill never gains speed, stalls, and is turned back downhill; airborne/standing/vehicle no-op; PARENA curve == defaults across 3,608 samples.
- `make test-wall-ride` (110-tick ride, unchanged), `make check-windows` (99 lobby sources compile for mingw), `make -B server`.

## Not done, named
- **Terrain only** — an authored box ramp has a per-box face normal, not a field under the player, so slides on those get nothing yet.
- The **server installs no PARENA copy**; its compiled-in defaults are the same numbers and the test enforces that equality, but a future retune would reach the lobby first.
- Everything else in the Skate spec — gesture recognition, 3P skate camera, grind/ledge snapping, manuals, the debug visualizer.

      #ifndef MATERIAL_SHADERS_H
      #define MATERIAL_SHADERS_H
      
      // material_shaders.h -- SHANKPIT's real, native, compiled-in material shader registry (S459-16,
      // founder real-time: "im sure somehow this is going to need to play with shaders too so build
      // that in from day 1 ... we are trying to actually make this look like a real game" / "build the
      // shaders in to the native and then refer to the shaders from NOCK directly? a shader registry
      // too but for now it will just be like the ffi names or whatever not the real shader code" /
      // "vs0 are any correct real shaders" / "build it in we dont have endless iterations").
      //
      // The real, load-bearing split this header exists to enforce: IDUNA/NOCK's own shankpit_materials
      // table stores a material's own ShaderName (a plain string, e.g. "standard") -- NEVER GLSL
      // source. This header is the one real place that name resolves to actual shader code. Adding a
      // new named shader (VS1's own real, deferred "flourescent light" emissive material, founder:
      // "if we could make a material and quickly turn it into a flourescent light that would be
      // amazing... think of that as vs1") means adding a new SHADER_* constant + program here, and a
      // matching new row in IDUNA's own real shader-name validation (internal/shankpit/
      // material_store.go's own validShaderNames) -- NOT a schema change, NOT a NOCK code-editor field.
      //
      // SHADER_STANDARD (VS0, this pass's own real, complete, working shader): a real Blinn-Phong
      // specular-highlight pass, additively blended on TOP of each box's own existing per-vertex CPU-
      // computed lighting (apps/lobby's own retro_eval_brush_lighting_rgb pipeline, completely
      // untouched) rather than replacing it -- same real "additive overlay, not a full lighting
      // rewrite" technique weapon 7's own draw_flashlight_beam already proved safe and cheap. A
      // material with near-zero specular (brick/concrete/wood) costs nothing extra: draw_material_
      // specular_box's own caller skips the draw call entirely below MATERIAL_SPECULAR_DRAW_THRESHOLD.
      //
      // Same real gl_shader.c/DynamicVBO foundation gband_draw_skinned (S144-02) and weapon 7's own
      // draw_flashlight_beam (S459-14) already proved -- genuinely reused, not reinvented a third time.
      
      #include "gl_shader.h"
      #include "sky_weather.h" /* SKYW_GLSL_FOG: highlights fade into weather fog with the surface under them */
      #include <math.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      #define SHADER_STANDARD "standard"
      #define MATERIAL_SPECULAR_DRAW_THRESHOLD 0.12f /* below this, the highlight is visually
          negligible -- brick(0.04)/concrete(0.03)/wood(0.06) all skip the draw call entirely;
          metal(0.85) always draws */
      
      static GLuint g_material_shader_program = 0;
      static DynamicVBO g_material_shader_vbo;
      static int g_material_shader_ready = 0;
      
      static const char *g_material_shader_vs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "attribute vec3 a_pos;\n"
          "attribute vec3 a_normal;\n"
          "uniform mat4 u_mvp;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_normal;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_world_pos;\n"
          "void main() {\n"
          "    v_normal = a_normal;\n"
          "    v_world_pos = a_pos;\n"
          "    gl_Position = u_mvp * vec4(a_pos, 1.0);\n"
          "}\n";
      
      // Real Blinn-Phong specular term ONLY (no ambient/diffuse -- those are already baked into the
      // box's own real, existing CPU-lit color this pass draws additively on top of). u_light_dir
      // points FROM the surface TOWARD the light (already normalized by the caller, taken from
      // RetroLightingState's own real sun_dir/moon_dir depending on day/night -- the exact same
      // dominant light direction every other box already shades against, so the highlight lands on the
      // correct side of a box, not an arbitrary fixed direction).
      static const char *g_material_shader_fs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_light_dir;\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_cam_pos;\n"
          "uniform float u_specular;\n"
          "uniform float u_shininess;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_normal;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_world_pos;\n"
          SKYW_GLSL_FOG
          "void main() {\n"
          "    vec3 n = normalize(v_normal);\n"
          "    vec3 v = normalize(u_cam_pos - v_world_pos);\n"
          "    vec3 l = normalize(u_light_dir);\n"
          "    vec3 h = normalize(l + v);\n"
          "    float spec = pow(max(dot(n, h), 0.0), u_shininess) * u_specular;\n"
          "    gl_FragColor = vec4(1.0, 0.97, 0.9, spec * skyw_fog());\n"
          "}\n";
      
      static inline void material_shader_init(void) {
          if (!gl_shader_load_extensions()) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: GL extension loading failed -- specular pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          GLuint vs = gl_compile_shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, g_material_shader_vs_src);
          GLuint fs = gl_compile_shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, g_material_shader_fs_src);
          g_material_shader_program = gl_link_program(vs, fs);
          if (!g_material_shader_program) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: shader link failed -- specular pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          if (!gl_dynamic_vbo_init(&g_material_shader_vbo, 48)) { /* one box = 6 faces * 6 verts (2 tris) = 36 */
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: dynamic VBO init failed -- specular pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          g_material_shader_ready = 1;
          SDL_Log("material_shaders: SHADER_STANDARD (Blinn-Phong specular) ready");
      }
      
      // draw_material_specular_box draws one box's own real specular highlight, additively, on top of
      // whatever's already been rendered there this frame (the caller draws the base lit+textured box
      // FIRST, then this). x/y/z/w/h/d match physics.h's own real Box convention (center + full
      // extents). mvp is camera-only (model is identity, the 36 verts below are already world-space --
      // same "bake the transform into the verts" contract draw_flashlight_beam established).
      static inline void draw_material_specular_box(float x, float y, float z, float w, float h, float d,
                                                      float specular, float shininess,
                                                      const float *mvp16, const float *light_dir,
                                                      const float *cam_pos) {
          if (!g_material_shader_ready) return;
          if (specular < MATERIAL_SPECULAR_DRAW_THRESHOLD) return;
      
          float hw = w * 0.5f, hh = h * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;
          // 6 faces, 2 triangles each, real per-face outward normals -- CCW winding matching every
          // other box-drawing call site's own existing GL_QUADS winding in this file (top/bottom/front/
          // back/left/right, same face order as draw_map's own textured box for easy visual comparison).
          float verts[36 * 6];
          int vi = 0;
      #define V(px, py, pz, nx, ny, nz) \
          verts[vi++] = x + (px); verts[vi++] = y + (py); verts[vi++] = z + (pz); \
          verts[vi++] = (nx); verts[vi++] = (ny); verts[vi++] = (nz);
          /* top (+y) */
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          /* bottom (-y) */
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          /* front (+z) */
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          /* back (-z) */
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          /* left (-x) */
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0)
          /* right (+x) */
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 1, 0, 0)
      #undef V
      
          glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
          glEnable(GL_BLEND);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
          gl_use_program(g_material_shader_program);
          gl_uniform_matrix4fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_material_shader_program, "u_mvp"), mvp16);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_material_shader_program, "u_light_dir"), light_dir);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_material_shader_program, "u_cam_pos"), cam_pos);
          gl_uniform1f(gl_get_uniform_location(g_material_shader_program, "u_specular"), specular);
          gl_uniform1f(gl_get_uniform_location(g_material_shader_program, "u_shininess"), shininess);
          gl_dynamic_vbo_draw(&g_material_shader_vbo, verts, 36, GL_TRIANGLES);
          gl_use_program(0);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
          glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
      }
      
      // SHADER_IPS_LIGHT (founder real-time, 2026-09-14: "can we design a material for an IPS light its
      // going to need a special shader build it in") -- a real, unlit EMISSIVE pass, genuinely
      // different from SHADER_STANDARD's additive-highlight-on-top-of-lit-color treatment: a light
      // fixture shouldn't itself go dark on its unlit side the way an ordinary wall correctly does.
      // draw_map's own material pass (apps/lobby/src/main.c) forces this box's base per-face lit_r/g/b
      // to full bright BEFORE texturing for ips_light boxes (skipping the normal day/night darkening
      // entirely), and this pass then adds a real, soft, view-independent glow on top -- a cool white-
      // blue tone matching a real IPS display panel's own backlight color, with a gentle center-hotspot
      // falloff (fresnel-ish, brighter face-on than at grazing angles, same real "v of view dir vs
      // normal" idea the specular pass above already uses for its own highlight) so a flat panel reads
      // as glowing, not just flat-painted.
      #define SHADER_IPS_LIGHT "ips_light"
      
      static GLuint g_ips_light_shader_program = 0;
      static DynamicVBO g_ips_light_shader_vbo;
      static int g_ips_light_shader_ready = 0;
      
      static const char *g_ips_light_fs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_cam_pos;\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_glow_color;\n"
          "uniform float u_intensity;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_normal;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_world_pos;\n"
          "void main() {\n"
          "    vec3 n = normalize(v_normal);\n"
          "    vec3 v = normalize(u_cam_pos - v_world_pos);\n"
          "    float facing = max(dot(n, v), 0.0);\n"
          "    float glow = mix(0.55, 1.0, facing);\n"
          "    gl_FragColor = vec4(u_glow_color * u_intensity * glow, 1.0);\n"
          "}\n";
      
      static inline void ips_light_shader_init(void) {
          if (!gl_shader_load_extensions()) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: GL extension loading failed -- ips_light pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          GLuint vs = gl_compile_shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, g_material_shader_vs_src);
          GLuint fs = gl_compile_shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, g_ips_light_fs_src);
          g_ips_light_shader_program = gl_link_program(vs, fs);
          if (!g_ips_light_shader_program) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: ips_light shader link failed -- pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          if (!gl_dynamic_vbo_init(&g_ips_light_shader_vbo, 48)) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: ips_light VBO init failed -- pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          g_ips_light_shader_ready = 1;
          SDL_Log("material_shaders: SHADER_IPS_LIGHT (emissive panel) ready");
      }
      
      // draw_material_emissive_box -- same real 36-vert box-with-outward-normals shape
      // draw_material_specular_box already builds (kept as a literal, separate copy rather than a
      // shared helper -- the two functions' own uniform sets genuinely differ, and this whole file's
      // own established pattern is one self-contained function per named shader, not a shared/branching
      // one). mvp is camera-only, same "bake the transform into the verts" contract as every other real
      // box-drawing call site in this codebase.
      static inline void draw_material_emissive_box(float x, float y, float z, float w, float h, float d,
                                                      const float *mvp16, const float *cam_pos) {
          if (!g_ips_light_shader_ready) return;
      
          float hw = w * 0.5f, hh = h * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;
          float verts[36 * 6];
          int vi = 0;
      #define V(px, py, pz, nx, ny, nz) \
          verts[vi++] = x + (px); verts[vi++] = y + (py); verts[vi++] = z + (pz); \
          verts[vi++] = (nx); verts[vi++] = (ny); verts[vi++] = (nz);
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 1, 0, 0)
      #undef V
      
          static const float glow_color[3] = {0.75f, 0.88f, 1.0f}; /* cool white-blue, real IPS-panel backlight tone */

          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
          gl_use_program(g_ips_light_shader_program);
          gl_uniform_matrix4fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_ips_light_shader_program, "u_mvp"), mvp16);

          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_ips_light_shader_program, "u_glow_color"), glow_color);
          gl_uniform1f(gl_get_uniform_location(g_ips_light_shader_program, "u_intensity"), intensity);
          gl_dynamic_vbo_draw(&g_ips_light_shader_vbo, verts, 36, GL_TRIANGLES);
          gl_use_program(0);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
          glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
      }
      
      // SHADER_HPS_LIGHT (founder real-time, 2026-09-14: "can you do it again for a high pressure
      // sodium light with a flicker like in this video" -- the referenced YouTube link couldn't
      // actually be fetched/watched from here, so this is built from well-documented real HPS
      // behavior instead: a dying/cycling HPS bulb repeatedly strikes, brightens, dims, nearly
      // extinguishes, and restrikes over a few real seconds -- a slow, semi-chaotic pulse, not a fast
      // strobe). Same real unlit-emissive treatment SHADER_IPS_LIGHT established, plus TWO real,
      // genuinely new things: a warm amber/orange sodium-vapor color (real HPS lamps emit an almost-
      // monochromatic yellow-orange, the sodium D line at ~589nm) and an animated flicker -- draw_map's
      // own per-frame hps_flicker (a sum of a few sine waves at different, non-harmonic frequencies,
      // the same real "avoid a too-regular/fake pulse" idea any real flicker effect needs) is CPU-
      // computed ONCE per frame (not per box, not per fragment) and passed in here as u_intensity,
      // exactly the same "compute once, pass as a uniform" discipline flashlight_face_boost/
      // material_light_dir already established elsewhere in this codebase -- also multiplied into the
      // box's own BASE texture tint in draw_map, so the whole fixture (texture AND glow) pulses
      // together, not just the additive overlay while the base stays static.
      #define SHADER_HPS_LIGHT "hps_light"
      
      static GLuint g_hps_light_shader_program = 0;
      static DynamicVBO g_hps_light_shader_vbo;
      static int g_hps_light_shader_ready = 0;
      
      static const char *g_hps_light_fs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_cam_pos;\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_glow_color;\n"
          "uniform float u_intensity;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_normal;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_world_pos;\n"
          "void main() {\n"
          "    vec3 n = normalize(v_normal);\n"
          "    vec3 v = normalize(u_cam_pos - v_world_pos);\n"
          "    float facing = max(dot(n, v), 0.0);\n"
          "    float glow = mix(0.5, 1.0, facing);\n"
          "    gl_FragColor = vec4(u_glow_color * u_intensity * glow, 1.0);\n"
          "}\n";
      
      static inline void hps_light_shader_init(void) {
          if (!gl_shader_load_extensions()) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: GL extension loading failed -- hps_light pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          GLuint vs = gl_compile_shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, g_material_shader_vs_src);
          GLuint fs = gl_compile_shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, g_hps_light_fs_src);
          g_hps_light_shader_program = gl_link_program(vs, fs);
          if (!g_hps_light_shader_program) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: hps_light shader link failed -- pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          if (!gl_dynamic_vbo_init(&g_hps_light_shader_vbo, 48)) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: hps_light VBO init failed -- pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          g_hps_light_shader_ready = 1;
          SDL_Log("material_shaders: SHADER_HPS_LIGHT (flickering sodium lamp) ready");
      }
      
      // draw_material_hps_box -- same real 36-vert box shape draw_material_emissive_box already
      // builds, kept as its own literal copy for the same "one self-contained function per named
      // shader" reason. flicker is the caller's own per-frame hps_flicker value in [0,1] -- this
      // function doesn't compute time/randomness itself, matching this codebase's own established
      // "CPU computes once per frame, GLSL just receives the number" discipline.
      static inline void draw_material_hps_box(float x, float y, float z, float w, float h, float d,
                                                const float *mvp16, const float *cam_pos, float flicker) {
          if (!g_hps_light_shader_ready) return;
      
          float hw = w * 0.5f, hh = h * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;
          float verts[36 * 6];
          int vi = 0;
      #define V(px, py, pz, nx, ny, nz) \
          verts[vi++] = x + (px); verts[vi++] = y + (py); verts[vi++] = z + (pz); \
          verts[vi++] = (nx); verts[vi++] = (ny); verts[vi++] = (nz);
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 1, 0, 0)
      #undef V
      
          static const float glow_color[3] = {1.0f, 0.55f, 0.10f}; /* warm sodium amber -- almost no blue, real HPS spectrum */
          const float intensity = 0.6f * flicker;
      
          glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
          glEnable(GL_BLEND);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
          gl_use_program(g_hps_light_shader_program);
          gl_uniform_matrix4fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_hps_light_shader_program, "u_mvp"), mvp16);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_hps_light_shader_program, "u_cam_pos"), cam_pos);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_hps_light_shader_program, "u_glow_color"), glow_color);
          gl_uniform1f(gl_get_uniform_location(g_hps_light_shader_program, "u_intensity"), intensity);
          gl_dynamic_vbo_draw(&g_hps_light_shader_vbo, verts, 36, GL_TRIANGLES);
          gl_use_program(0);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
          glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
      }
      
      // SHADER_GLASS (founder real-time, 2026-10-02: "add a new one for glass (add a shader with glass
      // transparency slight cyan tint - but make the tint parena programmable)"). A box whose material
      // uses this shader is NOT drawn by draw_map's opaque textured pass at all; draw_map collects those
      // boxes and draws them AFTER every opaque box, farthest first, through this pass: alpha-blended,
      // depth-write off (so glass never hides what is behind it), with a mild fresnel boost so panes
      // read brighter edge-on, plus a small specular glint from the dominant light. The RGBA tint is NOT
      // a constant here -- it comes from PARENA's on-glass-tint (stdlib/shankpit/brick_rules.prn, linked
      // in via packages/simulation/brick_mod.c, regenerated by scripts/gen_brick_mod.sh): edit four
      // numbers there and every glass box retints, no shader or host change.
      #define SHADER_GLASS "glass"
      
      int on_glass_tint(int channel); /* PARENA: 0 R, 1 G, 2 B, 3 A, each 0-255 */
      
      static GLuint g_glass_shader_program = 0;
      static DynamicVBO g_glass_shader_vbo;
      static int g_glass_shader_ready = 0;
      
      static const char *g_glass_fs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_cam_pos;\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_light_dir;\n"
          "uniform vec4 u_tint;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_normal;\n"
          "varying vec3 v_world_pos;\n"
          "void main() {\n"
          "    vec3 n = normalize(v_normal);\n"
          "    vec3 v = normalize(u_cam_pos - v_world_pos);\n"
          "    float facing = abs(dot(n, v));\n"
          "    float fresnel = pow(1.0 - facing, 3.0);\n"
          "    vec3 h = normalize(normalize(u_light_dir) + v);\n"
          "    float glint = pow(max(dot(n, h), 0.0), 96.0) * 0.6;\n"
          "    float a = clamp(u_tint.a + fresnel * 0.35 + glint, 0.0, 0.85);\n"
          "    gl_FragColor = vec4(u_tint.rgb + vec3(glint), a);\n"
          "}\n";
      
      static inline void glass_shader_init(void) {
          if (!gl_shader_load_extensions()) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: GL extension loading failed -- glass pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          GLuint vs = gl_compile_shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, g_material_shader_vs_src);
          GLuint fs = gl_compile_shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, g_glass_fs_src);
          g_glass_shader_program = gl_link_program(vs, fs);
          if (!g_glass_shader_program) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: glass shader link failed -- pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          if (!gl_dynamic_vbo_init(&g_glass_shader_vbo, 48)) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: glass VBO init failed -- pass disabled");
              return;
          }
          g_glass_shader_ready = 1;
          SDL_Log("material_shaders: SHADER_GLASS (transparent, PARENA-tinted) ready");
      }
      
      // draw_material_glass_box -- same 36-vert box-with-outward-normals shape the passes above build
      // (a deliberate per-shader copy, see draw_material_emissive_box's own note). Draws nothing and
      // returns 0 if the pass isn't ready, so the caller can fall back to the opaque path.
      static inline int draw_material_glass_box(float x, float y, float z, float w, float h, float d,
                                                const float *mvp16, const float *light_dir, const float *cam_pos) {
          if (!g_glass_shader_ready) return 0;
      
          float hw = w * 0.5f, hh = h * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;
          float verts[36 * 6];
          int vi = 0;
      #define V(px, py, pz, nx, ny, nz) \
          verts[vi++] = x + (px); verts[vi++] = y + (py); verts[vi++] = z + (pz); \
          verts[vi++] = (nx); verts[vi++] = (ny); verts[vi++] = (nz);
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 1, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, -1, 0) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, -1, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(-hw, -hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1) V(-hw, hh, hd, 0, 0, 1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(hw, -hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(-hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1) V(hw, hh, -hd, 0, 0, -1)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, -hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(-hw, -hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, hd, -1, 0, 0) V(-hw, hh, -hd, -1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, -hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0)
          V(hw, -hh, hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, -hd, 1, 0, 0) V(hw, hh, hd, 1, 0, 0)
      #undef V
      
          float tint[4] = { (float)on_glass_tint(0) / 255.0f, (float)on_glass_tint(1) / 255.0f,
                            (float)on_glass_tint(2) / 255.0f, (float)on_glass_tint(3) / 255.0f };
      
          glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
          glEnable(GL_BLEND);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
          gl_use_program(g_glass_shader_program);
          gl_uniform_matrix4fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_glass_shader_program, "u_mvp"), mvp16);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_glass_shader_program, "u_cam_pos"), cam_pos);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_glass_shader_program, "u_light_dir"), light_dir);
          gl_uniform4fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_glass_shader_program, "u_tint"), tint);
          gl_dynamic_vbo_draw(&g_glass_shader_vbo, verts, 36, GL_TRIANGLES);
          gl_use_program(0);
          glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
          return 1;
      }
      
      // draw_light_glow_billboard -- founder real-time, 2026-09-14: "ok cool but it looks like a
      // square can you do some gausian blur or something? vinyetting/ i dunno" -- the per-box wall
      // lighting fixture_light_face_contribution adds (apps/lobby/src/main.c) is real per-box FLAT
      // shading, so its own halo is necessarily blocky/square at box granularity; a true framebuffer
      // gaussian blur/bloom post-process is real, separate, much larger work (an offscreen render
      // target + a real multi-pass blur shader, nothing like this codebase's existing single-pass
      // forward-rendering pipeline). This is the real, standard, MUCH cheaper alternative every classic
      // forward-renderer uses for the same complaint: a soft, camera-facing, round glow BILLBOARD
      // (additively blended, alpha falls off radially from center) at each light fixture's own
      // position -- the same real "additive overlay on top of the existing pipeline, not a rewrite of
      // it" technique this whole file already uses throughout. Reads as a soft round glow regardless of
      // the underlying per-box wall halo's own blockiness, since the billboard is what actually draws
      // the dominant, up-close "this is a light" visual cue (same real relationship the flashlight's own
      // cone mesh + separate wall-lighting term already have).
      static GLuint g_light_glow_program = 0;
      static DynamicVBO g_light_glow_vbo;
      static int g_light_glow_ready = 0;
      
      static const char *g_light_glow_vs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "attribute vec3 a_pos;\n"
          "attribute vec3 a_normal;\n" /* .xy = local billboard UV in [-1,1], centered */
          "uniform mat4 u_mvp;\n"
          "varying vec2 v_uv;\n"
          "void main() {\n"
          "    v_uv = a_normal.xy;\n"
          "    gl_Position = u_mvp * vec4(a_pos, 1.0);\n"
          "}\n";
      
      static const char *g_light_glow_fs_src =
          "#version 120\n"
          "uniform vec3 u_color;\n"
          "uniform float u_intensity;\n"
          "varying vec2 v_uv;\n"
          "void main() {\n"
          "    float r = length(v_uv);\n"
          "    float alpha = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, r);\n"
          "    alpha = alpha * alpha;\n" /* extra softening -- a round, gently-fading glow, not a hard-edged disc */
          "    gl_FragColor = vec4(u_color * u_intensity, alpha);\n"
          "}\n";
      
      static inline void light_glow_shader_init(void) {
          if (!gl_shader_load_extensions()) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: GL extension loading failed -- light glow billboard disabled");
              return;
          }
          GLuint vs = gl_compile_shader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, g_light_glow_vs_src);
          GLuint fs = gl_compile_shader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, g_light_glow_fs_src);
          g_light_glow_program = gl_link_program(vs, fs);
          if (!g_light_glow_program) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: light glow shader link failed -- disabled");
              return;
          }
          if (!gl_dynamic_vbo_init(&g_light_glow_vbo, 6)) {
              SDL_Log("material_shaders: light glow VBO init failed -- disabled");
              return;
          }
          g_light_glow_ready = 1;
          SDL_Log("material_shaders: light glow billboard ready");
      }
      
      // cam_right/cam_up: the LOCAL VIEWER's own camera right/up vectors (derived from cam_yaw/
      // cam_pitch the same way draw_flashlight_beam derives its own right/up, just facing the real
      // current camera instead of a player's aim) -- a billboard always faces whoever is rendering,
      // unlike a world-anchored mesh, so the caller passes these in rather than this function deriving
      // its own facing from the light source (which has no "facing" of its own to derive from at all).
      static inline void draw_light_glow_billboard(float cx, float cy, float cz, float radius,
                                                    const float *color, float intensity,
                                                    const float *mvp16,
                                                    const float *cam_right, const float *cam_up) {
          if (!g_light_glow_ready) return;
          if (intensity <= 0.001f) return;
      
          float verts[GL_SHADER_VBO_FLOATS_PER_VERT * 6];
          int vi = 0;
      #define GV(u, v) \
          verts[vi++] = cx + cam_right[0] * (u) * radius + cam_up[0] * (v) * radius; \
          verts[vi++] = cy + cam_right[1] * (u) * radius + cam_up[1] * (v) * radius; \
          verts[vi++] = cz + cam_right[2] * (u) * radius + cam_up[2] * (v) * radius; \
          verts[vi++] = (u); verts[vi++] = (v); verts[vi++] = 0.0f;
          GV(-1.0f, -1.0f) GV(1.0f, -1.0f) GV(1.0f, 1.0f)
          GV(-1.0f, -1.0f) GV(1.0f, 1.0f) GV(-1.0f, 1.0f)
      #undef GV
      
          glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
          glEnable(GL_BLEND);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
          gl_use_program(g_light_glow_program);
          gl_uniform_matrix4fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_light_glow_program, "u_mvp"), mvp16);
          gl_uniform3fv(gl_get_uniform_location(g_light_glow_program, "u_color"), color);
          gl_uniform1f(gl_get_uniform_location(g_light_glow_program, "u_intensity"), intensity);
          gl_dynamic_vbo_draw(&g_light_glow_vbo, verts, 6, GL_TRIANGLES);
          gl_use_program(0);
          glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
          glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
      }
      
      #endif
      
- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit/material_rules.prn -- what a surface IS, as a total integer function of the tick.
      ;;
      ;; Founder 2026-10-31: "shankpit already has some lighting primitives like hps light and ips light
      ;; what other materials/shaders do we need for full doom/quake/half life/gta story telling?"
      ;;
      ;; The honest answer for THIS engine is not a PBR pipeline -- it is fixed-function GL 1.x with one
      ;; hand-loaded GL 2.0 shader path (gl_shader.h), and no VAO / #version 330 / 3D-texture support in
      ;; the build anywhere. So the storytelling vocabulary is authored as ANIMATION, not material science:
      ;; a material is (base look, how its UVs move, how its own light flickers, what colour the screen
      ;; goes when it hurts you). Every one of those is a pure function of the tick and a few integers, so
      ;; the server, every client and a headless test compute the same frame -- the only way a flicker can
      ;; be part of a deterministic simulation at all.
      ;;
      ;; The vocabulary Doom / Quake / Half-Life / GTA communicate fear with:
      ;;   Doom      palette-cycled hazard colours, scrolling toxic ooze, damage tints
      ;;   Quake     light styles ("aaaaaaazzzzz" strobes), the texture-warp look, dark corners
      ;;   HL        terminals as frame-loop materials, unstable fluorescents, alien flesh
      ;;   GTA       sodium streetlights over dark alleys, animated signage, flooded canals
      ;;
      ;; The renderer still has to draw it -- docs/RENDER_NORTHSTAR.md is explicit about what is wired and
      ;; what is not. Nothing here invents a texture: indices and timings only.
      
      (module shankpit/material-rules)
      (export mat-kind-count mat-scroll-speed-milli mat-scroll-u-milli mat-scroll-v-milli
              mat-frame-index mat-light-style-count light-style-level-permille mat-emissive-milli
              tint-low-health-milli tint-submerged-milli tint-acid-milli tint-shield-milli
              palette-index-256 vlm-axis-index-milli vlm-ambient-floor-milli)
      
      ;; ---- integer helpers --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn m-min [(a : I32) (b : I32)] : I32 (if (< a b) a b))
      (defn m-max [(a : I32) (b : I32)] : I32 (if (> a b) a b))
      (defn m-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32 (m-min hi (m-max lo x)))
      
      ;; Modulo that is never negative: a negative UV offset or palette index is a visible seam, and C's
      ;; truncating `/` would give one.
      (defn m-mod [(a : I32) (n : I32)] : I32
        (if (<= n 0) 0
          (let [r (- a (* (/ a n) n))]
            (if (< r 0) (+ r n) r))))
      
      ;; ---- material kinds ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; 0 plain, 1 scrolling (ooze / water / conveyor), 2 frame-loop sprite (terminals, cameras, timers),
      ;; 3 palette-LUT (indexed colour), 4 emissive flicker (a fixture's own face).
      (defn mat-kind-count [] : I32 5)
      
      ;; Scroll speed in permille of a texture per SECOND (1000 = one full tile/s). Ooze creeps, water
      ;; drifts, a conveyor is quick, a flickering sign scrolls slowly under its own glow.
      (defn mat-scroll-speed-milli [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 220 (if (= kind 3) 90 (if (= kind 4) 60 0))))
      
      ;; Offset in permille, 0..999, at a tick (60 ticks = one second).
      (defn mat-scroll-u-milli [(kind : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32
        (m-mod (/ (* (mat-scroll-speed-milli kind) (m-mod tick 60)) 60) 1000))
      
      ;; Toxic ooze also creeps sideways, slowly, which is what makes it read as thick rather than tiled.
      (defn mat-scroll-v-milli [(kind : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) (m-mod (/ (* 90 (m-mod tick 60)) 60) 1000) 0))
      
      ;; A frame-loop material's sprite index, stepped at `fps` (1..30): a terminal that blinks, a camera
      ;; that sweeps, a bomb timer that ticks -- one sheet, one offset per frame.
      (defn mat-frame-index [(fps : I32) (frames : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32
        (if (or (<= frames 0) (<= fps 0)) 0
          (m-mod (/ (* (m-mod tick 60) fps) 60) frames)))
      
      ;; ---- light styles (Quake's vocabulary, as integers) --------------------------------------------------
      ;; 0 steady, 1 strobe, 2 fluorescent (unstable), 3 broken, 4 pulse, 5 dying, 6 alarm, 7 candle.
      ;; Always 0..1000 permille of the fixture's own brightness.
      (defn mat-light-style-count [] : I32 8)
      
      (defn light-style-level-permille [(style : I32) (tick : I32)] : I32
        (let [t (m-mod tick 600)]
          (if (= style 1) (if (< (m-mod t 12) 6) 1000 0)
            (if (= style 2) (if (= (m-mod t 97) 0) 250 940)
              (if (= style 3) (if (< (m-mod (* t 37) 11) 3) 1000 180)
                (if (= style 4) (m-clamp 400 1000 (+ 400 (m-mod (* t 5) 600)))
                  (if (= style 5) (m-clamp 60 1000 (- 1000 (m-mod t 940)))
                    (if (= style 6) (if (< (m-mod t 8) 4) 1000 120)
                      (if (= style 7) (if (< (m-mod t 5) 2) 1000 (if (< (m-mod t 5) 4) 820 640))
                        1000)))))))))
      
      (defn mat-emissive-milli [(light_style : I32) (tick : I32) (room_light_milli : I32)] : I32
        (let [level (light-style-level-permille light_style tick)
              floor (if (< room_light_milli 250) 350 120)]
          (m-clamp floor 1000 level)))
      
      ;; ---- screen tints (0..1000; the renderer blends a colour quad at value/1000 alpha) ------------------
      (defn tint-low-health-milli [(hp : I32) (max_hp : I32)] : I32
        (if (<= max_hp 0) 0
          (let [pct (/ (* (m-clamp 0 max_hp hp) 1000) max_hp)]
            (if (>= pct 300) 0 (m-clamp 0 1000 (/ (* (- 300 pct) 1000) 300))))))
      
      (defn tint-submerged-milli [(depth_milli : I32)] : I32
        (m-clamp 0 1000 (/ (* (m-clamp 0 4000 depth_milli) 1000) 4000)))
      
      (defn tint-acid-milli [(acid_permille : I32)] : I32
        (/ (* (m-clamp 0 1000 acid_permille) 900) 1000))
      
      (defn tint-shield-milli [(shield : I32) (max_shield : I32)] : I32
        (if (<= max_shield 0) 0 (/ (* (m-clamp 0 max_shield shield) 700) max_shield)))
      
      ;; ---- palette LUT (Doom's 256-entry trick) -----------------------------------------------------------
      ;; A cycling palette runs past 255 and comes back round instead of wrapping into a negative texel.
      (defn palette-index-256 [(index : I32)] : I32 (m-mod index 256))
      
      ;; ---- voxel lightmap lookup (the cheap half of Source 2's probe volumes) -----------------------------
      ;; Map a world coordinate to a cell on one axis of a probe grid, clamped to the grid. World units
      ;; x1000 so this stays integer and identical everywhere.
      (defn vlm-axis-index-milli [(pos_milli : I32) (origin_milli : I32) (extent_milli : I32) (res : I32)] : I32
        (if (or (<= extent_milli 0) (<= res 0))
          0
          (let [local (m-clamp 0 1000 (/ (* (m-clamp 0 extent_milli (- pos_milli origin_milli)) 1000) extent_milli))]
            (m-clamp 0 (- res 1) (/ (* local (- res 1)) 1000)))))
      
      ;; Outside every probe volume there is still light, and it is deliberately dark: 120 permille is the
      ;; corner a zombie waits in, not a black hole the player cannot read.
      (defn vlm-ambient-floor-milli [] : I32 120)
