  "instructions": "Add the lightweight sphere-map reflection pass.",
  "content": "/* reflection.h -- a lightweight environment reflection for metal and glass, with no assets at all.\n *\n * Founder: \"we want to implement basic reflection in metal and glass materials i guess make a mirror\n * material? it needs to be lightweight\".\n *\n * WHAT THIS IS: fixed-function SPHERE MAPPING (GL_SPHERE_MAP), the cheapest real reflection GL 1.x\n * offers. The driver computes the lookup coordinate from the vertex normal and the camera basis, so\n * there is no render target, no second scene pass, no cube map, no shader, and no per-frame CPU work\n * -- one extra textured draw of the same 36-vertex box, additively blended over the base pass.\n *\n * WHAT IT IS NOT, said plainly: a sphere map is a photograph of a mirror ball, so the reflection is\n * approximate. It has no parallax (it does not slide as you walk past), it cannot reflect the actual\n * level in front of a surface, and a flat mirror built from it looks like brushed chrome rather than a\n * true mirror. That is the trade a 1996 renderer makes, and it is the right one here: a real planar\n * or cube reflection costs an extra scene render per frame, which this target cannot pay.\n *\n * THE MAP: generated procedurally at first use (no image file, matching proctex_* and every other\n * render asset in this engine). It reads as a bright sky above a darker horizon, a warm band of\n * low sun, and a few cool vertical streaks -- enough that a curved highlight MOVES as the camera does,\n * which is the entire visual cue that a surface is shiny. Tint and strength are per-material.\n *\n * STATE CONTRACT: reflection_begin() saves what it changes and reflection_end() puts it back --\n * texture binding, TEXTURE_GEN_S/T, GL_TEXTURE_2D, blend func, depth mask, colour. Callers may nest\n * nothing, and must call end() even if they draw nothing (every draw helper here does).\n *\n * Requires immediate mode with per-vertex NORMALS (sphere mapping reads them); the engine's own\n * box drawing already supplies them. No GL header is included here on purpose: include this after\n * <SDL2/SDL_opengl.h>, the same contract material_shaders.h uses.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_REFLECTION_H\n#define SHANKPIT_REFLECTION_H\n\n#define REFLECTION_MAP_SIZE 64\n\ntypedef struct {\n    GLuint tex;\n    GLint prev_tex;      /* the binding in force before an active pass, restored by _end() */\n    int active;\n    int ready;\n    int draws;           /* diagnostics: how many reflective draws have happened */\n} ReflectionState;\n\nstatic ReflectionState g_reflection;\n\n/* A small, deterministic environment: sky above, warm horizon, dark ground, a couple of neon streaks.\n * Written as a sphere map (an image of the world as seen in a mirror ball), so the top of the texture\n * is overhead and the bottom is underfoot. */\nstatic void reflection_build_map(unsigned char *px, int size) {\n    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++) {\n        float v = (float)y / (float)(size - 1);           /* 0 = overhead, 1 = underfoot */\n        for (int x = 0; x < size; x++) {\n            float u = (float)x / (float)(size - 1);\n            float r, g, b;\n            if (v < 0.42f) {                               /* sky */\n                float k = v / 0.42f;\n                r = 0.28f + 0.10f * k;\n                g = 0.42f + 0.12f * k;\n                b = 0.62f - 0.06f * k;\n            } else if (v < 0.56f) {                        /* horizon: warm low sun */\n                float k = (v - 0.42f) / 0.14f;\n                r = 0.38f + 0.42f * k;\n                g = 0.54f + 0.16f * k;\n                b = 0.56f - 0.18f * k;\n            } else {                                       /* ground */\n                float k = (v - 0.56f) / 0.44f;\n                r = 0.20f - 0.12f * k;\n                g = 0.21f - 0.13f * k;\n                b = 0.24f - 0.15f * k;\n            }\n            /* two cool vertical streaks, like a lit sign reflected in a window */\n            if ((u > 0.18f && u < 0.22f) || (u > 0.74f && u < 0.78f)) {\n                if (v > 0.34f && v < 0.62f) { r += 0.16f; g += 0.28f; b += 0.34f; }\n            }\n            /* a hot spot for a specular hit to travel across */\n            {\n                float dx = u - 0.34f, dy = v - 0.30f;\n                float d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;\n                if (d2 < 0.012f) {\n                    float k = 1.0f - d2 / 0.012f;\n                    r += 0.55f * k; g += 0.52f * k; b += 0.44f * k;\n                }\n            }\n            if (r > 1.0f) r = 1.0f;\n            if (g > 1.0f) g = 1.0f;\n            if (b > 1.0f) b = 1.0f;\n            {\n                int i = (y * size + x) * 4;\n                px[i + 0] = (unsigned char)(r * 255.0f);\n                px[i + 1] = (unsigned char)(g * 255.0f);\n                px[i + 2] = (unsigned char)(b * 255.0f);\n                px[i + 3] = 255;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/* reflection_init -- creates the sphere map. Safe to call twice; a no-op once ready. Called lazily by\n * reflection_begin() so a host cannot forget it (and so it never runs before a GL context exists). */\nstatic void reflection_init(void) {\n    static unsigned char pixels[REFLECTION_MAP_SIZE * REFLECTION_MAP_SIZE * 4];\n    if (g_reflection.ready) return;\n    reflection_build_map(pixels, REFLECTION_MAP_SIZE);\n    glGenTextures(1, &g_reflection.tex);\n    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, g_reflection.tex);\n    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);\n    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, GL_LINEAR);\n    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, GL_REPEAT);\n    glTexParameteri(GL_TEXTURE_2D, GL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE);\n    glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0, GL_RGBA, REFLECTION_MAP_SIZE, REFLECTION_MAP_SIZE, 0,\n                 GL_RGBA, GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE, pixels);\n    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, 0);\n    g_reflection.ready = 1;\n    g_reflection.draws = 0;\n}\n\nstatic int reflection_ready(void) {\n    if (!g_reflection.ready) reflection_init();\n    return g_reflection.ready;\n}\n\n/* reflection_begin -- sets up the additive sphere-map pass. `strength_permille` is how bright the\n * reflection reads (0 draws nothing; the caller should skip the draw entirely at 0). `tint` is an RGB\n * multiplier, which is what makes the same map read as chrome, steel or cyan glass. */\nstatic int reflection_begin(int strength_permille, const float tint[3]) {\n    if (strength_permille <= 0) return 0;\n    if (strength_permille > 1000) strength_permille = 1000;\n    if (!reflection_ready()) return 0;\n    if (g_reflection.active) return 0;   /* not re-entrant: the caller nests nothing, and this\n                                          * refuses rather than silently corrupting the saved state */\n\n    glGetIntegerv(GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D, &g_reflection.prev_tex);\n    glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);\n    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, g_reflection.tex);\n    glTexGeni(GL_S, GL_TEXTURE_GEN_MODE, GL_SPHERE_MAP);\n    glTexGeni(GL_T, GL_TEXTURE_GEN_MODE, GL_SPHERE_MAP);\n    glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_GEN_S);\n    glEnable(GL_TEXTURE_GEN_T);\n    /* Sphere mapping reads the vertex normal through the current MODELVIEW, so the modelview must be\n     * the world/camera one with no model transform bolted on. This engine bakes transforms into the\n     * vertices, so it already is -- documented here because a caller that ever adds a glTranslate\n     * around this pass would get a reflection that swims. */\n\n    glEnable(GL_BLEND);\n    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);   /* additive: a highlight, never an opaque coat */\n    glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);               /* it sits on a surface already written this frame */\n    glColor4f(tint[0] * (float)strength_permille / 1000.0f,\n              tint[1] * (float)strength_permille / 1000.0f,\n              tint[2] * (float)strength_permille / 1000.0f, 1.0f);\n    g_reflection.active = 1;\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic void reflection_end(void) {\n    if (!g_reflection.active) return;\n    glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_GEN_S);\n    glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_GEN_T);\n    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, (GLuint)g_reflection.prev_tex);\n    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);\n    glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);\n    glColor4f(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);\n    g_reflection.active = 0;\n}\n\n/* reflection_draw_box -- one reflective box, the same world-space 36-vertex shape the material\n * shaders use (x/y/z is the CENTRE, w/h/d full extents, matching physics.h's own Box convention).\n * Returns 1 if it drew. */\nstatic int reflection_draw_box(float x, float y, float z, float w, float h, float d,\n                               int strength_permille, const float tint[3]) {\n    float hw = w * 0.5f, hh = h * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;\n    if (!reflection_begin(strength_permille, tint)) return 0;\n\n    glBegin(GL_QUADS);\n    /* top (+y) */\n    glNormal3f(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);\n    glVertex3f(x - hw, y + hh, z + hd); glVertex3f(x + hw, y + hh, z + hd);\n    glVertex3f(x + hw, y + hh, z - hd); glVertex3f(x - hw, y + hh, z - hd);\n    /* bottom (-y) */\n    glNormal3f(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);\n    glVertex3f(x - hw, y - hh, z - hd); glVertex3f(x + hw, y - hh, z - hd);\n    glVertex3f(x + hw, y - hh, z + hd); glVertex3f(x - hw, y - hh, z + hd);\n    /* front (+z) */\n    glNormal3f(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);\n    glVertex3f(x - hw, y - hh, z + hd); glVertex3f(x + hw, y - hh, z + hd);\n    glVertex3f(x + hw, y + hh, z + hd); glVertex3f(x - hw, y + hh, z + hd);\n    /* back (-z) */\n    glNormal3f(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);\n    glVertex3f(x + hw, y - hh, z - hd); glVertex3f(x - hw, y - hh, z - hd);\n    glVertex3f(x - hw, y + hh, z - hd); glVertex3f(x + hw, y + hh, z - hd);\n    /* left (-x) */\n    glNormal3f(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);\n    glVertex3f(x - hw, y - hh, z - hd); glVertex3f(x - hw, y - hh, z + hd);\n    glVertex3f(x - hw, y + hh, z + hd); glVertex3f(x - hw, y + hh, z - hd);\n    /* right (+x) */\n    glNormal3f(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);\n    glVertex3f(x + hw, y - hh, z + hd); glVertex3f(x + hw, y - hh, z - hd);\n    glVertex3f(x + hw, y + hh, z - hd); glVertex3f(x + hw, y + hh, z + hd);\n    glEnd();\n\n    reflection_end();\n    g_reflection.draws++;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_REFLECTION_H */\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/render/reflection_map.h",
  "instructions": "Add the pure-C procedural sphere map generator.",
  "content": "/* reflection_map.h -- the reflection environment, as pixels, with no GL anywhere in it.\n *\n * Split out of reflection.h so the map itself can be tested headlessly: this is the only part with\n * behaviour worth asserting (it must be deterministic, must have a bright sky above a dark ground, and\n * must carry a hot spot for a highlight to travel across), and a machine with no GL context still has\n * every reason to check it.\n *\n * A SPHERE MAP is an image of the world as reflected in a mirror ball: the top of the image is\n * overhead, the bottom is underfoot, the middle is the horizon. The fixed-function driver turns a\n * vertex normal plus the camera basis into a lookup into it, which is why one tiny texture is enough\n * to make a surface read as metal.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_REFLECTION_MAP_H\n#define SHANKPIT_REFLECTION_MAP_H\n\n/* Fills `px` with size*size RGBA pixels (4 bytes each), row 0 = overhead. Deterministic: no time, no\n * random, no state -- the same call always produces the same bytes. */\nstatic void reflection_map_build(unsigned char *px, int size) {\n    if (!px || size < 2) return;\n    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++) {\n        float v = (float)y / (float)(size - 1);           /* 0 = overhead, 1 = underfoot */\n        for (int x = 0; x < size; x++) {\n            float u = (float)x / (float)(size - 1);\n            float r, g, b;\n            if (v < 0.42f) {                               /* sky */\n                float k = v / 0.42f;\n                r = 0.28f + 0.10f * k;\n                g = 0.42f + 0.12f * k;\n                b = 0.62f - 0.06f * k;\n            } else if (v < 0.56f) {                        /* horizon: warm low sun */\n                float k = (v - 0.42f) / 0.14f;\n                r = 0.38f + 0.42f * k;\n                g = 0.54f + 0.16f * k;\n                b = 0.56f - 0.18f * k;\n            } else {                                       /* ground */\n                float k = (v - 0.56f) / 0.44f;\n                r = 0.20f - 0.12f * k;\n                g = 0.21f - 0.13f * k;\n                b = 0.24f - 0.15f * k;\n            }\n            /* two cool vertical streaks, like a lit sign reflected in a window */\n            if ((u > 0.18f && u < 0.22f) || (u > 0.74f && u < 0.78f)) {\n                if (v > 0.34f && v < 0.62f) { r += 0.16f; g += 0.28f; b += 0.34f; }\n            }\n            /* a hot spot for a specular hit to travel across */\n            {\n                float dx = u - 0.34f, dy = v - 0.30f;\n                float d2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;\n                if (d2 < 0.012f) {\n                    float k = 1.0f - d2 / 0.012f;\n                    r += 0.55f * k; g += 0.52f * k; b += 0.44f * k;\n                }\n            }\n            if (r > 1.0f) r = 1.0f;\n            if (g > 1.0f) g = 1.0f;\n            if (b > 1.0f) b = 1.0f;\n            {\n                int i = (y * size + x) * 4;\n                px[i + 0] = (unsigned char)(r * 255.0f);\n                px[i + 1] = (unsigned char)(g * 255.0f);\n                px[i + 2] = (unsigned char)(b * 255.0f);\n                px[i + 3] = 255;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_REFLECTION_MAP_H */\n"
}

  "instructions": "Add the headless reflection map and strength test.",
  "content": "/* reflection_map_test.c -- the reflection environment and its per-material strengths, headless.\n *\n * This box has no GL context, so what is checked here is everything that is NOT a GL call: the sphere\n * map's pixels (deterministic, sky above ground, a hot spot for a highlight to travel across, every\n * pixel opaque) and the PARENA strengths that decide how mirror-like a material is. The GL plumbing in\n * reflection.h is compiled by `make check-windows` (the mingw lobby build includes it through\n * material_shaders.h) and is NOT run here -- stated rather than implied.\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"reflection_map.h\"\n#include \"../simulation/material_rules_host.h\"\n\nstatic int g_fail = 0, g_checks = 0;\nstatic void ok(int cond, const char *what) {\n    g_checks++;\n    if (!cond) { g_fail++; printf(\"FAIL  %s\\n\", what); }\n    else printf(\"ok    %s\\n\", what);\n}\n\n#define SIZE 64\nstatic unsigned char px[SIZE * SIZE * 4];\nstatic unsigned char px2[SIZE * SIZE * 4];\n\nstatic int lum(int x, int y) {\n    int i = (y * SIZE + x) * 4;\n    return px[i] + px[i + 1] + px[i + 2];\n}\n\nint main(void) {\n    reflection_map_build(px, SIZE);\n    reflection_map_build(px2, SIZE);\n    ok(memcmp(px, px2, sizeof px) == 0, \"the map is deterministic (same bytes every build)\");\n\n    {\n        int opaque = 1, distinct = 0, i;\n        for (i = 0; i < SIZE * SIZE; i++)\n            if (px[i * 4 + 3] != 255) { opaque = 0; break; }\n        for (i = 1; i < SIZE * SIZE; i++)\n            if (memcmp(&px[i * 4], &px[(i - 1) * 4], 3) != 0) distinct++;\n        printf(\"      %d pixels differ from their neighbour\\n\", distinct);\n        ok(opaque, \"every texel is opaque (a sphere map is a solid image)\");\n        ok(distinct > 500, \"the map is a real environment, not a flat colour\");\n    }\n\n    /* Sphere-map orientation: row 0 is overhead, the last row is underfoot. A shiny surface must read\n     * as bright sky above and dark ground below, or every highlight would look upside-down. */\n    {\n        int sky = lum(8, 4), ground = lum(8, SIZE - 4);\n        printf(\"      sky luminance %d, ground luminance %d\\n\", sky, ground);\n        ok(sky > ground + 60, \"the sky end is much brighter than the ground end\");\n        ok(px[(4 * SIZE + 8) * 4 + 2] > px[((SIZE - 4) * SIZE + 8) * 4 + 2] + 30,\n           \"and the sky is bluer than the ground (not just brighter)\");\n    }\n\n    /* The hot spot is what makes a highlight visibly travel as the camera turns. */\n    {\n        int hot_x = (int)(0.34f * (SIZE - 1)), hot_y = (int)(0.30f * (SIZE - 1));\n        int hot = lum(hot_x, hot_y), cold = lum((int)(0.60f * (SIZE - 1)), (int)(0.85f * (SIZE - 1)));\n        printf(\"      hot spot luminance %d vs a dull texel %d\\n\", hot, cold);\n        ok(hot > cold + 120, \"the mirror-ball hot spot is really there\");\n    }\n\n    /* The streaks: a couple of cold verticals in the horizon band. */\n    {\n        int streak = lum((int)(0.20f * (SIZE - 1)), (int)(0.50f * (SIZE - 1)));\n        int beside = lum((int)(0.30f * (SIZE - 1)), (int)(0.50f * (SIZE - 1)));\n        printf(\"      streak luminance %d, beside it %d\\n\", streak, beside);\n        ok(streak > beside + 30, \"the reflected-sign streaks are visible\");\n    }\n\n    /* A degenerate size is refused rather than writing past the buffer. */\n    {\n        unsigned char tiny[16];\n        memset(tiny, 0xAB, sizeof tiny);\n        reflection_map_build(tiny, 0);\n        reflection_map_build(tiny, 1);\n        ok(tiny[0] == 0xAB && tiny[15] == 0xAB, \"size < 2 writes nothing at all\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- strengths are PARENA's ------------------------------------------------------------- */\n    {\n        int mirror = mat_reflection_strength_permille(0);\n        int metal = mat_reflection_strength_permille(1);\n        int glass = mat_reflection_strength_permille(2);\n        int brick = mat_reflection_strength_permille(3);\n        int bogus = mat_reflection_strength_permille(-7);\n        printf(\"      strengths: mirror %d, metal %d, glass %d, other %d\\n\", mirror, metal, glass, brick);\n        ok(mirror > metal && metal > glass, \"mirror reflects most, then metal, then glass\");\n        ok(mirror <= 1000 && glass > 0, \"all three are inside 0..1000 and all three actually reflect\");\n        ok(brick == 0, \"a non-reflective material costs nothing at all\");\n        ok(bogus == 0, \"an out-of-range kind is 0, not a surprise mirror\");\n        ok(mirror == 900 && glass == 320, \"the shipped numbers are the ones in material_rules.prn\");\n    }\n\n    printf(\"\\n%d checks, %d failed\\n\", g_checks, g_fail);\n    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;\n}\n"
}

> _Reasoning_
> Only failure: "the map is a real environment, not a flat colour" — 293 pixels differ from their neighbour. My threshold of 500 was arbitrary. Is 293 reasonable for 64×64=4096 pixels with smooth gradients? A smooth vertical gradient changes each row, and horizontally only at streaks/hotspot. So "differ from the previous pixel" count ~ rows at boundaries (streaks) + gradient rounding. 293 distinct changes over 4096 is plausible for a mostly smooth image. My assertion was a bad proxy for "not flat". Better measure: count of distinct colors (unique RGB), which should be high (thousands). Let me change the check to count unique RGB values by sampling (or use a small hash set). Simple: count distinct luminance values across rows and distinct colors via a 2D sampling... Simplest robust: number of distinct RGB triples ≥ 100. With quantization 8-bit and gradients, easily thousands.
> 
> Implement: nested loops comparing all pairs is 4096² = 16M — fine (fast). Count unique by checking each pixel against all previous — 16M comparisons, ok at O1? ~ maybe 30ms. Acceptable but let me instead use a 4096-entry boolean over a hash of (r,g,b): hash = (r*7 + g*13 + b*29) & 4095; collisions possible but count of set bits still >> 100.
> 
> Simplest: count distinct luminance levels among a sample: for each of 64 rows, lum at x=8; count distinct; plus horizontal variety. Eh.
> 
> I'll do the hash-set approach with 65536 bits (2048 bytes static) — count distinct hashed colors; assert > 200. That's a real "rich environment" check.

The audit first: this renderer is fixed-function GL 1.x plus a couple of hand-loaded GL 2.0 passes (`material_shaders.h` already had specular, IPS/HPS emissive and a PARENA-tinted glass pass), so a **sphere map** is the cheap real option — the driver derives the lookup from the vertex normal and the camera basis, which means no render target, no second scene pass, no cube map, no shader and no per-frame CPU work. New `packages/render/reflection_map.h` is the environment as pixels (a pure-C, deterministic sphere map: bright sky above a warm horizon over dark ground, two cold \"reflected sign\" streaks, and a hot spot so a highlight visibly **travels** as you turn), and `packages/render/reflection.h` is the GL half: lazy texture creation at first use, `glTexGeni(GL_S/GL_T, GL_SPHERE_MAP)`, additive blend with depth-write off (a sheen, never an opaque coat), and a begin/end pair that **saves and restores the texture binding, texgen, blend and depth mask** — refusing a nested begin rather than corrupting its saved state. Strengths are PARENA's, not the renderer's: `mat-reflection-strength-permille(kind)` in `material_rules.prn` (**mirror 900, metal 380, glass 320, everything else 0**), so brick/concrete/wood cost exactly nothing. Wired inside `material_shaders.h` where the materials already live: `draw_material_specular_box` adds the sheen for anything at or above its own 0.6 metal threshold, `draw_material_glass_box` adds a subtle one after its transparent pass, and a new `draw_material_mirror_box` draws a near-black base so the environment IS the surface. Verified: `make test-reflection` — the map is byte-identical across builds, every texel opaque, **200+ distinct graded colours**, sky much brighter *and* bluer than the ground (so highlights are not upside-down), the hot spot 736 vs 99, the streaks visible, a degenerate size writing nothing, and the shipped strengths ordered mirror > metal > glass > 0 with an out-of-range kind reflecting nothing. Plus `make test-material-rules` (still green), `make check-windows` (99 lobby sources, which is what compiles the GL half through `material_shaders.h`) and `make -B server`. Honest limits, named: a sphere map has **no parallax** — it does not slide as you walk past and cannot reflect the actual level — so a \"mirror\" reads as polished chrome, not a true mirror; the real alternative costs an extra scene render per frame, which this target cannot pay. The GL state machine itself is **compiled but not run** here (no GPU, no SDL2/GL headers on this box, so the headless test covers the pixels and the numbers only), and nothing in the build yet *selects* a mirror material — `draw_material_mirror_box` exists for the material list that adds one.\n",

Done. Metal, glass and a mirror material all reflect now, using the cheapest real technique this renderer can afford.

## What's there

- **`packages/render/reflection_map.h`** — the environment as pixels, pure C, deterministic: bright sky above a warm horizon over dark ground, two cold "reflected sign" streaks, and a hot spot so a highlight visibly **travels** as you turn. No image file, matching this engine's `proctex_*` convention.
- **`packages/render/reflection.h`** — the GL half: lazy texture creation, `glTexGeni(GL_S/GL_T, GL_SPHERE_MAP)`, additive blend with depth-write off (a sheen, never an opaque coat), and a begin/end pair that saves and restores texture binding, texgen, blend and depth mask — refusing a nested begin rather than corrupting its saved state.
- **Strengths are PARENA's**, not the renderer's: `mat-reflection-strength-permille` in `material_rules.prn` → **mirror 900, metal 380, glass 320, everything else 0**, so brick/concrete/wood cost exactly nothing.
- **Wired in `material_shaders.h`** where the materials already live: the specular pass adds the sheen at its own ≥0.6 metal threshold, the glass pass adds a subtle one after its transparent draw, and new `draw_material_mirror_box` lays a near-black base so the environment *is* the surface.

## Checks actually run
`make test-reflection` — **13/13**: byte-identical map across builds, every texel opaque, 200+ distinct graded colours, sky much brighter **and bluer** than the ground (highlights aren't upside-down), hot spot 736 vs 99, streaks visible, degenerate size writes nothing, and strengths ordered mirror > metal > glass > 0 with an out-of-range kind reflecting nothing. Plus `make test-material-rules` (still green) and `make check-windows` (**99/99** sources — that's what compiles the GL half, since it reaches `main.c` through `material_shaders.h`). `make -B server` links.

One real bug caught by that Windows build: my helper block landed at the bottom of `material_shaders.h` while the specular pass using it sits near the top, so the call created an implicit declaration and the real definition conflicted. Fixed with forward declarations, then re-ran the check.

## Limits, named
- A sphere map has **no parallax** — it doesn't slide as you walk past and can't reflect the actual level, so a "mirror" reads as polished chrome, not a true mirror. A true planar/cube reflection costs an extra scene render per frame, which this target can't pay.
- The GL state machine is **compiled but never executed** here — no GPU, and no SDL2/GL headers natively — so the headless test covers the pixels and the numbers only.
- Nothing in the build yet *selects* a mirror material; `draw_material_mirror_box` is there for the material list that adds one.

      #ifndef EDU_BINDINGS_H
      #define EDU_BINDINGS_H
      
      #include "edu_entities.h"
      
      /* Level-authored programmable widgets (NOCK `edu_widgets` -> EduVM). A widget is a named machine with one
       * int state register; scripts address it by string id (set_state/read_state) or by its register address
       * (set_reg/read_sensor, which is what makes `while` loops over consecutive gates possible). PLATE is a
       * sensor: only the host writes it (edu_widget_host_set), a script can never forge one. */
      #define EDU_MAX_WIDGETS 16
      #define EDU_WIDGET_ID_MAX 32
      typedef enum {
          EDU_WIDGET_NONE = 0,
          EDU_WIDGET_GATE,
          EDU_WIDGET_BRIDGE,
          EDU_WIDGET_PORTAL,
          EDU_WIDGET_CRATE,
          EDU_WIDGET_PLATE,
          EDU_WIDGET_TYPE_COUNT
      } EduWidgetType;
      
      typedef struct {
          int active;
          char id[EDU_WIDGET_ID_MAX];
          int machine_type;
          int initial_state;
          int state;
          int reg;                 /* memory_address: the "hardware register" scripts read/write by number */
          float x, y, z, radius;   /* world position + sensor reach (plates), for the host to draw/trigger */
      } EduWidget;
      
      typedef struct {
          int crate_speed;
          int crate_x;
          int gate_open;
          int bridge_raised;
          int bridge_angle;
          int portal_stability;
          int portal_open;
          int enemy_count;
          int trial_complete;
          int switch_on;
          int grounded_test_platform;
          int quest_make_it_move;
          int quest_stop_the_fall;
          int quest_open_the_gate;
          int rift_hound_active;
          int rift_hound_hp;
          int enemy_marked[4];
          int enemy_slowed[4];
          int can_open_gate;
          int can_raise_bridge;
          int can_modify_portal;
          int can_affect_enemies;
          int can_spawn_entities;
          int puppet_active;
          int puppet_type;
          float puppet_x;
          float puppet_y;
          float puppet_z;
          float puppet_anim_t;
          int last_print;
          char last_message[96];
          Entity entities[MAX_EDU_ENTITIES];
          int entity_count;
          unsigned int entity_tick_last_ms;
          EduWidget widgets[EDU_MAX_WIDGETS];
          int widget_count;
      } EduWorldState;
      
      typedef enum {
          EDU_BUILTIN_SET_CRATE_SPEED = 0,
          EDU_BUILTIN_MOVE_CRATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_STOP_CRATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_OPEN_GATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_CLOSE_GATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SET_SWITCH,
          EDU_BUILTIN_IS_SWITCH_ON,
          EDU_BUILTIN_QUERY_GROUNDED,
          EDU_BUILTIN_MARK_QUEST_COMPLETE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_GET_QUEST_STATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_PRINT,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SHOW_MESSAGE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SCAN_GATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SCAN_PORTAL,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SCAN_ENEMY_COUNT,
          EDU_BUILTIN_RAISE_BRIDGE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_STABILIZE_PORTAL,
          EDU_BUILTIN_OPEN_PORTAL,
          EDU_BUILTIN_MARK_ENEMY,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SLOW_ENEMY,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SPAWN_PROP,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SET_ENTITY_POS,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SET_ENTITY_VEL,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SET_STATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_SET_REG,
          EDU_BUILTIN_READ_SENSOR,
          EDU_BUILTIN_READ_STATE,
          EDU_BUILTIN_COUNT
      } EduBuiltinId;

  content: |
      // story_buttons.h -- S485, real, reusable interact-triggered buttons. Founder real-time: "how am
      // i gonna put a button on a wall next to a door to open a door?" -> "we need a reusable button
      // that can be put in different places" -> "i want to follow the pub sub model ... the bridge
      // listens for a button the button has no idea the bridge exists."
      //
      // A button knows nothing about what it controls. Pressing it dispatches
      // REFLUX_ACTION_BUTTON_PRESSED(button_id, player_id, 0) into the shared REFLUX log
      // (packages/reflux/reflux_runtime.h) and stops -- any number of subscribers (today: doors with a
      // matching LevelDoor.subscribe_button_id, see story_doors.h) react independently, with zero
      // reference back to this file. Deliberately real, edge-triggered player INTERACT input (BTN_USE,
      // already wired end to end: apps/lobby's own F-key binding -> UserCmd.buttons -> p->in_use,
      // packages/common/net_sim.h), not walk-up proximity -- founder's own explicit reasoning: "a door
      // that is open and closable gives you more agency... in a situation with zombies... the zombies
      // cant hit the button." Story AI characters (packages/simulation/story_ai.c) are server-simulated
      // and never send a UserCmd at all, so an interact-driven button is automatically player-only --
      // no separate "exclude NPCs" check needed, it falls out of the input model for free. Mirrors
      // local_game.h's own established ctf_handle_use_interactions shape (same edge-trigger idiom,
      // same p->in_use/p->use_was_down fields), generalized to run in every game mode, not just one --
      // per S481c's own resolved policy, a general level feature is never hard-gated to one mode.
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_STORY_BUTTONS_H
      #define SHANKPIT_STORY_BUTTONS_H
      
      #include <math.h>
      
      #include "../world/level_boxes.h"
      #include "../reflux/reflux_runtime.h"
      
      // BUTTON_USE_RADIUS -- how close (world units) a player must be to a button's own box for a
      // press to register. Matches CTFB_USE_RADIUS's own order of magnitude (28.0f) loosely, but a
      // button is a small, deliberately-aimed-at wall fixture, not a flag pickup zone -- kept tighter
      // so a player can't fire a button from clear across a room.
      #define BUTTON_USE_RADIUS 6.0f
      
      typedef struct {
          int box_index;
          int button_id;
      } ButtonRuntime;
      
      #define STORY_BUTTONS_MAX LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_BUTTONS
      static ButtonRuntime g_story_buttons[STORY_BUTTONS_MAX];
      static int g_story_button_count = 0;
      
      static inline void story_buttons_init(const CustomLevelData *lvl) {
          g_story_button_count = 0;
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->button_count && g_story_button_count < STORY_BUTTONS_MAX; i++) {
              g_story_buttons[g_story_button_count].box_index = lvl->buttons[i].box_index;
              g_story_buttons[g_story_button_count].button_id = lvl->buttons[i].button_id;
              g_story_button_count++;
          }
      }
      
      // story_buttons_handle_use_interactions -- real, edge-triggered (fires once per real key-down,
      // not every tick held), called once per active player per server tick, same call shape
      // ctf_handle_use_interactions already established (see local_game.h). Checks every placed
      // button's own box distance; the first one in range wins (buttons are small, deliberately-placed
      // fixtures -- two buttons within BUTTON_USE_RADIUS of each other and of the player at once is a
      // real, unlikely level-design edge case, not defended against specially here).
      static inline void story_buttons_handle_use_interactions(PlayerState *p, unsigned int now_ms) {
          (void)now_ms; // no cooldown/timestamp bookkeeping needed yet -- reserved for parity with
                        // ctf_handle_use_interactions's own signature and real future use (e.g. a
                        // per-button re-press cooldown), not unused-and-forgotten.
          if (!p->in_use || p->use_was_down) return;
          for (int i = 0; i < g_story_button_count; i++) {
              ButtonRuntime *btn = &g_story_buttons[i];
              float bx, by, bz;
              if (!phys_custom_level_box_pos(btn->box_index, &bx, &by, &bz)) continue;
              float dx = p->x - bx, dy = p->y - by, dz = p->z - bz;
              float dist_sq = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
              if (dist_sq <= (BUTTON_USE_RADIUS * BUTTON_USE_RADIUS)) {
                  reflux_host_dispatch(REFLUX_ACTION_BUTTON_PRESSED, btn->button_id, p->id, 0);
                  return; // one press, one dispatch -- don't fire every button simultaneously in range
              }
          }
      }
      
      #endif // SHANKPIT_STORY_BUTTONS_H

No node knows what it looks like: a centrifuge is a motor, a lift is a\n;; motor plus a lever, a security door is a plate into a transistor into a gate.\n;;\n;; Power is 0..15, one integer, exactly like DEADWEIGHT's cable tiers -- low enough that a whole level\n;; fits in a byte per node and high enough to read a bar graph.\n;;\n;; All I32, total, no state. Retune here and `make regen-widget-rules`.\n(module shankpit/widget-rules)\n(export widget-kind-count widget-power-on widget-power-off widget-max-power\n        widget-delay-default-ticks widget-delay-min-ticks widget-delay-max-ticks\n        widget-output-power widget-delay-armed widget-delay-still-running\n        widget-lever-toggle widget-plate-power widget-motor-target\n        widget-focus-ok widget-focus-prompt-ms widget-panel-key-adjust)\n\n;; 0 LEVER, 1 PLATE, 2 DELAY, 3 TRANSISTOR, 4 MOTOR\n(defn widget-kind-count [] : I32 5)\n(defn widget-power-on [] : I32 15)\n(defn widget-power-off [] : I32 0)\n(defn widget-max-power [] : I32 15)\n\n;; Delay nodes count in ticks (60 = one second). The default is a half-second relay -- long enough to\n;; see a signal arrive and leave, short enough to still feel like a switch.\n(defn widget-delay-default-ticks [] : I32 30)\n(defn widget-delay-min-ticks [] : I32 1)\n(defn widget-delay-max-ticks [] : I32 600)\n\n(defn w-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n;; ---- the circuit ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; `armed` is the node's own latched output from the previous tick; for a lever that is its position,\n;; for a delay it is the pulse it is currently holding. Everything else ignores it except the delay,\n;; which is the one node whose output is not simply its input.\n;;\n;;   LEVER        outputs its own position (armed), regardless of input -- it is a source\n;;   PLATE        outputs its own sensor reading (armed): the host writes it, a script cannot\n;;   DELAY        outputs the pulse it is holding (armed); the host arms/clears it (see below)\n;;   TRANSISTOR   passes input ONLY when the gate input is powered (a real AND, not a diode)\n;;   MOTOR        follows its input: a lift, a centrifuge, a door -- whatever the level draws\n(defn widget-output-power [(kind : I32) (armed : I32) (src_power : I32) (gate_power : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= kind 0) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)\n    (if (= kind 1) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)\n      (if (= kind 2) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)\n        (if (= kind 3) (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 gate_power) 0) (w-clamp 0 15 src_power) 0)\n          (w-clamp 0 15 src_power))))))\n\n;; A delay's rising edge starts its timer (0 = not running). A fresh edge while it is already\n;; counting does NOT restart it -- a burst of pulses becomes one delayed pulse, not a stutter.\n(defn widget-delay-armed [(src_power : I32) (timer_ticks : I32) (armed : I32)] : I32\n  (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 src_power) 0) (if (<= timer_ticks 0) (if (<= (w-clamp 0 15 armed) 0) 1 0) 0) 0))\n\n;; A delay fires for exactly one tick when its timer hits zero, then clears until the input drops.\n(defn widget-delay-still-running [(src_power : I32) (timer_ticks : I32)] : I32\n  (if (and (> timer_ticks 0) (<= (w-clamp 0 15 src_power) 0)) 0 (if (> timer_ticks 0) 1 0)))\n\n;; ---- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; A lever is a light switch: press it and it stays where you put it.\n(defn widget-lever-toggle [(power : I32)] : I32\n  (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 power) 0) (widget-power-off) (widget-power-on)))\n\n;; A pressure plate reads bodies standing on it. Any real weight closes it; the count is capped so a\n;; crowd cannot produce a stronger signal than one person (this is a switch, not a scale).\n(defn widget-plate-power [(occupants : I32)] : I32\n  (if (> (w-clamp 0 8 occupants) 0) (widget-power-on) (widget-power-off)))\n\n;; A motor's discrete target: 0 down/idle, 1 up/running. The level decides what that means (a lift\n;; car's floor, a centrifuge's spin) -- the circuit only says the machine has power.\n(defn widget-motor-target [(power : I32)] : I32 (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 power) 0) 1 0))\n\n;; ---- the F interface ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; Whether a parked widget offers itself for interaction. Distance is in millimetres so the whole\n;; decision stays integer; a widget with no interaction radius (0) is scenery and never prompts.\n;; The prompt asks for the widget standing between the player and the surface they are looking at:\n;; closest wins, so a lever bolted to a terminal is reachable without reaching through it.\n(defn widget-focus-ok [(dist_mm : I32) (radius_mm : I32) (busy : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= busy 1) 0\n    (if (<= (w-clamp 0 1000000 radius_mm) 0) 0\n      (if (<= (w-clamp 0 1000000 dist_mm) (w-clamp 0 1000000 radius_mm)) 1 0))))\n\n;; How long the \"[F] USE\" prompt holds after the player stops moving, so it does not flicker when the\n;; distance wobbles across the radius boundary.\n(defn widget-focus-prompt-ms [] : I32 250)\n\n;; A panel's key repeat for a value the player is dialling (RPM, floor, intensity): one step per press,\n;; and the step size is the panel's own, clamped so a held key cannot spin a motor to nonsense.\n(defn widget-panel-key-adjust [(value : I32) (delta : I32) (lo : I32) (hi : I32)] : I32\n  (w-clamp (w-clamp -1000000 1000000 lo) (w-clamp -1000000 1000000 hi) (+ value delta)))\n"
}

This header\n * carries matching C defaults so packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h keeps working in every binary\n * and test that includes it without linking a generated file -- the same arrangement slide_rules.h and\n * drone_flight.h use, and the circuit test asserts the two curves agree.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_H\n#define SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_H\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int (*output_power)(int kind, int armed, int src_power, int gate_power);\n    int (*delay_armed)(int src_power, int timer_ticks, int armed);\n    int (*delay_still_running)(int src_power, int timer_ticks);\n    int (*lever_toggle)(int power);\n    int (*plate_power)(int occupants);\n    int (*motor_target)(int power);\n    int (*focus_ok)(int dist_mm, int radius_mm, int busy);\n    int (*panel_key_adjust)(int value, int delta, int lo, int hi);\n    int (*delay_default_ticks)(void);\n    int (*delay_min_ticks)(void);\n    int (*delay_max_ticks)(void);\n} WidgetRules;\n\nstatic inline int wg_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }\nstatic inline int wg_on(void) { return 15; }\nstatic inline int wg_off(void) { return 0; }\n\nstatic inline int wg_c_output_power(int kind, int armed, int src, int gate) {\n    if (kind == 0) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed);          /* lever */\n    if (kind == 1) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed);          /* plate */\n    if (kind == 2) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed);          /* delay: holds its own pulse */\n    if (kind == 3) return wg_clamp(0, 15, gate) > 0 ? wg_clamp(0, 15, src) : 0;  /* transistor */\n    return wg_clamp(0, 15, src);                            /* motor follows its input */\n}\nstatic inline int wg_c_delay_armed(int src, int timer, int armed) {\n    if (wg_clamp(0, 15, src) > 0) {\n        if (timer <= 0) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed) <= 0 ? 1 : 0;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\nstatic inline int wg_c_delay_running(int src, int timer) {\n    if (timer > 0 && wg_clamp(0, 15, src) <= 0) return 0;\n    return timer > 0 ? 1 : 0;\n}\nstatic inline int wg_c_lever_toggle(int power) { return wg_clamp(0, 15, power) > 0 ? wg_off() : wg_on(); }\nstatic inline int wg_c_plate_power(int occupants) { return wg_clamp(0, 8, occupants) > 0 ? wg_on() : wg_off(); }\nstatic inline int wg_c_motor_target(int power) { return wg_clamp(0, 15, power) > 0 ? 1 : 0; }\nstatic inline int wg_c_focus_ok(int dist_mm, int radius_mm, int busy) {\n    if (busy == 1) return 0;\n    if (wg_clamp(0, 1000000, radius_mm) <= 0) return 0;\n    return wg_clamp(0, 1000000, dist_mm) <= wg_clamp(0, 1000000, radius_mm) ? 1 : 0;\n}\nstatic inline int wg_c_panel_adjust(int value, int delta, int lo, int hi) {\n    return wg_clamp(wg_clamp(-1000000, 1000000, lo), wg_clamp(-1000000, 1000000, hi), value + delta);\n}\nstatic inline int wg_c_delay_default(void) { return 30; }\nstatic inline int wg_c_delay_min(void) { return 1; }\nstatic inline int wg_c_delay_max(void) { return 600; }\n\nstatic WidgetRules g_widget_rules = {\n    wg_c_output_power, wg_c_delay_armed, wg_c_delay_running, wg_c_lever_toggle, wg_c_plate_power,\n    wg_c_motor_target, wg_c_focus_ok, wg_c_panel_adjust, wg_c_delay_default, wg_c_delay_min, wg_c_delay_max\n};\n\nstatic inline void widget_set_rules(const WidgetRules *r) { if (r) g_widget_rules = *r; }\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_H */\n"

  "content": "/* widget_circuit.h -- composable world widgets: a tiny power circuit, an F interface, and panels.\n *\n * Founder: \"we already have a widget primative ... general interface like F to interact and then after\n * that it needs to be able to go into custom programmed affordances ... the widgets need to be\n * composible ... think light switches, basic circuits, an elevator is a widget of widgets ... bring in\n * edu vm script it all needs to play nice with that interpreter\".\n *\n * MODEL: every placed widget is one NODE in a directed circuit, evaluated once per tick in authoring\n * order (pins point at lower indices). Power is a single integer 0..15 -- the same tier range\n * DEADWEIGHT's own cables use -- so a whole level is a byte per node and any node can drive any other:\n *\n *   LEVER (6)       a light switch: press it, it stays. 0 or 15, no wiring needed.\n *   PLATE (5)       a pressure plate: the HOST writes it from bodies standing on it.\n *   DELAY (7)       a relay: output follows input N ticks late (both edges).\n *   TRANSISTOR (8)  a real AND: passes its input only while its gate input is powered.\n *   MACHINE (1..4)  a motor/actuator: follows its input. A lift is a motor plus a lever; a centrifuge\n *                   is a motor plus a plate; a security door is a plate -> transistor -> machine.\n *\n * EDUVM: every node can own a register. Its live value is mirrored into `reg_value` every tick, and a\n * terminal panel writes `reg_value`, so a script (set_reg / read_sensor) and the physical circuit are\n * looking at the same number instead of two copies of the world. This header does not include or call\n * the VM: it produces the values; the host that owns the EduWorldState copies them in.\n *\n * THE F INTERFACE: focus is a proximity query with hysteresis (the prompt holds for\n * widget-focus-prompt-ms, so it does not flicker at the edge of the radius). USE on a lever toggles it\n * and stays in the world; USE on anything with a register opens its PANEL, where a script-driven\n * affordance takes over the keys (that is the \"custom programmed affordance\" the founder asked for).\n *\n * NOT DONE, and named: nothing here draws. There is no prompt quad, no panel rendering and no lever\n * mesh -- those are renderer work, and this file deliberately contains no GL. Nothing calls\n * widget_circuit_tick from the game loop yet either: it is loaded and driven by the test, and wiring it\n * to a scene is the next step (see docs/WIDGET_AFFORDANCES.md).\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_WIDGET_CIRCUIT_H\n#define SHANKPIT_WIDGET_CIRCUIT_H\n\n#include <math.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"../world/level_boxes.h\"\n#include \"widget_rules.h\"\n\n#define WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS\n\n/* Kinds, matching the level schema's machine_type for the circuit-only ones. */\nenum {\n    WIDGET_KIND_LEVER = 0,\n    WIDGET_KIND_PLATE = 1,\n    WIDGET_KIND_DELAY = 2,\n    WIDGET_KIND_TRANSISTOR = 3,\n    WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR = 4,\n    WIDGET_KIND_NONE = -1\n};\n\nenum { WIDGET_MODE_WORLD = 0, WIDGET_MODE_PANEL = 1 };\n\n/* Panel keys, so this file never includes SDL. */\nenum { WIDGET_KEY_UP = 0, WIDGET_KEY_DOWN, WIDGET_KEY_LEFT, WIDGET_KEY_RIGHT, WIDGET_KEY_USE, WIDGET_KEY_BACK };\n\n#define WIDGET_PANEL_STEP 500\n#define WIDGET_PANEL_MIN 0\n#define WIDGET_PANEL_MAX 8000\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int active;\n    char id[32];\n    int kind;\n    int input_pin, gate_pin;   /* widget indices, or -1 */\n    int power;                 /* live output 0..15 */\n    int armed;                 /* latched: lever position, plate reading, delay's held value */\n    int timer_ticks;           /* delay countdown */\n    int delay_ticks;           /* this delay's own length; 0 = the rules' default */\n    int reg;                   /* EduVM register to mirror into; -1 = none */\n    int reg_value;             /* what the host copies into that register */\n    float x, y, z, radius;\n    int box_index;\n} WidgetNode;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    WidgetNode n[WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX];\n    int count;\n    int mode;              /* WIDGET_MODE_* */\n    int focused;           /* index, or -1 */\n    int focus_hold_ms;     /* prompt hysteresis */\n    int pressed;           /* index whose panel is open, or -1 */\n} WidgetCircuit;\n\n/* Which circuit kind an authored machine_type is. 1..4 are the education machines and behave as\n * motors here (a gate raises, a crate moves, a portal opens: all \"this node drives geometry\"); 5..8 are\n * the circuit kinds themselves. Everything else is scenery. */\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_kind_for_machine(int machine_type) {\n    if (machine_type == 5) return WIDGET_KIND_PLATE;\n    if (machine_type == 6) return WIDGET_KIND_LEVER;\n    if (machine_type == 7) return WIDGET_KIND_DELAY;\n    if (machine_type == 8) return WIDGET_KIND_TRANSISTOR;\n    if (machine_type >= 1 && machine_type <= 4) return WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR;\n    return WIDGET_KIND_NONE;\n}\n\nstatic inline void widget_circuit_init(WidgetCircuit *c) {\n    if (!c) return;\n    memset(c, 0, sizeof *c);\n    c->focused = -1;\n    c->pressed = -1;\n    c->mode = WIDGET_MODE_WORLD;\n}\n\n/* Loads every authored widget. A widget with an unknown kind or an empty id is skipped rather than\n * half-loaded, and a pin that points at itself or out of range is dropped to -1 -- a mis-wired level\n * must degrade to \"that switch does nothing\", never to a feedback loop or a crash. */\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_load(WidgetCircuit *c, const CustomLevelData *lvl) {\n    int loaded = 0;\n    widget_circuit_init(c);\n    if (!c || !lvl) return 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < lvl->edu_widget_count && c->count < WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX; i++) {\n        const LevelEduWidget *w = &lvl->edu_widgets[i];\n        int kind = widget_circuit_kind_for_machine(w->machine_type);\n        if (kind == WIDGET_KIND_NONE || !w->entity_id[0]) continue;\n        WidgetNode *n = &c->n[c->count];\n        memset(n, 0, sizeof *n);\n        n->active = 1;\n        snprintf(n->id, sizeof n->id, \"%s\", w->entity_id);\n        n->kind = kind;\n        n->armed = w->initial_state ? wg_on() : wg_off();\n        n->reg = w->memory_address;\n        n->reg_value = n->armed;\n        n->delay_ticks = w->delay_ticks > 0 ? w->delay_ticks : 0;\n        n->x = w->x; n->y = w->y; n->z = w->z;\n        n->radius = w->radius > 0.0f ? w->radius : 3.0f;   /* authored reach, or a room-scale default */\n        n->box_index = w->box_index;\n        n->input_pin = (w->input_pin >= 0 && w->input_pin < c->count) ? w->input_pin : -1;\n        n->gate_pin = (w->gate_pin >= 0 && w->gate_pin < c->count) ? w->gate_pin : -1;\n        c->count++;\n        loaded++;\n    }\n    return loaded;\n}\n\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_pin_power(const WidgetCircuit *c, int pin) {\n    if (!c || pin < 0 || pin >= c->count) return 0;\n    return c->n[pin].power;\n}\n\n/* The whole circuit, one tick. Sources first (lever/plate/delay resolve their own latched value), then\n * the pass-through nodes reading the values already computed this tick. */\nstatic inline void widget_circuit_tick(WidgetCircuit *c) {\n    if (!c) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++) {\n        WidgetNode *n = &c->n[i];\n        int src = widget_circuit_pin_power(c, n->input_pin);\n        int gate = widget_circuit_pin_power(c, n->gate_pin);\n        if (n->kind == WIDGET_KIND_DELAY) {\n            int delay = n->delay_ticks > 0 ? n->delay_ticks : g_widget_rules.delay_default_ticks();\n            if (delay < g_widget_rules.delay_min_ticks()) delay = g_widget_rules.delay_min_ticks();\n            if (delay > g_widget_rules.delay_max_ticks()) delay = g_widget_rules.delay_max_ticks();\n            if (g_widget_rules.delay_armed(src, n->armed, n->timer_ticks)) {\n                n->timer_ticks = delay;\n            } else if (n->timer_ticks > 0) {\n                n->timer_ticks--;\n                if (n->timer_ticks == 0) n->armed = src;   /* the relay closes on the new value */\n            }\n        }\n        n->power = g_widget_rules.output_power(n->kind, n->armed, src, gate);\n        /* A mirror, not a second copy: the register reads what the circuit actually did this tick. */\n        n->reg_value = n->power;\n    }\n}\n\n/* The host writes a plate from the bodies standing on it (a script can never forge a sensor). */\nstatic inline void widget_circuit_set_plate(WidgetCircuit *c, int index, int occupants) {\n    if (!c || index < 0 || index >= c->count) return;\n    if (c->n[index].kind != WIDGET_KIND_PLATE) return;\n    c->n[index].armed = g_widget_rules.plate_power(occupants);\n}\n\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_lever_toggle(WidgetCircuit *c, int index) {\n    if (!c || index < 0 || index >= c->count) return 0;\n    if (c->n[index].kind != WIDGET_KIND_LEVER) return 0;\n    c->n[index].armed = g_widget_rules.lever_toggle(c->n[index].armed);\n    return c->n[index].armed;\n}\n\n/* ---- the F interface ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */\n/* widget_circuit_focus -- the nearest in-reach widget, or -1. `busy` (a panel already open, a vehicle\n * seat, a cutscene) suppresses the prompt entirely. The hold timer keeps the LAST focus while nothing\n * qualifies, so the prompt does not strobe as the player walks along a shelf of levers. */\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_focus(WidgetCircuit *c, float px, float py, float pz, int busy, int dt_ms) {\n    int best = -1;\n    int best_mm = 0;\n    if (!c) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++) {\n        WidgetNode *n = &c->n[i];\n        float dx, dy, dz;\n        int dist_mm, radius_mm;\n        if (!n->active) continue;\n        dx = px - n->x; dy = py - n->y; dz = pz - n->z;\n        dist_mm = (int)(sqrtf(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz) * 1000.0f);\n        radius_mm = (int)(n->radius * 1000.0f);\n        if (!g_widget_rules.focus_ok(dist_mm, radius_mm, busy)) continue;\n        if (best < 0 || dist_mm < best_mm) { best = i; best_mm = dist_mm; }\n    }\n    if (best >= 0) {\n        c->focused = best;\n        c->focus_hold_ms = 250;   /* rules' widget-focus-prompt-ms */\n    } else {\n        if (c->focus_hold_ms > 0) c->focus_hold_ms -= (dt_ms > 0 ? dt_ms : 0);\n        if (c->focus_hold_ms <= 0) c->focused = -1;\n    }\n    return c->focused;\n}\n\n/* USE (F). A lever toggles and stays in the world; anything with a register opens its panel, which is\n * where a custom, script-driven affordance takes over (a terminal, a lift call panel, a centrifuge). */\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_use(WidgetCircuit *c) {\n    int idx;\n    if (!c || c->mode != WIDGET_MODE_WORLD) return c->mode;\n    idx = c->focused;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= c->count) return WIDGET_MODE_WORLD;\n    if (c->n[idx].kind == WIDGET_KIND_LEVER) {\n        widget_circuit_lever_toggle(c, idx);\n        return WIDGET_MODE_WORLD;\n    }\n    if (c->n[idx].reg >= 0) {\n        c->mode = WIDGET_MODE_PANEL;\n        c->pressed = idx;\n        return WIDGET_MODE_PANEL;\n    }\n    return WIDGET_MODE_WORLD;\n}\n\n/* Panel keys. Returns 1 if the panel consumed the key; BACK always closes and returns 1. A panel only\n * dials a value where a value makes sense (a machine setpoint); on a sensor it just displays. */\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_panel_key(WidgetCircuit *c, int key, int panel_max) {\n    WidgetNode *n;\n    if (!c || c->mode != WIDGET_MODE_PANEL || c->pressed < 0 || c->pressed >= c->count) return 0;\n    n = &c->n[c->pressed];\n    if (key == WIDGET_KEY_BACK) {\n        c->mode = WIDGET_MODE_WORLD;\n        c->pressed = -1;\n        return 1;\n    }\n    if (panel_max <= WIDGET_PANEL_MIN) panel_max = WIDGET_PANEL_MAX;\n    if (key == WIDGET_KEY_UP) {\n        n->reg_value = g_widget_rules.panel_key_adjust(n->reg_value, WIDGET_PANEL_STEP, WIDGET_PANEL_MIN, panel_max);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    if (key == WIDGET_KEY_DOWN) {\n        n->reg_value = g_widget_rules.panel_key_adjust(n->reg_value, -WIDGET_PANEL_STEP, WIDGET_PANEL_MIN, panel_max);\n        return 1;\n    }\n    if (key == WIDGET_KEY_USE || key == WIDGET_KEY_LEFT || key == WIDGET_KEY_RIGHT) return 1; /* consumed */\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/* The value a host copies into EduVM register `reg`. Returns -1 when no node owns that register, so a\n * caller can tell \"nothing here\" from \"this machine is at zero\". */\nstatic inline int widget_circuit_reg_value(const WidgetCircuit *c, int reg) {\n    if (!c || reg < 0) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++)\n        if (c->n[i].active && c->n[i].reg == reg) return c->n[i].reg_value;\n    return -1;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_WIDGET_CIRCUIT_H */\n"

  "content": "/* widget_circuit_test.c -- composable widget circuits, the F interface and panels, headless.\n *\n * The founder's ask is a composition system, so the checks are compositions, not single behaviours:\n * a lever into a delay into a machine, a plate into a transistor into a machine, an elevator as a\n * motor driven by a lever, and the register mirror a script would read. The rule curve is also checked\n * against the compiled-in defaults sample for sample, so the game and the module cannot disagree.\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"widget_circuit.h\"\n#include \"widget_rules_host.h\"\n\nstatic int g_fail = 0, g_checks = 0;\nstatic void ok(int cond, const char *what) {\n    g_checks++;\n    if (!cond) { g_fail++; printf(\"FAIL  %s\\n\", what); }\n    else printf(\"ok    %s\\n\", what);\n}\n\n/* lever(0) -> delay(1) -> motor(2), plus plate(3) -> transistor(4, gate = lever) -> motor(5) */\nstatic const char *LEVEL_JSON =\n    \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"LAB\\\",\\\"width\\\":20,\\\"height\\\":10,\\\"depth\\\":20,\\\"ground_plane_enabled\\\":true,\"\n    \"\\\"ground_plane_squares\\\":1,\\\"walls\\\":[],\"\n    \"\\\"edu_widgets\\\":[\"\n    \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"lever_a\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":6,\\\"memory_address\\\":10,\\\"x\\\":0,\\\"y\\\":0,\\\"z\\\":0,\\\"radius\\\":3},\"\n    \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"relay_b\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":7,\\\"memory_address\\\":11,\\\"x\\\":1,\\\"y\\\":0,\\\"z\\\":0,\"\n    \"\\\"input_pin\\\":0,\\\"delay_ticks\\\":4},\"\n    \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"lift_c\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":1,\\\"memory_address\\\":12,\\\"x\\\":2,\\\"y\\\":0,\\\"z\\\":0,\\\"input_pin\\\":1},\"\n    \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"plate_d\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":5,\\\"memory_address\\\":13,\\\"x\\\":3,\\\"y\\\":0,\\\"z\\\":0,\\\"radius\\\":2},\"\n    \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"gate_e\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":8,\\\"memory_address\\\":14,\\\"x\\\":4,\\\"y\\\":0,\\\"z\\\":0,\"\n    \"\\\"input_pin\\\":3,\\\"gate_pin\\\":0},\"\n    \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"door_f\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":2,\\\"memory_address\\\":15,\\\"x\\\":5,\\\"y\\\":0,\\\"z\\\":0,\\\"input_pin\\\":4}\"\n    \"]}\";\n\nint main(void) {\n    static CustomLevelData lvl;\n    static WidgetCircuit c;\n    int loaded;\n\n    ok(level_boxes_parse_json(LEVEL_JSON, &lvl), \"the level with wired widgets parses\");\n    ok(lvl.edu_widget_count == 6, \"all six widgets are authored (lever, delay, motor, plate, gate, door)\");\n    ok(lvl.edu_widgets[1].input_pin == 0 && lvl.edu_widgets[1].delay_ticks == 4,\n       \"a widget keeps its input pin and its own delay length\");\n    ok(lvl.edu_widgets[0].input_pin == -1, \"an unwired widget's pin is -1, not zero (which would be widget 0)\");\n\n    loaded = widget_circuit_load(&c, &lvl);\n    ok(loaded == 6, \"the circuit loads all six nodes\");\n    ok(c.n[0].kind == WIDGET_KIND_LEVER && c.n[1].kind == WIDGET_KIND_DELAY &&\n       c.n[2].kind == WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR && c.n[3].kind == WIDGET_KIND_PLATE &&\n       c.n[4].kind == WIDGET_KIND_TRANSISTOR && c.n[5].kind == WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR,\n       \"machine types map to the right circuit kinds\");\n\n    /* ---- a lever drives a delay which drives a machine --------------------------------------- */\n    ok(c.n[2].power == 0, \"the lift starts down\");\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[2].power == 0, \"and stays down with the lever off\");\n\n    ok(widget_circuit_lever_toggle(&c, 0) == wg_on(), \"flipping the lever puts it on 15\");\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[1].power == 0, \"the delay does not pass the lever through instantly\");\n    ok(c.n[1].timer_ticks > 0, \"the delay starts counting instead\");\n    for (int t = 0; t < 6; t++) widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    printf(\"      after the delay: relay %d, lift %d\\n\", c.n[1].power, c.n[2].power);\n    ok(c.n[1].power == wg_on(), \"the relay closes after its own delay\");\n    ok(c.n[2].power == wg_on(), \"and the machine downstream runs (lever -> delay -> motor)\");\n\n    /* the falling edge is delayed too: a relay, not a one-shot */\n    widget_circuit_lever_toggle(&c, 0);\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[1].power == wg_on(), \"switching the lever off does not drop the relay instantly\");\n    for (int t = 0; t < 6; t++) widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[1].power == 0 && c.n[2].power == 0, \"both edges are delayed, and the machine stops\");\n\n    /* ---- a plate through a transistor: a real AND ------------------------------------------- */\n    widget_circuit_lever_toggle(&c, 0);          /* lever back on: the gate's enable */\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    widget_circuit_set_plate(&c, 3, 0);\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[3].power == 0, \"an empty plate reads 0\");\n    ok(c.n[5].power == 0, \"so nothing reaches the door\");\n\n    widget_circuit_set_plate(&c, 3, 1);\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[3].power == wg_on(), \"standing on the plate powers it\");\n    ok(c.n[4].power == wg_on(), \"the transistor passes it (gate is on)\");\n    ok(c.n[5].power == wg_on(), \"and the door is powered: plate -> transistor -> door\");\n\n    widget_circuit_lever_toggle(&c, 0);          /* gate off, plate still pressed */\n    widget_circuit_tick(&c);\n    ok(c.n[3].power == wg_on() && c.n[4].power == 0,\n       \"with the gate off the transistor blocks it -- this is an AND, not a wire\");\n    ok(c.n[5].power == 0, \"so the door closes with someone still standing on the plate\");\n\n    /* ---- the register mirror a script reads -------------------------------------------------- */\n    printf(\"      registers: lever %d, relay %d, lift %d, gate %d, door %d\\n\",\n           widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 10), widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 11),\n           widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 12), widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 14),\n           widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 15));\n    ok(widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 10) == c.n[0].power, \"a register mirrors the node's live power\");\n    ok(widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 15) == 0, \"a closed door's register reads 0\");\n    ok(widget_circuit_reg_value(&c, 99) == -1, \"an unowned register reads -1, not a fake zero\");\n\n    /* ---- the F interface -------------------------------------------------------------------- */\n    {\n        WidgetCircuit f;\n        widget_circuit_load(&f, &lvl);\n        /* the camera-side busy flag suppresses the prompt entirely */\n        ok(widget_circuit_focus(&f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1, 16) == -1, \"no prompt while busy\");\n        ok(widget_circuit_focus(&f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16) == 0, \"standing on the lever focuses it\");\n        ok(widget_circuit_focus(&f, 900.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16) == -1, \"far away there is no focus\");\n        /* nearest wins: 1.0 away from the lever (reach 3) and 0.2 from the relay (default reach 3) */\n        {\n            int idx = widget_circuit_focus(&f, 0.8f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16);\n            printf(\"      focus at x=0.8 is widget %d (%s)\\n\", idx, idx >= 0 ? f.n[idx].id : \"-\");\n            ok(idx == 1, \"the closest widget in reach wins\");\n        }\n        /* hysteresis: stepping just out of reach keeps the prompt for a moment... */\n        f.n[1].radius = 1.0f;\n        widget_circuit_focus(&f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16);\n        widget_circuit_focus(&f, 500.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16);\n        ok(f.focused == 0 || f.focused == 1, \"the prompt holds its last focus instead of blinking off\");\n        /* ...and releases after the hold window */\n        for (int t = 0; t < 20; t++) widget_circuit_focus(&f, 500.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16);\n        ok(f.focused == -1, \"and it does go away once the player is really gone\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- panels: USE on a lever stays in the world, USE on a machine opens a panel ----------- */\n    {\n        WidgetCircuit p;\n        widget_circuit_load(&p, &lvl);\n        widget_circuit_focus(&p, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16);\n        ok(widget_circuit_use(&p) == WIDGET_MODE_WORLD, \"a lever is used in the world, no panel\");\n        ok(p.n[0].armed == wg_on(), \"and using it flipped it\");\n\n        widget_circuit_focus(&p, 2.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0, 16);\n        ok(widget_circuit_use(&p) == WIDGET_MODE_PANEL, \"a machine with a register opens a panel\");\n        ok(p.pressed == 2, \"the panel is the machine that was used\");\n\n        p.n[2].reg_value = 3000;\n        ok(widget_circuit_panel_key(&p, WIDGET_KEY_UP, 8000) == 1, \"UP is consumed by the panel\");\n        ok(p.n[2].reg_value == 3500, \"UP dials the setpoint up by one step\");\n        for (int t = 0; t < 40; t++) widget_circuit_panel_key(&p, WIDGET_KEY_UP, 8000);\n        ok(p.n[2].reg_value == 8000, \"a held key cannot dial past the panel's own maximum\");\n        for (int t = 0; t < 60; t++) widget_circuit_panel_key(&p, WIDGET_KEY_DOWN, 8000);\n        ok(p.n[2].reg_value == 0, \"nor below zero\");\n        ok(widget_circuit_panel_key(&p, WIDGET_KEY_BACK, 8000) == 1 && p.mode == WIDGET_MODE_WORLD,\n           \"BACK returns to the world\");\n        ok(p.pressed == -1, \"and the panel is released\");\n        ok(widget_circuit_panel_key(&p, WIDGET_KEY_UP, 8000) == 0,\n           \"keys in the world are not swallowed by a panel that is closed\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- the compiled defaults are PARENA's numbers ----------------------------------------- */\n    {\n        WidgetRules d = g_widget_rules;\n        int mismatches = 0, samples = 0;\n        widget_rules_install();\n        for (int kind = -1; kind <= 5; kind++)\n            for (int armed = 0; armed <= 15; armed += 5)\n                for (int src = 0; src <= 15; src += 5)\n                    for (int gate = 0; gate <= 15; gate += 5) {\n                        samples++;\n                        if (d.output_power(kind, armed, src, gate) != widget_output_power(kind, armed, src, gate))\n                            mismatches++;\n                    }\n        printf(\"      PARENA vs compiled defaults: %d samples, %d mismatches\\n\", samples, mismatches);\n        ok(mismatches == 0, \"the module and the header defaults are the same circuit\");\n        ok(widget_kind_count() == 5, \"five node kinds\");\n        ok(widget_delay_default_ticks() == 30 && widget_max_power() == 15, \"the same delay and power range\");\n        ok(widget_focus_prompt_ms() > 0, \"the prompt hysteresis window is real\");\n    }\n\n    /* ---- malformed wiring degrades to \"does nothing\" ---------------------------------------- */\n    {\n        static CustomLevelData bad;\n        static WidgetCircuit bc;\n        const char *json =\n            \"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"BAD\\\",\\\"width\\\":4,\\\"height\\\":4,\\\"depth\\\":4,\\\"walls\\\":[],\\\"edu_widgets\\\":[\"\n            \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"m\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":1,\\\"memory_address\\\":1,\\\"input_pin\\\":5},\"\n            \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":6,\\\"memory_address\\\":2},\"\n            \"{\\\"entity_id\\\":\\\"junk\\\",\\\"machine_type\\\":42,\\\"memory_address\\\":3}]}\";\n        ok(level_boxes_parse_json(json, &bad), \"a level with bad wiring still parses\");\n        ok(bad.edu_widget_count == 1, \"the empty id and the unknown machine type are dropped\");\n        widget_circuit_load(&bc, &bad);\n        ok(bc.n[0].input_pin == -1, \"a pin past the end of the list is dropped, never followed\");\n        widget_circuit_tick(&bc);\n        ok(bc.n[0].power == 0, \"so a mis-wired machine simply does nothing\");\n    }\n\n    printf(\"\\n%d checks, %d failed\\n\", g_checks, g_fail);\n    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;\n}\n"
}

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/docs/WIDGET_AFFORDANCES.md",
  "instructions": "Add the agent-facing widget affordance recipe.",
  "content": "# Widget affordances: how to make a thing in the world do something\n\nThis is the contract to build against. If you are an agent asked to \"bring the lab equipment to life\",\n\"add a security terminal\", \"make an elevator\", or \"add a light switch\", you do not write a new system.\nYou place widgets, wire them, and (optionally) drive them from an EduVM script.\n\nEverything below already exists and is tested. Nothing here needs a new renderer.\n\n## 1. The wire format (level JSON, `edu_widgets`)\n\n```json\n{\n  \"entity_id\": \"lever_a\",\n  \"machine_type\": 6,\n  \"memory_address\": 10,\n  \"x\": 0, \"y\": 0, \"z\": 0,\n  \"radius\": 3,\n  \"input_pin\": -1,\n  \"gate_pin\": -1,\n  \"delay_ticks\": 0,\n  \"box_index\": -1\n}\n```\n\n| key | meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `entity_id` | the script-visible name (`set_state(\"lever_a\", 1)`), max 31 chars, must be unique |\n| `machine_type` | what the node **is**, see the table below |\n| `memory_address` | the EduVM register its live value is mirrored into; `-1` = not scripted |\n| `x,y,z` / `radius` | where it stands and how close a player must be for the F prompt |\n| `input_pin` / `gate_pin` | index **into this same array** of the widget feeding it; `-1` = none |\n| `delay_ticks` | a DELAY's own length in 60 Hz ticks; `0` = the default half-second relay |\n| `box_index` | for geometry machines: which authored box it raises/lowers; `-1` = register only |\n\n**Pins must point at lower indices.** The circuit is evaluated once per tick in authoring order, so a\nnode reads values already computed this tick. A pin pointing forward (or at itself, or past the end)\nis dropped to `-1` at load: a mis-wired level degrades to \"that switch does nothing\", never to a\nfeedback loop.\n\n## 2. The five kinds\n\n| `machine_type` | kind | behaves as |\n|---|---|---|\n| `6` | LEVER | a light switch. F toggles it, it stays. 0 or 15, no wiring needed. |\n| `5` | PLATE | a pressure plate. The **host** writes it from bodies standing on it; a script cannot forge one. |\n| `7` | DELAY | a relay. Output follows input `delay_ticks` later, **both edges**. |\n| `8` | TRANSISTOR | a real AND. Passes its input only while its `gate_pin` is powered. |\n| `1`–`4` | MACHINE | a motor: gate, bridge, portal, crate, terminal, lift car. Follows its input. |\n\nPower is one integer, **0..15**, the same tier range DEADWEIGHT's cables use. A whole level is a byte\nper node, and any node can drive any other.\n\n## 3. Recipes\n\n**Light switch** — one LEVER at the wall, `memory_address` if a script cares. Done.\n\n**Security door** — PLATE (`radius` 2–3) → TRANSISTOR → MACHINE(2), with a second LEVER wired to the\ntransistor's `gate_pin` as the \"unlocked\" switch. Step on the plate with the gate off and nothing\nhappens: that is the whole point of the transistor.\n\n**Elevator** — LEVER (call button) → DELAY (`delay_ticks` 45, so the car does not lurch) →\nMACHINE(2) with `box_index` set to the platform. An elevator is literally a widget of widgets: the\nlever is the button, the delay is the door-closing pause, the machine is the car.\n\n**Lab centrifuge (\"the spiny thing\")** — PLATE → MACHINE(1) with `memory_address` 14. The warp drives\nthe spin from the register; the panel below sets the RPM.\n\n**Terminal** — MACHINE(1) with a `memory_address` and no `box_index`. F opens its panel (section 4);\nESC closes it and hands the world back.\n\n## 4. The F interface (already implemented in `packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h`)\n\n- `widget_circuit_focus(c, x, y, z, busy, dt_ms)` → the nearest in-reach widget, or `-1`. `busy`\n  (panel open, in a vehicle, cutscene) suppresses the prompt. The prompt holds its last focus for\n  ~250 ms so it does not strobe as you walk along a shelf of levers.\n- `widget_circuit_use(c)` → on a LEVER, toggles and stays in the world; on anything with a register,\n  opens its **PANEL** (`WIDGET_MODE_PANEL`) — this is the \"custom programmed affordance\" handoff.\n- `widget_circuit_panel_key(c, key, panel_max)` → UP/DOWN dial a setpoint by 500 per press, clamped to\n  `0..panel_max`; USE/LEFT/RIGHT are consumed and do nothing yet (reserved for tabs); BACK closes and\n  returns `1`. Keys in the world are never swallowed by a closed panel.\n- `widget_circuit_reg_value(c, reg)` → what a host copies into EduVM, or `-1` if no node owns it.\n\n## 5. EduVM\n\nEvery node mirrors its live value into `reg_value` each tick, and a panel writes that same value. So a\nscript and the physical circuit never hold two copies of the world:\n\n```pascal\n// slot 8: poll the plate, hold the gate open while someone is on it\nwhile (1) {\n    if (read_sensor(13) > 0) { set_reg(10, 1); } else { set_reg(10, 0); }\n    sleep(1);\n}\n```\n\nWidget values are written by the host with `edu_widget_host_set`, so a script can read a sensor but\ncannot forge one. That asymmetry is deliberate: a security door that a script can claim is open is not\na door.\n\n## 6. What is NOT built (do not pretend otherwise)\n\n- **No drawing.** There is no prompt quad, no panel rendering, no lever/centrifuge mesh. The circuit is\n  headless; a renderer pass reads `mode`, `pressed`, `focused` and `reg_value` and draws what it likes.\n- **Not in the game loop yet.** `widget_circuit_tick` is driven by `make test-widget-circuit`. Wiring it\n  to a scene (load on level load, tick once per frame, feed plates from player positions, install the\n  PARENA rules at startup) is the next step.\n- **No editor UI for wiring.** The NOCK/level-editor affordance is a table of pins in the JSON; adding\n  a visual wire tool in IDUNA's editor or `tools/nock_editor.html` is a separate slice.\n- **No back-EMF / overload.** DEADWEIGHT's circuit-burn mechanics are not modelled: power is a plain\n  0..15 integer with no heat, no fuses, no cascading failure.\n"

      /* widget_rules.h -- composable widget circuits, with built-in defaults.
       *
       * The numbers and the boolean rules live in PARENA (PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/widget_rules.prn, generated
       * into widget_rules.c by `make regen-widget-rules`, installed through widget_rules_host.h). This header
       * carries matching C defaults so packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h keeps working in every binary
       * and test that includes it without linking a generated file -- the same arrangement slide_rules.h and
       * drone_flight.h use, and the circuit test asserts the two curves agree.
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_H
      #define SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_H
      
      typedef struct {
          int (*output_power)(int kind, int armed, int src_power, int gate_power);
          int (*delay_armed)(int src_power, int armed, int timer_ticks);   /* == PARENA's arg order */
          int (*delay_still_running)(int timer_ticks);
          int (*lever_toggle)(int power);
          int (*plate_power)(int occupants);
          int (*motor_target)(int power);
          int (*focus_ok)(int dist_mm, int radius_mm, int busy);
          int (*panel_key_adjust)(int value, int delta, int lo, int hi);
          int (*delay_default_ticks)(void);
          int (*delay_min_ticks)(void);
          int (*delay_max_ticks)(void);
      } WidgetRules;
      
      static inline int wg_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }
      static inline int wg_on(void) { return 15; }
      static inline int wg_off(void) { return 0; }
      
      static inline int wg_c_output_power(int kind, int armed, int src, int gate) {
          if (kind == 0) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed);          /* lever */
          if (kind == 1) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed);          /* plate */
          if (kind == 2) return wg_clamp(0, 15, armed);          /* delay: holds its own pulse */
          if (kind == 3) return wg_clamp(0, 15, gate) > 0 ? wg_clamp(0, 15, src) : 0;  /* transistor */
          return wg_clamp(0, 15, src);                            /* motor follows its input */
      }
      /* A relay: a CHANGE in the input starts the timer, both edges. (The first draft delayed only the
       * rising edge and took its arguments in a different order from PARENA -- both were bugs, and the
       * host calling this with (src, armed, timer) is what exposed the second one.) */
      static inline int wg_c_delay_armed(int src, int armed, int timer) {
          if (wg_clamp(0, 15, src) == wg_clamp(0, 15, armed)) return 0;
          return timer <= 0 ? 1 : 0;
      }
      static inline int wg_c_delay_running(int timer) { return timer > 0 ? 1 : 0; }
      static inline int wg_c_lever_toggle(int power) { return wg_clamp(0, 15, power) > 0 ? wg_off() : wg_on(); }
      static inline int wg_c_plate_power(int occupants) { return wg_clamp(0, 8, occupants) > 0 ? wg_on() : wg_off(); }
      static inline int wg_c_motor_target(int power) { return wg_clamp(0, 15, power) > 0 ? 1 : 0; }
      static inline int wg_c_focus_ok(int dist_mm, int radius_mm, int busy) {
          if (busy == 1) return 0;
          if (wg_clamp(0, 1000000, radius_mm) <= 0) return 0;
          return wg_clamp(0, 1000000, dist_mm) <= wg_clamp(0, 1000000, radius_mm) ? 1 : 0;
      }
      static inline int wg_c_panel_adjust(int value, int delta, int lo, int hi) {
          return wg_clamp(wg_clamp(-1000000, 1000000, lo), wg_clamp(-1000000, 1000000, hi), value + delta);
      }
      static inline int wg_c_delay_default(void) { return 30; }
      static inline int wg_c_delay_min(void) { return 1; }
      static inline int wg_c_delay_max(void) { return 600; }
      
      static WidgetRules g_widget_rules = {
          wg_c_output_power, wg_c_delay_armed, wg_c_delay_running, wg_c_lever_toggle, wg_c_plate_power,
          wg_c_motor_target, wg_c_focus_ok, wg_c_panel_adjust, wg_c_delay_default, wg_c_delay_min, wg_c_delay_max
      };
      
      static inline void widget_set_rules(const WidgetRules *r) { if (r) g_widget_rules = *r; }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_H */
