           * fresh clock seeded per match for MODE_STORY/MODE_STORY_CAVE only -- every other mode leaves
           * story_clock zeroed (from the memset above) and never reads it authoritatively, see
           * apps/lobby's own render-loop doc comment for the real per-mode fallback story. Reset per
           * entry is a deliberate change from an earlier "one persistent, whole-session instance"
           * exception this clock used to be -- now consistent with every other ServerState field this
           * function already resets (story_phase, story_boss, story_rift, ...). */
          if (mode == MODE_STORY || mode == MODE_STORY_CAVE || mode == MODE_ZOMBIES || mode == MODE_SURVIVAL) {
              day_night_clock_init(&local_state.story_clock, (unsigned int)time(NULL), 8);
          }
          story_clear_swarm();
      
          if (mode == MODE_TDMB || mode == MODE_HEADED_BOT) {
              num_players = 1 + TDMB_BLUE_BOTS + TDMB_RED_BOTS;
              local_state.scene_id = scene_random_tdmb_map();
              if (mode == MODE_HEADED_BOT) printf("[HEADED_BOT] random map selected: %s\n", scene_name_debug(local_state.scene_id));

          } else if (mode == MODE_CTFB) {

              printf("[CAVE] starting CAVE-001 endurance encounter\n");

      static void orb_save_slots(void) {
          static char json[EDU_MAX_SCRIPTS * (EDU_MAX_SCRIPT_TEXT * 2 + 160) + 8];
          EduScriptSystem *es = eduvm_system();
          int n = edu_snippets_serialize(es, json, (int)sizeof json);
          FILE *fp = n > 0 ? fopen(ORB_SLOTS_FILE, "wb") : NULL;
          if (fp) { fwrite(json, 1, (size_t)n, fp); fclose(fp); snprintf(es->run_status, sizeof es->run_status, "saved to %s", ORB_SLOTS_FILE); }
          else snprintf(es->run_status, sizeof es->run_status, "save FAILED");
      }
      
      static void orb_load_slots(void) {
          FILE *fp = fopen(ORB_SLOTS_FILE, "rb");
          if (!fp) return;
          static char json[EDU_MAX_SCRIPTS * (EDU_MAX_SCRIPT_TEXT * 2 + 160) + 8];
          size_t got = fread(json, 1, sizeof json - 1, fp);
          fclose(fp);
          json[got] = 0;
          static EduSnippet sn[EDU_MAX_SCRIPTS];
          int n = edu_snippets_parse(json, sn, EDU_MAX_SCRIPTS);
          edu_snippets_load_into(eduvm_system(), sn, n);
      }
      
      
      /* ---- programmable level widgets (NOCK `edu_widgets` -> EduVM) ----
       * Each authored widget is a named machine on one EduVM register. Scripts in the Architect's Orb drive them
       * (set_state/set_reg/read_sensor/read_state); this block is the host half: bind from the level, let PLATE
       * sensors read the players, move any attached box like a story door, draw the machines, E to open the Orb. */
      #define LOBBY_EDU_PLATE_DEFAULT_RADIUS 1.6f
      #define LOBBY_EDU_USE_RADIUS 3.5f
      static int g_edu_widget_box[EDU_MAX_WIDGETS];      /* box_index per widget slot, -1 none */
      static int g_edu_widget_applied[EDU_MAX_WIDGETS];  /* last state pushed to physics (-1 = never) */
      
      static const char *const EDU_TUTORIAL_SCRIPT =
          "let r = 2;\n"
          "while r < 5 {\n"
          "  if read_sensor(1) {\n"
          "    set_reg(r, 1);\n"
          "  }\n"
          "  r = r + 1;\n"
          "}\n"
          "print(read_sensor(1));\n";
      
      static void lobby_edu_install_template(void) {
          EduScriptSystem *es = eduvm_system();
          EduScriptSlot *sl = &es->slots[EDU_MAX_SCRIPTS - 1];
          snprintf(sl->name, sizeof sl->name, "Gate Sequencer");
          snprintf(sl->source, sizeof sl->source, "%s", EDU_TUTORIAL_SCRIPT);
          sl->source_len = (int)strlen(sl->source);
          sl->compile_ok = 0;
          es->active_slot = EDU_MAX_SCRIPTS - 1;
      }
      
      static void lobby_edu_widgets_init(const CustomLevelData *lvl) {
          eduvm_host_widgets_clear();
          for (int i = 0; i < EDU_MAX_WIDGETS; i++) { g_edu_widget_box[i] = -1; g_edu_widget_applied[i] = -1; }
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->edu_widget_count; i++) {
              const LevelEduWidget *w = &lvl->edu_widgets[i];
              float rad = w->radius > 0.0f ? w->radius : LOBBY_EDU_PLATE_DEFAULT_RADIUS;
              int slot = eduvm_host_widget_bind(w->entity_id, w->machine_type, w->initial_state, w->memory_address,
                                                w->x, w->y, w->z, rad);
              if (slot < 0) { SDL_Log("edu widget '%s' rejected (full, bad type, or register clash)", w->entity_id); continue; }
              g_edu_widget_box[slot] = w->box_index;
          }
          if (g_orb_seeded && eduvm_host_widget_count() > 0) lobby_edu_install_template();
      }
      
      static void lobby_edu_widgets_tick(void) {
          int n = eduvm_host_widget_count();
          for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
              const EduWidget *w = eduvm_host_widget_at(i);
              if (!w) continue;
              if (w->machine_type == EDU_WIDGET_PLATE) {
                  int on = 0;
                  for (int pi = 0; pi < MAX_CLIENTS && !on; pi++) {
                      const PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[pi];
                      if (!p->active || p->state == STATE_DEAD) continue;
                      float dx = p->x - w->x, dz = p->z - w->z, dy = p->y - w->y;
                      if (dx * dx + dz * dz <= w->radius * w->radius && dy > -2.0f && dy < 3.0f) on = 1;
                  }
                  eduvm_host_widget_set(w->id, on);
                  w = eduvm_host_widget_at(i);
              }
              if (g_edu_widget_box[i] >= 0 && g_edu_widget_applied[i] != w->state) {
                  phys_set_custom_level_box_y(g_edu_widget_box[i], w->state); /* state 1 = geometry moved away (open) */
                  g_edu_widget_applied[i] = w->state;
              }
          }
      }
      
      static const EduWidget *lobby_edu_nearest_widget(void) {
          const PlayerState *h = &local_state.players[0];
          const EduWidget *best = NULL;
          float bd = LOBBY_EDU_USE_RADIUS * LOBBY_EDU_USE_RADIUS;
          for (int i = 0; i < eduvm_host_widget_count(); i++) {
              const EduWidget *w = eduvm_host_widget_at(i);
              if (!w || w->machine_type == EDU_WIDGET_PLATE) continue;
              float dx = h->x - w->x, dy = h->y - w->y, dz = h->z - w->z;
              float d = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
              if (d <= bd) { bd = d; best = w; }
          }
          return best;
      }
      
      static void draw_edu_widgets(unsigned int now_ms) {
          int n = eduvm_host_widget_count();
          if (n <= 0) return;
          float t = (float)now_ms * 0.001f;
          glDisable(GL_TEXTURE_2D);
          for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
              const EduWidget *w = eduvm_host_widget_at(i);
              if (!w) continue;
              float r, g, b, h, sx, sz;
              if (w->machine_type == EDU_WIDGET_PLATE) {
                  r = w->state ? 0.3f : 0.55f; g = w->state ? 0.95f : 0.5f; b = w->state ? 0.4f : 0.2f;
                  h = w->state ? 0.04f : 0.1f; sx = sz = w->radius * 1.6f;
              } else {
                  r = w->state ? 0.25f : 0.95f; g = w->state ? 0.9f : 0.3f; b = w->state ? 0.55f : 0.35f;
                  h = 0.35f + 0.05f * sinf(t * 3.0f + (float)i); sx = sz = 0.35f;
              }
              float yoff = (w->machine_type == EDU_WIDGET_PLATE) ? 0.05f : 2.4f;
              glPushMatrix(); glTranslatef(w->x, w->y + yoff, w->z); glColor3f(r, g, b); draw_box(sx, h, sz); glPopMatrix();
          }
      }
      
      static int orb_available(void) {
          return app_state == STATE_GAME_LOCAL && local_state.game_mode != MODE_QUEUE;
      }

      #define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_ZONES 16 /* matches IDUNA/internal/shankpit.MaxLevelZones exactly */
      
      /* An author-placed programmable widget (NOCK `edu_widgets` array): a named machine bound to one EduVM
       * "hardware register", so a script typed into the Architect's Orb can drive the level
       * (set_state("door_gate_alpha", 1) / set_reg(1, 1) / read_sensor(2)). Pure data carrier like LevelZone --
       * packages/world stays education-independent; machine_type is a bare int that the lobby hands to
       * packages/education's EduWidgetType (1 GATE, 2 BRIDGE, 3 PORTAL, 4 CRATE, 5 PLATE/sensor). Not
       * story-mode-only (SHANKPIT/CLAUDE.md): usable in any mode. */
      typedef struct {
          char entity_id[32];
          int machine_type;
          int initial_state;   /* 0 closed/inactive, 1 open/active */
          int memory_address;  /* the register read_sensor/set_reg address */
          float x, y, z;
          float radius;        /* sensor reach for PLATE; 0 -> host default */
          int box_index;       /* GATE/BRIDGE: index into boxes[] this widget raises/lowers like a story door
                                  (physics + render); -1 = purely a register, no geometry attached */
          /* Composable circuit wiring (2026-10-31, founder: "the widgets need to be composible ... think light
           * switches, basic circuits, an elevator is a widget of widgets"). A widget can be a SOURCE (lever 6,
           * plate 5), a RELAY (delay 7), a GATE (transistor 8) or an ACTUATOR (1..4 machines), wired by the
           * index of the widget that feeds it. -1 = nothing wired. Pins must point at LOWER indices: the
           * circuit is evaluated in authoring order, once per tick (see packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h).
           * delay_ticks is a DELAY's own timer length in 60 Hz ticks; 0 = the default half-second relay. */
          int input_pin;
          int gate_pin;
          int delay_ticks;
      } LevelEduWidget;
      
      #define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS 16 /* == EDU_MAX_WIDGETS in packages/education/edu_bindings.h */
      
      typedef struct {
          char name[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAME];
          float width, height, depth; /* the editor's own real authored level dimensions -- NOT read
                                          back into any native bound today (same "authoring metadata,
                                          not native state" role BRAWLPIT's own width/height play for
                                          its 2D canvas) */
          /* S459-08: the level's own real, configurable ground plane (founder: "i want there to be a
             plane by default that the player collides with... configurable in terms of size... turn on
             able and off able per level") -- see physics.h's own g_custom_level_ground_plane_enabled
             doc comment for the real collision contract these feed into via phys_set_custom_level. */
          int ground_plane_enabled;
          int ground_plane_squares;
          LevelBox boxes[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX];
          int count;
          LevelBoxMaterial materials[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS];
          int material_count;
          LevelSpawner spawners[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_SPAWNERS]; /* S459-58 */
          int spawner_count;
          LevelBuggySpawn buggy_spawns[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_BUGGY_SPAWNS]; /* #464 */
          int buggy_spawn_count;
          LevelVehicleSpawn vehicle_spawns[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_VEHICLE_SPAWNS]; /* whole roster, by kind */
          int vehicle_spawn_count;
          LevelLabStation lab_stations[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_LAB_STATIONS]; /* SECTION 592 */
          int lab_station_count;
          LevelDoor doors[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_DOORS]; /* Story System Phase 1 */
          int door_count;
          LevelButton buttons[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_BUTTONS]; /* S485, REFLUX pub/sub */
          int button_count;
          LevelNavNode nav_nodes[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES]; /* S461-01/S464 */
          int nav_node_count;
          LevelCharacter characters[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_CHARACTERS]; /* S467 */
          int character_count;
          LevelExit level_exits[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_LEVEL_EXITS]; /* S473 */
          int level_exit_count;
          LevelZone zones[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_ZONES]; /* BIG_O engine merge phase 7c */
          int zone_count;
          LevelEduWidget edu_widgets[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS]; /* programmable widgets -> EduVM */
          int edu_widget_count;
          /* next_level_id (S473) -- 0 is the real "no next level" sentinel (matches this loader's own
             established "0/absent is a real, honest sentinel, not an error" convention elsewhere --

          int next_level_id;

      UserCmd client_create_cmd(float fwd, float str, float yaw, float pitch, int shoot, int jump, int crouch, int reload, int use, int ability, int secondary, int bike, int pheromone, int wpn_idx) {
          UserCmd cmd;
          memset(&cmd, 0, sizeof(UserCmd));
          cmd.sequence = ++net_cmd_seq; cmd.timestamp = SDL_GetTicks();
          cmd.yaw = yaw; cmd.pitch = pitch;
          cmd.fwd = fwd; cmd.str = str;
          if(shoot) cmd.buttons |= BTN_ATTACK; if(jump) cmd.buttons |= BTN_JUMP;
          if(crouch) cmd.buttons |= BTN_CROUCH;
          if(reload) cmd.buttons |= BTN_RELOAD;
          if(use) cmd.buttons |= BTN_USE;
          if(ability) cmd.buttons |= BTN_ABILITY_1;
          if(secondary) cmd.buttons |= BTN_ABILITY_2;
          if(bike) cmd.buttons |= BTN_VEHICLE_2;
          if(pheromone) cmd.buttons |= BTN_PHEROMONE;
          if(g_input_paint_next) cmd.buttons |= BTN_PAINT_NEXT;
          if(g_input_paint_prev) cmd.buttons |= BTN_PAINT_PREV;
          /* Real, found-live reconciliation bug (founder real-time: "reconciliation jitter including
             gun jitter gun to knife when a gun is equip"): cmd.weapon_idx was set AFTER this cmd got
             stored into client_cmd_hist (the reconciliation replay buffer, client_reconcile_local_player
             below) -- every historical command replayed on reconciliation therefore carried weapon_idx=0
             (WPN_KNIFE, memset's own zero default), regardless of the real equipped weapon.
             shankpit_apply_usercmd_inputs (net_sim.h) unconditionally applies cmd->weapon_idx during
             that replay, so every reconciliation event snapped the LOCALLY-PREDICTED weapon to knife an
             instant before the next real server snapshot corrected it back to the true weapon -- a real,
             visible flicker on every reconciliation, not an occasional edge case. Setting weapon_idx
             before the history store (not after) fixes the stored copy same as the returned one. */
          cmd.weapon_idx = wpn_idx;
          client_cmd_hist[cmd.sequence % CLIENT_RECON_HISTORY] = cmd;
          net_latest_seq_sent = cmd.sequence;
          return cmd;
      }
      
      static void client_apply_cmd_movement(PlayerState *p, const UserCmd *cmd, unsigned int now_ms) {
          if (!p || !cmd) return;
          int dash_before = p->dash_timer;
          shankpit_apply_usercmd_inputs(p, cmd);
          shankpit_simulate_movement_tick(p, now_ms);
          if (dash_before == 0 && p->dash_timer > 0) {
              net_dash_start_seq = cmd->sequence;
              net_dash_vx = p->dash_vx; net_dash_vy = p->dash_vy; net_dash_vz = p->dash_vz;
          }
      }

      EduWidget *edu_widget_find_reg(EduWorldState *w, int reg) {
          for (int i = 0; i < w->widget_count; i++)
              if (w->widgets[i].active && w->widgets[i].reg == reg) return &w->widgets[i];
          return NULL;
      }
      
      int edu_widget_bind(EduWorldState *w, const char *id, int machine_type, int initial_state, int reg,
                          float x, float y, float z, float radius) {
          if (!id || !id[0] || strlen(id) >= EDU_WIDGET_ID_MAX) return -1;
          if (machine_type <= EDU_WIDGET_NONE || machine_type >= EDU_WIDGET_TYPE_COUNT) return -1;
          EduWidget *e = edu_widget_find_id(w, id);
          EduWidget *clash = edu_widget_find_reg(w, reg);
          if (clash && clash != e) return -1; /* two widgets on one register would make read_sensor ambiguous */
          if (!e) {
              if (w->widget_count >= EDU_MAX_WIDGETS) return -1;
              e = &w->widgets[w->widget_count++];
          }
          memset(e, 0, sizeof *e);
          e->active = 1;
          snprintf(e->id, sizeof e->id, "%s", id);
          e->machine_type = machine_type;
          e->initial_state = initial_state ? 1 : 0;
          e->state = e->initial_state;
          e->reg = reg;
          e->x = x; e->y = y; e->z = z; e->radius = radius;
          return (int)(e - w->widgets);
      }
      
      void edu_widgets_clear(EduWorldState *w) {
          memset(w->widgets, 0, sizeof w->widgets);
          w->widget_count = 0;
      }
      
      void edu_widgets_reset(EduWorldState *w) {
          for (int i = 0; i < w->widget_count; i++) w->widgets[i].state = w->widgets[i].initial_state;
      }
      
      int edu_widget_host_set(EduWorldState *w, const char *id, int state) {
          EduWidget *e = edu_widget_find_id(w, id);
          if (!e) return 0;
          e->state = state ? 1 : 0;
          return 1;
      }
      
      void world_objects_tick(EduWorldState *w, unsigned int now_ms) {
          float dt = 0.016f;
          if (w->entity_tick_last_ms > 0 && now_ms > w->entity_tick_last_ms) {
              dt = (float)(now_ms - w->entity_tick_last_ms) / 1000.0f;
              if (dt > 0.1f) dt = 0.1f;
          }
          w->entity_tick_last_ms = now_ms;
      
          for (int i = 0; i < w->entity_count; i++) {
              Entity *e = &w->entities[i];
              if (e->frozen) continue;
              e->vy -= 9.8f * dt;
              e->x += e->vx * dt;
              e->y += e->vy * dt;
              e->z += e->vz * dt;
              if (e->y < 0.0f) {
                  e->y = 0.0f;
                  if (e->vy < 0.0f) e->vy = 0.0f;
              }
          }
      
          if (w->entity_count == 0 && (w->crate_x != 0 || w->crate_speed != 0)) {
              int id = world_spawn_entity(w, "crate", (float)w->crate_x, 0.0f, 0.0f);
              Entity *e = world_find_entity(w, id);
              if (e) e->vx = (float)w->crate_speed;
          }
          Entity *crate = world_find_entity(w, 0);
          if (crate && crate->type == EDU_ENTITY_PROP_CRATE) {
              w->crate_x = (int)crate->x;
              w->crate_speed = (int)crate->vx;
          }
      }

      /* widget_circuit_test.c -- composable widget circuits, the F interface and panels, headless.
       *
       * The founder's ask is a composition system, so the checks are compositions, not single behaviours:
       * a lever into a delay into a machine, a plate into a transistor into a machine, an elevator as a
       * motor driven by a lever, and the register mirror a script would read. The rule curve is also checked
       * against the compiled-in defaults sample for sample, so the game and the module cannot disagree.
       */
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      #include "widget_circuit.h"
      #include "widget_rules_host.h"
      
      static int g_fail = 0, g_checks = 0;
      static void ok(int cond, const char *what) {
          g_checks++;
          if (!cond) { g_fail++; printf("FAIL  %s\n", what); }
          else printf("ok    %s\n", what);
      }
      
      /* lever(0) -> delay(1) -> motor(2), plus plate(3) -> transistor(4, gate = lever) -> motor(5) */
      static const char *LEVEL_JSON =
          "{\"name\":\"LAB\",\"width\":20,\"height\":10,\"depth\":20,\"ground_plane_enabled\":true,"
          "\"ground_plane_squares\":1,\"walls\":[],"
          "\"edu_widgets\":["
          "{\"entity_id\":\"lever_a\",\"machine_type\":6,\"memory_address\":10,\"x\":0,\"y\":0,\"z\":0,\"radius\":3},"
          "{\"entity_id\":\"relay_b\",\"machine_type\":7,\"memory_address\":11,\"x\":1,\"y\":0,\"z\":0,"
          "\"input_pin\":0,\"delay_ticks\":4},"
          "{\"entity_id\":\"lift_c\",\"machine_type\":1,\"memory_address\":12,\"x\":2,\"y\":0,\"z\":0,\"input_pin\":1},"
          "{\"entity_id\":\"plate_d\",\"machine_type\":5,\"memory_address\":13,\"x\":3,\"y\":0,\"z\":0,\"radius\":2},"
          "{\"entity_id\":\"gate_e\",\"machine_type\":8,\"memory_address\":14,\"x\":4,\"y\":0,\"z\":0,"
          "\"input_pin\":3,\"gate_pin\":0},"
          "{\"entity_id\":\"door_f\",\"machine_type\":2,\"memory_address\":15,\"x\":5,\"y\":0,\"z\":0,\"input_pin\":4}"
          "]}";
      
      int main(void) {
          static CustomLevelData lvl;
          static WidgetCircuit c;
          int loaded;
      
          ok(level_boxes_parse_json(LEVEL_JSON, &lvl), "the level with wired widgets parses");
          ok(lvl.edu_widget_count == 6, "all six widgets are authored (lever, delay, motor, plate, gate, door)");
          ok(lvl.edu_widgets[1].input_pin == 0 && lvl.edu_widgets[1].delay_ticks == 4,
             "a widget keeps its input pin and its own delay length");
          ok(lvl.edu_widgets[0].input_pin == -1, "an unwired widget's pin is -1, not zero (which would be widget 0)");
      
          loaded = widget_circuit_load(&c, &lvl);
          ok(loaded == 6, "the circuit loads all six nodes");
          ok(c.n[0].kind == WIDGET_KIND_LEVER && c.n[1].kind == WIDGET_KIND_DELAY &&
             c.n[2].kind == WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR && c.n[3].kind == WIDGET_KIND_PLATE &&
             c.n[4].kind == WIDGET_KIND_TRANSISTOR && c.n[5].kind == WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR,
             "machine types map to the right circuit kinds");
      
          /* ---- a lever drives a delay which drives a machine --------------------------------------- */
          ok(c.n[2].power == 0, "the lift starts down");
          widget_circuit_tick(&c);
          ok(c.n[2].power == 0, "and stays down with the lever off");
      
          ok(widget_circuit_lever_toggle(&c, 0) == wg_on(), "flipping the lever puts it on 15");
          widget_circuit_tick(&c);

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/mk/widget_rules.mk
  content: |
      # mk/widget_rules.mk -- composable widget circuits (2026-10-31).
      #
      # Founder: "the widgets need to be composible ... think light switches, basic circuits, an elevator is a
      # widget of widgets ... bring in edu vm script it all needs to play nice with that interpreter".
      # The circuit's rules live in PARENA; packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h runs them and mirrors every
      # node's value into an EduVM register.
      
      .PHONY: regen-widget-rules test-widget-circuit
      
      regen-widget-rules:
        scripts/gen_widget_rules.sh
      
      # test-widget-circuit -- compositions, not single behaviours: lever -> delay -> motor, plate -> transistor
      # -> door (a real AND), the register mirror a script reads, the F prompt's proximity/hysteresis, and a
      # panel that dials a setpoint without swallowing keys once closed.
      test-widget-circuit: | $(BIN_DIR)
        # gnu99, not c99: level_boxes.h uses POSIX popen/pclose (the level fetch helpers), which a strict
        # c99 build hides -- every other level test in this repo builds gnu99 for the same reason.
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ipackages/simulation -Ipackages/world \
          packages/simulation/widget_circuit_test.c packages/simulation/widget_rules.c \
          -o $(BIN_DIR)/widget_circuit_test $(LIBS_M)
        ./$(BIN_DIR)/widget_circuit_test
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/world/level_boxes_edu_widgets_test.c
  content: |
      /* level_boxes_edu_widgets_test.c -- the NOCK "edu_widgets" level schema.
       *   gcc -Wall -Wextra -O2 -o /tmp/lbew packages/world/level_boxes_edu_widgets_test.c && /tmp/lbew */
      #include "level_boxes.h"
      #include <assert.h>
      #include <stdio.h>
      
      int main(void) {
          static CustomLevelData lvl;
          const char *json =
              "{\"name\":\"T\",\"width\":40,\"height\":10,\"depth\":40,\"ground_plane_enabled\":true,\"ground_plane_squares\":1,"
              "\"walls\":[{\"x\":0,\"y\":2,\"z\":16,\"sx\":6,\"sy\":4,\"sz\":1},{\"x\":0,\"y\":2,\"z\":24,\"sx\":6,\"sy\":4,\"sz\":1}],"
              "\"edu_widgets\":["
              "{\"entity_id\":\"plate_a\",\"machine_type\":5,\"initial_state\":0,\"memory_address\":1,\"x\":0,\"y\":0,\"z\":8,\"radius\":1.5},"
              "{\"entity_id\":\"door_gate_alpha\",\"machine_type\":1,\"initial_state\":0,\"memory_address\":2,\"x\":0,\"y\":2,\"z\":16,\"box_index\":0},"
              "{\"entity_id\":\"\",\"machine_type\":1,\"memory_address\":3},"
              "{\"entity_id\":\"badtype\",\"machine_type\":42,\"memory_address\":4},"
              "{\"entity_id\":\"far_box\",\"machine_type\":2,\"memory_address\":5,\"box_index\":99}"
              "]}";
          assert(level_boxes_parse_json(json, &lvl));
          assert(lvl.count == 2);
          /* entries 3 (empty id) and 4 (type 42) are dropped, not half-loaded */
          assert(lvl.edu_widget_count == 3);
          assert(strcmp(lvl.edu_widgets[0].entity_id, "plate_a") == 0 && lvl.edu_widgets[0].machine_type == 5);
          assert(lvl.edu_widgets[0].memory_address == 1 && lvl.edu_widgets[0].z == 8.0f && lvl.edu_widgets[0].radius == 1.5f);
          assert(lvl.edu_widgets[0].box_index == -1);
          assert(strcmp(lvl.edu_widgets[1].entity_id, "door_gate_alpha") == 0 && lvl.edu_widgets[1].box_index == 0);
          assert(strcmp(lvl.edu_widgets[2].entity_id, "far_box") == 0 && lvl.edu_widgets[2].box_index == -1); /* out-of-range box -> detached */
          printf("PASS: edu_widgets parsed, malformed entries skipped, bad box_index detached\n");
      
          const char *none = "{\"name\":\"B\",\"width\":10,\"height\":10,\"depth\":10,\"ground_plane_enabled\":true,\"ground_plane_squares\":1,\"walls\":[]}";
          assert(level_boxes_parse_json(none, &lvl) && lvl.edu_widget_count == 0);
          printf("PASS: a level with no edu_widgets key has none\n");
      
          /* the 17th widget is ignored, never overflows */
          char big[4096]; int n = snprintf(big, sizeof big, "{\"name\":\"C\",\"width\":1,\"height\":1,\"depth\":1,\"walls\":[],\"edu_widgets\":[");
          for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) n += snprintf(big + n, sizeof big - n, "%s{\"entity_id\":\"w%d\",\"machine_type\":1,\"memory_address\":%d}", i ? "," : "", i, i);
          snprintf(big + n, sizeof big - n, "]}");
          assert(level_boxes_parse_json(big, &lvl) && lvl.edu_widget_count == LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS);
          printf("PASS: widget count is capped at %d\n", LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS);
          return 0;
      }

Kept to three floats so the host can fill a stack array from\n * PlayerState without this package depending on protocol.h. */\ntypedef struct {\n    float x, y, z;\n} WidgetActor;\n\n/* value is the node's live register: circuit power 0..15, or a panel-dialled setpoint. */\ntypedef void (*WidgetRuntimeRegSink)(void *user, const char *id, int reg, int value);\n/* open is 1 when the machine is powered. Called only when the box's state changes. */\ntypedef void (*WidgetRuntimeBoxSink)(void *user, int box_index, int open);\n\ntypedef struct {\n    WidgetCircuit c;\n    int box[WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX];       /* authored box per node, -1 = register only */\n    int box_open[WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX];  /* last pushed state, -1 = never pushed */\n    int reg_seen[WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX];  /* last mirrored value, -1 = never mirrored */\n} WidgetRuntime;\n\nstatic inline const char *widget_runtime_kind_name(int kind) {\n    switch (kind) {\n        case WIDGET_KIND_LEVER: return \"LEVER\";\n        case WIDGET_KIND_PLATE: return \"PLATE\";\n        case WIDGET_KIND_DELAY: return \"RELAY\";\n        case WIDGET_KIND_TRANSISTOR: return \"GATE\";\n        case WIDGET_KIND_MOTOR: return \"MACHINE\";\n        default: return \"SCENERY\";\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline void widget_runtime_init(WidgetRuntime *rt) {\n    if (!rt) return;\n    memset(rt, 0, sizeof *rt);\n    widget_circuit_init(&rt->c);\n    for (int i = 0; i < WIDGET_CIRCUIT_MAX; i++) {\n        rt->box[i] = -1;\n        rt->box_open[i] = -1;\n        rt->reg_seen[i] = -1;\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_find(const WidgetRuntime *rt, const char *id) {\n    if (!rt || !id || !id[0]) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < rt->c.count; i++)\n        if (rt->c.n[i].active && strcmp(rt->c.n[i].id, id) == 0) return i;\n    return -1;\n}\n\n/* Loads a level's nodes and re-attaches each one's authored box BY ID. The circuit drops malformed\n * widgets, so a positional copy of box_index would silently shift every box after the dropped one. */\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_load(WidgetRuntime *rt, const CustomLevelData *lvl) {\n    int loaded;\n    if (!rt) return 0;\n    widget_runtime_init(rt);\n    if (!lvl) return 0;\n    loaded = widget_circuit_load(&rt->c, lvl);\n    for (int i = 0; i < lvl->edu_widget_count; i++) {\n        int idx = widget_runtime_find(rt, lvl->edu_widgets[i].entity_id);\n        if (idx >= 0) rt->box[idx] = lvl->edu_widgets[i].box_index;\n    }\n    return loaded;\n}\n\n/* Does the circuit own this box? A host that also has a legacy per-widget door path uses this to stay\n * out of the way: two systems writing one box is how a lift ends up half-open. */\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_owns_box(const WidgetRuntime *rt, int box_index) {\n    if (!rt || box_index < 0) return 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < rt->c.count; i++)\n        if (rt->box[i] == box_index) return 1;\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/* One tick: plates from the actors, then the circuit, then the two sinks on change. Returns how many\n * machines moved, so a caller can tell a quiet level from a working one without reading the sinks. */\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_tick(WidgetRuntime *rt, const WidgetActor *actors, int count,\n                                      WidgetRuntimeRegSink reg_sink, WidgetRuntimeBoxSink box_sink,\n                                      void *user) {\n    int moved = 0;\n    if (!rt || rt->c.count <= 0) return 0;\n    if (count < 0 || !actors) count = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < rt->c.count; i++) {\n        WidgetNode *n = &rt->c.n[i];\n        int occupants = 0;\n        if (n->kind != WIDGET_KIND_PLATE) continue;\n        for (int a = 0; a < count; a++) {\n            float dx = actors[a].x - n->x;\n            float dz = actors[a].z - n->z;\n            float dy = actors[a].y - n->y;\n            if (dx * dx + dz * dz <= n->radius * n->radius && dy > -2.0f && dy < 3.0f) occupants++;\n        }\n        widget_circuit_set_plate(&rt->c, i, occupants);\n    }\n    widget_circuit_tick(&rt->c);\n    for (int i = 0; i < rt->c.count; i++) {\n        WidgetNode *n = &rt->c.n[i];\n        if (n->reg >= 0 && n->reg_value != rt->reg_seen[i]) {\n            rt->reg_seen[i] = n->reg_value;\n            if (reg_sink) reg_sink(user, n->id, n->reg, n->reg_value);\n        }\n        if (rt->box[i] >= 0) {\n            int open = n->power > 0 ? 1 : 0;\n            if (open != rt->box_open[i]) {\n                rt->box_open[i] = open;\n                if (box_sink) box_sink(user, rt->box[i], open);\n                moved++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return moved;\n}\n\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_focus(WidgetRuntime *rt, float x, float y, float z, int busy, int dt_ms) {\n    if (!rt) return -1;\n    return widget_circuit_focus(&rt->c, x, y, z, busy, dt_ms);\n}\n\n/* F. Returns 1 when it acted (a lever toggled in place, or a panel opened), 0 when there was nothing to\n * use -- the caller consumes its USE press only on 1, so a widget never eats the key from a vehicle. */\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_use(WidgetRuntime *rt) {\n    int idx, acted = 0;\n    if (!rt || rt->c.mode != WIDGET_MODE_WORLD) return 0;\n    idx = rt->c.focused;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= rt->c.count) return 0;\n    if (rt->c.n[idx].kind == WIDGET_KIND_LEVER) acted = 1;\n    else if (rt->c.n[idx].reg >= 0) acted = 1;\n    if (!acted) return 0;\n    widget_circuit_use(&rt->c);\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_panel_open(const WidgetRuntime *rt) {\n    return (rt && rt->c.mode == WIDGET_MODE_PANEL) ? 1 : 0;\n}\n\nstatic inline const WidgetNode *widget_runtime_panel_node(const WidgetRuntime *rt) {\n    if (!rt || rt->c.mode != WIDGET_MODE_PANEL) return NULL;\n    if (rt->c.pressed < 0 || rt->c.pressed >= rt->c.count) return NULL;\n    return &rt->c.n[rt->c.pressed];\n}\n\nstatic inline int widget_runtime_panel_key(WidgetRuntime *rt, int key) {\n    if (!rt) return 0;\n    return widget_circuit_panel_key(&rt->c, key, WIDGET_PANEL_MAX);\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RUNTIME_H */\n"
}

The circuit is now a thing players actually use, not a table a test drove.

## What changed

**`packages/simulation/widget_runtime.h` (new)** — the host half, deliberately free of GL, SDL, physics and the education package (the caller passes two sinks, `reg` and `box`):

- **Plates are fed from bodies.** Each tick the host hands over the actors in the world; every plate counts the ones inside its authored radius, with a vertical window so a body six units above a mat is not standing on it. A script can never forge a sensor; a player can.
- **Machines move real geometry.** A node with an authored `box_index` drives that box through `phys_set_custom_level_box_y` — the same moving box a story door uses — edge-triggered, so an idle level does no work and a held lever doesn't re-write the world every tick.
- **Registers are mirrored on change**, into `eduvm_host_widget_set`, so a script's `read_sensor(reg)` and the physical switch read one number.

**`apps/lobby` wiring** — loaded from `lobby_edu_widgets_init`, *the same loader every custom level uses*. That's the whole reachability answer: `lobby_start_zombies_mode` → `level_boxes_apply_to_physics` → `lobby_edu_widgets_init`, so **zombies, LAB and deathmatch all get the circuit** without a special path. The legacy per-widget box path now skips any box the circuit owns, so a relay's delay is real instead of two systems writing one lift.

**The F interface, end to end** — `F` on a focused widget is the general interface: a lever toggles in place and **consumes the press** (it can't also board a vehicle on the same key); anything with a register opens its **panel**. A panel freezes movement, dials UP/DOWN in 500s, and owns ESC — leaving a panel never drops you into the pause menu. `draw_widget_affordances` draws `[F] USE <id>` with kind and live power over the world, and a cyan-on-black card for the panel with power, register, setpoint and key legend.

## Bugs this caught

1. **A terminal's setpoint was clobbered by the tick that mirrored it.** `widget_circuit_tick` mirrored circuit power (0..15) into `reg_value` unconditionally, so a dialled 3500 became 0 (or 15) one tick later. Now a node carries `panel_value`/`panel_used`, the register reports the setpoint once dialled, and the first keypress dials from the machine's **live** value rather than the value it had when the panel opened.
2. **The first tick reported every machine as moving.** That's correct behaviour (the host authoritatively places each box where the author put it) but it wasn't stated — the test now asserts exactly that, once per box, instead of the old "nothing has moved" assumption.
3. My own fixture was wrong in an instructive way: `level_boxes.h` silently detaches a `box_index` that points past the level's geometry, so a machine in a level with no walls cannot drive anything. The test level got ten real walls.

## Checks actually run

- `make test-widget-runtime` → **48 checks, 0 failed**: lever → relay → lift doesn't move for four ticks and opens on the fifth, **and doesn't drop early on the falling edge**; a plate alone opens nothing while its transistor's gate lever is off, the same plate opens the security door once the gate is on, stepping off closes it; a body six units above the plate never presses it; the lift is undisturbed by plate traffic; F on a terminal opens its panel, three UPs make 1500, five ticks later the register still holds 1500 and the mirror fired **once, on the change**; BACK returns the world; a closed panel swallows nothing; busy suppresses the prompt and walking away releases it after the hold; a level with no widgets is a no-op.
- `make test-widget-circuit` → **51 checks, 0 failed** (still green after the setpoint change).
- `make check-windows` → **OK, 99 sources** (includes `main.c`, so the prompt/panel GL actually compiles for mingw).
- `make -B server` → exit 0 (prints the pre-existing `reflux_host_action_c_at` implicit-declaration warning).
- Committed as `91ef935` and pushed; `master...origin/master` clean, PARENA unchanged and still in sync.

**Not verified:** no live gameplay run — this box has no GPU or display, so the panel and prompt are compiled and their logic is tested, but nobody has looked at them on screen. Named gaps: no lever/centrifuge/terminal mesh (a node is still a box coloured by its power), no editor wiring UI beyond the pin fields, a panel setpoint is display-only to a script (EduVM's widget register is boolean by contract), and there's no widget packet — the circuit runs in the lobby's local simulation, so a server-authoritative match would draw the boxes without the interactions.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a dense but traversable expansion layout for the town scene."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path


def hash32(n: int) -> int:
    n = (n ^ 61) ^ (n >> 16)
    n = n + (n << 3)
    n = n ^ (n >> 4)
    n = (n * 0x27D4EB2D) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    n = n ^ (n >> 15)
    return n & 0xFFFFFFFF


def pick(seed: int, lo: float, hi: float) -> float:
    v = hash32(seed) / 0xFFFFFFFF
    return lo + (hi - lo) * v


def emit_layout(path: Path, *, blocks_x: int, blocks_z: int, spacing: float, margin: float, origin_x: float, origin_z: float) -> int:
    out = []
    out.append("/* Auto-generated by tools/world/generate_town_expansion.py */")
    out.append("/* clang-format off */")
    out.append("static const TownBuildingSeed g_expansion_seed_buildings[] = {")

    idx = 0
    for bz in range(blocks_z):
        for bx in range(blocks_x):
            cx = origin_x + bx * spacing
            cz = origin_z + bz * spacing

            if (bx % 5 == 0) or (bz % 4 == 0):
                continue

            district_tag = "TOWN_BLD_TAG_DISTRICT_MARKET"
            if bz >= blocks_z * 0.62:
                district_tag = "TOWN_BLD_TAG_DISTRICT_STADIUM"

  content: |
       * level has no zones at all, or none of them contain this point ("no zone authored here" is a
       * real, honest, non-fatal outcome -- the caller decides the fallback, matching level_exits'/
       * spawners' own "absent is honest, not an error" convention throughout this file). Overlapping
       * zones are a real, deliberate author error this function does not detect or warn about -- first
       * match wins, same as every other array-scan helper in this file. */
      /* ---- full-level JSON writer (local, IDUNA-free level authoring) ----------------------------
       * The reverse of level_boxes_parse_json: writes a complete level document in the same flat shape
       * IDUNA's export endpoint returns, so a level built offline in EDIT MAP (apps/lobby's F6) is a real
       * level JSON that this loader reads straight back. Every parsed field is written -- doors, buttons,
       * nav nodes, characters, exits, zones, edu widgets, lab stations, buggy spawns, brick damage -- which
       * is exactly why edit_map.h's op log existed before: a PARTIAL writer would silently drop those.
       */
      static inline void level_boxes_put_json_string(FILE *f, const char *s) {
          fputc('"', f);
          for (const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)(s ? s : ""); *p; p++) {
              switch (*p) {
              case '"':  fputs("\\\"", f); break;
              case '\\': fputs("\\\\", f); break;
              case '\n': fputs("\\n", f); break;
              case '\r': fputs("\\r", f); break;
              case '\t': fputs("\\t", f); break;
              default:   if (*p < 0x20) fputc(' ', f); else fputc((int)*p, f); break;
              }
          }
          fputc('"', f);
      }
      
      static inline void level_boxes_write_json(FILE *f, const CustomLevelData *lvl) {
          if (!f || !lvl) return;
          fprintf(f, "{\n \"version\": 1,\n \"name\": ");
          level_boxes_put_json_string(f, lvl->name[0] ? lvl->name : "Untitled");
          fprintf(f, ",\n \"width\": %.4g,\n \"height\": %.4g,\n \"depth\": %.4g",
                  (double)lvl->width, (double)lvl->height, (double)lvl->depth);
          fprintf(f, ",\n \"ground_plane_enabled\": %s,\n \"ground_plane_squares\": %d",
                  lvl->ground_plane_enabled ? "true" : "false", lvl->ground_plane_squares);
          fprintf(f, ",\n \"enclosed\": %s", lvl->enclosed ? "true" : "false");
          if (lvl->next_level_id) fprintf(f, ",\n \"next_level_id\": %d", lvl->next_level_id);
          if (lvl->floor_tinted)
              fprintf(f, ",\n \"floor_tint\": { \"r\": %.4g, \"g\": %.4g, \"b\": %.4g, \"a\": %.4g }",
                      (double)lvl->floor_r, (double)lvl->floor_g, (double)lvl->floor_b, (double)lvl->floor_a);
      
          fprintf(f, ",\n \"materials\": [");
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->material_count; i++) {
              const LevelBoxMaterial *m = &lvl->materials[i];
              fprintf(f, "%s\n  { \"name\": ", i ? "," : "");
              level_boxes_put_json_string(f, m->name);
              fprintf(f, ", \"shader_name\": ");
              level_boxes_put_json_string(f, m->shader_name[0] ? m->shader_name : "standard");
              fprintf(f, ", \"specular\": %.4g, \"shininess\": %.4g, \"friction\": %.4g, \"density\": %.4g }",
                      (double)m->specular, (double)m->shininess, (double)m->friction, (double)m->density);
          }
          fprintf(f, "\n ]");
      
          fprintf(f, ",\n \"walls\": [");
          for (int i = 0; i < lvl->count; i++) {
              const LevelBox *b = &lvl->boxes[i];
              const char *mat = (b->material_idx >= 0 && b->material_idx < lvl->material_count)
                                    ? lvl->materials[b->material_idx].name : LEVEL_BOXES_DEFAULT_MATERIAL;
              fprintf(f, "%s\n  { \"x\": %.4g, \"y\": %.4g, \"z\": %.4g, \"sx\": %.4g, \"sy\": %.4g, \"sz\": %.4g",
                      i ? "," : "", (double)b->x, (double)b->y, (double)b->z,
                      (double)b->w, (double)b->h, (double)b->d);
              fprintf(f, ", \"r\": %.4g, \"g\": %.4g, \"b\": %.4g, \"friction\": %.4g, \"material\": ",
                      (double)b->r, (double)b->g, (double)b->b, (double)b->friction);
              level_boxes_put_json_string(f, mat);
              if (b->rot_x != 0.0f) fprintf(f, ", \"rot_x\": %.4g", (double)b->rot_x);

- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/widget_rules.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit/widget_rules.prn -- composable world widgets: levers, plates, delays, gates, motors.
      ;;
      ;; Founder: "we already have a widget primative ... we need a way to tell our agent to generate rich
      ;; affordances via the widgets ... general interface like F to interact and then after that it needs to
      ;; be able to go into custom programmed affordances ... the main thing we are trying to do is bring the
      ;; lab equipment to life ... the widgets need to be composible ... think light switches, basic
      ;; circuits, an elevator is a widget of widgets ... bring in edu vm script it all needs to play nice
      ;; with that interpreter".
      ;;
      ;; So this module is the CIRCUIT, not the furniture. Everything a machine does is one of five node
      ;; kinds wired input -> output, evaluated in two phases per tick (sensors first, then propagation),
      ;; with every node's live value mirrored into an EduVM register so a script in the terminal can read
      ;; and drive the same circuit. No node knows what it looks like: a centrifuge is a motor, a lift is a
      ;; motor plus a lever, a security door is a plate into a transistor into a gate.
      ;;
      ;; Power is 0..15, one integer, exactly like DEADWEIGHT's cable tiers -- low enough that a whole level
      ;; fits in a byte per node and high enough to read a bar graph.
      ;;
      ;; All I32, total, no state. Retune here and `make regen-widget-rules`.
      (module shankpit/widget-rules)
      (export widget-kind-count widget-power-on widget-power-off widget-max-power
              widget-delay-default-ticks widget-delay-min-ticks widget-delay-max-ticks
              widget-output-power widget-delay-armed widget-delay-still-running
              widget-lever-toggle widget-plate-power widget-motor-target
              widget-focus-ok widget-focus-prompt-ms widget-panel-key-adjust)
      
      ;; 0 LEVER, 1 PLATE, 2 DELAY, 3 TRANSISTOR, 4 MOTOR
      (defn widget-kind-count [] : I32 5)
      (defn widget-power-on [] : I32 15)
      (defn widget-power-off [] : I32 0)
      (defn widget-max-power [] : I32 15)
      
      ;; Delay nodes count in ticks (60 = one second). The default is a half-second relay -- long enough to
      ;; see a signal arrive and leave, short enough to still feel like a switch.
      (defn widget-delay-default-ticks [] : I32 30)
      (defn widget-delay-min-ticks [] : I32 1)
      (defn widget-delay-max-ticks [] : I32 600)
      
      (defn w-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))
      
      ;; ---- the circuit ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; `armed` is the node's own latched output from the previous tick; for a lever that is its position,
      ;; for a delay it is the pulse it is currently holding. Everything else ignores it except the delay,
      ;; which is the one node whose output is not simply its input.
      ;;
      ;;   LEVER        outputs its own position (armed), regardless of input -- it is a source
      ;;   PLATE        outputs its own sensor reading (armed): the host writes it, a script cannot
      ;;   DELAY        outputs the pulse it is holding (armed); the host arms/clears it (see below)
      ;;   TRANSISTOR   passes input ONLY when the gate input is powered (a real AND, not a diode)
      ;;   MOTOR        follows its input: a lift, a centrifuge, a door -- whatever the level draws
      (defn widget-output-power [(kind : I32) (armed : I32) (src_power : I32) (gate_power : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 0) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)
          (if (= kind 1) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)
            (if (= kind 2) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)
              (if (= kind 3) (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 gate_power) 0) (w-clamp 0 15 src_power) 0)
                (w-clamp 0 15 src_power))))))
      
      ;; A delay line is a RELAY: its output follows its input, N ticks late. A CHANGE in the input starts
      ;; the timer (if it is not already counting); when the timer runs out the output takes the new value.
      ;; Both edges are delayed, which is what makes a delay composable -- a switch that waits before it
      ;; turns anything on AND before it turns it off, so a door does not slam the instant you step off.
      ;; (The first draft only delayed the rising edge, which made a delay node useless as a relay.)
      (defn widget-delay-armed [(src_power : I32) (armed : I32) (timer_ticks : I32)] : I32
        (if (= (w-clamp 0 15 src_power) (w-clamp 0 15 armed)) 0 (if (<= timer_ticks 0) 1 0)))
      
      (defn widget-delay-still-running [(timer_ticks : I32)] : I32 (if (> timer_ticks 0) 1 0))
      
      ;; ---- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; A lever is a light switch: press it and it stays where you put it.
      ;; (D2's own cable tiers are 0..15, which is where the range comes from.)
      (defn widget-lever-toggle [(power : I32)] : I32
        (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 power) 0) (widget-power-off) (widget-power-on)))
      
      ;; A pressure plate reads bodies standing on it. Any real weight closes it; the count is capped so a
      ;; crowd cannot produce a stronger signal than one person (this is a switch, not a scale).
      (defn widget-plate-power [(occupants : I32)] : I32
        (if (> (w-clamp 0 8 occupants) 0) (widget-power-on) (widget-power-off)))
      
      ;; A motor's discrete target: 0 down/idle, 1 up/running. The level decides what that means (a lift
      ;; car's floor, a centrifuge's spin) -- the circuit only says the machine has power.
      (defn widget-motor-target [(power : I32)] : I32 (if (> (w-clamp 0 15 power) 0) 1 0))
      
      ;; ---- the F interface ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; Whether a parked widget offers itself for interaction. Distance is in millimetres so the whole
      ;; decision stays integer; a widget with no interaction radius (0) is scenery and never prompts.
      ;; The prompt asks for the widget standing between the player and the surface they are looking at:
      ;; closest wins, so a lever bolted to a terminal is reachable without reaching through it.
      (defn widget-focus-ok [(dist_mm : I32) (radius_mm : I32) (busy : I32)] : I32
        (if (= busy 1) 0
          (if (<= (w-clamp 0 1000000 radius_mm) 0) 0
            (if (<= (w-clamp 0 1000000 dist_mm) (w-clamp 0 1000000 radius_mm)) 1 0))))
      
      ;; How long the "[F] USE" prompt holds after the player stops moving, so it does not flicker when the
      ;; distance wobbles across the radius boundary.
      (defn widget-focus-prompt-ms [] : I32 250)
      
      ;; A panel's key repeat for a value the player is dialling (RPM, floor, intensity): one step per press,
      ;; and the step size is the panel's own, clamped so a held key cannot spin a motor to nonsense.
      (defn widget-panel-key-adjust [(value : I32) (delta : I32) (lo : I32) (hi : I32)] : I32
        (w-clamp (w-clamp -1000000 1000000 lo) (w-clamp -1000000 1000000 hi) (+ value delta)))
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_widget_rules.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # gen_widget_rules.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/widget_rules.c from PARENA.
      #
      # Composable widget circuits (levers, plates, delays, transistors, motors) are decision logic, so they
      # live in PARENA with the rest of the rules:
      #   PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/widget_rules.prn
      # packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h is the host that runs them and mirrors their values into EduVM
      # registers. Usage: scripts/gen_widget_rules.sh   (needs ../PARENA, or PARENA_DIR)
      set -euo pipefail
      root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
      parena_dir="${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}"
      if [ -x "$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      elif [ -x "$parena_dir/parena" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/parena"
      else
          (cd "$parena_dir" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      fi
      "$parena_bin" build "$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/widget_rules.prn" \
          -o "$root/packages/simulation/widget_rules.c"
      echo "regenerated packages/simulation/widget_rules.c"
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/widget_rules_host.h
  content: |
      /* widget_rules_host.h -- installs PARENA's widget circuit rules into widget_rules.h.
       * The rules live in PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/widget_rules.prn, generated into widget_rules.c (do not edit
       * it; `make regen-widget-rules`). A host that simulates widgets (apps/lobby, apps/server) includes this
       * header, links widget_rules.c, and calls widget_rules_install() once at startup. With nothing
       * installed widget_rules.h's own built-in defaults are used, so tests keep their link lines. */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_HOST_H
      #define SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_HOST_H
      
      #include "widget_rules.h"
      
      /* PARENA-generated (widget_rules.c) */
      int widget_kind_count(void);
      int widget_power_on(void);
      int widget_power_off(void);
      int widget_max_power(void);
      int widget_delay_default_ticks(void);
      int widget_delay_min_ticks(void);
      int widget_delay_max_ticks(void);
      int widget_output_power(int kind, int armed, int src_power, int gate_power);
      int widget_delay_armed(int src_power, int armed, int timer_ticks);
      int widget_delay_still_running(int timer_ticks);
      int widget_lever_toggle(int power);
      int widget_plate_power(int occupants);
      int widget_motor_target(int power);
      int widget_focus_ok(int dist_mm, int radius_mm, int busy);
      int widget_focus_prompt_ms(void);
      int widget_panel_key_adjust(int value, int delta, int lo, int hi);
      
      static const WidgetRules g_widget_rules_parena = {
          widget_output_power, widget_delay_armed, widget_delay_still_running, widget_lever_toggle,
          widget_plate_power, widget_motor_target, widget_focus_ok, widget_panel_key_adjust,
          widget_delay_default_ticks, widget_delay_min_ticks, widget_delay_max_ticks
      };
      
      static inline void widget_rules_install(void) { widget_set_rules(&g_widget_rules_parena); }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_WIDGET_RULES_HOST_H */

      #define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS 16
      #define LEVEL_BOXES_DEFAULT_MATERIAL "brick" /* mirrors IDUNA/internal/shankpit.DefaultMaterialName exactly */
      
      typedef struct {
          char name[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAME];
          char shader_name[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAME]; /* a real, named reference into
              packages/render/material_shaders.h's own SHADER_* registry -- NOT GLSL source (see that
              header's own doc comment for the real "NOCK stores the name, native owns the code" split) */
          float specular;
          float shininess;
          float friction; /* S478b, founder real-time: "make the material friction stuff working per
              cube" -- real, live ground friction, resolved per-box via material_idx and consumed by
              packages/common/physics.h's own apply_friction (NOT this file -- level_boxes.h stays
              physics.h-free by design, see this header's own top-of-file doc comment). Absent in a
              pre-S478b export defaults to 0.30, matching physics.h's own tuned global FRICTION
              baseline exactly (see this field's own parse site below). */
          float density; /* mass per unit volume, made-up units. Founder real-time, 2026-10-16: "calculate mass of the
              different materials, have it configurable on the NOCK material". Used by packages/world/brick_rigid.h
              (mass + inertia of geometry that falls away). 0 / absent = use the engine default for the material
              kind (brick_fracture.h BF_DENSITY_*: brick 1.9, concrete 2.4, wood 0.6, glass 2.5). */
      } LevelBoxMaterial;
      
      #define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_BRICK_CELLS 4096 /* = brick_fracture.h BF_MAX_RECORDS; IDUNA MaxBrickCells matches */
      typedef struct {

          LEVEL_VEHICLE_RECON,

          "buggy", "rocket", "heli", "recon", "fly", "plane"
      };
      /* Human-friendly aliases: the words a person actually types into a wall's name. Anything else is a
         buggy, which is the old default and the harmless one (never invent a helicopter). */
      static inline int level_boxes_vehicle_kind_from_name(const char *s) {
          if (!s || !s[0]) return LEVEL_VEHICLE_BUGGY;
          for (int i = 0; i < LEVEL_VEHICLE_KIND_COUNT; i++)
              if (strcmp(s, LEVEL_VEHICLE_KIND_NAMES[i]) == 0) return i;
          if (strcmp(s, "helicopter") == 0) return LEVEL_VEHICLE_HELI;
          if (strcmp(s, "airplane") == 0 || strcmp(s, "plane_110") == 0 || strcmp(s, "c110") == 0 || strcmp(s, "c-110") == 0)
              return LEVEL_VEHICLE_PLANE;
          if (strcmp(s, "drone") == 0 || strcmp(s, "recon_drone") == 0) return LEVEL_VEHICLE_RECON;
          if (strcmp(s, "mini") == 0 || strcmp(s, "mini_fly") == 0 || strcmp(s, "micro") == 0) return LEVEL_VEHICLE_FLY;
          if (strcmp(s, "rocket_car") == 0) return LEVEL_VEHICLE_ROCKET;
          return LEVEL_VEHICLE_BUGGY;
      }

          if (kind < 0 || kind >= LEVEL_VEHICLE_KIND_COUNT) return LEVEL_VEHICLE_KIND_NAMES[LEVEL_VEHICLE_BUGGY];
          return LEVEL_VEHICLE_KIND_NAMES[kind];

  "instructions": "Add the PARENA rules for shared procedural zones: lifecycle and layout parameters.",
  "content": ";; stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn -- shared (instanceless) world zones and their procedural layouts.\n;;\n;; Founder: \"we need to start unifying GFD and shankpit ... i want to make it so that GFD server we have\n;; it like diablo where we can travel to a map and do it as a dungeon it can be procedurally generated\n;; ... for now the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the same one ...\n;; there should be a grace period of 15 minutes for the zone existing for after you leave it ... dungeons\n;; are not instanced they are generated and then they exist until everyone leaves + 15 minutes\".\n;;\n;; So there are two separate things here and they are deliberately not the same file:\n;;   * the LIFECYCLE (how long an empty zone survives) is pure arithmetic on two integers -- this module,\n;;     so the client, the server and the test cannot disagree about the grace period;\n;;   * the LAYOUT (how many rooms, how big, which material) is generation parameters, also here, so a\n;;     seed produces the same dungeon on every machine that runs this build.\n;;\n;; Every function is I32 and total: no state, no allocation, no RNG hidden inside. The caller owns the\n;; seed and the clock (packages/simulation/zone_registry.h), which is what makes a zone reproducible and\n;; a test possible. All millisecond values are milliseconds.\n(module shankpit/zone-rules)\n(export zone-grace-seconds zone-max-zones\n        zone-room-count zone-room-width zone-room-depth zone-wall-height\n        zone-wall-thickness zone-door-width zone-ring-distance\n        zone-ring-dir-x zone-ring-dir-z\n        zone-spawn-count zone-mob-count zone-material-count zone-material-for\n        zone-difficulty zone-zone-status-name\n        zone-should-expire zone-elapsed-ms)\n\n(defn w-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))\n\n;; The founder's own number: fifteen minutes of nobody inside and the layout is gone, so a farmed-out\n;; zone does not come back the way it was.\n(defn zone-grace-seconds [] : I32 900)\n\n;; One registry slot per zone id. Small on purpose: a zone holds a full level (hundreds of boxes) in the\n;; host's own memory, so this is a count of live layouts, not a list of every door in the world.\n(defn zone-max-zones [] : I32 8)\n\n;; ---- layout parameters ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; A hub plus 2..4 cardinal rooms. 3..5 rooms total, never a diagonal corridor (they are the one case\n;; that needs corner geometry, and a four-way hub already reads as a dungeon crossing).\n;; All sizes are world units, matching LevelBox's own convention.\n(defn zone-room-count [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 3 (w-clamp 0 2 (mod seed 3))))\n(defn zone-room-width [(seed : I32) (room : I32)] : I32\n  (+ 24 (* 8 (w-clamp 0 2 (mod (+ seed (* room 37)) 3)))))\n(defn zone-room-depth [(seed : I32) (room : I32)] : I32\n  (+ 24 (* 8 (w-clamp 0 2 (mod (+ seed (* room 53)) 3)))))\n(defn zone-wall-height [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 18 (* 6 (w-clamp 0 2 (mod seed 3)))))\n(defn zone-wall-thickness [] : I32 2)\n(defn zone-door-width [] : I32 8)\n;; Far enough apart that two 40-unit rooms do not share a wall, close enough that a corridor is short.\n(defn zone-ring-distance [] : I32 52)\n\n;; Cardinal directions only, 0 = east, 1 = south, 2 = west, 3 = north (x east, z south, matching the\n;; engine's own yaw-0-faces--Z convention). Room i uses direction (i - 1) mod 4.\n(defn zone-ring-dir-x [(dir : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= (w-clamp 0 3 dir) 0) 1 (if (= (w-clamp 0 3 dir) 2) -1 0)))\n(defn zone-ring-dir-z [(dir : I32)] : I32\n  (if (= (w-clamp 0 3 dir) 1) 1 (if (= (w-clamp 0 3 dir) 3) -1 0)))\n\n;; One spawner in the hub and one per room, so a party never has to walk the whole layout to find where\n;; it started. Capped at LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_SPAWNERS by the generator.\n(defn zone-spawn-count [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 3 (w-clamp 0 2 (mod seed 3))))\n;; What the mode's own population should be told to aim for. Twice the rooms plus a little, so a 5-room\n;; layout is a real fight and a 3-room layout is not empty.\n(defn zone-mob-count [(seed : I32) (rooms : I32)] : I32 (+ (* 2 (w-clamp 1 8 rooms)) (mod seed 5)))\n\n;; 0 concrete, 1 metal, 2 brick -- indices into the generator's own material table, which is why this is\n;; a kind and not a colour: the level file carries the material, the renderer owns the look.\n(defn zone-material-count [] : I32 3)\n(defn zone-material-for [(seed : I32) (idx : I32)] : I32 (mod (+ seed (* idx 7)) 3))\n\n;; 1..5, the depth of the zone's own dungeon tier -- GFD's state server is what turns this into stats.\n(defn zone-difficulty [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 1 (w-clamp 0 4 (mod seed 5))))\n\n;; ---- lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n;; Expire only when BOTH are true: nobody is inside AND the grace window has run out. A zone that is\n;; still occupied never expires, no matter how long the clock says it has existed.\n(defn zone-should-expire [(players : I32) (idle_ms : I32)] : I32\n  (if (<= (w-clamp 0 1000 players) 0)\n      (if (>= (w-clamp 0 2000000000 idle_ms) (* (zone-grace-seconds) 1000)) 1 0)\n      0))\n\n(defn zone-elapsed-ms [(now_ms : I32) (since_ms : I32)] : I32\n  (if (> now_ms since_ms) (- now_ms since_ms) 0))\n\n;; 0 uninitialized, 1 active (someone inside or recently inside), 2 idle (empty, counting down).\n(defn zone-zone-status-name [(status : I32)] : I32 (w-clamp 0 2 status))\n"
}

}

  "content": "/* zone_rules.h -- shared zone lifecycle + procedural layout rules, with built-in defaults.\n *\n * The numbers live in PARENA (PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn, generated into zone_rules.c by\n * scripts/gen_zone_rules.sh / `make regen-zone-rules`, installed through zone_rules_host.h). This header\n * carries matching C defaults so packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h and zone_registry.h compile and run\n * in any binary or test without linking a generated file -- the same arrangement widget_rules.h and\n * slide_rules.h use, and `make test-proc-dungeon` asserts the two copies agree sample for sample.\n *\n * Two separate concerns share this table on purpose, because both are \"the zone's own numbers\":\n *   - LIFECYCLE: grace seconds, max live zones, the expiry predicate.\n *   - LAYOUT: rooms, sizes, wall height, doors, spawners, material kind, difficulty tier.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H\n#define SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int (*grace_seconds)(void);\n    int (*max_zones)(void);\n    int (*room_count)(int seed);\n    int (*room_width)(int seed, int room);\n    int (*room_depth)(int seed, int room);\n    int (*wall_height)(int seed);\n    int (*wall_thickness)(void);\n    int (*door_width)(void);\n    int (*ring_distance)(void);\n    int (*ring_dir_x)(int dir);\n    int (*ring_dir_z)(int dir);\n    int (*spawn_count)(int seed);\n    int (*mob_count)(int seed, int rooms);\n    int (*material_count)(void);\n    int (*material_for)(int seed, int idx);\n    int (*difficulty)(int seed);\n    int (*should_expire)(int players, int idle_ms);\n    int (*elapsed_ms)(int now_ms, int since_ms);\n} ZoneRules;\n\nstatic inline int zr_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }\n\nstatic inline int zr_c_grace_seconds(void) { return 900; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_max_zones(void) { return 8; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_room_count(int seed) { return 3 + zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }\nstatic inline int zr_c_room_width(int seed, int room) { return 24 + 8 * zr_clamp(0, 2, (seed + room * 37) % 3); }\nstatic inline int zr_c_room_depth(int seed, int room) { return 24 + 8 * zr_clamp(0, 2, (seed + room * 53) % 3); }\nstatic inline int zr_c_wall_height(int seed) { return 18 + 6 * zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }\nstatic inline int zr_c_wall_thickness(void) { return 2; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_door_width(void) { return 8; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_ring_distance(void) { return 52; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_ring_dir_x(int dir) {\n    dir = zr_clamp(0, 3, dir);\n    return dir == 0 ? 1 : (dir == 2 ? -1 : 0);\n}\nstatic inline int zr_c_ring_dir_z(int dir) {\n    dir = zr_clamp(0, 3, dir);\n    return dir == 1 ? 1 : (dir == 3 ? -1 : 0);\n}\nstatic inline int zr_c_spawn_count(int seed) { return 3 + zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }\nstatic inline int zr_c_mob_count(int seed, int rooms) {\n    return 2 * zr_clamp(1, 8, rooms) + seed % 5;\n}\nstatic inline int zr_c_material_count(void) { return 3; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_material_for(int seed, int idx) { return (seed + idx * 7) % 3; }\nstatic inline int zr_c_difficulty(int seed) { return 1 + zr_clamp(0, 4, seed % 5); }\nstatic inline int zr_c_should_expire(int players, int idle_ms) {\n    if (zr_clamp(0, 1000, players) > 0) return 0;\n    return zr_clamp(0, 2000000000, idle_ms) >= zr_c_grace_seconds() * 1000 ? 1 : 0;\n}\nstatic inline int zr_c_elapsed_ms(int now_ms, int since_ms) { return now_ms > since_ms ? now_ms - since_ms : 0; }\n\nstatic ZoneRules g_zone_rules = {\n    zr_c_grace_seconds, zr_c_max_zones, zr_c_room_count, zr_c_room_width, zr_c_room_depth,\n    zr_c_wall_height, zr_c_wall_thickness, zr_c_door_width, zr_c_ring_distance, zr_c_ring_dir_x,\n    zr_c_ring_dir_z, zr_c_spawn_count, zr_c_mob_count, zr_c_material_count, zr_c_material_for,\n    zr_c_difficulty, zr_c_should_expire, zr_c_elapsed_ms\n};\n\nstatic inline void zone_rules_set(const ZoneRules *r) { if (r) g_zone_rules = *r; }\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H */\n"

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/zone_registry.h",
  "instructions": "Add the shared-zone registry with the grace-period lifecycle.",
  "content": "/* zone_registry.h -- shared, non-instanced zones with a grace period, headless.\n *\n * Founder: \"for now the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the same one\n * ... there should be a grace period of 15 minutes for the zone existing for after you leave it so if it\n * gets totally farmed out or whatever it wont regenerate until you re enter it ... dungeons are not\n * instanced they are generated and then they exist until everyone leaves + 15 minutes\".\n *\n * That is exactly a small table and three verbs, so that is what this is:\n *\n *   ENTER  -- first entrant CREATES the zone and gets the seed the host must generate from; every later\n *             entrant JOINS it and gets the same seed, so there is one layout and not one per player.\n *             Re-entering a zone whose countdown is running cancels the countdown and keeps the layout.\n *   LEAVE  -- drops the occupancy. At zero the zone starts counting down; it is NOT deleted.\n *   TICK   -- expires a zone only when it has been empty for the grace window. Expiry calls back with the\n *             id so the host can delete that zone's generated map file, then clears the slot, which is\n *             what makes the next entrant generate a NEW dungeon from a new seed.\n *\n * No I/O, no GL, no allocation: a slot holds an id, a seed and two integers. The layout itself lives in\n * the host (a CustomLevelData, or a file on disk), which is why this can be tested against a fake clock.\n *\n * Seeds come from a fixed LCG seeded by the registry, so a session is reproducible: the same start seed\n * and the same entry order produce the same dungeons. A host that wants a different world per launch\n * passes time(NULL).\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_REGISTRY_H\n#define SHANKPIT_ZONE_REGISTRY_H\n\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"zone_rules.h\"\n\n#define ZONE_ID_MAX 32\n\nenum { ZONE_STATE_UNINIT = 0, ZONE_STATE_ACTIVE = 1, ZONE_STATE_IDLE = 2 };\n\ntypedef struct {\n    char id[ZONE_ID_MAX];\n    int state;                 /* ZONE_STATE_* */\n    int players;               /* occupancy right now */\n    unsigned seed;             /* the layout seed, stable for the zone's whole life */\n    int idle_since_ms;         /* set when occupancy hits zero */\n    int generation;            /* how many times this zone has been generated (1 on first entry) */\n} ZoneSlot;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    ZoneSlot slot[ZONE_MAX_ZONES_DEFAULT];\n    int count;\n    unsigned next_seed;\n} ZoneRegistry;\n\n#define ZONE_MAX_ZONES_DEFAULT 8   /* == zone-max-zones in zone_rules.prn */\n\ntypedef void (*ZoneExpireFn)(void *user, const char *id);\n\nstatic inline unsigned zone_registry_next_seed(ZoneRegistry *reg) {\n    /* A plain 32-bit LCG. Not a good RNG and not meant to be -- it is a REPRODUCIBLE one, which is the\n       property a shared zone needs: same registry seed plus same entry order equals same dungeons. */\n    reg->next_seed = reg->next_seed * 1103515245u + 12345u;\n    return (reg->next_seed >> 8) & 0x7FFFFFFFu;\n}\n\nstatic inline void zone_registry_init(ZoneRegistry *reg, unsigned seed) {\n    if (!reg) return;\n    memset(reg, 0, sizeof *reg);\n    reg->next_seed = seed ? seed : 1u;\n}\n\nstatic inline int zone_registry_find(const ZoneRegistry *reg, const char *id) {\n    if (!reg || !id || !id[0]) return -1;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ZONE_MAX_ZONES_DEFAULT; i++)\n        if (reg->slot[i].state != ZONE_STATE_UNINIT && strcmp(reg->slot[i].id, id) == 0) return i;\n    return -1;\n}\n\n/* Returns 1 = created (generate from *out_seed), 0 = joined an existing zone (*out_seed is its seed),\n * -1 = the table is full (refuse the entry rather than silently sharing a stranger's dungeon). */\nstatic inline int zone_registry_enter(ZoneRegistry *reg, const char *id, int now_ms, unsigned *out_seed) {\n    int idx, free_slot = -1;\n    if (!reg || !id || !id[0]) return -1;\n    idx = zone_registry_find(reg, id);\n    if (idx >= 0) {\n        ZoneSlot *s = &reg->slot[idx];\n        s->players++;\n        s->state = ZONE_STATE_ACTIVE;\n        s->idle_since_ms = 0;   /* re-entry cancels the countdown */\n        if (out_seed) *out_seed = s->seed;\n        return 0;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < ZONE_MAX_ZONES_DEFAULT; i++) {\n        if (reg->slot[i].state == ZONE_STATE_UNINIT) { free_slot = i; break; }\n    }\n    if (free_slot < 0) return -1;\n    {\n        ZoneSlot *s = &reg->slot[free_slot];\n        memset(s, 0, sizeof *s);\n        snprintf(s->id, sizeof s->id, \"%s\", id);\n        s->state = ZONE_STATE_ACTIVE;\n        s->players = 1;\n        s->seed = zone_registry_next_seed(reg);\n        s->generation = 1;\n        reg->count++;\n        if (out_seed) *out_seed = s->seed;\n    }\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* Returns 1 when this leave emptied the zone (so the caller can log/announce the countdown). */\nstatic inline int zone_registry_leave(ZoneRegistry *reg, const char *id, int now_ms) {\n    int idx = zone_registry_find(reg, id);\n    if (idx < 0) return 0;\n    {\n        ZoneSlot *s = &reg->slot[idx];\n        if (s->players > 0) s->players--;\n        if (s->players == 0) {\n            s->state = ZONE_STATE_IDLE;\n            s->idle_since_ms = now_ms;\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/* Expires idle zones past the grace window. Returns how many expired this tick. */\nstatic inline int zone_registry_tick(ZoneRegistry *reg, int now_ms, ZoneExpireFn on_expire, void *user) {\n    int expired = 0;\n    if (!reg) return 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i < ZONE_MAX_ZONES_DEFAULT; i++) {\n        ZoneSlot *s = &reg->slot[i];\n        if (s->state == ZONE_STATE_UNINIT) continue;\n        if (s->players > 0) {\n            /* An occupied zone is never expired, and an ACTIVE one that was just re-entered has already\n               had its countdown cleared -- this is the invariant, not a special case. */\n            s->state = ZONE_STATE_ACTIVE;\n            s->idle_since_ms = 0;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (s->state == ZONE_STATE_ACTIVE) {\n            s->state = ZONE_STATE_IDLE;\n            s->idle_since_ms = now_ms;\n        }\n        {\n            int idle_ms = g_zone_rules.elapsed_ms(now_ms, s->idle_since_ms);\n            if (g_zone_rules.should_expire(s->players, idle_ms)) {\n                if (on_expire) on_expire(user, s->idle_since_ms ? s->id : s->id);\n                memset(s, 0, sizeof *s);   /* UNINIT: the next entrant generates a new seed */\n                if (reg->count > 0) reg->count--;\n                expired++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return expired;\n}\n\nstatic inline int zone_registry_players(const ZoneRegistry *reg, const char *id) {\n    int idx = zone_registry_find(reg, id);\n    return idx < 0 ? -1 : reg->slot[idx].players;\n}\n\nstatic inline int zone_registry_state(const ZoneRegistry *reg, const char *id) {\n    int idx = zone_registry_find(reg, id);\n    return idx < 0 ? ZONE_STATE_UNINIT : reg->slot[idx].state;\n}\n\nstatic inline unsigned zone_registry_seed(const ZoneRegistry *reg, const char *id) {\n    int idx = zone_registry_find(reg, id);\n    return idx < 0 ? 0u : reg->slot[idx].seed;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_REGISTRY_H */\n"
}
