Diagonal corridors are the\n * one case that needs corner geometry, and a four-way hub already reads as a dungeon crossing -- so the\n * layout stays something a person can draw on paper, and every wall is a real OBB the engine already\n * collides with.\n *\n * The output is a plain CustomLevelData, which means:\n *   - it goes through the same level_boxes_apply_to_physics as any NOCK level,\n *   - it saves with level_boxes_save_to_file (so a zone can be a file, and a co-op friend can be told its\n *     path or its seed),\n *   - it inherits destructible brick, lighting and the widget circuit for free, because it authors the\n *     same schema rather than a parallel one.\n *\n * The gate is authored as a REAL circuit, not a scripted special case: lever (6) -> relay (7) ->\n * machine (1) with that machine pointing at the gate wall's own box index. The relay's 45-tick delay is\n * why the gate does not slam the moment you flip the lever.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_PROC_DUNGEON_H\n#define SHANKPIT_PROC_DUNGEON_H\n\n#include <math.h>\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"../world/level_boxes.h\"\n#include \"zone_rules.h\"\n\n#define PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS 8\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int seed;\n    int rooms;\n    int difficulty;\n    int gate_box;          /* index in lvl->boxes of the gate the circuit opens */\n    int spawner_count;\n    float center_x[PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS];\n    float center_z[PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS];\n    float width[PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS];\n    float depth[PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS];\n} ProcDungeonInfo;\n\n/* Material table: index order matches zone-material-for's own numbering (0 concrete, 1 metal, 2 brick).\n * Friction is the live ground friction physics.h resolves per material, so a metal floor is slicker than\n * brick without a single line in the physics code. */\nstatic inline void proc_dungeon_materials(CustomLevelData *lvl) {\n    static const char *const names[3] = { \"concrete\", \"metal\", \"brick\" };\n    static const float spec[3] = { 0.10f, 0.55f, 0.06f };\n    static const float shin[3] = { 18.0f, 90.0f, 8.0f };\n    static const float fric[3] = { 0.34f, 0.26f, 0.30f };\n    static const float dens[3] = { 2.4f, 3.1f, 1.9f };\n    lvl->material_count = 3;\n    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {\n        LevelBoxMaterial *m = &lvl->materials[i];\n        memset(m, 0, sizeof *m);\n        snprintf(m->name, sizeof m->name, \"%s\", names[i]);\n        snprintf(m->shader_name, sizeof m->shader_name, \"standard\");\n        m->specular = spec[i];\n        m->shininess = shin[i];\n        m->friction = fric[i];\n        m->density = dens[i];\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline int proc_dungeon_add_box(CustomLevelData *lvl, float cx, float cz, float w, float h, float d,\n                                       int mat) {\n    LevelBox *b;\n    if (!lvl || lvl->count >= LEVEL_BOXES_MAX) return -1;\n    if (w <= 0.0f || d <= 0.0f || h <= 0.0f) return -1;\n    b = &lvl->boxes[lvl->count];\n    memset(b, 0, sizeof *b);\n    b->x = cx;\n    b->y = h * 0.5f;   /* LevelBox.y is the CENTRE, so a wall of height h stands on the floor */\n    b->z = cz;\n    b->w = w;\n    b->h = h;\n    b->d = d;\n    b->material_idx = (mat >= 0 && mat < lvl->material_count) ? mat : 0;\n    b->friction = lvl->materials[b->material_idx].friction;\n    if (b->material_idx == 1) { b->r = 0.34f; b->g = 0.40f; b->b = 0.46f; }\n    else if (b->material_idx == 2) { b->r = 0.58f; b->g = 0.31f; b->b = 0.26f; }\n    else { b->r = 0.46f; b->g = 0.46f; b->b = 0.50f; }\n    return lvl->count++;\n}\n\n/* A wall running along X (constant Z), and one running along Z (constant X). */\nstatic inline void proc_dungeon_wall_x(CustomLevelData *lvl, float z, float x0, float x1, float t, float h,\n                                       int mat) {\n    if (x1 - x0 < 0.01f) return;\n    proc_dungeon_add_box(lvl, (x0 + x1) * 0.5f, z, x1 - x0, h, t, mat);\n}\nstatic inline void proc_dungeon_wall_z(CustomLevelData *lvl, float x, float z0, float z1, float t, float h,\n                                       int mat) {\n    if (z1 - z0 < 0.01f) return;\n    proc_dungeon_add_box(lvl, x, (z0 + z1) * 0.5f, t, h, z1 - z0, mat);\n}\n\n/* One room. side: 0 north (-z), 1 south (+z), 2 west (-x), 3 east (+x), -1 = sealed. The doorway is a\n * real gap of door_w centred on that wall, because a wall with a hole in it is two walls and that is\n * exactly how the engine already builds one. */\nstatic inline void proc_dungeon_room(CustomLevelData *lvl, float cx, float cz, float w, float d, float h,\n                                     float t, int mat, int side, float door_w) {\n    float hw = w * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;\n    float g = door_w * 0.5f;\n\n    /* north / south */\n    if (side == 0) {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, cz - hd, cx - hw, cx - g, t, h, mat);\n        proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, cz - hd, cx + g, cx + hw, t, h, mat);\n    } else {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, cz - hd, cx - hw, cx + hw, t, h, mat);\n    }\n    if (side == 1) {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, cz + hd, cx - hw, cx - g, t, h, mat);\n        proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, cz + hd, cx + g, cx + hw, t, h, mat);\n    } else {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, cz + hd, cx - hw, cx + hw, t, h, mat);\n    }\n    /* west / east */\n    if (side == 2) {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, cx - hw, cz - hd, cz - g, t, h, mat);\n        proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, cx - hw, cz + g, cz + hd, t, h, mat);\n    } else {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, cx - hw, cz - hd, cz + hd, t, h, mat);\n    }\n    if (side == 3) {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, cx + hw, cz - hd, cz - g, t, h, mat);\n        proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, cx + hw, cz + g, cz + hd, t, h, mat);\n    } else {\n        proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, cx + hw, cz - hd, cz + hd, t, h, mat);\n    }\n}\n\n/* The hub has a doorway on every side that has a room, so the crossing is walkable in all directions. */\nstatic inline int proc_dungeon_side_has_room(const ProcDungeonInfo *info, int side) {\n    for (int i = 1; i < info->rooms; i++) {\n        int dir = (i - 1) % 4;\n        if (dir == side) return 1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/* Builds the layout into *out. Returns the box count (0 only if the rules produced nothing usable). */\nstatic inline int proc_dungeon_generate(CustomLevelData *out, const char *zone_id, unsigned seed) {\n    static ProcDungeonInfo info;\n    CustomLevelData *lvl = out;\n    float h, t, door_w, ring;\n    int mat_hub, gate_side = 0;\n\n    if (!lvl) return 0;\n    memset(lvl, 0, sizeof *lvl);\n    memset(&info, 0, sizeof info);\n    info.seed = (int)(seed & 0x7FFFFFFFu);\n    info.rooms = g_zone_rules.room_count(info.seed);\n    if (info.rooms < 2) info.rooms = 2;\n    if (info.rooms > PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS) info.rooms = PROC_DUNGEON_MAX_ROOMS;\n    info.difficulty = g_zone_rules.difficulty(info.seed);\n    h = (float)g_zone_rules.wall_height(info.seed);\n    t = (float)g_zone_rules.wall_thickness();\n    door_w = (float)g_zone_rules.door_width();\n    ring = (float)g_zone_rules.ring_distance();\n\n    snprintf(lvl->name, sizeof lvl->name, \"PROC %s %08x\", (zone_id && zone_id[0]) ? zone_id : \"zone\", seed);\n    proc_dungeon_materials(lvl);\n    lvl->ground_plane_enabled = 1;\n    lvl->ground_plane_squares = 96;\n    lvl->enclosed = 1;\n    lvl->width = (ring + 40.0f) * 2.0f;\n    lvl->height = h;\n    lvl->depth = lvl->width;\n\n    /* hub */\n    {\n        float w = (float)g_zone_rules.room_width(info.seed, 0);\n        float d = (float)g_zone_rules.room_depth(info.seed, 0);\n        int side;\n        mat_hub = g_zone_rules.material_for(info.seed, 0);\n        info.center_x[0] = 0.0f;\n        info.center_z[0] = 0.0f;\n        info.width[0] = w;\n        info.depth[0] = d;\n        /* Build the hub by hand so each side can carry a doorway; the generic room builder takes one. */\n        for (side = 0; side < 4; side++) {\n            int has = proc_dungeon_side_has_room(&info, side);\n            proc_dungeon_room(lvl, 0.0f, 0.0f, w, d, h, t, mat_hub, has ? side : -1, door_w);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* rooms + corridors */\n    for (int i = 1; i < info.rooms; i++) {\n        int dir = (i - 1) % 4;\n        float w = (float)g_zone_rules.room_width(info.seed, i);\n        float d = (float)g_zone_rules.room_depth(info.seed, i);\n        int mat = g_zone_rules.material_for(info.seed, i);\n        float cx = (float)g_zone_rules.ring_dir_x(dir) * ring;\n        float cz = (float)g_zone_rules.ring_dir_z(dir) * ring;\n        float hw_hub = info.width[0] * 0.5f, hd_hub = info.depth[0] * 0.5f;\n        float hw = w * 0.5f, hd = d * 0.5f;\n        int doorway_side = (dir + 2) % 4;   /* the side facing back to the hub */\n\n        info.center_x[i] = cx;\n        info.center_z[i] = cz;\n        info.width[i] = w;\n        info.depth[i] = d;\n        proc_dungeon_room(lvl, cx, cz, w, d, h, t, mat, doorway_side, door_w);\n\n        /* corridor: two parallel walls, inner width == the doorway it joins */\n        if (dir == 0 || dir == 2) {\n            float x0 = dir == 0 ? hw_hub : cx + hw;\n            float x1 = dir == 0 ? cx - hw : -hw_hub;\n            proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, (door_w + t) * 0.5f, x0, x1, t, h, mat);\n            proc_dungeon_wall_x(lvl, -(door_w + t) * 0.5f, x0, x1, t, h, mat);\n        } else {\n            float z0 = dir == 1 ? hd_hub : cz + hd;\n            float z1 = dir == 1 ? cz - hd : -hd_hub;\n            proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, (door_w + t) * 0.5f, z0, z1, t, h, mat);\n            proc_dungeon_wall_z(lvl, -(door_w + t) * 0.5f, z0, z1, t, h, mat);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* The gate: a real wall panel across the hub's north doorway, wired to a lever through a relay. It is\n       added last so its box index is stable and trivially inspectable in a saved level. */\n    gate_side = 0;\n    (void)gate_side;\n    {\n        float hd_hub = info.depth[0] * 0.5f;\n        int mat = g_zone_rules.material_for(info.seed, 7);\n        info.gate_box = proc_dungeon_add_box(lvl, 0.0f, -hd_hub + t * 0.5f, door_w, h, t, mat);\n    }\n\n    /* spawners: one at the hub, one per room, FFA */\n    {\n        int want = g_zone_rules.spawn_count(info.seed);\n        int sp = 0;\n        for (int i = 0; i < info.rooms && sp < want && lvl->spawner_count < LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_SPAWNERS; i++, sp++) {\n            LevelSpawner *ps = &lvl->spawners[lvl->spawner_count];\n            memset(ps, 0, sizeof *ps);\n            ps->x = info.center_x[i];\n            ps->y = 0.0f;\n            ps->z = info.center_z[i];\n            ps->yaw = (float)(i * 90);\n            ps->team = LEVEL_BOXES_SPAWNER_TEAM_FFA;\n            ps->id = lvl->spawner_count;\n            lvl->spawner_count++;\n            info.spawner_count++;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* The gate circuit. Pins point at LOWER indices (the circuit's own rule), and the machine points at\n       the gate box, so the door is a widget of widgets rather than a bespoke door type. */\n    if (info.gate_box >= 0) {\n        struct { const char *id; int type; int reg; float x, z; int input; int box; int delay; } w[3] = {\n            { \"proc_gate_lever\", 6, 40, 0.0f, 6.0f, -1, -1, 0 },\n            { \"proc_gate_relay\", 7, 41, 0.0f, 6.0f, 0, -1, 45 },\n            { \"proc_gate_motor\", 1, 42, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1, -1, 0 },\n        };\n        for (int i = 0; i < 3 && lvl->edu_widget_count < LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_EDU_WIDGETS; i++) {\n            LevelEduWidget *ew = &lvl->edu_widgets[lvl->edu_widget_count];\n            memset(ew, 0, sizeof *ew);\n            snprintf(ew->entity_id, sizeof ew->entity_id, \"%s\", w[i].id);\n            ew->machine_type = w[i].type;\n            ew->initial_state = 0;\n            ew->memory_address = w[i].reg;\n            ew->x = w[i].x;\n            ew->y = 0.0f;\n            ew->z = w[i].z;\n            ew->radius = 3.0f;\n            ew->box_index = -1;\n            ew->input_pin = w[i].input;\n            ew->gate_pin = -1;\n            ew->delay_ticks = w[i].delay;\n            lvl->edu_widget_count++;\n        }\n        /* the machine drives the gate box (index is valid: the box was just added) */\n        lvl->edu_widgets[lvl->edu_widget_count - 1].box_index = info.gate_box;\n    }\n\n    return lvl->count;\n}\n\n/* Saves the generated level as the real JSON a NOCK level uses. Returns 1 on success. */\nstatic inline int proc_dungeon_save(const char *path, const CustomLevelData *lvl) {\n    if (!path || !lvl) return 0;\n    return level_boxes_save_to_file(path, lvl);\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_PROC_DUNGEON_H */\n"
}

ok(refused == 0, \"the table holds its own maximum of zones\");\n        ok(zone_registry_enter(&full, \"overflow\", 0, NULL) == -1, \"and refuses one more entry\");\n    }\n\n    /* two zones do not interfere */\n    {\n        static ZoneRegistry two;\n        unsigned s1 = 0, s2 = 0;\n        zone_registry_init(&two, 9u);\n        ok(zone_registry_enter(&two, \"alpha\", 0, &s1) == 1 && zone_registry_enter(&two, \"beta\", 0, &s2) == 1,\n           \"two different zones can both be live\");\n        ok(s1 != s2, \"with different seeds\");\n        zone_registry_leave(&two, \"alpha\", 100);\n        ok(zone_registry_tick(&two, 100 + 900000, on_expire, NULL) >= 1 &&\n           zone_registry_state(&two, \"beta\") == ZONE_STATE_ACTIVE,\n           \"and expiring one leaves the other alone\");\n    }\n\n    printf(\"\\n%d checks, %d failed\\n\", g_checks, g_fail);\n    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;\n}\n"
}

Co-op note, named rather than implied: a\n * LAN friend joining this host would receive the same SEED and rebuild the identical dungeon -- there is\n * no zone packet yet, so today this is the local half of that story. */\nstatic ZoneRegistry g_zone_registry;\nstatic int g_zone_registry_ready = 0;\nstatic int g_dungeon_descent = 0;\n\nstatic void lobby_zone_expire(void *user, const char *zone_id) {\n    char path[256];\n    (void)user;\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"var/maps/proc_%s.json\", zone_id ? zone_id : \"zone\");\n    remove(path);\n    SDL_Log(\"DUNGEON: '%s' emptied and its grace period ran out -- layout deleted\", zone_id ? zone_id : \"?\");\n}\n\nstatic int lobby_start_proc_dungeon(const char *zone) {\n    static CustomLevelData lvl;\n    unsigned seed = 0;\n    int created, now;\n    char path[256];\n    PlayerState *hero;\n\n    if (!zone || !zone[0]) return 0;\n    if (!g_zone_registry_ready) {\n        zone_registry_init(&g_zone_registry, (unsigned)SDL_GetTicks() | 1u);\n        g_zone_registry_ready = 1;\n    }\n    now = (int)SDL_GetTicks();\n    zone_registry_tick(&g_zone_registry, now, lobby_zone_expire, NULL);\n    created = zone_registry_enter(&g_zone_registry, zone, now, &seed);\n    if (created < 0) { SDL_Log(\"DUNGEON: no free zone slot for '%s'\", zone); return 0; }\n\n    proc_dungeon_generate(&lvl, zone, seed);\n    snprintf(path, sizeof path, \"var/maps/proc_%s.json\", zone);\n    if (created) {\n        FILE *probe = fopen(\"var/maps\", \"rb\");\n        if (probe) fclose(probe);\n        else (void)system(\"mkdir -p var/maps\");\n        if (proc_dungeon_save(path, &lvl))\n            SDL_Log(\"DUNGEON: generated '%s' seed %08x -> %s (%d boxes)\", zone, seed, path, lvl.count);\n        else\n            SDL_Log(\"DUNGEON: generated '%s' seed %08x (%d boxes), could not write %s\", zone, seed, lvl.count, path);\n    } else {\n        SDL_Log(\"DUNGEON: joining the existing '%s' seed %08x (%d boxes)\", zone, seed, lvl.count);\n    }\n\n    local_init_match(1, MODE_ZOMBIES);   /* the sandbox that already populates a custom level */\n    level_boxes_apply_to_physics(&lvl);\n    scene_load(SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL);\n    hero = &local_state.players[0];\n    hero->scene_id = SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL;\n    local_state.story_phase = STORY_PHASE_PLAYING;\n    phys_respawn(hero, SDL_GetTicks());\n    g_snap_zombies = 1;\n    food_pickup_reset();\n    food_pickup_seed_ring(SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL, hero->x, hero->y, hero->z);\n    SDL_Log(\"DUNGEON: '%s' loaded, difficulty %d, %d spawners\",\n            zone, g_zone_rules.difficulty((int)seed), lvl.spawner_count);\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* F7 -- descend. The reachable version of the Diablo door; a menu tile for the archipelago can call the\n * same function once the level browser grows a dungeon entry. */\nstatic int lobby_descend_dungeon(void) {\n    char zone[32];\n    g_dungeon_descent++;\n    snprintf(zone, sizeof zone, \"dungeon_%d\", g_dungeon_descent);\n    app_state = STATE_GAME_LOCAL;\n    if (!lobby_start_proc_dungeon(zone)) { app_state = STATE_LOBBY; return 0; }\n    return 1;\n}\n\n#define THIRD_PERSON_CAM_DIST 6.0f",

# ---- Source-list export for CI ----
# CI (.github/workflows/{tests,release}.yml) compiles the Windows lobby and the Linux server with
# raw gcc/mingw lines instead of `make` (different libs/flags). Those lines used to carry a
# hand-copied copy of LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC and drifted NINE times -- including a 3-day red release
# pipeline (2026-09-28..10-01) -- so they now expand these two targets instead:
#   gcc $(make -s print-server-src) ...        x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc $(make -s print-lobby-src) ...
# A new packages/*.c added to LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC above is now picked up by CI automatically.
.PHONY: print-lobby-src print-server-src test-os-menu test-os-menu-gl check-windows

# Compile every Windows-client source under mingw-w64 (no link, so no .a/.dll objects needed). Catches
# compile-only breakage that otherwise waits for a release job -- see the script's own header comment.
check-windows:
  bash scripts/check_windows_build.sh
print-lobby-src:
  @echo $(LOBBY_SRC)
print-server-src:
  @echo $(SERVER_SRC)

# ---- Outputs ----
LOBBY_BIN    := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby
SERVER_BIN   := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_server
SERVERCTL_BIN:= $(BIN_DIR)/serverctl
GO_SERVER_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server
EMILY_BOT_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/emily-bot
EA_DIR       := dist/ea

# ---- Targets ----
.PHONY: test-witness-ai-zombies test-bullet-hole test-queue-level test-baked-levels test-level-save bake-levels all lobby server serverctl clean setup print go-server ea ea-windows emily-bot rigid-ragdoll test-physics test-audio-chain ux-screenshot-test

all: $(LOBBY_BIN) $(SERVER_BIN)

# Ensure bin/ exists even when building a single target
$(BIN_DIR):
  @mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)

setup: $(BIN_DIR)

# ---- EDITOR.GAME in-process widget (S559, 2026-09-27) ----
# Founder real-time: "the editor app fails to launch -- instead of having it launch it should pop
# a widget up on the screen ... deeply integrate it as a widget on the screen the notes auto
# save." apps/lobby/src/editor_widget_bridge.c links against EDITOR.GAME's own real
# editor_widget_* API, consumed as a sibling checkout (../EDITOR.GAME -- same path MODULE.bazel's
# own local_path_override already assumes). Same 5-file build EDITOR.GAME's own plain Makefile
# uses to produce its standalone `editor-game` binary, just linked into shank_lobby instead:
# gen/editor_full.c (the generated PARENA stdlib + examples/editor_main.c, concatenated -- see
# EDITOR.GAME/Makefile's own identical rule) and runtime/parena_runtime.c define/call the plain
# arena_init/arena_alloc/arena_strdup/arena_free_all names, which would otherwise collide at link
# time with SHANKPIT's own already-linked, deliberately-minimal packages/world/parena_runtime.c
# (same 4 names, real but different, narrower implementation) -- both files are compiled here with
# a matching -D rename so ONLY this pair's calls/definitions move to edg_arena_*, leaving
# SHANKPIT's own copy completely untouched. src/arena.c/src/fmt.c/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c are
# EDITOR.GAME's own SEPARATE compiler-internal bump allocator, already renamed to pf_arena_* by
# EDITOR.GAME's own PRNFMT_RENAME convention (unrelated to the edg_arena_* rename above -- two
# different collisions, two different renames, matching EDITOR.GAME's own Makefile/BUILD.bazel
# precedent exactly).
EDITOR_GAME_DIR    := ../EDITOR.GAME
# vec_i32_at -- PARENA's C emitter generates this Vec<i32> helper as a plain global (not static)
# in every translation unit that uses Vec<i32>; packages/world/png_decode_gen.c (SHANKPIT's own
# PARENA-generated code, already in LOBBY_SRC) happens to generate one too, so it collides the
# same way arena_init did -- confirmed via `nm -g` on both object files, exactly one overlap.
EDITOR_GAME_RENAME := -Darena_init=edg_arena_init -Darena_alloc=edg_arena_alloc -Darena_strdup=edg_arena_strdup -Darena_free_all=edg_arena_free_all -Dvec_i32_at=edg_vec_i32_at
EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT := -Darena_init=pf_arena_init -Darena_alloc=pf_arena_alloc -Darena_strdup=pf_arena_strdup -Darena_free_all=pf_arena_free_all
EDITOR_GAME_OBJS   := $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.o

$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_stdlib_gen.c $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/examples/editor_main.c
  cat $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_stdlib_gen.c $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/examples/editor_main.c > $@

$(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c | $(BIN_DIR)
  $(CC) -std=c99 -w -DEDITOR_WIDGET_TEST_BUILD $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -c $< -o $@

$(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.c | $(BIN_DIR)
  $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -c $< -o $@

$(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/arena.c | $(BIN_DIR)
  $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@

$(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/fmt.c | $(BIN_DIR)
  $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@

$(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c | $(BIN_DIR)
  $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src -c $< -o $@

# Windows (mingw) variants of the same 5 objects, for ea-windows below -- separate output
# filenames (.win.o) so a native `make lobby` and `make ea-windows` in the same tree never clobber
# each other's objects. Verified for real: EDITOR.GAME's own runtime/parena_runtime.c and
# generated stdlib code cross-compile under x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc with no source changes at all
# (checked directly, not assumed -- the only NEW cross-build requirement is SDL2_ttf's own mingw
# devel kit, same one PITVIPER/IDUNA.GAME/EDITOR.GAME's own standalone Windows builds already need,
# per SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX below).
MINGW_CC := x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN := $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.win.o

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/docs/PROC_DUNGEONS.md",
  "content": "# Shared procedural zones (SHANKPIT ARCHIPELAGO, phase 1)\n\nThe founder's shape, in their own words: *\"like diablo where we can travel to a map and do it as a\ndungeon it can be procedurally generated ... the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone\nelse enters the same one ... a grace period of 15 minutes ... dungeons are not instanced they are\ngenerated and then they exist until everyone leaves + 15 minutes.\"*\n\nThis is that, built and tested, plus the GFD map import. It is **not** the whole GFD merge — see\n`docs/GFD_UNIFICATION.md` for what is still a phase.\n\n## The three pieces\n\n| File | Owns |\n|---|---|\n| `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn` → `packages/simulation/zone_rules.c` | every number: 900-second grace, 8 live zones, rooms/sizes/walls/doors/spawners/materials/difficulty, and the expiry predicate |\n| `packages/simulation/zone_registry.h` | the shared-zone table and its clock — enter / leave / tick, no I/O, no allocation |\n| `packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h` | the layout: one seed → one `CustomLevelData`, saved as real level JSON |\n\n`packages/simulation/zone_rules.h` carries numerically identical C defaults so tests and any binary can\ncompile without the generated file; `make test-proc-dungeon` asserts the two copies agree (over 100\nsamples), the same contract `widget_rules.h` and `slide_rules.h` already keep.\n\n## Determinism is the feature\n\nThe generator uses only integer arithmetic from the rules plus an LCG seed, and every coordinate is an\nadd or a multiply of small integers — no `rand()`, no float trig, no time. So:\n\n- the same seed produces **byte-identical level JSON** (the test saves two and `strcmp`s them),\n- a co-op client given the seed rebuilds the same dungeon,\n- a farmed-out dungeon that expires comes back **different**, because expiry clears the slot and the next\n  entrant gets a new seed.\n\n## Lifecycle, exactly\n\n```\nENTER  first entrant  -> creates the slot, gets the seed, host generates and saves the zone\n       later entrants -> join the SAME slot and seed (one layout, not one per player)\n       re-entry while the countdown runs -> cancels the countdown, keeps the layout\nLEAVE  drops occupancy; at zero the zone goes IDLE and starts counting. It is not deleted.\nTICK   expires a zone only when empty for >= 900 s; the host callback deletes that zone's file and the\n       slot is cleared, so the next entrant generates from a new seed.\n```\n\nAn occupied zone never expires, however old it is — that is an invariant in `zone_registry_tick`, not a\nspecial case.\n\n## Shape of a generated dungeon\n\nA hub plus 2–4 cardinal rooms joined by corridors, all axis-aligned, enclosed, with a ground plane. The\nhub carries a gate that is authored as a **real circuit**, not a special door type:\n\n```\nproc_gate_lever (6 LEVER, reg 40) -> proc_gate_relay (7 DELAY, 45 ticks) -> proc_gate_motor (1 MACHINE, box_index = the gate)\n```\n\nSo the gate opens 45 ticks after the lever, through the same `widget_runtime.h` path a lab door uses, and\nthe lever is the familiar `[F] USE` prompt.\n\n## Reaching it\n\n- In game, **F7** descends: it creates/joins `dungeon_N` and loads it through the normal custom-level\n  loader (so lighting, destructible brick, the widget circuit and zombies population all apply).\n- `./bin/shank_lobby --dungeon [zone]` starts straight into a generated zone.\n\nBoth call the same `lobby_start_proc_dungeon`.\n\n## GFD maps\n\n`scripts/import_gfd_levels.py` reads a GoblinFoxDragon checkout and writes `var/maps/gfd_town.json`:\n\n- **Town** is real 3D content: 17 named buildings in `packages/world/town_map.c` plus the generated\n  expansion blocks, at `TOWN_WORLD_SCALE 3.0`. Each becomes a solid box, with a perimeter wall, materials\n  and spawners.\n- **Meadow** is *not* a level: `data/crystal_seed_meadow.json` is a 44×44 goblin **simulation** seed\n  (tick, goblins, kinds, grid coordinates) with no wall, floor or building in it. The script says so\n  rather than inventing geometry.\n\n## Not built yet (named, not implied)\n\n- **No zone packet.** The registry and seeds are host-side; a LAN friend is not yet sent the seed or the\n  map. That is the next slice (a `PACKET_ZONE_STATE` carrying zone id + seed + occupancy, and the client\n  generating from the seed instead of trusting a file).\n- **No menu tile.** F7 and `--dungeon` are the reachable paths; the archipelago browser is UI work.\n- **No GFD state server.** Job/stat/inventory progression is a separate phase (see the unification doc);\n  the dungeon carries a `difficulty` tier for it to consume later.\n- **No instanced dungeons.** By design: that is the founder's explicit choice, and the phase-1 behaviour\n  above is what \"not instanced\" means in practice.\n"
}

{

  "content": "# Unifying GoblinFoxDragon with SHANKPIT — plan, and what phase 1 actually shipped\n\nThe founder: *\"we need to start unifying gfd and shankpit archipelligo ... shankpit is the frontend for the\nMMO ... GFD is a fork of SHANKPIT maybe its time to unfork it and just merge GFD all of it needs to be\nbrought into shankpit and the shankpit engine improvements that are already in place dont get overwritten\n... including bringing in the GFD exclusive levels ... all mods based PARENA based.\"*\n\nGFD has been **cloned and read** (`../GoblinFoxDragon`, not guessed at). What is actually in it:\n\n| Path | What it is |\n|---|---|\n| `apps/mud`, `apps2/mud` | the text MUD / state engine (jobs, combat text, progression) — **no spatial data at all** |\n| `apps2/battlegrounds_gui`, `apps/lobby` | a 3D client, the fork of SHANKPIT's lobby |\n| `packages/world/town_map.c` + `generated/town_expansion_blocks.inl` | **Town**: 17 named buildings + expansion blocks as x/z/w/d/h seeds, scale 3.0 — real geometry |\n| `data/crystal_seed_meadow.json` | **Meadow**: a 44×44 goblin *simulation* seed (goblins, kinds, grid) — **not** geometry |\n| `server/`, `server-go/`, `services/` | Go services (field office, etc.) |\n\n## The rule that protects SHANKPIT\n\n**Nothing from GFD overwrites a SHANKPIT file.** GFD contributed data and ideas; the engine\n(XPBD `grb.c`, `structure.h`, `brick_*`, lighting, vehicles, widgets) is untouched. Where GFD had a\nparallel implementation, SHANKPIT's is the one that runs and GFD's content is imported *into* its schema.\n\n## Phases\n\n**Phase 1 — shipped (this change).**\n- `zone_rules.prn`: the shared-zone lifecycle (900 s grace, 8 zones) and the dungeon layout numbers, all\n  PARENA, with identical C defaults.\n- `zone_registry.h`: the non-instanced zone table — first entrant generates, later entrants join, expiry\n  after fifteen empty minutes, re-entry inside the window keeps the layout.\n- `proc_dungeon.h`: one seed → one `CustomLevelData`, byte-identical on every machine, saved as real level\n  JSON, with a gate that is a real lever → relay → machine circuit.\n- `scripts/import_gfd_levels.py`: Town → `var/maps/gfd_town.json` (boxes, perimeter, spawners). Meadow is\n  reported as a sim seed, not a level, rather than fabricated.\n- Reachable: **F7** in game and `--dungeon [zone]` on the command line.\n\n**Phase 2 — the zone packet (next).** `PACKET_ZONE_STATE` carrying zone id, seed, occupancy and the\ngrace countdown. A LAN client then generates the dungeon from the seed instead of being sent geometry,\nwhich is the same \"identical geometry compiled in\" contract `--level` already relies on. Client entry\nmust not stall the render thread while generating (generation is a few hundred boxes — measure before\noptimising).\n\n**Phase 3 — batteries-included host.** `--coop-host` that starts the authoritative server in-process (or\nas a child process) on the LAN interface, advertises over broadcast, and writes progress under `var/`.\nSingle-player = the same path with nobody else joining, which is the Minecraft model the founder named.\nThe current `--host/--port` client path already exists; what is missing is the host side owning both the\nUDP game loop and the zone registry.\n\n**Phase 4 — GFD state server.** Take the MUD's job/stat/inventory model, and **port its rules to PARENA**\n(`stats_bridge.prn`: job → cooldown/haste/evasion/max HP, equipment → affinities). The C side consumes a\nflat struct; it must not learn about 23 jobs. The dungeon's `difficulty` tier is the first input.\nPersistence is the state server's job (name-keyed JSON saves), not the client's.\n\n**Phase 5 — Meadow, properly.** Meadow has a *simulation* seed, not geometry. Turning it into a 3D zone\nmeans either authoring it as a NOCK level or teaching `proc_dungeon.h` a second layout kind (outdoor\ncells with heightfield sampling). Do that only when a scene needs it — inventing a conversion now would be\na fake import.\n\n## Honest state of \"multiplayer\"\n\nToday the zone registry and the dungeon are **host-local**. Two players on one machine's session share\nthe layout; a LAN friend cannot join a zone yet because there is no packet carrying the zone's identity or\nseed, and the learn-from-seed path is phase 2. Saying \"co-op works\" before that would be false.\n"
}

> _Reasoning_
> Two failures: different seeds produce identical JSON. Why? Because the generator's layout depends only on `room_count`, sizes, wall height, material — all derived from `seed % 3` etc. Two seeds 0x1234 and 0x9999 might coincide modulo 3 for every derived value! 0x1234 = 4660; 4660 % 3 = 1. 0x9999 = 39321; 39321 % 3 = 0. Hmm, not equal. But room_width uses (seed + room*37) % 3 — that shifts, so sequences differ... unless the layout ignores seed because of a bug: `info.rooms = g_zone_rules.room_count(info.seed)` — fine.
> 
> Wait, both saves identical? Maybe because `proc_dungeon_generate` writes `lvl->name` with the seed — that differs ("PROC dungeon_a 00001234" vs 00009999). So the JSON must differ at least in name... unless saving failed and slurp read the same old file? The test: `ok(n3 > 0 && proc_dungeon_save("/tmp/proc_c.json", &c), ...)` — if save succeeded, name differs. Unless `ja`/`jc` are the same buffer! Ah — `slurp` returns a `static char buf[262144]`, so `ja` and `jc` are the SAME pointer. Comparing them always says equal. The earlier byte-identical check passed trivially for the same reason — a real test bug: it proved nothing.

## What I found first (it changed the plan)

GFD is not in this tree, so I cloned it and read it. Its real contents are not what the pasted specs described:

- `apps/mud` / `apps2/mud` — the text state engine. **No spatial data at all**, which is consistent with your "the state from the GFD server is real time but I don't think it has any spatial data".
- **Town** is real 3D content: 17 named buildings in `packages/world/town_map.c` (auction house, town hall, blacksmith…) plus 744 generated expansion blocks, at `TOWN_WORLD_SCALE 3.0`.
- **Meadow** is not a level. `data/crystal_seed_meadow.json` is a 44×44 *goblin simulation* seed (48 goblins with grid coords) — no wall, floor or building in it. There is nothing to convert, and I did not invent geometry to pretend otherwise.

## Phase 1, built and tested

**`PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn`** → `zone_rules.c` — every number: 900-second grace, 8 live zones, rooms 3–5, sizes 24/32/40, wall height, 8-unit doors, 52-unit ring, spawners, material kind, difficulty 1–5, and the expiry predicate. `zone_rules.h` carries identical C defaults; the test asserts the two agree across 100+ samples.

**`packages/simulation/zone_registry.h`** — the shared-zone table, exactly your semantics:
- first entrant **creates** and gets the seed; later entrants **join the same seed** (one layout, not one per player)
- re-entry while the countdown runs **cancels** it and keeps the layout
- an occupied zone **never** expires, however old it is
- expiry only at `players == 0 && idle >= 900 s`, then the slot clears, so the next entrant gets a **new seed and a new dungeon**

**`packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h`** — one seed → one `CustomLevelData`: hub + 2–4 cardinal rooms, corridors, enclosed, ground plane, spawners. Determinism is structural, not hopeful: integer arithmetic only, no `rand()`, no float trig, no time. The gate is a **real circuit** — `lever → 45-tick relay → machine(box_index = the gate)` — so it opens on the relay's delay through the same `widget_runtime.h` path a lab door uses.

**Reachable:** **F7** descends into `dungeon_N`, and `./bin/shank_lobby --dungeon [zone]` starts straight into one. Both go through the ordinary custom-level loader, so lighting, destructible brick, the widget circuit and zombies population all apply.

**`scripts/import_gfd_levels.py`** — GFD Town → `var/maps/gfd_town.json`: **765 boxes, 8 spawners**, verified with a real parse (`OK GFD TOWN: 765 boxes, 8 spawners, 2 materials`). Committed, because it is content.

## Bugs this caught

1. **`w-clamp` collided across rule modules.** PARENA lowers a helper to a *global* C function, so `widget_rules.prn` and `zone_rules.prn` both emitting `w_clamp` is a duplicate-symbol link error. Renamed to `zr-clamp`; that would have broken the lobby link on the next build.
2. **`widget_rules.c` was never in `LOBBY_SRC`.** `main.c` has been calling `widget_rules_install()` with the generated file absent from the source list — a latent link break that `check-windows` (compile-only) could not see. Both generated rule files are now in `LOBBY_SRC`, and `zone_rules.c`/`widget_rules.c` in `SERVER_SRC`.
3. **My own test proved nothing at first:** `slurp` returned one `static` buffer, so "two files are byte-identical" compared a pointer to itself. Fixed to write into caller buffers — it now genuinely compares two saved levels.

## Checks actually run

- `make test-proc-dungeon` → **46 checks, 0 failed**: rules parity, same seed → identical saved bytes, saved level reloads with gate box + circuit + spawners intact, gate opens at 45–60 ticks (not on the press), second entrant same seed, 899,999 ms not enough, occupied zone never expires at 9,000,000 ms, expiry callback + slot clear + **different** seed → different dungeon, full table refuses a ninth zone, zones expire independently.
- `make test-widget-circuit` **51**, `make test-widget-runtime` **48**, `make check-windows` **101 sources**, `make -B server` exit 0.
- GFD import + parse probe: both exit 0.

## Not built, named

- **No zone packet.** A LAN friend cannot join a zone yet — the seed is host-local, so today this is the local half of co-op. That is phase 2 in `docs/GFD_UNIFICATION.md`.
- **No menu tile.** F7 and `--dungeon` are the reachable paths; the archipelago browser is UI work.
- **No GFD state server / stat bridge** (phase 4), and **no Meadow level**, because there is no geometry in GFD to convert.
- No live run: this box has no GPU/display, so the dungeon was generated, saved, parsed and simulated headlessly — never seen on screen. The lobby is compiled for mingw but not linked here.

The full phased plan (zone packet → `--coop-host` batteries-included server → PARENA stat bridge → Meadow as a second layout kind) is in **`docs/GFD_UNIFICATION.md`**, and the dungeon/lifecycle contract is in **`docs/PROC_DUNGEONS.md`**.

      /* server_broadcast_queue_level -- card #481, see PACKET_QUEUE_LEVEL in protocol.h. MODE_QUEUE only;
       * throttled to 1 Hz (the level only changes at a round boundary, the repeat heals a dropped datagram
       * and a late joiner). Separate packet from the snapshot, same zero-risk reasoning as the others. */
      void server_broadcast_queue_level(void) {
          if (local_state.game_mode != MODE_QUEUE) return;
          static unsigned int last_ms = 0;
          unsigned int now_ms = get_server_time();
          if (last_ms != 0 && (now_ms - last_ms) < 1000) return;
          last_ms = now_ms;
          NetQueueLevel pkt;
          memset(&pkt, 0, sizeof(pkt));
          pkt.hdr.type = PACKET_QUEUE_LEVEL;
          pkt.hdr.client_id = 0;
          pkt.hdr.timestamp = now_ms;
          pkt.level_id = g_queue_level_id;
          for (int i = 1; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
              if (!slots[i].active || !slots[i].welcomed) continue;
              sendto(sock, &pkt, sizeof(pkt), 0, (struct sockaddr*)&slots[i].addr, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in));
          }
      }

      static void server_shield_packs_tick(void) {
          if (local_state.game_mode != MODE_QUEUE || local_state.match_over) return;
          for (int i = 1; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
              PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[i];

              shield_packs_note_player(i, alive, p->x, p->y, p->z, rand() % 100);
              if (alive && p->shield < 100 && shield_packs_take(p->x, p->y, p->z)) {
                  p->shield = 100;
                  NET_SERVER_LOG("SHIELD_PACK_TAKEN player=%d", i);
              }
          }
      }

{
  "path": "MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/zone_sync.h",
  "instructions": "Add the zone wire decode and reload decision.",
  "content": "/* zone_sync.h -- the zone's IDENTITY on the wire, and the one decision a client makes from it.\n *\n * The founder's co-op shape: \"the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the\n * same one\". On a LAN that means the host owns the zone and the client must reach the SAME dungeon --\n * without a level transfer. So PACKET_ZONE_STATE carries (zone id, seed, players, state, idle_ms) and a\n * client rebuilds the layout locally from the seed with proc_dungeon.h.\n *\n * That is only sound because generation is deterministic: the same seed produces byte-identical level\n * JSON on every machine (`make test-proc-dungeon` asserts exactly that). This header is the small,\n * testable seam between \"a packet arrived\" and \"reload the world\":\n *\n *   zone_sync_decode      -- validate untrusted bytes (length, type, non-empty NUL-terminated id)\n *   zone_sync_should_reload -- reload only when the zone or its seed actually changed, never on a repeat\n *   zone_sync_fill        -- build the packet on the server side, so encode and decode cannot drift\n *\n * Deliberately no I/O and no networking: the caller owns the socket and the level load.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_SYNC_H\n#define SHANKPIT_ZONE_SYNC_H\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"../common/protocol.h\"\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int active;                     /* the packet described a zone that exists (state != 0) */\n    char zone_id[NET_ZONE_ID_MAX];\n    unsigned int seed;\n    int players;\n    int state;                      /* zone_registry.h's ZONE_STATE_* */\n    unsigned int idle_ms;\n} ZoneSync;\n\nstatic inline void zone_sync_clear(ZoneSync *s) {\n    if (s) memset(s, 0, sizeof *s);\n}\n\n/* Decodes one datagram. Returns 1 only for a complete, well-formed zone packet: a packet is untrusted\n * input, and a half-copied id would otherwise become a filename (the host saves var/maps/proc_<id>.json). */\nstatic inline int zone_sync_decode(ZoneSync *out, const void *buf, int len) {\n    const NetZoneState *p = (const NetZoneState *)buf;\n    if (!out || !buf || len < (int)sizeof(NetZoneState)) return 0;\n    if (p->hdr.type != PACKET_ZONE_STATE) return 0;\n    if (p->zone_id[0] == '\\0') return 0;\n    if (memchr(p->zone_id, '\\0', sizeof p->zone_id) == NULL) return 0;\n    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);\n    snprintf(out->zone_id, sizeof out->zone_id, \"%s\", p->zone_id);\n    out->seed = p->seed;\n    out->players = (int)p->players;\n    out->state = (int)p->state;\n    out->idle_ms = p->idle_ms;\n    out->active = (p->state != 0) ? 1 : 0;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* Reload only for a zone that exists and is not the one already loaded. A repeated packet (1 Hz) must be\n * a no-op: reloading geometry every second would drop every decal, spray and cached shot in the world. */\nstatic inline int zone_sync_should_reload(const ZoneSync *loaded, const ZoneSync *incoming) {\n    if (!incoming || !incoming->active) return 0;\n    if (!loaded || !loaded->active) return 1;\n    if (strcmp(loaded->zone_id, incoming->zone_id) != 0) return 1;\n    if (loaded->seed != incoming->seed) return 1;\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/* Server side: one place builds the packet, so the encode cannot drift from the decode. */\nstatic inline void zone_sync_fill(NetZoneState *pkt, const char *zone_id, unsigned int seed, int players,\n                                  int state, unsigned int idle_ms, unsigned int now_ms) {\n    if (!pkt) return;\n    memset(pkt, 0, sizeof *pkt);\n    pkt->hdr.type = PACKET_ZONE_STATE;\n    pkt->hdr.client_id = 0;\n    pkt->hdr.timestamp = now_ms;\n    snprintf(pkt->zone_id, sizeof pkt->zone_id, \"%s\", (zone_id && zone_id[0]) ? zone_id : \"\");\n    pkt->seed = seed;\n    pkt->idle_ms = idle_ms;\n    pkt->players = (unsigned char)(players < 0 ? 0 : (players > 255 ? 255 : players));\n    pkt->state = (unsigned char)state;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_SYNC_H */\n"
}

\"zone_sync.h\"\n\nstatic int g_fail = 0, g_checks = 0;\nstatic void ok(int cond, const char *what) {\n    g_checks++;\n    if (!cond) { g_fail++; printf(\"FAIL  %s\\n\", what); }\n    else printf(\"ok    %s\\n\", what);\n}\n\nint main(void) {\n    NetZoneState pkt;\n    ZoneSync in, loaded;\n\n    ok(PACKET_ZONE_STATE != PACKET_SNAPSHOT && PACKET_ZONE_STATE != PACKET_WELCOME &&\n       PACKET_ZONE_STATE != PACKET_QUEUE_LEVEL && PACKET_ZONE_STATE != PACKET_BRICK_STATE &&\n       PACKET_ZONE_STATE != PACKET_WORLD_CLOCK && PACKET_ZONE_STATE != PACKET_SPRAY_DECAL,\n       \"the zone packet has its own wire type\");\n\n    zone_sync_fill(&pkt, \"dungeon_7\", 0xDEADBEEFu, 3, 1, 0, 1234);\n    ok(pkt.hdr.type == PACKET_ZONE_STATE && pkt.hdr.timestamp == 1234, \"fill stamps the header\");\n    ok(strcmp(pkt.zone_id, \"dungeon_7\") == 0 && pkt.seed == 0xDEADBEEFu, \"with the zone's identity\");\n    ok(pkt.players == 3 && pkt.state == 1 && pkt.idle_ms == 0, \"and its occupancy\");\n\n    memset(&in, 0, sizeof in);\n    ok(zone_sync_decode(&in, &pkt, (int)sizeof pkt) == 1, \"the packet decodes\");\n    ok(strcmp(in.zone_id, \"dungeon_7\") == 0 && in.seed == 0xDEADBEEFu && in.players == 3 && in.state == 1 &&\n       in.active == 1, \"with every field intact\");\n\n    /* refusals -- a packet is untrusted input */\n    ok(zone_sync_decode(&in, &pkt, (int)sizeof pkt - 1) == 0, \"a short datagram is refused\");\n    {\n        NetZoneState wrong = pkt;\n        wrong.hdr.type = PACKET_SNAPSHOT;\n        ok(zone_sync_decode(&in, &wrong, (int)sizeof wrong) == 0, \"the wrong packet type is refused\");\n    }\n    {\n        NetZoneState bad = pkt;\n        memset(bad.zone_id, 'A', sizeof bad.zone_id);   /* no terminator: not a safe filename */\n        ok(zone_sync_decode(&in, &bad, (int)sizeof bad) == 0, \"an unterminated zone id is refused\");\n    }\n    {\n        NetZoneState empty = pkt;\n        empty.zone_id[0] = '\\0';\n        ok(zone_sync_decode(&in, &empty, (int)sizeof empty) == 0, \"an empty zone id is refused\");\n    }\n\n    /* the reload decision: exactly once per real change */\n    memset(&loaded, 0, sizeof loaded);\n    ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, &in) == 1, \"nothing loaded yet: the first packet loads the zone\");\n\n    loaded = in;\n    {\n        ZoneSync repeat = in;\n        ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, &repeat) == 0, \"the same zone at 1 Hz does NOT reload the world\");\n    }\n    {\n        ZoneSync same_zone_new_seed = in;\n        same_zone_new_seed.seed = 12345u;\n        ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, &same_zone_new_seed) == 1,\n           \"the same zone id with a new seed reloads (it expired and regenerated)\");\n    }\n    {\n        ZoneSync other = in;\n        snprintf(other.zone_id, sizeof other.zone_id, \"dungeon_8\");\n        ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, &other) == 1, \"a different zone reloads\");\n    }\n    {\n        ZoneSync dead = in;\n        dead.state = 0;\n        dead.active = 0;\n        ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, &dead) == 0, \"an uninitialized zone never reloads anything\");\n        ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, NULL) == 0, \"and a missing packet is not a reload\");\n    }\n\n    /* occupancy and the idle countdown ride along so a client can show them */\n    zone_sync_fill(&pkt, \"dungeon_7\", 0xDEADBEEFu, 0, 2, 42000, 9000);\n    ok(zone_sync_decode(&in, &pkt, (int)sizeof pkt) == 1 && in.state == 2 && in.players == 0 && in.idle_ms == 42000,\n       \"an idle zone's countdown survives the wire\");\n    {\n        ZoneSync same = in;\n        ok(zone_sync_should_reload(&loaded, &same) == 0,\n           \"and an idle zone with the same seed does not reload (it is still the same dungeon)\");\n    }\n\n    /* clamping rather than wrapping */\n    zone_sync_fill(&pkt, \"dungeon_7\", 1u, 1000, 1, 0, 1);\n    ok(pkt.players == 255, \"an absurd player count clamps instead of wrapping\");\n    zone_sync_fill(&pkt, NULL, 1u, -5, 1, 0, 1);\n    ok(pkt.zone_id[0] == '\\0' && pkt.players == 0, \"a missing id becomes empty, a negative count becomes zero\");\n\n    printf(\"\\n%d checks, %d failed\\n\", g_checks, g_fail);\n    return g_fail ? 1 : 0;\n}\n"

Phase 2 is in and pushed: **SHANKPIT `0c5f44d`**, `master` clean and level with origin (PARENA unchanged, still in sync).

## What a LAN client now gets

**`PACKET_ZONE_STATE 17`** (`packages/common/protocol.h`) — a fixed, self-contained packet carrying the zone's *identity*: `zone_id`, `seed`, `players`, `state`, `idle_ms`. No boxes. Both sides run the same deterministic generator, which is only sound because `make test-proc-dungeon` proves one seed writes byte-identical level JSON.

**`packages/simulation/zone_sync.h`** — the testable seam between "a datagram arrived" and "reload the world":
- `zone_sync_decode` treats the packet as untrusted input: length, packet type, non-empty **NUL-terminated** id. That last one is a path-safety boundary, not pedantry — the host saves `var/maps/proc_<id>.json`, so a half-copied id is a filename.
- `zone_sync_should_reload` is true only when the zone id or the seed actually changed. This is the important one: a 1 Hz packet that reloaded every second would drop every spray, decal and cached shot in the world.
- `zone_sync_fill` builds the packet in one place, so encode can't drift from decode.

**Server** — `./bin/shank_server --dungeon [zone]` generates the zone once, applies it through the ordinary custom-level path, and broadcasts state at 1 Hz beside the snapshot. Occupancy is the connected player count: first client in generates, last one out starts the fifteen-minute countdown, an idle zone with the same seed doesn't reload (it's still the same dungeon), expiry deletes the layout, clears the seed, and the next arrival regenerates from a **new** seed — which is exactly what makes clients reload.

**Client** — decodes the packet, and when the id or seed changes, rebuilds the identical dungeon locally, loads it, and logs `ZONE_RX id=… seed=… (N boxes)`. A reconnect clears its learned zone.

## The bug the live run caught

`server_zone_begin` copied `g_server_zone_id` **into itself** with `snprintf`. Overlapping buffers are undefined and glibc produced `''` — so the server generated a zone, then advertised a nameless one and stopped broadcasting (its own "has an id" guard failed). Caught by actually running the server, not by compiling it: the log said `[ZONE] generated '' seed …`. Fixed by passing the caller's id through and guarding the copy; the same run now logs `[ZONE] generated 'dungeon_1' seed 002a7921 (41 boxes, difficulty 2)`.

## Checks actually run

- `make test-zone-sync` → **20 checks, 0 failed**: own wire type; every field round-trips; refuses a short datagram, the wrong type, an empty id and an unterminated id; repeated packet does **not** reload; new seed and new zone **do**; missing packet and uninitialized zone never reload; idle countdown survives the wire; absurd counts clamp instead of wrapping.
- **Live headless server**: `./bin/shank_server --dungeon dungeon_1` generated a zone, wrote `var/maps/proc_dungeon_1.json`, and `/tmp/lvlcheck` parsed it back — `41 boxes, 4 spawners, 3 materials, 3 widgets`. The runtime file was deleted afterwards; only the imported `gfd_town.json` is committed.
- `make test-proc-dungeon` **46**, `test-widget-circuit` **51**, `test-widget-runtime` **48**, `make check-windows` **101 sources**, `make -B server` exit 0 (with the pre-existing `reflux_host_action_c_at` warning).

## What this still isn't

- **No second process was connected.** The client's handler is compiled for mingw and its decision logic is unit-tested, but a real two-process LAN round trip wasn't exercised — there's no automated way to do that here, and I won't claim it.
- **No `--coop-host`.** The server is started separately; one command that hosts in-process and advertises on the LAN is phase 3.
- **No explicit "enter zone".** On the server, occupancy is presence, so the zone generates when the first client connects rather than when someone walks through a door. The registry already supports the lifecycle a portal trigger would call.
- **No menu tile**, and no render check (no GPU/display on this box).

Docs are current: `docs/PROC_DUNGEONS.md` (contract + how to run it) and `docs/GFD_UNIFICATION.md` (phase 2 marked shipped, phases 3–5 named).

/* server_broadcast_brick_state -- destructible brick (packages/simulation/brick_world.h), see
 * PACKET_BRICK_STATE in protocol.h. Sends this tick's brick-cell changes, scheduled repeats and a
 * slice of the rotating refresh to every welcomed client; sends nothing when no level with
 * destructible brick is loaded or nothing is due. Separate packet from the snapshot on purpose, same
 * reason server_broadcast_world_clock is: zero risk to the live snapshot path. */
void server_broadcast_brick_state(void) {
    if (!brick_world_is_active()) return;
    NetBrickState pkt;
    memset(&pkt, 0, sizeof(pkt));
    unsigned int now_ms = get_server_time();
    int n = brick_world_net_collect(pkt.e, NET_BRICK_MAX_ENTRIES, now_ms);
    if (n <= 0) return;
    pkt.hdr.type = PACKET_BRICK_STATE;
    pkt.hdr.client_id = 0;
    pkt.hdr.timestamp = now_ms;
    pkt.count = (unsigned char)n;
    int len = (int)(sizeof(NetHeader) + 4 + (size_t)n * sizeof(NetBrickEntry));
    for (int i = 1; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
        if (!slots[i].active || !slots[i].welcomed) continue;
        sendto(sock, (const char *)&pkt, len, 0, (struct sockaddr*)&slots[i].addr, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in));
    }
}

       * Until now the local NOCK map tools needed a separate `make local-nock` in another terminal (or a
       * Windows .bat) before the editor was reachable. As an APPS entry, NOCK is one click: it starts the
       * same server itself and opens http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ in the system browser, and the browser tab
       * plus the in-game EDIT MAP live session are the same room (levels save to levels/<name>.json and
       * are committed, exactly as `make local-nock` does).
       *
       * The server binary is the PARENA one: bin/local_nock_parena in a dev tree (make local-nock-parena),
       * or bundled/dw_nock{,.exe} in a packaged build. Everything the server needs is passed as ARGS
       * (--port/--root) rather than environment variables, because that is what CreateProcessA on Windows
       * can express without building an environment block.
       *
       * Deliberate behaviour: the server is spawned DETACHED, so it outlives the lobby and the editor keeps
       * working after quitting the game; and if the port already answers (a previous click, or the user's
       * own `make local-nock`), nothing is spawned -- this just re-opens the tab. */
      #define NOCK_LOCAL_PORT 8787
      
      static int nock_dir_exists(const char *path) {
          struct stat st;
          return stat(path, &st) == 0 && (st.st_mode & S_IFDIR) != 0;
      }
      
      /* nock_port_open -- is something already listening on the loopback port? A non-blocking connect with
       * a 100 ms budget: no DNS, no blocking connect, no sleeping for a fixed time and hoping. */
      static int nock_port_open(int port) {
          struct sockaddr_in addr;
          memset(&addr, 0, sizeof addr);
          addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
          addr.sin_port = htons((unsigned short)port);
          addr.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK);
      #ifdef _WIN32
          static int wsa_ready = 0;
          if (!wsa_ready) {
              WSADATA w;
              if (WSAStartup(MAKEWORD(2, 2), &w) == 0) wsa_ready = 1;
          }
          SOCKET s = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
          if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) return 0;
          u_long nonblocking = 1;
          ioctlsocket(s, FIONBIO, &nonblocking);
          int rc = connect(s, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof addr);
          if (rc != 0 && WSAGetLastError() != WSAEWOULDBLOCK) { closesocket(s); return 0; }
          fd_set wr;
          FD_ZERO(&wr);
          FD_SET(s, &wr);
          struct timeval tv;
          tv.tv_sec = 0;
          tv.tv_usec = 100000;
          rc = select(0, NULL, &wr, NULL, &tv);
          int ok = rc > 0;
          closesocket(s);
          return ok;
      #else
          int s = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
          if (s < 0) return 0;
          int flags = fcntl(s, F_GETFL, 0);
          fcntl(s, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK);
          int rc = connect(s, (struct sockaddr *)&addr, sizeof addr);
          if (rc == 0) { close(s); return 1; }
          if (errno != EINPROGRESS) { close(s); return 0; }
          fd_set wr;
          FD_ZERO(&wr);
          FD_SET(s, &wr);
          struct timeval tv;
          tv.tv_sec = 0;
          tv.tv_usec = 100000;
          rc = select(s + 1, NULL, &wr, NULL, &tv);
          int ok = rc > 0;
          if (ok) {
              int soerr = 0;
              socklen_t len = sizeof soerr;
              if (getsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_ERROR, &soerr, &len) == 0) ok = (soerr == 0);
          }
          close(s);
          return ok;
      #endif
      }

          if (nock_dir_exists(probe)) {

          } else {
              snprintf(probe, sizeof probe, "%sbundled/levels", base);

              else snprintf(root, sizeof root, "%s..", base);
          }

              snprintf(app_launch_status, sizeof app_launch_status,

          }
      
          int started = 0;

              STARTUPINFOA si;
              PROCESS_INFORMATION pi;
              ZeroMemory(&si, sizeof si);
              si.cb = sizeof si;
              ZeroMemory(&pi, sizeof pi);
              if (CreateProcessA(NULL, cmdline, NULL, NULL, FALSE, CREATE_NO_WINDOW, NULL, NULL, &si, &pi)) {

                  execl(server, server, "--port", "8787", "--root", root, (char *)NULL);

      LIBS_M   := -lm
      
      # ---- Sources ----
      EDU_LOBBY_SRC := packages/education/edu_lexer.c packages/education/edu_parser.c packages/education/edu_bytecode.c packages/education/edu_vm.c packages/education/edu_bindings.c packages/education/edu_script.c packages/education/eduvm_host.c packages/education/eduvm_snippets.c packages/education/eduvm_mod_unit.c
      LOBBY_SRC    := apps/lobby/src/main.c apps/lobby/src/editor_widget_bridge.c packages/simulation/story_ai.c packages/simulation/ai_nav.c packages/simulation/humanness.c packages/simulation/cutscene.c packages/simulation/typing_lesson.c packages/simulation/tyler_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_e03_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_fb01_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_vh02_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_vh03_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_vh04_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_voice_mod.c packages/simulation/day_night_clock.c packages/simulation/world_rules.c packages/simulation/witness_ai.c packages/simulation/witness_sim.c packages/simulation/witness_rules.c packages/simulation/npc_archetype.c packages/simulation/zombie_values.c packages/simulation/avian_values.c packages/simulation/ai_brain_rules.c packages/simulation/world_alerts_mod.c packages/simulation/world_alert_bridge.c packages/simulation/zombies_awareness_rules.c packages/simulation/zombies_hud_bridge.c packages/simulation/zombies_pheromone_rules.c packages/simulation/food_pickup.c packages/simulation/lab_station_host.c packages/simulation/lab_station_rules.c packages/simulation/shadow_war_host.c packages/simulation/shadow_war_rules.c packages/simulation/gun_items.c packages/simulation/chests.c packages/simulation/chest_rules.c packages/simulation/shield_packs.c packages/simulation/giant_bug_values.c packages/simulation/giant_bug_brain.c packages/render/proc_tex.c packages/render/retro_material.c packages/render/retro_sky.c packages/render/sky_weather.c packages/render/retro_lighting.c packages/render/env_matrix.c packages/render/gl_shader.c packages/render/bloom.c packages/world/terrain.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c packages/world/png_decode_gen.c packages/ui/menu_gen.c packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.c packages/audio/audio.c packages/audio/audio_wav.c packages/audio/audio_chain.c packages/audio/audio_dsp_gen.c packages/goldenband/gband.c packages/goldenband/gskel.c packages/goldenband/gmesh.c packages/goldenband/gband_mesh_rig.c packages/goldenband/gseq.c packages/goldenband/gpose.c packages/goldenband/gsync.c packages/goldenband/gband_skel_npc.c packages/reflux/reflux_runtime.c packages/reflux/reflux_mod.c packages/simulation/brick_mod.c packages/simulation/brick_bodies.c packages/simulation/ambient_rules.c packages/simulation/lighting_rules.c packages/simulation/structure_rules.c packages/simulation/buggy_rules.c packages/simulation/heli_rules.c packages/simulation/rocket_car_rules.c packages/simulation/drone_rules.c packages/simulation/airplane_rules.c packages/simulation/vehicle_burn_rules.c packages/simulation/br_stadium.c packages/simulation/anim_rules.c packages/simulation/slide_rules.c packages/simulation/empire_rules.c packages/render/camera_rules.c packages/simulation/ragdoll_pool.c packages/simulation/rigid_ragdoll.c packages/simulation/ragdoll_rules.c packages/goldenband/grb.c packages/simulation/mission.c packages/simulation/party_rules.c packages/simulation/chat_rules.c packages/simulation/hoverboard_rules.c packages/simulation/widget_rules.c packages/simulation/zone_rules.c $(EDU_LOBBY_SRC)
      SERVER_SRC   := apps/server/src/main.c packages/simulation/shield_packs.c packages/simulation/story_ai.c packages/simulation/ai_nav.c packages/simulation/humanness.c packages/simulation/tyler_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_e03_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_fb01_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_vh02_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_vh03_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_vh04_coldopen.c packages/simulation/tyler_voice_mod.c packages/simulation/day_night_clock.c packages/simulation/world_rules.c packages/simulation/witness_ai.c packages/simulation/witness_sim.c packages/simulation/witness_rules.c packages/simulation/npc_archetype.c packages/simulation/zombie_values.c packages/simulation/avian_values.c packages/simulation/ai_brain_rules.c packages/simulation/giant_bug_values.c packages/simulation/giant_bug_brain.c packages/simulation/zombies_awareness_rules.c packages/simulation/zombies_hud_bridge.c packages/simulation/zombies_pheromone_rules.c packages/world/terrain.c packages/reflux/reflux_runtime.c packages/reflux/reflux_mod.c packages/simulation/brick_mod.c packages/simulation/brick_bodies.c packages/simulation/structure_rules.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c packages/goldenband/grb.c packages/simulation/buggy_rules.c packages/simulation/heli_rules.c packages/simulation/rocket_car_rules.c packages/simulation/drone_rules.c packages/simulation/airplane_rules.c packages/simulation/br_stadium.c packages/simulation/zone_rules.c packages/simulation/widget_rules.c
      SERVERCTL_SRC:= apps/server/serverctl.c
      
      # ---- Source-list export for CI ----
      # CI (.github/workflows/{tests,release}.yml) compiles the Windows lobby and the Linux server with
      # raw gcc/mingw lines instead of `make` (different libs/flags). Those lines used to carry a
      # hand-copied copy of LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC and drifted NINE times -- including a 3-day red release
      # pipeline (2026-09-28..10-01) -- so they now expand these two targets instead:
      #   gcc $(make -s print-server-src) ...        x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc $(make -s print-lobby-src) ...
      # A new packages/*.c added to LOBBY_SRC/SERVER_SRC above is now picked up by CI automatically.
      .PHONY: print-lobby-src print-server-src test-os-menu test-os-menu-gl check-windows
      
      # Compile every Windows-client source under mingw-w64 (no link, so no .a/.dll objects needed). Catches
      # compile-only breakage that otherwise waits for a release job -- see the script's own header comment.
      check-windows:
        bash scripts/check_windows_build.sh
      print-lobby-src:
        @echo $(LOBBY_SRC)
      print-server-src:
        @echo $(SERVER_SRC)
      
      # ---- Outputs ----
      LOBBY_BIN    := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby
      SERVER_BIN   := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_server
      SERVERCTL_BIN:= $(BIN_DIR)/serverctl
      GO_SERVER_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server
      EMILY_BOT_BIN := $(BIN_DIR)/emily-bot
      EA_DIR       := dist/ea
      
      # ---- Targets ----
      .PHONY: test-witness-ai-zombies test-bullet-hole test-queue-level test-baked-levels test-level-save bake-levels all lobby server serverctl clean setup print go-server ea ea-windows emily-bot rigid-ragdoll test-physics test-audio-chain ux-screenshot-test
      
      all: $(LOBBY_BIN) $(SERVER_BIN)
      
      # Ensure bin/ exists even when building a single target
      $(BIN_DIR):
        @mkdir -p $(BIN_DIR)
      
      setup: $(BIN_DIR)
      
      # ---- EDITOR.GAME in-process widget (S559, 2026-09-27) ----
      # Founder real-time: "the editor app fails to launch -- instead of having it launch it should pop
      # a widget up on the screen ... deeply integrate it as a widget on the screen the notes auto
      # save." apps/lobby/src/editor_widget_bridge.c links against EDITOR.GAME's own real
      # editor_widget_* API, consumed as a sibling checkout (../EDITOR.GAME -- same path MODULE.bazel's
      # own local_path_override already assumes). Same 5-file build EDITOR.GAME's own plain Makefile
      # uses to produce its standalone `editor-game` binary, just linked into shank_lobby instead:
      # gen/editor_full.c (the generated PARENA stdlib + examples/editor_main.c, concatenated -- see
      # EDITOR.GAME/Makefile's own identical rule) and runtime/parena_runtime.c define/call the plain
      # arena_init/arena_alloc/arena_strdup/arena_free_all names, which would otherwise collide at link
      # time with SHANKPIT's own already-linked, deliberately-minimal packages/world/parena_runtime.c
      # (same 4 names, real but different, narrower implementation) -- both files are compiled here with
      # a matching -D rename so ONLY this pair's calls/definitions move to edg_arena_*, leaving
      # SHANKPIT's own copy completely untouched. src/arena.c/src/fmt.c/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c are
      # EDITOR.GAME's own SEPARATE compiler-internal bump allocator, already renamed to pf_arena_* by
      # EDITOR.GAME's own PRNFMT_RENAME convention (unrelated to the edg_arena_* rename above -- two
      # different collisions, two different renames, matching EDITOR.GAME's own Makefile/BUILD.bazel
      # precedent exactly).
      EDITOR_GAME_DIR    := ../EDITOR.GAME
      # vec_i32_at -- PARENA's C emitter generates this Vec<i32> helper as a plain global (not static)
      # in every translation unit that uses Vec<i32>; packages/world/png_decode_gen.c (SHANKPIT's own
      # PARENA-generated code, already in LOBBY_SRC) happens to generate one too, so it collides the
      # same way arena_init did -- confirmed via `nm -g` on both object files, exactly one overlap.
      EDITOR_GAME_RENAME := -Darena_init=edg_arena_init -Darena_alloc=edg_arena_alloc -Darena_strdup=edg_arena_strdup -Darena_free_all=edg_arena_free_all -Dvec_i32_at=edg_vec_i32_at
      EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT := -Darena_init=pf_arena_init -Darena_alloc=pf_arena_alloc -Darena_strdup=pf_arena_strdup -Darena_free_all=pf_arena_free_all
      EDITOR_GAME_OBJS   := $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.o
      
      $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_stdlib_gen.c $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/examples/editor_main.c
        cat $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_stdlib_gen.c $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/examples/editor_main.c > $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w -DEDITOR_WIDGET_TEST_BUILD $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/arena.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/fmt.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src -c $< -o $@
      
      # Windows (mingw) variants of the same 5 objects, for ea-windows below -- separate output
      # filenames (.win.o) so a native `make lobby` and `make ea-windows` in the same tree never clobber
      # each other's objects. Verified for real: EDITOR.GAME's own runtime/parena_runtime.c and
      # generated stdlib code cross-compile under x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc with no source changes at all
      # (checked directly, not assumed -- the only NEW cross-build requirement is SDL2_ttf's own mingw
      # devel kit, same one PITVIPER/IDUNA.GAME/EDITOR.GAME's own standalone Windows builds already need,
      # per SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX below).
      MINGW_CC := x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
      EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN := $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.win.o $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.win.o
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_full.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/gen/editor_full.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w -DEDITOR_WIDGET_TEST_BUILD $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_runtime.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/parena_runtime.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_RENAME) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_arena.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/arena.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_fmt.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src/fmt.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -c $< -o $@
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/editor_pf_bridge.win.o: $(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime/prnfmt_bridge.c | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(MINGW_CC) -std=c99 -w $(EDITOR_GAME_PRNFMT) -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/runtime -I$(EDITOR_GAME_DIR)/src -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      # ---- PELLEGRINO in-phone browser (SHANKPIT-PELLEGRINO-APP-02) ----
      # Pre-built objects linked at the end (NOT in LOBBY_SRC): needs its own mbedTLS copts/includes that
      # the rest of the lobby must never see. mbedTLS source comes from ../PELLEGRINO's pinned fetch script.
      PGB_DIR     := packages/pellegrino_browser_embed
      PELLEGRINO_DIR ?= ../PELLEGRINO
      PGB_MBEDTLS  = $(shell [ -d $(PELLEGRINO_DIR) ] && cd $(PELLEGRINO_DIR) && bash scripts/fetch_mbedtls.sh 2>/dev/null)
      PGB_DEFS    := -DPARENA_WITH_TLS -DPARENA_TLS_STATIC_HEAP -DPARENA_TLS_HEAP_STATS -DPARENA_WITH_QUIC_CRYPTO "-DMBEDTLS_USER_CONFIG_FILE=\"pellegrino_user_config.h\""
      PGB_OBJ_DIR := $(BIN_DIR)/pgb
      PGB_MBED_OBJS = $(patsubst %.c,$(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/mbed_%.o,$(notdir $(wildcard $(PGB_MBEDTLS)/library/*.c)))
      PGB_OBJS     = $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/phone_browser_embed.o $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/monocypher.o $(PGB_MBED_OBJS)
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR):
        mkdir -p $@
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/phone_browser_embed.o: $(PGB_DIR)/phone_browser_embed.c $(PGB_DIR)/pellegrino_gen.inc | $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -w $(PGB_DEFS) -I$(PGB_DIR) -I$(PGB_DIR)/runtime -I$(PGB_MBEDTLS)/include -c $< -o $@
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/monocypher.o: $(PGB_DIR)/runtime/aead/monocypher.c | $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -w -c $< -o $@
      
      $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)/mbed_%.o: | $(PGB_OBJ_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O2 -w $(PGB_DEFS) -I$(PGB_DIR)/runtime -I$(PGB_MBEDTLS)/include -I$(PGB_MBEDTLS)/library -c $(PGB_MBEDTLS)/library/$*.c -o $@
      
      # ---- CLIENT / LOBBY ----
      lobby: $(LOBBY_BIN)
      
      $(LOBBY_BIN): $(LOBBY_SRC) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS) $(PGB_OBJS) | $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🔨 Building Lobby Client..."
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LOBBY_SRC) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS) $(PGB_OBJS) -o $@ $(LIBS_GL) -lSDL2_ttf
      
      # ---- OS menu through PELLEGRINO (kanban #627) ----
      # Headless (SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy): builds the HTML menu, paints it with PELLEGRINO, clicks every tile, checks the
      # index mapping and keyboard activation. Links packages/world/parena_runtime.c too, to prove the pgm_ rename
      # (packages/pellegrino_embed/pg_rename.h) keeps the engine's runtime from colliding with the lobby's.
      test-os-menu: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -w -Ipackages/pellegrino_embed -Ipackages/world packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.c packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed_test.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_embed_test -lSDL2 -lm
        SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_embed_test
      
      # Same menu through the lobby's real GL path (packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_gl.h) in a real GL context:
      # needs a display (xvfb-run make test-os-menu-gl) and libGL; checks tile colours at screen positions + hit mapping.
      test-os-menu-gl: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -w -Ipackages/pellegrino_embed -Ipackages/world packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_embed.c packages/pellegrino_embed/os_menu_gl_test.c packages/world/parena_runtime.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_gl_test -lSDL2 -lGL -lm
        $(BIN_DIR)/os_menu_gl_test
      
      # ---- GAME SERVER ----
      server: $(SERVER_BIN)
      
      $(SERVER_BIN): $(SERVER_SRC) | $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🔨 Building Game Server..."
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(SERVER_SRC) -o $@ $(LIBS_M)
      
      # ---- RIGID BODY PHYSICS (GOLDEN BAND grb, vendored in packages/goldenband) ----
      # Founder real-time 2026-09-27: "upgrade shankpit ... to formal rigid body physics".
      PHYSICS_SRC := packages/simulation/rigid_ragdoll.c packages/goldenband/grb.c packages/goldenband/gskel.c packages/goldenband/gpose.c
      
      rigid-ragdoll: $(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll
      
      $(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll: tools/rigid_ragdoll/main.c $(PHYSICS_SRC) | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wextra $(INCLUDES) $^ -o $@ $(LIBS_M)
      
      # Headless physics tests (run from the repo root -- they load assets/goldenband/*.gskel).
      test-physics: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Wextra $(INCLUDES) packages/simulation/rigid_ragdoll_test.c $(PHYSICS_SRC) -o $(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll_test $(LIBS_M)
        ./$(BIN_DIR)/rigid_ragdoll_test
      
      # Real, live UX regression test -- boots the real lobby binary under headless Xvfb, opens the
      # real LEVELS overlay via a synthetic XTEST Enter keypress, fails if either screen renders
      # suspiciously close to solid black (the blank-screen symptom this was written to catch). Needs
      # lobby already built (make lobby); needs Xvfb/ImageMagick/python3-xlib installed.
      ux-screenshot-test: lobby
        ./scripts/ux_screenshot_test.sh
      
      # ---- SERVER CONTROL (OPTIONAL, LOCAL ONLY) ----
      serverctl: $(SERVERCTL_BIN)
      
      $(SERVERCTL_BIN): $(SERVERCTL_SRC) | $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🖥 Building Server Control (requires ncurses)..."
        $(CC) -O2 $< -o $@ -lncurses
      
      # ---- GO MATCHMAKER / SCENE SERVER ----
      go-server: $(GO_SERVER_BIN)
      
      $(GO_SERVER_BIN): $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "🔨 Building Go scene server..."
        GOWORK=off go build -o $(GO_SERVER_BIN) ./apps2/server-go/
      
      # ---- EMILY BOT (Go headless player) ----
      emily-bot: $(EMILY_BOT_BIN)
      
      $(EMILY_BOT_BIN): $(BIN_DIR)
        @echo "Building Emily bot client..."
        GOWORK=off go build -o $(EMILY_BOT_BIN) ./apps2/emily-bot/
      
      # ---- STEAM EA BUILD (Linux) ----
      # Packages: headless Go scene server + C lobby client + README into dist/ea/
      # Prerequisites: SDL2 + OpenGL development libraries installed
      ea: $(LOBBY_BIN) $(GO_SERVER_BIN)
        @echo "📦 Packaging EA build (Linux)..."
        @mkdir -p $(EA_DIR)
        @cp $(LOBBY_BIN)  $(EA_DIR)/shank_lobby
        @cp $(GO_SERVER_BIN) $(EA_DIR)/shank_go_server
        @cp docs/EA_BUILD.md $(EA_DIR)/README.txt
        @echo "✅ EA build ready at $(EA_DIR)/"
        @ls -lh $(EA_DIR)/
      
      # ---- STEAM EA BUILD (Windows cross-compile, requires mingw-w64) ----
      # Real, found-live fix (S459-41 follow-up): this target used to target i686-w64-mingw32-gcc, but
      # the only real mingw SDL2 dev kit checked out on this box (/tmp/sdl2_mingw) is x86_64, matching
      # the Go server's own GOARCH=amd64 above -- 32-bit and 64-bit mingw libs are never interchangeable
      # (verified live: linking against the x86_64 archive with the i686 compiler leaves real symbols
      # like SDL_GetError undefined, since the .o members are a different COFF machine type entirely).
      # SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX is overridable for a box with its dev kit somewhere else.
      SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX ?= /tmp/sdl2_mingw
      ea-windows: $(BIN_DIR) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN)
        @echo "🪟 Cross-compiling Go server for Windows..."
        GOWORK=off GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build -o $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server.exe ./apps2/server-go/
        @echo "🔨 Cross-compiling C client for Windows (requires x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc)..."
        # -lSDL2_ttf (S559, EDITOR.GAME in-process widget) needs SDL2_ttf's own mingw devel kit merged
        # into $(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX) -- same one PITVIPER/IDUNA.GAME/EDITOR.GAME's own standalone
        # Windows builds already fetch (see .github/workflows/release.yml's own "Install Dependencies"
        # step); the base SDL2 mingw devel kit alone does not ship it.
        # Real in-phone PELLEGRINO browser if scripts/build_pgb_windows.sh succeeds (needs ../PELLEGRINO), else the stub.
        -bash scripts/build_pgb_windows.sh $(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)
        x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) -I$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/include $(LOBBY_SRC) $(EDITOR_GAME_OBJS_WIN) \
          $(if $(wildcard $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/phone_browser_embed.o),$(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/phone_browser_embed.o $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/monocypher.o $(wildcard $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/mbed/*.o) -lbcrypt,packages/pellegrino_browser_embed/phone_browser_stub.c) \
          -o $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby.exe \
          -L$(SDL2_MINGW_PREFIX)/lib -lSDL2 -lSDL2_ttf -lopengl32 -lglu32 -lm -static-libgcc \
          -lws2_32 -ldinput8 -ldxguid -ldxerr8 -luser32 -lgdi32 -lwinmm -limm32 -lole32 -loleaut32 -lshell32 -lsetupapi -lversion -luuid
        @echo "📦 Packaging EA build (Windows)..."
        @mkdir -p dist/ea-windows
        @cp $(BIN_DIR)/shank_go_server.exe dist/ea-windows/
        @cp $(BIN_DIR)/shank_lobby.exe dist/ea-windows/
        @[ -f $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/cacert.pem ] && cp $(BIN_DIR)/pgb_win/cacert.pem dist/ea-windows/ || true
        @cp docs/EA_BUILD.md dist/ea-windows/README.txt
        @echo "✅ Windows EA build ready at dist/ea-windows/"
      
      clean:
        @echo "🧹 Cleaning..."
        rm -rf $(BIN_DIR) dist/
      
      print:
        @echo "LOBBY_BIN=$(LOBBY_BIN)"
        @echo "SERVER_BIN=$(SERVER_BIN)"
        @echo "GO_SERVER_BIN=$(GO_SERVER_BIN)"
        @echo "EA_DIR=$(EA_DIR)"
      
      # test-bullet-hole -- per-gun bullet-hole decals (2026-10-01): shot detection, slot/size/ray mapping,
      # ring buffer, and that the 4 NOCK-exported PNGs (PARENA-authored, ImageMagick-paletted) decode through
      # PARENA's own png_decode. No SDL/GL needed.
      test-bullet-hole:
        $(CC) -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Ipackages/world -o /tmp/bullet_hole_test packages/world/bullet_hole_test.c \
