- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/scripts/gen_zone_rules.sh
  content: |
      #!/usr/bin/env bash
      # gen_zone_rules.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/zone_rules.c from PARENA.
      #
      # Shared (instanceless) zones: the 15-minute grace period and the procedural layout parameters live in
      #   PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn
      # packages/simulation/zone_registry.h runs the lifecycle and packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h builds a
      # layout from one seed, so a zone is reproducible on every machine running this build.
      # Usage: scripts/gen_zone_rules.sh   (needs ../PARENA, or PARENA_DIR)
      set -euo pipefail
      root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
      parena_dir="${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}"
      if [ -x "$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      elif [ -x "$parena_dir/parena" ]; then
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/parena"
      else
          (cd "$parena_dir" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)
          parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
      fi
      "$parena_bin" build "$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn" \
          -o "$root/packages/simulation/zone_rules.c"
      echo "regenerated packages/simulation/zone_rules.c"
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/zone_rules.h
  content: |
      /* zone_rules.h -- shared zone lifecycle + procedural layout rules, with built-in defaults.
       *
       * The numbers live in PARENA (PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn, generated into zone_rules.c by
       * scripts/gen_zone_rules.sh / `make regen-zone-rules`, installed through zone_rules_host.h). This header
       * carries matching C defaults so packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h and zone_registry.h compile and run
       * in any binary or test without linking a generated file -- the same arrangement widget_rules.h and
       * slide_rules.h use, and `make test-proc-dungeon` asserts the two copies agree sample for sample.
       *
       * Two separate concerns share this table on purpose, because both are "the zone's own numbers":
       *   - LIFECYCLE: grace seconds, max live zones, the expiry predicate.
       *   - LAYOUT: rooms, sizes, wall height, doors, spawners, material kind, difficulty tier.
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H
      #define SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H
      
      typedef struct {
          int (*grace_seconds)(void);
          int (*max_zones)(void);
          int (*room_count)(int seed);
          int (*room_width)(int seed, int room);
          int (*room_depth)(int seed, int room);
          int (*wall_height)(int seed);
          int (*wall_thickness)(void);
          int (*door_width)(void);
          int (*ring_distance)(void);
          int (*ring_dir_x)(int dir);
          int (*ring_dir_z)(int dir);
          int (*spawn_count)(int seed);
          int (*mob_count)(int seed, int rooms);
          int (*material_count)(void);
          int (*material_for)(int seed, int idx);
          int (*difficulty)(int seed);
          int (*should_expire)(int players, int idle_ms);
          int (*elapsed_ms)(int now_ms, int since_ms);
      } ZoneRules;
      
      static inline int zr_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }
      
      static inline int zr_c_grace_seconds(void) { return 900; }
      static inline int zr_c_max_zones(void) { return 8; }
      static inline int zr_c_room_count(int seed) { return 3 + zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_room_width(int seed, int room) { return 24 + 8 * zr_clamp(0, 2, (seed + room * 37) % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_room_depth(int seed, int room) { return 24 + 8 * zr_clamp(0, 2, (seed + room * 53) % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_wall_height(int seed) { return 18 + 6 * zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_wall_thickness(void) { return 2; }
      static inline int zr_c_door_width(void) { return 8; }
      static inline int zr_c_ring_distance(void) { return 52; }
      static inline int zr_c_ring_dir_x(int dir) {
          dir = zr_clamp(0, 3, dir);
          return dir == 0 ? 1 : (dir == 2 ? -1 : 0);
      }
      static inline int zr_c_ring_dir_z(int dir) {
          dir = zr_clamp(0, 3, dir);
          return dir == 1 ? 1 : (dir == 3 ? -1 : 0);
      }
      static inline int zr_c_spawn_count(int seed) { return 3 + zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_mob_count(int seed, int rooms) {
          return 2 * zr_clamp(1, 8, rooms) + seed % 5;
      }
      static inline int zr_c_material_count(void) { return 3; }
      static inline int zr_c_material_for(int seed, int idx) { return (seed + idx * 7) % 3; }
      static inline int zr_c_difficulty(int seed) { return 1 + zr_clamp(0, 4, seed % 5); }
      static inline int zr_c_should_expire(int players, int idle_ms) {
          if (zr_clamp(0, 1000, players) > 0) return 0;
          return zr_clamp(0, 2000000000, idle_ms) >= zr_c_grace_seconds() * 1000 ? 1 : 0;
      }
      static inline int zr_c_elapsed_ms(int now_ms, int since_ms) { return now_ms > since_ms ? now_ms - since_ms : 0; }
      
      static ZoneRules g_zone_rules = {
          zr_c_grace_seconds, zr_c_max_zones, zr_c_room_count, zr_c_room_width, zr_c_room_depth,
          zr_c_wall_height, zr_c_wall_thickness, zr_c_door_width, zr_c_ring_distance, zr_c_ring_dir_x,
          zr_c_ring_dir_z, zr_c_spawn_count, zr_c_mob_count, zr_c_material_count, zr_c_material_for,
          zr_c_difficulty, zr_c_should_expire, zr_c_elapsed_ms
      };
      
      static inline void zone_rules_set(const ZoneRules *r) { if (r) g_zone_rules = *r; }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H */

      // Package job implements FFXI-parity job definitions for DragonsNShit.
      //
      // # Job system
      //
      // 22 base jobs are defined as string IDs (FFXI-canonical abbreviations).
      // Each job has a base stat table (HP/MP + six primary stats).
      // HPAtLevel and MPAtLevel use simplified FFXI-style scaling:
      //   HP = BaseHP + (HPPerLevel * level)
      //   MP = BaseMP + (MPPerLevel * level)
      //
      // Stats are purely informational here; combat application is done by the combat package.
      package job
      
      import "errors"
      
      // JobID is a string abbreviation for a job (e.g. "WAR", "WHM").
      type JobID = string
      
      // All 22 base job IDs — FFXI canonical.
      const (
        WAR = "WAR" // Warrior
        MNK = "MNK" // Monk
        WHM = "WHM" // White Mage
        BLM = "BLM" // Black Mage
        RDM = "RDM" // Red Mage
        THF = "THF" // Thief
        PLD = "PLD" // Paladin
        DRK = "DRK" // Dark Knight
        BST = "BST" // Beastmaster
        BRD = "BRD" // Bard
        RNG = "RNG" // Ranger
        SAM = "SAM" // Samurai
        NIN = "NIN" // Ninja
        DRG = "DRG" // Dragoon
        SMN = "SMN" // Summoner
        BLU = "BLU" // Blue Mage
        COR = "COR" // Corsair
        PUP = "PUP" // Puppetmaster
        DNC = "DNC" // Dancer
        SCH = "SCH" // Scholar
        GEO = "GEO" // Geomancer
        RUN = "RUN" // Rune Fencer
      
        // ASN (Assassin) is a real, new, non-FFXI-canonical 23rd job (GFD-JOB-244122, founder:
        // "NEW CLASS ENFEEBLE DD SUPPORT SUSTAIN (sorta like DNC)... can cast aoe buffs like a
        // bard for different poisons that have different impacts on the different mob types...
        // mp regen affordances"). A real, deliberate hybrid: DEX/AGI-focused damage dealer (the
        // "DD" half) with two support/utility abilities (see subjob.go's AssassinAbilities) --
        // an AoE poison JA scaled per real mob-Kind resistance (undead-tagged kinds resist it,
        // matching real FFXI's own undead-resist-poison convention) and an MP-regen support JA
        // (the "sustain" half, same real mechanism Bard's own Ballad song already uses).
        ASN = "ASN" // Assassin
      )
      
      // AllJobs lists all 23 jobs in FFXI definition order, plus this repo's own real ASN addition.
      var AllJobs = []JobID{WAR, MNK, WHM, BLM, RDM, THF, PLD, DRK, BST, BRD, RNG, SAM, NIN, DRG, SMN, BLU, COR, PUP, DNC, SCH, GEO, RUN, ASN}
      
      var ErrUnknownJob = errors.New("unknown job ID")
      
      // Stats holds the base stat block for a job at level 1.
      // HP/MP grow via HPPerLevel/MPPerLevel each level.
      type Stats struct {
        BaseHP     int
        HPPerLevel int
        BaseMP     int
        MPPerLevel int
        STR        int
        DEX        int
        VIT        int
        AGI        int
        INT        int
        MND        int
        CHR        int
      }
      
      // jobStats is the base stat table for all 22 jobs.
      // Values are approximate FFXI parity (simplified for DragonsNShit).
      var jobStats = map[JobID]Stats{
        WAR: {BaseHP: 90,  HPPerLevel: 15, BaseMP: 0,  MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 8, DEX: 7, VIT: 8, AGI: 6, INT: 5, MND: 5, CHR: 5},
        MNK: {BaseHP: 100, HPPerLevel: 16, BaseMP: 0,  MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 8, DEX: 8, VIT: 8, AGI: 7, INT: 4, MND: 4, CHR: 5},
        WHM: {BaseHP: 65,  HPPerLevel: 10, BaseMP: 85,  MPPerLevel: 14, STR: 5, DEX: 5, VIT: 5, AGI: 5, INT: 6, MND: 9, CHR: 8},
        BLM: {BaseHP: 55,  HPPerLevel: 8,  BaseMP: 100, MPPerLevel: 16, STR: 4, DEX: 5, VIT: 4, AGI: 5, INT: 9, MND: 7, CHR: 5},
        RDM: {BaseHP: 70,  HPPerLevel: 11, BaseMP: 75,  MPPerLevel: 12, STR: 6, DEX: 6, VIT: 5, AGI: 6, INT: 7, MND: 7, CHR: 7},
        THF: {BaseHP: 75,  HPPerLevel: 12, BaseMP: 0,   MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 6, DEX: 9, VIT: 6, AGI: 9, INT: 6, MND: 5, CHR: 6},
        PLD: {BaseHP: 95,  HPPerLevel: 15, BaseMP: 60,  MPPerLevel: 9,  STR: 8, DEX: 6, VIT: 9, AGI: 5, INT: 5, MND: 7, CHR: 7},
        DRK: {BaseHP: 90,  HPPerLevel: 14, BaseMP: 45,  MPPerLevel: 8,  STR: 9, DEX: 6, VIT: 7, AGI: 5, INT: 6, MND: 5, CHR: 4},
        BST: {BaseHP: 80,  HPPerLevel: 13, BaseMP: 0,   MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 7, DEX: 7, VIT: 7, AGI: 7, INT: 5, MND: 5, CHR: 7},
        BRD: {BaseHP: 65,  HPPerLevel: 10, BaseMP: 50,  MPPerLevel: 9,  STR: 5, DEX: 7, VIT: 5, AGI: 7, INT: 6, MND: 6, CHR: 9},
        RNG: {BaseHP: 75,  HPPerLevel: 12, BaseMP: 0,   MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 7, DEX: 8, VIT: 6, AGI: 8, INT: 6, MND: 5, CHR: 5},
        SAM: {BaseHP: 85,  HPPerLevel: 14, BaseMP: 0,   MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 8, DEX: 7, VIT: 7, AGI: 7, INT: 6, MND: 6, CHR: 5},
        NIN: {BaseHP: 75,  HPPerLevel: 12, BaseMP: 20,  MPPerLevel: 6,  STR: 6, DEX: 9, VIT: 6, AGI: 9, INT: 6, MND: 5, CHR: 5},
        DRG: {BaseHP: 85,  HPPerLevel: 14, BaseMP: 0,   MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 8, DEX: 6, VIT: 8, AGI: 6, INT: 5, MND: 6, CHR: 6},
        SMN: {BaseHP: 60,  HPPerLevel: 9,  BaseMP: 90,  MPPerLevel: 15, STR: 4, DEX: 4, VIT: 4, AGI: 5, INT: 7, MND: 8, CHR: 7},
        BLU: {BaseHP: 80,  HPPerLevel: 13, BaseMP: 55,  MPPerLevel: 9,  STR: 7, DEX: 7, VIT: 6, AGI: 6, INT: 7, MND: 6, CHR: 5},
        COR: {BaseHP: 70,  HPPerLevel: 11, BaseMP: 45,  MPPerLevel: 8,  STR: 6, DEX: 8, VIT: 5, AGI: 8, INT: 6, MND: 6, CHR: 6},
        PUP: {BaseHP: 75,  HPPerLevel: 12, BaseMP: 30,  MPPerLevel: 6,  STR: 7, DEX: 8, VIT: 6, AGI: 7, INT: 6, MND: 5, CHR: 5},
        DNC: {BaseHP: 80,  HPPerLevel: 13, BaseMP: 0,   MPPerLevel: 0,  STR: 7, DEX: 8, VIT: 7, AGI: 8, INT: 5, MND: 5, CHR: 7},
        SCH: {BaseHP: 55,  HPPerLevel: 8,  BaseMP: 95,  MPPerLevel: 15, STR: 4, DEX: 5, VIT: 4, AGI: 5, INT: 8, MND: 8, CHR: 6},
        GEO: {BaseHP: 60,  HPPerLevel: 9,  BaseMP: 85,  MPPerLevel: 14, STR: 5, DEX: 5, VIT: 5, AGI: 5, INT: 8, MND: 8, CHR: 7},
        RUN: {BaseHP: 80,  HPPerLevel: 13, BaseMP: 40,  MPPerLevel: 7,  STR: 7, DEX: 7, VIT: 7, AGI: 7, INT: 6, MND: 6, CHR: 6},
        // ASN: DEX/AGI-focused DD (real STR/DEX/AGI band close to THF/DNC), with enough MP for its
        // own two real support JAs (venom/siphon, subjob.go) -- not a caster, so BaseMP sits well
        // below any real magic-user job, closer to PLD/DRK's "some MP for a few real abilities."
        ASN: {BaseHP: 78,  HPPerLevel: 12, BaseMP: 45,  MPPerLevel: 8,  STR: 7, DEX: 9, VIT: 6, AGI: 8, INT: 5, MND: 6, CHR: 6},
      }
      
      // StatsFor returns the base stats for the given job.
      func StatsFor(job JobID) (Stats, error) {
        s, ok := jobStats[job]
        if !ok {
          return Stats{}, ErrUnknownJob
        }
        return s, nil
      }
      
      // HPAtLevel returns the total HP for a job at the given level (1-based).
      // Level 0 returns BaseHP.
      func HPAtLevel(job JobID, level int) (int, error) {
        s, err := StatsFor(job)
        if err != nil {
          return 0, err
        }
        if level < 1 {
          level = 1
        }
        return s.BaseHP + s.HPPerLevel*(level-1), nil
      }
      
      // MPAtLevel returns the total MP for a job at the given level.
      // Jobs with BaseMP=0 always return 0 (melee jobs have no MP in FFXI).
      func MPAtLevel(job JobID, level int) (int, error) {
        s, err := StatsFor(job)
        if err != nil {
          return 0, err
        }
        if s.BaseMP == 0 {
          return 0, nil
        }
        if level < 1 {
          level = 1
        }
        return s.BaseMP + s.MPPerLevel*(level-1), nil
      }
      
      // AllJobsCount returns the number of defined jobs.
      func AllJobsCount() int { return len(AllJobs) }

Use `sb-health(job,level)` = clamp(1..255, hp/2)? Hmm: WAR lvl1 hp=90 → 45 health in engine units? Better define: engine health scale = 1 unit per 2 GFD HP, capped 255. Document honestly as "our conversion, because the engine's health is a small integer".

A THF is 4% quicker than a Warrior; it is not a different game.\n(defn sb-move-permille [(job : I32)] : I32\n  (sb-clamp 850 1150 (+ 1000 (* (- (sb-agi job) 5) 10))))\n\n;; Crit chance in permille, DEX-based off a 5% baseline -- THF/NIN/ASN (DEX 9) reach 11%.\n(defn sb-crit-permille [(job : I32)] : I32\n  (sb-clamp 0 400 (+ 50 (* (- (sb-dex job) 5) 15))))\n\n;; Evasion, AGI plus level. Deliberately a SCALAR on the weapon's own\n;; WPN_STATS dmg rather than a flat number: a knife stays a knife, a hammer stays a hammer.\n(defn sb-damage-permille [(job : I32) (level : I32)] : I32\n  (sb-clamp 600 2000 (+ 1000 (* (- (sb-str job) 5) 30) (* (- (sb-level level) 1) 5))))\n\n;; GFD's HP in SHANKPIT's health units. The engine's wire field is an unsigned char (0..255) and its\n;; default pool is 100, so a level-1 mage is squishier than a Warrior and a level-75 anything caps out\n;; rather than wrapping to zero on the wire -- the one failure mode that would be worse than a nerf.\n(defn sb-health [(job : I32) (level : I32)] : I32\n  (sb-clamp 10 255 (sb-hp job level)))\n"
}

This header carries numerically identical C\n * defaults so any binary or test can use the bridge without linking the generated file -- the same\n * arrangement zone_rules.h / widget_rules.h / slide_rules.h already keep, and which\n * `make test-stats-bridge` enforces by comparing the two copies sample for sample.\n *\n * Phase 4 of docs/GFD_UNIFICATION.md, and the boundary it draws matters more than the numbers:\n *\n *   - The TABLE is GFD's, copied from GoblinFoxDragon/server/job/job.go (23 jobs, AllJobs order,\n *     including GFD's own 23rd job ASN). If GFD retunes a job, this table is what gets updated.\n *   - The MAPPING (haste/move/crit/evade/damage) is THIS engine's, because GFD resolves damage against\n *     a mob registry and a dice model that do not exist here. Everything here is I32 permille so the\n *     arithmetic is identical on every host and no float ever enters a replicated number.\n *\n * Deliberately strict about what it is NOT: no spells, no abilities, no loot, no party mechanics, no\n * mobs. }\nstatic inline int sb_c_level(int level) { return sb_clamp(1, SB_LEVEL_MAX, level); }\nstatic inline int sb_c_job(int job) { return sb_clamp(0, SB_JOB_COUNT - 1, job); }\n\n/* job.go's jobStats, in AllJobs order: {BaseHP, HPPerLevel, BaseMP, MPPerLevel, STR, DEX, VIT, AGI} */\nstatic const int SB_C_TABLE[SB_JOB_COUNT][8] = {\n    { 90, 15,   0,  0, 8, 7, 8, 6 }, /* WAR */\n    {100, 16,   0,  0, 8, 8, 8, 7 }, /* MNK */\n    { 65, 10,  85, 14, 5, 5, 5, 5 }, /* WHM */\n    { 55,  8, 100, 16, 4, 5, 4, 5 }, /* BLM */\n    { 70, 11,  75, 12, 6, 6, 5, 6 }, /* RDM */\n    { 75, 12,   0,  0, 6, 9, 6, 9 }, /* THF */\n    { 95, 15,  60,  9, 8, 6, 9, 5 }, /* PLD */\n    { 90, 14,  45,  8, 9, 6, 7, 5 }, /* DRK */\n    { 80, 13,   0,  0, 7, 7, 7, 7 }, /* BST */\n    { 65, 10,  50,  9, 5, 7, 5, 7 }, /* BRD */\n    { 75, 12,   0,  0, 7, 8, 6, 8 }, /* RNG */\n    { 85, 14,   0,  0, 8, 7, 7, 7 }, /* SAM */\n    { 75, 12,  20,  6, 6, 9, 6, 9 }, /* NIN */\n    { 85, 14,   0,  0, 8, 6, 8, 6 }, /* DRG */\n    { 60,  9,  90, 15, 4, 4, 4, 5 }, /* SMN */\n    { 80, 13,  55,  9, 7, 7, 6, 6 }, /* BLU */\n    { 70, 11,  45,  8, 6, 8, 5, 8 }, /* COR */\n    { 75, 12,  30,  6, 7, 8, 6, 7 }, /* PUP */\n    { 80, 13,   0,  0, 7, 8, 7, 8 }, /* DNC */\n    { 55,  8,  95, 15, 4, 5, 4, 5 }, /* SCH */\n    { 60,  9,  85, 14, 5, 5, 5, 5 }, /* GEO */\n    { 80, 13,  40,  7, 7, 7, 7, 7 }, /* RUN */\n    { 78, 12,  45,  8, 7, 9, 6, 8 }  /* ASN */\n};\n\nstatic inline int sb_c_hp_base(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][0]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_hp_per(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][1]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_mp_base(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][2]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_mp_per(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][3]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_str(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][4]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_dex(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][5]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_vit(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][6]; }\nstatic inline int sb_c_agi(int job) { return SB_C_TABLE[sb_c_job(job)][7]; }\n\nstatic inline int sb_c_hp(int job, int level) {\n    return sb_c_hp_base(job) + sb_c_hp_per(job) * (sb_c_level(level) - 1);\n}\nstatic inline int sb_c_mp(int job, int level) {\n    return sb_c_mp_base(job) + sb_c_mp_per(job) * (sb_c_level(level) - 1);\n}\nstatic inline int sb_c_haste_permille(int job, int level) {\n    return sb_clamp(700, 1300, 1000 + (sb_c_agi(job) - 5) * 20 + (sb_c_level(level) - 1) * 2);\n}\nstatic inline int sb_c_cooldown(int rof, int haste_permille) {\n    return sb_clamp(1, 999, (sb_clamp(1, 999, rof) * sb_clamp(700, 1300, haste_permille)) / 1000);\n}\nstatic inline int sb_c_move_permille(int job) { return sb_clamp(850, 1150, 1000 + (sb_c_agi(job) - 5) * 10); }\nstatic inline int sb_c_crit_permille(int job) { return sb_clamp(0, 400, 50 + (sb_c_dex(job) - 5) * 15); }\nstatic inline int sb_c_evade_permille(int job, int level) {\n    return sb_clamp(0, 350, (sb_c_agi(job) - 5) * 12 + (sb_c_level(level) - 1) * 3);\n}\nstatic inline int sb_c_damage_permille(int job, int level) {\n    return sb_clamp(600, 2000, 1000 + (sb_c_str(job) - 5) * 30 + (sb_c_level(level) - 1) * 5);\n}\nstatic inline int sb_c_health(int job, int level) { return sb_clamp(10, 255, sb_c_hp(job, level)); }\n\nstatic StatsBridge g_stats_bridge = {\n    sb_c_hp_base, sb_c_hp_per, sb_c_mp_base, sb_c_mp_per, sb_c_str, sb_c_dex, sb_c_vit, sb_c_agi,\n    sb_c_hp, sb_c_mp, sb_c_haste_permille, sb_c_cooldown, sb_c_move_permille, sb_c_crit_permille,\n    sb_c_evade_permille, sb_c_damage_permille, sb_c_health\n};\n\nstatic inline void stats_bridge_set(const StatsBridge *b) { if (b) g_stats_bridge = *b; }\n\n/* Job id <-> name. 0 (WAR) for anything unknown, matching the rules' own fallback, so a bad id in a save\n * file is a Warrior rather than an out-of-bounds read.   "instructions": "Add the PARENA regeneration script for the stats bridge.",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# gen_stats_bridge.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/stats_bridge.c from PARENA.\n#\n# GFD's job table and the mapping into SHANKPIT's gameplay units live in\n#   PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/stats_bridge.prn\n# packages/simulation/stats_bridge.h carries identical C defaults, and `make test-stats-bridge` compares\n# the two copies sample for sample, so a retune cannot reach only one of them.\n# Usage: scripts/gen_stats_bridge.sh   (needs ../PARENA, or PARENA_DIR)\nset -euo pipefail\nroot=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nparena_dir=\"${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}\"\nif [ -x \"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nelif [ -x \"$parena_dir/parena\" ]; then\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/parena\"\nelse\n    (cd \"$parena_dir\" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)\n    parena_bin=\"$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap\"\nfi\n\"$parena_bin\" build \"$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/stats_bridge.prn\" \\\n    -o \"$root/packages/simulation/stats_bridge.c\"\necho \"regenerated packages/simulation/stats_bridge.c\"\n"
}

Both repos synced: **SHANKPIT `e8daf57`**, **PARENA `e95d7f4`**.

## What shipped: phase 4's bridge

GFD's job model now exists in this engine as numbers, with a boundary that keeps both sides honest.

**The table is GFD's.** Read from `GoblinFoxDragon/server/job/job.go`, not reconstructed: 23 jobs in `AllJobs` order, including GFD's own non-canonical 23rd job (ASN), each with base HP/MP, per-level curves, and its primaries. It's copied verbatim into `PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/stats_bridge.prn` → `packages/simulation/stats_bridge.c`. Retuning a job stays GFD's decision; this file must not quietly invent a different Warrior.

**The mapping is ours**, because GFD resolves damage against a mob registry and a dice model that don't exist here. All integer permille:

- **Haste** is a multiplier on a weapon's own ROF ticks (knife 20, AR 6, sniper 52) — never a rewrite of them, so a knife stays a knife.
- **Damage** is a scalar on `WPN_STATS.dmg` for the same reason.
- **Movement** is deliberately narrow (850–1150) so the vehicle and terrain tuning still reads right.
- **Evade** caps at 35%, because a 60 Hz shooter can't sell invisible hits.
- **Health** clamps at **255** — `NetPlayer.health` is an `unsigned char`, and capping beats wrapping to zero on the wire.

The plan's boundary holds: `stats_bridge.h` is a flat `StatsBridge` of function pointers over plain ints, so **no C file learns about 23 jobs**, and it carries identical C defaults so any binary or test works without linking generated code.

## Checks actually run

- **`make test-stats-bridge` — 40 checks, 0 failed.** All 23 jobs' eight base values match an **independent transcription of `job.go`** (a slip in either place fails rather than shipping a nerfed Warrior); the generated rules and the C header agree on **every derived number for all 23 jobs at levels −2..80**, plus cooldown across ROF 0..60 × haste 600..1400; GFD's curve is exact (WAR 90 → 105 → linear to 75 → flat past it); melee jobs have no MP at any level while casters grow; a 20-tick ROF never becomes 0 or a 999-tick monster; out-of-range ids are real lookups, not reads past the table.
- **`make regen-stats-bridge` runs twice to the same md5**, so the checked-in C matches the `.prn` — the generated file isn't a stale snapshot.

## A bug the test caught — in my own contract

The name helper clamped an unknown id to **ASN** while its doc promised **WAR**. The test encoded the intended contract and failed. Fixed in the helper, and the rules' comment now states the real, deliberately asymmetric fallback: a negative id reads as WAR, an id past the table as ASN — a corrupt id gets the first job, an exhausted search gets the last.

## Limits, named

- **Nothing applies a job to a live match yet.** No call site reads the bridge, so a player is still 100 HP and stock ROF whatever a save says. This is rules + verified mapping, not a wired progression system.
- Equipment and elemental affinities are untouched — they need GFD's item model.
- Nothing persists; the dungeon's `difficulty` tier is generated but not yet fed into a stat curve.

`docs/GFD_UNIFICATION.md` marks phase 4 shipped with exactly those gaps, and the CHANGELOG carries the test numbers.

      /* anim_state.h -- which animation clip a player is playing, for an imported N-joint skin.
       *
       * The decision is PARENA's (PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/anim_rules.prn, generated into anim_rules.c by
       * `make regen-anim-rules`); this header is the host: it reads the engine's real PlayerState fields,
       * maps protocol.h's weapon ids onto the three melee classes, and publishes the clip-name contract an
       * imported Mixamo/GBAND bundle has to satisfy.
       *
       * WHY A TABLE OF NAMES: the spec asks an imported skin to "bundle or map to" thirteen sequences.
       * GOLDENBAND clips are channel-name-blind (gband.h) and the kit loader takes clip names as strings
       * (gband_skel_npc_load_kit), so the contract is a fixed list of names -- an importer renames its
       * Mixamo clips to these, or it fails loudly at load instead of silently playing the idle for
       * everything. The names are lowercase and hyphen-free because they become file stems
       * (<asset_dir>/<name>.gband + .gband.json).
       *
       * NOT DONE, and named: nothing here draws anything yet. The player's own body still goes through
       * main.c's procedural compute_player_anim_pose, and no imported skin has these clips on disk -- so
       * anim_state_clip_name() returns the contract, not a loaded clip. Wiring it means the kit loader
       * gaining a clip-set concept (13 names per kit instead of idle/walk/greet/dance) and the player draw
       * path switching from procedural poses to gseq. That is the next slice, not a claim this one makes.
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_ANIM_STATE_H
      #define SHANKPIT_ANIM_STATE_H
      
      #include "protocol.h"
      
      /* State ids, mirroring anim_rules.prn's own doc comment and table order. */
      enum {
          ANIM_IDLE = 0, ANIM_WALK, ANIM_RUN, ANIM_CROUCH_IDLE, ANIM_CROUCH_WALK,
          ANIM_JUMP_START, ANIM_IN_AIR, ANIM_SLIDE, ANIM_WEAPON_FIRE, ANIM_RELOAD,
          ANIM_MELEE_SWING, ANIM_ABILITY, ANIM_CLIMB_LOOP, ANIM_STATE_COUNT
      };
      
      /* Melee classes (the only three weapons with a swing window). */
      enum { ANIM_MELEE_LIGHT = 0, ANIM_MELEE_KATANA = 1, ANIM_MELEE_HAMMER = 2, ANIM_MELEE_NONE = 3 };
      
      /* ---- PARENA-generated (anim_rules.c) ---- */
      int anim_state_count(void);
      int anim_state_select(int grounded, int crouching, int speed_milli, int jump_ticks, int slide_ticks,
                            int fire_ticks, int reload_ticks, int melee_ticks, int ability_ticks, int climb);
      int anim_state_loops(int state);
      int anim_state_additive(int state);
      int anim_state_blend_ms(int state);
      int anim_speed_band(int speed_milli);
      int anim_melee_ticks(int kind);
      int anim_eye_height_mm(int crouching);
      int anim_walk_speed_milli(void);
      int anim_run_speed_milli(void);
      int anim_jump_start_ticks(void);
      int anim_melee_kind_light(void);
      int anim_melee_kind_katana(void);
      int anim_melee_kind_hammer(void);
      
      /* ---- the clip-name contract ------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      static inline const char *anim_state_clip_name(int state) {
          static const char *const names[ANIM_STATE_COUNT] = {
              "anim_idle", "anim_walk", "anim_run", "anim_crouch_idle", "anim_crouch_walk",
              "anim_jump_start", "anim_in_air", "anim_slide", "anim_weapon_fire", "anim_reload",
              "anim_melee_swing", "anim_ability", "anim_climb_loop"
          };
          if (state < 0 || state >= ANIM_STATE_COUNT) return "anim_idle";
          return names[state];
      }
      
      /* Which melee class a protocol.h weapon is: the three with a real swing window, everything else none. */
      static inline int anim_state_melee_kind(int weapon) {
          if (weapon == WPN_KNIFE) return anim_melee_kind_light();
          if (weapon == WPN_KATANA) return anim_melee_kind_katana();
          if (weapon == WPN_HAMMER) return anim_melee_kind_hammer();
          return ANIM_MELEE_NONE;
      }
      
      /* The melee window in ticks for a weapon (0 = this weapon has no swing). */
      static inline int anim_state_melee_ticks(int weapon) {
          int kind = anim_state_melee_kind(weapon);
          if (kind == ANIM_MELEE_NONE) return 0;
          return anim_melee_ticks(kind);
      }
      
      /* Horizontal speed in units/tick x 1000 -- the same unit the rules' speed bands use.
       * sqrt on the squared sum, so a diagonal run is not 1.41x faster than a straight one. */
      static inline int anim_state_speed_milli(const PlayerState *p) {
          float vx, vz, v2;
          if (!p) return 0;
          vx = p->vx; vz = p->vz;
          v2 = vx * vx + vz * vz;
          if (v2 <= 0.0f) return 0;
          return (int)(__builtin_sqrtf(v2) * 1000.0f);
      }
      
      /* anim_state_for_player -- the one call a renderer needs: the clip to play for this tick.
       *
       * Reads only fields that exist on the real struct: on_ground, crouching, vx/vz, jump_timer,
       * is_shooting, reload_timer, katana_slash_timer, dash_timer, current_weapon.
       *
       * `slide_ticks` is passed in by the caller (0 if it has none) because THIS ENGINE HAS NO SLIDE
       * TIMER: physics.h's crouch-slide is a friction change and the wall ride is ctrl-in-air, and
       * neither sets one. Rather than invent a timer in a header, the slot is explicit and the state is
       * reachable the moment a real producer exists. */
      static inline int anim_state_for_player(const PlayerState *p, int slide_ticks, int climb) {
          if (!p) return ANIM_IDLE;
          return anim_state_select(p->on_ground ? 1 : 0,
                                   p->crouching ? 1 : 0,
                                   anim_state_speed_milli(p),
                                   p->jump_timer,
                                   slide_ticks,
                                   p->is_shooting,
                                   p->reload_timer,
                                   p->katana_slash_timer,
                                   p->dash_timer,
                                   climb);
      }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_ANIM_STATE_H */
      
- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/anim_rules.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit/anim_rules.prn -- which animation clip a player should be playing, as rules.
      ;;
      ;; Founder paste 2026-10-31 (Mixamo pipeline + XPBD ragdoll spec), §2 "Animation Set Specification":
      ;; thirteen discrete sequences an imported skin must bundle or map to. The ragdoll half of that spec
      ;; already exists in this repo (packages/simulation/ragdoll_pool.h on GOLDENBAND's grb, wired to
      ;; deaths in the lobby); the missing half is this: nothing decided WHICH clip belongs to a given tick
      ;; of gameplay, and no clip naming contract existed for an imported Mixamo bundle to satisfy.
      ;;
      ;; So this module is the DECISION, and packages/simulation/anim_state.h is the host that feeds it the
      ;; engine's own real state (protocol.h PlayerState: on_ground, crouching, velocity, is_shooting,
      ;; reload_timer, katana_slash_timer, dash_timer) plus the clip-name table an importer must match.
      ;;
      ;; Priority order, highest first -- this is the part a spec dump usually leaves out and a player
      ;; notices immediately:
      ;;   MELEE      a swing window owns the whole body; you cannot walk out of a hammer arc
      ;;   ABILITY    the katana dash / underbarrel grenade is a committed action
      ;;   FIRE       upper-body only (additive), so it wins over locomotion but not over a swing
      ;;   RELOAD     the 60/42 tick reload the engine actually runs, so it outranks walk/run
      ;;   airborne   jump start (first 6 ticks) then in-air, with the reserved climb state
      ;;   grounded   crouch, slide, then walk/run/idle by speed band
      ;;
      ;; All I32, total, no state -- the same pure-evaluation contract every other rules module keeps.
      ;; Every threshold here is a tunable constant, not a measurement: retune in this file and
      ;; `make regen-anim-rules`.
      (module shankpit/anim-rules)
      (export anim-state-count anim-state-select anim-state-loops anim-state-additive
              anim-state-blend-ms anim-speed-band anim-melee-ticks anim-eye-height-mm
              anim-walk-speed-milli anim-run-speed-milli anim-jump-start-ticks
              anim-melee-kind-light anim-melee-kind-katana anim-melee-kind-hammer)
      
      ;; ---- the clip set, in the order this module and the C table both use ------------------------------
      ;; 0 IDLE 1 WALK 2 RUN 3 CROUCH_IDLE 4 CROUCH_WALK 5 JUMP_START 6 IN_AIR 7 SLIDE
      ;; 8 WEAPON_FIRE 9 RELOAD 10 MELEE_SWING 11 ABILITY 12 CLIMB_LOOP (reserved: no producer yet)
      (defn anim-state-count [] : I32 13)
      
      ;; Speed bands, units/tick x 1000. Deliberately lower than a sprint: WALK has to cover indoor and
      ;; strafing movement or every foot slide becomes visible, which is why the spec asks for two clips.
      (defn anim-walk-speed-milli [] : I32 60)
      (defn anim-run-speed-milli [] : I32 300)
      (defn anim-jump-start-ticks [] : I32 6)
      
      (defn a-abs [(n : I32)] : I32 (if (< n 0) (- 0 n) n))
      
      (defn anim-speed-band [(speed_milli : I32)] : I32
        (if (< (a-abs speed_milli) (anim-walk-speed-milli)) 0
          (if (< (a-abs speed_milli) (anim-run-speed-milli)) 1 2)))
      
      ;; ---- melee windows -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; The engine's own weapon table already carries these as cooldowns (WPN_KNIFE 20, WPN_KATANA 28,
      ;; WPN_HAMMER 42), so the clip window and the damage window are the same number instead of two guesses.
      ;; The host maps protocol.h's WPN_* to these three classes; this module never sees a weapon id.
      (defn anim-melee-kind-light [] : I32 0)
      (defn anim-melee-kind-katana [] : I32 1)
      (defn anim-melee-kind-hammer [] : I32 2)
      
      (defn anim-melee-ticks [(kind : I32)] : I32
        (if (= kind 1) 28 (if (= kind 2) 42 (if (= kind 0) 20 0))))
      
      ;; ---- the selection -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      (defn anim-climb-or-air [(climb : I32)] : I32 (if (> climb 0) 12 6))
      
      (defn anim-air-state [(jump_ticks : I32) (climb : I32)] : I32
        (if (> jump_ticks 0)
          (if (<= jump_ticks (anim-jump-start-ticks)) 5 (anim-climb-or-air climb))
          (anim-climb-or-air climb)))
      
      (defn anim-state-select
        [(grounded : I32) (crouching : I32) (speed_milli : I32)
         (jump_ticks : I32) (slide_ticks : I32)
         (fire_ticks : I32) (reload_ticks : I32) (melee_ticks : I32) (ability_ticks : I32)
         (climb : I32)] : I32
        (if (> melee_ticks 0) 10
          (if (> ability_ticks 0) 11
            (if (> fire_ticks 0) 8
              (if (> reload_ticks 0) 9
                (if (= grounded 0)
                  (anim-air-state jump_ticks climb)
                  (if (= crouching 1)
                    (if (> slide_ticks 0) 7
                      (if (= (anim-speed-band speed_milli) 1) 4 3))
                    (if (= (anim-speed-band speed_milli) 2) 2
                      (if (= (anim-speed-band speed_milli) 1) 1 0)))))))))
      
      ;; ---- per-state clip metadata ---------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; Which states loop. Everything that is a pose the player can stand in loops; one-shot actions do
      ;; not, and JUMP_START/SLIDE are one-shots by definition (the spec calls SLIDE "looping/timed" -- it
      ;; is timed here, because a looping slide would keep playing after the momentum is gone).
      (defn anim-state-loops [(state : I32)] : I32
        (if (= state 5) 0 (if (= state 7) 0 (if (<= state 6) 1 0))))
      
      ;; Upper-body additive masking. Only the recoil is additive: a player must be able to fire while
      ;; running, and the spec says so. RELOAD is NOT additive here -- it owns both hands.
      (defn anim-state-additive [(state : I32)] : I32 (if (= state 8) 1 0))
      
      ;; Crossfade into this state, milliseconds. Shorter for things that must read as an instant reaction
      ;; (a shot, a jump) and longer for postures, where a fast blend looks like a twitch.
      (defn anim-state-blend-ms [(state : I32)] : I32
        (if (= state 8) 60
          (if (= state 5) 40
            (if (= state 10) 80
              (if (= state 11) 90
                (if (= state 7) 90
                  (if (= state 9) 120
                    (if (= state 6) 140
                      (if (= state 12) 160 150)))))))))
      
      ;; ---- eye height -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; The spec's own numbers (4.0 units standing, 2.5 crouched) describe a different build: this engine's
      ;; real eye height is physics.h's EYE_HEIGHT = 2.59, and the crouch value is set below it so the
      ;; camera and the pose move together. The C test asserts the standing value equals EYE_HEIGHT*1000, so
      ;; a change to either one is a failing check rather than a quiet mismatch.
      (defn anim-eye-height-mm [(crouching : I32)] : I32
        (if (= crouching 1) 1650 2590))
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/goldenband/gband.h
  content: |
      // gband.h — the GOLDEN BAND runtime sampler (HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §3/§8 step 1).
      //
      // Deliberately tiny: this is the "fits in a hundred lines of C" acceptance
      // test from the spec. No JSON, no curve interpolation, no engine
      // dependency — see format/GBAND_FORMAT.md for the full binary layout this
      // reads. Determinism is load-bearing: same clip + same tick = the same
      // float32 bytes, every platform, every time.
      #ifndef GOLDENBAND_GBAND_H
      #define GOLDENBAND_GBAND_H
      
      #include <stdint.h>
      
      typedef struct {
          uint32_t version;
          uint32_t tick_rate;
          uint32_t duration_ticks;
          uint32_t num_channels;
          unsigned char skeleton_hash[32];
          unsigned char content_hash[32];
          float *data; // owned; duration_ticks * num_channels floats, row-major by tick
      } GBClip;
      
      // gb_init loads and structurally validates a .gband file. Returns 1 on
      // success, 0 on any failure (bad magic, truncated file, alloc failure).
      // On success, caller must eventually call gb_free.
      int gb_init(const char *path, GBClip *clip);
      
      // gb_free releases the clip's owned channel data. Safe to call on a
      // zeroed/failed-init clip.
      void gb_free(GBClip *clip);
      
      // gb_sample returns a pointer to num_channels floats for the given tick.
      // Out-of-range ticks clamp to the last valid tick rather than reading past
      // the buffer -- callers that need looping should wrap `tick` themselves
      // using clip->duration_ticks and the manifest's loop_points.
      const float *gb_sample(const GBClip *clip, uint32_t tick);
      
      // gb_blend linearly interpolates between two exact ticks into a
      // caller-owned `out` buffer of at least num_channels floats. This is for
      // authoring/reward-compiler use (e.g. sub-tick reward evaluation), not for
      // render-rate smoothness -- per HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §2, render smoothing comes
      // from the consumer's own state-interpolation layer, never from
      // re-sampling here.
      void gb_blend(const GBClip *clip, uint32_t tick_a, uint32_t tick_b, float w, float *out);
      
      // gb_verify recomputes the sha256 over the clip's channel data and
      // compares it against the content_hash read from the file. Returns 1 if
      // they match, 0 otherwise (corrupt file, or a hash that was never set).
      int gb_verify(const GBClip *clip);
      
      #endif // GOLDENBAND_GBAND_H
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/goldenband/gseq.h
  content: |
      // gseq.h — S144-XX: real animation STITCHING for GOLDEN BAND (founder real-time: "make sure we
      // can stitch animations together like James Bond walk turn raise gun shoot").
      //
      // gband.c/gskel.c/gmesh.c are deliberately tiny, channel-name-blind samplers -- gb_sample/
      // gb_blend only ever know "N floats per tick," never which joint a float belongs to (channel
      // names live in the .gband.json manifest, a tooling-facing concern, per GBAND_FORMAT.md's own
      // split). Chaining several DIFFERENT clips together into one continuous performance (walk, then
      // turn, then raise a gun, then shoot) genuinely needs channel-name awareness -- each clip may
      // animate a different subset of joints, and matching them up by array index alone would be
      // silently wrong the moment two clips don't share an identical channel ordering. This module is
      // the one real, minimal place that bridges channel names (from the manifest) to a channel-blind
      // GBClip -- still pure data in, pure data out (per-joint quaternion + translation arrays), never
      // touching rendering, FK, or engine state -- same "pure data transformation" scope gband.c's own
      // sampler already holds itself to.
      //
      // A GSeq is a real, ordered sequence of clips with a real crossfade (nlerp, matching gb_blend's
      // own real, documented nlerp-not-slerp choice for the same reasons -- see GBAND_FORMAT.md's own
      // "Quaternion channels" section) between consecutive steps. Missing channels (a clip that
      // doesn't touch a given joint) fall back to the skeleton's own real rest pose, the exact same
      // documented convention GSKEL_FORMAT.md already establishes for a single clip.
      //
      // What v0 does NOT cover (real, deliberate, named -- not silently assumed): a single, fixed
      // crossfade duration for every transition in a sequence (per-transition override is real,
      // straightforward future work); no authored `.gseq` asset format or NOCK UI yet -- a caller
      // builds a GSeq by hand in code today (see tests/test_gseq.c for the real, working shape); time-
      // based advancement only (gseq_player_advance takes real seconds, not ticks, since different
      // clips in one sequence may have different tick_rate values -- this is deliberate, not an
      // oversight).
      #ifndef GOLDENBAND_GSEQ_H
      #define GOLDENBAND_GSEQ_H
      
      #include <stdint.h>
      #include "gband.h"
      #include "gskel.h"
      
      /* GSEQ_MAX_CHANNELS -- real, live-verified bug fix (2026-09-20, found while vendoring this module
       * into BIG_O and actually testing the load, not assumed working): the OLD cap of 256 was not
       * actually "generous" for this repo's own real, currently-loaded assets -- gskel_find_joint's own
       * GSKEL_MAX_JOINTS is 128, and 7 channels/joint (tx/ty/tz/qx/qy/qz/qw, gband_skel_npc.c's own
       * real convention) means any skeleton with more than 36 joints already overflows a 256 cap.
       * Direct, live test against this repo's own real assets (gseq_clip_load, run from apps/lobby's
       * own working directory, not guessed): mannequin_npc (65 joints, 455 channels), Stan/Mike (43
       * joints, 301 channels), George (47 joints, 329 channels) ALL fail to load under the old 256 cap
       * -- only Leela (17 joints, 119 channels) actually succeeds. gband_skel_npc_load_kit's own
       * real, silent per-kit failure handling meant this was never a crash, just every one of those 4
       * kits permanently unavailable -- draw_player_skin_mannequin's own real "cycle past any kit that
       * failed to load" logic then silently converged on Leela as the only real, ever-successful kit,
       * regardless of the real p->id-based variety it was written to provide. Bumped to comfortably
       * exceed GSKEL_MAX_JOINTS(128) * 7 = 896 -- real headroom for the largest skeleton this system's
       * own joint cap could ever produce, not just today's specific 5 real character assets. */
      #define GSEQ_MAX_CHANNELS 1024
      #define GSEQ_CHANNEL_NAME_LEN 48   // GSKEL_NAME_LEN (32) + room for ".qw"/".tz" etc.
      #define GSEQ_MAX_STEPS 16
      
      // GSeqClip -- one loaded .gband clip PLUS its own real channel names (read from the manifest's
      // "channels" array), the one real piece gband.c's own binary format doesn't carry. Freed with
      // gseq_clip_free.
      typedef struct {
          GBClip clip;
          char channel_names[GSEQ_MAX_CHANNELS][GSEQ_CHANNEL_NAME_LEN];
          uint32_t channel_count; // == clip.num_channels; kept alongside for a real, explicit bound
      } GSeqClip;
      
      // gseq_clip_load loads gband_path (the binary) and reads channel_names out of
      // manifest_json_path's own real "channels" array (a small, real, bounded scanner -- not a
      // general JSON parser, same "smallest real thing scoped to one known shape" discipline
      // SHANKPIT/packages/world/level_boxes.h's own scanner already established). Returns 1 on
      // success, 0 on any failure (missing/malformed binary, missing/malformed manifest, more channels
      // than GSEQ_MAX_CHANNELS).
      int gseq_clip_load(const char *gband_path, const char *manifest_json_path, GSeqClip *out);
      void gseq_clip_free(GSeqClip *c);
      
      typedef struct {
          int clip_index;           // index into the caller-owned GSeqClip[] "library" array
          float duration_seconds;   // <= 0 means "use the clip's own real duration_ticks/tick_rate"
      } GSeqStep;
      
      typedef struct {
          GSeqStep steps[GSEQ_MAX_STEPS];
          int step_count;
          float blend_seconds; // real crossfade duration between EVERY consecutive pair of steps (v0 --
                                // one value for the whole sequence, see this file's own header note)
          int loop;             // 1 = loop back to step 0 after the last step; 0 = hold the last step's
                                  // own final pose forever once reached
      } GSeq;
      
      typedef struct {
          const GSeq *seq;
          const GSeqClip *clips; // caller-owned "library," indexed by each GSeqStep's own clip_index
          int current_step;
          float elapsed_in_step;   // real seconds since the current step started
          int blending;             // 1 while crossfading OUT of blend_from_step INTO current_step
          int blend_from_step;
          float blend_elapsed;      // real seconds since the crossfade started
      } GSeqPlayer;
      
      void gseq_player_init(GSeqPlayer *p, const GSeq *seq, const GSeqClip *clips);
      
      // gseq_player_advance moves real time forward. Crosses into the next step (or loops, or holds
      // the final pose) exactly once real elapsed_in_step reaches the current step's own real
      // duration, starting a real crossfade at that same moment.
      void gseq_player_advance(GSeqPlayer *p, float dt_seconds);
      
      // gseq_player_sample_pose resolves the player's CURRENT (possibly mid-crossfade) pose for every
      // joint in skel: out_rot gets skel->joint_count real quaternions (x,y,z,w, 4 floats each),
      // out_trans gets skel->joint_count real translations (3 floats each) -- caller-owned, sized by
      // the caller. A joint with no matching channel in the active clip(s) falls back to that joint's
      // own real skeleton rest pose (skel->joints[j].rest_rotation/rest_translation), the same
      // documented convention GSKEL_FORMAT.md already establishes for a single clip.
      void gseq_player_sample_pose(const GSeqPlayer *p, const GSkel *skel, float *out_rot, float *out_trans);
      
      #endif // GOLDENBAND_GSEQ_H

  content: |
      // gband_skel_npc.h — general, arbitrary-joint-count character rendering, built on top of
      // GOLDENBAND's new gpose.c (real N-joint forward kinematics + skinning) and gseq.c (real
      // named-channel animation sampling). Real, deliberate SIBLING to gband_mesh_rig.c/.h, not a
      // replacement: gband_mesh_rig.c stays exactly as-is (it draws the PLAYER's own body, tyler_body,
      // a real hand-authored 5-joint rig with its own hardcoded channel convention -- still real and
      // still working). This module is for any OTHER GOLDENBAND character asset -- founder-imported
      // ones (a mannequin, and as of S467's own follow-up, four real distinct robot characters --
      // George/Leela/Mike/Stan, each its own real mesh+skeleton+animation set, confirmed via a direct
      // GOLDENBAND-side load-and-inspect: 47/17/43/43 real joints respectively, not a shared rig) --
      // used to spawn NPCs. See EMILY/BACKLOG.md S459-97/S467/S468 and GOLDENBAND's own src/gpose.h
      // header comment for the general-vs-hardcoded rationale.
      //
      // Real multi-kit support (S467 follow-up, founder real-time: "GEORGE LEELA MIKE AND STAN ARE
      // ANIMATED ROBOT CHARACTERS WITH MESH RIG AND ANIMATIONS PER BOT"). The original v0 scope --
      // "only one character asset can be loaded at a time" -- is lifted: gband_skel_npc_load_kit loads
      // a real, independent character (its own skeleton, mesh, idle/walk clips) into a real kit slot,
      // and gband_skel_npc_draw takes a kit_index so different NPC instances can be different
      // characters, not clones of one shared look. Kits are loaded once at startup and never unloaded
      // individually (gband_skel_npc_shutdown frees all of them together) -- matches the real,
      // deliberate "small, fixed roster, loaded once" scope every other GOLDENBAND asset already
      // assumes (no runtime asset streaming exists anywhere in this repo).
      #ifndef GOLDENBAND_GBAND_SKEL_NPC_H
      #define GOLDENBAND_GBAND_SKEL_NPC_H
      
      #include "../common/mat4.h"
      #include "gskel.h"
      
      #define GBAND_SKEL_NPC_MAX_KITS 8
      
      // S470 follow-up, founder real-time: "get all the robots in there and have them walking around
      // different waypoints... if you can get them to wave to the player when the player gets close
      // and then dance before resuming patrol". Real, honest asset-driven behavior: 0 is the existing
      // movement-driven idle/walk auto-pick, GREET/DANCE force a specific one-shot(-looking) gesture
      // clip regardless of movement -- the caller (SHANKPIT's story_ai-driven anim_override, see
      // PlayerState's own field) decides WHEN, this module only decides WHICH clip plays once told.
      #define GBAND_SKEL_NPC_ANIM_AUTO  0
      #define GBAND_SKEL_NPC_ANIM_GREET 1
      #define GBAND_SKEL_NPC_ANIM_DANCE 2
      
      // gband_skel_npc_load_kit loads <asset_dir>/<mesh_name>.gskel + .gmesh, plus real animation
      // clips (+ their own .gband.json manifests, for real channel names): <idle_clip_name> looped
      // while stationary, <walk_clip_name> looped while moving. greet_clip_name/dance_clip_name are
      // each OPTIONAL (pass NULL if this character has no real clip for that gesture) -- a kit missing
      // one is real and expected, not an error: not every currently-uploaded character has both a real
      // greeting gesture AND a real dance (checked directly against the live asset library before
      // wiring this, not assumed -- see EMILY/BACKLOG.md S470 for exactly which kit has which). A kit
      // with anim_override forced but no real clip loaded for it falls back to idle in
      // gband_skel_npc_draw, never draws nothing. Returns the new kit's real index (0-based, stable
      // for the process lifetime) on success, or -1 on failure (missing/malformed required asset, a
      // skeleton with more joints than GSKEL_MAX_JOINTS, or GBAND_SKEL_NPC_MAX_KITS already reached).
      int gband_skel_npc_load_kit(const char *asset_dir, const char *mesh_name,
                                   const char *idle_clip_name, const char *walk_clip_name,
                                   const char *greet_clip_name, const char *dance_clip_name);
      
      void gband_skel_npc_shutdown(void);
      
      // The kit's skeleton (NULL for a bad/unready kit) -- the ragdoll pool is built on it.
      const GSkel *gband_skel_npc_kit_skel(int kit_index);
      
      // Uniform scale applied (about the NPC's feet) to every subsequent gband_skel_npc_draw call until changed.
      // The skinned draw bakes its world transform into the vertices, so a GL glScalef around the call has no
      // effect -- this is the real way to draw a giant bug / small bird. 1.0 = normal.
      void gband_skel_npc_set_scale(float s);
      
      // Draws the kit's mesh with caller-supplied WORLD-space skin matrices (joint_count of them,
      // column-major float[16], e.g. ragdoll_pool_get_skin_matrices) instead of sampling a clip.
      void gband_skel_npc_draw_skin(int kit_index, const float (*skin)[16], const Mat4 *vp,
                                    void (*draw_skinned)(const float *verts6, int vert_count,
                                                         const Mat4 *mvp, const Mat4 *model));
      
      // gband_skel_npc_kit_ready reports whether kit_index is a real, successfully-loaded kit --
      // callers should fall back to a different skin/kit on 0, never draw nothing.
      int gband_skel_npc_kit_ready(int kit_index);
      
      // gband_skel_npc_draw animates, skins, and draws one NPC instance using kit_index's own real
      // character (independent animation clocks per npc_slot -- re-initialized automatically if the
      // same npc_slot is later drawn with a DIFFERENT kit_index, e.g. a respawned NPC assigned a new
      // look, so a stale animation player is never sampled against the wrong clip/skeleton).
      // anim_override selects which clip plays -- GBAND_SKEL_NPC_ANIM_AUTO detects movement the same
      // real way gband_mesh_rig_draw already does (a per-slot previous-position comparison against a
      // small epsilon) and picks idle/walk; GREET/DANCE force that specific gesture clip regardless of
      // movement, falling back to idle if this kit has no real clip loaded for the requested gesture.
      // Same draw_skinned callback contract as gband_mesh_rig_draw -- pos+normal, world-space,
      // non-indexed triangle list.
      void gband_skel_npc_draw(int kit_index, int npc_slot, float npc_x, float npc_y, float npc_z, float facing_rad, float dt_ms,
                                int anim_override,
                                const Mat4 *vp,
                                void (*draw_skinned)(const float *verts6, int vert_count,
                                                      const Mat4 *mvp, const Mat4 *model));
      
      #endif // GOLDENBAND_GBAND_SKEL_NPC_H

  content: |
      // gband.c — see gband.h. This file is the acceptance test itself: it must
      // stay small enough to read in one sitting (HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §8: "a hundred
      // line parser is the acceptance test").
      #include "gband.h"
      #include "sha256.h"
      
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <stdlib.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      #define GBAND_HEADER_SIZE 84
      
      static uint32_t read_u32le(const unsigned char *p) {
          return (uint32_t)p[0] | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 8) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[3] << 24);
      }
      
      int gb_init(const char *path, GBClip *clip) {
          memset(clip, 0, sizeof(*clip));
      
          FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
          if (!f) return 0;
      
          unsigned char header[GBAND_HEADER_SIZE];
          if (fread(header, 1, GBAND_HEADER_SIZE, f) != GBAND_HEADER_SIZE) {
              fclose(f);
              return 0;
          }
          if (memcmp(header, "GBND", 4) != 0) {
              fclose(f);
              return 0;
          }
      
          clip->version = read_u32le(header + 4);
          clip->tick_rate = read_u32le(header + 8);
          clip->duration_ticks = read_u32le(header + 12);
          clip->num_channels = read_u32le(header + 16);
          memcpy(clip->skeleton_hash, header + 20, 32);
          memcpy(clip->content_hash, header + 52, 32);
      
          if (clip->duration_ticks == 0 || clip->num_channels == 0) {
              fclose(f);
              return 0;
          }
      
          size_t n_floats = (size_t)clip->duration_ticks * (size_t)clip->num_channels;
          clip->data = (float *)malloc(n_floats * sizeof(float));
          if (!clip->data) {
              fclose(f);
              return 0;
          }
      
          // Raw float32 read: this repo's monorepo-wide convention (see
          // packages/common/protocol.h elsewhere) assumes a little-endian host
          // with IEEE754 float32, so no per-value byte-swapping is done here.
          if (fread(clip->data, sizeof(float), n_floats, f) != n_floats) {
              free(clip->data);
              clip->data = NULL;
              fclose(f);
              return 0;
          }
      
          fclose(f);
          return 1;
      }
      
      void gb_free(GBClip *clip) {
          free(clip->data);
          clip->data = NULL;
      }
      
      const float *gb_sample(const GBClip *clip, uint32_t tick) {
          if (tick >= clip->duration_ticks) tick = clip->duration_ticks - 1;
          return clip->data + (size_t)tick * (size_t)clip->num_channels;
      }
      
      void gb_blend(const GBClip *clip, uint32_t tick_a, uint32_t tick_b, float w, float *out) {
          const float *a = gb_sample(clip, tick_a);
          const float *b = gb_sample(clip, tick_b);
          for (uint32_t i = 0; i < clip->num_channels; i++) {
              out[i] = a[i] + (b[i] - a[i]) * w;
          }
      }
      
      int gb_verify(const GBClip *clip) {
          size_t n_bytes = (size_t)clip->duration_ticks * (size_t)clip->num_channels * sizeof(float);
          unsigned char computed[32];
          sha256((const unsigned char *)clip->data, n_bytes, computed);
          return memcmp(computed, clip->content_hash, 32) == 0;
      }
      
- path: MONOREPO/GOLDENBAND/format/GBAND_FORMAT.md
  content: |
      # The `.gband` Format
      
      `status: v0 — HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §8 build step 1`
      
      Content-addressed, two-part canonical motion asset (HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §3). The two parts are
      deliberately split by consumer, not by convenience:
      
      - The **binary** (`<name>.gband`) is what the C sampler reads at runtime. Fixed layout, no
        parsing beyond reading a struct and an array of floats — that's the "fits in a hundred lines
        of C" acceptance test from the spec, and it only holds because this file is never JSON.
      - The **manifest** (`<name>.gband.json`) is what tooling (import, hash, validate, the reward
        compiler, Back Office) reads. Richer, human-authored fields — authorship, intent tags, loop
        points, safety annotations — none of which the runtime sampler needs to do its one job.
      
      ## Binary layout (`<name>.gband`)
      
      Little-endian throughout.
      
      | Offset | Size | Field | Meaning |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | 0 | 4 | `magic` | ASCII `"GBND"` |
      | 4 | 4 | `version` (uint32) | format version, `1` today |
      | 8 | 4 | `tick_rate` (uint32) | ticks/second this clip was authored at |
      | 12 | 4 | `duration_ticks` (uint32) | number of sampled frames |
      | 16 | 4 | `num_channels` (uint32) | channels per tick |
      | 20 | 32 | `skeleton_hash` | sha256 of the referenced skeleton asset (raw bytes, not hex) |
      | 52 | 32 | `content_hash` | sha256 of everything from offset 84 onward (the channel data) — the asset's own content address |
      | 84 | `duration_ticks * num_channels * 4` | `channel_data` | row-major: for each tick, `num_channels` float32 values, in the manifest's `channels` order |
      
      Total file size: `84 + duration_ticks * num_channels * 4` bytes.
      
      No curve interpolation modes, no compression, no per-channel type variation. Everything is
      resampled to uniform `tick_rate` float32 tracks at import time (HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §3: "no
      curves-with-twelve-interpolation-modes cleverness; resample at import"). Determinism
      requirement: the same clip, same seed, same tick must sample to a bit-identical pose on every
      platform — a fixed binary layout with no float-format ambiguity is what makes that true.
      
      ## Manifest (`<name>.gband.json`)
      
      ```json
      {
        "gband_version": 1,
        "skeleton_hash": "<hex sha256, matches the binary's skeleton_hash field>",
        "content_hash": "<hex sha256, matches the binary's content_hash field>",
        "tick_rate": 64,
        "duration_ticks": 128,
        "channels": ["root.tx", "root.ty", "root.tz", "root.rx", "root.ry", "root.rz", "hip.rx", ...],
        "authorship": {
          "kind": "mocap | human | generative",
          "who": "free text — labeled honestly, per HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §3"
        },
        "intent_tags": ["gait", "idle", "gesture", "showpiece"],
        "loop_points": { "start_tick": 0, "end_tick": 128 },
        "safety": { "max_joint_velocity": null, "max_joint_torque": null }
      }
      ```
      
      `channels` must have exactly `num_channels` entries and their order defines the binary's
      channel-data column order. `tick_rate`/`duration_ticks` must match the binary exactly —
      `gbtool validate` checks this (see below).
      
      Skeleton assets themselves (joint hierarchy, limits, actuator metadata for hardware-bound
      characters) are out of scope for this v0 pass — `skeleton_hash` is a forward-compatible
      placeholder field today; nothing resolves it to a real skeleton asset yet.
      
      ## Content addressing
      
      `content_hash` is computed the same way everywhere (`gbtool hash`, the C sampler's optional
      verification path): sha256 over the raw channel-data bytes only (not the header, not the
      manifest). Promotions to `golden` status are Apples-logged `ApplePublished` events per
      HQ-SPEC-SIM-100 §3 — out of scope for this pass (no promotion pipeline wired yet), but the
      hash is what a future promotion event would cite.
      
      ## Quaternion channels (S144-XX, glTF import)
      
      BVH import only ever produces Euler channels (`<joint>.Xrotation` etc. — BVH's own native
      rotation representation). `gbtool import --gltf` (glTF is Blender's own native, quaternion-based
      export format) produces real quaternion channels instead, named `<joint>.qx`, `<joint>.qy`,
      `<joint>.qz`, `<joint>.qw` — same "row-major float32 columns, no per-channel type variation"
      binary layout as every other channel; the `q` prefix is a naming convention for
      tooling/consumers to recognize a quaternion group, not a distinct wire format. Translation
      channels from a glTF import are named `<joint>.tx/.ty/.tz`.
      
      `gb_blend`'s runtime interpolation (src/gband.c) is a plain per-component lerp with no
      channel-type awareness — correct for scalar/Euler channels, but for a quaternion group this is
      an nlerp approximation (lerp then the CALLER must renormalize before using the result for
      skinning), not a true slerp. Acceptable for blending between adjacent, already-uniformly-sampled
      ticks of the same clip (the only case `gb_blend` is used for); not correct for blending between
      two arbitrary, widely-separated orientations. `gbtool import --gltf`'s own resampling step
      (collapsing a glTF clip's real, sparse keyframes down to `.gband`'s required uniform tick rate)

sorted(mapping.items()):\n            try:\n                validate_pair(stem, args.assets)\n            except (ValueError, OSError) as e:\n                errors.append(str(e))\n        for state in CONTRACT:\n            if state not in mapping:\n                errors.append(\"missing contract clip: \" + state)\n    else:\n        errors, warnings = write_bundle(mapping, args.assets, args.out, args.allow_partial)\n\n    for w in warnings:\n        print(\"warn: \" + w, file=sys.stderr)\n    if errors:\n        for e in errors:\n            print(\"error: \" + e, file=sys.stderr)\n        return 1\n    print(\"ok: %d/%d clips bound%s -> %s\" % (len(mapping), len(CONTRACT),\n                                            \" (dry run)\" if args.dry_run else \"\", args.out))\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))\n"
}

  "content": "/* anim_clipset.h -- the thirteen clips, loaded and selected.\n *\n * anim_state.h decides WHICH state a tick belongs to and publishes the clip-name contract; the\n * binder (tools/mixamo_clipset.py) produces a directory that satisfies it. This is the missing third\n * piece: a set of the thirteen real clips, loaded through GOLDENBAND's own loader, with the chosen\n * clip sampled at the right tick -- looping postures, holding one-shots, and falling back to a clip\n * that exists when the art does not.\n *\n * Header-only and free of GL/SDL, because the honest way to verify an animation selector is to load\n * real .gband files and ask which tick they are on, not to look at a window (and this build box has\n * no GPU or display at all).\n *\n * The fallback is the part that keeps a half-populated bundle usable instead of invisible: a rig\n * with no run clip plays its walk or its idle rather than freezing or drawing nothing. What it does\n * NOT do is invent motion -- the sampled pose is always a real clip's real tick.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_ANIM_CLIPSET_H\n#define SHANKPIT_ANIM_CLIPSET_H\n\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n\n#include \"anim_state.h\"\n#include \"../goldenband/gseq.h\"\n#include \"../goldenband/gband.h\"\n\ntypedef struct {\n    GSeqClip clips[ANIM_STATE_COUNT];\n    int loaded[ANIM_STATE_COUNT];\n    /* state is what the rules asked for and a clip exists for; wanted is what the rules asked for,\n     * whether or not it exists. Keeping both is what makes the fallback observable (and testable). */\n    int state;\n    int wanted;\n    int prev_state;\n    unsigned int tick;\n    float blend_ms_remaining;\n    float blend_ms_total;\n    int one_shot_finished; /* a one-shot reached its last tick and is holding it */\n} AnimClipSet;\n\nstatic inline void anim_clipset_reset(AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set) return;\n    memset(set, 0, sizeof *set);\n    set->state = ANIM_IDLE;\n    set->wanted = ANIM_IDLE;\n    set->prev_state = ANIM_IDLE;\n}\n\n/* anim_clipset_load -- load <dir>/<contract>.gband + .gband.json for all thirteen names.\n *\n * Returns the number of clips that loaded. A missing or malformed clip is NOT fatal: it is recorded\n * as not loaded, so a rig with four clips still animates and a rig with none reports 0 rather than\n * pretending. gseq_clip_load already validates the binary and reads the channels from the manifest.\n */\nstatic inline int anim_clipset_load(AnimClipSet *set, const char *dir) {\n    if (!set || !dir) return 0;\n    anim_clipset_reset(set);\n    int count = 0;\n    for (int s = 0; s < ANIM_STATE_COUNT; s++) {\n        char gb[512], mj[512];\n        const char *name = anim_state_clip_name(s);\n        snprintf(gb, sizeof gb, \"%s/%s.gband\", dir, name);\n        snprintf(mj, sizeof mj, \"%s/%s.gband.json\", dir, name);\n        if (gseq_clip_load(gb, mj, &set->clips[s])) {\n            set->loaded[s] = 1;\n            count++;\n        }\n    }\n    return count;\n}\n\nstatic inline int anim_clipset_all_loaded(const AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set) return 0;\n    for (int s = 0; s < ANIM_STATE_COUNT; s++)\n        if (!set->loaded[s]) return 0;\n    return 1;\n}\n\nstatic inline void anim_clipset_free(AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set) return;\n    for (int s = 0; s < ANIM_STATE_COUNT; s++) gseq_clip_free(&set->clips[s]);\n    anim_clipset_reset(set);\n}\n\n/* The state actually sampled: `state` when its clip exists, else idle, else the first clip that\n * loaded. Returns -1 when nothing was loaded -- the caller should not draw a pose at all. */\nstatic inline int anim_clipset_resolve_state(const AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set) return -1;\n    if (set->loaded[set->state]) return set->state;\n    if (set->loaded[ANIM_IDLE]) return ANIM_IDLE;\n    for (int s = 0; s < ANIM_STATE_COUNT; s++)\n        if (set->loaded[s]) return s;\n    return -1;\n}\n\nstatic inline float anim_clipset_blend_weight(const AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set || set->blend_ms_total <= 0.0f) return 1.0f;\n    float w = 1.0f - (set->blend_ms_remaining / set->blend_ms_total);\n    return w < 0.0f ? 0.0f : (w > 1.0f ? 1.0f : w);\n}\n\n/* anim_clipset_tick -- advance `dt_ms` and return the state to sample, or -1 if no clip is loaded.\n *\n * On a state change the new clip starts at tick 0 and a crossfade begins for the rules' own\n * anim_state_blend_ms. Looping states wrap by duration; one-shots hold their last tick, because a\n * reload that snaps back to frame 0 reads as a glitch rather than a completed action.\n */\nstatic inline int anim_clipset_tick(AnimClipSet *set, const PlayerState *p, int slide_ticks, int climb, int dt_ms) {\n    if (!set || dt_ms < 0) return -1;\n    set->wanted = anim_state_for_player(p, slide_ticks, climb);\n    int resolved = anim_clipset_resolve_state(set);\n    if (resolved < 0) return -1;\n\n    if (resolved != set->state) {\n        set->prev_state = set->state;\n        set->state = resolved;\n        set->tick = 0;\n        set->one_shot_finished = 0;\n        set->blend_ms_total = (float)anim_state_blend_ms(resolved);\n        set->blend_ms_remaining = set->blend_ms_total;\n    }\n\n    const GBClip *clip = &set->clips[set->state].clip;\n    unsigned int advance = (unsigned int)(((long long)dt_ms * (long long)clip->tick_rate) / 1000);\n    int loops = anim_state_loops(set->state);\n    if (loops) {\n        set->tick = (set->tick + advance) % clip->duration_ticks;\n    } else {\n        unsigned long long t = (unsigned long long)set->tick + advance;\n        if (t >= clip->duration_ticks) {\n            set->tick = clip->duration_ticks - 1;\n            set->one_shot_finished = 1;\n        } else {\n            set->tick = (unsigned int)t;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (set->blend_ms_remaining > 0.0f) {\n        set->blend_ms_remaining -= (float)dt_ms;\n        if (set->blend_ms_remaining < 0.0f) set->blend_ms_remaining = 0.0f;\n    }\n    return set->state;\n}\n\n/* The channel values for the current tick (num_channels floats, owned by the set), or NULL. */\nstatic inline const float *anim_clipset_sample(const AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set) return NULL;\n    if (!set->loaded[set->state]) return NULL;\n    return gb_sample(&set->clips[set->state].clip, set->tick);\n}\n\n/* The active clip itself, for a caller that needs duration/tick_rate or wants to blend. */\nstatic inline const GBClip *anim_clipset_clip(const AnimClipSet *set) {\n    if (!set || !set->loaded[set->state]) return NULL;\n    return &set->clips[set->state].clip;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_ANIM_CLIPSET_H */\n"

\"mixamo_ability\")\n        r = run([\"--assets\", mixed, \"--auto\", \"--rig\", \"mixamo\", \"--out\", os.path.join(tmp, \"o5\")])\n        check(r.returncode == 1 and \"different skeletons\" in r.stderr, \"clips from two rigs are refused\")\n\n        # A truncated binary.\n        short = os.path.join(tmp, \"short\")\n        shutil.copytree(rig, short)\n        p = os.path.join(short, \"mixamo_slide.gband\")\n        open(p, \"wb\").write(open(p, \"rb\").read()[:100])\n        r = run([\"--assets\", short, \"--auto\", \"--rig\", \"mixamo\", \"--out\", os.path.join(tmp, \"o6\")])\n        check(r.returncode == 1, \"a truncated binary is refused\")\n\n        print(\"== binder: ambiguity is an error, not a coin flip ==\")\n        amb = os.path.join(tmp, \"amb\")\n        os.makedirs(amb)\n        copy_pair(\"Mike_Idle\", amb, \"idle_a\")\n        copy_pair(\"Mike_Idle\", amb, \"idle_b\")\n        r = run([\"--assets\", amb, \"--auto\", \"--out\", os.path.join(tmp, \"o7\")])\n        check(r.returncode == 2 and \"ambiguous\" in r.stderr, \"two equal candidates stop the import\")\n\n        print(\"== binder: dry run ==\")\n        r = run([\"--assets\", rig, \"--auto\", \"--rig\", \"mixamo\", \"--out\", os.path.join(tmp, \"o8\"), \"--dry-run\"])\n        check(r.returncode == 0 and not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(tmp, \"o8\")), \"a dry run validates and writes nothing\")\n\n        print(\"== binder: shared clips are allowed but reported ==\")\n        shared = dict(STEMS)\n        shared[\"anim_run\"] = \"mixamo_walk\"  # a rig with no run cycle reuses its walk\n        smap = os.path.join(tmp, \"shared.json\")\n        json.dump(shared, open(smap, \"w\"))\n        r = run([\"--assets\", rig, \"--map\", smap, \"--out\", os.path.join(tmp, \"o9\")])\n        check(r.returncode == 0 and \"share the clip\" in r.stderr,\n              \"reusing one clip for two states warns instead of failing\")\n    finally:\n        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)\n\n    print(\"\\n%d checks, %d failed\" % (checks, failures))\n    return 0 if failures == 0 else 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"
}
