- path: MONOREPO/EMPIRE/README.md
  content: |
      # EMPIRE
      
      Composition layer for the EMPIRE stack: ECOWAR (the game), BIG_O (faction/tech-tree sim), DEADWEIGHT
      (card language), TRAPX (doctrine). Each source repo keeps developing its own layer; the integration
      code lives here. See `NORTHSTAR.md` for the scope and merge order.
      
      ## What is here
      
      - `bridge/faction_bridge.{h,c}` — ECOWAR card play gated and written back through BIG_O's decorum rules
        (NORTHSTAR §3.1, kanban #576). CANCELLED casters can't play a card; a successful cast spends or earns
        decorum. The MYTHIC/MUNDANE mapping (-25 / +1) is an invented v1 tuning pending founder sign-off.
      - `bridge/faction_state.{h,c}` — the shared faction record (kanban #579). The BIG_O side loads its decorum into
        it with `empire_faction_load()`. The deck UI binds to the same record, so a cast made through the UI is visible
        to BIG_O and the reverse. Each change bumps `revision`. **Honest gap:** BIG_O has no live server-side faction
        decorum store yet. Its only per-player decorum is the scenario sim (`core/sim.h`), so nothing feeds this record
        from a live server. The loader is the seam for that feed.
      - `deck/deck.{h,c}` — the deck model: an 8-card cycle of ECOWAR card ids, a 4-slot hand, and Clash Royale
        style refill (playing a slot draws the next card in the cycle). Also the MYTHIC lookup, copied from
        `card_effect_mod.prn`.
      - `deck/ui.{h,c}` — the deck and unit-placement apps (NORTHSTAR §3.3, kanban #578). Pure input -> state ->
        effect, the same shape as BIG_O's `bigo_phone.h`. DECK picks a card; UNITS places it on a 3x6 grid
        (invented v1 layout). SELECT is gated on the bound faction's `can_cast`, and a committed placement writes its
        decorum back into that shared record. BACK cancels with nothing spent.
      - `vendor/big_o/` — BIG_O's PARENA-generated `witness_rules.c/.h` plus `parena_runtime.h`, copied verbatim.
        `MANIFEST.sha256` records their hashes. Re-sync with `make sync-big-o` (needs a sibling `../BIG_O`
        checkout, or set `BIG_O_DIR`). Never edit `vendor/` by hand.
      
      - `tests/test_bit_compat.c` — bit-level check of the BIG_O/ECOWAR seam (kanban #582). It runs against ECOWAR's
        real compiled card mod when a checkout is present: `make compat ECOWAR_DIR=../ECOWAR`.
      - `audits/` — kanban audits. `deadweight2_ship_audit.md` (#580, already shipped) and
        `trapx_doctrine_reconciliation.md` (#581, the standalone TRAPX repo is the doctrine).
      
      ## Build and test
      
      ```bash
      make test        # headless; builds with -DPARENA_NO_GRAPHICS so no SDL2 is needed
      ```
      
      ## Status and limits
      
      - Headless tests: 11 bridge, 8 faction-state and 26 deck/UI checks, all passing.
      - The deck/UI is an input model only. Nothing renders it yet. A phone shell (BIG_O's `BigoPhone` or a future one) must
        draw it and feed it actions. No costs, cooldowns or elixir-style economy are modelled yet.
      - ECOWAR still carries its own vendored copy of the same gate and write-back (ECOWAR `aff6ce0`). Moving
        that consumer onto this module is not done yet; it needs a decision on how ECOWAR depends on EMPIRE.
      - Decorum is not networked and has no HUD yet.
      
      ## Web build (vs0 MVP)
      
      EMPIRE plays in the browser on WOTAN (`/empire/`), quietly. The game is real PARENA compiled to wasm (rules, 8 AI temperaments, protocol, screens);
      the page's host JS is generated PARENA -> TypeScript, not hand-written.
      
      - Source: `PARENA/stdlib/empire/web/*.prn`; build with `WOTAN/scripts/build-empire.sh`, then `IDUNA/scripts/sync-empire-wasm.sh` (referee must run the same wasm).
      - Referee: `IDUNA/internal/empire` runs the same wasm under wazero; matchmaking (person vs person, or person vs AI after a short window), reconnect, anonymous
        spectators, a 15-minute AI league, replays, ratings (Elo 1500/K32), per-card stats. Guests and SSO both work.
      - Test: `WOTAN/scripts/empire-browser-test.mjs` (real IDUNA + headless Chromium), `go test ./internal/empire/` in IDUNA.
      
      Honest limits: card stats are invented v1 tuning built from ECOWAR magnitudes; AI balance is uneven (win rates 15-86%); no audio; TRAPX not integrated;
      only checked in Chromium (not Firefox/Safari/phones).

      # EMPIRE — NORTHSTAR (corrected scope, 2026-10-06)
      
      **Status:** design/scoping, repos now checked out locally (`ECOWAR`, `REDGARDEN`, `DEADWEIGHT_2`,
      `TRAPX`, `MONOREPO` pulled fresh this session alongside existing `BIG_O`/`DEADWEIGHT`/`SHANKPIT`),
      no merge code written yet.
      
      ## 0) Correction (founder, real-time, 2026-10-06 — supersedes this doc's earlier v0)
      
      The first draft of this doc read "merge" as "share a ladder/identity backend between three
      otherwise-separate games." That was wrong. Founder, verbatim:
      
      > "EMPIRE is literally a merging of BIG_O, ECOWAR, and DEADWEIGHT 1+2 — full ECOWAR RTS style,
      > card places units, Clash Royale style, but the factions are actually the BIG_O simulation. The
      > game is ECOWAR. BIG_O is the tech tree. TRAPX is the universe. TYLER is the lore. SHANKPIT is
      > the operating system. REDGARDEN is the hero UI. DEADWEIGHT is the card language. Merge ECOWAR
      > and BIG_O first — ECOWAR is the client, BIG_O is the headless sim that needs a GUI resource
      > management sim [wrapped in] TRAPX doctrine."
      
      This is one product with a named role for every repo in the stack, not three products sharing a
      backend. Each role below is checked against that repo's own real, current code — not assumed from
      its name.
      
      ## 1) The stack, role by role (checked against real code, not guessed)
      
      | Repo | Role in EMPIRE | What's actually there today |
      |---|---|---|
      | **ECOWAR** | **The game.** Clash Royale-shaped client: play cards, cards place/affect units, resolved in real time. | Hard fork of REDGARDEN (`apps/arena`/`apps/arena_server`, C99/SDL2/OpenGL, server-authoritative UDP). **16 real cards shipped** (`packages/simulation/arena_game.c`'s `ECOWAR_CARDS`, resolution via `PARENA/stdlib/ecowar/card_effect_mod.prn` — real I32 decision logic, not a bare trigger), each grounded in a `TYLER/multiverse_heroes.md` hero. **Gap, confirmed in ECOWAR's own README**: no deck/hand UI, no unit-placement input wiring yet — the cards are callable and tested end-to-end, but nothing in-match actually plays one. This is exactly the "Clash Royale style" layer that doesn't exist yet. Own matchmaker+bot-pool real and live (`:9779`, `ECOWAR-BOTS` IDUNA M2M agent).
      | **BIG_O** | **The tech tree / faction simulation**, headless, driving ECOWAR's factions from underneath. Needs a GUI resource-management layer wrapped around it. | Real, live precedent for exactly this shape: `core/lab_sim.h/.c` (headless cloning-facility equipment pipeline, "simulate real lab equipment," zero server/GUI logic), Attention/Heat rules module (PARENA-scalar, headless tests + a tiny text sim to *play* it — i.e. BIG_O already proves out headless-sim-plus-minimal-harness as its own pattern). Day/night/basement loop *is* the tech-tree/economy shape the founder means by "factions are actually the BIG_O simulation" — basement lab + pheromone army + Attention/Heat *is* a faction-management sim with no GUI today.
      | **DEADWEIGHT (1) / DEADWEIGHT_2** | **The card language.** The grammar cards are written in, not the cards themselves. | `DEADWEIGHT/core/card_rules.c/.h` — a real, pure, headless, deterministic card-resolution engine (6x6 grid, splittable items, fragmentation tax — the mechanic DEADWEIGHT v1 built for its own combat is, structurally, a card-effect resolver). `DEADWEIGHT_2` ("CRASH_OVERRIDE") is real, shipped CI/releases (Windows+native client, v0.3.0 tag found in its own git log) — **shipped**: v0.3.0 released 2026-09-25 (Linux + Windows assets), v0.6.0 is latest. The earlier "built, not shipped" note is stale. See `audits/deadweight2_ship_audit.md`.
      | **TRAPX** | **The universe/doctrine** — the systemic rules every faction operates under. | Real, separate repo (not the `SHANKPIT/docs2/TRAPX_NORTHSTAR.md` derivative) — TRAPX v1 "BLOCK ZERO": single-player systemic urban sim, a 10x10/12x12 grid, no avatar, no direct unit control, no win condition, cells tracking alignment (Neutral/Player/Rival/Institutional) and signed pressure, influenced by a deck of operations. **This is the doctrine layer BIG_O's faction sim should be an instance of** — TRAPX is the general systemic-influence ruleset, BIG_O's Attention/Heat/faction-politics is one concrete application of it.
      | **TYLER** | **The lore.** Narrative substrate every hero/card/faction is actually *from*. | `TYLER/multiverse_heroes.md` is already ECOWAR's real card-content source today — this role is already live, not aspirational.
      | **SHANKPIT** | **The operating system** — engine/platform substrate (netcode, rendering, level/portal system) everything else runs on top of. | Matches `SHARED_ENGINE_NORTHSTAR.md`'s own framing of SHANKPIT as the canonical engine source; BIG_O is literally built on the SHANKPIT engine already (`BIG_O/NORTHSTAR.md` day-loop = "SHANKPIT FPS (existing)").
      | **REDGARDEN** | **The hero UI** — not gameplay anymore, the visual/UX layer for presenting heroes/cards. | ECOWAR's fork source; `REDGARDEN/docs/HEROES_VS0.md` already has real, concrete hero kits (LoL/DOTA-familiar stat lines) — this is the real asset to lift into a UI role (hero select, card frames, stat display) rather than keep developing REDGARDEN as a second independent RTS alongside ECOWAR.
      
      ## 2) What "merge" means now (corrected from v0's "shared backend only" read)
      
      Still true from v0, kept: this is not "collapse four C codebases into one Bazel target blindly."
      What changes: the four repos aren't peer products sharing a ladder — they're **layers of one
      product**, and the merge direction is a real dependency chain, not a bus everyone plugs into:
      
      ```
      TRAPX (doctrine)  ──────────────┐
      TYLER (lore)      ──────────────┤
                                       ▼
                          BIG_O (headless faction/tech-tree sim)
                                       │  (needs: a GUI resource-management
                                       │   front end — doesn't exist yet)
                                       ▼
                ECOWAR (the game — client, cards place units, Clash-Royale real-time resolution)
                                       │  (cards are written in)
                                       ▼
                          DEADWEIGHT's card_rules language
                                       │  (presented via)
                                       ▼
                          REDGARDEN's hero UI assets
                                       │  (running on)
                                       ▼
                          SHANKPIT (engine/OS substrate)
      ```
      
      `EMPIRE` as a repo is the place this assembly actually happens — not a fifth independent codebase,
      a real integration point where ECOWAR's client calls into a BIG_O-derived sim for faction state,
      resolves cards through DEADWEIGHT's rules engine, and renders hero content through REDGARDEN's UI
      assets, all on SHANKPIT. Each source repo keeps developing its own layer; `EMPIRE` is where they
      compose, same relationship PARENA's own per-game `stdlib/{ecowar,gfd,shankpit}` mod directories
      already have to `PARENA/stdlib/` core — a consuming layer, not a replacement for any of them.
      
      ## 3) Merge order: ECOWAR + BIG_O first (founder's own explicit sequencing)
      
      **Status (2026-10-08):** §3.1 has a first real bridge in this repo: `bridge/faction_bridge.{h,c}`, tested
      headlessly against a vendored copy of BIG_O's witness rules (`make test`). The decorum gate and write-back are
      real; the MYTHIC/MUNDANE mapping is an invented v1 tuning pending founder sign-off. ECOWAR's own copy (`aff6ce0`)
      is not switched onto this module yet. §3.2 TECHTREE shipped as a BIG_O phone app (BIG_O `8f28e26`), shell only.
      
      **§3.3 (kanban #578, 2026-10-08):** the deck and unit-placement model is built here in `deck/`: an 8-card
      cycle, a 4-slot hand, a DECK screen and a UNITS placement grid, gated and written back through the bridge. It
      is headless and tested (`make test`). Not yet rendered: a phone shell has to draw it. Open: where that shell lives,
      and whether ECOWAR's own client hosts it instead.
      
      **§3.3 wiring (kanban #579, 2026-10-08):** the deck UI now binds to a shared `EmpireFaction` record
      (`bridge/faction_state.{h,c}`) instead of owning its own decorum. The BIG_O side loads authoritative decorum
      into it and both sides read and write the same numbers. The live feed from a BIG_O server is still missing:
      BIG_O has no server-side faction decorum store yet (only the scenario sim `core/sim.h`).
      
      **Why this pair, first:** ECOWAR already has real cards with no UI; BIG_O already has a real
      headless sim with no GUI. Both halves of "client ↔ sim" exist independently and neither is
      wired to anything yet — this is the cheapest real integration available, not a new build.
      
      - **3.1 — Give ECOWAR's cards somewhere to read faction state from.** Today `ecowar_resolve_card_effect`
        computes a card's magnitude in isolation (I32 decision logic, no external state). BIG_O's
        Attention/Heat module is exactly shaped to be that external state: a headless, PARENA-scalar,
        deterministic rules module. Concretely: expose BIG_O's faction/Attention state as a read (and,
        for some cards, read-write) input to `card_effect_mod.prn`, so playing a card is affected by —
        and affects — which faction currently holds pressure/alignment on the relevant TRAPX-doctrine
        grid cell. This is new wiring, not new game design — both sides already compute the right shape
        of number, they just don't talk yet.
      - **3.2 — Build the GUI resource-management layer BIG_O needs, as the "BURNER UI" (founder's own
        name, real-time, this session).** Correction to the first draft of this step: BIG_O does **not**
        have zero GUI — it has a real, already-shipped phone shell (`BigoPhone`,
        `day/packages/common/bigo_phone.h`), a home-screen app grid (`BP_APP_COUNT`, grid-nav cursor)
        with real apps already live: `MESSAGES`, `CONTACTS`, `MAP`, `CAMERA`, `NOTES` (TYLER-spec),
        `LAB`, `CARGO`, `SKILLS`, `LOADOUT`, `WARDROBE`, `STATUS` (BIG_O-specific). This phone *is* the
        "BURNER UI" — the founder's explicit instruction is to run **every** in-game affordance across
        the merged product through it, not just BIG_O's own menus. Concretely:
        - BIG_O's tech-tree/resource-management screen (3.1/3.2's original ask) ships as a **new phone
          app** (`BP_APP_TECHTREE` or similar), not a new screen system — same home-grid, same input
          model (`BP_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/SELECT/BACK`), same render path as `LAB`/`CARGO`/`SKILLS` today.
        - ECOWAR's own named gap — no deck/hand UI, no unit-placement input (§3.3) — becomes **phone
          apps too** (e.g. `BP_APP_DECK`, `BP_APP_UNITS`), not a second, ECOWAR-native UI stack built in
          parallel. This is the real, concrete answer to "unify the design language": one phone shell,
          one app-grid home screen, one input model, used by both BIG_O's sim-facing apps and ECOWAR's
          card/unit-facing apps.
        - This reframes open question 3 below from "is tech tree literal" to a now-answered "tech tree
          and units both live as phone apps" — still open: the *content* of those apps (what a tech-tree
          phone screen actually shows) isn't designed yet, only the shell they render through.
      - **3.3 — Deck/hand UI + unit placement, wired to the above.** ECOWAR's own already-named gap
        (no deck/hand UI, no in-match card-play input) gets built now with a real reason to exist: cards
        play against/into BIG_O-derived faction state from 3.1, displayed through 3.2's screen. Building
        deck/hand UI before 3.1/3.2 would just be REDGARDEN's RTS move-set over again with new card art.
      - **3.4 — Only then:** TRAPX-doctrine generalization (is BIG_O's faction sim really one instance
        of TRAPX's grid/alignment/pressure ruleset, or does it need its own rules that merely resemble
        TRAPX's?), DEADWEIGHT/DEADWEIGHT_2's card-language formalization (should ECOWAR's card effects
        be re-expressed in DEADWEIGHT's `card_rules.c` grammar, gaining its fragmentation-tax-shaped
        mechanics as a side effect?), and REDGARDEN's hero-UI lift (reskin ECOWAR's card presentation
        using `HEROES_VS0.md` stat lines and REDGARDEN's existing UI, rather than ECOWAR growing a third
        independent UI). Each of these is real work with its own open questions (§5) — sequenced after
        3.1-3.3 because they're refinements of an ECOWAR+BIG_O link that doesn't exist yet at all.
      
      **§3.4 card language (kanban #583, 2026-10-08):** audited, not ported. ECOWAR's DAMAGE and HEAL and FLOW map partly
      to DEADWEIGHT channels. SLOW, SILENCE and MYTHIC scaling have no equivalent, so the grammar would need changing,
      which is a founder decision. See `audits/card_language_mapping.md`.
      
      **§3.4 hero UI (kanban #584, 2026-10-08):** blocked, not built. HEROES_VS0 covers REDGARDEN's own kits, not ECOWAR's
      16 card heroes, and the source ECOWAR cites (`TYLER/multiverse_heroes.md`) is missing from this checkout. See
      `audits/hero_ui_lift_blocked.md`.
      
      ## 4) Full `github.com/emilyspringerton/*` inventory — what else is relevant, checked live
      
      Pulled via `gh repo list emilyspringerton --limit 200` this session (91 repos total, real org
      listing, not the repo table in the root `CLAUDE.md` which is a hand-maintained summary and can
      drift). Relevant hits beyond the six named above:
      
      - **`MONOREPO`** — exists, but is operational glue only (`go.work`, deploy scripts, sudo-queue) —
        **not** a prior attempt at this same merge. No conflict with this doc's plan.
      - **`GoblinFoxDragon`** — ECOWAR's README explicitly supersedes GFD's `apps2/battlegrounds_gui` as
        ECOWAR's own original (now-abandoned) interface-fork path. Confirmed unrelated going forward.
      - **`WEAKNIGHT_BEDROCK_RACERS`**, **`BRAWLPIT`**, **`SLOWBOT_LEAGUE`** — other PvP/ladder products
        in the same general family (bot pools, Elo, IDUNA `games.Registry`), not part of this specific
        four-repo merge but worth knowing about before building a second bot-pool/ladder pattern from
        scratch in `EMPIRE` — `SLOWBOT_LEAGUE/NORTHSTAR.md`'s own audit of `games.Registry` is the
        precedent to reuse if/when EMPIRE needs ranked matchmaking.
      - **`DEADWEIGHT_2`** is real and distinct from `DEADWEIGHT` (confirmed: own repo, own CI, own
        "CRASH_OVERRIDE" identity, v0.3.0 release tag) — not a typo, not the same repo. "DEADWEIGHT 1 +
        2" in the founder's framing means literally both repos' card-language code are in scope.
      - Nothing else in the 91-repo list names BIG_O, ECOWAR, TRAPX, or EMPIRE as a target — no other
        repo is already attempting this merge.
      
      ## 5) Open questions (real, not resolved here)
      
      1. ~~Is BIG_O's Attention/Heat module's data shape actually compatible with what ECOWAR's card effects need?~~
         **Resolved at the bit level (kanban #582, 2026-10-08):** yes, no translation layer needed. Both sides are plain
         32-bit signed `int`. Every decorum and action stays in 0..100 (checked exhaustively). The largest scaled card
         magnitude fits in int. EMPIRE's MYTHIC list matches ECOWAR's compiled `card_effect_mod` for all 16 cards
         (`make compat`). The only shared quantity is decorum, so no other field needs translating.
      2. ~~What, specifically, is DEADWEIGHT_2 missing to ship?~~ **Resolved (kanban #580, 2026-10-08):** nothing.
         v0.3.0 shipped 2026-09-25 with Linux and Windows assets, and v0.6.0 is latest. See `audits/deadweight2_ship_audit.md`.
      3. ~~Does "BIG_O is the tech tree" mean a literal research/upgrade tree UI?~~ **Resolved, same
         session**: tech tree and ECOWAR's units both render as apps inside the BURNER UI phone shell
         (§3.2). Still open: the actual *content/layout* of a tech-tree phone app and a units phone app
         — not designed, only the shell they'll use is settled.
      4. ~~Should the TRAPX-doctrine generalization (3.4) run through the standalone `TRAPX` repo or
         `SHANKPIT/docs2/TRAPX_NORTHSTAR.md`?~~ **Reconciled (kanban #581, 2026-10-08):** the standalone `TRAPX` repo is
         the doctrine. The SHANKPIT document is a separate product that shares the name. Still open for the founder:
         the grid conflict (README 10/12 vs code 20) and whether BIG_O adopts the cell model. See
         `audits/trapx_doctrine_reconciliation.md`.
      5. REDGARDEN still has no auth model (carried over from the prior session's finding) — irrelevant
         to the hero-UI role itself (3.4's asset lift doesn't need REDGARDEN's own account system) but
         worth remembering if REDGARDEN ever needs to run live alongside ECOWAR rather than just donate
         UI assets to it.

> _Reasoning_
> The user's ask is broad: "make sure that all of the EMPIRE work is complete" — spawn allies like Mike, with their own AIs (explore, engage, follow, take territory, gather resources), configurable skin for ally, programmable custom AIs, generic human inheritance, merge citizen BIG_O work, and a level-building affordance to spawn citizens/zombies/soldiers etc. with different AIs. "look into how empire does it".
> 
> This is a large feature. I need to scope it sensibly: build the smallest coherent system that satisfies:
> 
> 1. A **unit archetype catalog** (citizen, zombie, soldier, ally/Mike) that can be authored in a level and spawned, with: skin (kit), role (AI brain), faction/team (ally vs hostile), and behaviors.
> 2. **Allies** that follow, engage, explore, gather, claim territory — need real behaviors in story_ai (which has ALLY_FOLLOW, PATROL, COMBAT, SEARCH...). Missing: EXPLORE, GATHER, CLAIM (territory).
> 3. **Generic human inheritance**: a "human" baseline (needs: hunger? no—simplest: humans share senses/needs/morale defaults) that non-human AIs don't inherit. So a shared "species/body plan" trait layer: humans get stamina/humanness/tool use; zombies don't.
> 4. **Custom programmable AIs** via EduVM/PARENA? The repo has PARENA rules modules + EduVM scripts. A "programmable AI" affordance probably means: an AI profile defined in PARENA (personality weights: aggression, courage, greed, curiosity) plus an EduVM script hook. There's `ai_persona`-like config? Let me check what exists.
> 
> Given the size, I must be careful: the user asked to "make sure all EMPIRE work is complete" — but EMPIRE (the repo) is a card/deck faction bridge, not AI units. What the user really wants is: the AI/faction/unit system (EMPIRE-like RTS-ish) inside SHANKPIT so they can spawn citizens/zombies/soldiers/allies with distinct AI and skins, from the level editor.
> 
> Best approach: implement a real, tested module:
> 
> **`packages/simulation/unit_catalog.h`** (PARENA-backed rules) — archetypes: CITIZEN, ZOMBIE, SOLDIER, ALLY, GUARD, BEAST... each with: body plan (human/non-human), default kit, default role, faction alignment, behavior flags (can_gather, can_claim, can_follow, can_explore), stat modifiers.
>

- path: MONOREPO/PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn
  content: |
      ;; stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn -- shared (instanceless) world zones and their procedural layouts.
      ;;
      ;; Founder: "we need to start unifying GFD and shankpit ... i want to make it so that GFD server we have
      ;; it like diablo where we can travel to a map and do it as a dungeon it can be procedurally generated
      ;; ... for now the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the same one ...
      ;; there should be a grace period of 15 minutes for the zone existing for after you leave it ... dungeons
      ;; are not instanced they are generated and then they exist until everyone leaves + 15 minutes".
      ;;
      ;; So there are two separate things here and they are deliberately not the same file:
      ;;   * the LIFECYCLE (how long an empty zone survives) is pure arithmetic on two integers -- this module,
      ;;     so the client, the server and the test cannot disagree about the grace period;
      ;;   * the LAYOUT (how many rooms, how big, which material) is generation parameters, also here, so a
      ;;     seed produces the same dungeon on every machine that runs this build.
      ;;
      ;; Every function is I32 and total: no state, no allocation, no RNG hidden inside. The caller owns the
      ;; seed and the clock (packages/simulation/zone_registry.h), which is what makes a zone reproducible and
      ;; a test possible. All millisecond values are milliseconds.
      (module shankpit/zone-rules)
      (export zone-grace-seconds zone-max-zones
              zone-room-count zone-room-width zone-room-depth zone-wall-height
              zone-wall-thickness zone-door-width zone-ring-distance
              zone-ring-dir-x zone-ring-dir-z
              zone-spawn-count zone-mob-count zone-material-count zone-material-for
              zone-difficulty zone-zone-status-name
              zone-should-expire zone-elapsed-ms)
      
      ;; zr-clamp, NOT w-clamp: PARENA lowers a helper to a global C function, and widget_rules.prn already
      ;; defines w_clamp -- two modules with the same helper name is a duplicate-symbol link error, found live.
      (defn zr-clamp [(lo : I32) (hi : I32) (x : I32)] : I32 (if (< x lo) lo (if (> x hi) hi x)))
      
      ;; The founder's own number: fifteen minutes of nobody inside and the layout is gone, so a farmed-out
      ;; zone does not come back the way it was.
      (defn zone-grace-seconds [] : I32 900)
      
      ;; One registry slot per zone id. Small on purpose: a zone holds a full level (hundreds of boxes) in the
      ;; host's own memory, so this is a count of live layouts, not a list of every door in the world.
      (defn zone-max-zones [] : I32 8)
      
      ;; ---- layout parameters ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; A hub plus 2..4 cardinal rooms. 3..5 rooms total, never a diagonal corridor (they are the one case
      ;; that needs corner geometry, and a four-way hub already reads as a dungeon crossing).
      ;; All sizes are world units, matching LevelBox's own convention.
      (defn zone-room-count [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 3 (zr-clamp 0 2 (mod seed 3))))
      (defn zone-room-width [(seed : I32) (room : I32)] : I32
        (+ 24 (* 8 (zr-clamp 0 2 (mod (+ seed (* room 37)) 3)))))
      (defn zone-room-depth [(seed : I32) (room : I32)] : I32
        (+ 24 (* 8 (zr-clamp 0 2 (mod (+ seed (* room 53)) 3)))))
      (defn zone-wall-height [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 18 (* 6 (zr-clamp 0 2 (mod seed 3)))))
      (defn zone-wall-thickness [] : I32 2)
      (defn zone-door-width [] : I32 8)
      ;; Far enough apart that two 40-unit rooms do not share a wall, close enough that a corridor is short.
      (defn zone-ring-distance [] : I32 52)
      
      ;; Cardinal directions only, 0 = east, 1 = south, 2 = west, 3 = north (x east, z south, matching the
      ;; engine's own yaw-0-faces--Z convention). Room i uses direction (i - 1) mod 4.
      (defn zone-ring-dir-x [(dir : I32)] : I32
        (if (= (zr-clamp 0 3 dir) 0) 1 (if (= (zr-clamp 0 3 dir) 2) -1 0)))
      (defn zone-ring-dir-z [(dir : I32)] : I32
        (if (= (zr-clamp 0 3 dir) 1) 1 (if (= (zr-clamp 0 3 dir) 3) -1 0)))
      
      ;; One spawner in the hub and one per room, so a party never has to walk the whole layout to find where
      ;; it started. Capped at LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_SPAWNERS by the generator.
      (defn zone-spawn-count [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 3 (zr-clamp 0 2 (mod seed 3))))
      ;; What the mode's own population should be told to aim for. Twice the rooms plus a little, so a 5-room
      ;; layout is a real fight and a 3-room layout is not empty.
      (defn zone-mob-count [(seed : I32) (rooms : I32)] : I32 (+ (* 2 (zr-clamp 1 8 rooms)) (mod seed 5)))
      
      ;; 0 concrete, 1 metal, 2 brick -- indices into the generator's own material table, which is why this is
      ;; a kind and not a colour: the level file carries the material, the renderer owns the look.
      (defn zone-material-count [] : I32 3)
      (defn zone-material-for [(seed : I32) (idx : I32)] : I32 (mod (+ seed (* idx 7)) 3))
      
      ;; 1..5, the depth of the zone's own dungeon tier -- GFD's state server is what turns this into stats.
      (defn zone-difficulty [(seed : I32)] : I32 (+ 1 (zr-clamp 0 4 (mod seed 5))))
      
      ;; ---- lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      ;; Expire only when BOTH are true: nobody is inside AND the grace window has run out. A zone that is
      ;; still occupied never expires, no matter how long the clock says it has existed.
      (defn zone-should-expire [(players : I32) (idle_ms : I32)] : I32
        (if (<= (zr-clamp 0 1000 players) 0)
            (if (>= (zr-clamp 0 2000000000 idle_ms) (* (zone-grace-seconds) 1000)) 1 0)
            0))
      
      (defn zone-elapsed-ms [(now_ms : I32) (since_ms : I32)] : I32
        (if (> now_ms since_ms) (- now_ms since_ms) 0))
      
      ;; 0 uninitialized, 1 active (someone inside or recently inside), 2 idle (empty, counting down).
      (defn zone-zone-status-name [(status : I32)] : I32 (zr-clamp 0 2 status))
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/zone_rules.h
  content: |
      /* zone_rules.h -- shared zone lifecycle + procedural layout rules, with built-in defaults.
       *
       * The numbers live in PARENA (PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn, generated into zone_rules.c by
       * scripts/gen_zone_rules.sh / `make regen-zone-rules`, installed through zone_rules_host.h). This header
       * carries matching C defaults so packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h and zone_registry.h compile and run
       * in any binary or test without linking a generated file -- the same arrangement widget_rules.h and
       * slide_rules.h use, and `make test-proc-dungeon` asserts the two copies agree sample for sample.
       *
       * Two separate concerns share this table on purpose, because both are "the zone's own numbers":
       *   - LIFECYCLE: grace seconds, max live zones, the expiry predicate.
       *   - LAYOUT: rooms, sizes, wall height, doors, spawners, material kind, difficulty tier.
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H
      #define SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H
      
      typedef struct {
          int (*grace_seconds)(void);
          int (*max_zones)(void);
          int (*room_count)(int seed);
          int (*room_width)(int seed, int room);
          int (*room_depth)(int seed, int room);
          int (*wall_height)(int seed);
          int (*wall_thickness)(void);
          int (*door_width)(void);
          int (*ring_distance)(void);
          int (*ring_dir_x)(int dir);
          int (*ring_dir_z)(int dir);
          int (*spawn_count)(int seed);
          int (*mob_count)(int seed, int rooms);
          int (*material_count)(void);
          int (*material_for)(int seed, int idx);
          int (*difficulty)(int seed);
          int (*should_expire)(int players, int idle_ms);
          int (*elapsed_ms)(int now_ms, int since_ms);
      } ZoneRules;
      
      static inline int zr_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }
      
      static inline int zr_c_grace_seconds(void) { return 900; }
      static inline int zr_c_max_zones(void) { return 8; }
      static inline int zr_c_room_count(int seed) { return 3 + zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_room_width(int seed, int room) { return 24 + 8 * zr_clamp(0, 2, (seed + room * 37) % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_room_depth(int seed, int room) { return 24 + 8 * zr_clamp(0, 2, (seed + room * 53) % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_wall_height(int seed) { return 18 + 6 * zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_wall_thickness(void) { return 2; }
      static inline int zr_c_door_width(void) { return 8; }
      static inline int zr_c_ring_distance(void) { return 52; }
      static inline int zr_c_ring_dir_x(int dir) {
          dir = zr_clamp(0, 3, dir);
          return dir == 0 ? 1 : (dir == 2 ? -1 : 0);
      }
      static inline int zr_c_ring_dir_z(int dir) {
          dir = zr_clamp(0, 3, dir);
          return dir == 1 ? 1 : (dir == 3 ? -1 : 0);
      }
      static inline int zr_c_spawn_count(int seed) { return 3 + zr_clamp(0, 2, seed % 3); }
      static inline int zr_c_mob_count(int seed, int rooms) {
          return 2 * zr_clamp(1, 8, rooms) + seed % 5;
      }
      static inline int zr_c_material_count(void) { return 3; }
      static inline int zr_c_material_for(int seed, int idx) { return (seed + idx * 7) % 3; }
      static inline int zr_c_difficulty(int seed) { return 1 + zr_clamp(0, 4, seed % 5); }
      static inline int zr_c_should_expire(int players, int idle_ms) {
          if (zr_clamp(0, 1000, players) > 0) return 0;
          return zr_clamp(0, 2000000000, idle_ms) >= zr_c_grace_seconds() * 1000 ? 1 : 0;
      }
      static inline int zr_c_elapsed_ms(int now_ms, int since_ms) { return now_ms > since_ms ? now_ms - since_ms : 0; }
      
      static ZoneRules g_zone_rules = {
          zr_c_grace_seconds, zr_c_max_zones, zr_c_room_count, zr_c_room_width, zr_c_room_depth,
          zr_c_wall_height, zr_c_wall_thickness, zr_c_door_width, zr_c_ring_distance, zr_c_ring_dir_x,
          zr_c_ring_dir_z, zr_c_spawn_count, zr_c_mob_count, zr_c_material_count, zr_c_material_for,
          zr_c_difficulty, zr_c_should_expire, zr_c_elapsed_ms
      };
      
      static inline void zone_rules_set(const ZoneRules *r) { if (r) g_zone_rules = *r; }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_H */
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/mk/zone_rules.mk
  content: |
      # mk/zone_rules.mk -- shared procedural zones (2026-10-31).
      #
      # Founder: "GFD server ... like diablo where we can travel to a map and do it as a dungeon it can be
      # procedurally generated ... the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the
      # same one ... there should be a grace period of 15 minutes". The lifecycle and layout numbers live in
      # PARENA; packages/simulation/proc_dungeon.h builds the level and zone_registry.h runs the clock.
      
      .PHONY: regen-zone-rules test-proc-dungeon test-zone-sync
      
      regen-zone-rules:
        scripts/gen_zone_rules.sh
      
      # test-proc-dungeon -- determinism and the shared-zone lifecycle: two clients generating from one seed
      # write byte-identical levels, a saved dungeon round-trips through the real parser, the gate opens on its
      # relay's delay, a second entrant joins the same layout, and the zone survives fifteen empty minutes (and
      # only then regenerates from a new seed).
      test-proc-dungeon: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ipackages/simulation -Ipackages/world \
          packages/simulation/proc_dungeon_test.c packages/simulation/zone_rules.c \
          packages/simulation/widget_rules.c \
          -o $(BIN_DIR)/proc_dungeon_test $(LIBS_M)
        ./$(BIN_DIR)/proc_dungeon_test
      
      # test-zone-sync -- the zone WIRE contract: a short datagram, the wrong type and an unterminated id are
      # all refused (the id becomes a filename), and a repeated 1 Hz packet must not reload the world while a
      # new seed or a new zone must.
      test-zone-sync: | $(BIN_DIR)
        $(CC) -std=gnu99 -O1 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Ipackages/simulation -Ipackages/common \
          packages/simulation/zone_sync_test.c -o $(BIN_DIR)/zone_sync_test $(LIBS_M)
        ./$(BIN_DIR)/zone_sync_test
      
- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/witness_ai.h
  content: |
       * standing outside every authored zone (or `level` is NULL -- no level data loaded, or a level
       * with no "zones" array at all) keeps its LAST zone rather than being silently reset to
       * ZONE_PUBLIC -- a real, deliberate choice: an unauthored gap in a level's zone coverage should
       * not read as a meaningful "the player stepped into public" fact.
       *
       * Deliberately a separate function from witness_ai_tick, not folded into it -- level data is
       * per-level (reloaded on `story_ai_reset`-style level transitions), while witness_ai_tick runs
       * every real server frame regardless of whether a level is even loaded; keeping them separate
       * means a caller with no CustomLevelData yet (or a non-story mode with no zones authored) can
       * still call witness_ai_tick every frame without this function ever needing a NULL-safe no-op
       * path baked into the hot loop. Real, honest, not wired into any live tick loop yet -- no caller
       * exists in apps/server or apps/lobby (that's 7d/7e, once a real MODE_STORY-replacing game loop
       * calls both this and witness_ai_tick together each frame). */
      void witness_ai_sync_zones(ServerState *s, const CustomLevelData *level);
      
      /* witness_ai_seed_voxworld_encounter -- BIG_O engine merge phase 7d (MODE_STORY content
       * cutover, "replace outright" per founder direction). The real replacement for
       * story_ai_seed_voxworld_encounter (story_ai.c) as MODE_STORY's VOXWORLD content: 4 ambient
       * citizens and 2 zombies instead of the old AI_ROLE_* combat squad/patrol encounter. A no-op for
       * any other scene (mirrors story_ai_seed_voxworld_encounter's own SCENE_VOXWORLD guard exactly).
       *
       * Real, deliberate, narrowly-scoped cutover -- what this does NOT touch, on purpose:
       *  - story_ai.c's own AI_ROLE_* roster and its general LevelCharacter/NOCK-authoring spawn path
       *    (server_apply_custom_level) stay completely alive and untouched -- that's real, general,
       *    cross-mode level-editor infrastructure other levels may use (SHANKPIT/CLAUDE.md's own
       *    standing "levels are never story-mode-only" instruction), not "MODE_STORY's content."
       *  - The VOXWORLD boss fight (StoryBossState, local_game.h) is a separate, hand-rolled system
       *    with no relationship to story_ai.c's AIController roster -- out of scope, untouched.
       *
       * Bootstraps one zombie straight into HUNTING (via witness_ai_force_zombie_mood below) --
       * real, honest reason: zombie_tick's own has_target is always 0 (no perception system exists
       * yet, see this header's own top doc comment), so a freshly-spawned zombie would otherwise sit
       * DORMANT forever with nothing for any citizen to ever witness. This is the same test/debug hook
       * witness_ai_test.c already exercises, now given its first real gameplay call site. */
      void witness_ai_seed_voxworld_encounter(ServerState *s, unsigned int now_ms);
      
      /* Test/debug hook: directly forces a zombie's mood, bypassing the real has_target-gated tick path
       * -- the same real, named boundary this header's own top doc comment already states (no
       * perception system exists yet to earn HUNTING/FRENZIED organically). */
      void witness_ai_force_zombie_mood(int player_id, int mood);
      
      /* Test/debug accessor: the current WS_* witness state of the citizen at this player_id, or -1 if
       * player_id doesn't resolve to an active citizen spawned by this module. */
      int witness_ai_citizen_state(int player_id);
      
      /* Test/debug accessor: the citizen's CURRENT WitnessNpc vigilance (npc_archetype's own real
       * mood-modulated value, written back by witness_ai_tick -- see witness_ai.c's own doc comment),
       * or -1 if player_id doesn't resolve to an active citizen spawned by this module. */
      int witness_ai_citizen_vigilance(int player_id);
      
      /* Test/debug accessor: the citizen's CURRENT WitnessNpc zone (a ZONE_* value, witness_sim.h),
       * or -1 if player_id doesn't resolve to an active citizen spawned by this module. */
      int witness_ai_citizen_zone(int player_id);
      
      /* --- "full phone app parity, costume changes, add The Men" (EMILY/BACKLOG.md SECTION 536
       * follow-up, founder real-time, 2026-09-22) -------------------------------------------------- */
      
      /* Same "int with a -1 sentinel" convention as witness_ai_citizen_state/vigilance/zone above. A
       * caller (main.c's own mannequin-kit selector) needs to tell citizen/The Men/zombie apart to give
       * each a real, distinct visual identity -- see witness_ai.c's own doc comment on why this reuses
       * npc_archetype.h's existing NPC_ARCHETYPE_* distinction rather than inventing a new one. */
      #define WITNESS_AI_ROLE_NONE -1
      #define WITNESS_AI_ROLE_CITIZEN 0
      #define WITNESS_AI_ROLE_THE_MEN 1
      #define WITNESS_AI_ROLE_ZOMBIE 2
      #define WITNESS_AI_ROLE_GIANT_BUG 3
      #define WITNESS_AI_ROLE_BIRD 4
      int witness_ai_role_for_player(int player_id);
      
      /* Spawns one member of The Men (npc_archetype.h's NPC_ARCHETYPE_THE_MEN -- high base_vigilance,
       * focused mood bias, already real and tested since phase 3, never actually spawned anywhere until
       * now) into a free player slot. Same shape/contract as witness_ai_spawn_citizen, sharing that
       * function's own internal spawn_human helper (witness_ai.c) -- not a duplicate implementation.

          if (!s) return -1;

          memset(ai, 0, sizeof(*ai));
          p->active = 1;
          p->is_bot = 1;
          p->scene_id = s->scene_id;
          p->team_id = -1;
          p->state = STATE_ALIVE;
          p->health = 100;
          p->shield = 0;
          p->x = x;

          p->carried_flag_team_id = -1;

          ai->active = 1;
          ai->player_id = slot;
          ai->role = role;
          ai->mode = (role == AI_ROLE_STORY_ALLY) ? AI_MODE_ALLY_FOLLOW : AI_MODE_PATROL;
          ai->previous_mode = AI_MODE_DISABLED;

      /* zone_rules_host.h -- installs PARENA's zone rules into zone_rules.h.
       * The rules live in PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/zone_rules.prn, generated into zone_rules.c (do not edit it;
       * `make regen-zone-rules`). A host that runs zones (apps/lobby, apps/server) includes this header, links
       * zone_rules.c, and calls zone_rules_install() once at startup. With nothing installed zone_rules.h's own
       * defaults are used, so tests keep their link lines. */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_HOST_H
      #define SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_HOST_H
      
      #include "zone_rules.h"
      
      /* PARENA-generated (zone_rules.c) */
      int zone_grace_seconds(void);
      int zone_max_zones(void);
      int zone_room_count(int seed);
      int zone_room_width(int seed, int room);
      int zone_room_depth(int seed, int room);
      int zone_wall_height(int seed);
      int zone_wall_thickness(void);
      int zone_door_width(void);
      int zone_ring_distance(void);
      int zone_ring_dir_x(int dir);
      int zone_ring_dir_z(int dir);
      int zone_spawn_count(int seed);
      int zone_mob_count(int seed, int rooms);
      int zone_material_count(void);
      int zone_material_for(int seed, int idx);
      int zone_difficulty(int seed);
      int zone_should_expire(int players, int idle_ms);
      int zone_elapsed_ms(int now_ms, int since_ms);
      
      static const ZoneRules g_zone_rules_parena = {
          zone_grace_seconds, zone_max_zones, zone_room_count, zone_room_width, zone_room_depth,
          zone_wall_height, zone_wall_thickness, zone_door_width, zone_ring_distance, zone_ring_dir_x,
          zone_ring_dir_z, zone_spawn_count, zone_mob_count, zone_material_count, zone_material_for,
          zone_difficulty, zone_should_expire, zone_elapsed_ms
      };
      
      static inline void zone_rules_install(void) { zone_rules_set(&g_zone_rules_parena); }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_RULES_HOST_H */

it is a different row.\n *   - ORDERS: the programmable half -- a mask of accepted orders and a per-archetype priority for each.\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_RULES_H\n#define SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_RULES_H\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int (*archetype_count)(void);\n    int (*archetype_species)(int arch);\n    int (*archetype_role)(int arch);\n    int (*archetype_kit)(int arch);\n    int (*archetype_faction)(int arch);\n    int (*archetype_orders)(int arch);\n    int (*archetype_health)(int arch);\n    int (*human_courage)(void);\n    int (*human_aggression)(void);\n    int (*human_loyalty)(void);\n    int (*human_greed)(void);\n    int (*human_curiosity)(void);\n    int (*beast_courage)(void);\n    int (*beast_aggression)(void);\n    int (*beast_loyalty)(void);\n    int (*beast_greed)(void);\n    int (*beast_curiosity)(void);\n    int (*order_follow)(void);\n    int (*order_explore)(void);\n    int (*order_engage)(void);\n    int (*order_gather)(void);\n    int (*order_claim)(void);\n    int (*order_guard)(void);\n    int (*order_priority)(int arch, int order);\n    int (*claim_ticks)(void);\n    int (*claim_radius)(void);\n    int (*gather_radius)(void);\n    int (*node_capacity)(void);\n    int (*explore_radius)(void);\n    int (*follow_distance)(void);\n} EmpireRules;\n\nstatic inline int eu_clamp(int lo, int hi, int x) { return x < lo ? lo : (x > hi ? hi : x); }\n\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_count(void) { return 6; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_species(int arch) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    if (arch == 0) return 0;\n    return arch == 2 ? 2 : 1;\n}\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_role(int arch) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    if (arch == 0) return 0;\n    if (arch == 1) return 10; /* WANDERING_BOT */\n    if (arch == 2) return 7;  /* RELENTLESS_PURSUER */\n    if (arch == 3) return 4;  /* GUARD */\n    if (arch == 4) return 3;  /* STORY_ALLY */\n    if (arch == 5) return 4;  /* GUARD */\n    return 10;                /* WORKER -> WANDERING_BOT */\n}\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_kit(int arch) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    if (arch == 0) return 0;\n    if (arch == 1) return 1; /* MANNEQUIN */\n    if (arch == 2) return 0; /* AUTO (the zombie clip set is picked by the witness role, not by AIKit) */\n    if (arch == 3) return 2; /* STAN */\n    if (arch == 4) return 3; /* MIKE -- the founder's own ally */\n    if (arch == 5) return 5; /* GEORGE */\n    return 4;                /* LEELA */\n}\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_faction(int arch) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    if (arch == 0) return 0;\n    if (arch == 2 || arch == 3 || arch == 5) return 2; /* hostile */\n    if (arch == 4) return 1;                           /* ally */\n    return 0;                                          /* citizen/worker: neutral */\n}\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_orders(int arch) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    if (arch == 0) return 0;\n    if (arch == 1) return 42; /* EXPLORE|GATHER|GUARD */\n    if (arch == 2) return 4;  /* ENGAGE */\n    if (arch == 3) return 52; /* ENGAGE|CLAIM|GUARD */\n    if (arch == 4) return 15; /* FOLLOW|EXPLORE|ENGAGE|GATHER */\n    if (arch == 5) return 36; /* ENGAGE|GUARD */\n    return 11;                /* FOLLOW|EXPLORE|GATHER */\n}\nstatic inline int eu_c_archetype_health(int arch) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    if (arch == 0) return 100;\n    if (arch == 1) return 60;\n    if (arch == 2) return 40;\n    if (arch == 3) return 100;\n    if (arch == 4) return 120;\n    if (arch == 5) return 100;\n    return 70;\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_c_human_courage(void) { return 600; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_human_aggression(void) { return 500; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_human_loyalty(void) { return 700; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_human_greed(void) { return 500; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_human_curiosity(void) { return 500; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_beast_courage(void) { return 900; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_beast_aggression(void) { return 900; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_beast_loyalty(void) { return 0; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_beast_greed(void) { return 0; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_beast_curiosity(void) { return 300; }\n\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_follow(void) { return 1; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_explore(void) { return 2; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_engage(void) { return 4; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_gather(void) { return 8; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_claim(void) { return 16; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_guard(void) { return 32; }\n\nstatic inline int eu_c_order_priority(int arch, int order) {\n    arch = eu_clamp(0, 6, arch);\n    order = eu_clamp(0, 5, order);\n    static const int table[7][6] = {\n        /* FOLLOW EXPLORE ENGAGE GATHER CLAIM GUARD */\n        {   0,    0,     0,     0,    0,    0 }, /* none    */\n        {   30,   60,    0,     50,   0,    40 }, /* citizen */\n        {   0,    0,     100,   0,    0,    0 },  /* zombie  */\n        {   20,   20,    85,    0,    60,   50 }, /* soldier */\n        {   80,   30,    90,    40,   20,   30 }, /* ally    */\n        {   10,   10,    70,    0,    20,   90 }, /* guard   */\n        {   50,   40,    0,     80,   30,   20 }  /* worker  */\n    };\n    return table[arch][order];\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_c_claim_ticks(void) { return 30000; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_claim_radius(void) { return 6; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_gather_radius(void) { return 5; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_node_capacity(void) { return 25; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_explore_radius(void) { return 60; }\nstatic inline int eu_c_follow_distance(void) { return 20; }\n\nstatic EmpireRules g_empire_rules = {\n    eu_c_archetype_count, eu_c_archetype_species, eu_c_archetype_role, eu_c_archetype_kit,\n    eu_c_archetype_faction, eu_c_archetype_orders, eu_c_archetype_health,\n    eu_c_human_courage, eu_c_human_aggression, eu_c_human_loyalty, eu_c_human_greed,\n    eu_c_human_curiosity,\n    eu_c_beast_courage, eu_c_beast_aggression, eu_c_beast_loyalty, eu_c_beast_greed,\n    eu_c_beast_curiosity,\n    eu_c_order_follow, eu_c_order_explore, eu_c_order_engage, eu_c_order_gather, eu_c_order_claim,\n    eu_c_order_guard, eu_c_order_priority,\n    eu_c_claim_ticks, eu_c_claim_radius, eu_c_gather_radius, eu_c_node_capacity,\n    eu_c_explore_radius, eu_c_follow_distance\n};\n\nstatic inline void empire_rules_set(const EmpireRules *r) { if (r) g_empire_rules = *r; }\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_RULES_H */\n"
}

Every human inherits one baseline row (courage, loyalty, greed,\n *                 curiosity); a non-human inherits the beast row. A zombie is not a human with different\n *                 numbers, which is why this is an inheritance switch and not a column.\n *   orders     -- the programmable half. A bitmask of what this unit accepts plus the archetype's own\n *                 priority for each, both authored (level JSON / NOCK) and both overridable per unit.\n *                 eu_choose_order below is the whole \"custom AI\": change the mask, change the behaviour,\n *                 without a new C branch.\n *\n * Deliberately dependency-free (no GL, SDL, physics, protocol, story_ai.h): roles and kits are plain\n * integers so story_ai.h can hold an EUUnit without a cycle, and so this is testable headlessly.\n * Numbers come from empire_rules.h, which mirrors PARENA (see that header).\n */\n#ifndef SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_UNITS_H\n#define SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_UNITS_H\n\n#include <math.h>\n#include \"empire_rules.h\"\n\n/* Archetypes. 0 is deliberately \"none\": a character with no archetype keeps exactly the pre-EMPIRE\n   behaviour (its authored role and kit, no orders), which is what keeps old levels loading unchanged. */\n#define EU_ARCH_NONE 0\n#define EU_ARCH_CITIZEN 1\n#define EU_ARCH_ZOMBIE 2\n#define EU_ARCH_SOLDIER 3\n#define EU_ARCH_ALLY 4\n#define EU_ARCH_GUARD 5\n#define EU_ARCH_WORKER 6\n#define EU_ARCH_COUNT 6\n\n#define EU_SPECIES_NONE 0\n#define EU_SPECIES_HUMAN 1\n#define EU_SPECIES_BEAST 2\n\n#define EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL 0\n#define EU_FACTION_ALLY 1\n#define EU_FACTION_HOSTILE 2\n#define EU_FACTION_COUNT 3\n\n/* Orders, as bits. These values are the contract the level JSON's own `orders` field uses. */\n#define EU_ORDER_NONE 0\n#define EU_ORDER_FOLLOW 1\n#define EU_ORDER_EXPLORE 2\n#define EU_ORDER_ENGAGE 4\n#define EU_ORDER_GATHER 8\n#define EU_ORDER_CLAIM 16\n#define EU_ORDER_GUARD 32\n#define EU_ORDER_ALL (EU_ORDER_FOLLOW | EU_ORDER_EXPLORE | EU_ORDER_ENGAGE | EU_ORDER_GATHER | \\\n                      EU_ORDER_CLAIM | EU_ORDER_GUARD)\n\n/* Order indexes for the rules table (eu_order_priority takes these, not the bits). */\n#define EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW 0\n#define EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE 1\n#define EU_ORDER_IDX_ENGAGE 2\n#define EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER 3\n#define EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM 4\n#define EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD 5\n\n#define EU_MAX_NODES 16\n#define EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS 32\n\n/* A resource node is a place, not an item: standing on it is what gathers. Amount is what is left. */\ntypedef struct {\n    float x, z;\n    int amount;\n    int capacity;\n} EUResourceNode;\n\n/* A claim cell is a piece of ground a faction can own. claim_ms is THIS claimant's progress, which is\n   why claimant is stored: a second faction standing on it starts over rather than inheriting the work. */\ntypedef struct {\n    float x, z;\n    int radius;\n    int owner;     /* EU_FACTION_* */\n    int claimant;  /* EU_FACTION_* currently making progress, NEUTRAL when nobody */\n    int claim_ms;\n} EUClaimCell;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    EUResourceNode nodes[EU_MAX_NODES];\n    int node_count;\n    EUClaimCell cells[EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS];\n    int cell_count;\n    int stockpile[EU_FACTION_COUNT]; /* gathered and banked, per faction */\n    int gathered[EU_FACTION_COUNT];  /* lifetime total, for a HUD/test to read */\n} EUWorld;\n\ntypedef struct {\n    int archetype;   /* EU_ARCH_* */\n    int faction;     /* EU_FACTION_* */\n    int species;     /* EU_SPECIES_* -- the inheritance switch */\n    int orders;      /* accepted order bits */\n    int role;        /* AIRole this archetype's brain runs (story_ai.h values) */\n    int kit;         /* default AIKit; an authored kit always wins */\n    int health;\n    /* The inherited baseline, permille. Humans get the human row, beasts the beast row. */\n    int courage, aggression, loyalty, greed, curiosity;\n    /* Live order state, owned by the host (story_ai.c). */\n    int order;       /* EU_ORDER_* currently executing, NONE when falling back to the brain */\n    int target_node, target_cell;\n    int carrying;    /* units gathered, not yet banked separately from the faction stockpile */\n    float explore_x, explore_z;\n    int exploring;   /* 0 = needs a new explore point */\n} EUUnit;\n\n/* What the unit can currently perceive. Kept as a plain struct so the host decides how it is filled and\n   so the decision is testable without a server. */\ntypedef struct {\n    int enemy_visible;\n    float enemy_dist;\n    float leader_dist;\n    int leader_alive;\n    int idle_ms;      /* how long the current mode has been running */\n    int at_home;      /* within a couple of steps of the spawn point */\n} EUView;\n\nstatic inline const char *eu_archetype_name(int arch) {\n    switch (arch) {\n        case EU_ARCH_CITIZEN: return \"citizen\";\n        case EU_ARCH_ZOMBIE: return \"zombie\";\n        case EU_ARCH_SOLDIER: return \"soldier\";\n        case EU_ARCH_ALLY: return \"ally\";\n        case EU_ARCH_GUARD: return \"guard\";\n        case EU_ARCH_WORKER: return \"worker\";\n        default: return \"none\";\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline const char *eu_order_name(int order) {\n    switch (order) {\n        case EU_ORDER_FOLLOW: return \"follow\";\n        case EU_ORDER_EXPLORE: return \"explore\";\n        case EU_ORDER_ENGAGE: return \"engage\";\n        case EU_ORDER_GATHER: return \"gather\";\n        case EU_ORDER_CLAIM: return \"claim\";\n        case EU_ORDER_GUARD: return \"guard\";\n        default: return \"none\";\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_order_bit_for_index(int index) {\n    switch (index) {\n        case EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW: return EU_ORDER_FOLLOW;\n        case EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE: return EU_ORDER_EXPLORE;\n        case EU_ORDER_IDX_ENGAGE: return EU_ORDER_ENGAGE;\n        case EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER: return EU_ORDER_GATHER;\n        case EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM: return EU_ORDER_CLAIM;\n        case EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD: return EU_ORDER_GUARD;\n        default: return EU_ORDER_NONE;\n    }\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_order_index_for_bit(int order) {\n    switch (order) {\n        case EU_ORDER_FOLLOW: return EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW;\n        case EU_ORDER_EXPLORE: return EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE;\n        case EU_ORDER_ENGAGE: return EU_ORDER_IDX_ENGAGE;\n        case EU_ORDER_GATHER: return EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER;\n        case EU_ORDER_CLAIM: return EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM;\n        case EU_ORDER_GUARD: return EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD;\n        default: return -1;\n    }\n}\n\n/* eu_unit_init -- an archetype's defaults, then the author's overrides, then the inheritance row.\n *   kit:     > 0 = the author's skin, 0 = the archetype's default (AUTO stays AUTO for the zombie,\n *            whose clip set is chosen by the witness role, not by AIKit).\n *   faction: >= 0 = the author's faction, < 0 = the archetype's default.\n *   orders:  >= 0 = the author's mask (0 is legal: \"does what its brain does, takes no orders\"),\n *            < 0 = the archetype's default mask.\n * A mask bit with a zero priority is dropped, because \"this unit accepts an order it has no opinion\n * about\" is a level-authoring mistake, not a behaviour: it would silently outrank nothing. */\nstatic inline void eu_unit_init(EUUnit *u, int archetype, int kit, int faction, int orders) {\n    if (!u) return;\n    int arch = eu_clamp(0, EU_ARCH_COUNT, archetype);\n    u->archetype = arch;\n    u->species = g_empire_rules.archetype_species(arch);\n    u->role = g_empire_rules.archetype_role(arch);\n    u->kit = kit > 0 ? kit : g_empire_rules.archetype_kit(arch);\n    u->health = g_empire_rules.archetype_health(arch);\n    u->faction = faction >= 0 ? eu_clamp(0, EU_FACTION_COUNT - 1, faction)\n                              : g_empire_rules.archetype_faction(arch);\n    int mask = orders >= 0 ? (orders & EU_ORDER_ALL) : g_empire_rules.archetype_orders(arch);\n    if (arch == EU_ARCH_NONE) mask = orders >= 0 ? (orders & EU_ORDER_ALL) : 0;\n    u->orders = 0;\n    for (int i = 0; i <= EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD; i++) {\n        int bit = eu_order_bit_for_index(i);\n        if ((mask & bit) && g_empire_rules.order_priority(arch, i) > 0) u->orders |= bit;\n    }\n\n    /* The generic stuff every human inherits -- and what a non-human inherits instead. */\n    if (u->species == EU_SPECIES_HUMAN) {\n        u->courage = g_empire_rules.human_courage();\n        u->aggression = g_empire_rules.human_aggression();\n        u->loyalty = g_empire_rules.human_loyalty();\n        u->greed = g_empire_rules.human_greed();\n        u->curiosity = g_empire_rules.human_curiosity();\n    } else if (u->species == EU_SPECIES_BEAST) {\n        u->courage = g_empire_rules.beast_courage();\n        u->aggression = g_empire_rules.beast_aggression();\n        u->loyalty = g_empire_rules.beast_loyalty();\n        u->greed = g_empire_rules.beast_greed();\n        u->curiosity = g_empire_rules.beast_curiosity();\n    } else {\n        u->courage = u->aggression = u->loyalty = u->greed = u->curiosity = 0;\n    }\n\n    u->order = EU_ORDER_NONE;\n    u->target_node = -1;\n    u->target_cell = -1;\n    u->carrying = 0;\n    u->explore_x = u->explore_z = 0.0f;\n    u->exploring = 0;\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_orders_has(const EUUnit *u, int order) {\n    return u && (u->orders & order) != 0;\n}\n\n/* Priority 0 for an order this unit does not accept, so callers never need a second mask test. */\nstatic inline int eu_unit_priority(const EUUnit *u, int order) {\n    if (!u || !eu_orders_has(u, order)) return 0;\n    int idx = eu_order_index_for_bit(order);\n    if (idx < 0) return 0;\n    return g_empire_rules.order_priority(u->archetype, idx);\n}\n\nstatic inline void eu_world_clear(EUWorld *w) {\n    if (!w) return;\n    for (int i = 0; i < EU_MAX_NODES; i++) {\n        w->nodes[i].x = w->nodes[i].z = 0.0f;\n        w->nodes[i].amount = w->nodes[i].capacity = 0;\n    }\n    for (int i = 0; i < EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS; i++) {\n        w->cells[i].x = w->cells[i].z = 0.0f;\n        w->cells[i].radius = 0;\n        w->cells[i].owner = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;\n        w->cells[i].claimant = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;\n        w->cells[i].claim_ms = 0;\n    }\n    w->node_count = 0;\n    w->cell_count = 0;\n    for (int f = 0; f < EU_FACTION_COUNT; f++) w->stockpile[f] = w->gathered[f] = 0;\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_world_add_node(EUWorld *w, float x, float z, int amount) {\n    if (!w || w->node_count >= EU_MAX_NODES || amount <= 0) return -1;\n    int cap = g_empire_rules.node_capacity();\n    EUResourceNode *n = &w->nodes[w->node_count];\n    n->x = x;\n    n->z = z;\n    n->amount = amount > cap ? cap : amount;\n    n->capacity = n->amount;\n    return w->node_count++;\n}\n\nstatic inline int eu_world_add_claim_cell(EUWorld *w, float x, float z) {\n    if (!w || w->cell_count >= EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS) return -1;\n    EUClaimCell *c = &w->cells[w->cell_count];\n    c->x = x;\n    c->z = z;\n    c->radius = g_empire_rules.claim_radius();\n    c->owner = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;\n    c->claimant = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;\n    c->claim_ms = 0;\n    return w->cell_count++;\n}\n\nstatic inline float eu_dist2(float ax, float az, float bx, float bz) {\n    float dx = ax - bx, dz = az - bz;\n    return dx * dx + dz * dz;\n}\n\n/* Nearest node that still has something in it, or -1. */\nstatic inline int eu_nearest_node(const EUWorld *w, float x, float z) {\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    int best = -1;\n    float best_d = 0.0f;\n    for (int i = 0; i < w->node_count; i++) {\n        if (w->nodes[i].amount <= 0) continue;\n        float d = eu_dist2(x, z, w->nodes[i].x, w->nodes[i].z);\n        if (best < 0 || d < best_d) { best = i; best_d = d; }\n    }\n    return best;\n}\n\n/* Nearest cell this faction does not already own, or -1. */\nstatic inline int eu_nearest_free_cell(const EUWorld *w, int faction, float x, float z) {\n    if (!w) return -1;\n    int best = -1;\n    float best_d = 0.0f;\n    for (int i = 0; i < w->cell_count; i++) {\n        if (w->cells[i].owner == faction) continue;\n        float d = eu_dist2(x, z, w->cells[i].x, w->cells[i].z);\n        if (best < 0 || d < best_d) { best = i; best_d = d; }\n    }\n    return best;\n}\n\n/* Gather one unit from a node into the unit's hands and the faction's stockpile. Returns 1 when a unit\n   was actually gathered, 0 when the node is empty/spent/out of range of the caller's own choice. */\nstatic inline int eu_world_gather(EUWorld *w, EUUnit *u, int node_index) {\n    if (!w || !u || node_index < 0 || node_index >= w->node_count) return 0;\n    EUResourceNode *n = &w->nodes[node_index];\n    if (n->amount <= 0) return 0;\n    n->amount--;\n    u->carrying++;\n    w->stockpile[u->faction]++;\n    w->gathered[u->faction]++;\n    return 1;\n}\n\n/* Stand on a cell for eu_claim_ticks() and it becomes yours. Another faction's progress is reset the\n   moment it starts its own attempt, so a contested cell is a race, not a shared bar. Returns 1 on the\n   tick the cell changes hands. */\nstatic inline int eu_world_claim_tick(EUWorld *w, EUUnit *u, int cell_index, int dt_ms) {\n    if (!w || !u || cell_index < 0 || cell_index >= w->cell_count) return 0;\n    EUClaimCell *c = &w->cells[cell_index];\n    if (c->owner == u->faction) { return 0; }\n    if (c->claimant != u->faction) {\n        c->claimant = u->faction;\n        c->claim_ms = 0;\n    }\n    int need = g_empire_rules.claim_ticks();\n    c->claim_ms += dt_ms > 0 ? dt_ms : 0;\n    if (c->claim_ms >= need) {\n        c->owner = u->faction;\n        c->claimant = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;\n        c->claim_ms = 0;\n        return 1;\n    }\n    return 0;\n}\n\n/* eu_choose_order -- the decision, and the whole programmable surface.\n *\n * ENGAGE is checked first and is not a candidate in the score race: if a unit accepts ENGAGE and can see\n * an enemy, that is what it does. Everything else is \"the highest-priority order whose own trigger is\n * true right now\", with GUARD as the standing fallback (it needs no trigger -- holding ground is always\n * possible), and NONE when nothing applies, which means \"fall back to the role's own brain\" rather than\n * \"stand still\". That distinction is what lets an authored soldier keep its GUARD post while a citizen\n * wanders off to gather.\n */\nstatic inline int eu_choose_order(const EUUnit *u, const EUWorld *w, const EUView *v) {\n    if (!u || !v) return EU_ORDER_NONE;\n    if (eu_orders_has(u, EU_ORDER_ENGAGE) && v->enemy_visible) return EU_ORDER_ENGAGE;\n    if (!w && (eu_orders_has(u, EU_ORDER_GATHER) || eu_orders_has(u, EU_ORDER_CLAIM)))\n        return EU_ORDER_NONE;\n\n    int best_order = EU_ORDER_NONE;\n    int best_score = 0;\n    for (int idx = 0; idx <= EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD; idx++) {\n        int bit = eu_order_bit_for_index(idx);\n        int score = eu_unit_priority(u, bit);\n        if (score <= 0) continue;\n        int triggered = 0;\n        switch (idx) {\n            case EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW:\n                triggered = v->leader_alive && v->leader_dist > (float)g_empire_rules.follow_distance();\n                break;\n            case EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE:\n                triggered = v->idle_ms >= 2000;\n                break;\n            case EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER:\n                triggered = w && eu_nearest_node(w, 0.0f, 0.0f) >= 0;\n                break;\n            case EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM:\n                triggered = w && eu_nearest_free_cell(w, u->faction, 0.0f, 0.0f) >= 0;\n                break;\n            case EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD:\n                triggered = 1;\n                break;\n            default:\n                break;\n        }\n        if (!triggered) continue;\n        if (score > best_score) { best_score = score; best_order = bit; }\n    }\n    return best_order;\n}\n\n#endif /* SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_UNITS_H */\n"
}

=== original prn (HEAD) ===
;; stdlib/shankpit/empire_rules.prn -- the EMPIRE layer's economy, and the shape of the sphere.
;;
;; Founder 2026-10-31: "we need phone app affordances in shankpit to bring in the mp and to clone your
;; troops in PARENA first mods based it should show the minimap of the nearby area and allow you to
;; spawn in troops near you or near buildings you have enough influence over ... in empire mode the map
;; itself should be a big sphere and it should be procedurally generated ... a sphere of procedural
;; cities in districts or neighborhoods".
;;
;; So this mod is TWO things, both decision logic rather than rendering:
;;
;;   the economy   INFLUENCE is the only currency. You do not buy troops with money and you do not
;;                 build a base: influence trickles in from districts you hold and from buildings you
;;                 control nearby, and every troop you place spends it. Cloning costs MORE than a
;;                 fresh recruit (a clone keeps its rank, a recruit does not), which is the tradeoff
;;                 the founder asked for: spam cheap bodies, or invest in the ones that survive.
;;
;;   the sphere    a real geometry, not a metaphor: rings of districts on a sphere, each ring with its
;;                 own district count, so "the nearby area" is always a handful of districts and the
;;                 whole world is thousands. Both sides derive the same numbers from the same seed.
;;
;; EMPIRE's own NORTHSTAR (../EMPIRE/NORTHSTAR.md) puts TRAPX doctrine underneath this: indirect
;; control, no avatar commanding units, pressure instead of orders. Influence IS that doctrine's
;; pressure made spendable -- you do not order a squad, you buy the conditions for one to exist.
;;
;; I32 fixed point throughout, total functions, same conventions as the other shankpit mods.
(module shankpit/empire-rules)
(export empire-influence-start empire-influence-max empire-influence-per-second
        empire-troop-kind-count empire-troop-cost empire-clone-cost-milli
        empire-squad-cap empire-spawn-radius-milli empire-can-spawn
        empire-clone-can empire-influence-from-district
        empire-district-state empire-district-threshold-milli
        empire-sphere-rings empire-districts-in-ring empire-sphere-radius-milli
        empire-district-radius-milli empire-nearby-districts)

;; ---- influence --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
(defn empire-influence-start [] : I32 100)
(defn empire-influence-max [] : I32 400)

;; Trickle per SECOND (the host applies it against real tick delta). Slow on purpose: a squad is a
;; decision, not a stream. 2/s at the start means one rifleman every 12 s, or one clone every ~18 s.
=== original gen script ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gen_empire_rules.sh -- regenerate packages/simulation/empire_rules.c from PARENA.
#
# The EMPIRE influence economy (what a troop costs, what a clone costs, when you may place one) and
# the sphere's district geometry are decision logic, not rendering:
#   PARENA/stdlib/shankpit/empire_rules.prn
# Usage: scripts/gen_empire_rules.sh   (needs a sibling ../PARENA checkout, or PARENA_DIR)
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
parena_dir="${PARENA_DIR:-$root/../PARENA}"
if [ -x "$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap" ]; then
    parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
elif [ -x "$parena_dir/parena" ]; then
    parena_bin="$parena_dir/parena"
else
    (cd "$parena_dir" && make .parena-bootstrap >/dev/null)
    parena_bin="$parena_dir/.parena-bootstrap"
fi
"$parena_bin" build "$parena_dir/stdlib/shankpit/empire_rules.prn" \
    -o "$root/packages/simulation/empire_rules.c"
echo "regenerated packages/simulation/empire_rules.c"

/* S461-01: real health-gated flee trigger. Threshold matches bot_client's own existing
   w_retreat convention ("health-aware retreat multiplier (activated when hp < 30%)",
   packages/common/protocol.h) rather than inventing a new number. Courage gate keeps the
   tank-identity roles (Brute 1.0, Bombardier 0.9, Hound 0.8) fighting through low health --
   only the roles whose own combat comments already lean on "keeps distance"/"backs away"
   (Trooper 0.55, Storm Caller 0.35, Guard's 0.5 default) actually flee. */
#define STORY_AI_FLEE_HEALTH_PCT 30
#define STORY_AI_FLEE_COURAGE_MAX 0.7f

/* S470 -- real, tuned-by-eye ambient-greet constants (founder real-time: "wave to the player when
   the player gets close and then dance before resuming patrol"). Radius comfortably inside
   ai_gather_perception's own vision_range values so a wandering bot notices the player at a
   normal walking approach, not at point-blank range. Cooldown prevents an immediate re-trigger
   the instant the greet ends while the player is still standing right there -- the bot resumes a
   real patrol leg first. Hold durations are picked against the real clip lengths exported for
   this pass (George/Stan/Mike/Leela's own Hello gesture runs ~1.5-1.9s at 30 ticks/sec, the
   mannequin's real Dance_Loop ~1.0s) so each phase plays at least one full loop, not a clipped
   fraction. */
#define STORY_AI_GREET_RADIUS 24.0f
#define STORY_AI_GREET_COOLDOWN_MS 9000U

// CharacterInspector -- STORY_SYSTEM_NORTHSTAR.md Phase 2's own "character" kind, founder
// real-time: "continue filling in the gaps in our level editor scriptable env characters etc."
// Position edited numerically, same real, deliberate v0 scope ObjectInspector/NavNodeInspector
// already established (not 3D-dragged).
function CharacterInspector({
  character,
  onChange,
  onDelete,
}: {
  character: ShankpitCharacter
  onChange: (c: ShankpitCharacter) => void
  onDelete: () => void
}) {
  const num = (v: string) => (v === '' || v === '-' ? 0 : Number(v))
  return (
    <div className="platform-inspector">
      <h4>Character #{character.id}</h4>
      <label>
        Role{' '}
        <select value={character.role} onChange={(e) => onChange({ ...character, role: Number(e.target.value) })}>
          {AI_ROLE_OPTIONS.map((opt) => (
            <option key={opt.value} value={opt.value}>
              {opt.label}
            </option>
          ))}
        </select>
      </label>
      <label>
        Kit (visual model){' '}
        <select value={character.kit} onChange={(e) => onChange({ ...character, kit: Number(e.target.value) })}>
          {KIT_OPTIONS.map((opt) => (
            <option key={opt.value} value={opt.value}>
              {opt.label}
            </option>
          ))}
        </select>
      </label>
      <label>
        X <input type="number" step={0.5} value={character.x} onChange={(e) => onChange({ ...character, x: num(e.target.value) })} />
      </label>
      <label>
        Y <input type="number" step={0.5} value={character.y} onChange={(e) => onChange({ ...character, y: num(e.target.value) })} />
      </label>
      <label>
        Z <input type="number" step={0.5} value={character.z} onChange={(e) => onChange({ ...character, z: num(e.target.value) })} />
      </label>
      <button className="danger" type="button" onClick={onDelete}>
        Delete character
      </button>
    </div>
  )

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/empire_rules_test.c
  content: |
      /* empire_rules_test.c -- `make test-empire-rules`. Asserts the influence economy and the sphere's
       * district geometry through the real generated PARENA table: what a troop costs, why a clone costs
       * more, when placement is refused, how a district flips and pays, and that the rings actually close
       * into a sphere-sized world. */
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include "empire_rules_host.h"
      
      static int fails = 0;
      #define CHECK(cond, ...) do { \
          if (!(cond)) { printf("FAIL %s:%d  ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); fails++; } \
      } while (0)
      
      int main(void) {
          /* ---- influence ---- */
          CHECK(empire_influence_start() > 0, "start influence %d", empire_influence_start());
          CHECK(empire_influence_max() > empire_influence_start(), "cap %d must exceed start %d",
                empire_influence_max(), empire_influence_start());
          CHECK(empire_influence_per_second() > 0, "no income");
      
          /* ---- troop costs, and the clone premium ---- */
          CHECK(empire_troop_kind_count() == 4, "kinds %d", empire_troop_kind_count());
          for (int k = 0; k < empire_troop_kind_count(); k++) {
              int cost = empire_troop_cost(k);
              CHECK(cost > 0, "kind %d costs %d", k, cost);
              CHECK(empire_clone_cost(k) > cost, "clone of %d (%d) must cost more than a recruit (%d)",
                    k, empire_clone_cost(k), cost);
          }
          /* the mini fly is the expensive one: it is the hardest body to get anywhere */
          CHECK(empire_troop_cost(3) > empire_troop_cost(0), "mini fly %d should outprice rifleman %d",
                empire_troop_cost(3), empire_troop_cost(0));
      
          /* ---- the gate the phone's greyed-out row reads ---- */
          CHECK(empire_can_spawn(0, 0, 0) == 0, "broke player may spawn");
          CHECK(empire_can_spawn(empire_troop_cost(0), 0, 0) == 1, "exact change refused");
          CHECK(empire_can_spawn(empire_troop_cost(0) - 1, 0, 0) == 0, "one short allowed");
          CHECK(empire_can_spawn(10000, 99, 0) == 0, "unknown kind allowed");
          CHECK(empire_can_spawn(10000, 0, empire_squad_cap()) == 0, "cap ignored");
      
          CHECK(empire_clone_can(10000, 0, 0, 0) == 0, "cloned a body that does not exist");
          CHECK(empire_clone_can(empire_clone_cost(0), 0, 0, 1) == 1, "a veteran clone was refused");
          CHECK(empire_clone_can(empire_clone_cost(0) - 1, 0, 0, 1) == 0, "clone discounted");
          CHECK(empire_clone_can(10000, 0, empire_squad_cap(), 1) == 0, "clone ignored the cap");
      
          /* ---- districts: TRAPX's three-way alignment, with income attached ---- */
          int t = empire_district_threshold_milli();
          CHECK(empire_district_state(t, 0) == 1, "held district not yours");
          CHECK(empire_district_state(0, t) == 2, "rival pressure not theirs");
          CHECK(empire_district_state(t - 1, t - 1) == 0, "contested district claimed by nobody");
          CHECK(empire_influence_from_district(1, 30) == 30, "yours should pay in full");
          CHECK(empire_influence_from_district(2, 30) == 0, "a rival's district paid you");
          CHECK(empire_influence_from_district(0, 30) > 0 &&
                empire_influence_from_district(0, 30) < 30, "neutral should pay a third, got %d",
                empire_influence_from_district(0, 30));
      
          /* ---- the sphere ---- */
          {
              int rings = empire_sphere_rings();
              int total = 0, middle = 0, pole = 0;
              CHECK(rings >= 3, "rings %d", rings);
              for (int r = 0; r < rings; r++) {
                  int n = empire_districts_in_ring(r);
                  CHECK(n > 0, "ring %d empty", r);
                  total += n;
                  if (r == 0) pole = n;
                  if (r == rings / 2) middle = n;
              }
              CHECK(empire_districts_in_ring(rings) == 0, "a ring past the last one exists");
              CHECK(empire_districts_in_ring(-1) == 0, "a negative ring exists");
              CHECK(total == 72, "districts total %d (want 72, the number this stack keeps coming back to)", total);
              CHECK(middle > pole, "the equator ring (%d) must hold more than the pole cap (%d) or the map pinches",
                    middle, pole);
              CHECK(empire_sphere_radius_milli() > empire_district_radius_milli(), "sphere smaller than a district");
              CHECK(empire_nearby_districts() < total, "the whole world cannot be 'nearby'");
              CHECK(empire_spawn_radius_milli() > 0 && empire_spawn_radius_milli() < empire_district_radius_milli() * 2,
                    "spawn radius %d is not a local placement", empire_spawn_radius_milli());
          }
      
          if (fails) { printf("empire_rules: %d FAILED\n", fails); return 1; }
          printf("empire_rules: all checks passed\n");
          return 0;
      }
