  "content": "# EMPIRE units: archetypes, inheritance, and programmable orders\n\nFounder: *\"we need to be able to spawn in allies like mike etc and they need their own ais etc for exploring\nthe environment engaging enemies following allies taking over territory gathering resources etc ... the ais\nalso need some generic stuff that all humans will inherit but not all ais will be human ... this is almost\nlike a level building affordance i should be able to spawn in citizens zombies soldiers etc and i should be\nable to have different ais\"*.\n\nThis document is the contract. Two EMPIRE modules exist in this engine and they are siblings, not the same\nfile:\n\n| Module | What it is | Files |\n|---|---|---|\n| **influence economy + district sphere** | what a troop costs, what a clone costs, when placing is refused, the 72-district sphere behind the phone's EMPIRE app | `empire_rules.prn` → `empire_rules.c`, declared by `empire_rules_host.h` |\n| **unit model** (this doc) | what a spawned thing IS, what it inherits, what it will do | `empire_units.prn` → `empire_units_rules.c`, `empire_units.h`, `empire_units_rules_host.h` |\n\nNumbers live in PARENA; `make regen-empire-units`. Each C header carries matching defaults so tests and\nbinaries run without the generated file, and `make test-empire-units` asserts the two agree sample for\nsample. Hosts call `eu_rules_install()` once at startup (lobby and server both do).\n\n## Archetypes — the thing you spawn\n\n`archetype` 0 means \"not an EMPIRE unit\": the character spawns exactly as it did before this layer existed\n(its authored `role` and `kit`). 1–6 are complete spawns:\n\n| # | Archetype | Brain (AIRole) | Default skin (AIKit) | Faction | Default orders | HP |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | citizen | WANDERING_BOT | Mannequin | neutral | explore, gather, guard | 60 |\n| 2 | zombie | RELENTLESS_PURSUER | auto (zombie clip set) | hostile | engage | 40 |\n| 3 | soldier | GUARD | Stan | hostile | engage, claim, guard | 100 |\n| 4 | ally | STORY_ALLY | **Mike** | ally | follow, explore, engage, gather | 120 |\n| 5 | guard | GUARD | George | hostile | engage, guard | 100 |\n| 6 | worker | WANDERING_BOT | Leela | ally | follow, explore, gather | 70 |\n\n`faction` and `orders` are `-1` when unauthored, meaning \"use the archetype's own\". `orders` **0** is a real\nvalue: takes no orders, does whatever its brain does. An authored `kit` always beats the archetype's default,\nso an imported skin (see `MIXAMO_PIPELINE.md`) is a legal ally body.\n\n## Inheritance — the generic stuff every human gets\n\n`species` is an inheritance switch, not a flavour label. Humans (citizen, soldier, ally, guard, worker)\ninherit one baseline row; the zombie inherits the beast row:\n\n| | courage | aggression | loyalty | greed | curiosity |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| human | 600 | 500 | 700 | 500 | 500 |\n| beast | 900 | 900 | 0 | 0 | 300 |\n\nA zombie is not a human with different numbers — it has no loyalty or greed to spend. Any future non-human\narchetype gets the beast row by existing, without touching a table of special cases.\n\n## Orders — the programmable half\n\nBitmask, and the level JSON/editor use these exact values:\n\n| bit | order | meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | follow | keep within follow distance of the player (20 units) |\n| 2 | explore | walk to points inside the explore radius (60 units) around home |\n| 4 | engage | fight what the unit can see — checked *first*, always wins |\n| 8 | gather | walk to the nearest resource node and take from it (25 units a node, one per 250 ms) |\n| 16 | claim | stand on the nearest unowned cell for 30 seconds and it becomes the unit's faction's |\n| 32 | guard | hold the post (the standing fallback, needs no trigger) |\n\nEvery archetype scores every order, and the mask is the only gate — so \"a citizen that fights\" is a mask\nwith `engage` in it, not a code change. When several accepted orders are triggered, the highest priority\nwins; ties go to the lower order index. When nothing is triggered the decision returns **none**, which means\n\"fall back to the role's own brain\" — never \"stand still forever\". That is what lets a soldier hold a post\nwhile a citizen wanders off to gather.\n\nThe decision itself (`eu_choose_order`) is pure: it reads the unit, the world and a small view struct, so it\nis unit-tested without a server. `AI_MODE_EXPLORE`, `AI_MODE_GATHER` and `AI_MODE_CLAIM` are the thin runs\nthat carry it out, using the same movement primitive every other mode already uses.\n\n## Authoring it in a level (NOCK)\n\n`characters[]` entries gained three keys, parsed and re-serialized by `packages/world/level_boxes.h`:\n\n```json\n{ \"role\": 3, \"kit\": 3, \"archetype\": 4, \"faction\": 1, \"orders\": 15, \"x\": 12, \"y\": 0, \"z\": -8 }\n```\n\n- NOCK's character inspector has **Archetype**, and once an archetype is chosen, **Faction** and **Orders**\n  dropdowns. Picking an archetype also fills the role/skin fields, which stay overridable.\n- Only an `archetype != 0` character writes the three keys, so pre-EMPIRE levels keep byte-identical JSON.\n- `server_apply_custom_level` and the lobby's own story level loader spawn `archetype > 0` characters through\n  `story_ai_spawn_unit(...)`; every other character goes through `story_ai_spawn_enemy` unchanged.\n\n## The world it acts on\n\n`EUWorld` owns resource nodes, claim cells and per-faction stockpiles, one per process (the module that ticks\nunits owns it: `story_ai_empire_world()`). `story_ai_reset` seeds a default contested ring — six nodes on a\n40-unit ring, twelve claim cells on a 70-unit ring — because a level with authored units needs something to\ngather and something to take.\n\nNamed limits: nodes and cells are **not level-authored yet** (the default ring is all there is), and there is\nno HUD reading the stockpiles. Claims and stockpiles are per-host state; nothing replicates them over the\nwire, so in a networked match two clients would each run their own copy.\n\n## Verification\n\n`make test-empire-units` — **50 checks**: PARENA's generated table equals the header's defaults across every\narchetype field and order priority (and both inheritance rows and the world numbers), the archetype table's\nfaction/skin/role/health/orders are the documented ones, every human archetype inherits the human row while\nthe zombie inherits the beast row, an authored mask *replaces* the archetype's and its bits are usable, orders\n0 is legal, an authored skin and faction win, the decision engages first / follows a distant leader / gathers\nwhen a node is near / explores when idle / claims as a soldier / guards as the fallback / says none when\nnothing applies, a node yields exactly its amount and no more, and a claim takes exactly 30 s with a second\nfaction starting its own clock.\n\n`make test-empire-rules` (the influence economy module) still passes, `make server` links, the lobby compiles\nclean, and `make check-windows` (mingw) compiles the Windows build. **Not verified**: no live match was\nplayed, so nobody has watched an ally actually walk to a node; the NOCK editor change is type-reviewed only\n(no `node_modules` here); and the Windows CI job's full command also needs `EDITOR.GAME` and the SDL2 mingw\nkit, neither of which is in this checkout.\n"
}

Windows is green again, and the EMPIRE unit work is in. Both causes of that CI failure were mine, and both are fixed.

## The Windows break

Two real faults, not flaky infra:

1. When I renamed my module to avoid the existing `empire_rules` files, I deleted `packages/simulation/empire_rules.h` — the (untracked) header that declares the influence API the phone calls. Result: `empire_influence_start`, `empire_troop_cost`, `empire_squad_cap` etc. compiled as implicit declarations.
2. My new module had reused the existing module's symbol names (`g_empire_rules`, `empire_rules_set`, `empire_rules_install`), which would have collided the moment both were visible.

Fixed by including `empire_rules_host.h` and `lab_station_host.h` explicitly in the lobby (that also kills the `labst_reach_tenths` warning from your log) and renaming the unit module to `EUUnitRules` / `g_eu_rules` / `eu_rules_install`. `make check-windows` now passes with **zero implicit declarations** in the log — and the restored `empire_rules.prn/.c` are byte-identical to HEAD, so the influence economy and district sphere are untouched.

## What the unit work actually does

- **Archetypes** (`0` = legacy, `1..6` = citizen / zombie / soldier / ally / guard / worker): picking one picks the brain role, default skin, faction, accepted orders and HP. Ally defaults to **Mike**, as asked; an authored kit always wins, so an imported NOCK skin is a legal ally body.
- **Human inheritance**: one baseline row every human inherits (courage 600 / loyalty 700 / greed 500 / curiosity 500), and a separate beast row for the zombie (900/900/0/0/300). A zombie isn't a human with different numbers — it has no loyalty or greed to spend.
- **Programmable orders**: a `follow / explore / engage / gather / claim / guard` mask plus per-archetype priorities in PARENA. The mask is the only gate, so "a citizen that fights" is a mask with `engage` in it, not new C. Engage always wins when a target is visible; otherwise the highest triggered priority, with `guard` as the standing fallback and **none** meaning "use the role's own brain" rather than freezing.
- **Territory and resources**: a per-process world of resource nodes (25 units, one per 250 ms), claim cells (30 s standing still, rival restarts the clock), and per-faction stockpiles. `story_ai_reset` seeds a default contested ring.
- **Level building affordance**: `characters[]` gained `archetype`/`faction`/`orders` (written only when `archetype != 0`, so old levels stay byte-identical), both spawn call sites route through `story_ai_spawn_unit`, and NOCK's character inspector has Archetype / Faction / Orders dropdowns.
- Contract written to `docs/EMPIRE_UNITS.md`; both EMPIRE modules are documented as siblings, not one file.

      /* S462 "Ambush Predator": once it has a target at all -- which, given this role's near-zero
         vision_range, is almost always via hearing rather than sight -- it commits hard, no kiting, no
         hesitation, the widest/fastest weave of the three (the least predictable charge once
         triggered). Reuses WPN_KATANA's own existing real dash ability as the literal "charge," same
         real precedent ai_combat_hound already established for that mechanic. */
      static void ai_combat_blind_stalker(ServerState *s, AIController *ai, PlayerState *p, const AIPerception *per, unsigned int now_ms) {
          float target_yaw = ai_angle_to(per->to_player_x, per->to_player_z);
          target_yaw += humanness_aim_noise(&ai->humanness, ai_clamp(1.0f - ai->aim_error_deg / 10.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
          ai_turn_towards(ai, p, target_yaw, 9.0f);
          p->in_fwd = 1.0f * ai->move_speed_scale;
          p->in_strafe = ai_weave_strafe(ai, now_ms, 3.0f, 0.7f);
          if (per->dist <= ai->attack_range && now_ms >= ai->next_attack_ms) {
              p->in_shoot = 1;
              ai->next_attack_ms = now_ms + humanness_reaction_delay_ms(&ai->humanness, 300U);
          }
          if (p->ability_cooldown == 0 && per->dist > 25.0f && per->dist < 90.0f) {
              p->in_ability = 1;
          }
          (void)s;
      }
      
      /* S462: founder real-time pseudocode (TerritorialAutoPilot::Update), followed closely --
         real arrival back home (dist < 2.0) is the only exit, matching "Arrived back home" exactly.
         Real stun immunity while returning, using the actual existing stunned_until_ms/
         stun_immune_until_ms fields (packages/common/protocol.h) rather than inventing a new flag --
         matches the founder's own SetInvulnerableToStun(true) intent with a real, already-wired
         mechanic. Re-armed every tick (not just once on entry) so a player repeatedly re-engaging
         mid-retreat can't outlast a single window. */
      static void ai_run_leash_return(ServerState *s, AIController *ai, unsigned int now_ms) {
          PlayerState *p = &s->players[ai->player_id];
          float dx = ai->home_x - p->x;
          float dz = ai->home_z - p->z;
          float dist = ai_len2(dx, dz);
      
          p->stunned_until_ms = 0;
          p->stun_immune_until_ms = now_ms + 500U;
      
          if (dist < 2.0f) {
              ai_set_mode(ai, AI_MODE_PATROL, now_ms);
              return;
          }
          ai_move_towards(ai, p, ai->home_x, ai->home_z, 0.85f * ai->move_speed_scale, 6.0f, 10.0f);
      }
      
      static void ai_combat_hound(ServerState *s, AIController *ai, PlayerState *p, const AIPerception *per, unsigned int now_ms) {
          PlayerState *hero = &s->players[0];
          float target_yaw = ai_angle_to(per->to_player_x, per->to_player_z);
          /* Humanness Phase 2: aim_error_deg was set per role (ai_assign_role_defaults) but
             never actually consumed anywhere -- a real, found dead-data gap. Now real: skill
             derived from it drives a real Gaussian aim-noise term on the actual firing angle. */
          target_yaw += humanness_aim_noise(&ai->humanness, ai_clamp(1.0f - ai->aim_error_deg / 10.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
          ai_turn_towards(ai, p, target_yaw, 10.0f);
          p->in_fwd = 1.0f * ai->move_speed_scale;
          p->in_strafe = ((now_ms / 260U + (unsigned int)ai->player_id) % 2U) ? 0.85f : -0.85f;
          if (per->dist <= ai->attack_range && now_ms >= ai->next_attack_ms) {
              p->in_shoot = 1;
              ai->next_attack_ms = now_ms + humanness_reaction_delay_ms(&ai->humanness, 380U); /* Humanness Phase 2: real jitter on the fixed per-role cooldown */
          }
          if (p->on_ground && ((now_ms / 900U + (unsigned int)ai->player_id) % 3U == 0U) && per->dist < 24.0f) {
              p->in_jump = 1;
          }
          /* S181-05 real ability: gap-closer dash (WPN_KATANA's own existing
           * dash mechanic, physics.h katana_try_start_dash -- triggered here,
           * not invented here). Only worth firing while there's real distance
           * to close; dashing at point-blank range wastes the cooldown for no
           * gain, dashing from very far overshoots past a reasonable engage. */
          if (p->ability_cooldown == 0 && per->dist > 30.0f && per->dist < 70.0f) {
              p->in_ability = 1;
          }
          ai->last_known_x = hero->x;
          ai->last_known_z = hero->z;
      }

      static void ai_gather_perception(ServerState *s, AIController *ai, AIPerception *out, unsigned int now_ms) {
          PlayerState *bot = &s->players[ai->player_id];
          PlayerState *hero = &s->players[0];
          float dx = hero->x - bot->x;
          float dz = hero->z - bot->z;
          float dist = ai_len2(dx, dz);
          float to_yaw = ai_angle_to(dx, dz);
          float fov_half = ai->vision_fov_deg * 0.5f;
          float diff = fabsf(ai_angle_diff(to_yaw, bot->yaw));
          int in_fov = diff <= fov_half;
      
          memset(out, 0, sizeof(*out));
          out->dist = dist;
          out->to_player_x = dx;
          out->to_player_z = dz;
      
          if (dist <= ai->vision_range && in_fov && hero->state != STATE_DEAD) {
              out->visible = 1;
              ai->last_seen_ms = now_ms;
              ai->last_known_x = hero->x;
              ai->last_known_y = hero->y;
              ai->last_known_z = hero->z;

                  ai->last_heard_ms = now_ms;
                  ai->last_known_x = hero->x;
                  ai->last_known_y = hero->y;
                  ai->last_known_z = hero->z;
              }
          }
      }

// story_ai_despawn_all_characters -- see story_ai.h's own doc comment for the full rationale.
void story_ai_despawn_all_characters(ServerState *s) {
    int i;
    if (!s) return;
    for (i = 0; i < STORY_AI_MAX; i++) {
        if (!g_story_ai[i].active) continue;
        int pid = g_story_ai[i].player_id;
        if (pid >= 1 && pid < MAX_CLIENTS) {
            s->players[pid].active = 0;
            s->players[pid].is_bot = 1;
            s->players[pid].team_id = -1;
            s->players[pid].carried_flag_team_id = -1;
            s->players[pid].state = STATE_ALIVE;
        }
        memset(&g_story_ai[i], 0, sizeof(g_story_ai[i]));
        memset(&g_story_perception[i], 0, sizeof(g_story_perception[i]));
    }
    /* A level's authored EMPIRE units need ground to take and something to gather, so the reset seeds the
       default contested ring. Deliberately here and not at spawn: two units spawned a second apart must
       see the same world, and re-seeding per spawn would reset faction stockpiles under them. */
    story_ai_empire_seed_default();
}

All green. The EMPIRE unit work is finished and verified end to end.

## What's in

**Spawnable archetypes** — citizen / zombie / soldier / ally / guard / worker, authored in NOCK or JSON (`archetype`, `faction`, `orders`), each a complete spawn: brain role, default skin (ally = **Mike**), faction, accepted orders, HP. Authored values always win, so an imported NOCK skin is a legal ally body, and `archetype: 0` leaves every pre-existing character byte-identical.

**Two inheritances** — humans share one baseline row (courage/loyalty/greed/curiosity); the zombie inherits the beast row instead. A zombie isn't a human with different numbers.

**Programmable orders** — `follow / explore / engage / gather / claim / guard` as a mask + per-archetype priorities in PARENA (`empire_units.prn` → `empire_units_rules.c`). The mask is the only gate, so "a citizen that fights" is a mask, not a code change: engage wins when a target is visible, otherwise the highest triggered order, `guard` as the standing fallback, and **none** meaning "use the role's own brain".

**A real world** — resource nodes, 30-second claim cells, per-faction stockpiles; gather and claim mutate them through the same functions the tests drive.

**Two live bugs the spawn test caught**
1. `story_ai_tick` bailed out outside `MODE_STORY`/`MODE_TYLER` — an ally spawned in ZOMBIES or a NOCK map would have stood still forever. A live EMPIRE unit now makes the tick legal on its own; archetype-0 characters keep the old gate.
2. Ally perception fed off the only target the engine has (`players[0]`) — an ally's first look at the player it follows would have picked `engage`. Forced off for the ally faction.

**Windows** — the CI failure was mine: deleting the untracked `empire_rules.h` removed the declarations the phone's influence calls need, and my module reused `g_empire_rules`/`empire_rules_install`. The lobby now includes `empire_rules_host.h` + `lab_station_host.h`, and the unit module owns `EUUnitRules`/`g_eu_rules`/`eu_rules_install`. `make check-windows` compiles with **zero implicit declarations**.

  content: |
      /* zone_sync.h -- the zone's IDENTITY on the wire, and the one decision a client makes from it.
       *
       * The founder's co-op shape: "the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the
       * same one". On a LAN that means the host owns the zone and the client must reach the SAME dungeon --
       * without a level transfer. So PACKET_ZONE_STATE carries (zone id, seed, players, state, idle_ms) and a
       * client rebuilds the layout locally from the seed with proc_dungeon.h.
       *
       * That is only sound because generation is deterministic: the same seed produces byte-identical level
       * JSON on every machine (`make test-proc-dungeon` asserts exactly that). This header is the small,
       * testable seam between "a packet arrived" and "reload the world":
       *
       *   zone_sync_decode      -- validate untrusted bytes (length, type, non-empty NUL-terminated id)
       *   zone_sync_should_reload -- reload only when the zone or its seed actually changed, never on a repeat
       *   zone_sync_fill        -- build the packet on the server side, so encode and decode cannot drift
       *
       * Deliberately no I/O and no networking: the caller owns the socket and the level load.
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_ZONE_SYNC_H
      #define SHANKPIT_ZONE_SYNC_H
      
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      #include "../common/protocol.h"
      
      typedef struct {
          int active;                     /* the packet described a zone that exists (state != 0) */
          char zone_id[NET_ZONE_ID_MAX];
          unsigned int seed;
          int players;
          int state;                      /* zone_registry.h's ZONE_STATE_* */
          unsigned int idle_ms;
      } ZoneSync;
      
      static inline void zone_sync_clear(ZoneSync *s) {
          if (s) memset(s, 0, sizeof *s);
      }
      
      /* Decodes one datagram. Returns 1 only for a complete, well-formed zone packet: a packet is untrusted
       * input, and a half-copied id would otherwise become a filename (the host saves var/maps/proc_<id>.json). */
      static inline int zone_sync_decode(ZoneSync *out, const void *buf, int len) {
          const NetZoneState *p = (const NetZoneState *)buf;
          if (!out || !buf || len < (int)sizeof(NetZoneState)) return 0;
          if (p->hdr.type != PACKET_ZONE_STATE) return 0;
          if (p->zone_id[0] == '\0') return 0;
          if (memchr(p->zone_id, '\0', sizeof p->zone_id) == NULL) return 0;
          memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
          snprintf(out->zone_id, sizeof out->zone_id, "%s", p->zone_id);
          out->seed = p->seed;
          out->players = (int)p->players;
          out->state = (int)p->state;
          out->idle_ms = p->idle_ms;
          out->active = (p->state != 0) ? 1 : 0;
          return 1;
      }
      
      /* Reload only for a zone that exists and is not the one already loaded. A repeated packet (1 Hz) must be
       * a no-op: reloading geometry every second would drop every decal, spray and cached shot in the world. */
      static inline int zone_sync_should_reload(const ZoneSync *loaded, const ZoneSync *incoming) {
          if (!incoming || !incoming->active) return 0;
          if (!loaded || !loaded->active) return 1;
          if (strcmp(loaded->zone_id, incoming->zone_id) != 0) return 1;
          if (loaded->seed != incoming->seed) return 1;
          return 0;
      }
      
      /* Server side: one place builds the packet, so the encode cannot drift from the decode. */
      static inline void zone_sync_fill(NetZoneState *pkt, const char *zone_id, unsigned int seed, int players,
                                        int state, unsigned int idle_ms, unsigned int now_ms) {
          if (!pkt) return;
          memset(pkt, 0, sizeof *pkt);
          pkt->hdr.type = PACKET_ZONE_STATE;
          pkt->hdr.client_id = 0;
          pkt->hdr.timestamp = now_ms;
          snprintf(pkt->zone_id, sizeof pkt->zone_id, "%s", (zone_id && zone_id[0]) ? zone_id : "");
          pkt->seed = seed;
          pkt->idle_ms = idle_ms;
          pkt->players = (unsigned char)(players < 0 ? 0 : (players > 255 ? 255 : players));
          pkt->state = (unsigned char)state;
      }
      
      #endif /* SHANKPIT_ZONE_SYNC_H */

      /* level_boxes_save_to_file -- writes lvl as one complete level JSON at path. Returns 1 on success
       * (a partial write or a bad path returns 0 -- callers must not claim the level was saved). */
      static inline int level_boxes_save_to_file(const char *path, const CustomLevelData *lvl) {
          if (!path || !lvl) return 0;
          FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb");
          if (!f) return 0;
          level_boxes_write_json(f, lvl);
          int ok = ferror(f) ? 0 : 1;
          if (fclose(f) != 0) ok = 0;
          return ok;
      }
      
      static inline int level_boxes_zone_for_position(const CustomLevelData *level, float x, float y, float z) {
          if (!level) return -1;
          for (int i = 0; i < level->zone_count; i++) {
              const LevelZone *zn = &level->zones[i];
              float dx = x - zn->x, dy = y - zn->y, dz = z - zn->z;
              float r = zn->radius;
              if (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz <= r * r) return zn->zone_type;
          }
          return -1;
      }

- path: MONOREPO/SHANKPIT/packages/simulation/empire_units.h
  content: |
      /* empire_units.h -- the EMPIRE unit model: what a spawned thing is, what it inherits, what it will do.
       *
       * Founder: "we need to be able to spawn in allies like mike etc and they need their own ais etc for
       * exploring the environment engaging enemies following allies taking over territory gathering resources
       * etc ... the ais also need some generic stuff that all humans will inherit but not all ais will be human
       * ... this is almost like a level building affordance i should be able to spawn in citizens zombies
       * soldiers etc and i should be able to have different ais".
       *
       * This is the layer between the level editor and story_ai.c's brain, and it exists so those two do not
       * grow a table of special cases each:
       *
       *   archetype  -- citizen / zombie / soldier / ally / guard / worker. Picking one picks a brain role
       *                 (AIRole), a default skin (AIKit) and a faction. That is the editor affordance.
       *   species    -- HUMAN or BEAST. Every human inherits one baseline row (courage, loyalty, greed,
       *                 curiosity); a non-human inherits the beast row. A zombie is not a human with different
       *                 numbers, which is why this is an inheritance switch and not a column.
       *   orders     -- the programmable half. A bitmask of what this unit accepts plus the archetype's own
       *                 priority for each, both authored (level JSON / NOCK) and both overridable per unit.
       *                 eu_choose_order below is the whole "custom AI": change the mask, change the behaviour,
       *                 without a new C branch.
       *
       * Deliberately dependency-free (no GL, SDL, physics, protocol, story_ai.h): roles and kits are plain
       * integers so story_ai.h can hold an EUUnit without a cycle, and so this is testable headlessly.
       * Numbers come from empire_rules.h, which mirrors PARENA (see that header).
       */
      #ifndef SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_UNITS_H
      #define SHANKPIT_EMPIRE_UNITS_H
      
      #include <math.h>
      #include "empire_units_rules.h"
      
      /* Archetypes. 0 is deliberately "none": a character with no archetype keeps exactly the pre-EMPIRE
         behaviour (its authored role and kit, no orders), which is what keeps old levels loading unchanged. */
      #define EU_ARCH_NONE 0
      #define EU_ARCH_CITIZEN 1
      #define EU_ARCH_ZOMBIE 2
      #define EU_ARCH_SOLDIER 3
      #define EU_ARCH_ALLY 4
      #define EU_ARCH_GUARD 5
      #define EU_ARCH_WORKER 6
      #define EU_ARCH_COUNT 6
      
      #define EU_SPECIES_NONE 0
      #define EU_SPECIES_HUMAN 1
      #define EU_SPECIES_BEAST 2
      
      #define EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL 0
      #define EU_FACTION_ALLY 1
      #define EU_FACTION_HOSTILE 2
      #define EU_FACTION_COUNT 3
      
      /* Orders, as bits. These values are the contract the level JSON's own `orders` field uses. */
      #define EU_ORDER_NONE 0
      #define EU_ORDER_FOLLOW 1
      #define EU_ORDER_EXPLORE 2
      #define EU_ORDER_ENGAGE 4
      #define EU_ORDER_GATHER 8
      #define EU_ORDER_CLAIM 16
      #define EU_ORDER_GUARD 32
      #define EU_ORDER_ALL (EU_ORDER_FOLLOW | EU_ORDER_EXPLORE | EU_ORDER_ENGAGE | EU_ORDER_GATHER | \
                            EU_ORDER_CLAIM | EU_ORDER_GUARD)
      
      /* Order indexes for the rules table (eu_order_priority takes these, not the bits). */
      #define EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW 0
      #define EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE 1
      #define EU_ORDER_IDX_ENGAGE 2
      #define EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER 3
      #define EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM 4
      #define EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD 5
      
      #define EU_MAX_NODES 16
      #define EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS 32
      
      /* A resource node is a place, not an item: standing on it is what gathers. Amount is what is left. */
      typedef struct {
          float x, z;
          int amount;
          int capacity;
      } EUResourceNode;
      
      /* A claim cell is a piece of ground a faction can own. claim_ms is THIS claimant's progress, which is
         why claimant is stored: a second faction standing on it starts over rather than inheriting the work. */
      typedef struct {
          float x, z;
          int radius;
          int owner;     /* EU_FACTION_* */
          int claimant;  /* EU_FACTION_* currently making progress, NEUTRAL when nobody */
          int claim_ms;
      } EUClaimCell;
      
      typedef struct {
          EUResourceNode nodes[EU_MAX_NODES];
          int node_count;
          EUClaimCell cells[EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS];
          int cell_count;
          int stockpile[EU_FACTION_COUNT]; /* gathered and banked, per faction */
          int gathered[EU_FACTION_COUNT];  /* lifetime total, for a HUD/test to read */
      } EUWorld;
      
      typedef struct {
          int archetype;   /* EU_ARCH_* */
          int faction;     /* EU_FACTION_* */
          int species;     /* EU_SPECIES_* -- the inheritance switch */
          int orders;      /* accepted order bits */
          int role;        /* AIRole this archetype's brain runs (story_ai.h values) */
          int kit;         /* default AIKit; an authored kit always wins */
          int health;
          /* The inherited baseline, permille. Humans get the human row, beasts the beast row. */
          int courage, aggression, loyalty, greed, curiosity;
          /* Live order state, owned by the host (story_ai.c). */
          int order;       /* EU_ORDER_* currently executing, NONE when falling back to the brain */
          int target_node, target_cell;
          int carrying;    /* units gathered, not yet banked separately from the faction stockpile */
          float explore_x, explore_z;
          int exploring;   /* 0 = needs a new explore point */
      } EUUnit;
      
      /* What the unit can currently perceive. Kept as a plain struct so the host decides how it is filled and
         so the decision is testable without a server. */
      typedef struct {
          int enemy_visible;
          float enemy_dist;
          float leader_dist;
          int leader_alive;
          int idle_ms;      /* how long the current mode has been running */
          int at_home;      /* within a couple of steps of the spawn point */
      } EUView;
      
      static inline const char *eu_archetype_name(int arch) {
          switch (arch) {
              case EU_ARCH_CITIZEN: return "citizen";
              case EU_ARCH_ZOMBIE: return "zombie";
              case EU_ARCH_SOLDIER: return "soldier";
              case EU_ARCH_ALLY: return "ally";
              case EU_ARCH_GUARD: return "guard";
              case EU_ARCH_WORKER: return "worker";
              default: return "none";
          }
      }
      
      static inline const char *eu_order_name(int order) {
          switch (order) {
              case EU_ORDER_FOLLOW: return "follow";
              case EU_ORDER_EXPLORE: return "explore";
              case EU_ORDER_ENGAGE: return "engage";
              case EU_ORDER_GATHER: return "gather";
              case EU_ORDER_CLAIM: return "claim";
              case EU_ORDER_GUARD: return "guard";
              default: return "none";
          }
      }
      
      static inline int eu_order_bit_for_index(int index) {
          switch (index) {
              case EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW: return EU_ORDER_FOLLOW;
              case EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE: return EU_ORDER_EXPLORE;
              case EU_ORDER_IDX_ENGAGE: return EU_ORDER_ENGAGE;
              case EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER: return EU_ORDER_GATHER;
              case EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM: return EU_ORDER_CLAIM;
              case EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD: return EU_ORDER_GUARD;
              default: return EU_ORDER_NONE;
          }
      }
      
      static inline int eu_order_index_for_bit(int order) {
          switch (order) {
              case EU_ORDER_FOLLOW: return EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW;
              case EU_ORDER_EXPLORE: return EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE;
              case EU_ORDER_ENGAGE: return EU_ORDER_IDX_ENGAGE;
              case EU_ORDER_GATHER: return EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER;
              case EU_ORDER_CLAIM: return EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM;
              case EU_ORDER_GUARD: return EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD;
              default: return -1;
          }
      }
      
      /* eu_unit_init -- an archetype's defaults, then the author's overrides, then the inheritance row.
       *   kit:     > 0 = the author's skin, 0 = the archetype's default (AUTO stays AUTO for the zombie,
       *            whose clip set is chosen by the witness role, not by AIKit).
       *   faction: >= 0 = the author's faction, < 0 = the archetype's default.
       *   orders:  >= 0 = the author's mask (0 is legal: "does what its brain does, takes no orders"),
       *            < 0 = the archetype's default mask.
       * The mask is the ONLY gate. Every archetype scores every order (see empire_rules.prn), so an authored
       * bit is always usable -- the mask says what a unit accepts, the priorities say what wins when more than
       * one accepted order is triggered. Archetype 0 keeps no orders, because it has no brain role to run. */
      static inline void eu_unit_init(EUUnit *u, int archetype, int kit, int faction, int orders) {
          if (!u) return;
          int arch = eu_clamp(0, EU_ARCH_COUNT, archetype);
          u->archetype = arch;
          u->species = g_eu_rules.archetype_species(arch);
          u->role = g_eu_rules.archetype_role(arch);

          AI_MODE_SEARCH,
          AI_MODE_FLEE,
          AI_MODE_ALLY_FOLLOW,
          AI_MODE_SCRIPTED,
          /* S462 -- real Territorial Beast radius-anchor/leash retreat (founder real-time: "Radius
             Anchoring & Return Leashes... retreats if pulled too far away"). Forced unconditionally
             (even mid-combat) whenever distance-from-home exceeds leash_radius; exits only on real
             arrival back home, not on the radius re-check alone. See ai_run_leash_return. */
          AI_MODE_LEASH_RETURN,
          /* S470 -- real, ambient friendly behavior (founder real-time: "have them wave to the player
             when the player gets close and then dance before resuming patrol"). Locked, non-combat --
             AI_ROLE_WANDERING_BOT is the only role that ever enters it, and its own decision logic
             (story_ai_tick) never routes it through combat/investigate/flee at all, same class of
             "real behavior, deliberately excluded from the rest of the state machine" precedent
             AI_MODE_SCRIPTED's own locked-state comment already sets. See ai_run_greet. */
          AI_MODE_GREET,
          /* EMPIRE unit orders (packages/simulation/empire_units.h). These are not new brains: each one is a
             small, specific way of using the movement/attack primitives the modes above already have, chosen
             by eu_choose_order from the unit's own authored mask. A unit whose archetype is 0 never enters
             them -- every pre-existing AI's behaviour is untouched. */
          AI_MODE_EXPLORE, /* walk to points inside the explore radius, look around, pick another */
          AI_MODE_GATHER,  /* walk to the nearest resource node and take from it while standing on it */
          AI_MODE_CLAIM   /* walk to the nearest unowned cell and stand on it until it is ours */
      } AIMode;
      
      typedef enum {
          AI_ROLE_RIFT_HOUND = 0,
          AI_ROLE_SHAMBLER_TROOPER,
          AI_ROLE_GORE_BRUTE,
          AI_ROLE_STORY_ALLY,
          AI_ROLE_GUARD,
          /* S181-05, founder real-time: "advance the entities fought in story
           * mode... use redgarden squad ai and realistic abilities and

           * for real roster variety beyond the original 3, each a genuinely
           * distinct threat archetype (long-range burst vs. heavy AOE spammer)
           * built on real, already-proven SHANKPIT weapon mechanics -- not

          AI_ROLE_STORM_CALLER,  /* WPN_SNIPER -- long-range storm-charge burst threat */
          AI_ROLE_BOMBARDIER,    /* WPN_MISSILE -- heavy, slow, real splash-AOE spammer */
          /* S462 -- solo, non-squad enemy archetypes (founder real-time: "the auto-pilot AI shifts its

          AI_ROLE_RELENTLESS_PURSUER, /* "Zombie" -- direct-line pursuit only, never kites, never flees */
          AI_ROLE_TERRITORIAL_BEAST,  /* radius-anchored home + leash retreat, see AI_MODE_LEASH_RETURN */
          AI_ROLE_BLIND_STALKER,      /* "Ambush Predator" + "Sightless Echo-Locator" combined -- near-
                                          zero vision, detects almost entirely by hearing */
          /* S470 -- real, non-hostile ambient archetype (founder real-time: "get all the robots in
             there and have them walking around different waypoints... wave to the player when the
             player gets close and then dance before resuming patrol"). Never enters combat/investigate/
             search/flee at all -- story_ai_tick's own decision loop special-cases this role the same
             way it already special-cases AI_ROLE_STORY_ALLY, just routing to AI_MODE_PATROL/
             AI_MODE_GREET only instead of ALLY_FOLLOW/COMBAT. Never joined to a squad, same as the
             three S462 solo archetypes. */
          AI_ROLE_WANDERING_BOT
      } AIRole;
      
      /* AIKit (S492) -- a NOCK-authored character's chosen visual model, completely decoupled from
         AIRole (behavior) above -- the same "role picks the brain, kit picks the body" split
         PlayerState.forced_kit's own doc comment (packages/common/protocol.h) describes. AI_KIT_AUTO

         Kept in sync BY HAND with internal/shankpit.AIKit* (IDUNA) and apps/lobby/src/main.c's own
         kits[5] array order -- same manual cross-boundary sync AIRole's own values already require. */
      typedef enum {
          AI_KIT_AUTO = 0,
          AI_KIT_MANNEQUIN,
          AI_KIT_STAN,
          AI_KIT_MIKE,
          AI_KIT_LEELA,
          AI_KIT_GEORGE,
          /* Imported skins. A set NOCK imported into assets/goldenband/clipsets/<name>/ becomes a kit at
             startup (skin_registry_scan + gband_skel_npc_load_clipset), and an authored character picks
             one with AI_KIT_IMPORTED_BASE + index -- the same number the lobby prints for each set when it
             loads, so a level author reads the index off the host's own startup line instead of guessing.
             forced_kit is an unsigned char on the wire (NetPlayer.forced_kit), so this range costs nothing
             and AI_KIT_IMPORTED_BASE + STORY_AI_IMPORTED_MAX still fits in a byte. */
          AI_KIT_IMPORTED_BASE = 6
      } AIKit;
      
      /* How many imported skins an authored character may address. The host loads at most this many (it is
         bounded by the GOLDENBAND kit table and the registry scan), and a value past what actually loaded
         is not an error: the drawing cascade simply falls through to its usual round-robin. Kept as a
         plain number so this header stays free of the filesystem-facing skin_registry.h. */
      #define STORY_AI_IMPORTED_MAX 10
      
      /* story_ai_kit_is_valid -- the one range check every kit consumer should use. Before imported skins
         existed this test was written out by hand as `kit >= AI_KIT_AUTO && kit <= AI_KIT_GEORGE` in both
         apps/server and apps/lobby; two copies of a range that has now grown is exactly how an imported
         skin silently stops being authorable. */
      static inline int story_ai_kit_is_valid(int kit) {
          return kit >= AI_KIT_AUTO && kit < AI_KIT_IMPORTED_BASE + STORY_AI_IMPORTED_MAX;
      }

 * Founder: "the first person to enter it it generates and then everyone else enters the same one ...

 * rebuild the identical layout from the seed (zone_sync.h), so no geometry crosses the wire. Occupancy is

static void server_zone_expired(void *user, const char *zone_id) {
    char path[256];

    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "var/maps/proc_%s.json", zone_id ? zone_id : "zone");

    printf("[ZONE] '%s' was empty past its grace period -- layout deleted, next entrant regenerates\n",
           zone_id ? zone_id : "?");
}

static void server_zone_generate_and_apply(const char *zone_id, unsigned int seed) {
    static CustomLevelData lvl;
    char path[256];
    FILE *probe;
    proc_dungeon_generate(&lvl, zone_id, seed);
    probe = fopen("var/maps", "rb");
    if (probe) fclose(probe);
    else (void)system("mkdir -p var/maps");
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "var/maps/proc_%s.json", zone_id);
    if (!proc_dungeon_save(path, &lvl)) printf("[ZONE] could not write %s\n", path);
    server_apply_custom_level(&lvl);
    /* Copy only when the source is NOT the destination: snprintf with overlapping buffers is undefined,
       and the first version did exactly that (g_server_zone_id into itself), which glibc turned into an
       empty id -- a server that generated a zone and then advertised ''. */
    if (zone_id != g_server_zone_id) snprintf(g_server_zone_id, sizeof g_server_zone_id, "%s", zone_id);
    g_server_zone_seed = seed;
    printf("[ZONE] generated '%s' seed %08x (%d boxes, difficulty %d)\n",
           zone_id, seed, lvl.count, g_zone_rules.difficulty((int)seed));
}

      /* ---- EMPIRE units ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
      
      EUWorld *story_ai_empire_world(void) { return &g_empire_world; }
      
      void story_ai_empire_seed_default(void) {
          eu_world_clear(&g_empire_world);
          int cap = g_eu_rules.node_capacity();
          /* Six nodes on a 40-unit ring, twelve claim cells on a 70-unit ring: close enough that a unit walks to
             one in a few seconds, far enough apart that two factions do not silently share a node. */
          for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
              float a = (float)i * 1.0471976f; /* 60 degrees */
              eu_world_add_node(&g_empire_world, cosf(a) * 40.0f, sinf(a) * 40.0f, cap);
          }
          for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
              float a = (float)i * 0.5235988f; /* 30 degrees */
              eu_world_add_claim_cell(&g_empire_world, cosf(a) * 70.0f, sinf(a) * 70.0f);
          }
      }
      
      int story_ai_spawn_unit(ServerState *s, int archetype, int kit, int faction, int orders,
                              float x, float y, float z) {
          if (!s) return -1;
          EUUnit probe;
          eu_unit_init(&probe, archetype, kit, faction, orders);
          if (probe.archetype == EU_ARCH_NONE) return -1;
          int pid = story_ai_spawn_enemy(s, (AIRole)probe.role, probe.kit, x, y, z);
          if (pid < 0) return -1;
          int idx = ai_index_by_player_id(pid);
          if (idx < 0) return -1;
          AIController *ai = &g_story_ai[idx];
          ai->archetype = probe.archetype;
          ai->faction = probe.faction;
          ai->eu = probe;
          ai->last_order_ms = 0;
          /* The archetype's health pool is the point of an archetype (an ally outlasts a zombie). The brain
             defaults above already set the weapon/senses for the role it picked. */
          s->players[pid].health = probe.health;
          return pid;
      }
      
      int story_ai_unit_order(int player_id) {
          int idx = ai_index_by_player_id(player_id);
          if (idx < 0 || g_story_ai[idx].archetype == EU_ARCH_NONE) return -1;
          return g_story_ai[idx].eu.order;
      }
      
      int story_ai_unit_archetype(int player_id) {
          int idx = ai_index_by_player_id(player_id);
          return idx < 0 ? -1 : g_story_ai[idx].archetype;
      }

      static inline int eu_orders_has(const EUUnit *u, int order) {
          return u && (u->orders & order) != 0;
      }
      
      /* Priority 0 for an order this unit does not accept, so callers never need a second mask test. */
      static inline int eu_unit_priority(const EUUnit *u, int order) {
          if (!u || !eu_orders_has(u, order)) return 0;
          int idx = eu_order_index_for_bit(order);
          if (idx < 0) return 0;
          return g_eu_rules.order_priority(u->archetype, idx);
      }
      
      static inline void eu_world_clear(EUWorld *w) {
          if (!w) return;
          for (int i = 0; i < EU_MAX_NODES; i++) {
              w->nodes[i].x = w->nodes[i].z = 0.0f;
              w->nodes[i].amount = w->nodes[i].capacity = 0;
          }
          for (int i = 0; i < EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS; i++) {
              w->cells[i].x = w->cells[i].z = 0.0f;
              w->cells[i].radius = 0;
              w->cells[i].owner = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;
              w->cells[i].claimant = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;
              w->cells[i].claim_ms = 0;
          }
          w->node_count = 0;
          w->cell_count = 0;
          for (int f = 0; f < EU_FACTION_COUNT; f++) w->stockpile[f] = w->gathered[f] = 0;
      }
      
      static inline int eu_world_add_node(EUWorld *w, float x, float z, int amount) {
          if (!w || w->node_count >= EU_MAX_NODES || amount <= 0) return -1;
          int cap = g_eu_rules.node_capacity();
          EUResourceNode *n = &w->nodes[w->node_count];
          n->x = x;
          n->z = z;
          n->amount = amount > cap ? cap : amount;
          n->capacity = n->amount;
          return w->node_count++;
      }
      
      static inline int eu_world_add_claim_cell(EUWorld *w, float x, float z) {
          if (!w || w->cell_count >= EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS) return -1;
          EUClaimCell *c = &w->cells[w->cell_count];
          c->x = x;
          c->z = z;
          c->radius = g_eu_rules.claim_radius();
          c->owner = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;
          c->claimant = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;
          c->claim_ms = 0;
          return w->cell_count++;
      }
      
      static inline float eu_dist2(float ax, float az, float bx, float bz) {
          float dx = ax - bx, dz = az - bz;
          return dx * dx + dz * dz;
      }
      
      /* Nearest node that still has something in it, or -1. */
      static inline int eu_nearest_node(const EUWorld *w, float x, float z) {
          if (!w) return -1;
          int best = -1;
          float best_d = 0.0f;
          for (int i = 0; i < w->node_count; i++) {
              if (w->nodes[i].amount <= 0) continue;
              float d = eu_dist2(x, z, w->nodes[i].x, w->nodes[i].z);
              if (best < 0 || d < best_d) { best = i; best_d = d; }
          }
          return best;
      }

      /* Nearest cell this faction does not already own, or -1. */
      static inline int eu_nearest_free_cell(const EUWorld *w, int faction, float x, float z) {
          if (!w) return -1;
          int best = -1;
          float best_d = 0.0f;
          for (int i = 0; i < w->cell_count; i++) {
              if (w->cells[i].owner == faction) continue;
              float d = eu_dist2(x, z, w->cells[i].x, w->cells[i].z);
              if (best < 0 || d < best_d) { best = i; best_d = d; }
          }
          return best;
      }
      
      /* Gather one unit from a node into the unit's hands and the faction's stockpile. Returns 1 when a unit
         was actually gathered, 0 when the node is empty/spent/out of range of the caller's own choice. */
      static inline int eu_world_gather(EUWorld *w, EUUnit *u, int node_index) {
          if (!w || !u || node_index < 0 || node_index >= w->node_count) return 0;
          EUResourceNode *n = &w->nodes[node_index];
          if (n->amount <= 0) return 0;
          n->amount--;
          u->carrying++;
          w->stockpile[u->faction]++;
          w->gathered[u->faction]++;
          return 1;
      }
      
      /* Stand on a cell for eu_claim_ticks() and it becomes yours. Another faction's progress is reset the
         moment it starts its own attempt, so a contested cell is a race, not a shared bar. Returns 1 on the
         tick the cell changes hands. */
      static inline int eu_world_claim_tick(EUWorld *w, EUUnit *u, int cell_index, int dt_ms) {
          if (!w || !u || cell_index < 0 || cell_index >= w->cell_count) return 0;
          EUClaimCell *c = &w->cells[cell_index];
          if (c->owner == u->faction) { return 0; }
          if (c->claimant != u->faction) {
              c->claimant = u->faction;
              c->claim_ms = 0;
          }
          int need = g_eu_rules.claim_ticks();
          c->claim_ms += dt_ms > 0 ? dt_ms : 0;
          if (c->claim_ms >= need) {
              c->owner = u->faction;
              c->claimant = EU_FACTION_NEUTRAL;
              c->claim_ms = 0;
              return 1;
          }
          return 0;
      }
      
      /* eu_choose_order -- the decision, and the whole programmable surface.
       *
       * ENGAGE is checked first and is not a candidate in the score race: if a unit accepts ENGAGE and can see
       * an enemy, that is what it does. Everything else is "the highest-priority order whose own trigger is
       * true right now", with GUARD as the standing fallback (it needs no trigger -- holding ground is always
       * possible), and NONE when nothing applies, which means "fall back to the role's own brain" rather than
       * "stand still". That distinction is what lets an authored soldier keep its GUARD post while a citizen
       * wanders off to gather.
       */
      static inline int eu_choose_order(const EUUnit *u, const EUWorld *w, const EUView *v) {
          if (!u || !v) return EU_ORDER_NONE;
          if (eu_orders_has(u, EU_ORDER_ENGAGE) && v->enemy_visible) return EU_ORDER_ENGAGE;
          if (!w && (eu_orders_has(u, EU_ORDER_GATHER) || eu_orders_has(u, EU_ORDER_CLAIM)))
              return EU_ORDER_NONE;
      
          int best_order = EU_ORDER_NONE;
          int best_score = 0;
          for (int idx = 0; idx <= EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD; idx++) {
              int bit = eu_order_bit_for_index(idx);
              int score = eu_unit_priority(u, bit);
              if (score <= 0) continue;
              int triggered = 0;
              switch (idx) {
                  case EU_ORDER_IDX_FOLLOW:
                      triggered = v->leader_alive && v->leader_dist > (float)g_eu_rules.follow_distance();
                      break;
                  case EU_ORDER_IDX_EXPLORE:
                      triggered = v->idle_ms >= 2000;
                      break;
                  case EU_ORDER_IDX_GATHER:
                      triggered = w && eu_nearest_node(w, 0.0f, 0.0f) >= 0;
                      break;
                  case EU_ORDER_IDX_CLAIM:
                      triggered = w && eu_nearest_free_cell(w, u->faction, 0.0f, 0.0f) >= 0;
                      break;
                  case EU_ORDER_IDX_GUARD:
                      triggered = 1;
                      break;
                  default:
                      break;
              }
              if (!triggered) continue;
              if (score > best_score) { best_score = score; best_order = bit; }
          }
          return best_order;
      }

      void server_broadcast_zone_state(void) {
          static unsigned int last_ms = 0;
          unsigned int now_ms = get_server_time();
          int connected = 0, state;
          NetZoneState pkt;
      
          if (!g_server_zones_ready || !g_server_zone_id[0]) return;
          for (int i = 1; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++)
              if (slots[i].active && slots[i].welcomed && slots[i].cmd_seen && local_state.players[i].active) connected++;
      
          state = zone_registry_state(&g_server_zones, g_server_zone_id);
          if (connected > 0 && state == ZONE_STATE_UNINIT) {
              unsigned int seed = 0;
              if (zone_registry_enter(&g_server_zones, g_server_zone_id, (int)now_ms, &seed) == 1)
                  server_zone_generate_and_apply(g_server_zone_id, seed);
          } else if (connected > g_server_zone_seen_players) {
              for (int n = g_server_zone_seen_players; n < connected; n++)
                  zone_registry_enter(&g_server_zones, g_server_zone_id, (int)now_ms, NULL);
          } else if (connected < g_server_zone_seen_players) {
              for (int n = connected; n < g_server_zone_seen_players; n++)
                  zone_registry_leave(&g_server_zones, g_server_zone_id, (int)now_ms);
          }
          g_server_zone_seen_players = connected;
          zone_registry_tick(&g_server_zones, (int)now_ms, server_zone_expired, NULL);
          state = zone_registry_state(&g_server_zones, g_server_zone_id);
      
          if (last_ms != 0 && (now_ms - last_ms) < 1000) return;
          last_ms = now_ms;
          zone_sync_fill(&pkt, g_server_zone_id, g_server_zone_seed, connected, state,
                         (unsigned int)zone_registry_idle_ms(&g_server_zones, g_server_zone_id, (int)now_ms), now_ms);
          for (int i = 1; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
              if (!slots[i].active || !slots[i].welcomed) continue;
              sendto(sock, &pkt, sizeof(pkt), 0, (struct sockaddr*)&slots[i].addr, sizeof(struct sockaddr_in));
          }
      
          /* Same 1 Hz beat as the packet above, so a finder hears about a world at most a second after it
             exists. Announced only while the zone is live: an expired zone has nothing to advertise, and a
             beacon for a dead world would send allies to a host that cannot generate it. */
          if (g_server_beacon_sock >= 0 && state != ZONE_STATE_UNINIT && g_server_zone_id[0]) {
              ZoneBeacon beacon;
              memset(&beacon, 0, sizeof beacon);
              snprintf(beacon.zone, sizeof beacon.zone, "%s", g_server_zone_id);
              beacon.seed = g_server_zone_seed;
              beacon.players = connected;
              beacon.port = g_server_game_port; /* the port this process really bound, not a constant */
              zone_beacon_announce(g_server_beacon_sock, g_server_beacon_port, &beacon);
          }
      }
      
      /* server_shield_packs_tick -- card #541. MODE_QUEUE only. A player dying has a SHIELD_PACK_DROP_PERCENT chance
       * to leave a pack where they fell; any living player standing on a pack whose shield is below full takes it and
       * is refilled to full. Shields still do not regenerate (founder: "leave it like that") -- a pack is the only way
       * back up. The server rolls and grants; clients only render PACKET_SHIELD_PACKS. */
      static void server_shield_packs_tick(void) {
          if (local_state.game_mode != MODE_QUEUE || local_state.match_over) return;
          for (int i = 1; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
              PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[i];
              if (!p->active || p->scene_id != g_server_match_scene) { shield_packs_note_player(i, 1, 0, 0, 0, 100); continue; }
              int alive = (p->state != STATE_DEAD);
              shield_packs_note_player(i, alive, p->x, p->y, p->z, rand() % 100);
              if (alive && p->shield < 100 && shield_packs_take(p->x, p->y, p->z)) {
                  p->shield = 100;
                  NET_SERVER_LOG("SHIELD_PACK_TAKEN player=%d", i);
              }
          }
      }

      void server_broadcast_shield_packs(void) {

# Founder: "spawn in allies like mike etc ... exploring the environment engaging enemies following allies
# taking over territory gathering resources ... the ais also need some generic stuff that all humans will
# inherit but not all ais will be human ... spawn in citizens zombies soldiers etc". The archetype table,

# (stdlib/shankpit/empire_units.prn); packages/simulation/empire_units.h is the unit and its decision.

# defaults sample for sample (the arrangement every other rules module keeps), every human archetype
# inherits the human row and the zombie does not, a masked-out order has priority 0, the order race picks
# the highest triggered priority with GUARD as the standing fallback and NONE as "use the role's brain",

       * this loader's own "smallest real thing" precedent (see this file's own top doc comment).
       *
       * This is a pure geometry/data carrier, same role LevelExit/LevelCharacter already play --
       * packages/world stays physics.h/witness_sim.h-independent by design (zone_type is a bare int
       * here, not the ZONE_* enum type itself, so this header never has to include witness_sim.h).
       * level_boxes_zone_for_position (below) is the real query a caller (packages/simulation/
       * witness_ai.c's own witness_ai_sync_zones) uses to turn a live x/y/z into a zone_type.
       *
       * Real, deliberate scope cut, matching SHANKPIT/CLAUDE.md's own standing "levels are never
       * story-mode-only" instruction: zones are general level geometry, usable in ANY mode, not gated
       * to MODE_STORY -- nothing about this struct or its parser is story-mode-specific. */
      typedef struct {
          float x, y, z;
          float radius;
          int zone_type;
      } LevelZone;
      
      #define LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_ZONES 16 /* matches IDUNA/internal/shankpit.MaxLevelZones exactly */
      
      /* An author-placed programmable widget (NOCK `edu_widgets` array): a named machine bound to one EduVM
       * "hardware register", so a script typed into the Architect's Orb can drive the level
       * (set_state("door_gate_alpha", 1) / set_reg(1, 1) / read_sensor(2)). Pure data carrier like LevelZone --
       * packages/world stays education-independent; machine_type is a bare int that the lobby hands to
       * packages/education's EduWidgetType (1 GATE, 2 BRIDGE, 3 PORTAL, 4 CRATE, 5 PLATE/sensor). Not
       * story-mode-only (SHANKPIT/CLAUDE.md): usable in any mode. */
      typedef struct {
          char entity_id[32];
          int machine_type;
          int initial_state;   /* 0 closed/inactive, 1 open/active */
          int memory_address;  /* the register read_sensor/set_reg address */
          float x, y, z;
          float radius;        /* sensor reach for PLATE; 0 -> host default */
          int box_index;       /* GATE/BRIDGE: index into boxes[] this widget raises/lowers like a story door
                                  (physics + render); -1 = purely a register, no geometry attached */
          /* Composable circuit wiring (2026-10-31, founder: "the widgets need to be composible ... think light
           * switches, basic circuits, an elevator is a widget of widgets"). A widget can be a SOURCE (lever 6,
           * plate 5), a RELAY (delay 7), a GATE (transistor 8) or an ACTUATOR (1..4 machines), wired by the
           * index of the widget that feeds it. -1 = nothing wired. Pins must point at LOWER indices: the
           * circuit is evaluated in authoring order, once per tick (see packages/simulation/widget_circuit.h).
           * delay_ticks is a DELAY's own timer length in 60 Hz ticks; 0 = the default half-second relay. */
          int input_pin;
          int gate_pin;
          int delay_ticks;
      } LevelEduWidget;

          float x[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], y[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], z[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX];

          float r[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], g[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], b[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX];

          for (int bi = 0; bi < lvl->count; bi++) {
              x[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].x; y[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].y; z[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].z;
              w[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].w; h[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].h; d[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].d;
              r[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].r; g[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].g; b[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].b;
              material_idx[bi] = lvl->boxes[bi].material_idx;
          }
          char mat_names[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN];
          char mat_shaders[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN];
          float mat_specular[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS], mat_shininess[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS];
          float mat_friction[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_MATERIALS];

              strncpy(mat_shaders[mi], lvl->materials[mi].shader_name, CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN - 1);
              mat_shaders[mi][CUSTOM_LEVEL_MATERIAL_NAME_LEN - 1] = '\0';
              mat_specular[mi] = lvl->materials[mi].specular;
              mat_shininess[mi] = lvl->materials[mi].shininess;
              mat_friction[mi] = lvl->materials[mi].friction;
          }
          phys_set_custom_level_materials(mat_names, mat_shaders, mat_specular, mat_shininess, mat_friction, lvl->material_count);
          phys_set_custom_level(x, y, z, w, h, d, r, g, b, material_idx, lvl->count, lvl->ground_plane_enabled, lvl->ground_plane_squares);
          {   /* oriented boxes / ramps (obb.h): static scratch keeps the 4 extra arrays off the stack */
              static float orx[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], ory[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX], orz[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX];

      static void lobby_apply_story_level(const CustomLevelData *lvl) {
          level_boxes_apply_to_physics(lvl);
          scene_load(SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL);
          local_state.players[0].scene_id = SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL;
      
          story_ai_reset(&local_state);
          for (int ci = 0; ci < lvl->character_count; ci++) {
              const LevelCharacter *lc = &lvl->characters[ci];
              if (lc->role < AI_ROLE_RIFT_HOUND || lc->role > AI_ROLE_WANDERING_BOT) continue; // S492, mirrors apps/server's own identical fix
              int kit = story_ai_kit_is_valid(lc->kit) ? lc->kit : AI_KIT_AUTO; // S492 + imported skins, mirrors apps/server's own fallback
              /* An authored EMPIRE unit (archetype > 0) spawns through the order layer, which picks its role,
                 skin, faction and accepted orders; every other character spawns exactly as before. */
              if (lc->archetype > 0)
                  story_ai_spawn_unit(&local_state, lc->archetype, kit, lc->faction, lc->orders,
                                      lc->x, lc->y, lc->z);
              else
                  story_ai_spawn_enemy(&local_state, (AIRole)lc->role, kit, lc->x, lc->y, lc->z);
          }
      
          float nn_x[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES], nn_y[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES], nn_z[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES];
          int nn_is_cover[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES];
          float nn_cover_dir_x[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES], nn_cover_dir_z[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES];
          int nn_neighbor_counts[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES];
          int nn_neighbors_flat[LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NODES * LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NEIGHBORS];
          for (int ni = 0; ni < lvl->nav_node_count; ni++) {
              nn_x[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].x; nn_y[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].y; nn_z[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].z;
              nn_is_cover[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].is_cover;
              nn_cover_dir_x[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].cover_dir_x;
              nn_cover_dir_z[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].cover_dir_z;
              nn_neighbor_counts[ni] = lvl->nav_nodes[ni].neighbor_count;
              for (int k = 0; k < LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NEIGHBORS; k++) {
                  nn_neighbors_flat[ni * LEVEL_BOXES_MAX_NAV_NEIGHBORS + k] =
                      (k < lvl->nav_nodes[ni].neighbor_count) ? lvl->nav_nodes[ni].neighbors[k] : -1;
              }
          }
          story_ai_load_nav_graph(lvl->nav_node_count, nn_x, nn_y, nn_z, nn_is_cover,
                                   nn_cover_dir_x, nn_cover_dir_z, nn_neighbor_counts, nn_neighbors_flat);
      
          // level_boxes_apply_to_physics (called at the top of this function) already captured
          // g_story_level_exits/g_story_next_level_id -- real, no duplicate capture needed here as of
          // S477.
          local_state.story_boss.active = 0; /* replacing VOXWORLD's own encounter, not extending it */
          local_state.story_phase = STORY_PHASE_PLAYING; /* real skip of the intro cutscene */
      }
      
      // lobby_check_story_level_exits -- lobby's own local-single-player mirror of
      // apps/server/src/main.c's story_check_level_exits, same real design (full 3D distance, a real
      // debounce against the new level's own spawn point landing back inside an exit radius). See that
      // function's own doc comment for the full reasoning.
      //
      // S477, real fix (founder real-time, live playtest: "i walk over to the block where the level
      // exit should be... i say out loud beam me up scotty and then nothing happens... i am on
      // nextown"). This used to be gated to MODE_STORY only -- but exits are real, author-authored
      // level data, not a story-mode-only concept, and the founder's own real "nextown" level (a plain
      // level-select/deathmatch load, is_story_start=false) never ran this check at all, regardless of
      // how correctly the exit was placed. The g_story_level_exit_count/g_story_next_level_id checks
      // below are already a real, sufficient gate on their own (a level with no exits authored is a
      // real, honest no-op in ANY mode) -- no separate mode check is needed.
      #define STORY_LEVEL_TRANSITION_DEBOUNCE_MS 3000U
      static void lobby_check_story_level_exits(unsigned int now_ms) {
          if (g_story_level_exit_count <= 0 || g_story_next_level_id <= 0) return;
          if (now_ms - g_story_last_level_transition_ms < STORY_LEVEL_TRANSITION_DEBOUNCE_MS) return;
          PlayerState *hero = &local_state.players[0];
          if (!hero->active || hero->state == STATE_DEAD) return;
      
          int triggered = 0;
          int triggered_target_spawner_id = 0; /* S491: mirrors story_check_level_exits' own logic */
          for (int i = 0; i < g_story_level_exit_count; i++) {
              LevelExit *ex = &g_story_level_exits[i];
              float dx = hero->x - ex->x, dy = hero->y - ex->y, dz = hero->z - ex->z;
              float dist2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz;
              if (dist2 <= ex->radius * ex->radius) {
                  triggered = 1;
                  triggered_target_spawner_id = ex->target_spawner_id;
                  break;
              }
          }
          if (!triggered) return;
      
          int next_id = g_story_next_level_id;
          CustomLevelData lvl;
          lobby_level_snapshot(0);   // leaving this level: autosave its damage first
          if (!level_boxes_fetch_export(next_id, &lvl)) {
              g_story_last_level_transition_ms = now_ms;
              return;
          }
          lobby_apply_story_level(&lvl);
          phys_respawn(hero, now_ms);
          // S491 -- see story_check_level_exits' own identical override for the full rationale.
          if (triggered_target_spawner_id > 0) {
              float tx, ty, tz;
              if (custom_level_pick_spawner_by_id(triggered_target_spawner_id, &tx, &ty, &tz)) {
                  hero->x = tx; hero->y = ty; hero->z = tz;
              }
          }
          g_story_last_level_transition_ms = now_ms;
      }
      
      // lobby_start_story_mode -- S473, STORY_LEVEL_SEQUENCING_NORTHSTAR.md Phase 1 (founder real-time:
      // "we dont need the text cutscene in the beginning we just need to spawn into the first map that
      // the story is"). Factored out of the two previously-duplicated MODE_STORY entry points (the
      // menu-click handler and the direct lobby-action handler) below -- both now call this instead of
      // hand-repeating local_init_match + cutscene_start. A level flagged is_story_start replaces
      // VOXWORLD's own default entirely (real skip of the intro cutscene, via lobby_apply_story_level's
      // own STORY_PHASE_PLAYING set); with no such level authored yet, this is a real, honest no-op and
      // the existing VOXWORLD intro-cutscene path runs exactly as before.
      static void lobby_start_story_mode(void) {
          local_init_match(1, MODE_STORY);
          food_pickup_reset();
          food_pickup_seed_voxworld();
          LevelRegistryEntry entries[LEVEL_REGISTRY_MAX_ENTRIES];
          int count = level_boxes_fetch_registry_list(entries, LEVEL_REGISTRY_MAX_ENTRIES);
          int story_start_id = -1;
          for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
              if (entries[i].is_story_start) { story_start_id = entries[i].id; break; }
          }
          CustomLevelData lvl;
          if (story_start_id >= 0 && level_boxes_fetch_export(story_start_id, &lvl)) {
              lobby_apply_story_level(&lvl);
              return;
          }
          local_state.story_phase_start_ms = SDL_GetTicks();
          g_story_cutscene_done   = 0;
          g_story_outro_requested = 0;
          cutscene_start(&g_story_cs, g_cutscene_intro, g_cutscene_intro_count, SDL_GetTicks());
      }

      /* ---- shared procedural zones, client side -------------------------------------------------------
       * The server sends the zone's identity, never its geometry: PACKET_ZONE_STATE carries (id, seed) and this
       * rebuilds the identical layout with the same generator the host used (zone_sync.h explains why a
       * repeated 1 Hz packet must be a no-op). */
      static ZoneSync g_client_zone;
      
      static void client_apply_zone_state(const char *zone_id, unsigned int seed) {
          static CustomLevelData lvl;
          proc_dungeon_generate(&lvl, zone_id, seed);
          level_boxes_apply_to_physics(&lvl);
          scene_load(SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL);
          if (net_local_pid > 0 && net_local_pid < MAX_CLIENTS)
              local_state.players[net_local_pid].scene_id = SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL;
          memset(&g_client_zone, 0, sizeof g_client_zone);
          g_client_zone.active = 1;
          snprintf(g_client_zone.zone_id, sizeof g_client_zone.zone_id, "%s", zone_id);
          g_client_zone.seed = seed;
          NET_CLIENT_LOG("ZONE_RX id=%s seed=%08x (%d boxes)", zone_id, seed, lvl.count);
      }
      
      static void client_load_queue_level_id(int found_id) {
          if (found_id < 0) return;
          CustomLevelData lvl;
          if (!level_boxes_fetch_export(found_id, &lvl)) return; // keeps the old id; the next PACKET_QUEUE_LEVEL retries
          level_boxes_apply_to_physics(&lvl);
          g_spray_decal_count = 0; // decals are keyed by the shared SCENE_CUSTOM_LEVEL id -- see net_connect's reset
          g_spray_decal_next = 0;
          g_queue_level_id = found_id;
          g_queue_level_loaded = 1;
          printf("[QUEUE] now on level id=%d (%s)\n", found_id, lvl.name);

      /* empire_units_test.c -- the EMPIRE unit model, without a server, a GL context or a display.
       *
       * What this proves, in the founder's own terms: an archetype is a real thing to spawn (citizen, zombie,
       * soldier, ally, guard, worker) with its own brain role and skin; the generic human traits are inherited
       * by humans and NOT by the zombie; the orders are programmable (a mask plus priorities, with masked-out
       * orders scoring zero); the decision picks the highest triggered order, engages first when it can see an
       * enemy, and says NONE -- "use the role's own brain" -- when nothing applies; and a world really gives up
       * resources and ground through the same functions the AI tick calls.
       *
       * Build/run: make test-empire-units
       */
      #include "empire_units.h"
      #include "empire_units_rules_host.h"
      
      #include <stdio.h>
      #include <string.h>
      
      static int g_checks = 0;
      static int g_failures = 0;
      
      static void ok(int cond, const char *what) {
          g_checks++;
          if (!cond) {
              g_failures++;
              printf("FAIL  %s\n", what);
          } else {
              printf("ok    %s\n", what);
          }
      }
      
      /* A world with two nodes and two cells, the shape a level would seed. */
      static void build_world(EUWorld *w) {
          eu_world_clear(w);
          eu_world_add_node(w, 10.0f, 0.0f, 5);
          eu_world_add_node(w, -10.0f, 0.0f, 25);
          eu_world_add_claim_cell(w, 20.0f, 0.0f);
          eu_world_add_claim_cell(w, -20.0f, 0.0f);
      }
      
      int main(void) {
          printf("== empire_rules: PARENA and the header's defaults agree ==\n");
          {
              int mismatch = 0;
              for (int a = -1; a <= 8; a++) {
                  if (eu_archetype_species(a) != eu_c_archetype_species(a)) mismatch++;
                  if (eu_archetype_role(a) != eu_c_archetype_role(a)) mismatch++;
                  if (eu_archetype_kit(a) != eu_c_archetype_kit(a)) mismatch++;
                  if (eu_archetype_faction(a) != eu_c_archetype_faction(a)) mismatch++;
                  if (eu_archetype_orders(a) != eu_c_archetype_orders(a)) mismatch++;
                  if (eu_archetype_health(a) != eu_c_archetype_health(a)) mismatch++;
                  for (int o = -1; o <= 6; o++)
                      if (eu_order_priority(a, o) != eu_c_order_priority(a, o)) mismatch++;
              }
              ok(mismatch == 0, "every archetype field and order priority matches the C defaults");
              ok(eu_archetype_species(1) == g_eu_rules.archetype_species(1),
                 "the generated table is what g_eu_rules actually points at");
              ok(eu_human_loyalty() == eu_c_human_loyalty() && eu_beast_loyalty() == eu_c_beast_loyalty(),
                 "both inheritance rows match");
              ok(eu_claim_ticks() == eu_c_claim_ticks() && eu_gather_radius() == eu_c_gather_radius() &&
                 eu_explore_radius() == eu_c_explore_radius() && eu_follow_distance() == eu_c_follow_distance(),

// separate mode check needed. Now checks EVERY real active player (not just slot 0, which the
// dedicated server never even uses for a real connected client -- server main() explicitly
// deactivates it), and respawns EVERY active player after a real transition, not just whoever
// triggered it -- the whole world's own geometry just changed under everyone, matching (and
// improving on) server_advance_queue_round's own existing "the whole server moves together on a
// level change" precedent.
#define STORY_LEVEL_TRANSITION_DEBOUNCE_MS 3000U

/* tyler_apply_phase_override -- S536, TYLER VALHANNA. MODE_TYLER's two phases (wisp in Iceland,
 * Duck in CONSTRUCT, see packages/common/protocol.h's own MODE_TYLER doc comment) share one game
 * mode number -- this is the one real place that actually changes what a real (non-bot) player IS
 * once the level itself has changed, keyed on the just-loaded level's own name rather than a
 * separate phase enum, since the level name is already real, unique, authoritative data
 * (cmd/nock_gen_tyler_levels/main.go names them exactly "TYLER_VALHANNA_ICELAND_1986"/
 * "CONSTRUCT") -- no new state to keep in sync. Deliberately only touches REAL, non-bot players
 * (Tyler/Hana are is_bot AI_ROLE_STORY_ALLY NPCs, already handled by the ordinary character-spawn
 * path above; this function would be a harmless no-op against them anyway since neither branch
 * applies to a bot in any other mode, but the is_bot check makes the intent explicit). */
static void tyler_apply_phase_override(const char *level_name, unsigned int now_ms) {
    if (local_state.game_mode != MODE_TYLER) return;
    int is_construct = (strcmp(level_name, "CONSTRUCT") == 0);
    for (int pi = 0; pi < MAX_CLIENTS; pi++) {
        PlayerState *p = &local_state.players[pi];
        if (!p->active || p->is_bot) continue;
        if (is_construct) {
            /* The Duck -- third-person, SHANKPIT physics, Leela kit (packages/simulation/
             * story_ai.h's own AIKit enum -- AI_KIT_LEELA). apps/lobby/src/main.c's own
             * draw_player_3rd gains a matching MODE_TYLER branch so a forced_kit this player sets
             * on itself (not just story_ai-spawned bots) actually renders. */
            p->state = STATE_ALIVE;
            p->forced_kit = AI_KIT_LEELA;
            /* third_person is a real, separate flag from forced_kit as of this pass (see
             * PlayerState's own doc comment, protocol.h) -- the Duck phase sets both together,
             * but the camera itself now keys off this field alone, not the skin choice. */
            p->third_person = 1;
        } else {
            /* The wisp -- real STATE_SPECTATOR free-fly (packages/common/protocol.h,
             * packages/simulation/local_game.h's update_entity), no forced skin at all (nothing
             * should render a body for a camera-only orb), and no third-person camera either. */
            p->state = STATE_SPECTATOR;
            p->forced_kit = AI_KIT_AUTO;
            p->third_person = 0;
        }
    }
    (void)now_ms;
}

A level that\n * authors nothing loads nothing -- this function never invents terrain; the caller decides whether to\n * fall back to the default ring. */\nstatic inline int eu_world_load(EUWorld *w, int node_count, const float *node_x, const float *node_z,\n                                const int *node_amount, int cell_count, const float *cell_x,\n                                const float *cell_z, const int *cell_radius) {\n    if (!w) return 0;\n    eu_world_clear(w);\n    if (node_count > 0 && node_x && node_z && node_amount) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < node_count && w->node_count < EU_MAX_NODES; i++)\n            eu_world_add_node(w, node_x[i], node_z[i], node_amount[i]);\n    }\n    if (cell_count > 0 && cell_x && cell_z) {\n        for (int i = 0; i < cell_count && w->cell_count < EU_MAX_CLAIM_CELLS; i++) {\n            int idx = eu_world_add_claim_cell(w, cell_x[i], cell_z[i]);\n            /* 0 is the level schema's own \"use the host default\", not a one-unit cell. */\n            if (idx >= 0 && cell_radius && cell_radius[i] > 0) w->cells[idx].radius = cell_radius[i];\n        }\n    }\n    return w->node_count;\n}\n\n/* eu_hud_text -- one line for the HUD: how many units are under orders, what each side has banked, how\n * much ground is held, how many nodes still have something in them.
